# Roadmap: anabelian geometry and nonabelian Chabauty

**Summary.** Build arithmetic path torsors and continuous nonabelian cohomology from finite étale covers, use them to construct unipotent fundamental groups, cohomology varieties and Albanese maps, and obtain Chabauty–Kim finiteness and quadratic height equations. In parallel, reconstruct hyperbolic curves from source-qualified arithmetic fundamental groups. The final layer distinguishes proved injectivity and conditional dimension estimates from the section and eventual-equality conjectures.

## Scope and ownership

This roadmap owns the arithmetic refinement of geometric paths, the additional coefficient-action twisting, torsor classification and kernel-orbit calculus on Tau Ceti's continuous nonabelian H¹, the curve-specific étale `K(π,1)` assemblies, unipotent path realizations, anabelian reconstruction, nonabelian Selmer geometry, Albanese maps and quadratic Chabauty equations. Generic sites, schemes, Picard functors, cycle operations, period rings, continuous abelian cohomology and p-adic integration retain their owners. The specific comparisons joining these objects are stated below with their domains and hypotheses.

Mathlib supplies natural isomorphisms, abstract Galois categories, affine finite étale fibres, group actions and their orbit and coset quotients. Its `FixedPoints.subgroup` is `H⁰`. Tau Ceti supplies absolute Galois groups, finite Kummer classes, homogeneous continuous cohomology, explicit restriction and coefficient maps, maximal pro-p quotients and reconstruction for the finite comodules of an already specified Hopf algebra. These are inputs. PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology §RD.6.64 (`RD6.neutralTannakian_recognition`) supplies reconstruction from an arbitrary neutral tensor category. This roadmap constructs the two-fibre-functor torsor and unit-extension/pro-unipotent specialization using that equivalence.

Tau Ceti supplies all-degree finite-quotient cohomology, classwise killing on an open subgroup and positive-degree vanishing for the trivial group. They are in the Tau Ceti modules `RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/FiniteQuotient/AllDegreeColimit`, `…/ContCohomology/ClosedSubgroup` and `…/ContCohomology/TrivialGroup`, which carry out TauCetiRoadmap.ProfiniteCohomology Layer 10. Tau Ceti also supplies continuous ordered nonabelian cocycles, their gauge quotient, compatible-pair maps, restriction, descent, inflation injectivity and compact-discrete finite-quotient surjectivity through the native modules specified below. Layer 0 adds their categorical finite-colimit refinement and the further twisting, torsor, kernel-orbit and central-H² comparisons; same-subgroup gauge reflection is part of the supplied inflation proof.

TauCetiRoadmap.ProfiniteArithmetic supplies continuous automorphism and outer-automorphism groups and outer actions. The centre-free extension comparison used here is the additional pullback identification, rather than a new outer-automorphism group. TauCetiRoadmap.PeripheralActions supplies generic peripheral power actions; Chen's good and symmetric paths below impose geometric normalization and inversion conditions on tangential paths. TauCetiRoadmap.AlgebraicCurves Layers 4, 7, 9 and 12 supply Riemann–Roch, Hurwitz, complete-DVR differentials and the function-field/scheme dictionary. TauCetiRoadmap.JacobianChallenge Layers A, B, D, E and F supply line bundles, coherent cohomology, Picard and Jacobian schemes, abelian-variety theory and Abel–Jacobi maps. TauCetiRoadmap.AlgebraicVectorBundles Layers 0A and 0B supply coherent and locally free sheaves and their tensor operations.

SchemeAndStackFoundations §3.6 owns Picard torsors, and JacobianChallenge Layer D owns the obstruction from a relative Picard point to a line bundle. InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups §IG.0.T1 and AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli §A4.4 supply the finite-level curve–Jacobian and H¹/Tate-module comparisons; SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.15 owns stable pointed moduli and their level covers; its Layer 5 owns Chow groups, Chern classes, intersection, pushforward and pullback. These supply the portions of the reconstruction and correspondence arguments that require no general theory of motives. ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.1, R02.2 and D7 own compact coefficient limits and arithmetic Hochschild–Serre; its R02.3.2 owns function-field reciprocity. Mixed extensions and Nekovář's p-adic heights are constructed in Layer 6, in the generality the quadratic Chabauty equations need; a general theory of height pairings on Selmer complexes is outside this roadmap.

The common continuous carrier for PELModuli §M0.9, the EllipticCurves Layer 5 twist classification and the unipotent coefficients here is `TauCeti.NonabelianH1.Cocycle` with class set `TauCeti.NonabelianH1`. PELModuli supplies the algebraic Galois torsor comparison for smooth affine groups, including disconnected groups, using discrete geometric points; Layer 0 here adds the general topological torsor classification and coefficient-action twisting needed by Layers 4–7. These specializations and their comparisons use that same native carrier. The fppf homogeneous quotient sheaf `G/N` of an affine group by a closed, not necessarily normal, subgroup, with its torsor property, is supplied by Tau Ceti (`CommHopfAlgCat.fppfHomogeneousQuotient`, the sheafification of `CommHopfAlgCat.homogeneousQuotientPresheaf`; `CommHopfAlgCat.isPullback_fppfHomogeneousQuotientTorsor` and `CommHopfAlgCat.isLocallySurjective_fppfHomogeneousQuotientSheafProjection` give the torsor property); representability of `U/H` and the point formula for unipotent groups in characteristic zero are constructed in Layer 2 ([Unipotent groups and their homogeneous quotients in characteristic zero](#split-unipotent-quotients)). The complex-analytic statement that Artin neighbourhoods are `K(π,1)` is InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups §IG.3.1; Layer 1 here proves the étale finite-coefficient statement over any field of characteristic zero.

HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions §§1.15a–1.16 owns the integral formal groups, formal identity charts and normalized convergent formal logarithms. Layer 5 here owns their extension to the global abelian logarithm for arbitrary abelian varieties over finite p-adic fields, its compatible `ℂ_p` interface, the regular Coleman/abelian comparison, residue-chart specialization of analytic zero bounds and Mordell–Weil closure comparisons. RestrictedPowerSeries owns the restricted-series carriers and Strassmann theorem; ColemanIntegration owns the analytic Coleman algebra, primitives and polylogarithms. Layer 5 compares those supplied functions with the tensor paths of Layer 2. Effective Diophantine methods may use these comparisons and applications. The supplied neutral tensor reconstruction and the character formulas in Layers 2 and 7 require no motive or modular-form theory. Applications with a specified rank, finite local height-value sets or a complete list of zeros carry those facts as explicit hypotheses of the final theorem. The mathematical finiteness and height equations are targets here.

## Conventions

A product `gh` acts as g after h. A path p from b to x is a natural isomorphism of fibre functors. Its right translation by a source automorphism is `p·u = p ∘ u`. Arithmetic paths restrict to the identity on constant covers. The geometric kernel, rather than the entire arithmetic group, acts on them.

For a group acting by automorphisms on U, a cocycle satisfies `c(gh)=c(g)(g•c(h))`. Gauge translation is `u·c(g)=u c(g)(g•u)⁻¹`. A nonempty right U-torsor with a semilinear G-action and point p gives `g(p)=p·c_p(g)`; replacing p by `p·u` gives gauge translation by `u⁻¹`. `H¹` is a pointed set. In the abelian comparison, coefficients are written multiplicatively using `Multiplicative`; Mathlib's inhomogeneous additive differential is `d¹a(g,h)=g•a(h)−a(gh)+a(g)`.

The positive defect of a lift b is `D_b(g,h)=b(g)(g•b(h))b(gh)⁻¹`. It agrees with this additive differential. The opposite defect used in a displayed convention of Kim has the negative `H²` class; both have the same zero locus. The twist by c has `g⋆u=c(g)(g•u)c(g)⁻¹`, and the repointing map sends a twisted cocycle d to the original cocycle `g↦d(g)c(g)`.

The lower central series starts `at Γ₁U=U` and has `Γₙ₊₁U=[U,ΓₙU]`. Depth n means `U⟨n⟩=U/Γₙ₊₁U`, with depth zero trivial and depth one the abelianization. Kim's `U_(n+1)` is this depth n. The finite length module `A/I^(n+1)` is a module over the completed enveloping or group algebra, rather than a Hopf quotient. Multiplication of words is concatenation; coordinate functions are dual and have shuffle multiplication.

For a Frobenius-fixed path `pφ` and a Hodge path pH, write `pφ·u=pH`. The period is the right homogeneous coset of u in `U/F⁰U`. In word coordinates u is `I⁻¹γ`; replacing it by `γI⁻¹` changes the convention in the noncommutative case. `F⁰U` need not be normal. Crystalline objects over `K₀` are extended to K before comparison with the de Rham realization. Over a finite extension `K/ℚ_p`, dimension comparisons are made over K after the specified scalar extension, or over `ℚ_p` after Weil restriction on both sides.

Sections of an arithmetic exact sequence are identified only under conjugation by the geometric kernel. A relative outer homomorphism is over the fixed quotient Galois group and is identified under target geometric conjugation. Geometrically pro-p retains the full arithmetic quotient; it does not replace that quotient by its maximal pro-p group.

At a prime v away from p, the stringent quadratic Chabauty condition is membership in the local Kummer image. At p it is crystalline. The global depth-one cut is the rational Mordell–Weil Kummer image, rather than a rank substitution in the whole Selmer group. For a global height `h=h_p+Σ_(v≠p)h_v`, the correction set is `Υ={−Σ_v t_v | t_v∈Γ_v}`. A single away-place value 3 therefore contributes −3.

The geometric carriers and comparisons below carry their own hypotheses: arithmetic paths restrict to the identity on constants; unipotent length is extension length in the specified tensor category; relative maps are taken modulo target geometric conjugacy; and Selmer conditions use native nonabelian H¹ with arithmetic localization maps. Periods lie in right homogeneous cosets. Correspondences use the geometric cycle maps, heights use the stated splitting corrections, and determinants use fixed feature coordinates. Sections are taken modulo geometric conjugacy, dimension conditions use the represented schemes, and eventual equality retains its tail quantifier.

For algebra-valued unipotent points, the final topology is declared on each finite coordinate power. A continuous cochain on a compact domain has finite-dimensional coordinate image. Polynomial operations on these images give the compact-cochain continuity needed for gauge classes and central induction. An ordinary product-topology group structure is an additional specialization, with its compatibility hypothesis stated explicitly; it is not assumed for an arbitrary coefficient algebra.

## Exact supplier contracts

### From Mathlib and Tau Ceti

Use Mathlib `ContinuousMap`, `ContinuousMonoidHom`, `MulDistribMulAction`, `ContinuousSMul`, `IsTopologicalGroup`, `FixedPoints.subgroup`, `MulAction.orbitRel.Quotient`, `QuotientGroup` and `IsQuotientMap` with their topologies. `MonoidHom.ker`, subgroup comaps and cosets are used as they stand. The quotient action requires a normal source subgroup and an action on its fixed coefficient subgroup. A surjective continuous homomorphism alone is not a quotient-topology hypothesis. The fixed-gauge descent assertion does not assume compactness or a discrete coefficient group.

Use `CategoryTheory.Aut`, `CategoryTheory.Functor.isoWhiskerLeft`, `CategoryTheory.PreGaloisCategory.autEmbedding_isClosedEmbedding` and `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale.fiber` with their arrow directions. `Aut F` is a natural automorphism, not a group of labels. Its topology is the evaluation topology. `TauCeti.AbsoluteGaloisGroup`, `TauCeti.kummerMap` and `TauCeti.kummerMap_eq_kummerCocycleClass` provide the field and finite Kummer interfaces, with the coefficient order invertible in the field. The Abel–Jacobi rational Tate-module comparison below requires more than these finite classes.

Canonical abelian cohomology is `continuousCohomology` of a topological representation. The low-degree `TauCeti.ContCohomology` cocycle carriers and their canonical comparisons, explicit coefficient maps, restriction and inflation fix the additive comparison maps used in Layer 0. Use `TauCeti.ContCohomology.continuousFiniteQuotientColimit` and `TauCeti.ContCohomology.exists_continuousFiniteQuotientComparisonApp_eq` for the all-degree comparison, and `TauCeti.ContinuousCohomology.exists_openSubgroup_res_eq_zero` and `TauCeti.ContinuousCohomology.subsingleton_continuousCohomology_succ_of_subsingleton` for killing and vanishing, through the ProfiniteCohomology boundary above. The Tau Ceti quotient `TauCeti.maximalProPQuotient` (module `TauCeti.Topology.Algebra.Group.Profinite.MaximalProP`) supplies the geometric maximal pro-p quotient. `TauCeti.Tannaka.fgPointTensorIsoEquiv` identifies algebra-valued points of a given Hopf algebra with tensor automorphisms of its finite-comodule scalar-extension functor; PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology §RD.6.64 supplies general neutral reconstruction from a tensor category.

<a id="native-nonabelian-h1"></a>

The native continuous nonabelian supplier is Tau Ceti's `RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/Nonabelian/Basic.lean` and `Nonabelian/Inflation.lean` at [ce47fe1](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/tree/ce47fe1230545b9a6998d23746b87c8bdbaeb9e1/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/Nonabelian). Adoption requires a Tau Ceti dependency containing these modules and imports of those individual modules before implementing the carrier-dependent Layer 0 targets. At the `a91d3aa` pin these modules are absent, so `Suggested.lean` states no carrier-dependent Layer 0 theorem.

Use `TauCeti.NonabelianH1.Cocycle`, its `setoid`, and `TauCeti.NonabelianH1` directly. The names `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1` and `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1` below denote compatibility aliases to these carriers, rather than new structures or quotients. Native `Cocycle.apply_one`, `Cocycle.apply_inv`, `mk_eq_mk_iff`, `mk_eq_one_iff`, compatible-pair `Cocycle.map`/`map` and `res` supply their basic identities and functoriality. The native gauge `c.twist(a)(g)=a⁻¹c(g)(g•a)` equals this roadmap's `x·c` with `a=x⁻¹`. In particular native `Cocycle.twist` changes a representative by a constant gauge; the coefficient action `g⋆u=c(g)(g•u)c(g)⁻¹` constructed here is a different operation.

Native `Cocycle.descend`, `infl`, `infl_injective`, `res_eq_one_iff` and `exists_mem_range_infl` supply descent, same-kernel gauge reflection, inflation–restriction and finite-stage existence. Listed names for these operations are aliases or compatibility lemmas with our parameter convention. Additional inverse equivalences, quotient-transition diagrams and their categorical colimit use these results. The native carrier and quotient require only groups, topologies and `MulDistribMulAction`; this includes §4.2's weak coefficient topology. Closure of cocycles under representative gauge translation or under coefficient-action twisting uses the continuity hypotheses stated where those constructions are applied.

**IG.0 and IG.1.** Use the category of finite étale covers, its geometric fibre functors and profinite automorphism group, the finite continuous π-set equivalence, pointed connected refinements and tame tangential fibres at a boundary point (§IG.1.2). EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.0.2 supplies the finite étale category, geometric fibre functors, `π₁^ét`, paths and finite lisse monodromy; §§F.0.A0–F.0.A2 supply the field and multiplicative-group identifications, decomposition and inertia, and the arithmetic exact sequence. No separate completed-cohomology construction is made here. The required five-term maps are inflation and restriction on the canonical carriers. Finiteness and Euler characteristic hypotheses include the ramification set, the coefficient lattice and the real-place correction. Rational `H³` vanishes even when `p=2` and a real place contributes integral 2-torsion.

The tame local abelian extension correspondence needed for finite-field tame reconstruction is TauCetiRoadmap.ClassFieldTheory Layer 8 (`localAbelianExistence_primeToResidueCharacteristic`, `localClassFieldCorrespondence_primeToResidueCharacteristic`), stated for every nonarchimedean local field and index prime to the residue characteristic. Mixed-characteristic local duality comes from TauCetiRoadmap.ClassFieldTheory Layer 5. Full equal-characteristic p-primary local existence is not used.

**SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0, L2 and L4.** Import S-unit Kummer, compact/rational global Selmer kernels, unramified conditions, Bloch–Kato finite conditions and rational duality. For abelian varieties over number fields, SelmerIwasawaCohomology §2.12a supplies `abelianKummer`, the local images `KummerLocal`, `abelianSelmerGroup`, `abelianSha`, `abelianDescent_exact` and `abelianSelmerGroup_finite`. Use HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions §1.1 for the fppf comparison and §§1.6–1.7 for weak Mordell–Weil and finite generation, and [Rational abelian Kummer and Sha comparison](#abelian-kummer-mordell-weil) for the inverse limit over `[p^k]` and rational Tate-module form. At depth one the geometric path class is compared to the Jacobian Kummer class by Layer 2. The Selmer group includes the Tate module of Sha unless a vanishing hypothesis is imposed; rank alone never removes it. The `subgroup H¹_g` and the inclusions `H¹_e⊆H¹_f⊆H¹_g` are the Layer 4 target [The Bloch–Kato subgroups `H¹_e⊆H¹_f⊆H¹_g`](#bloch-kato-subgroups).

**Mixed extensions and p-adic heights.** No lower-tier roadmap states mixed extensions or Nekovář's heights. ## How to read the build

Layer 0 gives the nonabelian cohomology used by paths. Layer 1 supplies the finite-cover geometric foundation. Layer 2 constructs unipotent realizations independently of curve reconstruction; Layer 3 can then use its two-step quotient. Layers 4 and 5 turn path classes into Selmer varieties, periods and finite loci. Layer 6 opens with mixed extensions and Nekovář's p-adic heights, then adds rational correspondences and the height equations. Layer 7 records the conjectural endpoints and proves the precise conditional implications. Within each layer, the prerequisite links of a target point backward in the construction order. In Layer 0 each definition carries the results about it as a list of named statements, each with its proof sketch and its own anchor; such an entry may use later results of the same layer, which it names. Heavy geometric constructions are specified here; Suggested.lean contains only representative signatures over the pinned carriers.

## Layer 0: Continuous nonabelian cohomology

Use the [native continuous nonabelian H¹](#native-nonabelian-h1) pointed set. Construct its additional coefficient-action twists, torsor classification, kernel-orbit descriptions, central obstruction theory and categorical finite-colimit comparison, retaining the order of multiplication and the topology; no commutativity of the coefficient group is imposed.

**Standing hypotheses.** Many targets of this layer share their hypotheses. They are collected here once, and each such target names its set; any further hypothesis is stated with the target.

- **(H1)** G is a group with a topology; coefficient groups U,U′,U″ have topologies and G-actions by automorphisms. For `H¹` and gauge compatibility, each coefficient group is a topological group and the action is jointly continuous. Coefficient homomorphisms are continuous and G-equivariant. No compactness, discreteness, commutativity, finiteness, or topology of a unipotent algebraic group is assumed. The `H⁰` maps require only group structures and equivariant homomorphisms; no topology or continuity hypothesis enters them.

- **(H2)** G and U,U′,U″ are groups, with G acting by automorphisms on each coefficient group. Coefficient homomorphisms are G-equivariant. No topology or continuity hypothesis is required.

- **(H3)** No compactness, discreteness, finite coefficient group, commutativity or geometric realization is assumed. `H¹` and gauge assertions require jointly continuous actions on topological coefficient groups.

- **(H4)** G is a group endowed with a topology; U is a group endowed with a topology and G acts on U by group automorphisms. N is an arbitrary subgroup with its subtype topology and restricted action. U is a topological group and the joint G-action on U is continuous. No normality, compactness, openness, closedness, discreteness or commutativity is required for restriction and inverse-gauge normalization.

- **(H5)** For `H⁰`, only groups and automorphism actions are needed, with `h·u=φ(h)·u`; no topology or continuity is required.

### 0.1 Continuous cocycles and H¹
<a id="nc-3-continuous-cocycles"></a>

**Continuous 1-cocycles and invariants with nonabelian coefficients.** Let G be a topological group and U a topological group on which G acts by group automorphisms, continuously (`G × U → U` continuous). The invariants are `H⁰(G, U) := U^G = {u ∈ U : g•u = u for all g}`, a subgroup of U (Mathlib FixedPoints.subgroup). Use the supplied `TauCeti.NonabelianH1.Cocycle G U` for `Z¹(G,U)`, with equation `c(gh)=c(g)·(g•c(h))`, and its trivial cocycle 1 as base point.

G is a topological group and U a topological group with an action of G by group automorphisms (MulDistribMulAction G U) such that the action map `G × U → U` is continuous (ContinuousSMul G U). No commutativity of U; for U commutative written additively the definitions agree with Tau Ceti's explicit continuous cohomology ([Comparison with abelian continuous cohomology](#nc-3-abelian-comparison)).

Definition as stated; `H⁰` is FixedPoints.subgroup for the MulDistribMulAction. Elementary identities: `c(1) = 1` (put `g = h = 1`), `c(g⁻¹) = g⁻¹•(c(g)⁻¹)` (put `h = g⁻¹`), and the coboundaries `g ↦ u·(g•u)⁻¹` are cocycles: `u·(gh•u)⁻¹ = u(g•u)⁻¹·g•(u(h•u)⁻¹)` because g acts by automorphisms. The coboundary of u is continuous since `g ↦ g•u` is continuous. Trivial action: then the cocycle condition says c is a homomorphism, so `Z¹(G, U)` is the set of continuous homomorphisms `G → U (ContinuousMonoidHom)`.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1`: Compatibility alias for `TauCeti.NonabelianH1.Cocycle`, with the same underlying function and ordered cocycle equation.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.mem_iff`: A function `f:G→U` is the underlying function of a continuous cocycle if and only if f is continuous and `f(gh)=f(g)·(g•f(h))` for all g,h.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.instOne`: The trivial cocycle `g ↦ 1`, the base point.
- <a id="nc-3-cocycle-map-one"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.map_one` (*Identity value of a nonabelian cocycle*): For every continuous nonabelian cocycle c, `c(1)=1`. Under (H12). *Proof.* Use `c(1)=c(1)c(1)` from the cocycle identity `at(1,1)` and cancel the left factor. Source: [Native nonabelian H¹](#native-nonabelian-h1), `Cocycle.apply_one`; the displayed calculation is an elementary deduction from the cocycle equation.
- <a id="nc-3-cocycle-map-inverse"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.map_inv` (*Inverse value of a nonabelian cocycle*): For every c and g, `c(g⁻¹)=g⁻¹•c(g)⁻¹`. Under (H12). *Proof.* Evaluate the cocycle identity `at(g⁻¹,g)`. Since `c(1)=1`, `c(g⁻¹)` is the inverse of `g⁻¹•c(g)`. The automorphism action preserves inverses. Source: [Native nonabelian H¹](#native-nonabelian-h1), `Cocycle.apply_inv`; the displayed calculation is an elementary deduction from the cocycle equation. Uses [Identity value of a nonabelian cocycle](#nc-3-cocycle-map-one).
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.coboundary`: For `u ∈ U`, the cocycle `g ↦ u·(g•u)⁻¹`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.equivContinuousMonoidHomOfTrivial`: If G acts trivially, `Z¹(G, U) ≃ (G →ₜ* U)`, continuous homomorphisms.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.ext`: Two cocycles are equal iff they agree at every g.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.trivial_group`: If G is the trivial group, `Z¹(G, U) = {1}`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.trivial_action_hom`: For `G = ℤ/2` (discrete) acting trivially on the symmetric group `S₃` (discrete), `Z¹(G, S₃)` has exactly 4 elements: the trivial map and the three maps sending the generator to a transposition.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.factor_order`: For discrete `G = U = S₃` with trivial action, construct the identity continuous cocycle c. At `g=(01)`, `h=(12)`, `c(gh)=c(g)·(g•c(h))`, whereas `c(gh)≠(g•c(h))·c(g)`. Evaluate the identity cocycle in `Z¹`, so the two noncommuting permutation products discriminate the definition.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.invariants`: For `G = ℤ/2` acting on `U = ℤ` by negation, `H⁰(G, U) = {0}`; for the trivial action `H⁰ = U`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.continuity`: For `G = ∏_{n ∈ ℕ} ℤ/2` (profinite) acting trivially on `U = ℤ/2` (discrete), `Z¹(G, U)` is countable (continuous characters factor through finitely many coordinates), whereas the abstract homomorphisms `G → ℤ/2` are uncountable: dropping continuity changes `Z¹`.
- The order of the factors matters when U is not commutative: the condition `c(gh) = (g•c(h))·c(g)` of Mathlib's commutative IsMulCocycle₁ defines a different set for nonabelian U (test below).
- Continuity is part of the definition. For compact G and discrete U, every continuous cocycle is identically 1 on some open normal N, is constant on its cosets and takes values in the `U^N`. The quotient is finite. Descent must retain `U^N`; the action on all U need not factor through `G/N`.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, p. 6; [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, p. 6; [Bjorn Poonen](#reference-poonen-rational-points), §1.3.5, Definition 1.3.14 and Proposition 1.3.15, pp. 11–12, for Galois-cohomology notation and Hilbert 90 background only.

Use `MulDistribMulAction`; `FixedPoints.subgroup`; `ContinuousSMul`; `IsTopologicalGroup`; `ContinuousMap`; `ContinuousMonoidHom`; `groupCohomology.IsMulCocycle₁`.
<a id="nc-3-nonabelian-h1"></a>

**Nonabelian first cohomology as a pointed set.** In the situation of [Continuous 1-cocycles and invariants with nonabelian coefficients](#nc-3-continuous-cocycles), U acts on `Z¹(G, U)` by `(u·c)(g) := u·c(g)·(g•u)⁻¹`. Use `TauCeti.NonabelianH1 G U`, the quotient by the native cocycle setoid, pointed by the class of the trivial cocycle. Its equivalence with the orbit set for the displayed inverse-parameter action is a compatibility description on this carrier; two cocycles in one orbit are called cohomologous. The class of c is trivial iff c is a coboundary `g ↦ u·(g•u)⁻¹`.

G is a topological group and U a topological group with an action of G by group automorphisms (MulDistribMulAction G U) such that the action map `G × U → U` is continuous (ContinuousSMul G U).

The formula defines a group action: `(u·(v·c))(g) = u v c(g) (g•v)⁻¹ (g•u)⁻¹ =` (uv) `c(g)` (g•(uv))⁻¹, since g acts by automorphisms; `1·c = c`. `u·c` is again a cocycle: `(u·c)(gh) = u c(g) g•c(h) (gh•u)⁻¹`, and `(u·c)(g)·g•((u·c)(h)) = u c(g) (g•u)⁻¹ g•u g•c(h) g•(h•u)⁻¹`, which agree. Continuity: `u·c` is a product of continuous maps (`g ↦ g•u` is continuous). The orbit of the trivial cocycle is the set of coboundaries `g ↦ u·(g•u)⁻¹`, by definition of the action. `H¹` is a pointed set, not a group: there is no natural composition law when U is not commutative.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.instMulAction`: The action `(u·c)(g) = u·c(g)·(g•u)⁻¹` of U on `Z¹(G, U)`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1`: Compatibility alias for `TauCeti.NonabelianH1 G U`; express its native setoid as the orbits of the displayed gauge action without introducing a second quotient.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.mk`: The class map `Z¹(G, U) → H¹(G, U)`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.mk_surjective`: Every class has a representing cocycle.
- <a id="nc-3-h1-orbit-criterion"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.mk_eq_mk_iff` (*Equality of nonabelian cohomology classes*): For continuous cocycles c,c′, their classes in `H¹(G,U)` are equal if and only if there is `x∈U` with `x·c=c′`, where `(x·c)(g)=x c(g)(g•x)⁻¹`. The equality criterion uses the genuine gauge action, not multiplication by a coboundary. Hypotheses: G is a group endowed with a topology. U is a topological group with a group-automorphism action of G whose joint action is continuous. `H¹` is the twisted-conjugation orbit set of continuous nonabelian cocycles, with the class of the constant identity cocycle as base point. *Proof.* Unfold the orbit-set class map. Quotient equality is the orbit relation; reverse its arguments to match the stated `x·c=c′` orientation. Use the orbit-relation membership and orbit witness formulas. Source: [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed p. 6, continuous cocycle and gauge-orbit definitions; derived fixed-normal-subgroup argument.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.instOne`: The base point, the class of the trivial cocycle.
- <a id="nc-3-h1-neutral-criterion"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.mk_eq_one_iff` (*Neutral class as a coboundary*): For any continuous cocycle c, `[c]=1` if and only if there is `x∈U` with `c(g)=x(g•x)⁻¹` for all g. Under (H4). *Proof.* Apply the genuine orbit criterion with the identity cocycle as source. Evaluate the gauge action on that cocycle and use cocycle extensionality for the converse. Source: [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed pp. 5–6, continuous cocycle and gauge definitions; authored inflation–restriction deduction. Uses [Equality of nonabelian cohomology classes](#nc-3-h1-orbit-criterion).
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.equivOfTrivial`: For trivial action, `H¹(G, U) ≃ (G →ₜ* U)` modulo conjugation by U.
- <a id="nc-3-h1-gauge-class"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.mk_smul` (*Gauge invariance of the cohomology class*): For every `x∈U` and `c∈Z¹(G,U)`, `[x·c]=[c]`. Under (H4). *Proof.* The orbit criterion identifies [c] and `[x·c]` using the witness x; reverse the equality. Source: [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed pp. 5–6, continuous cocycle and gauge definitions; authored inflation–restriction deduction. Uses [Equality of nonabelian cohomology classes](#nc-3-h1-orbit-criterion).

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.h1_trivial_group`: If G is the trivial group, `H¹(G, U)` is a single point.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.h1_S3`: For `G = ℤ/2` acting trivially on `S₃` (both discrete), `H¹(G, S₃)` has exactly 2 elements: the base point and the class of the transpositions.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.not_coboundary_quotient`: In the same example, identifying cocycles c, c′ when `c′(g) = c(g)·u(g•u)⁻¹` for some u gives 4 classes (the action is trivial, so every such b is trivial), not 2: the correct relation is twisted conjugation.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.h1_abelian`: For `G = ℤ/2` acting on `U = ℤ/3` (additive, discrete) by negation, `H¹` is a single point, agreeing with Tau Ceti's ContCohomology.H1 (the orders are coprime).
- For trivial action, `H¹(G, U)` is the set of continuous homomorphisms `G → U` modulo conjugation by U.
- Cohomologous means related by the action; for nonabelian U this is not `'c′ = c·b` for a coboundary b' (test below).
- Two gauge-related cocycles have equal classes even if their functions differ. For a trivial action the criterion is conjugacy of homomorphisms.
- This is invariance under the whole coefficient gauge group, without an abelian quotient law.
- Neutrality is gauge triviality; it does not require the chosen representing function to equal 1.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, p. 6; [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Introduction, pp. 94–95.

Use [Continuous 1-cocycles and invariants with nonabelian coefficients](#nc-3-continuous-cocycles); `MulAction.orbitRel`; `MulAction.orbitRel.Quotient`.

### 0.2 Comparison with abelian continuous cohomology
<a id="nc-3-abelian-comparison"></a>

**Comparison with abelian continuous cohomology.** Let M be a commutative topological group written additively, with a continuous action of G by additive automorphisms, and `U = Multiplicative M`. With the induced action on U (Mathlib has no instance for it, so one is supplied), `Z¹(G, U)` is Tau Ceti's group of explicit continuous 1-cocycles ContCohomology.Z1 G M (cocycles `c(gh) = c(g) + g•c(h)`, in Mathlib's IsCocycle₁ convention), the action of U on `Z¹` is translation by the coboundaries `d⁰(m)(g) = g•m − m` up to sign, and the class map induces a bijection of pointed sets `H¹(G, U) ≅ ContCohomology.H1 G M`, sending the base point to 0. Consequently `H¹(G, U)` inherits a commutative group structure, `H⁰(G, U) = ContCohomology.H0 G M`, and for discrete G the cocycles are Mathlib's groupCohomology.IsMulCocycle₁ maps (the factor order being immaterial for commutative M).

M a commutative topological additive group with a continuous DistribMulAction of G; G a topological group.

The multiplicative cocycle identity for Multiplicative M is additive: `c(gh) = c(g) + g•c(h)`; continuity is the same condition. This is Tau Ceti's d¹-kernel description `(ContCohomology.d1_apply: d¹f(g,h) = g•f(h) − f(gh) + f(g))`. The action: `(m·c)(g) = m + c(g) − g•m = c(g) − (d⁰m)(g)`, so orbits are cosets of `B¹ = range d⁰` (Tau Ceti ContCohomology.B1) inside `Z¹`, and the orbit set is `Z¹/B¹ = ContCohomology.H1 G M`. Invariants: FixedPoints.subgroup of the multiplicative action is FixedPoints.addSubgroup of the additive one (Tau Ceti ContCohomology.H0). For discrete G and commutative M, `c(gh) = c(g)·g•c(h)` and Mathlib's IsMulCocycle₁ `c(gh) = g•c(h)·c(g)` coincide.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.instMulDistribMulActionMultiplicative`: A DistribMulAction of G on the additive group M induces a MulDistribMulAction of G on Multiplicative M (not an instance in Mathlib at the pin), and continuity of the action transfers.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.equivContCohomology`: `Z¹(G, Multiplicative M) ≃ ContCohomology.Z1 G M`, the identity on underlying functions.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.equivContCohomology`: `H¹(G, Multiplicative M) ≃ ContCohomology.H1 G M`, compatible with the class maps.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.equivContCohomology_one`: The base point goes to 0.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H0.equivContCohomology`: `H⁰(G, Multiplicative M)` corresponds to ContCohomology.H0 G M.

**Checks.**

- For the trivial action of `C₂` on additive `ℤ/2`, both pointed sets have two elements, distinguished by the generator value.
- For the negation action of `C₂` on additive `ℤ`, cocycles are indexed by an integer and coboundaries by even integers, giving two H¹ classes. The inverse gauge parameter changes the coboundary sign and leaves the quotient unchanged.

- For trivial action, both sides are the continuous homomorphisms `G → M` (Tau Ceti ContCohomology.H1EquivOfSmulEqSelf).

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, p. 6.

Use [Nonabelian first cohomology as a pointed set](#nc-3-nonabelian-h1); `TauCeti.ContCohomology.Z1`; `TauCeti.ContCohomology.B1`; `TauCeti.ContCohomology.H1`; `TauCeti.ContCohomology.H1pi`; `TauCeti.ContCohomology.H0`; `TauCeti.ContCohomology.d0`; `TauCeti.ContCohomology.d1`; `TauCeti.ContCohomology.H1EquivOfSmulEqSelf`; `groupCohomology.IsMulCocycle₁`; `Multiplicative`.

### 0.3 Coefficient maps on cocycles

Use native `TauCeti.NonabelianH1.Cocycle.map` with the identity source map; the names below specialize its compatible-pair API.

<a id="nc-3-coefficient-cocycle-map"></a>

**Coefficient map on continuous cocycles.** For a continuous G-equivariant homomorphism `f:U→U′`, use the native compatible-pair cocycle map `c↦f∘c`. Its exact evaluation, neutral cocycle and gauge formulas determine the induced pointed-set map.

Standing hypotheses (H1).

Continuity is composition. Apply f to the ordered cocycle identity and use its multiplication law and equivariance. The map is evaluated at every g; it is not an arbitrary choice of a cocycle with the same class.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.map`: For a continuous G-equivariant homomorphism `f:U→U′`, use the native compatible-pair cocycle map `c↦f∘c`. Its exact evaluation, neutral cocycle and gauge formulas determine the induced pointed-set map.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.map_apply`: The exact cocycle-map value at g is `f(c(g))`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.map_trivial`: The trivial cocycle maps to the trivial cocycle.
- <a id="nc-3-coefficient-cocycle-gauge"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.map_smul` (*Gauge compatibility of coefficient cocycle maps*): For every `x∈U` and cocycle c, mapping the gauge transform `x·c` equals the gauge transform `f(x)·(f∘c)`. *Proof.* Apply cocycle extensionality, keeping factor order, and expand `f(x c(g) (g·x)⁻¹)`. Use homomorphism multiplication/inverse preservation and G-equivariance. Uses [Nonabelian first cohomology as a pointed set](#nc-3-nonabelian-h1).
- <a id="nc-3-coefficient-cocycle-identity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.map_id` (*Identity coefficient map on cocycles*): The coefficient cocycle map induced by `id_U` is the identity function. *Proof.* The underlying pointwise function is the identity; the subtype proofs are propositionally irrelevant.
- <a id="nc-3-coefficient-cocycle-composition"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.map_comp` (*Composition of coefficient cocycle maps*): The cocycle map induced by `f′∘f` equals the composite of the cocycle maps induced by f and f′, in that order. *Proof.* Both sides evaluate exactly as `f′(f(c(g)))`. Composition supplies continuity and equivariance of the composite.

**Checks.**

- `coefficientCocyclesTests.identity`: The identity coefficient homomorphism fixes every continuous cocycle.
- `coefficientCocyclesTests.constant`: The coefficient homomorphism with constant value one takes every cocycle to the trivial cocycle.
- `coefficientCocyclesTests.value`: For every f,c,g the cocycle-map value is exactly `f(c(g))`.
- `coefficientCocyclesTests.transposition`: For the `S₂→S₃` transposition cocycle with trivial action, the identity coefficient map sends the source transposition to the same target transposition.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, continuous cocycles and gauge orbits, printed pp. 5–6; coefficient-functor paragraph after Proposition 1, printed p. 7.

Use [Continuous 1-cocycles and invariants with nonabelian coefficients](#nc-3-continuous-cocycles); `Continuous.comp`; `map_mul`.

### 0.4 Coefficient maps on H¹ and restriction along the source

Use native `TauCeti.NonabelianH1.map` for the class map; the coefficient and source specializations below share this implementation.

<a id="nc-3-coefficient-h1-map"></a>

**Coefficient map on nonabelian cohomology.** The continuous equivariant coefficient homomorphism f induces the map on gauge-orbit `H¹`, taking [c] to `[f∘c]`. It preserves the distinguished class and obeys identity and composition; `H¹` remains a pointed set. No injectivity is asserted for arbitrary f.

Standing hypotheses (H1).

Lift the cocycle-map class through the orbit quotient. If the source relation relates representatives via x, gauge compatibility relates their images via `f(x)`, with inversion where the orbit-relation orientation requires it. Compute on representatives; surjectivity of the class map proves the stated identity/composition laws.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.map`: The continuous equivariant coefficient homomorphism f induces the map on gauge-orbit `H¹`, taking [c] to `[f∘c]`. It preserves the distinguished class and obeys identity and composition; `H¹` remains a pointed set. No injectivity is asserted for arbitrary f.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.map_mk`: The map takes the class of c to the class of the cocycle `f∘c`.
- <a id="nc-3-coefficient-h1-one"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.map_one` (*Neutral class under coefficient maps*): The `H¹` coefficient map sends the neutral class to the neutral class. *Proof.* The cocycle map sends the constant-one cocycle to itself, because `f(1)=1`. Take its class.
- <a id="nc-3-coefficient-h1-identity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.map_id` (*Identity coefficient map on cohomology*): The `H¹` map induced by `id_U` is the identity of the pointed set. *Proof.* Use class-map surjectivity and compute on each cocycle representative. Uses [Identity coefficient map on cocycles](#nc-3-coefficient-cocycle-identity).
- <a id="nc-3-coefficient-h1-composition"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.map_comp` (*Composition of coefficient cohomology maps*): The pointed-set map on `H¹` induced by `f′∘f` equals `H¹(f′)∘H¹(f)`. *Proof.* Use class-map surjectivity and the ordered cocycle composition formula. Uses [Composition of coefficient cocycle maps](#nc-3-coefficient-cocycle-composition).

**Checks.**

- `coefficientClassesTests.identity`: The identity coefficient map fixes every `H¹` class.
- `coefficientClassesTests.gauge`: A gauge-transformed representative maps to the class of `f∘c`, independently of the gauge witness.
- `coefficientClassesTests.one`: Every coefficient map takes the neutral class to the neutral class.
- `coefficientClassesTests.noninjective`: The `S₂→S₃` transposition class is nonneutral but maps to the neutral class under the constant-one coefficient homomorphism. Arbitrary coefficient maps are not injective.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, continuous cocycles and gauge orbits, printed pp. 5–6; coefficient-functor paragraph after Proposition 1, printed p. 7.

Use [Gauge compatibility of coefficient cocycle maps](#nc-3-coefficient-cocycle-gauge); [Equality of nonabelian cohomology classes](#nc-3-h1-orbit-criterion).
<a id="nc-3-coefficient-invariant-map"></a>

**Coefficient homomorphism on invariant groups.** A G-equivariant group homomorphism `f:U→U′` induces the group homomorphism `U^G→(U′)^G` with value `x↦f(x)`. No topology or continuity condition is needed. It preserves the group operations and obeys identity and composition.

Standing hypotheses (H2).

For fixed x, equivariance identifies `g·f(x)` with `f(g·x)=f(x)`. Bundle the pointwise restriction as the MonoidHom between fixed subgroups; its multiplication and unit laws come from f.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H0.map`: A G-equivariant group homomorphism `f:U→U′` induces the group homomorphism `U^G→(U′)^G` with value `x↦f(x)`. No topology or continuity condition is needed. It preserves the group operations and obeys identity and composition.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H0.map_apply`: The underlying invariant-subgroup value is exactly `f(x)`.
- <a id="nc-3-coefficient-invariant-identity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H0.map_id` (*Identity coefficient homomorphism on invariants*): The invariant-group homomorphism induced by `id_U` is the identity homomorphism. *Proof.* The underlying map and fixed-subgroup witnesses agree; proof irrelevance identifies the bundled data.
- <a id="nc-3-coefficient-invariant-composition"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H0.map_comp` (*Composition of invariant coefficient homomorphisms*): The invariant-group homomorphism induced by `f′∘f` equals the composite of the restricted invariant homomorphisms. *Proof.* Compute both underlying homomorphisms as `x↦f′(f(x))`, using the subgroup carriers.

**Checks.**

- `invariantCoefficientsTests.identity`: The identity homomorphism fixes every element of the invariant subgroup.
- `invariantCoefficientsTests.constant`: The constant-one coefficient homomorphism sends every invariant element to one.
- `invariantCoefficientsTests.value`: The restricted invariant homomorphism has value `f(x)` in the ambient coefficient group.
- `invariantCoefficientsTests.transposition`: For `S₃` with trivial S₂-action, the invariant transposition is fixed by the identity coefficient homomorphism.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, continuous cocycles and gauge orbits, printed pp. 5–6; coefficient-functor paragraph after Proposition 1, printed p. 7.

Use [Continuous 1-cocycles and invariants with nonabelian coefficients](#nc-3-continuous-cocycles); `FixedPoints.subgroup`; `FixedPoints.mem_subgroup`; `map_one`; `map_mul`.

<a id="nc-3-source-cocycle-restriction"></a>

**Restriction along a continuous source homomorphism.** Let G,H,K be groups with topologies, U a group with a topology and actions by automorphisms, `φ:H→G` a continuous homomorphism, and `h·u=φ(h)·u`. Write `res_φ` for precomposition on continuous cocycles. Construct `res_φ:Z¹(G,U)→Z¹(H,U)` by `c↦c∘φ`.

Standing hypotheses (H3).

Compose the continuous function with `φ`. The homomorphism identity and action compatibility turn the G-cocycle identity into the H-cocycle identity.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-source-cocycle-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.res_apply` (*Values of source restriction*): Let G,H,K be groups with topologies, U a group with a topology and actions by automorphisms, `φ:H→G` a continuous homomorphism, and `h·u=φ(h)·u`. Write `res_φ` for precomposition on continuous cocycles. For `h∈H`, `res_φ(c)(h)=c(φ(h))`. *Proof.* Evaluate the defining precomposition.
- <a id="nc-3-source-cocycle-neutral"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.res_one` (*The neutral restricted cocycle*): Let G,H,K be groups with topologies, U a group with a topology and actions by automorphisms, `φ:H→G` a continuous homomorphism, and `h·u=φ(h)·u`. Write `res_φ` for precomposition on continuous cocycles. `res_φ(1)=1`. *Proof.* Precomposing the constant-one function leaves it constant one.
- <a id="nc-3-source-cocycle-identity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.res_id` (*Identity source restriction on cocycles*): Let G,H,K be groups with topologies, U a group with a topology and actions by automorphisms, `φ:H→G` a continuous homomorphism, and `h·u=φ(h)·u`. Write `res_φ` for precomposition on continuous cocycles. `res_id` is the identity on `Z¹(G,U)`. *Proof.* Function and subtype extensionality reduce to `c(id(g))=c(g)`.
- <a id="nc-3-source-cocycle-composition"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.res_comp` (*Contravariant composition on cocycles*): Let G,H,K be groups with topologies, U a group with a topology and actions by automorphisms, `φ:H→G` a continuous homomorphism, and `h·u=φ(h)·u`. Write `res_φ` for precomposition on continuous cocycles. For continuous `ψ:K→H` with `k·u=ψ(k)·u`, `res_(φ∘ψ)=res_ψ∘res_φ`, using the composite action compatibility. *Proof.* Evaluate both functions `at k∈K`: each has value `c(φ(ψ(k)))`.
- <a id="nc-3-source-cocycle-surjective-injection"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.res_injective` (*Surjective sources detect cocycles*): Let G,H,K be groups with topologies, U a group with a topology and actions by automorphisms, `φ:H→G` a continuous homomorphism, and `h·u=φ(h)·u`. Write `res_φ` for precomposition on continuous cocycles. If `φ` is surjective, `res_φ` is injective on cocycles. *Proof.* Choose an H-preimage of each `g∈G` and evaluate equality of restricted cocycles there. Uses [Values of source restriction](#nc-3-source-cocycle-value).
- <a id="nc-3-source-cocycle-subgroup"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.res_subgroup` (*Agreement with subgroup cocycle restriction*): Let G,H,K be groups with topologies, U a group with a topology and actions by automorphisms, `φ:H→G` a continuous homomorphism, and `h·u=φ(h)·u`. Write `res_φ` for precomposition on continuous cocycles. For every `subgroup N≤G` with induced topology and action, res along N.subtype equals the Z1.restrict N. No closedness is needed for this cocycle equality. *Proof.* Both maps evaluate c on the underlying element of N. Uses [Restriction of continuous nonabelian cocycles](#nc-3-cocycle-restriction).
- <a id="nc-3-source-cocycle-gauge"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.res_smul` (*Gauge compatibility of source restriction*): Let G,H,K be groups with topologies, U a group with a topology and actions by automorphisms, `φ:H→G` a continuous homomorphism, and `h·u=φ(h)·u`. Write `res_φ` for precomposition on continuous cocycles. With jointly continuous actions on topological U, `res_φ(x·c)=x·res_φ(c)` for `x∈U`. *Proof.* Expand `x c(φ(h)) (φ(h)·x)⁻¹` and replace `φ(h)·x` by `h·x`. Uses [Values of source restriction](#nc-3-source-cocycle-value); [Nonabelian first cohomology as a pointed set](#nc-3-nonabelian-h1).
- <a id="nc-3-source-coefficient-cocycle-square"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.res_map` (*Coefficient change commutes with source restriction*): Let G,H,K be groups with topologies, U a group with a topology and actions by automorphisms, `φ:H→G` a continuous homomorphism, and `h·u=φ(h)·u`. Write `res_φ` for precomposition on continuous cocycles. For a continuous G-equivariant `f:U→V` and pulled-back H-actions on U,V, `res_φ∘map_f=map_f∘res_φ` on cocycles. The H-equivariance of f follows from G-equivariance and the two action equalities. *Proof.* Both maps have value `f(c(φ(h))) at h`; rewrite the action equalities to provide the induced H-equivariance proof. Uses [Coefficient map on continuous cocycles](#nc-3-coefficient-cocycle-map).

**Checks.**

- `sourceCocyclesTests.value`: For every compatible `φ,c,h`, `res_φ(c)(h)=c(φ(h))`.
- `sourceCocyclesTests.identity`: For every cocycle c, restriction along `id_G` sends c to c.
- `sourceCocyclesTests.constantSource`: If H acts through the constant-one source homomorphism `H→G`, then `res_1(c)` is the neutral cocycle for every c.
- `sourceCocyclesTests.subgroup`: For every `N≤G`, general restriction along N.subtype agrees with the subgroup cocycle restriction on every c.
- No local unramified/crystalline condition, geometric torsor comparison or representability result follows from this abstract topological calculation.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §4, restriction paragraph, p. 127.

- <a id="nc-3-source-h1-surjective-injection"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.res_injective` (*Surjective sources detect cohomology classes*): Let G,H,K be groups with topologies, U a group with a topology and actions by automorphisms, `φ:H→G` a continuous homomorphism, and `h·u=φ(h)·u`. Write `res_φ` for precomposition on continuous cocycles. For `H¹`, require U to be a topological group and the actions jointly continuous; `H¹` is the gauge-orbit pointed set, not a group. If `φ` is surjective, `res_φ` is injective on `H¹(G,U)`. *Proof.* Choose representative cocycles. Equality after restriction gives a gauge witness `x∈U`. Gauge compatibility and surjective-source injectivity on cocycles give `x·c=d` before restriction. Uses [Restriction on a cocycle class](#nc-3-source-h1-representative); [Surjective sources detect cocycles](#nc-3-source-cocycle-surjective-injection).
- <a id="nc-3-source-h1-subgroup"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.res_subgroup` (*Agreement with subgroup cohomology restriction*): Let G,H,K be groups with topologies, U a group with a topology and actions by automorphisms, `φ:H→G` a continuous homomorphism, and `h·u=φ(h)·u`. Write `res_φ` for precomposition on continuous cocycles. For `H¹`, require U to be a topological group and the actions jointly continuous; `H¹` is the gauge-orbit pointed set, not a group. For every `subgroup N≤G`, res along N.subtype equals the H1.restrict N, with induced topology and action. *Proof.* Reduce to a cocycle representative; both quotient maps use the same restricted cocycle. Uses [Restriction on a cocycle class](#nc-3-source-h1-representative); [Agreement with subgroup cocycle restriction](#nc-3-source-cocycle-subgroup); [Restriction of nonabelian cohomology classes](#nc-3-h1-restriction).
- <a id="nc-3-source-coefficient-h1-square"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.res_map` (*The source and coefficient square on cohomology*): Let G,H,K be groups with topologies, U a group with a topology and actions by automorphisms, `φ:H→G` a continuous homomorphism, and `h·u=φ(h)·u`. Write `res_φ` for precomposition on continuous cocycles. For `H¹`, require U to be a topological group and the actions jointly continuous; `H¹` is the gauge-orbit pointed set, not a group. For a continuous G-equivariant `f:U→V` between topological groups with jointly continuous compatible actions, `res_φ∘map_f=map_f∘res_φ` on `H¹`. *Proof.* Choose a cocycle representative and use the commuting cocycle square; quotient lifting preserves equality. Uses [Restriction on a cocycle class](#nc-3-source-h1-representative); [Coefficient change commutes with source restriction](#nc-3-source-coefficient-cocycle-square); [Coefficient map on nonabelian cohomology](#nc-3-coefficient-h1-map).

**Checks.**

- `sourceClassesTests.one`: For every compatible continuous `φ`, H1.res `φ` sends the neutral class to the neutral class.
- `sourceClassesTests.gauge`: For every `x∈U` and `c∈Z¹(G,U)`, `res_φ([x·c])=[res_φ(c)]`.
- `sourceClassesTests.subgroup`: For every `N≤G` and `a∈H¹(G,U)`, general restriction along N.subtype equals the H1.restrict N a.
- `sourceClassesTests.surjectiveReflection`: If `φ:H→G` is surjective, then `res_φ(a)=1` iff `a=1`.
- `sourceClassesTests.noninjective`: Let `G=S₂` and `U=S₃` be discrete with trivial action, and c send the nonidentity permutation to (01). Its class is nonneutral, but restriction along the constant-one homomorphism `G→G` sends it to the neutral class. General source restriction is not asserted injective.
- `sourceClassesTests.nativePullbackAction`: For every continuous `φ:H→G`, using MulDistribMulAction.compHom and `MulAction.continuousSMul_compHom` to pull back a jointly continuous G-action, H1.res `φ` sends the neutral class to neutral.
- No local unramified/crystalline condition, geometric torsor comparison or representability result follows from this abstract topological calculation.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §4, restriction paragraph, p. 127.

<a id="nc-3-source-invariant-restriction"></a>

**Restriction of invariant subgroups.** For `H⁰`, only groups and automorphism actions are needed, with `h·u=φ(h)·u`; no topology or continuity is required. Construct the homomorphism `res_φ:U^G→U^H` sending an invariant element to the same element of U.

Standing hypotheses (H5).

The G-fixed element is fixed by `φ(h)`, hence by h. Multiplication and identity are inherited from the common ambient group.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-source-invariant-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H0.res_apply` (*Underlying invariant restriction*): For `H⁰`, only groups and automorphism actions are needed, with `h·u=φ(h)·u`; no topology or continuity is required. The underlying U-element of `res_φ(x)` is x. *Proof.* Unfold the inclusion between fixed subgroups.
- <a id="nc-3-source-invariant-identity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H0.res_id` (*Identity restriction of invariants*): For `H⁰`, only groups and automorphism actions are needed, with `h·u=φ(h)·u`; no topology or continuity is required. Restriction along `id_G` is the identity homomorphism of `U^G`. *Proof.* The underlying function is identity, and proof fields agree by proof irrelevance.
- <a id="nc-3-source-invariant-composition"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H0.res_comp` (*Composition of invariant restrictions*): For `H⁰`, only groups and automorphism actions are needed, with `h·u=φ(h)·u`; no topology or continuity is required. For `ψ:K→H` with compatible action, `res_(φ∘ψ)=res_ψ∘res_φ` as group homomorphisms. *Proof.* Both homomorphisms preserve the underlying element of U.
- <a id="nc-3-source-invariant-injection"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H0.res_injective` (*Invariant restriction is injective*): For `H⁰`, only groups and automorphism actions are needed, with `h·u=φ(h)·u`; no topology or continuity is required. The map `res_φ:U^G→U^H` is injective for every `φ`, without a surjectivity hypothesis. *Proof.* Take underlying U-values of an equality and apply subtype extensionality. Uses [Underlying invariant restriction](#nc-3-source-invariant-value).
- <a id="nc-3-source-coefficient-invariant-square"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H0.res_map` (*The source and coefficient square on invariants*): For `H⁰`, only groups and automorphism actions are needed, with `h·u=φ(h)·u`; no topology or continuity is required. For G-equivariant `f:U→V` and compatible H-actions, `res_φ∘map_f=map_f∘res_φ` as group homomorphisms between fixed subgroups. *Proof.* Both homomorphisms send x to `f(x)`; H-equivariance follows by rewriting the compatible actions. Uses [Coefficient homomorphism on invariant groups](#nc-3-coefficient-invariant-map).

**Checks.**

- `sourceInvariantsTests.one`: For every compatible `φ`, invariant restriction sends 1 to 1.
- `sourceInvariantsTests.identity`: For every `x∈U^G`, restriction along `id_G` returns x.
- `sourceInvariantsTests.value`: For every compatible `φ` and `x∈U^G`, the underlying U-element of `res_φ(x)` is exactly x.
- No local unramified/crystalline condition, geometric torsor comparison or representability result follows from this abstract topological calculation.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §4, restriction paragraph, p. 127.

### 0.6 Restriction of cocycles

Use native `Cocycle.map` along subgroup inclusion for the displayed cocycle restriction.

<a id="nc-3-cocycle-restriction"></a>

**Restriction of continuous nonabelian cocycles.** Use native `Cocycle.map` for `res_N:Z¹(G,U)→Z¹(N,U)` by `res_N(c)(n)=c(n)`, using the subgroup inclusion and restricted action. This keeps continuity and the ordered cocycle law.

G is a group endowed with a topology; U is a group endowed with a topology and G acts on U by group automorphisms. N is an arbitrary subgroup with its subtype topology and restricted action.

Compose the continuous cocycle with subgroup inclusion. The inherited automorphism action on N evaluates through that inclusion; the ordered cocycle law specializes to `n,m∈N`.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.restrict_apply`: For `n∈N`, `res_N(c)(n)=c(n)` through subgroup inclusion.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.restrict_one`: Restriction sends the identity cocycle to the identity cocycle.
- <a id="nc-3-cocycle-restriction-equivariance"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.restrict_smul` (*Gauge equivariance of cocycle restriction*): For `x∈U` and `c∈Z¹(G,U)`, `res_N(x·c)=x·res_N(c)`. The gauge element belongs to all U, not necessarily `U^N`. Under (H4). *Proof.* Restricted scalar multiplication evaluates through subgroup inclusion. Both cocycle values are `x c(n)(n•x)⁻¹`; equality is definitional. Uses [Nonabelian first cohomology as a pointed set](#nc-3-nonabelian-h1).

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.restrict.test_one`: Restriction of the identity cocycle to any subgroup is the identity cocycle.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.restrict.test_subgroup_value`: At any subgroup element n, restriction evaluates to the original `c(n)`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.restrict.test_bottom`: Every cocycle restricts to the identity cocycle on `N={1}`.
- Restriction is genuine evaluation on the subgroup, not a constant cocycle. The bottom subgroup sees only `c(1)=1`.
- A non-N-fixed witness is allowed; imposing fixedness here would change restriction on classes.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed pp. 5–6, continuous cocycle and gauge definitions; authored inflation–restriction deduction.

Use [Continuous 1-cocycles and invariants with nonabelian coefficients](#nc-3-continuous-cocycles); `continuous_subtype_val`; `Continuous.comp`.

### 0.7 Restriction of classes and neutral classes

The supplied class map is `TauCeti.NonabelianH1.res`; use its `res_mk` and `res_one` formulas.

<a id="nc-3-h1-restriction"></a>

**Restriction of nonabelian cohomology classes.** Use native `res` for the pointed-set map `res_N:H¹(G,U)→H¹(N,U)` sending [c] to `[res_N(c)]`. It uses the gauge-orbit quotients and the whole U-gauge action on both sides.

Standing hypotheses (H4).

Lift `c↦[res_N(c)]` through the genuine orbit quotient. Its relation `c=x·d` and restriction equivariance give `[res_N(c)]=[x·res_N(d)]=[res_N(d)]`. Representative evaluation is the quotient-lift computation. Identity-cocycle restriction proves basepoint preservation.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.restrict_mk`: Restriction of [c] is the class of `res_N(c)`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.restrict_one`: Restriction preserves the distinguished point.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.restrict_mk_eq_one_iff`: For a representing cocycle c, `res_N([c])=1` if and only if there is `x∈U` with `c(n)=x(n•x)⁻¹` for every `n∈N`.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.restrict.test_one`: Restriction of the distinguished class to any subgroup is distinguished.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.restrict.test_gauge`: For `x∈U`, restricting `[x·c]` gives the same class as restricting [c].
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.restrict.test_bottom`: Every `H¹` class restricts to the distinguished point on `N={1}`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.restrict.test_top_detects`: For `N=G`, `res_N(a)=1` if and only if `a=1`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.restrict.test_neutral_not_pointwise`: For discrete `U=S₃` and G=ConjAct(U), `x=(01)(12)`, `c=x·1` and `N=G`, `res_N([c])=1` while the restricted cocycle `res_N(c)≠1`. Neutrality cannot be tested by literal triviality of a chosen representative.
- Restricting to the top subgroup detects the neutral class. A neutral restricted class can have a nonidentity restricted representing cocycle.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed pp. 5–6, continuous cocycle and gauge definitions; authored inflation–restriction deduction.

### 0.8 Twisting by a cocycle
<a id="nc-3-twisting"></a>

**Twisting by a cocycle.** Let `c ∈ Z¹(G, U)`. The twisted group ₍c₎U is U with the action `g ⋆ u := c(g)·(g•u)·c(g)⁻¹`, again a continuous action by automorphisms. The map `τ_c : Z¹(G, ₍c₎U) → Z¹(G, U)`, `c′ ↦ (g ↦ c′(g)·c(g))`, is a bijection carrying the trivial cocycle to c and the twisted-conjugation action of U on the left to that on the right; it induces a bijection of underlying sets `H¹(G, ₍c₎U) ≅ H¹(G, U)` sending the source base point to [c]; it becomes a pointed equivalence only when the target is repointed at [c]. Twisting is compatible with G-stable subgroups (for cocycles with values in them) and with quotients by normal ones, so that fibres of the maps in [Kernel of inclusion in nonabelian cohomology](#nc-3-exact-sequence) over [c] become fibres over the base point after twisting. The equation-level calculation identifies the twisted cocycle equation for d with the original equation for `g↦d(g)c(g)`, without constructing a second cocycle carrier.

G is a topological group and U a topological group with an action of G by group automorphisms (MulDistribMulAction G U) such that the action map `G × U → U` is continuous (ContinuousSMul G U). c a continuous cocycle.

`g ⋆ −` is an automorphism of U (conjugation composed with the automorphism `g•−`), and `(gh) ⋆ u = c(gh)(gh•u)c(gh)⁻¹ = c(g) g•c(h) g•(h•u) g•c(h)⁻¹ c(g)⁻¹ = g ⋆ (h ⋆ u)` by the cocycle identity; continuity from continuity of c and of the action. `τ_c(c′)` is a cocycle for `U: c′(gh)c(gh) = c′(g)·(g ⋆ c′(h))·c(g)·g•c(h) = c′(g)c(g)·g•(c′(h)c(h))`. The inverse is `c″ ↦ c″·c⁻¹`. For `u ∈ U`, `τ_c(u·c′)(g) = u c′(g)(g ⋆ u)⁻¹ c(g) = u c′(g) c(g) (g•u)⁻¹ = (u·τ_c(c′))(g)`. Hence the bijection of orbit sets; the trivial cocycle maps to c. Compatibility with subgroups and quotients: twisting by a cocycle with values in a G-stable subgroup A preserves A; if A is normal every twist preserves A, and the quotient map `U → U/A` is equivariant for the twists by c and by its image.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist`: The type synonym ₍c₎U of U with the twisted action `g ⋆ u = c(g)(g•u)c(g)⁻¹`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.smul_def`: `g ⋆ u = c(g)·(g•u)·c(g)⁻¹`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.continuousSMul`: The twisted action is continuous.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.twistEquiv`: The bijection `Z¹(G, ₍c₎U) ≃ Z¹(G, U)`, `c′ ↦ c′·c`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistEquiv`: The induced bijection `H¹(G, ₍c₎U) ≃ H¹(G, U)`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistEquiv_one`: twistEquiv sends the base point to the class of c.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.self`: Twisting by the trivial cocycle is the original action.
- <a id="nc-3-twist-underlying-group"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.toOriginal` (*Underlying group of a cocycle twist*): The underlying group identification `j_c:Twist(c)≃*U` is MulEquiv.refl U. It preserves multiplication and the original topology, but need not preserve the original G-action. Under (H6). *Proof.* Use the inherited underlying group and topology instances on the type synonym. Specialize MulEquiv.refl; its two inverse identities and multiplicativity are the ones, not stored comparison oracles. The action remains twisted. Source: [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1 continuous cocycle/gauge definitions and Proposition 1 proof, pp. 5–7.
- <a id="nc-3-twist-invariant-criterion"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.mem_fixed_iff` (*Invariants of the twisted action*): For `x∈Twist(c)`, x belongs to `H⁰(G,Twist(c))` if and only if `c(g)·g(j_c(x))=j_c(x)·c(g)` for every `g∈G`. Under (H6). *Proof.* Apply the underlying group identification to the fixed-point equality `g⋆x=x`. Multiply on the right by `c(g)` to obtain the stated commutation equation; conversely divide by `c(g)` and use the equivalence injectivity. Source: [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1 continuous cocycle/gauge definitions and Proposition 1 proof, pp. 5–7. Uses [Underlying group of a cocycle twist](#nc-3-twist-underlying-group).
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.toOriginal_apply`: For every `x∈Twist(c)`, `j_c(x)` is exactly x regarded in U. This is the identity equivalence on the underlying group, not an unspecified automorphism.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.twist_trivial`: Twisting by the trivial cocycle gives back U with its action, and twistEquiv is the identity.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.twist_abelian`: For U commutative, `g ⋆ u = g•u` for every c, and twistEquiv is translation by c.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.twist_S3`: For `G = ℤ/2` acting trivially on `S₃` and c sending the generator to a transposition `τ`, the twisted action is conjugation by `τ`, whose invariants form the `subgroup {1, τ}` of order 2.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.twist_changes_invariants`: A twist need not be isomorphic to U as a G-group: for `G = ℤ/2` acting trivially on `S₃` and `c(σ) = τ` a transposition, `H⁰(G, ₍c₎S₃) = {1, τ}` has order 2 while `H⁰(G, S₃) = S₃` has order 6; and twistEquiv sends the base point to [c], not to the base point.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.twist_commutative_action`: If the original multiplication on U commutes, the twisted action `g⋆x` agrees with the original action `g(x)`, for every c.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.twist_transposition_invariants`: For the same discrete `S₂→S₃` transposition cocycle with trivial original action, `x∈H⁰(G,Twist(c))` if and only if `x=1` or `x=τ`. The twisted action has exactly these two invariants, whereas the original trivial action fixes all six elements.
- For trivial action and U commutative, twisting by any c does not change the action, and `τ_c` is translation by c.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, proof of Proposition 1, p. 6; [Bjorn Poonen](#reference-poonen-rational-points), §4.5, p. 105.

Use [Nonabelian first cohomology as a pointed set](#nc-3-nonabelian-h1); [Continuous 1-cocycles and invariants with nonabelian coefficients](#nc-3-continuous-cocycles); `MulAut.conj`; `MulDistribMulAction.toMulAut`.

### 0.9 Inner twists: source comparison, pullback and the twisting equivalence
<a id="nc-3-twisted-source-equivalence"></a>

**Source comparison of inner twists.** Construct `e_φ,c:Twist(c)≃*Twist(res_φ c)` as `j_(res_φ c)⁻¹∘j_c`. The underlying topological groups coincide; the following semiequivariance lemma compares their source actions.

Standing hypotheses (H7).

Compose the group identifications, using the inverse in the target direction.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-twisted-source-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.sourceEquiv_apply` (*Value of the source comparison*): For `x∈Twist(c)`, `j_(res_φ c)(e_φ,c(x))=j_c(x)`. *Proof.* Unfold the composed equivalence.
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-source-inverse-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.sourceEquiv_symm_apply` (*Inverse source comparison*): For `y∈Twist(res_φ c)`, `j_c(e_φ,c⁻¹(y))=j_(res_φ c)(y)`. *Proof.* Unfold the inverse equivalence.
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-source-continuity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.sourceEquiv_continuous` (*Continuity of source comparison*): The function underlying `e_φ,c` is continuous for the topologies. *Proof.* Under `j_c` and `j_(res_φ c)` the function is the identity on U; use continuity of the identity. Uses [Value of the source comparison](#nc-3-twisted-source-value).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-source-inverse-continuity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.sourceEquiv_symm_continuous` (*Continuity of inverse source comparison*): The inverse function `e_φ,c⁻¹` is continuous. Thus the group equivalence is also a homeomorphism. *Proof.* The inverse is the same identity map on the inherited topology. Uses [Inverse source comparison](#nc-3-twisted-source-inverse-value).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-source-semilinearity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.sourceEquiv_smul` (*Source semiequivariance of inner twists*): For `h∈H` and `x∈Twist(c)`, `e_φ,c(φ(h)⋆_c x)=h⋆_(res_φ c)e_φ,c(x)`, using the G and H inner actions. *Proof.* Apply `j_(res_φ c)` injectively. Both sides contain the same `c(φ(h))` and its inverse; replace `h•j_c(x)` by `φ(h)•j_c(x)` using the explicit action compatibility. Uses [Value of the source comparison](#nc-3-twisted-source-value); [Twisting by a cocycle](#nc-3-twisting); [Values of source restriction](#nc-3-source-cocycle-value).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-source-gauge-square"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.sourceEquiv_gauge` (*Source comparison and gauge conjugation*): For `b∈U` and `x∈Twist(c)`, `j_(res_φ(b•c))(e_φ,b•c(e_c,b(x)))=j_(b•res_φ c)(e_(res_φ c),b(e_φ,c(x)))`. Ordinary restriction identifies `res_φ(b•c)=b•res_φ c`; the equality is stated under the underlying identifications to retain the exact dependent targets. *Proof.* Both sides are `b j_c(x)b⁻¹`. Use the identification formulas and the ordinary cocycle restriction/gauge identity. Uses [Value of the source comparison](#nc-3-twisted-source-value); [Gauge transport value](#nc-3-gauge-value); [Gauge compatibility of source restriction](#nc-3-source-cocycle-gauge).

**Checks.**

- `Twist.sourceEquiv.test_inverse`: For every `φ,c,x`, the inverse of `e_φ,c` applied to `e_φ,c(x)` is x.
- `Twist.sourceEquiv.test_semilinear`: For `h∈H` and `x∈Twist(c)`, `j_(res_φ c)(h⋆e_φ,c(x))=c(φ(h))(φ(h)•j_c(x))c(φ(h))⁻¹`.
- `Twist.sourceEquiv.test_noncommutative_action`: Give `S₂` and `S₃` discrete topologies and the trivial original S₂-action on `S₃`; let c(nonidentity)=(01), `φ=id`, `g=(01)∈S₂` and `x=(12)∈Twist(c)`. Then `j_(res_id c)(e_id,c(g⋆x))=(02)`, which differs from `j_c(x)=(12)`. This rejects reuse of the raw trivial action on the inner twist.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, cocycle and gauge definitions and Proposition 1 proof, printed pp. 5–7; representative-change sentence on p. 7.
