- <a id="nc-3-twisted-source-cocycle-neutral"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.twistRes_one` (*Neutral twisted cocycle pullback*): `R¹_φ,c` sends the constant one cocycle to the constant one cocycle. *Proof.* Use cocycle extensionality and multiplicativity of the equivalence at one. Uses [Value of twisted cocycle pullback](#nc-3-twisted-source-cocycle-value).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-source-cocycle-gauge"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.twistRes_smul` (*Gauge compatibility of twisted pullback*): For `x∈Twist(c)` and `z∈Z¹(G,Twist(c))`, `R¹_φ,c(x•z)=e_φ,c(x)•R¹_φ,c(z)`. This uses the gauge actions for their distinct inner source actions. *Proof.* Evaluate at h. Expand the ordered gauge formula, preserve products/inverses with `e_φ,c`, and use its semiequivariance. Uses [Value of twisted cocycle pullback](#nc-3-twisted-source-cocycle-value); [Nonabelian first cohomology as a pointed set](#nc-3-nonabelian-h1).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-source-cocycle-square"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.twistRes_translation` (*Twisting and source restriction square*): For `z∈Z¹(G,Twist(c))`, `τ_(res_φ c)(R¹_φ,c(z))=res_φ(τ_c(z))` as continuous cocycles. *Proof.* Evaluate at h. The left side is `j_c(z(φ(h)))c(φ(h))`; this is the right side by ordinary restriction and the inherited translation formula. Uses [Value of twisted cocycle pullback](#nc-3-twisted-source-cocycle-value); [Value of the source comparison](#nc-3-twisted-source-value); [Continuous cocycles under inner twisting](#nc-3-twist-cocycle-equivalence); [Values of source restriction](#nc-3-source-cocycle-value).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-source-cocycle-injection"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.twistRes_injective` (*Surjective source maps detect twisted cocycles*): If `φ` is surjective as a function, then `R¹_φ,c` is injective. Neither continuity nor group-homomorphism structure alone implies this conclusion. *Proof.* Translate both inputs by `τ_c`, apply ordinary source restriction injectivity, and use the proved cocycle translation square and injectivity of `τ_c`. Uses [Twisting and source restriction square](#nc-3-twisted-source-cocycle-square); [Surjective sources detect cocycles](#nc-3-source-cocycle-surjective-injection); [Continuous cocycles under inner twisting](#nc-3-twist-cocycle-equivalence).

**Checks.**

- `Z1.twistRes.test_identity`: For `φ=id` and every twisted cocycle z and g, `j_(res_id c)(R¹_id,c(z)(g))=j_c(z(g))`.
- `Z1.twistRes.test_gauge_translation`: For `x∈Twist(c)` and z a twisted cocycle, `τ_(res_φ c)(R¹_φ,c(x•z))=j_c(x)•res_φ(τ_c(z))`.
- `Z1.twistRes.test_surjective_detection`: For surjective `φ`, `R¹_φ,c(z)=1` iff `z=1`; the cocycle pullback detects the neutral cocycle.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, cocycle and gauge definitions and Proposition 1 proof, printed pp. 5–7; representative-change sentence on p. 7.

Use [Source comparison of inner twists](#nc-3-twisted-source-equivalence); [Continuity of source comparison](#nc-3-twisted-source-continuity); [Source semiequivariance of inner twists](#nc-3-twisted-source-semilinearity); [Continuous 1-cocycles and invariants with nonabelian coefficients](#nc-3-continuous-cocycles); `Continuous.comp`; `map_mul`.

<a id="nc-3-twisted-source-h1-map"></a>

**Source restriction on twisted orbit sets.** Construct `R_φ,c:H¹(G,Twist(c))→H¹(H,Twist(res_φ c))` by `[z]↦[R¹_φ,c(z)]` on the gauge-orbit quotient.

Standing hypotheses (H7).

Lift the directly constructed cocycle pullback to the quotient. A gauge witness x maps to the witness `e_φ,c(x)`, by cocycle gauge compatibility.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-twisted-source-h1-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistRes_mk` (*Representative of twisted H¹ restriction*): For every twisted cocycle z, `R_φ,c([z])=[R¹_φ,c(z)]`. *Proof.* Unfold the quotient lift.
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-source-h1-neutral"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistRes_one` (*Pointedness of twisted source restriction*): `R_φ,c(1)=1` in `H¹(H,Twist(res_φ c))`. The target neutral point is in the twisted target, while `T_(res_φ c)(1)=[res_φ c]` in the original coefficient `H¹`. *Proof.* Use the representative formula and the neutral cocycle pullback. Uses [Representative of twisted `H¹` restriction](#nc-3-twisted-source-h1-value); [Neutral twisted cocycle pullback](#nc-3-twisted-source-cocycle-neutral).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-source-h1-square"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistRes_translation` (*Source naturality of the twisting equivalence*): For every `a∈H¹(G,Twist(c))`, `T_(res_φ c)(R_φ,c(a))=res_φ(T_c(a))` in the original `H¹(H,U)`. This square is proved for the direct quotient lift, not inserted into its definition. *Proof.* Choose a cocycle representative of a; use quotient evaluation and the cocycle translation square. Uses [Representative of twisted `H¹` restriction](#nc-3-twisted-source-h1-value); [Twisting and source restriction square](#nc-3-twisted-source-cocycle-square); [Gauge-orbit bijection under twisting](#nc-3-twist-h1-equivalence); [Restriction on a cocycle class](#nc-3-source-h1-representative).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-source-h1-injection"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistRes_injective` (*Surjective source maps detect twisted classes*): If `φ` is surjective as a function, then `R_φ,c` is injective on the `H¹` orbit sets. In particular it reflects their neutral classes. *Proof.* Compare after `T_c`; ordinary `H¹` restriction is injective for a surjective `φ`. Apply the translation square and cancel `T_c`. Uses [Source naturality of the twisting equivalence](#nc-3-twisted-source-h1-square); [Surjective sources detect cohomology classes](#nc-3-source-h1-surjective-injection); [Gauge-orbit bijection under twisting](#nc-3-twist-h1-equivalence).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-source-representative-square"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistRes_representative` (*Source naturality of representative comparison*): If `[c]=[d]`, then `R_φ,d∘C_c,d=C_(res_φ c),(res_φ d)∘R_φ,c`. The target class equality is `res_φ([c])=res_φ([d])`; no gauge witness or canonical coefficient-group isomorphism is chosen. *Proof.* Apply injectivity of `T_(res_φ d)`. The representative square and the two source translation squares identify both sides with `res_φ(T_c(a))`. Uses [Source naturality of the twisting equivalence](#nc-3-twisted-source-h1-square); [Common translation of representative comparisons](#nc-3-representative-square); [Restriction on a cocycle class](#nc-3-source-h1-representative).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-source-identity-square"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistRes_identity_translation` (*Identity law under twisting translation*): For the identity source map on G, `T_(res_id c)(R_id,c(a))=T_c(a)`. This states the identity law with the dependent twist targets visible; no arbitrary identification of actions is suppressed. *Proof.* Use the source translation square and the ordinary `H¹` identity law. Uses [Source naturality of the twisting equivalence](#nc-3-twisted-source-h1-square); [Identity restriction on cohomology](#nc-3-source-h1-identity).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-source-composition-square"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistRes_comp_translation` (*Composition law under twisting translation*): For `ψ:K→*H` and `φ:H→*G` with continuous maps and compatible K,H,G actions, `T_(res_ψ(res_φ c))(R_ψ,res_φ c(R_φ,c(a)))=res_(φ∘ψ)(T_c(a))`. The composite compatibility is `k•x=ψ(k)•x=φ(ψ(k))•x`. Applying the one-step square to `φ∘ψ` gives the same translated value; comparisons of dependent twist targets are explicit. *Proof.* Apply the two source translation squares successively, then the ordinary `H¹` source composition law. Uses [Source naturality of the twisting equivalence](#nc-3-twisted-source-h1-square); [Contravariant composition on cohomology](#nc-3-source-h1-composition).

**Checks.**

- `H1.twistRes.test_neutral`: `T_(res_φ c)(R_φ,c(1))=[res_φ c]`, retaining the repointed target; this value need not be neutral in the original coefficient `H¹`.
- `H1.twistRes.test_gauge_classes`: For `x∈Twist(c)` and a cocycle z, `R_φ,c([x•z])=R_φ,c([z])` on the gauge-orbit quotient.
- `H1.twistRes.test_surjective_reflection`: For surjective `φ`, `R_φ,c(a)=1` iff `a=1` on the twisted `H¹` orbit sets.
- `H1.twistRes.test_nonsurjective_loss`: If `φ(h)=1` for every h and `[c]≠1` in the original `H¹`, then `a=T_c⁻¹(1)` is nonneutral but `R_φ,c(a)=1`. The discrete `S₂→S₃` cocycle supplies a consistent nonneutral c, with trivial original actions and the constant homomorphism. This rejects injectivity or neutral reflection without surjectivity.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, cocycle and gauge definitions and Proposition 1 proof, printed pp. 5–7; representative-change sentence on p. 7.

Use [Pullback of twisted cocycles](#nc-3-twisted-source-cocycle-map); [Gauge compatibility of twisted pullback](#nc-3-twisted-source-cocycle-gauge); [Nonabelian first cohomology as a pointed set](#nc-3-nonabelian-h1); [Gauge invariance of the cohomology class](#nc-3-h1-gauge-class); `MulAction.orbitRel_apply`.

<a id="nc-3-twist-cocycle-equivalence"></a>

**Continuous cocycles under inner twisting.** Construct `τ_c:Z¹(G,Twist(c))≃Z¹(G,U)` with `τ_c(d)(g)=j_c(d(g))·c(g)`, and inverse `e(g)·c(g)⁻¹` viewed in `Twist(c)`. Both maps return continuous cocycles.

Standing hypotheses (H6).

The constructed twisted action obeys its unit/product/automorphism laws by the cocycle equation; joint continuity follows from c and the ambient action. Multiply the twisted cocycle equation by `c(gh)` on the right; cancel the adjacent `c(g)` inverse to get the original cocycle equation in exactly the stated order. The inverse divides on the right by `c(g)`, with continuity from inversion and multiplication; cancellation gives both inverse identities.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-twist-cocycle-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.twistEquiv_apply` (*Value of the twisting equivalence*): For every `d∈Z¹(G,Twist(c))` and `g∈G`, `τ_c(d)(g)=j_c(d(g))·c(g)`. *Proof.* Evaluate the forward cocycle construction. This fixes the multiplication order in a noncommutative group.
- <a id="nc-3-twist-cocycle-inverse-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.twistEquiv_symm_apply` (*Value of the inverse twisting equivalence*): For every `e∈Z¹(G,U)` and `g∈G`, `τ_c⁻¹(e)(g)` is `e(g)·c(g)⁻¹`, viewed in `Twist(c)`. *Proof.* Evaluate the inverse cocycle construction; its inverse is on the right.
- <a id="nc-3-twist-gauge-equivariance"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.twistEquiv_smul` (*Gauge compatibility of inner twisting*): For every `x∈Twist(c)` and `d∈Z¹(G,Twist(c))`, `τ_c(x·d)=j_c(x)·τ_c(d)`. The same underlying gauge witness is used on both sides. *Proof.* Expand the twisted and original ordered gauge actions. Use `g⋆x=c(g) g(j_c(x)) c(g)⁻¹` and cancel in U. Both sides equal `j_c(x) j_c(d(g)) c(g) g(j_c(x))⁻¹`. Uses [Value of the twisting equivalence](#nc-3-twist-cocycle-value); [Nonabelian first cohomology as a pointed set](#nc-3-nonabelian-h1).

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.twist_unit_value`: For every c and g, `τ_c(1)(g)=c(g)`; the source neutral cocycle becomes the chosen cocycle.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.twist_untwist`: For every original continuous cocycle e, `τ_c(τ_c⁻¹(e))=e` as cocycles, with no new representative choice.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.twist_translation_order`: For every twisted continuous cocycle d and g, `τ_c⁻¹(τ_c(d))(g)=d(g)`. Division on the right exactly cancels multiplication on the right.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.twist_right_translation_S3`: Take discrete `G=U=S₃` with trivial original action, the identity cocycle c, `x=(01)` in `Twist(c)`, the twisted coboundary `d(g)=x·(g⋆x)⁻¹`, and `g=(12)`. The forward cocycle equivalence satisfies `τ_c(d)(g)=xgx⁻¹`, and this value differs from `c(g)·j_c(d(g))`. Thus swapping the forward multiplication order fails on a twisted cocycle.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1 continuous cocycle/gauge definitions and Proposition 1 proof, pp. 5–7.

Use [Twisting by a cocycle](#nc-3-twisting); [Underlying group of a cocycle twist](#nc-3-twist-underlying-group); [Continuous 1-cocycles and invariants with nonabelian coefficients](#nc-3-continuous-cocycles).

<a id="nc-3-twist-h1-equivalence"></a>

**Gauge-orbit bijection under twisting.** Construct the quotient equivalence `H¹(G,Twist(c))≃H¹(G,U)` induced by `τ_c`. It is a bijection of underlying sets; it carries the source neutral point to [c].

Standing hypotheses (H6).

Prove equivalence of the two orbit relations using exactly the same underlying gauge witness and the proved cocycle equivariance. For the reverse implication apply `τ_c` injectivity to the witness equation. Use Quotient.congr to construct the quotient equivalence with both inverse identities. The trivial twisted cocycle maps pointwise to c, hence its gauge class maps to [c].

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-twist-h1-representative"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistEquiv_mk` (*Twisting on a H¹ representative*): For every `d∈Z¹(G,Twist(c))`, `H¹.twistEquiv(c)([d])=[τ_c(d)]`. *Proof.* Evaluate the quotient congruence on a representative.
- <a id="nc-3-twist-h1-neutral-fibre"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistEquiv_eq_class_iff` (*Neutral source fibre under twisting*): For every `a∈H¹(G,Twist(c))`, H¹.twistEquiv(c)(a)=[c] if and only if `a=1`. *Proof.* The constructed orbit equivalence maps 1 to [c]. Apply its injectivity to compare a with 1. This does not say the equivalence preserves the original target neutral point.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistEquiv_one`: The quotient equivalence sends the source neutral class to the class [c].

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.twist_neutral_fibre`: The inverse orbit equivalence sends [c] to the source neutral class.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.twist_class_representative`: For every twisted cocycle d, the quotient equivalence applied to [d] is the class of the cocycle `τ_c(d)`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.twist_not_neutral`: Take discrete `G=S₂` acting trivially on `U=S₃` and `c(g)=1` for `g=1`, otherwise the transposition `τ=(01)`. Then H¹.twistEquiv(c)(1)≠1. A bijection claimed to preserve the original target neutral point fails this example.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1 continuous cocycle/gauge definitions and Proposition 1 proof, pp. 5–7.

Use [Continuous cocycles under inner twisting](#nc-3-twist-cocycle-equivalence); [Gauge compatibility of inner twisting](#nc-3-twist-gauge-equivariance); [Nonabelian first cohomology as a pointed set](#nc-3-nonabelian-h1); `Quotient.congr`; `MulAction.orbitRel_apply`.

<a id="nc-3-representative-equivalence"></a>

**Canonical comparison for cohomologous representatives.** For `c,d∈Z¹(G,U)` with `h:[c]=[d]`, construct `C_c,d:H¹(G,Twist(c))≃H¹(G,Twist(d))` by `T_d⁻¹∘T_c`. The formula makes no choice of a gauge witness; its pointedness is proved separately using h.

Standing hypotheses (H8).

Compose the inherited orbit-set equivalences `T_c` and `T_d⁻¹` using Equiv composition. The original class equality is retained as an input to the comparison API.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-representative-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.changeRepresentative_apply` (*Representative comparison value*): For `h:[c]=[d]` and `a∈H¹(G,Twist(c))`, `C_c,d(a)=T_d⁻¹(T_c(a))`. *Proof.* Evaluate the composite equivalence.
- <a id="nc-3-representative-neutral"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.changeRepresentative_one` (*Neutral class under representative comparison*): For `h:[c]=[d]`, `C_c,d(1)=1`. Equality of the original classes is essential; the raw composite for arbitrary unrelated cocycles need not be pointed. *Proof.* Apply injectivity of `T_d`; its value on the left is `T_c(1)=[c]` and its value on the right is [d]. Use h. Uses [Representative comparison value](#nc-3-representative-value).
- <a id="nc-3-representative-gauge"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.changeRepresentative_gauge` (*Representative comparison equals gauge pushforward*): For `b∈U` and `h:[c]=[b•c]` supplied by the gauge-class lemma, `C_c,b•c` equals the `H¹` pushforward induced by `e_c,b`, as a function on `H¹(G,Twist(c))`. *Proof.* Apply injectivity of `T_(b•c)` to each argument. Both sides become `T_c(a)`, by cancellation of inverse equivalences and the proved `H¹` gauge square. Uses [Representative comparison value](#nc-3-representative-value); [Cohomology translation under gauge transport](#nc-3-gauge-h1-square); [Gauge invariance of the cohomology class](#nc-3-h1-gauge-class).
- <a id="nc-3-representative-identity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.changeRepresentative_id` (*Identity representative comparison*): `C_c,c` is the identity equivalence of `H¹(G,Twist(c))`. *Proof.* Use equivalence extensionality and cancel `T_c⁻¹` after `T_c at` each point. Uses [Representative comparison value](#nc-3-representative-value).
- <a id="nc-3-representative-composition"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.changeRepresentative_comp` (*Composition of representative comparisons*): Given `h_cd:[c]=[d]` and `h_de:[d]=[e]`, composing `C_c,d` followed by `C_d,e` equals `C_c,e` for `h_cd.trans(h_de)`, as equivalences. *Proof.* Expand the composites at an arbitrary class and cancel the adjacent `T_d∘T_d⁻¹`. No gauge representatives or group multiplication choices enter. Uses [Representative comparison value](#nc-3-representative-value).
- <a id="nc-3-representative-inverse"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.changeRepresentative_symm` (*Inverse representative comparison*): For `h:[c]=[d]`, the inverse of `C_c,d` is `C_d,c` with the symmetric class equality. *Proof.* Unfold the inverse of the composite equivalence; its two functions are the reversed pair of twisting equivalences.
- <a id="nc-3-representative-square"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.changeRepresentative_twistEquiv` (*Common translation of representative comparisons*): For `h:[c]=[d]` and `a∈H¹(G,Twist(c))`, `T_d(C_c,d(a))=T_c(a)`. *Proof.* Cancel `T_d` after its inverse in the defining formula. Uses [Representative comparison value](#nc-3-representative-value).
- <a id="nc-3-representative-uniqueness"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.changeRepresentative_eq_map` (*Uniqueness from the twisting comparison square*): Fix `h:[c]=[d]`. If `f:Twist(c)→*Twist(d)` is continuous and G-equivariant and its `H¹` pushforward satisfies `T_d(f_*a)=T_c(a)` for every a, then `f_*` equals `C_c,d`. The square is an explicit hypothesis for this uniqueness lemma, and is already proved for the concrete gauge maps above. *Proof.* At each a, compare `C_c,d(a)` and `f_*a` by injectivity of `T_d`, using the representative square and the given square for f. Uses [Common translation of representative comparisons](#nc-3-representative-square); [Coefficient map on nonabelian cohomology](#nc-3-coefficient-h1-map).

**Checks.**

- `H1.changeRepresentative.test_neutral`: For equal original classes `[c]=[d]`, the comparison `C_c,d` sends the neutral twisted class to the neutral twisted class.
- `H1.changeRepresentative.test_nonneutral`: If `[c]=[d]` is nonneutral, `C_c,d(T_c⁻¹(1))` is nonneutral in `H¹(G,Twist(d))`, even though its translation by `T_d` is the original neutral class. The comparison cannot be replaced by the constant neutral map.
- `H1.changeRepresentative.test_class_hypothesis`: If [c] is nonneutral, the raw composite `T_1⁻¹∘T_c` sends the neutral twisted class to a nonneutral class. Dropping equality of the original classes invalidates pointedness.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, continuous cocycle/gauge definitions and Proposition 1 and its proof, printed pp. 5–7; final representative-change sentence on p. 7.

Use [Gauge-orbit bijection under twisting](#nc-3-twist-h1-equivalence); `Equiv.trans`; `Equiv.symm`.

<a id="nc-3-twist-coefficient-map"></a>

**Coefficient homomorphism between inner twists.** Construct the continuous equivariant group homomorphism `f_c:Twist(c)→*Twist(f∘c)` with `j_(f∘c)(f_c(x))=f(j_c(x))`. Its underlying homomorphism is exactly f.

Standing hypotheses (H9).

Use the underlying group/topology synonyms and the mapped cocycle `f∘c`. Reuse f as the group homomorphism. Continuity is hf; equivariance expands to `f(c(g)g(x)c(g)⁻¹)=f(c(g))g(f(x))f(c(g))⁻¹` by multiplicativity, preservation of inverse and the given original equivariance.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-twist-coefficient-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.map_apply` (*Value of a twisted coefficient map*): For every `x∈Twist(c)`, `j_(f∘c)(f_c(x))=f(j_c(x))`. *Proof.* Evaluate the homomorphism on the underlying synonym; the equality is definitional.
- <a id="nc-3-twist-coefficient-continuity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.map_continuous` (*Continuity of a twisted coefficient map*): The coefficient homomorphism `f_c:Twist(c)→Twist(f∘c)` is continuous. *Proof.* Both topologies are the inherited coefficient topologies. The continuity proof is hf.
- <a id="nc-3-twist-coefficient-equivariance"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.map_smul` (*Equivariance between the two twisted actions*): For every `g∈G` and `x∈Twist(c)`, `f_c(g⋆x)=g⋆f_c(x)`, with the target action twisted by `f∘c`. *Proof.* Apply injectivity of `j_(f∘c)` to compare values in V. Expand both inner actions, apply `map_mul` twice, `map_inv`, and original G-equivariance. Do not commute any factors. Uses [Value of a twisted coefficient map](#nc-3-twist-coefficient-value).
- <a id="nc-3-twist-coefficient-identity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.map_id` (*Identity coefficient map under twisting*): For every c, the twisted coefficient map induced by `id_U` equals `id_(Twist(c))` as a group homomorphism. *Proof.* The mapped cocycle under the identity and both underlying homomorphisms agree definitionally.
- <a id="nc-3-twist-coefficient-composition"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.map_comp` (*Composition of twisted coefficient maps*): For every c, `(f′∘f)_c=(f′)_(f∘c)∘f_c` as group homomorphisms, with the composite continuity and equivariance proofs. *Proof.* Use the definitional equality of mapped cocycles under composition and the original homomorphism composition. The topology/action proof arguments do not change the underlying homomorphism.
- <a id="nc-3-twist-coefficient-cocycle-square"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.twistEquiv_map` (*Coefficient naturality of the cocycle twisting equivalence*): For every `d∈Z¹(G,Twist(c))`, `τ_(f∘c)((f_c)_*d)=f_*(τ_c(d))` as continuous cocycles. *Proof.* Apply cocycle extensionality. At g the left side is `f(j_c(d(g)))f(c(g))`, while the right side is `f(j_c(d(g))c(g))`; `map_mul` identifies them in exactly this order. Uses [Continuity of a twisted coefficient map](#nc-3-twist-coefficient-continuity); [Equivariance between the two twisted actions](#nc-3-twist-coefficient-equivariance); [Continuous cocycles under inner twisting](#nc-3-twist-cocycle-equivalence).
- <a id="nc-3-twist-coefficient-h1-square"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistEquiv_map` (*Coefficient naturality on the H¹ orbit quotient*): For every `a∈H¹(G,Twist(c))`, `T_(f∘c)((f_c)_*a)=f_*(T_c(a))`. *Proof.* Choose a cocycle representative via `H1.mk_surjective`. Evaluate both quotient maps on that representative using `map_mk` and `twistEquiv_mk`; the cocycle square identifies their images. Uses [Coefficient naturality of the cocycle twisting equivalence](#nc-3-twist-coefficient-cocycle-square); [Coefficient map on nonabelian cohomology](#nc-3-coefficient-h1-map); [Gauge-orbit bijection under twisting](#nc-3-twist-h1-equivalence).

**Checks.**

- `twistCoefficientTests.value`: For every x, the twisted coefficient value is `f(j_c(x))` under the target underlying-group identification.
- `twistCoefficientTests.identity`: The twisted identity coefficient map fixes every x.
- `twistCoefficientTests.constant`: The constant-one coefficient homomorphism maps every twisted x to 1; no coefficient injectivity can be inferred from the twisting square.
- `twistCoefficientTests.cocycle_square`: The continuous cocycle coefficient square commutes, with multiplication by `c(g)` on the right.
- `twistCoefficientTests.repointed_neutral`: The image of `T_c(1)` under the coefficient `H¹` map is the gauge class `[f∘c]`.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1 ordered continuous cocycle/gauge formulas and coefficient functor, pp. 5–7.

### 0.10 Kernel membership for a twisted map
<a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-membership"></a>

**Kernel membership for a twisted map.** For `F_c=Twist.map c f`, x belongs to its kernel `K_c` exactly when `f(j_c(x))=1`.

Standing hypotheses (H10).

Unfold the kernel and the twisted map; their underlying equality is definitionally the original coefficient-map equality.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, continuous cocycle/gauge definitions, Proposition 1 and its proof, coefficient functor and central-quotient paragraph; pp. 5–7.

### 0.11 The twisted kernel and its H¹
<a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-action"></a>

**Continuous automorphism action on the twisted kernel.** Construct the restricted `MulDistribMulAction G K_c` by `g⋆(x,hx)=(g⋆_c x, kernel_stable hx)`.

Standing hypotheses (H10).

Use the twisted automorphism action, lift by kernel stability and discharge all action/distributivity laws by Subtype.ext.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-stability"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.kernel_stable` (*Stability of the twisted kernel*): If `x∈K_c` then `g⋆_c x∈K_c` for every `g∈G`. *Proof.* Use the proved equivariance of `F_c` and `g⋆1=1`; retain the conjugated action on the domain, not the original action on U. Uses [Kernel membership for a twisted map](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-membership); [Equivariance between the two twisted actions](#nc-3-twist-coefficient-equivariance).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-action-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.kernelAction_value` (*Underlying value of the restricted kernel action*): With kernelAction installed, the value of `g⋆x` in `Twist(c)` is `g⋆_c` x.val. *Proof.* Unfold the restricted action; the equality is definitional.
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-action-continuity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.kernelContinuousSMul` (*Joint continuity on the twisted kernel*): With kernelAction installed, `ContinuousSMul G K_c` holds for the subgroup topology. *Proof.* Compose the joint twisted action with the product/subtype projections, then lift the continuous map into `K_c`. Separate continuity is not substituted for joint continuity.

**Checks.**

- `Twist.kernelAction.test_unit`: Every g fixes the group identity in the twisted kernel.
- `Twist.kernelAction.test_joint_continuity`: The restricted action map `G×K_c→K_c` is jointly continuous for the product and subgroup topologies.
- `Twist.kernelAction.test_noncommutative_action`: For discrete `S₂` acting trivially on `S₃` before twisting, c(nonidentity)=(01), `f=1` and `x=(12)`, the restricted twisted action of (01) sends x to (02), different from x. The raw trivial action fails this test.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, continuous cocycle/gauge definitions, Proposition 1 and its proof, coefficient functor and central-quotient paragraph; pp. 5–7.

Use [Stability of the twisted kernel](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-stability).
<a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-h1-inclusion"></a>

**H¹ map from the twisted kernel.** Construct `H¹(G,K_c)→H¹(G,Twist(c))` as the H1.map of the subgroup inclusion, using kernelAction and its proved joint continuity.

Standing hypotheses (H10).

The subgroup inclusion is continuous and equivariant by its restricted action. Use the gauge-orbit H1.map; injectivity on groups alone does not imply injectivity on `H¹`.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-h1-representative"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistedKernelInclusion_mk` (*Kernel inclusion on cocycle representatives*): The `H¹` inclusion sends [d] to [g↦(d(g)).val], using the Z1.map of the subgroup inclusion. *Proof.* Evaluate the orbit quotient lift at a representative; the equality is definitional.
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-h1-neutral"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistedKernelInclusion_one` (*Neutral class under kernel inclusion*): The twisted-kernel `H¹` inclusion sends 1 to 1. *Proof.* Its coefficient inclusion sends the trivial cocycle to the trivial cocycle, hence its orbit class to the neutral class.
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-h1-image"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistedKernelInclusion_image` (*Kernel inclusion maps into the neutral image fibre*): Every `a∈H¹(G,K_c)` maps under H1.map `F_c` after twistedKernelInclusion to the neutral class in `H¹(G,Twist(f∘c))`. *Proof.* Choose a cocycle representative. Each of its values belongs to `ker(F_c)`, so the composite coefficient map gives the trivial cocycle; descend this equality to `H¹`. Uses [Kernel inclusion on cocycle representatives](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-h1-representative).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-h1-repointed-fibre"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistedKernelInclusion_fibre` (*Kernel inclusion maps to the fibre over the image cocycle*): For every `a∈H¹(G,K_c)`, H1.map `f (T_c(twistedKernelInclusion a))=[f∘c]`, where `T_c` is the twist `H¹` translation. This is one image inclusion, without surjectivity onto the fibre. *Proof.* Apply the repointed-fibre equivalence to the proved neutral image. No continuous lift or converse exactness is presumed. Uses [Kernel inclusion maps into the neutral image fibre](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-h1-image); [Neutral fibre after coefficient twisting and repointing](#nc-3-twist-coefficient-repointed-fibre).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-h1-mapped-converse"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.exists_twistedKernelInclusion_of_map_eq_one` (*Lift from a surjective coefficient-map neutral fibre*): If f is surjective, every `a∈H¹(G,Twist(c))` killed by the mapped twisted coefficient homomorphism `F_c` lies in the image of twistedKernelInclusion. No quotient-map, openness or continuous-section hypothesis on f is required. Under (H18). *Proof.* Choose a representative d and a gauge witness y in the target inner twist to neutrality of its mapped `H¹` class. Lift the one element y along the surjective `F_c`. Inverse-gauge normalization makes the mapped cocycle pointwise identity. Construct the continuous kernel cocycle and identify its included class with [d]. Continuity comes from a constant gauge and the subspace restriction, without a continuous section or inverse quotient comparison. Source: [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, pp. 5–9, continuous cocycle and ordered gauge definitions, coefficient functor and subgroup exactness paragraph. Uses [Neutral class as a coboundary](#nc-3-h1-neutral-criterion); [Gauge invariance of the cohomology class](#nc-3-h1-gauge-class); [Inverse gauge after a lifted coboundary](#nc-3-mapped-inverse-gauge-normalization); [Kernel lift followed by the coefficient inclusion](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-cocycle-lift-inclusion); [Kernel inclusion on cocycle representatives](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-h1-representative); [Surjectivity of the twisted coefficient map](#nc-3-twisted-map-surjectivity).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-h1-mapped-range"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistedKernelInclusion_range_iff` (*Exact image under a surjective coefficient map*): For surjective f and every `a∈H¹(G,Twist(c))`, a lies in the range of twistedKernelInclusion if and only if `H1.map(F_c)(a)=1`. Kernel-H¹ injectivity is not asserted. Under (H18). *Proof.* Combine the inherited kernel image inclusion with the mapped neutral-fibre converse. Source: [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, pp. 5–9, continuous cocycle and ordered gauge definitions, coefficient functor and subgroup exactness paragraph. Uses [Lift from a surjective coefficient-map neutral fibre](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-h1-mapped-converse); [Kernel inclusion maps into the neutral image fibre](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-h1-image).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-h1-original-fibre-range"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistedKernelInclusion_fibre_range_iff` (*Entire repointed fibre of a surjective coefficient map*): For surjective f and every `a∈H¹(G,U)`, a lies in the range of `b↦T_c(twistedKernelInclusion(b))` if and only if H1.map(f)(a)=[f∘c], where `T_c` is the twist translation. The distinguished fibre is over `[f∘c]`, which need not be neutral. Under (H18). *Proof.* Apply the mapped range criterion to `T_c⁻¹(a)`. Use the inherited coefficient-map/twist fibre criterion, and transport witnesses through the genuine `H¹` equivalence. This gives existence in the correct fibre, without uniqueness or kernel-H¹ injectivity. Source: [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, pp. 5–9, continuous cocycle and ordered gauge definitions, coefficient functor and subgroup exactness paragraph. Uses [Exact image under a surjective coefficient map](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-h1-mapped-range); [Neutral fibre after coefficient twisting and repointing](#nc-3-twist-coefficient-repointed-fibre).

**Checks.**

- `H1.twistedKernelInclusion.test_neutral`: The `H¹` inclusion sends the neutral class to the neutral class.
- `H1.twistedKernelInclusion.test_gauge_classes`: Gauge-equivalent cocycles in `K_c` have the same image under the `H¹` inclusion.
- `H1.twistedKernelInclusion.test_repointed_fibre`: After twist translation, every class from `K_c` lies in the coefficient-map fibre over `[f∘c]`, without claiming the converse.
- `H1.kernelImage.test_no_quotient_map`: For any continuous equivariant surjective f, mapped neutrality gives a kernel-H¹ preimage without any IsQuotientMap or continuous-section premise.
- `H1.kernelImage.test_non_neutral_rejected`: A class whose mapped twisted-coefficient `H¹ image` is non-neutral cannot lie in the kernel-inclusion range, even without surjectivity.
- `H1.kernelImage.test_shifted_basepoint`: If `[f∘c]≠1`, the neutral class of `H¹(G,U)` does not belong to the twist-translated kernel-inclusion range.
- `H1.kernelImage.test_constant_map`: For the constant-identity coefficient homomorphism into arbitrary V, every class of `H¹(G,Twist(c))` lies in the kernel-inclusion range; no surjectivity onto V is assumed.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, continuous cocycle/gauge definitions, Proposition 1 and its proof, coefficient functor and central-quotient paragraph; pp. 5–7.

Use [Continuous automorphism action on the twisted kernel](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-action); [Joint continuity on the twisted kernel](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-action-continuity); [Nonabelian first cohomology as a pointed set](#nc-3-nonabelian-h1); [Coefficient map on nonabelian cohomology](#nc-3-coefficient-h1-map).

### 0.12 Coefficient naturality of twisting and neutral fibres
<a id="nc-3-twist-coefficient-repointed-fibre"></a>

**Neutral fibre after coefficient twisting and repointing.** For every `a∈H¹(G,Twist(c))`, `f_*(T_c(a))=[f∘c]` if and only if `(f_c)_*(a)=1`. This identifies the fibre over the mapped chosen class without asserting injectivity of the coefficient map.

Standing hypotheses (H9).

Rewrite `f_*T_c(a)` using the proved coefficient/H¹ square. The equivalence `T_(f∘c)` sends exactly the source neutral class to `[f∘c]`, so its neutral-fibre criterion gives the equivalence.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1 ordered continuous cocycle/gauge formulas and coefficient functor, pp. 5–7.

Use [Coefficient naturality on the `H¹` orbit quotient](#nc-3-twist-coefficient-h1-square); [Neutral source fibre under twisting](#nc-3-twist-h1-neutral-fibre).

### 0.13 Twisted quotients and the quotient comparison
<a id="nc-3-twisted-quotient-action"></a>

**Continuous automorphism action on the twisted quotient.** Construct the quotient `Q_c=Twist(c)/ker(F_c)` with G-action `g⋆[x]=[g⋆_c x]`, extending Mathlib’s coset action to MulDistribMulAction. The quotient group and quotient topology are unchanged.

Standing hypotheses (H11).

Use the QuotientAction criterion: for `x⁻¹y∈ker(F_c)`, the ordered difference `(g⋆x)⁻¹(g⋆y)=g⋆(x⁻¹y)` also belongs to the kernel, by twisted kernel stability. Adopt the quotient MulAction, prove preservation of the identity and multiplication by quotient representatives; no new quotient carrier or inferred raw untwisted action is introduced.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-twisted-quotient-projection-action"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.quotientAction_mk` (*Equivariance of the twisted quotient projection*): With the descended action installed, `g⋆π_c(x)=π_c(g⋆_c x)` for every g and x, where `π_c` is the quotient projection. *Proof.* Use the coset-action evaluation on representatives, with exactly the action constructed above.
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-quotient-action-continuity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.quotientContinuousSMul` (*Joint continuity of the descended inner action*): The descended action `G×Q_c→Q_c` is jointly continuous for the product and quotient topologies. This requires no surjectivity or quotient-map assumption on f. *Proof.* The quotient projection from `Twist(c)` is open, continuous and surjective because `Twist(c)` is a topological group; closedness of its kernel is unnecessary. Its product with the identity on G is an open quotient map. The action after this precomposition is `π_c(g⋆_c x)`, continuous by the joint twisted action. Apply the open-quotient continuity criterion on this product; the original f need not be a quotient map. Source: [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, continuous cocycle/gauge definitions, Proposition 1 proof and coefficient-functor/central-quotient paragraphs, printed pp. 5–7; motivation in Proposition 2 central extension, printed pp. 8–9. Uses [Twisting by a cocycle](#nc-3-twisting); [Equivariance of the twisted quotient projection](#nc-3-twisted-quotient-projection-action).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-quotient-comparison-equivariance"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.quotientEquiv_smul` (*Equivariance of the quotient comparison*): If f is surjective, the group equivalence `e_c:Q_c≃*Twist(f∘c)` is G-equivariant for the descended action: `e_c(g⋆q)=g⋆_{f∘c}e_c(q)`. *Proof.* Choose a quotient representative x for q; evaluate both `e_c` and the quotient action on its class, then use the equivariance of `F_c`. No continuity of the inverse is used. Source: [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, continuous cocycle/gauge definitions, Proposition 1 proof and coefficient-functor/central-quotient paragraphs, printed pp. 5–7; motivation in Proposition 2 central extension, printed pp. 8–9. Uses [Equivariance of the twisted quotient projection](#nc-3-twisted-quotient-projection-action); [Quotient comparison on representatives](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-quotient-value); [Equivariance between the two twisted actions](#nc-3-twist-coefficient-equivariance).

**Checks.**

- `Twist.quotientAction.test_unit`: Every g fixes the identity of the quotient, for every f, without surjectivity or a quotient-map hypothesis.
- `Twist.quotientAction.test_projection`: The quotient projection is G-equivariant for the inner action: `g⋆[x]=[c(g)(g•j_c(x))c(g)⁻¹]`.
- `Twist.quotientAction.test_joint_continuity`: The descended action `G×Q_c→Q_c` is jointly continuous for the quotient topology, even when f is not a quotient map.
- `Twist.quotientAction.test_nontrivial_twist`: For `f=id` and any genuine inner-twist value `g⋆_c x≠x`, the induced quotient action moves [x]. Replacing the twist by a trivial raw action fails this test; the hypothesis is not asserted for all twists.

The construction and its conventions follow [Mathlib contributors](#reference-mathlibnativetwistedquotients-6b7abb3), GroupTheory/GroupAction/Quotient.lean: QuotientAction, quotient and `smul_mk`, repository pin 6b7abb3; Kim continuous coefficient conventions motivate the use.

Use [Stability of the twisted kernel](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-stability); `MulAction.QuotientAction`; `MulAction.quotient`; `QuotientGroup.Quotient.group`.
<a id="nc-3-twisted-quotient-cocycle-map"></a>

**Projection of continuous twisted cocycles.** Construct `Z¹(G,Twist(c))→Z¹(G,Q_c)`, `d↦π_c∘d`, as the Z1.map of Mathlib’s quotient homomorphism. Surjectivity of f is not needed.

Standing hypotheses (H11).

Use the coefficient-cocycle map for the continuous quotient homomorphism and its proved action compatibility; the cocycle identity is transported, not assumed.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-twisted-quotient-cocycle-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.twistedQuotient_apply` (*Value of twisted cocycle projection*): At every `g∈G`, the projected cocycle has value `[d(g)]` in the quotient `Q_c`. *Proof.* Evaluate the coefficient-cocycle composition and quotient homomorphism.
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-quotient-cocycle-neutral"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.twistedQuotient_one` (*Neutral cocycle under quotient projection*): The twisted quotient cocycle projection sends the trivial cocycle to the trivial cocycle. *Proof.* Apply the neutral-cocycle law for coefficient maps.
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-quotient-cocycle-gauge"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.twistedQuotient_gauge` (*Ordered gauge compatibility of quotient cocycles*): For `x∈Twist(c)` and `d∈Z¹(G,Twist(c))`, projection(x·d)=[x]·projection(d), with the ordered gauge actions and quotient class [x]. *Proof.* Apply the coefficient-map gauge identity to the quotient homomorphism, whose equivariance and continuity were proved; retain multiplication order. Uses [Joint continuity of the descended inner action](#nc-3-twisted-quotient-action-continuity); [Gauge compatibility of coefficient cocycle maps](#nc-3-coefficient-cocycle-gauge).

**Checks.**

- `Z1.twistedQuotient.test_value`: The projected cocycle at g is the quotient class `[d(g)]`, not a lift or an arbitrary representative.
- `Z1.twistedQuotient.test_constant_map`: For the constant coefficient homomorphism `f=1`, its kernel is all of `Twist(c)`, and every projected cocycle is the trivial cocycle on the quotient.
- `Z1.twistedQuotient.test_gauge`: Ordered gauge change descends exactly by the quotient class of its gauge element; no commutativity of U is assumed.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, continuous cocycle/gauge definitions, Proposition 1 proof and coefficient-functor/central-quotient paragraphs, printed pp. 5–7; motivation in Proposition 2 central extension, printed pp. 8–9.

Use [Equivariance of the twisted quotient projection](#nc-3-twisted-quotient-projection-action); [Coefficient map on continuous cocycles](#nc-3-coefficient-cocycle-map); `QuotientGroup.mk'`; `QuotientGroup.continuous_mk`.

<a id="nc-3-twisted-quotient-h1-map"></a>

**Quotient map on twisted H¹ orbit sets.** Construct `H¹(G,Twist(c))→H¹(G,Q_c)` as the H1.map of `π_c`, for the continuous gauge-orbit quotients and the jointly continuous descended action.

Standing hypotheses (H11).

Use the quotient lift of coefficient maps; the projected gauge identity makes it independent of representatives. No surjectivity on `H¹`, injectivity on `H¹` or converse kernel-image theorem follows merely from the group projection.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-twisted-quotient-h1-representative"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistedQuotient_mk` (*Quotient H¹ on representatives*): For every `d∈Z¹(G,Twist(c))`, the quotient `H¹` map sends [d] to `[π_c∘d]`. *Proof.* Evaluate the orbit quotient lift at a cocycle representative. - <a id="nc-3-twisted-quotient-h1-neutral"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistedQuotient_one` (*Pointedness of the twisted quotient H¹ map*): The twisted quotient `H¹` map sends the neutral class to the neutral class, without surjectivity of f. *Proof.* Use the coefficient `H¹` map’s neutral-class law. - <a id="nc-3-twisted-quotient-h1-kernel-image"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistedQuotient_kernel` (*Kernel inclusion is killed by the quotient*): Every class in `H¹(G,K_c)` maps under the restricted kernel inclusion and the new quotient `H¹` map to 1. This is one image inclusion, not its converse or injectivity. *Proof.* Choose a kernel-valued cocycle representative. Each quotient class of its value is 1 by kernel membership and `eq_one_iff`. The projected cocycle is thus the trivial cocycle; its orbit class is neutral. No whole-function lift is required. Uses [Kernel inclusion on cocycle representatives](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-h1-representative); [Quotient `H¹` on representatives](#nc-3-twisted-quotient-h1-representative); [Value of twisted cocycle projection](#nc-3-twisted-quotient-cocycle-value).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-h1-quotient-range"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistedQuotient_range_iff` (*Exact image for the twisted quotient*): For every `a∈H¹(G,Twist(c))`, a lies in the range of twistedKernelInclusion if and only if twistedQuotient(a)=1, without assumptions of surjectivity or quotient topology on f. Under (H18). *Proof.* The inherited quotient-kernel image supplies one implication; the single-gauge lifting lemma supplies the converse. Source: [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, pp. 5–9, continuous cocycle and ordered gauge definitions, coefficient functor and subgroup exactness paragraph. - <a id="nc-3-twisted-map-surjectivity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.map_surjective` (*Surjectivity of the twisted coefficient map*): Surjectivity of f implies surjectivity of its twisted coefficient map `F_c`. The underlying map is f on the identical coefficient carrier. Under (H10). *Proof.* The original-group identifications preserve the underlying f; equivalently transport a preimage through `j_c` and the target identification. The proof uses the underlying function. Source: [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, continuous cocycle/gauge definitions, Proposition 1 and its proof, coefficient functor and central-quotient paragraph; pp. 5–7. Uses [Coefficient homomorphism between inner twists](#nc-3-twist-coefficient-map); [Value of a twisted coefficient map](#nc-3-twist-coefficient-value).

- `H1.twistedQuotient.test_neutral`: The orbit-quotient map preserves the neutral class without any surjectivity assumption on f.
- `H1.twistedQuotient.test_representative`: The quotient `H¹` map on a cocycle class is the class of the projected cocycle, so the construction agrees with the H1.map.
- `H1.twistedQuotient.test_kernel`: Every class from the restricted twisted kernel is killed by the quotient `H¹` map; no converse or injectivity of the kernel inclusion is presumed.
- `H1.kernelImage.test_quotient_neutral`: The neutral class of the ambient inner twist belongs to the kernel-inclusion range.

<a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-quotient-equivalence"></a>

**Quotient comparison for a surjective twisted map.** If f is surjective, construct `Twist(c)/K_c≃*Twist(f∘c)` using Mathlib’s quotientKerEquivOfSurjective `F_c`.

Standing hypotheses (H10).

The twisted map has the same underlying function as f and thus is surjective. Import the first isomorphism theorem with its normal kernel and quotient-group carrier.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-quotient-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.quotientEquiv_mk` (*Quotient comparison on representatives*): For every `x∈Twist(c)`, `quotientEquiv([x])=F_c(x)`. *Proof.* Unfold Mathlib’s quotient-by-kernel equivalence on a quotient representative; evaluation is definitionally `F_c`.
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-quotient-continuous"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.quotientEquiv_continuous` (*Continuity of the quotient comparison*): For surjective continuous f, the quotient comparison is continuous for the quotient-group topology. *Proof.* Apply the quotient-map criterion to the group projection; its composite is the continuous `F_c`. Uses [Quotient comparison on representatives](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-quotient-value).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-quotient-inverse-continuous"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.quotientEquiv_symm_continuous` (*Continuity of the inverse quotient comparison*): If f is also a quotient map, the inverse quotientEquiv⁻¹ is continuous. *Proof.* Twist preserves the original topologies, so `F_c` is a quotient map. The composite `quotientEquiv⁻¹∘F_c` is the continuous group projection by inverse cancellation. Uses [Quotient comparison on representatives](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-quotient-value).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-quotient-topology-criterion"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.quotientEquiv_symm_continuous_iff` (*Exact topology criterion for the quotient inverse*): For surjective continuous equivariant f, Continuous(quotientEquiv⁻¹) if and only if IsQuotientMap f. Thus surjectivity and continuity alone cannot supply a topological isomorphism. *Proof.* For the forward implication package the equivalence and assumed inverse continuity into a homeomorphism, then compose its quotient-map property with the group quotient projection to recover IsQuotientMap `F_c=f`. The reverse implication is the proved inverse-continuity lemma. This is algebraic equivariance and does not assert inverse continuity. Under (H11). *Proof.* Apply the injective equivalence `e_c` to both sides, then use its forward equivariance and inverse identities. Source: [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, continuous cocycle/gauge definitions, Proposition 1 proof and coefficient-functor/central-quotient paragraphs, printed pp. 5–7; motivation in Proposition 2 central extension, printed pp. 8–9. ### 0.14 Functoriality of nonabelian H⁰ and H¹

The cocycle and H¹ maps and their identity/composition laws are the native compatible-pair API. The remaining targets compare these with invariants, inner coefficient-action twisting and geometric local conditions.

<a id="nc-3-functoriality"></a>

**Functoriality of nonabelian H⁰ and H¹.** (a) A continuous G-equivariant group homomorphism `f : U → U′` induces a homomorphism `H⁰(G, U) → H⁰(G, U′)` and maps `Z¹(G, U) → Z¹(G, U′)`, `c ↦ f ∘ c`, and `H¹(G, U) → H¹(G, U′)`, preserving base points, compatible with identities and composition, and with `f(u·c) = f(u)·(f ∘ c)`. (b) A continuous group homomorphism `φ : G′ → G`, with G′ acting on U through `φ`, induces the restriction maps `H⁰(G, U) → H⁰(G′, U)` (inclusion) and `Z¹(G, U) → Z¹(G′, U)`, `c ↦ c ∘ φ`, and `H¹(G, U) → H¹(G′, U)`, base point preserving and functorial; in particular for a closed `subgroup H ≤ G` there is restriction `H¹(G, U) → H¹(H, U)`. Maps of pointed sets that are compatible in this way are what the exact sequences ([Kernel of inclusion in nonabelian cohomology](#nc-3-exact-sequence)) are built from.

G is a topological group and U a topological group with an action of G by group automorphisms (MulDistribMulAction G U) such that the action map `G × U → U` is continuous (ContinuousSMul G U). In (a) U′ satisfies the same hypotheses and f is continuous with `f(g•u) = g•f(u)`; in `(b) φ` is continuous and G′ acts on U by `g′•u = φ(g′)•u`.

The coefficient-map leaves supply part (a). The supplied source-restriction maps give part (b) on cocycles, gauge-orbit classes and fixed subgroups, with identity/composition and mixed coefficient/source squares. Their subgroup comparisons identify the previously constructed restrictions. The geometric, additive and local-condition comparisons use their separate construction targets. `(a) f ∘ c` is continuous and `f(c(gh)) = f(c(g))·f(g•c(h)) = f(c(g))·g•f(c(h))`; `f(u·c) = f(u)·(f∘c)` because `f(u c(g) (g•u)⁻¹) = f(u) f(c(g)) (g•f(u))⁻¹`. So the map descends to orbits and sends the trivial cocycle to the trivial cocycle. `(b) c ∘ φ` is continuous and `(c∘φ)(g′h′) = c(φg′)·φ(g′)•c(φh′)`; the U-actions correspond, so the map descends. Identities and composition hold on cocycles, hence on classes. For repointed twisting comparisons under source restriction, import the direct twisted-source map, its proved translation square, representative-change naturality and translated composition law. The geometric localization and local-condition identifications are supplied by the coefficient-family and local-condition constructions of Layer 4; the abstract square alone does not imply them. Apply H1.map to the restricted twisted-kernel inclusion using its joint action continuity. The quotient action and `H¹` comparison are supplied by [Continuous automorphism action on the twisted quotient](#nc-3-twisted-quotient-action) through [Quotient neutral fibre and the original image cocycle](#nc-3-twisted-quotient-h1-repointed-fibre); the continuous equivalence requires surjectivity and a quotient map. The single-gauge lift in [Lift from a surjective coefficient-map neutral fibre](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-h1-mapped-converse) gives the converse image statement when f is surjective, without requiring a continuous section. General inclusion injectivity is governed by the invariant action, not by functoriality alone. Geometric local-condition compatibility uses the realization and local-condition constructions of Layer 4.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.map`: The map `H¹(G, U) → H¹(G, U′)` induced by a continuous equivariant homomorphism.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.map_one`: H1.map f sends the base point to the base point.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.map_id`: H1.map `id = id`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.map_comp`: H1.map `(f′ ∘ f) =` H1.map `f′ ∘` H1.map f.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.res`: The restriction `H¹(G, U) → H¹(G′, U)` along a continuous homomorphism `G′ → G`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.res_comp`: Restriction along a composite is the composite of restrictions.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H0.map`: The homomorphism of invariants induced by an equivariant homomorphism.

**Checks.**

- For identity source and coefficient maps, a nontrivial transposition class in `H¹(C₂,S₃)` is fixed.
- For the trivial action on `C₃⊂S₃`, coefficient inclusion identifies the two nontrivial `C₃→C₃` classes by conjugacy in S₃. Functoriality does not imply injectivity.

- Restriction to the decomposition group at a place v, `H¹(G_T, U) → H¹(G_v, U)`, is the case (b) of the inclusion `G_v → G_T` used for Selmer conditions.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §4, restriction paragraph, p. 127; [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, p. 7.

### 0.15 The canonical additive comparison
<a id="nc-3-canonical-comparison-naturality"></a>

**Canonical additive comparison.** For a continuous G-action on an additive topological abelian group M, use the parent comparison `α: H1(G,Multiplicative M) ≃ ContCohomology.H1 G M` induced by c↦toAdd∘c, with `α(1)=0`. For a compatible pair `φ:H→G` and continuous additive `f:M→N`, `α_H,N∘(φ,f)_*=explicitMap1(φ,f)∘α_G,M`. On cocycles the gauge by m translates by −d0(m); hence the quotient comparison is independent of the sign of the B1 generator. The comparison is the identity on underlying cocycle functions, not an arbitrary bijection.

G,H topological groups M,N topological additive abelian groups with jointly continuous automorphism actions `φ` continuous homomorphism and f continuous additive equivariant for `φ`.

Use the accepted parent cocycle equivalence and H1 quotient equivalence. Read the explicitMap1 representative formula and compare both composites at every `h∈H`. Use class-map surjectivity for equality on H1; check gauge m becomes `m+c−g·m`.

**Checks.**

- The neutral class maps to zero; cocycle representatives remain unchanged after writing the operation additively.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), Section 1, continuous cochains and gauge equivalence, printed pp. 4–6.

### 0.16 Descent of cocycles to quotients

Use native `Cocycle.apply_mul_of_mem`, `Cocycle.smul_apply_of_mem`, `Cocycle.descend` and `Cocycle.map_descend`. The displayed deductions identify their formulas and our gauge parameter; they do not assign a second descent construction.

<a id="nc-3-cocycle-right-cosets"></a>

**Trivial restriction gives right-coset constancy.** For any subgroup N on which c is identically 1, c(gn)=c(g) for all `n∈N`. Normality, compactness and discrete U are not needed.

Standing hypotheses (H12).

Use c(gn)=c(g)(g•c(n)) and `c(n)=1`. This is the right-coset relation, not a homomorphism property.

**Checks.**

- For `N={1}`, right-coset constancy specializes to `c(g1)=c(g)` for every cocycle.
- For `N=G` and the trivial cocycle, every coset has value 1.
- For the conjugation action on S₃ and `c(h)=τ(h•τ)⁻¹` with `τ=(01)`, the nonnormal subgroup generated by τ is killed. Right-coset constancy still holds although left-coset constancy can fail.

The construction and its conventions follow [Native nonabelian H¹](#native-nonabelian-h1), `Cocycle.apply_mul_of_mem`; the displayed proof is an elementary deduction.

Use [Continuous 1-cocycles and invariants with nonabelian coefficients](#nc-3-continuous-cocycles).
<a id="nc-3-cocycle-left-cosets"></a>

**Normality gives left-coset constancy.** If N is normal and `c|N=1`, then c(ng)=c(g) for all `n∈N`.

Standing hypotheses (H12).

Normality places g⁻¹ng in N. Rewrite ng=g(g⁻¹ng) and apply right-coset constancy.

**Checks.**

- For `N={1}`, the conclusion is `c(1g)=c(g)` for every cocycle.
- For `N=G` and the trivial cocycle, both left and right translates have value 1.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.mul_left_eq_of_trivial.test_requires_normal`: Let G=ConjAct(S₃) act on `U=S₃` by conjugation, `τ=(01)`, `n=τ`, `g=(12)`, and `c(h)=τ(h•τ)⁻¹`. Then `c(n)=1` and c(gn)=c(g), but c(ng)≠c(g). The cocycle one-fibre is the nonnormal centralizer of `τ`. Thus killing a subgroup alone does not imply left-coset constancy.

The construction and its conventions follow [Native nonabelian H¹](#native-nonabelian-h1), `Cocycle.apply_mul_of_mem`, applied to `g(g⁻¹ng)`; the displayed proof is an elementary deduction.

Use [Trivial restriction gives right-coset constancy](#nc-3-cocycle-right-cosets); `Subgroup.Normal.conj_mem'`.

<a id="nc-3-cocycle-values-fixed"></a>

**Trivial normal restriction fixes each value.** If N is normal and `c|N=1`, then `n•c(g)=c(g)` for all `g∈G` and `n∈N`. This fixes the coefficient target for quotient descent; it does not say N acts trivially on all U.

Standing hypotheses (H12).

The cocycle identity gives c(ng)=n•c(g). Normal left-coset constancy gives c(ng)=c(g). Compare them.

**Checks.**

- For `N={1}`, every value is fixed, without a triviality hypothesis on the full G-action.
- For `N=G`, trivial restriction forces every cocycle value to be 1, which is fixed by every automorphism.
- Under the trivial G-action, each cocycle value is N-fixed for every normal N that it kills; the quotient cocycle can still be nontrivial.

The construction and its conventions follow [Native nonabelian H¹](#native-nonabelian-h1), `Cocycle.smul_apply_of_mem`; the displayed proof is an elementary deduction.

Use [Normality gives left-coset constancy](#nc-3-cocycle-left-cosets); [Continuous 1-cocycles and invariants with nonabelian coefficients](#nc-3-continuous-cocycles).

<a id="nc-3-cocycle-values-invariants"></a>

**Values lie in the invariant coefficient subgroup.** If N is normal and `c|N=1`, every `c(g)` belongs to the FixedPoints.subgroup N U under the restricted subgroup action. This is `U^N`, which can be a proper subgroup and can be infinite.

Standing hypotheses (H12).

Use the imported fixed-subgroup membership criterion; for each n:N, the preceding pointwise invariance theorem gives its scalar action fixing `c(g)`. No parallel fixed-point carrier is introduced.

**Checks.**

- For `N={1}`, the fixed coefficient subgroup is all U and the value map is unchanged.
- For the conjugation action of `G=S₃` on U=S₃ and `N=G`, `U^N` is the trivial centre; a transposition is excluded.

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.values_mem_fixedPoints.test_top_trivial`: The trivial cocycle at any g is 1 and belongs to the `U^G` even when `U^G` is proper; the target is not all of U.

The construction and its conventions follow [Native nonabelian H¹](#native-nonabelian-h1), `Cocycle.smul_apply_of_mem` and Mathlib `FixedPoints.subgroup`; the displayed proof is an elementary deduction.

Use [Trivial normal restriction fixes each value](#nc-3-cocycle-values-fixed); `FixedPoints.subgroup`; `FixedPoints.mem_subgroup`.

<a id="nc-3-quotient-cocycle-descent"></a>

**Descent of a cocycle to the quotient.** For a normal subgroup N of G and a continuous nonabelian cocycle c with `c(n)=1` for every `n∈N`, use native `Cocycle.descend` for the continuous cocycle `d:G/N→U^N` with `d([g])=c(g)`. Here `U^N` is Mathlib FixedPoints.subgroup N U with its quotient automorphism action and subspace topology; `G/N` has the quotient topology. Neither compactness, openness of N, discreteness nor finiteness of U is required. For an abelian coefficient group written additively it agrees with the pinned Tau Ceti declaration `TauCeti.ContCohomology.descendZ1`.

Standing hypotheses (H13).

Use the quotient action on the fixed-point subgroup. Send g to the subtype element `c(g)∈U^N`. The coset relation `a⁻¹b∈N` and right-coset constancy prove representative independence, so use the ordinary quotient lift, not a quotient homomorphism lift of the nonhomomorphic c. The quotient-map continuity criterion reduces continuity to the original continuous c valued in the subtype. Quotient induction on both arguments proves the ordered cocycle law using the representative action.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.descend_apply`: For every g, inclusion into U sends descended `c([g])` to `c(g)`.
- <a id="nc-3-quotient-cocycle-unique"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.descend_unique` (*Uniqueness of quotient cocycle descent*): Under the descent hypotheses, any cocycle `d:G/N→U^N` whose value at [g], included in U, is `c(g)` for every g equals the constructed descent. Equality is in the cocycle type, not merely equality of classes. *Proof.* Apply cocycle extensionality; lift each quotient element to a representative by quotient induction and apply subtype extensionality to the given value equality.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.descend_one`: Descending the trivial cocycle gives the trivial quotient cocycle.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.descend_proof_independent`: The descended cocycle is independent of the proof that c is trivial on N.
- <a id="nc-3-inflate-descended-cocycle"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.inflate_descend` (*Recovery after quotient descent*): For c trivial on normal N, inflating its descent recovers c exactly in `Z¹(G,U)`. *Proof.* Cocycle extensionality and the quotient-lift computation at [g] make the equality pointwise definitional. Uses [Inflation of quotient cocycles](#nc-3-quotient-cocycle-inflation).
- <a id="nc-3-quotient-cocycle-gauge"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.descend_gauge_iff` (*Exact N-fixed gauge witnesses after descent*): For continuous cocycles c,d both trivial on normal N, there exists `x∈U` with `d(g)=x c(g)(g•x)⁻¹` for all g if and only if there exists `x∈U^N` with descended `d(q)=x` descended `c(q)(q•x)⁻¹` for every `q∈G/N`. No refinement of N or `H¹` quotient construction is used. *Proof.* The inherited gauge-witness lemma proves any global witness x is N-fixed from triviality of both cocycles. Package x in the fixed subgroup and prove the quotient gauge equation by quotient induction, subtype extensionality and the representative action. Conversely, evaluate the quotient equation at [g] and apply the subgroup inclusion. This establishes the pointwise witness bridge but does not define quotient `H¹` inflation. Uses [A same-stage gauge witness is already invariant](#nc-3-gauge-witness-fixed).

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.descend.test_one`: The descent of the trivial cocycle is the quotient trivial cocycle.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.descend.test_representative`: For `n∈N`, the descended values at [gn] and [g] agree in `U^N`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.descend.test_proper_invariants`: For ConjAct `S₃` acting on `S₃` and `N=G`, the transposition(01) is not in `U^N`: conjugation by(12) changes it. The coefficient target cannot be replaced by all U.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.descend.test_identity_S3_values`: For discrete `G=U=S₃` with trivial G-action, `N={1}`, and the identity homomorphism cocycle `c(g)=g`, the descended cocycle at [(01)] has underlying U-value (01), which is not 1.
- For a normal subgroup N of G and a continuous nonabelian cocycle c with `c(n)=1` for every `n∈N`, use native `Cocycle.descend` for the continuous cocycle `d:G/N→U^N` with `d([g])=c(g)`. Here `U^N` is Mathlib FixedPoints.subgroup N U with its quotient automorphism action and subspace topology; `G/N` has the quotient topology. Neither compactness, openness of N, discreteness nor finiteness of U is required.

The construction and its conventions follow [Native nonabelian H¹](#native-nonabelian-h1), `Cocycle.descend`, `Cocycle.coe_descend_apply` and `Cocycle.map_descend`; the displayed proof is an elementary deduction.

### 0.17 Inflation and the quotient transition maps

Inflation is native `TauCeti.NonabelianH1.infl`, and same-kernel class injectivity is `infl_injective`. The pointwise fixed-gauge deduction below is the argument inside its native proof. Construct only the further transition and compatibility API on those carriers.

<a id="nc-3-quotient-cocycle-inflation"></a>

**Inflation of quotient cocycles.** For any normal `N≤G` and any continuous cocycle `d:G/N→U^N` with the quotient action, use native `Cocycle.map` for its inflation `c:G→U` with `c(g)=d([g])` included in U. It is continuous, satisfies the ordered cocycle law, and is identically 1 on N. No `H¹` pointed-set map is asserted. For an abelian coefficient group written additively it agrees with the pinned Tau Ceti declaration `TauCeti.ContCohomology.explicitInfl1`.

Standing hypotheses (H13).

Compose the continuous projection `G→G/N`, the continuous d and subgroup inclusion `U^N→U`. The quotient multiplication/action representative formulas turn d's ordered cocycle law into the ordered G-law after applying subgroup inclusion. For `n∈N` the quotient class is 1, and `d(1)=1`; no coefficient action on all U is forced to factor through `G/N`.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.inflate_apply`: At g the inflated cocycle is inclusion of `d([g])` from the fixed subgroup.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.inflate_trivialOn`: Every inflated cocycle is identically 1 on N.
- <a id="nc-3-quotient-cocycle-inflation-one"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.inflate_one` (*Trivial cocycle under inflation*): Inflation of the constant identity cocycle on `G/N` with coefficients `U^N` is the constant identity cocycle on G with coefficients U. Hypotheses: G and U are groups endowed with topologies, G acts on U by group automorphisms, and N is an arbitrary normal subgroup. The quotient action on the `subgroup U^N` is used. Joint action continuity and continuous group operations are not required for this identity of cocycles. *Proof.* Evaluate at every g; the fixed-subgroup inclusion sends 1 to 1. Apply cocycle extensionality. Source: [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed p. 6, continuous cocycle and gauge-orbit definitions; derived fixed-normal-subgroup argument.
- <a id="nc-3-descend-inflated-cocycle"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.descend_inflate` (*Recovery after cocycle inflation*): For every `d∈Z¹(G/N,U^N)`, descend its inflation using the proved triviality on N; the result equals d in `Z¹(G/N,U^N)`. *Proof.* Use uniqueness of descent and the pointwise inflation formula on every representative. Uses [Uniqueness of quotient cocycle descent](#nc-3-quotient-cocycle-unique).
- <a id="nc-3-quotient-cocycle-inflation-injective"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.inflate_injective` (*Injectivity of quotient-cocycle inflation*): For every normal N, inflation `Z¹(G/N,U^N)→Z¹(G,U)` is injective. Hypotheses: G and U are groups with topologies, with a G-action on U by group automorphisms. Use the continuous ordered cocycles `c(gh)=c(g)(g•c(h))`, quotient topologies and fixed coefficient subgroups. N is a normal subgroup of G. No compactness, openness/closedness, discrete coefficients, continuity of the action or commutativity is required for cocycle inflation injectivity. *Proof.* If two cocycles have equal inflations, descend both to N and apply the descend-inflate identity. This gives reflection at the same finite quotient. Source: [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed pp. 5–7, continuous cocycle and gauge definitions; [Native nonabelian H¹](#native-nonabelian-h1), `Cocycle.map`, `infl_mk` and the fixed-gauge argument in `infl_injective`; the displayed proof is an elementary deduction. Uses [Recovery after cocycle inflation](#nc-3-descend-inflated-cocycle).
- <a id="nc-3-quotient-inflation-equivariance"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.inflate_smul` (*Gauge equivariance of cocycle inflation*): For `x∈U^N` and `d∈Z¹(G/N,U^N)`, `inflate_N(x·d)=x·inflate_N(d)`, with x included in U on the right. The products and inverses stay in their printed order. Under (H14). *Proof.* Evaluate the cocycles at any `g∈G`. The quotient representative and fixed-subgroup inclusion formulas identify both gauge expressions. Apply cocycle extensionality. No representative section or coefficient action on all U through `G/N` is introduced. Source: [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed p. 6, continuous cocycle and gauge-orbit definitions; derived fixed-normal-subgroup argument. Uses [Nonabelian first cohomology as a pointed set](#nc-3-nonabelian-h1).
- <a id="nc-3-quotient-inflation-gauge-reflection"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.inflate_gauge_iff` (*Same-subgroup reflection of gauge witnesses*): For `d,e∈Z¹(G/N,U^N)`, there is `x∈U` with `x·inflate_N(d)=inflate_N(e)` if and only if there is `x∈U^N` with `x·d=e`. This is the same N on both sides, with no replacement by a smaller subgroup. Under (H14). *Proof.* Evaluate a global gauge equality on each `n∈N`. Both inflated cocycles take value 1, so the `gauge_witness_fixed` theorem forces that very witness into `U^N`. Use this genuine subgroup element and quotient representative induction, then subtype/cocycle extensionality, to obtain `x·d=e`. The converse follows by inflation equivariance and inclusion of the fixed gauge witness. Source: [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed p. 6, continuous cocycle and gauge-orbit definitions; derived fixed-normal-subgroup argument. Uses [A same-stage gauge witness is already invariant](#nc-3-gauge-witness-fixed); [Gauge equivariance of cocycle inflation](#nc-3-quotient-inflation-equivariance); [Nonabelian first cohomology as a pointed set](#nc-3-nonabelian-h1).

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.inflate.test_one`: Inflation preserves the trivial cocycle.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.inflate.test_native_projection`: Inflation evaluates as the d composed with the quotient projection and subgroup inclusion.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.inflate.test_subgroup`: At any `n∈N` the inflated cocycle is 1; no arbitrary chosen quotient representative is used.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.inflate.test_identity_S3_values`: For discrete `G=U=S₃` with trivial G-action, `N={1}`, and d the descent of `c(g)=g`, `inflate_N(d)((01))=(01)≠1`.
- For any normal `N≤G` and any continuous cocycle `d:G/N→U^N` with the quotient action, use native `Cocycle.map` for its inflation `c:G→U` with `c(g)=d([g])` included in U. It is continuous, satisfies the ordered cocycle law, and is identically 1 on N. No `H¹` pointed-set map is asserted.
- The identity value is that of the coefficient group, rather than an arbitrary selected cocycle.
- A nonidentity fixed gauge element gives the same equality; the assertion holds for noncommutative U.
- The forward implication keeps the original witness, rather than assuming a fixed witness or refining N. Infinite U is allowed.

The construction and its conventions follow [Native nonabelian H¹](#native-nonabelian-h1), `Cocycle.map`, `infl_mk` and the fixed-gauge argument in `infl_injective`; the displayed proof is an elementary deduction.

<a id="nc-3-cocycle-transition"></a>

**Reverse-inclusion transition of quotient cocycles.** For `M≤N`, construct `tᴺ_M:Z¹(G/N,U^N)→Z¹(G/M,U^M)` by descending `inflate_N(d)` to M. On representatives its underlying U-value `at [g]_M` is `d([g]_N)`. Thus it combines pullback along `G/M→G/N` with inclusion `U^N→U^M`.

G and U are groups with topologies, with a G-action on U by group automorphisms. Use the continuous ordered cocycles `c(gh)=c(g)(g•c(h))`, quotient topologies and fixed coefficient subgroups. `M≤N` are normal subgroups of G. Neither openness/closedness nor compactness, commutativity or discreteness is required for cocycle transitions.

`inflate_N(d)` is identically 1 on N, hence on M. Apply the descent to M; its representative formula gives the stated value. Inflating the result recovers `inflate_N(d)`. Same-subgroup cocycle injectivity then proves identity, composition, preservation of the identity cocycle and injectivity. No choice of quotient representative or new coefficient action is introduced.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.transition_apply`: The underlying U-value of `tᴺ_M(d) at [g]_M` is `d([g]_N)`.
- <a id="nc-3-cocycle-transition-inflation"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.inflate_transition` (*Inflation commutes with cocycle transition*): For `M≤N`, `inflate_M(tᴺ_M(d))=inflate_N(d)`. *Proof.* Apply recovery after descent to the inflated N-level cocycle.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.transition_refl`: `tᴺ_N(d)=d`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.transition_trans`: For `P≤M≤N`, `tᴹ_P(tᴺ_M(d))=tᴺ_P(d)`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.transition_one`: `tᴺ_M(1)=1`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.transition_injective`: Each transition on quotient cocycles is injective.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.transition.test_one`: The identity quotient cocycle maps to the identity cocycle.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.transition.test_value`: At the class of each `g∈G`, the underlying value is exactly `d([g]_N)`. Reversing the subgroup inclusion or forgetting the fixed coefficient target fails this interface.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.transition.test_identity`: The self-transition fixes every cocycle, including nonidentity ones.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed pp. 5–7, continuous cocycle and gauge definitions; [Native nonabelian H¹](#native-nonabelian-h1), `Cocycle.map` and `Cocycle.map_map`, specialized to the quotient projections; the displayed proof is an elementary deduction.
