<a id="nc-3-h1-inflation"></a>

**Inflation of nonabelian cohomology classes.** Construct the pointed-set map `inflate_N:H¹(G/N,U^N)→H¹(G,U)` by sending the class of d to the class of the inflated cocycle `g↦d([g])` included in U. It descends the cocycle inflation through the gauge-orbit quotients and sends the base point to the base point.

Standing hypotheses (H14).

Lift the cocycle-to-class function through the orbit quotient. If the relation says `d=x·e`, equivariance and the inverse gauge element show that their inflated classes agree; the relation has this argument orientation. The representative formula is the quotient-lift computation. The proved identity-cocycle inflation theorem gives preservation of the distinguished point. Reflection of the distinguished point follows from the separately proved same-N injectivity result and point preservation. No group structure, additive law, image=fibre assertion or colimit is included in the construction.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.inflate_mk`: At the class of d, `H¹` inflation is the class of cocycle inflation.
- <a id="nc-3-h1-inflation-one"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.inflate_one` (*Inflation preserves the distinguished cohomology class*): Inflation sends the distinguished class of `H¹(G/N,U^N)` to the distinguished class of `H¹(G,U)`. *Proof.* Represent the distinguished class by the identity cocycle. Use the inflation representative API and [Trivial cocycle under inflation](#nc-3-quotient-cocycle-inflation-one), then identify the resulting identity-cocycle class with the distinguished point by definition. Source: [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed pp. 5–7, continuous cocycle/gauge definitions; authored library-based inflation–restriction deduction.
- <a id="nc-3-h1-inflation-injective"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.inflate_injective` (*Injectivity of nonabelian inflation*): For this fixed normal subgroup N, `inflate_N:H¹(G/N,U^N)→H¹(G,U)` is injective. Equality of inflated classes implies equality of source classes at the same N. *Proof.* Apply quotient induction to representatives d,e of the two source classes. The representative computation is definitional. The proved class equality criterion gives a global gauge witness for the inflated cocycles. Same-N gauge reflection gives a genuine `U^N` witness between d,e, and the same class criterion identifies their source classes. Uses [Same-subgroup reflection of gauge witnesses](#nc-3-quotient-inflation-gauge-reflection).
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.inflate_eq_one_iff`: For `a∈H¹(G/N,U^N)`, `inflate_N(a)=1` if and only if `a=1`. This reflects the neutral point; it does not assert image=neutral restriction fibre.
- <a id="nc-3-gauge-witness-fixed"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.gauge_witness_fixed` (*A same-stage gauge witness is already invariant*): Let c,d be continuous cocycles both identically 1 on N. If `d(g)=x c(g)(g•x)⁻¹` for a fixed `x∈U` and every g, then `n•x=x` for every `n∈N`. No refinement of N is needed, and no normality, discreteness or compactness is required for this pointwise assertion. This is the witness lemma for same-stage `H¹` inflation injectivity; it does not by itself construct inflation or prove quotient pointed-set injectivity. Under (H12). *Proof.* Evaluate the gauge equation `at n∈N`. It becomes `1=x(n•x)⁻¹`. Group cancellation forces `n•x=x`. The inverse/gauge factor order is retained. Source: [Native nonabelian H¹](#native-nonabelian-h1), `infl` and `infl_mk`; the displayed proof is an elementary deduction. Uses [Continuous 1-cocycles and invariants with nonabelian coefficients](#nc-3-continuous-cocycles).

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.inflate.test_one`: Inflation of the source distinguished point is the target distinguished point.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.inflate.test_gauge`: For any quotient cocycle d and any `x∈U^N`, inflation of the class of `x·d` equals inflation of the class of d.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.inflate.test_neutral_reflection`: For every source class a, `inflate_N(a)=1` if and only if `a=1`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.inflate.test_nonabelian_transposition`: Let `G=S₂` and `U=S₃` with discrete topologies and trivial G-action, `N={1}`, and c the homomorphism sending the nonidentity element of `S₂` to the transposition(01) of `S₃`. If d is the quotient descent of c, then `inflate_N([d])≠1`. Thus the construction cannot be a constant-basepoint map; the coefficient group is genuinely noncommutative.
- The map is independent of the quotient cocycle representative. The concrete discrete `S₂→S₃` transposition class `at N={1}` has nonneutral inflation; a constant-basepoint map fails the test.
- Inflation reflects the neutral point. Neither replacing N by a refinement nor injectivity of the underlying cocycle map alone proves this assertion.
- The equality concerns the gauge-orbit classes and the same normal subgroup.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.gauge_witness_fixed.test_full_subgroup`: If1=x(g•x)⁻¹ for every g, then x is a member of FixedPoints.subgroup G U, even for nonabelian U.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed p. 6, continuous cocycle and gauge-orbit definitions; derived fixed-normal-subgroup argument.

<a id="nc-3-h1-transition"></a>

**Reverse-inclusion transition on nonabelian cohomology.** For `M≤N`, construct the pointed map `tᴺ_M:H¹(G/N,U^N)→H¹(G/M,U^M)` sending [d] to `[tᴺ_M(d)]`. These are gauge-orbit sets; no group law on `H¹` is imposed.

Standing hypotheses (H15).

Lift the cocycle transition through the orbit quotient. For gauge-equivalent representatives, their M-level images have equal inflations by [Inflation commutes with cocycle transition](#nc-3-cocycle-transition-inflation) and well-defined N-level inflation. Same-M `H¹` inflation injectivity makes the images equal. The representative formula is definitional. Identity, composition and injectivity follow by applying same-subgroup inflation injectivity. Basepoint preservation uses inflation of the identity class.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.transition_mk`: `tᴺ_M([d])=[tᴺ_M(d)]`.
- <a id="nc-3-h1-transition-inflation"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.inflate_transition` (*Inflation commutes with cohomology transition*): For `M≤N` and every class a, `inflate_M(tᴺ_M(a))=inflate_N(a)`. *Proof.* Choose a representative and apply the cocycle identity, then take its gauge class.
- <a id="nc-3-h1-transition-identity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.transition_refl` (*Identity law for quotient cohomology transition*): For every class a at N, `tᴺ_N(a)=a`. *Proof.* Both classes have the same N-level inflation by the proved compatibility. Apply its injectivity. Uses [Inflation commutes with cohomology transition](#nc-3-h1-transition-inflation).
- <a id="nc-3-h1-transition-composition"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.transition_trans` (*Composition law for quotient cohomology transition*): For `P≤M≤N`, `tᴹ_P(tᴺ_M(a))=tᴺ_P(a)`. *Proof.* Inflate both sides from P. Use the proved compatibility twice on the left and once on the right, then same-P injectivity. Uses [Inflation commutes with cohomology transition](#nc-3-h1-transition-inflation).
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.transition_one`: The distinguished class maps to the distinguished class.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.transition_injective`: Each pointed-set transition is injective.
- <a id="nc-3-quotient-fixed-action-continuity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.quotientFixedContinuousSMul` (*Joint continuity of the fixed-subgroup quotient action*): The action `(G/N) × U^N → U^N`, `([g],u) ↦ g•u`, is jointly continuous. Thus the fixed subgroup with its induced topology has ContinuousSMul for `G/N`, without a separate [Equivariant subgroup coset action](#nc-3-quotient-action) continuity input. Hypotheses: G is a group with a topology and separately continuous multiplication; in particular every topological group satisfies this assumption. U is a group with a topology and a jointly continuous G-action by group automorphisms. N is an arbitrary normal subgroup. Use the quotient topology on `G/N` and the topology and quotient action on the fixed `subgroup U^N`. No compactness, open/closed N, discrete/finite coefficients or commutativity is assumed. *Proof.* `QuotientGroup.isOpenQuotientMap_mk` and IsOpenQuotientMap.id, followed by IsOpenQuotientMap.prodMap, provide the open quotient map `G × U^N → (G/N) × U^N`. Apply `IsOpenQuotientMap.continuous_comp_iff`. The native [Equivariant subgroup coset action](#nc-3-quotient-action) coercion law identifies the lifted action included in U with `(g,u) ↦ g•u`. Use `continuous_induced_rng` for the subgroup topology. Continuous.smul applied to `continuous_fst` and `continuous_subtype_val` composed with `continuous_snd` proves continuity of this ambient map in both arguments. Source: [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed pp. 5–7, continuous cocycle/gauge definitions; authored library-based inflation–restriction deduction.

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.transition.test_one`: `tᴺ_M(1)=1`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.transition.test_gauge`: For every `x∈U^N` and d, transitioning `[x·d]` gives `[tᴺ_M(d)]`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.transition.test_nonneutral`: For every `a≠1`, `tᴺ_M(a)≠1`. The `S₂→S₃` transposition class supplies a nonneutral input; collapsing classes to the basepoint fails.

- No topology on U is changed to the discrete topology; continuity is joint, not just fixed-vector continuity.

The two transitioned classes at K have equal inflations by [Inflation commutes with cohomology transition](#nc-3-h1-transition-inflation), so they are equal by same-K inflation injectivity. The criterion constructs the universal map using a finite-level representative; common refinement proves independence and uniqueness. This proves universality of the named maps, not merely existence of an abstract bijection.

**Positive central defect.** For topological groups G,B with continuous G-action by automorphisms and a function `b:G→B` define `D_b(g,h)=b(g)·g(b(h))·b(gh)−1` in that order. It is continuous if b is continuous. If `q:B→C` is an equivariant homomorphism and `q∘b` is a cocycle then `D_b` takes values in `ker(q)`.

G,B topological groups continuous automorphism action on B b continuous when asserting continuity.

Form the displayed product using multiplication, inverse, action and group multiplication. Apply q, the cocycle law and cancellation to prove the kernel assertion. For cocycle tests use `D=1` iff the multiplicative cocycle law.

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.NC3.positiveDefect_eq_one_iff`: D is identically one iff b is a cocycle.

### 0.20 Connecting cocycles of invariant coset lifts
<a id="nc-3-connecting-cocycle"></a>

**Connecting cocycle of an invariant coset lift.** For `b ∈ B` with `b⁻¹(g•b) ∈ i(A)` for every `g ∈ G`, construct the continuous A-valued cocycle `c_b` uniquely specified by `i(c_b(g)) = b⁻¹(g•b)`. The membership condition expresses that the left coset `b i(A)` is G-invariant. No normality of `i(A)`, quotient group structure or continuous quotient section is assumed.

Standing hypotheses (H17).

For each g choose the unique preimage in A of `b⁻¹(g•b)`, using membership and injectivity of i. The composite with i is continuous by continuity of the action at the fixed b and multiplication by `b⁻¹`. Apply `Topology.IsEmbedding.continuous_iff` to the embedding underlying i, obtaining continuity into A; pointwise choices need no continuous section. Apply i to `c_b(gh)` and `c_b(g)(g•c_b(h))`; equivariance and cancellation give the same element `b⁻¹((gh)•b)`. Injectivity proves the cocycle identity. Package the function and both properties in the continuous `Z¹` carrier.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.connectingCocycle_apply`: For every g, `i(c_b(g)) = b⁻¹(g•b)`. This is the content of [Image of the connecting cocycle](#nc-3-connecting-cocycle-image).
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.connectingCocycle_unique`: Every A-valued continuous cocycle c with `i(c(g)) = b⁻¹(g•b)` for all g equals `c_b`, independent of the proof of membership or pointwise preimage choices.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.connectingCocycle_eq_one_of_fixed`: If b is G-fixed, `c_b` is the constant identity cocycle.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.connecting_fixed_lift`: A G-fixed lift b gives `c_b = 1` for every equivariant closed embedding i.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.connecting_identity_embedding`: For i the identity embedding of B and arbitrary b, `c_b =` coboundary(b⁻¹), with coboundary(u)(g)=u(g•u)⁻¹.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.connecting_proof_independence`: Two proofs that `b⁻¹(g•b)` lies in `i(A)` yield equal cocycles for the same b.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.connecting_right_lift`: Whenever b and `b i(a)` satisfy membership, their connecting `H¹` classes agree, although their cocycles differ by the gauge `a⁻¹`.
- Works for nonnormal closed G-stable subgroups and arbitrary continuous automorphism actions.
- The formula uses `b⁻¹(g•b)`; reversing the factors is invalid for noncommutative B.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed pp. 5–6 (cocycle and orbit conventions), p. 9 (subgroup exactness).

<a id="nc-3-connecting-change-lift"></a>

**Change of lift for a connecting cocycle.** For a `∈ A` and an admissible b, `b i(a)` is also admissible and `c_{b i(a)} = a⁻¹•c_b` under the cocycle action `(u•c)(g)=u c(g)(g•u)⁻¹`. Consequently the `H¹` class depends only on the left coset `b i(A)`.

Standing hypotheses (H17).

Expand `(b i(a))⁻¹(g•(b i(a)))` as `i(a⁻¹) b⁻¹(g•b) i(g•a)`; subgroup closure proves membership. Apply [Image of the connecting cocycle](#nc-3-connecting-cocycle-image) to both lifts, expand the gauge action and use injectivity pointwise. This proves the cocycle equality. The `H¹` orbit quotient identifies cocycles in the same A-orbit. No normality is used.

**Checks.**

- The gauge is `a⁻¹`, not a; a nonabelian finite test distinguishes them.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed pp. 5–6 (cocycle and orbit conventions), p. 9 (subgroup exactness).

Use [Image of the connecting cocycle](#nc-3-connecting-cocycle-image); [Nonabelian first cohomology as a pointed set](#nc-3-nonabelian-h1).

<a id="nc-3-connecting-fixed-orbits"></a>

**Fibres of the connecting class.** Suppose `c,c′ ∈ Z¹(G,A)` and `b,b′ ∈ B` satisfy `i(c(g))=b⁻¹(g•b)` and `i(c′(g))=b′⁻¹(g•b′)` for all g. Then `[c]=[c′]` if and only if there exist a G-fixed `t ∈ B` and a `∈ A` such that `b′ = t b i(a)`. Thus equal connecting classes correspond exactly to the left `B^G`-orbits of invariant left cosets.

Standing hypotheses (H17).

By the orbit quotient `[c]=[c′]` iff `c′=a⁻¹•c` for some a `∈ A` (invert the gauge variable in the inherited equality characterisation). Apply i and the displayed cocycle formulas. Direct cancellation shows `t=b′ i(a)⁻¹ b⁻¹` is G-fixed; rearrange to `b′=t b i(a)`. Conversely fixedness of t and `b′=t b i(a)` give `i(c′(g))=i(a⁻¹ c(g)(g•a))`; injectivity and cocycle extensionality give the gauge equality and hence equal classes.

**Checks.**

- No commutativity or normality is assumed. The `B^G` action is on the left, while lift changes multiply by `i(a)` on the right.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed pp. 5–6 (cocycle and orbit conventions), p. 9 (subgroup exactness).

Use [Nonabelian first cohomology as a pointed set](#nc-3-nonabelian-h1); [Continuous 1-cocycles and invariants with nonabelian coefficients](#nc-3-continuous-cocycles).

### 0.21 Gauge transport between inner twists
<a id="nc-3-gauge-equivalence"></a>

**Continuous gauge transport between inner twists.** For `c∈Z¹(G,U)` and `b∈U`, construct the group equivalence `e_c,b:Twist(c)≃*Twist(b•c)` whose underlying map is `x↦b j_c(x)b⁻¹`. Its inverse is conjugation by `b⁻¹`; the following API proves continuity and G-equivariance.

Standing hypotheses (H8).

Reuse MulAut.conj b on the twist synonyms; their group structures and topologies are the inherited ones on U. No new general conjugation or topological-group carrier is introduced.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-gauge-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.gaugeEquiv_apply` (*Gauge transport value*): For `x∈Twist(c)`, `j_(b•c)(e_c,b(x))=b j_c(x)b⁻¹`. *Proof.* Evaluate the conjugation map and the inherited underlying identifications.
- <a id="nc-3-gauge-inverse-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.gaugeEquiv_symm_apply` (*Inverse gauge transport value*): For `y∈Twist(b•c)`, `j_c(e_c,b⁻¹(y))=b⁻¹ j_(b•c)(y)b`, where `e_c,b⁻¹` denotes the inverse equivalence, not transport to an unspecified twist. *Proof.* Evaluate the inverse function of the same MulAut.conj equivalence.
- <a id="nc-3-gauge-continuity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.gaugeEquiv_continuous` (*Continuity of gauge transport*): The monoid homomorphism underlying `e_c,b` is continuous for the topologies. *Proof.* Use continuity of multiplication with the two constant factors `b,b⁻¹` and the identity function. Uses [Gauge transport value](#nc-3-gauge-value).
- <a id="nc-3-gauge-inverse-continuity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.gaugeEquiv_symm_continuous` (*Continuity of inverse gauge transport*): The inverse function of `e_c,b` is continuous for the topologies. Thus the group equivalence is a homeomorphism as well as an algebraic isomorphism. *Proof.* Use the explicit inverse formula and continuity of multiplication by the constants `b⁻¹` and b. Uses [Inverse gauge transport value](#nc-3-gauge-inverse-value).
- <a id="nc-3-gauge-equivariance"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.gaugeEquiv_smul` (*Equivariance of gauge transport*): For every `g∈G` and `x∈Twist(c)`, `e_c,b(g⋆_c x)=g⋆_(b•c)e_c,b(x)`. Both sides use their actual, generally different, inner actions. *Proof.* Expand both inner actions and `(b•c)(g)=b c(g)g(b)⁻¹`. Distribute g over products/inverses, then cancel adjacent inverse pairs without commuting factors. Uses [Gauge transport value](#nc-3-gauge-value); [Twisting by a cocycle](#nc-3-twisting); [Continuous 1-cocycles and invariants with nonabelian coefficients](#nc-3-continuous-cocycles).
- <a id="nc-3-gauge-identity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.gaugeEquiv_one` (*Identity gauge transport*): Under the underlying identifications, `e_c,1` is the identity: `j_(1•c)(e_c,1(x))=j_c(x)`. *Proof.* Evaluate the conjugation formula at the group identity. Uses [Gauge transport value](#nc-3-gauge-value).
- <a id="nc-3-gauge-composition"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.gaugeEquiv_comp` (*Ordered composition of gauge transports*): For `a,b∈U` and `x∈Twist(c)`, `j_(a•(b•c))(e_(b•c),a(e_c,b(x)))=j_((ab)•c)(e_c,ab(x))`. The resulting gauge element is ab; the cocycle targets agree by the gauge action law. *Proof.* Expand both conjugations and cancel the middle `b⁻¹a⁻¹` against the inverse of ab in the prescribed order. Compare through the underlying identifications to avoid an implicit choice of dependent transport. Uses [Gauge transport value](#nc-3-gauge-value); [Continuous 1-cocycles and invariants with nonabelian coefficients](#nc-3-continuous-cocycles).
- <a id="nc-3-gauge-cocycle-square"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.twistEquiv_gaugeMap` (*Cocycle translation under gauge transport*): For `z∈Z¹(G,Twist(c))`, `τ_(b•c)((e_c,b)_*z)=b•τ_c(z)`, where the pushforward is the continuous equivariant coefficient map on cocycles. This is equality of cocycles, with the ordered products unchanged. *Proof.* Apply cocycle extensionality; expand the coefficient map, `τ` and the gauge formula. The adjacent `b⁻¹b` cancels, leaving `b(j_c(z(g))c(g))g(b)⁻¹`. Uses [Equivariance of gauge transport](#nc-3-gauge-equivariance); [Continuity of gauge transport](#nc-3-gauge-continuity); [Coefficient map on continuous cocycles](#nc-3-coefficient-cocycle-map); [Value of the twisting equivalence](#nc-3-twist-cocycle-value); [Continuous 1-cocycles and invariants with nonabelian coefficients](#nc-3-continuous-cocycles).
- <a id="nc-3-gauge-h1-square"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistEquiv_gaugeMap` (*Cohomology translation under gauge transport*): For every `a∈H¹(G,Twist(c))`, `T_(b•c)((e_c,b)_*a)=T_c(a)`, with the pushforward supplied by the coefficient map on `H¹`. *Proof.* Choose a cocycle representative, apply the cocycle square and use that a gauge translate has the same original `H¹` class. Uses [Cocycle translation under gauge transport](#nc-3-gauge-cocycle-square); [Coefficient map on nonabelian cohomology](#nc-3-coefficient-h1-map); [Twisting on a `H¹` representative](#nc-3-twist-h1-representative); [Gauge invariance of the cohomology class](#nc-3-h1-gauge-class).

**Checks.**

- `Twist.gaugeEquiv.test_inverse`: For any c,b,x, the inverse of `e_c,b` applied to `e_c,b(x)` is x.
- `Twist.gaugeEquiv.test_identity`: For `b=1`, gauge transport is the identity under the underlying group identifications.
- `Twist.gaugeEquiv.test_noncommutative_direction`: Give `S₂` and `S₃` discrete topologies and the trivial original S₂-action on `S₃`. Let c send the nonidentity element to (01), and let `b=(01)(12)`. Then `e_c,b` sends (01) to (12), whereas `b⁻¹(01)b` is not (12). This rejects conjugation in the reverse direction.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, continuous cocycle/gauge definitions and Proposition 1 and its proof, printed pp. 5–7; final representative-change sentence on p. 7.

Use [Underlying group of a cocycle twist](#nc-3-twist-underlying-group); `MulAut.conj`.

### 0.22 The kernel of an inclusion on H¹
<a id="nc-3-exact-sequence"></a>

**Kernel of inclusion in nonabelian cohomology.** For an equivariant closed embedding `i:A → B` of topological G-groups and `x ∈ H¹(G,A)`, `i_*(x)=1` if and only if there exist `b ∈ B` and `c ∈ Z¹(G,A)` such that `x=[c]` and `i(c(g))=b⁻¹(g•b)` for every g. Equivalently, the classes killed by inclusion are exactly the connecting classes of invariant left cosets. Normality and a continuous quotient section are not required.

Standing hypotheses (H17).

Represent x by c. By the `H¹` basepoint characterisation, `i_*x=1` iff `i(c(g))=u(g•u)⁻¹` for one `u ∈ B` and all g. Put `b=u⁻¹` to obtain the displayed formula. Conversely that formula makes the image cocycle the B-coboundary of `b⁻¹`, so its class is the basepoint. The formula supplies membership in `i(A)` for each g and therefore an admissible [Connecting cocycle of an invariant coset lift](#nc-3-connecting-cocycle) input. Its image identity and injectivity identify it with c. Change of lift and the separate fixed-orbit theorem give the coset interpretation. For a nonneutral coefficient-map fibre, [Translation of the neutral coefficient fibre](#nc-3-twist-neutral-fibre-equivalence) replaces the fibre over `[f∘c]` by the neutral fibre of the twisted coefficient map. Geometric local-condition identifications use the realization targets of Layer 4. For cohomologous representatives use H1.changeRepresentative, its concrete gauge realization and composition law. The source and coefficient naturality squares are supplied.

**Checks.**

- For identity inclusion `A=B`, the induced map on `H¹` is identity and its neutral fibre contains only the base point.
- Kim's crystalline condition: for `U_n(R) ≤ U_n(B_cr ⊗ R)`, the image of `H⁰(G_v, U_n(B_cr ⊗ R)/U_n(R)) → H¹(G_v, U_n(R))` is the set of crystalline torsors (Kim 2009, §2, pp. 118–119); this is (a) for a subgroup that is not normal.
- Exactness is of pointed sets: two elements of `H¹(G, A)` with the same image in `H¹(G, B)` need not differ by an element of `(B/A)^G` unless one of them is the base point; the fibres over other points are described after twisting ([Twisting by a cocycle](#nc-3-twisting)).

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, p. 9; [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §2, pp. 118–119.

Use [Nonabelian first cohomology as a pointed set](#nc-3-nonabelian-h1); [Functoriality of nonabelian `H⁰` and `H¹`](#nc-3-functoriality); [Image of the connecting cocycle](#nc-3-connecting-cocycle-image); [Change of lift for a connecting cocycle](#nc-3-connecting-change-lift); [Fibres of the connecting class](#nc-3-connecting-fixed-orbits); [Neutral fibre after coefficient twisting and repointing](#nc-3-twist-coefficient-repointed-fibre); [Neutral class under representative comparison](#nc-3-representative-neutral); [Representative comparison equals gauge pushforward](#nc-3-representative-gauge); [Composition of representative comparisons](#nc-3-representative-composition).

### 0.23 Kernel cocycle lifts and exact images
<a id="nc-3-mapped-inverse-gauge-normalization"></a>

**Inverse gauge after a lifted coboundary.** For a continuous equivariant coefficient homomorphism `f:U→V`, a continuous cocycle d, and `x∈U` with `f(d(g))=f(x)(g•f(x))⁻¹` for all g, mapping the inverse gauge `x⁻¹•d` gives the neutral cocycle.

Standing hypotheses (H18).

Apply equivariance of the cocycle map to the inverse gauge. Evaluate at g, use `f(x⁻¹)=f(x)⁻¹` and the given ordered coboundary formula. Cancellation gives the identity without commuting any factors.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, pp. 5–9, continuous cocycle and ordered gauge definitions, coefficient functor and subgroup exactness paragraph.

Use [Coefficient map on continuous cocycles](#nc-3-coefficient-cocycle-map); [Gauge compatibility of coefficient cocycle maps](#nc-3-coefficient-cocycle-gauge).
<a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-cocycle-lift"></a>

**Cocycle valued in the twisted kernel.** Given `d∈Z¹(G,Twist(c))` and `F_c(d(g))=1` for every g, construct its unique value-preserving cocycle `k∈Z¹(G,K_c)`, where `F_c=Twist.map(c,f)`, `K_c=ker(F_c)`, and `K_c` has its restricted inner action and subspace topology.

Standing hypotheses (H18).

Take the subtype-valued function `g↦⟨d(g),F_c(d(g))=1⟩`. `Continuous.subtype_mk` supplies continuity into the subspace topology. Transfer the cocycle identity through the injective subtype inclusion and the already specified restricted action.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-cocycle-lift-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.twistedKernelLift_apply` (*Value of the kernel cocycle lift*): For every g, the underlying value of twistedKernelLift(c,f,d) at g is exactly `d(g)`. *Proof.* Unfold the subtype-valued lift and project its underlying value.
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-cocycle-lift-inclusion"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.twistedKernelLift_inclusion` (*Kernel lift followed by the coefficient inclusion*): Mapping twistedKernelLift(c,f,d) by the `K_c→Twist(c)` inclusion returns the exact cocycle d. *Proof.* Use continuous-cocycle extensionality. Each value is `d(g)` by the value formula; the inclusion is the continuous subtype inclusion. Uses [Value of the kernel cocycle lift](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-cocycle-lift-value); [Underlying value of the restricted kernel action](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-action-value).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-cocycle-lift-neutral"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.twistedKernelLift_one` (*Neutral kernel cocycle lift*): The kernel lift of the neutral cocycle with its canonical identity-value witness is the neutral cocycle in `K_c`. *Proof.* Use cocycle extensionality and equality of the subtype values.
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-cocycle-lift-gauge"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.twistedKernelLift_gauge` (*Kernel-valued gauges of the cocycle lift*): For `x∈K_c`, whenever d and x.val•d have their specified pointwise kernel witnesses, lifting x.val•d gives x•twistedKernelLift(c,f,d) as `K_c`-valued continuous cocycles. *Proof.* Use cocycle extensionality and the injective subtype inclusion. The two ordered gauge expressions have identical underlying values, with the restricted inner action. Uses [Joint continuity on the twisted kernel](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-action-continuity).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-cocycle-lift-detection"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.twistedKernelLift_injective` (*Equality detected by the kernel cocycle lift*): For two cocycles d,e with specified pointwise kernel witnesses, their `K_c`-valued lifts agree if and only if `d=e`. This is equality of cocycles, not injectivity on `H¹`. *Proof.* Project equality at each g through the subtype inclusion; conversely substitute equal cocycles and use proof irrelevance for membership witnesses. Uses [Value of the kernel cocycle lift](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-cocycle-lift-value).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-h1-quotient-converse"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.exists_twistedKernelInclusion_of_quotient_eq_one` (*Lift from the quotient neutral fibre*): Every `a∈H¹(G,Twist(c))` killed by the quotient map `Twist(c)→Twist(c)/K_c` lies in the image of `H¹(G,K_c)→H¹(G,Twist(c))`. This needs neither surjectivity nor a quotient-map hypothesis on f. *Proof.* Choose a continuous representative d and a quotient gauge witness y to the neutrality of its mapped class. Lift the single y using quotient-projection surjectivity. Normalize d by the inverse gauge of that lift. `QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff` identifies each normalized value with `K_c`. Construct its continuous kernel cocycle with twistedKernelLift. The inclusion returns the normalized cocycle, whose class is [d] by gauge invariance. No continuous lifting function is chosen. Uses [Neutral class as a coboundary](#nc-3-h1-neutral-criterion); [Gauge invariance of the cohomology class](#nc-3-h1-gauge-class); [Inverse gauge after a lifted coboundary](#nc-3-mapped-inverse-gauge-normalization); [Kernel lift followed by the coefficient inclusion](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-cocycle-lift-inclusion); [Kernel inclusion on cocycle representatives](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-h1-representative); [Projection of continuous twisted cocycles](#nc-3-twisted-quotient-cocycle-map); [Quotient `H¹` on representatives](#nc-3-twisted-quotient-h1-representative); [Joint continuity of the descended inner action](#nc-3-twisted-quotient-action-continuity).

**Checks.**

- `Z1.twistedKernelLift.test_value`: The underlying lifted value at any g is exactly `d(g)`.
- `Z1.twistedKernelLift.test_inclusion`: The inclusion maps the lifted kernel cocycle to d.
- `Z1.twistedKernelLift.test_neutral`: The canonical lift of the identity cocycle is the identity cocycle of `K_c`.
- `Z1.twistedKernelLift.test_detection`: Equality of two kernel lifts is equivalent to equality of the original cocycles, with their specified kernel witnesses.
- `Z1.twistedKernelLift.test_gauge`: A kernel-valued gauge agrees before and after the cocycle lift.
- `Z1.twistedKernelLift.test_non_kernel_rejected`: If `F_c(d(g))≠1 at` one g, no `K_c`-valued cocycle can have every underlying value equal to d.
- `Z1.kernelImage.test_inverse_gauge_order`: For G=ConjAct(S₃), `U=S₃` with the conjugation action and discrete topologies, `x=(01)(12)` and `d=x•1`, the inverse gauge `x⁻¹•d` equals 1, whereas `x•d` does not equal 1.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, pp. 5–9, continuous cocycle and ordered gauge definitions, coefficient functor and subgroup exactness paragraph.

Use [Continuous 1-cocycles and invariants with nonabelian coefficients](#nc-3-continuous-cocycles); [Continuous automorphism action on the twisted kernel](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-action); [Coefficient map on continuous cocycles](#nc-3-coefficient-cocycle-map); `Continuous.subtype_mk`.

<a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-equivalence"></a>

**Underlying group comparison for twisted kernels.** Construct `K_c≃*ker(f)` by `x↦j_c(x)`, with inverse `j_c⁻¹` on the same subgroup. This compares underlying groups and subspace topologies, not their G-actions.

Standing hypotheses (H10).

Apply kernel membership in each direction; inherited multiplication and both inverse laws are definitionally those of U. Do not invent another kernel carrier.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-equivalence-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.kernelEquiv_value` (*Value of the kernel comparison*): The underlying U-value of kernelEquiv(x) is `j_c(x)`. *Proof.* Unfold the subtype map; its value is the original-group identification.
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-equivalence-continuous"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.kernelEquiv_continuous` (*Continuity of the kernel comparison*): The map `K_c→ker(f)` underlying kernelEquiv is continuous for the subgroup topologies. *Proof.* Use continuity of the subtype projection and lift into the target subtype; `Twist(c)` has exactly the topology of U.
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-equivalence-inverse-continuous"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.kernelEquiv_symm_continuous` (*Continuity of the inverse kernel comparison*): The inverse `ker(f)→K_c` is continuous for the subgroup topologies. *Proof.* Use the same subtype continuity argument in the inverse direction.

**Checks.**

- `Twist.kernelEquiv.test_inverse`: The kernel comparison and its inverse cancel on every kernel element.
- `Twist.kernelEquiv.test_identity_kernel`: For the identity coefficient homomorphism, the underlying value of every element of the twisted kernel is 1.
- `Twist.kernelEquiv.test_constant_kernel`: For the constant identity-valued coefficient map, every x in `Twist(c)` lies in its kernel and kernelEquiv retains the value `j_c(x)`.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, continuous cocycle/gauge definitions, Proposition 1 and its proof, coefficient functor and central-quotient paragraph; pp. 5–7.

Use [Kernel membership for a twisted map](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-membership); [Underlying group of a cocycle twist](#nc-3-twist-underlying-group).

### 0.24 Named kernels
<a id="nc-3-named-kernel-equivalence"></a>

**Named subgroup identified with the twisted kernel.** Construct the multiplicative equivalence `e:S≃K_c`, `K_c=ker(F_c)`, by the unchanged underlying value, where `F_c:Twist(c)→Twist(f∘c)` is the equivariant coefficient map. The two subgroups carry their subspace topologies.

Standing hypotheses (H19).

Use the exact membership witness hS to form the two subtype maps. Their values are unchanged, so the inverse and multiplication identities hold by subtype equality.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-named-kernel-equivalence-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.namedKernelEquiv_apply` (*Underlying value of the named kernel identification*): For `x∈S`, applying e then the underlying twist identification gives exactly x.val. *Proof.* Evaluate the forward subtype map.
- <a id="nc-3-named-kernel-equivalence-inverse-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.namedKernelEquiv_symm_apply` (*Underlying value of the inverse identification*): For `k∈K_c`, the value of `e⁻¹(k)` is the original underlying value of k. *Proof.* Evaluate the inverse subtype map.
- <a id="nc-3-named-kernel-equivalence-continuity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.namedKernelEquiv_continuous` (*Continuity of the named kernel identification*): The forward map `e:S→K_c` is continuous in the induced topologies. *Proof.* Restrict the continuous subtype inclusion using the exact pointwise kernel witness.
- <a id="nc-3-named-kernel-equivalence-inverse-continuity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.namedKernelEquiv_symm_continuous` (*Continuity of the inverse kernel identification*): The inverse map `e⁻¹:K_c→S` is continuous in the induced topologies. *Proof.* Restrict the continuous subtype inclusion in the other direction using hS.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.namedKernelEquiv.test_constant_top`: For the constant identity-valued homomorphism `f:U→V`, take `S=⊤` and the canonical membership witness; the kernel identification sends every `x∈U` to a twisted-kernel element with exactly underlying value x.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.namedKernelEquiv.test_identity_bot`: For the identity homomorphism `U→U`, take `S=⊥`; every identified twisted-kernel value is 1.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.namedKernelEquiv.test_wrong_subgroup_rejected`: If some `x∈S` satisfies `f(x)≠1`, then the exact kernel-membership witness `∀y,y∈S` iff `f(y)=1` is impossible.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1 continuous cocycle/gauge conventions and subgroup exactness paragraph, printed pp. 5–9.

Use [Underlying group comparison for twisted kernels](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-equivalence); [Coefficient homomorphism between inner twists](#nc-3-twist-coefficient-map); [Underlying group of a cocycle twist](#nc-3-twist-underlying-group); `MulEquiv`; `Subgroup.subtype`.
<a id="nc-3-named-kernel-inner-action"></a>

**Inner action on a named coefficient kernel.** Transport the restricted G-action on `K_c` through e to obtain a MulDistribMulAction G S. Its value is `c(g)(g•x)c(g)⁻¹` in U.

Standing hypotheses (H20).

Define `g•x=e⁻¹(g•e(x))`. Check identity, composition, identity element and multiplication using the multiplicative equivalence and restricted kernel action.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-named-kernel-inner-action-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.namedKernelAction_value` (*Conjugated value of the named kernel action*): For `g∈G` and `x∈S`, the underlying value of the transported action is c(g)(g•x.val)c(g)⁻¹, in this order. *Proof.* Evaluate the transport and the inherited restricted inner action; no commuting of factors. Uses [Underlying value of the restricted kernel action](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-action-value).
- <a id="nc-3-named-kernel-equivalence-equivariance"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.namedKernelEquiv_smul` (*Equivariance of the kernel identification*): For the transported S-action and restricted `K_c`-action, `e(g•x)=g•e(x)`. *Proof.* Cancel e with its inverse in the transported action formula.
- <a id="nc-3-named-kernel-inner-action-continuity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.namedKernelContinuousSMul` (*Joint continuity on the named kernel*): The transported G-action on S is jointly continuous for the subspace topology. *Proof.* Compose c with the first projection, multiply with the continuous original action and inverse c-value, then restrict into S using pointwise membership. Uses [Conjugated value of the named kernel action](#nc-3-named-kernel-inner-action-value).

### 0.25 Exactness for a normal coefficient subgroup
<a id="nc-3-normal-h1-kernel"></a>

**Exactness for a normal coefficient subgroup.** Let `π:B → C` be a continuous open surjective equivariant homomorphism to a topological G-group C, with `ker π=i(A)`. For `y ∈ H¹(G,B)`, `π_*(y)=1` if and only if y lies in the image of `i_*:H¹(G,A) → H¹(G,B)`. No continuous section of `π` is required.

G, A and B are groups with topologies; A and B are topological groups. Continuous actions of G on A and B by automorphisms; `i:A → B` is a closed embedding and group homomorphism commuting with G. C is a topological group with continuous G-action by automorphisms; `π` is equivariant, continuous, open, surjective and has kernel `i(A)`.

Choose a continuous cocycle d representing y. Triviality of `π_*y` supplies `x ∈ C` with `π(d(g))=x(g•x)⁻¹`. Lift the single element x to `b ∈ B` by surjectivity; the gauge `b⁻¹•d` takes values in `ker π=i(A)`. Restrict it to A using unique pointwise preimages, and transfer continuity with the embedding `continuous_iff` theorem. The cocycle law follows by equivariance and injectivity. Its `H¹` class maps to y because it is a gauge transform of d. Conversely `π∘i=1`, so every class in the image is killed. Openness allows application to the canonical topological-group quotient; it is not used to lift a whole function. The twisted-kernel range targets give both directions for the quotient neutral fibre; for surjective f the mapped neutral fibre also equals the kernel-H¹ image. Translation gives the original fibre over `[f∘c]`. Only one constant gauge element is lifted; neither a continuous section nor a quotient-map assumption on f is needed for this mapped range equality. The named-native-kernel and abstract-embedded-kernel comparisons now transport these image criteria. For an abstract `i:A→U`, topological embedding and `range(i)=ker(f)` supply inverse continuity and uniqueness of each point preimage. These comparisons do not give unconditional `H¹` injectivity. The invariant-action and orbit targets classify the remaining ambiguity; the central `H²` construction uses the [Positive central defect](#nc-3-positive-defect) comparison, and geometric local conditions use the realization targets of Layer 4.

**Checks.**

- Canonical quotient by a closed normal subgroup is an instance; the `H⁰` connecting cocycle for a nonnormal subgroup does not require this theorem.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed pp. 5–6 (cocycle and orbit conventions), p. 9 (subgroup exactness).

### 0.27 Central extensions and the connecting map to H²
<a id="nc-3-central-extension"></a>

**Central extensions: the action of H¹(G, Z) and the connecting map to H².** Let `Z ≤ B` be a closed G-stable subgroup contained in the centre of B, and `C := B/Z`. (a) The abelian group `H¹(G, Z)` ([Comparison with abelian continuous cohomology](#nc-3-abelian-comparison)) acts on `H¹(G, B)` by `[z]·[c] := [g ↦ z(g)c(g)]`, and the fibres of `H¹(G, B) → H¹(G, C)` are exactly the orbits of this action. (b) Suppose the projection `B → C` has a continuous (set-theoretic) section s. Then there is a connecting map `δ² : H¹(G, C) → H²(G, Z)`, Tau Ceti's explicit continuous `H²` (`ContCohomology.H2` of Z written additively), sending the class of c̄ to the class of the 2-cocycle `(g, h) ↦ c(g)·(g•c(h))·c(gh)⁻¹` for the continuous lift `c = s ∘ c̄`; and the image of `H¹(G, B) → H¹(G, C)` is `δ²⁻¹(0)`. (c) If, for every `c ∈ Z¹(G, B)`, the group C twisted by the image of c ([Twisting by a cocycle](#nc-3-twisting)) has only the trivial G-invariant element, then the action in (a) is free, so each nonempty fibre is a principal homogeneous space of `H¹(G, Z)`. The convention in (b) is the positive defect matching Tau Ceti's additive `d¹`. Kim arXiv v1, printed p.5, defines dc(g,h)=c(gh)(g•c(h))⁻¹c(g)⁻¹, its inverse. Thus `δ²` here is the negative of Kim's printed connecting class under the additive identification of the central coefficient; their zero loci agree.

G is a topological group and B a topological group with an action of G by group automorphisms (MulDistribMulAction G B) such that the action map `G × B → B` is continuous (ContinuousSMul G B). Z closed, G-stable and central in B. For (b), a continuous section of `B → C` (for unipotent algebraic groups an algebraic splitting of the extension exists, as in Kim's proof). For (c), the stated vanishing of twisted invariants.

`(a) z·c` is a continuous cocycle because Z is central: `z(gh)c(gh) = z(g)(g•z(h))c(g)(g•c(h)) = (z(g)c(g))·g•(z(h)c(h))`. The action is compatible with twisted conjugation by B (central z commutes with u), so it descends to classes; it preserves the image in `H¹(G, C)`. Conversely if `[c₁]`, `[c₂]` have the same image, replace `c₂` by `u·c₂` so that the images in `Z¹(G, C)` agree (lift one element of C); then `z := c₁⁻¹c₂` is Z-valued, continuous and, Z being central, a cocycle. (b) For the lift `c = s ∘ c̄`, the defect `(g, h) ↦ c(g)(g•c(h))c(gh)⁻¹` lies in Z (its image in C is 1), is continuous, and satisfies the 2-cocycle identity in Z (a direct computation using centrality). Changing c̄ within its class or changing the lift by a Z-valued continuous 1-cochain changes the defect by a 2-coboundary of a continuous cochain, so `δ²` is well defined into `Z²/B²` with Tau Ceti's `B²` (coboundaries of continuous cochains). `δ²[c̄] = 0` iff the lift can be corrected by a continuous Z-valued cochain to a cocycle, i.e. iff [c̄] lifts to `H¹(G, B)`. Sign comparison: the inverse of `c(g)(g•c(h))c(gh)⁻¹` is `c(gh)(g•c(h))⁻¹c(g)⁻¹`, exactly Kim's printed boundary. In central additive coefficients, taking inverse negates the 2-cochain and its class. Tau Ceti's `d¹a(g,h)=g•a(h)−a(gh)+a(g)` fixes the positive convention. For a changed lift `c′(g)=z(g)c(g)`, centrality gives `D(c′)=D(c)+d¹z` in additive notation. The independence and obstruction-exactness interfaces must use this convention; negation does not change whether the obstruction vanishes. (c) If `z·c = u·c` with `u ∈ B`, then projecting to C gives `ū·c̄ = c̄`, i.e. ū is invariant for the action twisted by c̄; by hypothesis `ū = 1`, so `u ∈ Z` and `z(g) = u(g•u)⁻¹` is a coboundary of Z (Kim's argument). Identify the central subgroup with the kernel of its quotient projection, then use the named or abstract embedded-kernel comparison. The inner action on a central kernel is the original restricted action. The quotient has its descended jointly continuous action. Its continuous `H¹` comparison with the coefficient target requires surjectivity and a quotient map; the image-converse argument instead lifts one constant gauge element and requires only surjectivity. Use the [Positive central defect](#nc-3-positive-defect), [Continuous central H2 bridge](#nc-3-continuous-central-obstruction), lift-exactness and gauge-descent constructions for the genuine `H²` class. The kernel orbit description supplies the remaining `H¹` fibre ambiguity. The algebra-valued point topology, filtered torsor descent and local conditions are constructed separately in Layer 4.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.central_defect_sign_C3_C9`: In the trivial-action `C₉→C₃` extension, the least-residue section has positive defect 3 at (2,1), and the inverse convention has value 6; the values differ. These correspond to 1 and −1 in the central `C₃`. The continuous central obstruction transports this same defect into the canonical `H²` carrier, preserving the sign.
- For the lower central series of a unipotent group U with `H⁰(G, U^i/U^{i+1}) = 0`, (c) applies at every step, which is how Kim shows `H¹(G, U_{n+1}) ≅ H¹(G, U^{n+1}/U^{n+2}) × δ²⁻¹(0)` (Kim 2005, Proposition 2).
- Without the section hypothesis, `H¹(G, C) → H²(G, Z)` need not be definable with continuous cochains; (a) and (c) do not need it.
- For the trivial-action central extension `0→C₃→C₉→C₃→0`, use the lift s taking least residues. At `(g,h)=(2,1)`, `D=s(2)+s(1)−s(0)=3` in `C₉`, while the printed Kim boundary is `−D=6`. Identifying the central subgroup by `a↦3a` gives 1 and −1 in `C₃`. They are different. The central obstruction interface identifies these positive and negative classes in the canonical `H²` carrier.
