### 0.29 Kernel gauges and the invariant action on kernel classes
<a id="nc-3-kernel-invariant-gauge"></a>

**Gauge cocycles within the kernel.** For `K≤U` with `u∈K` iff `f(u)=1` and a supplied continuous G-action compatible with its inclusion, f equivariant, `u∈U` and `f(u)∈H⁰(G,V)`, construct the continuous K-valued cocycle `g↦u c(g)(g•u)⁻¹` from `c∈Z¹(G,K)`.

Standing hypotheses (H21).

Gauge the ambient inclusion of c by u. Apply f to prove every value lies in K, using fixedness of `f(u)`. Restrict the continuous map to the subgroup; reflect the cocycle identity through its inclusion.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-kernel-invariant-gauge-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.kernelGauge_apply` (*Kernel gauge value*): The underlying U-value of kernelGauge(u,c)(g) is `u c(g)(g•u)⁻¹`. *Proof.* Evaluate the subtype map.
- <a id="nc-3-kernel-invariant-gauge-unit"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.kernelGauge_one` (*Identity kernel gauge*): The gauge construction for `u=1` equals the original K-valued cocycle. *Proof.* Reflect equality pointwise through the subgroup inclusion and cancel the identity factors. Uses [Kernel gauge value](#nc-3-kernel-invariant-gauge-value).
- <a id="nc-3-kernel-invariant-gauge-product"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.kernelGauge_mul` (*Ordered product of kernel gauges*): For `f(u),f(v)` fixed, kernelGauge(uv,c)=kernelGauge(u,kernelGauge(v,c)). *Proof.* Expand pointwise, use the automorphism multiplication identity, and cancel adjacent factors in the noncommutative order. Uses [Kernel gauge value](#nc-3-kernel-invariant-gauge-value).
- <a id="nc-3-kernel-invariant-gauge-equivariance"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.kernelGauge_gauge` (*Kernel gauge respects gauge equivalence*): kernelGauge(u,a•c)=(u a u⁻¹)•kernelGauge(u,c) for `a∈K`. The conjugate lies in K by applying f. *Proof.* Prove membership of the conjugate in K, then expand both ordered gauge expressions and cancel. This produces a real gauge witness, not an assumed quotient equality. Uses [Kernel gauge value](#nc-3-kernel-invariant-gauge-value).
- <a id="nc-3-kernel-invariant-gauge-inclusion"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.kernelGauge_inclusion` (*Kernel gauge and ambient inclusion*): The inclusion of kernelGauge(u,c) equals u•(inclusion of c) as U-valued continuous cocycles. *Proof.* Reflect cocycle equality pointwise; the underlying maps are identical.
- <a id="nc-3-kernel-invariant-lift-independence"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.kernelInvariantAction_lift_independent` (*Lift independence on cohomology classes*): If `f(u)=f(w)` is fixed, the classes of kernelGauge(u,c) and kernelGauge(w,c) agree, whether or not f is surjective. This does not assert equality of cocycles. *Proof.* The kernel element `w u⁻¹` gauges the first cocycle to the second. Verify membership by applying f and the gauge identity by ordered cancellation. Uses [Kernel gauge value](#nc-3-kernel-invariant-gauge-value).

**Checks.**

- `kernel_gauge_identity`: The identity ambient element gives back the original K-valued continuous cocycle.
- `kernel_gauge_native_inclusion`: Inclusion of the constructed kernel cocycle is the ordinary ambient gauge of the included cocycle.
- `kernel_gauge_trivial_value`: For the trivial input cocycle the underlying value is `u(g•u)⁻¹`; it is not silently replaced by 1.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1 continuous cocycle and gauge conventions, printed pp. 5–6; Proposition 2 invariant projection in the freeness proof, pp. 8–9.

Use [Coefficient map on continuous cocycles](#nc-3-coefficient-cocycle-map).
<a id="nc-3-kernel-preimage-class-action"></a>

**Preimage invariants act on kernel classes.** Construct the MulAction of `E=f⁻¹(H⁰(G,V))` on `H¹(G,K)` by u•[c]=[kernelGauge(u,c)].

Standing hypotheses (H21).

Use Quotient.lift on the gauge-orbit set, with the conjugate gauge witness. The preceding unit and ordered product lemmas prove the group-action laws.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-kernel-preimage-class-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.kernelPreimageAction_mk` (*Preimage action on a representative*): For `u∈E`, u•[c]=[kernelGauge(u,c)] under the constructed action. *Proof.* Evaluate the quotient lift.
- <a id="nc-3-kernel-preimage-class-kernel"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.kernelPreimageAction_kernel` (*Kernel elements act trivially on classes*): If `u∈E` and `f(u)=1`, then `u•a=a` for every `a∈H¹(G,K)`. *Proof.* Represent a by a continuous cocycle. Identify kernelGauge(u,c) with the ordinary gauge by the element `u∈K`; its inverse is the gauge witness for class equality. Uses [Preimage action on a representative](#nc-3-kernel-preimage-class-value); [Kernel gauge value](#nc-3-kernel-invariant-gauge-value).
- <a id="nc-3-kernel-preimage-permutation-kernel"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.kernelPreimageAction_perm_kernel` (*Permutation action kills the projection kernel*): For the E-action on `H¹(G,K)`, `ker(E→H⁰(G,V))` lies in ker(E→*Perm(H¹(G,K))). *Proof.* Reflect permutation equality pointwise and apply triviality of the kernel-element action. Uses [Kernel elements act trivially on classes](#nc-3-kernel-preimage-class-kernel); [Project preimage invariants](#nc-3-invariant-preimage-projection).

**Checks.**

- `preimage_action_representative`: The preimage action on a cocycle class is exactly the class of the kernel gauge.
- `preimage_kernel_acts_trivially`: Every preimage element mapping to 1 acts trivially on every kernel `H¹` class.
- `preimage_inverse_roundtrip`: Acting first by u and then by `u⁻¹` gives back the same class.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1 continuous cocycle and gauge conventions, printed pp. 5–6; Proposition 2 invariant projection in the freeness proof, pp. 8–9.

Use [Kernel gauge respects gauge equivalence](#nc-3-kernel-invariant-gauge-equivariance); [Identity kernel gauge](#nc-3-kernel-invariant-gauge-unit); [Ordered product of kernel gauges](#nc-3-kernel-invariant-gauge-product).

<a id="nc-3-invariant-preimage-projection"></a>

**Project preimage invariants.** Specialize the subgroup restriction of f to the homomorphism `E=f⁻¹(H⁰(G,V))→*H⁰(G,V)`, `u↦f(u)`.

Standing hypotheses (H21).

Restrict the original homomorphism to the two subgroups. Membership and group laws come directly from f; no new generic subgroup or homomorphism carrier is defined.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-invariant-preimage-projection-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H0.preimageProjection_apply` (*Invariant projection value*): The V-value of the projection `at u∈E` equals `f(u)`. *Proof.* Evaluate the subtype construction.
- <a id="nc-3-invariant-preimage-projection-kernel"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H0.preimageProjection_mem_ker` (*Exact invariant projection kernel*): For `u∈E`, u belongs to the projection kernel exactly when `f(u)=1`. Under the specified exact-image condition this is equivalent to `u∈K`. *Proof.* Use the homomorphism kernel membership theorem and subtype equality.
- <a id="nc-3-invariant-preimage-projection-surjective"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H0.preimageProjection_surjective` (*Surjective invariant projection*): If the original `f:U→*V` is surjective, the projection `E→*H⁰(G,V)` is surjective. No fixed lift in U is required. *Proof.* Lift the underlying V-value using f-surjectivity. Its image fixedness places the lift in E; subtype equality proves the required projection equation.

**Checks.**

- `invariant_projection_identity`: The projection sends the identity subgroup element to the identity invariant.
- `invariant_projection_exact_kernel`: Membership in the projection kernel is exactly membership of the underlying U-value in K.
- `invariant_projection_lifts`: For surjective f every quotient invariant has a lift in the preimage subgroup.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1 continuous cocycle and gauge conventions, printed pp. 5–6; Proposition 2 invariant projection in the freeness proof, pp. 8–9.

Use [Continuous 1-cocycles and invariants with nonabelian coefficients](#nc-3-continuous-cocycles).

<a id="nc-3-kernel-invariant-class-action"></a>

**Quotient invariants act on kernel classes.** If f is surjective, construct a MulAction of `H⁰(G,V)` on `H¹(G,K)` descending the E-action. For a lift u of v, it sends [c] to `[g↦u c(g)(g•u)⁻¹]`. This is a set action; it need not preserve the neutral class.

Standing hypotheses (H21).

Represent the E-action by Mathlib’s homomorphism to the group of permutations. Factor it through the surjective invariant projection using the MonoidHom.liftOfSurjective and its kernel condition. Pull back the permutation action with MulAction.compHom.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-kernel-invariant-class-lift"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.kernelInvariantAction_lift` (*Invariant action agrees with each preimage lift*): The action of the projection of `u∈E` on `a∈H¹(G,K)` equals the preimage action of u, for every such u and a. *Proof.* Apply the liftOfRightInverse composition identity to the permutation homomorphism, then evaluate at a.
- <a id="nc-3-kernel-invariant-class-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.kernelInvariantAction_mk` (*Invariant action on a cocycle*): For `v∈H⁰(G,V)`, `u∈U` with `f(u)=v` and `c∈Z¹(G,K)`, v•[c]=[kernelGauge(u,c)]. *Proof.* Put u in the preimage subgroup, compare its projection with v, then apply the action-lift and quotient evaluation lemmas. Uses [Invariant action agrees with each preimage lift](#nc-3-kernel-invariant-class-lift); [Preimage action on a representative](#nc-3-kernel-preimage-class-value).
- <a id="nc-3-kernel-invariant-ambient-constant"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.kernelInvariantAction_inclusion` (*Ambient image is invariant under the action*): The inclusion `H¹(G,K)→H¹(G,U)` is constant on every orbit of the H⁰(G,V)-action. *Proof.* Represent a kernel class, choose one lift of the fixed quotient element, and identify its included cocycle with an ordinary ambient gauge. The inverse lift gives the quotient witness. Uses [Invariant action on a cocycle](#nc-3-kernel-invariant-class-value); [Kernel gauge and ambient inclusion](#nc-3-kernel-invariant-gauge-inclusion); [Coefficient map on nonabelian cohomology](#nc-3-coefficient-h1-map).
- <a id="nc-3-kernel-invariant-fibre-orbit"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.kernelInvariantAction_fibre_iff` (*Ambient fibres are exactly invariant orbits*): For surjective equivariant f and the `subgroup K=ker(f)` with its compatible continuous G-action, two classes `a,b∈H¹(G,K)` have equal images in `H¹(G,U)` exactly when there exists `v∈H⁰(G,V)` with `v•a=b`. No centrality, trivial invariants, quotient-map hypothesis or continuous section is required. *Proof.* Represent a,b by cocycles. An ambient gauge u between their included cocycles projects under f to a fixed element, by applying f and cancelling the kernel values. Its kernel gauge is the second cocycle, so the lifted action gives the orbit witness. Conversely apply constancy of the ambient image on the orbit. Uses [Invariant action on a cocycle](#nc-3-kernel-invariant-class-value); [Ambient image is invariant under the action](#nc-3-kernel-invariant-ambient-constant); [Coefficient map on nonabelian cohomology](#nc-3-coefficient-h1-map).

**Checks.**

- `invariant_action_identity`: The identity quotient invariant fixes every kernel `H¹` class.
- `invariant_action_ambient_constant`: The ambient `H¹` inclusion takes the same value before and after the quotient-invariant action.
- `odd_invariant_exchanges_distinct_kernel_classes`: For discrete trivial C₃-actions and the kernel of sign:S₃→ℤˣ, the three-cycle and inverse cocycles give distinct kernel `H¹` classes. The invariant -1 acts by the transposition (01), exchanging those classes. Thus the quotient-invariant action need not be trivial, even though its ambient image is constant.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1 continuous cocycle and gauge conventions, printed pp. 5–6; Proposition 2 invariant projection in the freeness proof, pp. 8–9.

Use [Preimage invariants act on kernel classes](#nc-3-kernel-preimage-class-action); [Surjective invariant projection](#nc-3-invariant-preimage-projection-surjective); [Permutation action kills the projection kernel](#nc-3-kernel-preimage-permutation-kernel); `MonoidHom.liftOfSurjective`; `MulAction.toPermHom`; `MulAction.compHom`; `Equiv.Perm.sign`; `Equiv.Perm.sign_surjective`.

<a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-invariant-action"></a>

**Twisted kernel invariant action.** For surjective continuous equivariant f and a continuous cocycle c, construct the action of `A_c=H⁰(G,V_(f∘c))` on `H¹(G,K_c)`, where `K_c=ker(f_c)` is the inner-twisted kernel with its restricted topology and G-action. A lift `u∈U_c` of `v∈A_c` acts on a kernel cocycle d by the class of `g↦u d(g)(g⋆_c u)⁻¹`. The kernel-valued cocycle is the kernelGauge. Its class, not its representative, is independent of the lift.

Standing hypotheses (H22).

Instantiate the kernel invariant action with the continuous equivariant `f_c` and its kernel. Kernel membership and inclusion equivariance are definitional; the inherited construction already descends lift choices at class level.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-invariant-action-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistedKernelInvariantAction_mk` (*Invariant action on representatives*): For `v∈A_c`, any `u∈U_c` with `f_c(u)=v` and every continuous `K_c`-valued cocycle d, `v·[d]` equals the class of the kernelGauge cocycle `g↦u d(g)(g⋆_c u)⁻¹`. No continuous family of lifts is required. *Proof.* Apply the representative formula to `f_c` and its kernel; invariance of v supplies the kernelGauge membership witness. Uses [Invariant action on a cocycle](#nc-3-kernel-invariant-class-value).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-invariant-inclusion"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistedKernelInvariantAction_inclusion` (*Invariant action preserves inclusion*): For every `v∈A_c` and `a∈H¹(G,K_c)`, `j_c(v·a)=j_c(a)` in `H¹(G,U_c)`, where `j_c` is the twisted-kernel inclusion. Thus `T_c∘j_c` is constant on these invariant orbits. *Proof.* Specialize the invariant-action inclusion identity, then apply the `T_c` when the translated equality is needed. Uses [Ambient image is invariant under the action](#nc-3-kernel-invariant-ambient-constant); [`H¹` map from the twisted kernel](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-h1-inclusion).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-invariant-fibre-orbit"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistedKernelInvariantAction_fibre_iff` (*Twisted inclusion fibres are invariant orbits*): For `a,b∈H¹(G,K_c)`, `T_c(j_c(a))=T_c(j_c(b))` if and only if some `v∈A_c` satisfies `v·a=b`. This is an orbit criterion, not equality of kernel classes. *Proof.* Reflect the translated equality through injectivity of `T_c` and specialize the kernel fibre-orbit criterion to `f_c`. Uses [Ambient fibres are exactly invariant orbits](#nc-3-kernel-invariant-fibre-orbit); [Gauge-orbit bijection under twisting](#nc-3-twist-h1-equivalence).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-invariant-injectivity-iff"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistedKernelInvariantAction_injective_iff` (*Twisted kernel injectivity criterion*): The translated kernel-class map `T_c∘j_c` is injective exactly when the entire `A_c`-action on `H¹(G,K_c)` is trivial: `v·a=a` for every v and a. Triviality of `A_c` is sufficient but not necessary, and no unconditional unique kernel class is asserted. *Proof.* Injectivity of `T_c` reflects and preserves injectivity of `j_c`. Apply the necessary-and-sufficient trivial-action criterion to `f_c`. Uses [Kernel injectivity and the invariant action](#nc-3-kernel-invariant-injectivity-characterisation); [Gauge-orbit bijection under twisting](#nc-3-twist-h1-equivalence).

**Checks.**

- `twisted_invariant_action_unit`: The identity element of the twisted invariant group `A_c` fixes every kernel cohomology class.
- `twisted_invariant_action_lift_value`: For every invariant v, every lift u with `f_c(u)=v` and every continuous kernel cocycle d, `v·[d]` is the gauge class of the kernelGauge cocycle `g↦u d(g)(g⋆_c u)⁻¹`.
- `twisted_invariant_action_translated_constant`: For every `v∈A_c` and every kernel class a, the original class `T_c(j_c(v·a))` equals `T_c(j_c(a))`.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, pp. 5–9; cocycle/gauge conventions and both complete Proposition proofs.

Use [Quotient invariants act on kernel classes](#nc-3-kernel-invariant-class-action); [Coefficient homomorphism between inner twists](#nc-3-twist-coefficient-map); [Equivariance between the two twisted actions](#nc-3-twist-coefficient-equivariance); [Continuous automorphism action on the twisted kernel](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-action); [Joint continuity on the twisted kernel](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-action-continuity); [Surjectivity of the twisted coefficient map](#nc-3-twisted-map-surjectivity).

<a id="nc-3-kernel-orbit-image-equivalence"></a>

**Kernel orbits and the inclusion image.** For surjective equivariant `f:U→V` and `K=ker(f)`, construct the equivalence `H¹(G,K)/H⁰(G,V) ≃ image(j)`, where `j:H¹(G,K)→H¹(G,U)` is the inclusion map and the quotient is by the previously constructed invariant action. Its forward map sends the orbit of a to `j(a)`, with its range witness.

Standing hypotheses (H23).

Descend j to the action-orbit quotient using orbit constancy. Reflect equal quotient values using the exact fibre/orbit criterion; range witnesses give surjectivity. Apply the equivalence constructor for a bijective function.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-kernel-orbit-image-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.kernelOrbitImageEquiv_mk` (*Orbit image evaluation*): The underlying ambient class of the orbit of a under the image equivalence is exactly `j(a)`. *Proof.* Evaluate the quotient lift and equivalence forward map.
- <a id="nc-3-kernel-orbit-image-inverse-witness"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.kernelOrbitImageEquiv_symm_mk` (*Image inverse on a range witness*): The inverse image equivalence sends `j(a)`, equipped with its range witness a, to the invariant orbit of a. *Proof.* Apply the equivalence left inverse to the orbit of a.
- <a id="nc-3-kernel-orbit-image-inverse-projection"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.kernelOrbitImageEquiv_symm_projection` (*Projection after the image inverse*): For every range element z, applying the equivalence after its inverse has underlying ambient value z. *Proof.* Apply the right inverse and project the subtype value.
- <a id="nc-3-kernel-orbit-image-choice-independence"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.kernelOrbitImageEquiv_choice_independent` (*Independence of kernel-class witnesses*): If `j(a)=j(b)`, the invariant orbits of a and b are equal. Thus the inverse determines an orbit independently of a chosen range witness, without claiming `a=b`. *Proof.* Apply injectivity of the image equivalence to the equality of the two subtype values.
- <a id="nc-3-kernel-invariant-injectivity-characterisation"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.kernelInvariantAction_injective_iff` (*Kernel injectivity and the invariant action*): For surjective f, j is injective exactly when every invariant `v∈H⁰(G,V)` fixes every class in `H¹(G,K)`. This requires triviality of the action, not triviality of its acting group. *Proof.* Injectivity and orbit constancy force every action value to equal its input. Conversely, the fibre/orbit criterion supplies an invariant carrying a to b; trivial action then gives `a=b`.
- <a id="nc-3-kernel-inclusion-neutral-range"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.kernelInclusion_range_iff` (*Kernel image equals the neutral coefficient fibre*): For continuous surjective equivariant f between topological groups with jointly continuous actions, `a∈H¹(G,U)` belongs to `image(j)` exactly when `f₁(a)=1` in `H¹(G,V)`, where `f₁` is the continuous coefficient map. *Proof.* Kernel-valued representatives map to the constant identity cocycle. Conversely represent a, extract its image coboundary witness y, choose x with `f(x)=y`, and apply the already proved inverse-gauge normalization. Restrict the normalized continuous cocycle to K, reflecting the cocycle identity through its compatible inclusion; its included class equals a by gauge equivalence. Uses [Inverse gauge after a lifted coboundary](#nc-3-mapped-inverse-gauge-normalization); [Neutral class as a coboundary](#nc-3-h1-neutral-criterion); [Gauge invariance of the cohomology class](#nc-3-h1-gauge-class).

**Checks.**

- `kernel_orbit_image_cocycle_projection`: For a continuous K-valued cocycle c, the image equivalence sends the invariant orbit of its gauge class to the gauge class of its included cocycle.
- `kernel_orbit_image_inverse_witness`: The inverse sends the inclusion `image j(a)`, with range witness a, to the invariant orbit of a.
- `kernel_orbit_image_quotient_roundtrip`: For every orbit q, applying the image equivalence and then its inverse returns q, without choosing a fixed cocycle representative.
- `kernel_orbit_sign_distinct_classes_identified`: With discrete trivial C₃-actions and the sign kernel of `S₃`, the three-cycle and inverse cocycles have distinct kernel cohomology classes but equal quotient orbits: the invariant −1 lifts to the transposition (01), which exchanges them. An inverse taking values in unique kernel classes would be wrong.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1 printed pp. 5–6 cocycle/gauge definitions and Proposition 1; pp. 7–9 Proposition 2 proof, invariant projection and orbit classification.

Use [Quotient invariants act on kernel classes](#nc-3-kernel-invariant-class-action); [Ambient image is invariant under the action](#nc-3-kernel-invariant-ambient-constant); [Ambient fibres are exactly invariant orbits](#nc-3-kernel-invariant-fibre-orbit); [Coefficient map on nonabelian cohomology](#nc-3-coefficient-h1-map); `Equiv.ofBijective`; `MulAction.orbitRel`; `MulAction.orbitRel_apply`.

<a id="nc-3-kernel-orbit-neutral-fibre-equivalence"></a>

**Kernel orbits and the neutral fibre.** For continuous surjective equivariant f, construct `H¹(G,K)/H⁰(G,V) ≃ {a∈H¹(G,U) : f₁(a)=1}`. Compose the orbit/image equivalence with the equality of the inclusion image and the neutral fibre. The source base point is the orbit of the neutral kernel class; no action-fixedness of that class is assumed.

Standing hypotheses (H23).

Identify the two subsets using the exact kernel-range criterion and compose with the equivalence of equal set subtypes.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-kernel-orbit-neutral-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.kernelOrbitNeutralFibreEquiv_mk` (*Neutral-fibre orbit evaluation*): The underlying ambient value of the neutral-fibre equivalence on the orbit of a is `j(a)`. *Proof.* Evaluate the composite; the equal-set subtype equivalence preserves the underlying element.
- <a id="nc-3-kernel-orbit-neutral-inverse-witness"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.kernelOrbitNeutralFibreEquiv_symm_mk` (*Neutral-fibre inverse on a kernel image*): The inverse neutral-fibre equivalence sends `j(a)`, with its proved neutral-fibre membership, to the invariant orbit of a. *Proof.* Apply the composite equivalence left inverse to the orbit.
- <a id="nc-3-kernel-orbit-neutral-basepoint"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.kernelOrbitNeutralFibreEquiv_one` (*Neutral-fibre base point*): The equivalence sends the orbit of the neutral kernel class to the neutral ambient class. This is a statement about the quotient base point, not a claim that each invariant fixes the neutral kernel class. *Proof.* The forward map is inclusion, and the coefficient inclusion preserves the neutral class. Uses [Neutral class under coefficient maps](#nc-3-coefficient-h1-one).
- <a id="nc-3-kernel-orbit-neutral-inverse"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.kernelOrbitNeutralFibreEquiv_inverse` (*Complete neutral-fibre inverse law*): For every neutral-fibre element a, mapping its inverse orbit forward returns the identical subtype element a, including the cohomology value. *Proof.* Apply the equivalence right inverse, with proof irrelevance for fibre membership.

**Checks.**

- `kernel_orbit_neutral_identity`: The orbit of the neutral kernel class maps to the neutral ambient class.
- `kernel_orbit_neutral_image_witness`: The inverse `at j(a)`, with its neutral-fibre membership proof, returns the invariant orbit of a.
- `kernel_orbit_neutral_full_inverse`: For every element of the neutral coefficient fibre, applying the inverse equivalence and then the forward equivalence returns the same fibre element.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1 printed pp. 5–6 cocycle/gauge definitions and Proposition 1; pp. 7–9 Proposition 2 proof, invariant projection and orbit classification.

Use [Kernel orbits and the inclusion image](#nc-3-kernel-orbit-image-equivalence); [Kernel image equals the neutral coefficient fibre](#nc-3-kernel-inclusion-neutral-range); `Set.equivOfEq`.

<a id="nc-3-twist-neutral-fibre-equivalence"></a>

**Translation of the neutral coefficient fibre.** For every continuous equivariant `f:U→V` and continuous cocycle c, restrict the twisting equivalence `T_c` to an equivalence from the neutral fibre of `(f_c)₁:H¹(G,U_c)→H¹(G,V_(f∘c))` to the original fibre `{a∈H¹(G,U) : f₁(a)=[f∘c]}`. The underlying map is `T_c`, with inverse `T_c⁻¹`, and its source neutral class maps to [c]. Surjectivity of f is not required.

Standing hypotheses (H22).

Apply the subtype-equivalence constructor to the `T_c` and the proved coefficient-fibre comparison. Its inverse restricts `T_c⁻¹` and both inverse laws are inherited from `T_c`.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-twist-neutral-fibre-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistNeutralFibreEquiv_apply` (*Fibre translation evaluation*): For every element z of the twisted neutral coefficient fibre, the underlying original cohomology class of its translation is `T_c(z)`. *Proof.* Evaluate the restricted equivalence forward map.
- <a id="nc-3-twist-neutral-fibre-inverse-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistNeutralFibreEquiv_symm_apply` (*Inverse fibre translation evaluation*): For every z in the original fibre over `[f∘c]`, the underlying twisted cohomology class of the inverse translation is `T_c⁻¹(z)`. *Proof.* Evaluate the restricted equivalence inverse map.
- <a id="nc-3-twist-neutral-fibre-basepoint"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistNeutralFibreEquiv_basepoint` (*The translated fibre base point*): Translation sends the neutral twisted class, with its neutral coefficient-image proof, to [c] in the original fibre. It does not send it to the original neutral class unless `[c]=1`. *Proof.* Evaluate `T_c at` the source neutral class using the twisting base-point identity.

**Checks.**

- `twist_fibre_translation_value`: The fibre translation sends every twisted neutral-fibre element z to `T_c(z)`, with the same original cohomology value.
- `twist_fibre_translation_basepoint`: The twisted neutral class translates to [c], not necessarily to the original neutral class.
- `twist_fibre_translation_inverse`: For every element of the original fibre over `[f∘c]`, the forward translation after its inverse is the same subtype element.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, pp. 5–9; cocycle/gauge conventions and both complete Proposition proofs.

Use [Gauge-orbit bijection under twisting](#nc-3-twist-h1-equivalence); [Neutral fibre after coefficient twisting and repointing](#nc-3-twist-coefficient-repointed-fibre); `Equiv.subtypeEquiv`.

<a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-orbit-fibre-equivalence"></a>

**Twisted kernel orbits and the original fibre.** For surjective continuous equivariant f and continuous c, construct `H¹(G,K_c)/A_c ≃ {a∈H¹(G,U) : f₁(a)=[f∘c]}`, using the invariant-action orbit quotient. The forward value of the orbit of b is `T_c(j_c(b))`; the inverse returns an invariant orbit, independently of any kernel-class or gauge-lift witness. The orbit of the neutral kernel class is the source base point, and maps to [c].

Standing hypotheses (H22).

Apply the kernel-orbit neutral-fibre equivalence to `f_c` with its kernel, then compose with the neutral-to-original fibre translation. Both constructions carry genuine inverse laws.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-orbit-fibre-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistedKernelOrbitFibreEquiv_mk` (*Original-fibre orbit evaluation*): For every `b∈H¹(G,K_c)`, the underlying value of its invariant orbit under the original-fibre equivalence is `T_c(j_c(b))`. For a cocycle d this is represented by `g↦d(g)c(g)`, with inclusion into U understood, in this order. *Proof.* Evaluate the composite quotient map, inclusion and twist translation.
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-orbit-fibre-inverse-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistedKernelOrbitFibreEquiv_symm_mk` (*Inverse on a translated kernel image*): The inverse original-fibre equivalence sends `T_c(j_c(b))`, with its fibre-membership proof, to the invariant orbit of b. It does not select b uniquely. *Proof.* Apply the composite equivalence left inverse to the orbit of b; fibre-proof irrelevance identifies the subtype argument. Uses [Kernel inclusion maps to the fibre over the image cocycle](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-h1-repointed-fibre).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-orbit-fibre-left-inverse"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistedKernelOrbitFibreEquiv_left_inv` (*Complete orbit inverse law*): For every invariant orbit q, the inverse original-fibre equivalence applied after its forward map returns q. *Proof.* Apply the composite equivalence left inverse to arbitrary q.
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-orbit-fibre-right-inverse"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistedKernelOrbitFibreEquiv_right_inv` (*Complete original-fibre inverse law*): For every original coefficient-fibre element z over `[f∘c]`, mapping its inverse orbit forward returns exactly z as a subtype element, with the same cohomology value. *Proof.* Apply the composite equivalence right inverse.
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-orbit-fibre-basepoint"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistedKernelOrbitFibreEquiv_basepoint` (*The original-fibre orbit base point*): The orbit of the neutral kernel class maps to [c]. This is a statement about the quotient base point, not a claim that every `v∈A_c` fixes the neutral kernel class or that [c] is neutral. *Proof.* Use the orbit evaluation, the inclusion neutral identity and the `T_c` neutral-to-[c] identity. Uses [Original-fibre orbit evaluation](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-orbit-fibre-value); [Neutral class under kernel inclusion](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-h1-neutral); [Gauge-orbit bijection under twisting](#nc-3-twist-h1-equivalence).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-orbit-fibre-choice-independent"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistedKernelOrbitFibreEquiv_choice_independent` (*Independence of original-fibre witnesses*): If `T_c(j_c(a))=T_c(j_c(b))`, the invariant orbits of a and b are equal. Consequently the inverse original-fibre classification does not depend on a chosen kernel-class witness, although a and b may be different. *Proof.* Apply injectivity of the constructed orbit equivalence to equality of the subtype values and use its evaluation identity. Uses [Original-fibre orbit evaluation](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-orbit-fibre-value).

**Checks.**

- `twisted_orbit_actual_cocycle_value`: For a continuous `K_c`-valued cocycle d, the original-fibre equivalence sends the orbit of [d] to the class represented by `g↦d(g)c(g)`, after inclusion, in this order.
- `twisted_orbit_repointed_basepoint`: The invariant orbit of the neutral kernel class maps to [c] in the original coefficient fibre.
- `twisted_orbit_inverse_on_included_class`: The inverse `at T_c(j_c(a))`, with its original-fibre membership proof, is the invariant orbit of a, without selecting a uniquely.
- `twisted_orbit_quotient_roundtrip`: For every invariant orbit q, the forward original-fibre equivalence followed by its inverse returns q.
- `twisted_orbit_fibre_roundtrip`: For every original coefficient-fibre element z over `[f∘c]`, applying the inverse orbit equivalence and then its forward map returns exactly z.
- `twisted_orbit_identity_fibre_nonneutral`: Take discrete `G=S₂` acting trivially on `U=V=S₃`, `f=id` and `c(1)=1`, `c(g)=(01)` for `g≠1`. The orbit of the neutral kernel class maps to [c], and `[c]≠1`: its value on the nonidentity element is a nonidentity transposition, whereas every coboundary for a trivial action has value 1. A replacement target neutral fibre or identity-valued forward map fails this test.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, pp. 5–9; cocycle/gauge conventions and both complete Proposition proofs.

Use [Twisted kernel invariant action](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-invariant-action); [Kernel orbits and the neutral fibre](#nc-3-kernel-orbit-neutral-fibre-equivalence); [Translation of the neutral coefficient fibre](#nc-3-twist-neutral-fibre-equivalence); [Continuity of a twisted coefficient map](#nc-3-twist-coefficient-continuity); [Surjectivity of the twisted coefficient map](#nc-3-twisted-map-surjectivity).

### 0.30 Abstract embedded kernels
<a id="nc-3-embedded-kernel-equivalence"></a>

**Abstract embedded kernel equivalence.** Construct `e:A≃*K_c`, where `K_c=ker(F_c)` in `Twist(c)`, by composing Mathlib’s injective-homomorphism range equivalence with the previously constructed named-kernel equivalence. Its underlying value at a is `i(a)`.

Standing hypotheses (H24).

Use MonoidHom.ofInjective for `i:A→U` and hi.injective. Apply the exact image witness hK to identify its range with the twisted kernel. Compose these genuine multiplicative equivalences.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-embedded-kernel-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.embeddedKernelEquiv_apply` (*Embedded kernel forward value*): For `a∈A`, the original U-value of `e(a)` is `i(a)`. *Proof.* Unfold the composition only far enough to evaluate the range inclusion; the value is definitionally `i(a)`.
- <a id="nc-3-embedded-kernel-inverse-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.embeddedKernelEquiv_symm_apply` (*Embedded kernel inverse value*): For `k∈K_c`, `i(e⁻¹(k))` is the original U-value of k. *Proof.* Apply the original-value map to `e(e⁻¹(k))=k`. This determines the chosen inverse uniquely because i is injective. Uses [Embedded kernel forward value](#nc-3-embedded-kernel-value).
- <a id="nc-3-embedded-kernel-continuity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.embeddedKernelEquiv_continuous` (*Continuous embedded kernel equivalence*): The forward map `e:A→K_c` is continuous for the given topology on A and subspace topology on `K_c`. *Proof.* The forward value is i, continuous by the topological embedding hypothesis. Restrict its codomain to the subtype using membership.
- <a id="nc-3-embedded-kernel-inverse-continuity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.embeddedKernelEquiv_symm_continuous` (*Continuous inverse on the abstract kernel*): The inverse `e⁻¹:K_c→A` is continuous for the supplied topology on A. *Proof.* Use `IsEmbedding.continuous_iff` to test inverse continuity after composition with i. The inverse-value formula identifies this composite with the continuous kernel inclusion. Injectivity and continuity alone would not justify this step. Uses [Embedded kernel inverse value](#nc-3-embedded-kernel-inverse-value).

**Checks.**

- `embedded_kernel_wrong_image`: If `f(x)=1` but x is outside `range(i)`, the required exactness witness is impossible; merely having `f∘i=1` is insufficient.
- `embedded_kernel_noninjective`: Distinct `x,y∈A` with `i(x)=i(y)` rule out the required topological embedding.
- `embedded_kernel_inverse_topology`: If a multiplicative equivalence `A≃U` has a discontinuous inverse, its underlying forward map cannot satisfy the topological embedding hypothesis, even if it is algebraically bijective.
- `embedded_kernel_constant_nonsurjective`: For `f:U→V` constant at 1 and `i=id`, any `v≠1` proves f is not surjective, but the embedded-kernel equivalence is still defined and has original value x for every `x∈U`.
- `embedded_kernel_inverse_coordinate`: For a commutative topological group C, `i(x)=x⁻¹` and `f:C→C` constant at 1, if `x⁻¹≠x` then the forward kernel-equivalence value differs from x. An implementation silently replacing i by identity fails.
- With trivial source G, `U=S₃`, `V=C₂`, f the sign and `A=A₃`, the kernel identification fixes (012) and its inverse; neither is collapsed to the identity.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1 continuous cocycle/gauge definitions and coefficient maps, printed pp. 5–7; Proposition 2 and subgroup paragraph, pp. 7–9.

Use [Named subgroup identified with the twisted kernel](#nc-3-named-kernel-equivalence); [Coefficient homomorphism between inner twists](#nc-3-twist-coefficient-map); `MonoidHom.ofInjective`.
<a id="nc-3-embedded-kernel-inner-action"></a>

**Inner action on the abstract kernel.** Equip the group A with `g⋆a=e⁻¹(g⋆e(a))`, where the target action is the restricted inner action on `K_c`. This is an action by group automorphisms preserving A’s original multiplication.

Standing hypotheses (H25).

Transport the kernel action through the multiplicative equivalence. Prove the identity/composition and preservation-of-one/product laws by cancelling e with `e⁻¹`; do not replace A’s multiplication by an unrelated transferred operation.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-embedded-kernel-action-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.embeddedKernelAction_value` (*Embedded inner action formula*): For every `g∈G` and `a∈A`, `i(g⋆a)=c(g)·(g•i(a))·c(g)⁻¹`, in that order. *Proof.* Evaluate the inverse map on `g⋆e(a)`; apply its inverse-value formula and the kernel action formula. Uses [Embedded kernel inverse value](#nc-3-embedded-kernel-inverse-value).
- <a id="nc-3-embedded-kernel-equivariance"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.embeddedKernelEquiv_smul` (*Equivariant abstract kernel comparison*): The multiplicative equivalence satisfies `e(g⋆a)=g⋆e(a)`. *Proof.* Expand the transported action and use `e(e⁻¹(x))=x`.
- <a id="nc-3-embedded-kernel-action-continuity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.embeddedKernelContinuousSMul` (*Joint continuity of the transported action*): The action `G×A→A` is jointly continuous in the given topology on A. *Proof.* Test continuity after the inducing map i. The value formula is the product of continuous c, the jointly continuous ambient action composed with i, and inverse c. This does not require G’s multiplication to be continuous. Uses [Embedded inner action formula](#nc-3-embedded-kernel-action-value).

**Checks.**

- `embedded_kernel_neutral_action`: For `c=1` the transported action satisfies `i(g⋆a)=g•i(a)`, with the original action on the ambient U.
- `embedded_kernel_inner_action_order`: If `c(g)(g•i(a))c(g)⁻¹` differs from `g•i(a)`, then `i(g⋆a)` also differs from `g•i(a)`; dropping conjugation is rejected.
- `embedded_kernel_action_multiplication`: For `g∈G` and `x,y∈A`, i(g⋆(xy))=i(g⋆x)i(g⋆y), using A’s original multiplication.
- With trivial source G, `U=S₃`, `V=C₂`, f the sign and `A=A₃`, the kernel identification fixes (012) and its inverse; neither is collapsed to the identity.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1 continuous cocycle/gauge definitions and coefficient maps, printed pp. 5–7; Proposition 2 and subgroup paragraph, pp. 7–9.

Use [Abstract embedded kernel equivalence](#nc-3-embedded-kernel-equivalence); [Continuous automorphism action on the twisted kernel](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-action).

<a id="nc-3-embedded-kernel-h1-equivalence"></a>

**Continuous H¹ of an abstract embedded kernel.** Construct the pointed bijection `E:H¹(G,A_c)≃H¹(G,K_c)` on continuous cocycle gauge-orbit sets, induced by e and `e⁻¹`.

Standing hypotheses (H25).

Use the `H¹` coefficient map in both directions. Derive inverse equivariance by applying e and cancelling its inverse. Lift each class to a cocycle; the two composites are equal by cocycle extensionality and the two inverse identities.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-embedded-kernel-h1-one"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.embeddedKernelEquiv_one` (*Abstract kernel neutral class*): E sends the neutral continuous `H¹` class to the neutral class of the kernel. *Proof.* Apply the coefficient `H¹` map’s neutral-class law.
- <a id="nc-3-embedded-kernel-h1-representative"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.embeddedKernelEquiv_mk` (*Abstract kernel comparison on cocycles*): For a continuous cocycle `d:G→A_c`, `E([d])=[e∘d]`, using the continuous equivariant coefficient pushforward. *Proof.* Evaluate the quotient lift on a represented class; its representative is the coefficient-map cocycle.
- <a id="nc-3-embedded-kernel-h1-inclusion-comparison"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.embeddedKernelEquiv_inclusion` (*Comparison of the two H¹ inclusions*): For every `a∈H¹(G,A_c)`, `j_native(E(a))=j(a)`, with both inclusion maps into `H¹(G,Twist(c))`. *Proof.* Choose a cocycle representing a; both inclusions have the same pointwise value `i(d(g))`, hence equal gauge classes. Uses [Abstract kernel inclusion on `H¹`](#nc-3-embedded-kernel-h1-inclusion); [Embedded kernel forward value](#nc-3-embedded-kernel-value).

**Checks.**

- `embedded_kernel_h1_inverse`: For every `a∈H¹(G,A_c)`, `E⁻¹(E(a))=a` on the gauge quotient.
- `embedded_kernel_h1_neutral`: The class represented by the constant identity cocycle on `A_c` maps to the neutral class of the kernel.
- `embedded_kernel_h1_forward_inverse`: For every `k∈H¹(G,K_c)`, `E(E⁻¹(k))=k`; the comparison covers every kernel class.
- With trivial source G, `U=S₃`, `V=C₂`, f the sign and `A=A₃`, the kernel identification fixes (012) and its inverse; neither is collapsed to the identity.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1 continuous cocycle/gauge definitions and coefficient maps, printed pp. 5–7; Proposition 2 and subgroup paragraph, pp. 7–9.

Use [Continuous embedded kernel equivalence](#nc-3-embedded-kernel-continuity); [Continuous inverse on the abstract kernel](#nc-3-embedded-kernel-inverse-continuity); [Equivariant abstract kernel comparison](#nc-3-embedded-kernel-equivariance); [Joint continuity of the transported action](#nc-3-embedded-kernel-action-continuity); [Coefficient map on nonabelian cohomology](#nc-3-coefficient-h1-map).

<a id="nc-3-embedded-kernel-h1-inclusion"></a>

**Abstract kernel inclusion on H¹.** Construct `j:H¹(G,A_c)→H¹(G,Twist(c))` by the monoid homomorphism i, its embedding continuity and the inner-action value formula.

Standing hypotheses (H25).

Retype i’s target as the inner twist. Its multiplication and topology are unchanged; the action-value theorem proves equivariance. Apply the continuous `H¹` coefficient map.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-embedded-kernel-inclusion-representative"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.embeddedKernelInclusion_mk` (*Abstract inclusion on cocycles*): For a continuous cocycle `d:G→A_c`, `j([d])=[i∘d]` in `H¹(G,Twist(c))`. *Proof.* Evaluate the coefficient quotient lift on the representative; no choice of a class representative enters the map definition.
- <a id="nc-3-embedded-kernel-inclusion-range"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.embeddedKernelInclusion_range` (*Equality of abstract and kernel images*): The range of j equals the range of the twisted-kernel inclusion. *Proof.* For an abstract class use E as the image witness. For a class use surjectivity of E. This gives image equality, not injectivity of either ambient inclusion. Uses [Comparison of the two `H¹` inclusions](#nc-3-embedded-kernel-h1-inclusion-comparison).
- <a id="nc-3-embedded-kernel-quotient-range"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.embeddedKernelInclusion_quotient_range_iff` (*Abstract kernel image in the quotient neutral fibre*): For every continuous equivariant f, `a∈H¹(G,Twist(c))` lies in `range(j)` exactly when its image in `H¹(G,Twist(c)/K_c)` is neutral. *Proof.* Rewrite to the image and use quotient exactness. The quotient projection is surjective regardless of f; no surjectivity assumption on f is inserted. Uses [Equality of abstract and kernel images](#nc-3-embedded-kernel-inclusion-range); [Exact image for the twisted quotient](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-h1-quotient-range).
- <a id="nc-3-embedded-kernel-mapped-range"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.embeddedKernelInclusion_mapped_range_iff` (*Abstract kernel image in the mapped neutral fibre*): If f is surjective, `a∈H¹(G,Twist(c))` lies in `range(j)` exactly when `F_c*(a)=1` in `H¹(G,Twist(f∘c))`. Hypotheses: G is a group with any topology; U,V are groups with topologies and actions of G by automorphisms. `c:G→U` is a continuous cocycle and `f:U→V` is a continuous equivariant homomorphism. A is an independently supplied group with its given topology. `i:A→U` is a group homomorphism which is a topological embedding (inducing and injective). Exactness is the pointwise witness `x∈range(i)` iff `f(x)=1`. Neither a chosen inverse nor a homeomorphism is assumed as an input. For the transported-action and `H¹` declarations U,V are topological groups with jointly continuous G-actions. For `H¹`, A is also a topological group; this is automatic from i being inducing (Mathlib `Topology.IsInducing.isTopologicalGroup`). No closedness, Hausdorffness, compactness, discreteness, commutativity, openness, quotient-map condition or continuous section is assumed. The action on A is the new transported inner action; no unrelated pre-A-action is used. `H¹` is a pointed set of continuous gauge classes, with no ambient-inclusion injectivity assertion. `f:U→V` is surjective. This assumption is absent from the quotient neutral-fibre criterion. *Proof.* Rewrite the image as the kernel image and apply the surjective coefficient-map exactness theorem. Only a single gauge element is lifted, so no continuous section or quotient-map hypothesis on f is used. Uses [Equality of abstract and kernel images](#nc-3-embedded-kernel-inclusion-range); [Exact image under a surjective coefficient map](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-h1-mapped-range).
- <a id="nc-3-embedded-kernel-repointed-range"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.embeddedKernelInclusion_fibre_range_iff` (*Abstract kernel image in the original repointed fibre*): If f is surjective, `a∈H¹(G,U)` lies in the range of b↦twistEquiv(c)(j(b)) exactly when `f*(a)=[f∘c]`. Hypotheses: G is a group with any topology; U,V are groups with topologies and actions of G by automorphisms. `c:G→U` is a continuous cocycle and `f:U→V` is a continuous equivariant homomorphism. A is an independently supplied group with its given topology. `i:A→U` is a group homomorphism which is a topological embedding (inducing and injective). Exactness is the pointwise witness `x∈range(i)` iff `f(x)=1`. Neither a chosen inverse nor a homeomorphism is assumed as an input. For the transported-action and `H¹` declarations U,V are topological groups with jointly continuous G-actions. For `H¹`, A is also a topological group; this is automatic from i being inducing (Mathlib `Topology.IsInducing.isTopologicalGroup`). No closedness, Hausdorffness, compactness, discreteness, commutativity, openness, quotient-map condition or continuous section is assumed. The action on A is the new transported inner action; no unrelated pre-A-action is used. `H¹` is a pointed set of continuous gauge classes, with no ambient-inclusion injectivity assertion. `f:U→V` is surjective. This assumption is absent from the quotient neutral-fibre criterion. *Proof.* Transport the inclusion-image equality through the `H¹` twist equivalence and use the original-fibre theorem. The target point is `[f∘c]`, which need not be neutral. Uses [Equality of abstract and kernel images](#nc-3-embedded-kernel-inclusion-range); [Comparison of the two `H¹` inclusions](#nc-3-embedded-kernel-h1-inclusion-comparison); [Entire repointed fibre of a surjective coefficient map](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-h1-original-fibre-range).

**Checks.**

- `embedded_kernel_repointed_non_neutral`: For surjective f with `[f∘c]` nonneutral, the neutral class of `H¹(G,U)` is outside the translated embedded-kernel inclusion image.
- `embedded_kernel_inclusion_neutral`: The inclusion sends the class of the identity cocycle on `A_c` to the neutral class in `H¹(G,Twist(c))`.
- `embedded_kernel_inclusion_killed`: Every embedded-kernel `H¹` class maps to the neutral class under the quotient projection, without assuming f surjective.

### 0.31 Invariant orbit transport
<a id="nc-3-invariant-orbit-transport"></a>

**Invariant orbit transport.** For a surjective continuous equivariant `f:U→V` and `c∈Z1(G,U)`, let `K_c` be the kernel in the inner twist and `A_c=H0(G,V_{f∘c})`. Transport the parent `A_c`-action along its named-kernel or embedded-kernel H1 equivalence E, defining `v·a=E−1(v·E(a))`. E is orbit-equivariant and induces an equivalence of orbit quotients with the fibre `f_*−1([f∘c])`; its representative maps to `[g↦i(d(g))c(g)]`. Inclusion squares, stabilizers and conjugate actions under change of c commute. No equality of kernel classes is claimed when only invariant orbits agree.

Parent action, orbit-fibre equivalence and kernel homeomorphisms embedded i retains its given topology f surjective.

Use the parent E and its inverse to transport the action and prove the action laws. Use E equivariance for orbit and stabilizer equivalences and the parent inclusion triangle for the fibre map. For a representative change `c′=u·c`, conjugation by u identifies the two twists, kernels and invariant groups; compare representatives with the gauge law.

**Checks.**

- Transported stabilizers equal stabilizers; the orbit of the neutral kernel class maps to [c], which can be nonneutral.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), Section 1, twisting and nonabelian exactness, printed pp. 4–6.

Use [Twisted kernel invariant action](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-invariant-action); [Twisted kernel orbits and the original fibre](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-orbit-fibre-equivalence); [`Continuous H¹` comparison for the named kernel](#nc-3-named-kernel-h1-equivalence); [Comparison with the ambient inclusion](#nc-3-named-kernel-h1-inclusion-triangle); [`Continuous H¹` of an abstract embedded kernel](#nc-3-embedded-kernel-h1-equivalence); [Comparison of the two `H¹` inclusions](#nc-3-embedded-kernel-h1-inclusion-comparison).

### 0.32 Trivial connecting classes
<a id="nc-3-connecting-class-zero"></a>

**Trivial connecting class and fixed lifts.** For an admissible b and any `c ∈ Z¹(G,A)` with `i(c(g))=b⁻¹(g•b)`, `[c]=1` if and only if there is a `∈ A` for which `b i(a)` is G-fixed.

Standing hypotheses (H17).

Use the orbit-quotient characterisation: `[c]=1` iff `c(g)=a(g•a)⁻¹` for one a and all g. After applying i, rearrange `b⁻¹(g•b)=i(a)(g•i(a))⁻¹` into `g•(b i(a))=b i(a)`. Reverse the calculation for the converse.

**Checks.**

- This is exactness at invariant cosets expressed entirely in group carriers.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed pp. 5–6 (cocycle and orbit conventions), p. 9 (subgroup exactness).

Use [Nonabelian first cohomology as a pointed set](#nc-3-nonabelian-h1).

### 0.33 Equivariant torsors and their classification
<a id="nc-3-equivariant-topological-torsors"></a>

**Equivariant topological torsors and their isomorphisms.** For topological groups G and U with a jointly continuous G-action by automorphisms on U, a (G,U)-torsor is a NONEMPTY topological space P with a continuous right U-action, every orbit map `u↦p·u` a homeomorphism, and a jointly continuous left G-action satisfying g(p·u)=(gp)·(gu). An isomorphism `P≅Q` is a homeomorphism commuting with both actions. Existence of such an isomorphism defines an equivalence relation on torsors. A point p defines the continuous cocycle `c_p` by `gp=p·c_p(g)`. A continuous cocycle c gives the torsor model U with right multiplication and `g⋆u=c(g)·g(u)`, up to the harmless universe lift represented by its specified homeomorphism `U≅P_c`. Package the underlying right-action torsor as Torsor `Uᵐᵒᵖ P` with IsTopologicalTorsor P; only the compatible continuous G-action and its semilinearity are new data.

G and U are topological groups. The G-action on U is by group automorphisms and is jointly continuous. The carrier P is nonempty; a free transitive action stated without nonemptiness would also admit the empty space. Orbit maps have continuous inverses, not merely continuous bijections.

Reuse Torsor `Uᵐᵒᵖ P` and IsTopologicalTorsor P, including nonemptiness, free transitivity and continuous scalar division. Their orbit homeomorphism is Homeomorph.smulConst p; compose with MulOpposite.opHomeomorph to obtain `U≃P`. Conversely the original right-action/homeomorphic-orbit description gives the continuous scalar division by choosing one point and using its global coordinates, so this is the same mathematical object. Add only the semilinear continuous G-action. Reflexivity, symmetry and composition of action-compatible homeomorphisms prove the isomorphism relation is a setoid. The inverse of the orbit homeomorphism sends gp to `c_p(g)`. Semilinearity and cancellation yield `c_p(gh)=c_p(g)·g(c_p(h))`; its continuity is composition with the continuous G-orbit map. At `p·u` the cocycle is `u⁻¹c_p(g)g(u)`, exactly inverse-gauge translation under the Z1 action. An isomorphism carries p to a point with the same cocycle. In the model `P_c`, associativity of `g⋆u=c(g)g(u)` is the cocycle law. Joint continuity follows from the cocycle and original action. Right multiplication is semilinear, and left translation by a fixed point is a homeomorphism. These are authored topological abstractions of the pointwise calculation in Kim Proposition 1. Its filtered affine-algebra hypotheses, scheme descent and representability are not consequences of this abstraction.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor`: The semilinear G-action bundle over Torsor `Uᵐᵒᵖ P` and IsTopologicalTorsor P; torsor theory supplies nonemptiness and the homeomorphic orbit maps.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.Iso`: An isomorphism `P→Q` is a homeomorphism respecting the right U-action and the left G-action.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.Iso.ext`: Two torsor isomorphisms are equal when their underlying functions agree at every point.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.Iso.refl`: The identity homeomorphism is a torsor isomorphism `P→P`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.Iso.symm`: A torsor isomorphism `P→Q` has an inverse torsor isomorphism `Q→P`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.Iso.trans`: Composing torsor isomorphisms `P→Q` and `Q→R` gives an isomorphism `P→R`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.orbitHomeomorph`: For `p∈P`, the map `u↦p·u` is bundled as the homeomorphism `U≅P`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.orbitHomeomorph_apply`: The orbit homeomorphism at p evaluates at u to `p·u`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.ofCocycle`: For `c∈Z¹(G,U)`, construct the semilinear torsor model with action `g⋆u=c(g)g(u)`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.ofCocycleHomeomorph`: The model `P_c` has a specified homeomorphism `U≅P_c`, so universes do not force a definitional equality of carriers.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.ofCocycleHomeomorph_right`: The model homeomorphism sends xy to the right translate by y of the image of x.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.ofCocycleHomeomorph_left`: The G-translate of the model image of x equals the model image of `c(g)g(x)`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.cocycle`: The unique continuous cocycle `c_p` with `gp=p·c_p(g)`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.cocycle_spec`: `gp=p·c_p(g)` for every g.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.cocycle_change_point`: `c_(p·u)=u⁻¹·c_p` under the gauge action.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.cocycle_map_iso`: For an action-compatible homeomorphism `e:P→Q`, `c_(e(p))=c_p`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.cocycle_ofCocycle`: The cocycle of the model at the image of 1 is exactly c.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.isoSetoid`: The setoid relation on torsors is existence of an action-compatible homeomorphism, using its identity, inverse and composition.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.torsor_orbit_at_identity`: The orbit homeomorphism at p sends 1 to p.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.torsor_coboundary_isomorphic`: For every `u∈U`, the model of the coboundary `u·g(u)⁻¹` is isomorphic as a (G,U)-torsor to the model of the trivial cocycle.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.torsor_gauge_isomorphic`: The models of `u·c` and c are isomorphic as equivariant topological torsors.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.torsor_nonneutral_no_fixed_point`: If `[c]≠1`, the model `P_c` has no G-fixed point; an interface forgetting the G-action would wrongly identify it with the trivial torsor.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.torsor_inequivalent_not_isomorphic`: If `[c]≠[d]`, there is no action-compatible homeomorphism `P_c→P_d`, even though both underlying spaces are homeomorphic to U.
- The empty space is excluded explicitly.
- Do not quotient all torsor homeomorphisms: both the G-action and the U-action must be preserved.
- The model of a nonneutral cocycle has no G-fixed point; a gauge change gives an isomorphic model.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, Proposition 1 and its proof, printed pp. 5–7 (arXiv v1).

Use [Continuous 1-cocycles and invariants with nonabelian coefficients](#nc-3-continuous-cocycles); [Nonabelian first cohomology as a pointed set](#nc-3-nonabelian-h1); `Homeomorph`; `Torsor`; `IsTopologicalTorsor`; `Homeomorph.smulConst`; `MulOpposite.opHomeomorph`.
<a id="nc-3-torsor-classification"></a>

**Torsors under U with compatible G-action are classified by H¹(G, U).** A (G, U)-torsor is a nonempty topological space P with a continuous right action of U that is free and transitive, such that for one (equivalently every) `p ∈ P` the orbit map `U → P`, `u ↦ p·u`, is a homeomorphism, together with a continuous left action of G satisfying `g•(p·u) = (g•p)·(g•u)`. For `p ∈ P` let `c_p(g) ∈ U` be the unique element with `g•p = p·c_p(g)`. Then `c_p ∈ Z¹(G, U)`, `c_{p·u} = u⁻¹·c_p` under the twisted-conjugation action, so `[P] := [c_p] ∈ H¹(G, U)` is independent of p and of the isomorphism class of P; `P ↦ [P]` is a bijection from isomorphism classes of (G, U)-torsors to `H¹(G, U)`, the trivial torsor U corresponds to the base point, and P has a G-fixed point iff [P] is the base point. The inverse sends [c] to U with the twisted G-action `g ∗ u := c(g)·(g•u)`.

G is a topological group and U a topological group with an action of G by group automorphisms (MulDistribMulAction G U) such that the action map `G × U → U` is continuous (ContinuousSMul G U). Torsors are topological, with the orbit maps homeomorphisms; isomorphisms of torsors are homeomorphisms compatible with both actions.

Cocycle: `(gh)•p = g•(p·c_p(h)) = (g•p)·(g•c_p(h)) = p·c_p(g)·g•c_p(h)`, and freeness gives `c_p(gh) = c_p(g)·g•c_p(h)`. Continuity: `c_p` is the composite of `g ↦ g•p` with the inverse of the orbit homeomorphism. Change of point: `g•(p·u) = p·c_p(g)·(g•u) = (p·u)·u⁻¹c_p(g)(g•u)`, so `c_{pu}(g) = u⁻¹c_p(g)(g•u) = (u⁻¹·c_p)(g)`. An isomorphism of torsors carries p to a point with the same cocycle. Inverse: for `c ∈ Z¹`, the formula `g ∗ u := c(g)(g•u)` is a continuous action (cocycle identity) compatible with right multiplication, and its cocycle at the point 1 is c. Cohomologous cocycles give isomorphic torsors (left multiplication by u), and a torsor is isomorphic to the one built from `c_p` via the orbit map at p. A G-fixed point p has `c_p = 1`; conversely, if `c_p(g) = u·(g•u)⁻¹` for all g, then `g•(p·u) = p·c_p(g)·(g•u) = p·u`, so `p·u` is fixed.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.classOf`: The class `[c_p]` is independent of p.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.classOf_eq_mk_cocycle`: For every point p, `classOf(P)=[c_p]`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.classOf_ofCocycle`: `classOf(P_c)=[c]`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.classOf_eq_classOf_iff`: `classOf(P)=classOf(Q)` if and only if there exists an action-compatible homeomorphism `P→Q`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.classOf_surjective`: Every continuous `H¹` class is the class of a topological torsor model.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.classification`: The quotient of torsors by existence of action-compatible homeomorphisms is equivalent to `H¹(G,U)`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.classification_mk`: The equivalence sends the quotient class of P to `classOf(P)`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.classOf_eq_one_iff`: `classOf(P)=1` if and only if P has a G-fixed point.

**Checks.**

- The abstract right-torsor classification is applied to geometric path torsors through the effective filtered affine comparison in Layer 4; that comparison retains the algebraic coaction and filtration.
- After the separate Galois-descent/effectivity comparison, Poonen's §5.12 algebraic torsor classification agrees with the point-space class map for `G=Gal(k_s/k)`, `U=H(k_s)` discrete, in the smooth algebraic group scope. An arbitrary equivariant homeomorphism is not yet an algebraic torsor isomorphism.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, Proposition 1 and its proof, printed pp. 5–7 (arXiv v1); [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, proof of Proposition 1, p. 6; [Bjorn Poonen](#reference-poonen-rational-points), §5.12.4, Remark 5.12.13, p. 154.

### 0.34 Invariant cosets and the exact sequence of pointed sets
<a id="nc-3-quotient-action"></a>

**Equivariant subgroup coset action.** Equivariance of i makes the G-action on B descend to Mathlib’s left coset set `B/i(A)`, by supplying MulAction.QuotientAction `G i(A)`. Its action on representatives is `g·[b]=[g·b]`. This quotient is a set even when `i(A)` is nonnormal.

Groups G,A,B, actions by automorphisms on A and B, and an equivariant homomorphism i. Topology and injectivity are unnecessary for this set-action lemma.

If `b⁻¹b′=i(a)`, then `(g·b)⁻¹(g·b′)=g·(b⁻¹b′)=i(g·a)`. This is exactly the QuotientAction compatibility field. Install that proposition locally and use the pinned MulAction.quotient instance. Do not rebuild a quotient relation or assert group operations on `B/i(A)`.

**Checks.**

- The subgroup generated by a transposition in `S₃`, with trivial G-action, qualifies and gives three left cosets. Normality would wrongly exclude it.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed pp. 5–6 (continuous cocycle and gauge conventions) and p. 9 (subgroup exactness).

Use `MulDistribMulAction`; `MulAction.QuotientAction`; `MulAction.quotient`; `QuotientGroup.leftRel_apply`.
<a id="nc-3-fixed-coset-criterion"></a>

**Invariant coset membership criterion.** With the descended action, [b] belongs to the fixed-point set `(B/i(A))^G` if and only if `b⁻¹(g·b)` lies in `i(A)` for every g. This identifies the genuine invariant-coset carrier with the membership hypothesis of connectingCocycle.

Standing hypotheses (H26).

Use `MulAction.mem_fixedPoints` to test each g. `Quotient.smul_mk` identifies `g·[b]` with `[g·b]`. Apply QuotientGroup.eq to `[b]=[g·b]`, reversing the fixedness equality if necessary. The difference is `b⁻¹(g·b)`, in that order.

**Checks.**

- For `C₂` acting by negation on `C₄` with subgroup {0,2}, both cosets are invariant, although the odd coset has no fixed representative.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed pp. 5–6 (continuous cocycle and gauge conventions) and p. 9 (subgroup exactness).

Use [Equivariant subgroup coset action](#nc-3-quotient-action); `MulAction.fixedPoints`; `MulAction.mem_fixedPoints`; `MulAction.Quotient.smul_mk`; `QuotientGroup.eq`.

<a id="nc-3-invariant-coset-projection"></a>

**Projection of invariant elements to cosets.** Construct `π⁰:B^G → (B/i(A))^G` by sending the fixed element b to its left coset [b]. Here `B^G` is the fixed-point subgroup and `(B/i(A))^G` is the fixed-point subset of the coset type. The base point is `π⁰(1)`; no group structure is imposed on the coset set.

Standing hypotheses (H26).

The quotient class of b is fixed because every g fixes b. Package the class and this proof in the fixed-point subset. Use a local abbreviation InvariantCosets only to instantiate the two Mathlib carriers with the descended action; it is not a second invariant or quotient definition. The representative projection is literal. Right multiplication by an element of `i(A^G)` changes no left coset.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-invariant-coset-image"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.invariantCoset_apply` (*Underlying invariant coset projection*): For `b∈B^G`, the underlying coset of `π⁰(b)` equals [b] in `B/i(A)`. *Proof.* Unfold the subtype packaging of invariantCoset. The underlying value is the canonical quotient class.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.invariantCoset_one`: The underlying coset of `π⁰(1)` is [1], specifying the distinguished point without assuming a quotient group.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.invariantCoset_mul_image`: For `b∈B^G` and `a∈A^G`, `π⁰(b·i(a))=π⁰(b)`.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.invariantCoset_identity`: For `i=id_B` and every `b∈B^G`, `π⁰(b)=π⁰(1)`: the coset space is a singleton.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.invariantCoset_trivial_subgroup`: If `i(A)` is the trivial subgroup, `π⁰:B^G → (B/i(A))^G` is injective. A constant projection fails whenever `B^G` has two elements.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.invariantCoset_nonnormal`: For discrete `G=C₂` acting trivially on `B=S₃` and A the subgroup {1,(01)}, the invariant-coset type has cardinality three. The subgroup is nonnormal; a quotient-group requirement is invalid.
- The construction accepts a nonnormal subgroup. `π⁰` is a pointed-set map, not claimed to be a homomorphism on a nonexistent quotient group.
- The identity representative gives the distinguished coset [1].

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed pp. 5–6 (continuous cocycle and gauge conventions) and p. 9 (subgroup exactness).

Use [Equivariant subgroup coset action](#nc-3-quotient-action); [Invariant coset membership criterion](#nc-3-fixed-coset-criterion); [Continuous 1-cocycles and invariants with nonabelian coefficients](#nc-3-continuous-cocycles); [Functoriality of nonabelian `H⁰` and `H¹`](#nc-3-functoriality); `FixedPoints.subgroup`; `QuotientGroup.eq`.

<a id="nc-3-connecting-map"></a>

**Connecting map on invariant cosets.** Construct `δ:(B/i(A))^G → H¹(G,A)` on the invariant coset set. For an invariant coset q choose a representative b and put `δ(q)=[c_b]`, where `i(c_b(g))=b⁻¹(g·b)`. The result is independent of the representative. The source is a pointed set with point `π⁰(1)`; `δ` sends that point to the `H¹` base point.

Standing hypotheses (H26).

Choose b as the quotient representative q.out. `QuotientGroup.out_eq′` and [Invariant coset membership criterion](#nc-3-fixed-coset-criterion) turn q’s fixedness proof into the membership required by connectingCocycle. Apply the previously constructed continuous connectingCocycle and take its class in the previously constructed orbit quotient `H¹`. Continuity is already supplied by the embedding argument; this definition is not an arbitrary function admitted into `H¹`. Any second representative is `b·i(a)` for some a by QuotientGroup.eq and range membership (or `mk_out_eq_mul`). [Change of lift for a connecting cocycle](#nc-3-connecting-change-lift) gauges `c_b` by `a⁻¹` and hence preserves its `H¹` class. An invariant representative has trivial connecting cocycle; apply this to 1 to get preservation of the distinguished point. No topology on the coset set or continuous quotient section is needed for the set-valued map.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- <a id="nc-3-connecting-map-lift"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.connecting_mk` (*Representative formula for the connecting map*): If `q∈(B/i(A))^G` is represented by b and `b⁻¹(g·b)∈i(A)` for every g, then `δ(q)=[c_b]` with the previously constructed continuous connecting cocycle. This holds for every proof of membership and every representative. *Proof.* Compare the chosen representative q.out with b using equality of their left cosets. The coset equality criterion provides `a∈A` with q.out=b·i(a). [Change of lift for a connecting cocycle](#nc-3-connecting-change-lift) identifies the two cocycles by the gauge `a⁻¹`; the `H¹` orbit quotient gives equality of classes. Proof irrelevance and uniqueness of the lifted cocycle dispose of membership witnesses.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.connecting_invariantCoset`: For `b∈B^G`, `δ(π⁰(b))=1`. In particular `δ` preserves the distinguished point.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.connecting_change_representative`: If q and q′ have representatives b and `b·i(a)`, then `δ(q′)=δ(q)`. This compares coset inputs, not only their lift cocycles.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.connecting_coset_fixed`: For every equivariant closed embedding i and `b∈B^G`, the coset-map value `δ(π⁰(b))` is the base point.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.connecting_coset_identity`: For `i=id_B`, `δ(q)=1` for every invariant coset q, agreeing with `c_b=coboundary(b⁻¹)`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.connecting_coset_nontrivial`: For discrete `G=C₂`, `A=C₂` with trivial action, `B=C₄` with negation action, and `i(a)=2a` (doubling natural representatives modulo 4), the invariant odd coset `q=[1]` has `δ(q)≠1`. Its cocycle sends the nonidentity of G to the nonidentity of A; A-coboundaries are trivial. No fixed lift of q exists.
- The negation action on `C₄` gives a nontrivial boundary on its odd invariant coset modulo {0,2}. A constant boundary map fails this test.
- Both even lifts represent the even coset of `C₄/{0,2}`, and both odd lifts represent the odd coset. The class remains unchanged within each pair.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed pp. 5–6 (continuous cocycle and gauge conventions) and p. 9 (subgroup exactness).

<a id="nc-3-invariants-injection"></a>

**Injectivity on invariant subgroups.** The map `i⁰:A^G → B^G` induced by an equivariant closed embedding i is injective. Thus its base-point fibre is {1}, giving the initial exactness `at A^G` in `1 → A^G → B^G → (B/i(A))^G`.

Standing hypotheses (H26).

Equality of mapped fixed elements gives equality of their values under i. A closed embedding is injective. Apply that injectivity and subtype extensionality.

**Checks.**

- For the doubling `C₂ ↪ C₄` with the actions above, `A^G=C₂` maps bijectively onto `B^G={0,2}`.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed pp. 5–6 (continuous cocycle and gauge conventions) and p. 9 (subgroup exactness).

Use [Functoriality of nonabelian `H⁰` and `H¹`](#nc-3-functoriality); [Continuous 1-cocycles and invariants with nonabelian coefficients](#nc-3-continuous-cocycles).

<a id="nc-3-invariants-kernel"></a>

**Exactness at the invariant ambient group.** For `b∈B^G`, `π⁰(b)=π⁰(1)` if and only if b lies in the image of `i⁰:A^G → B^G`. This is pointed-set exactness `at B^G` for a subgroup that need not be normal.

Standing hypotheses (H26).

By [Underlying invariant coset projection](#nc-3-invariant-coset-image) and the quotient equality criterion, `π⁰(b)=π⁰(1)` says `b∈i(A)`. Choose `a∈A` with `i(a)=b`. Since b is fixed, equivariance gives `i(g·a)=g·i(a)=i(a)`; injectivity of i proves that a is fixed. Its subtype is a preimage under `i⁰`. Conversely an image element has coset [1], directly by range membership. Subtype extensionality identifies the fixed-coset elements.

**Checks.**

- With trivial C₂-action on `S₃` and the transposition subgroup, the base-coset fibre has two elements, precisely `A^G`, while there are three invariant cosets.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed pp. 5–6 (continuous cocycle and gauge conventions) and p. 9 (subgroup exactness).

Use [Underlying invariant coset projection](#nc-3-invariant-coset-image); [Functoriality of nonabelian `H⁰` and `H¹`](#nc-3-functoriality); [Injectivity on invariant subgroups](#nc-3-invariants-injection); `QuotientGroup.eq`.

<a id="nc-3-invariant-coset-kernel"></a>

**Exactness at invariant cosets.** For `q∈(B/i(A))^G`, `δ(q)=1` if and only if q is in the image of `π⁰:B^G → (B/i(A))^G`. Thus vanishing of the connecting class is equivalent to existence of a G-fixed representative of the coset.

Standing hypotheses (H26).

Choose b=q.out and use [Representative formula for the connecting map](#nc-3-connecting-map-lift) to evaluate `δ(q)`. [Trivial connecting class and fixed lifts](#nc-3-connecting-class-zero) says `[c_b]=1` exactly when `b·i(a)` is fixed for some `a∈A`. Such a fixed lift t represents q by the coset equality criterion. Package t in `B^G` and use [Underlying invariant coset projection](#nc-3-invariant-coset-image) to obtain `q=π⁰(t)`. Conversely `q=π⁰(t)` is represented by fixed t; evaluate `δ` by [Representative formula for the connecting map](#nc-3-connecting-map-lift) and use `connectingCocycle_eq_one_of_fixed`.

**Checks.**

- With trivial G-action every coset has a fixed representative and δ is the constant neutral class.
- For identity inclusion `A=B`, the coset set is a point and its boundary is neutral.
- For negation on `C₄` modulo {0,2}, only the even coset is in this kernel: the odd coset is invariant but has no fixed lift.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed pp. 5–6 (continuous cocycle and gauge conventions) and p. 9 (subgroup exactness).

Use [Representative formula for the connecting map](#nc-3-connecting-map-lift); [Trivial connecting class and fixed lifts](#nc-3-connecting-class-zero); [Underlying invariant coset projection](#nc-3-invariant-coset-image); `QuotientGroup.eq`.

<a id="nc-3-connecting-image-kernel"></a>

**Exactness at nonabelian first cohomology.** For `x∈H¹(G,A)`, `i_*(x)=1` in `H¹(G,B)` if and only if x lies in the image of the map `δ:(B/i(A))^G → H¹(G,A)`. This is the lift-form inclusion-kernel theorem transported to the coset carrier.

Standing hypotheses (H26).

[Kernel of inclusion in nonabelian cohomology](#nc-3-exact-sequence) supplies b and a continuous cocycle c with `x=[c]` and `i(c(g))=b⁻¹(g·b)`. This proves membership for each g. Use [Invariant coset membership criterion](#nc-3-fixed-coset-criterion) to package [b] as an invariant coset. Uniqueness of connectingCocycle and [Representative formula for the connecting map](#nc-3-connecting-map-lift) show that `δ([b])=[c]=x`. Conversely choose a representative of an invariant coset. Its connecting cocycle maps to the B-coboundary of `b⁻¹`, so the previously constructed inclusion-kernel theorem kills its class.

**Checks.**

- Identity inclusion has kernel consisting of its one neutral class.
- If G is trivial, both `H¹` sets are singletons and the connecting map reaches that class.
- For `C₂ ↪ C₄` as above, both `H¹(C₂,C₂)` classes are killed in `H¹(C₂,C₄)`, and the two invariant cosets supply precisely those two classes. This concerns the fibre over 1, not arbitrary untwisted fibres.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed pp. 5–6 (continuous cocycle and gauge conventions) and p. 9 (subgroup exactness).

<a id="nc-3-connecting-quotient-fibres"></a>

**Invariant ambient group orbits in boundary fibres.** For invariant cosets q,q′, `δ(q)=δ(q′)` if and only if `q′=[t·b]` for some `t∈B^G` and a representative b of q. Equivalently the fibres of `δ` are exactly the left `B^G`-orbits on the coset set. In the suggested form b is q.out; the condition is independent of that choice.

Standing hypotheses (H26).

Represent q and q′ by b and b′ and evaluate both boundaries by [Representative formula for the connecting map](#nc-3-connecting-map-lift). [Fibres of the connecting class](#nc-3-connecting-fixed-orbits) gives a fixed `t∈B` and `a∈A` with `b′=t·b·i(a)`. The coset equality criterion erases the right `i(a)` factor, giving `q′=[t·b]`. Conversely `q′=[t·b]` supplies a right factor `i(a)` between representatives. Apply the same fixed-orbit criterion and [Representative formula for the connecting map](#nc-3-connecting-map-lift). Left translation is well-defined because `(t·b)⁻¹(t·b′)=b⁻¹b′`. If t is fixed, `g·[t·b]=[t·(g·b)]=[t·b]`. This is the left coset action restricted to `B^G`, not quotient multiplication.

**Checks.**

- For identity inclusion the coset set and its unique boundary fibre are singletons.
- With trivial G-action on `C₂` and `A=1`, its two cosets have the same neutral boundary and form one `C₂`-orbit.
- With trivial G-action on `S₃` all three transposition-subgroup cosets form one left `B^G`-orbit and `δ` is trivial. For negation on `C₄`, `B^G={0,2}` fixes both cosets individually; their `δ` values differ.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed pp. 5–6 (continuous cocycle and gauge conventions) and p. 9 (subgroup exactness).
