### 0.35 Inflation–restriction exactness and the finite-quotient equivalence

Inflation–restriction exactness is supplied by native `res_eq_one_iff`, and uniqueness by `infl_injective`. The cocycle/neutral-fibre equivalences and categorical finite-colimit comparison below package these supplied maps with their specified forward formulas.

<a id="nc-3-finite-family-normal-killing"></a>

**Simultaneous killing for finite discrete cocycle families.** Let G be compact. For a finite index type I, discrete groups `U_i` with automorphism actions and continuous cocycles `c_i∈Z¹(G,U_i)`, there is one open normal N with `c_i(n)=1` for all i and `n∈N`. Groups and actions may vary with i, and `U_i` need not be finite. The empty family is included. Infinite families and nondiscrete coefficients do not satisfy this conclusion in general.

Standing hypotheses (H12).

Intersect the finitely many clopen one-fibre carriers; finite-intersection topology gives a clopen set containing 1. Apply the compact-group clopen-neighbourhood theorem once and read each coordinate membership from the intersection. No infinite intersection or uniform choice of subgroup for all cocycles is used.

**Checks.**

- For `G=∏_(n∈ℕ)C₂`, the first r coordinate characters are killed by their common finite-index kernel. All coordinate characters together have trivial common kernel, which is not open.

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.exists_openNormal_killing_family.test_empty`: For `I=Fin0` the class-killing condition is vacuous and an open normal subgroup exists.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.exists_openNormal_killing_family.test_single`: Specializing the varying-coefficient family theorem to Fin1 and one c gives its pointwise normal-open killing conclusion.

The construction and its conventions follow [Native nonabelian H¹](#native-nonabelian-h1), the proof of `exists_mem_range_infl`, applied to the finite intersection of one-fibres; the displayed proof is an elementary deduction.

<a id="nc-3-quotient-cocycle-equivalence"></a>

**Equivalence of cocycle spaces.** For any normal `N≤G`, the subtype of continuous G-cocycles trivial on N is equivalent to `Z¹(G/N,U^N)`. Forward map is descent and inverse is inflation together with its proved triviality on N; both inverse identities hold. This is a cocycle-level equivalence, not a full `H¹` equivalence.

Standing hypotheses (H13).

Package the two cocycle maps and their inverse identities in Equiv. Subtype extensionality removes only the proof of triviality, not the genuine condition.

<a id="nc-3-h1-inflation-restriction-image"></a>

**Nonabelian inflation–restriction exactness.** For every `a∈H¹(G,U)`, a belongs to the set-theoretic image of `inflate_N:H¹(G/N,U^N)→H¹(G,U)` if and only if `res_N(a)=1`. This is equality with the neutral restriction fibre as pointed sets, not equality of group kernels.

Standing hypotheses (H27).

An inflated class has neutral restriction by the preceding lemma. For the reverse implication choose a cocycle representative c. The representative restriction API and neutral-class criterion give a `x∈U` with `c(n)=x(n•x)⁻¹` on N. The proved inverse-gauge normalization constructs `c′=x⁻¹·c` identically 1 on N. Descent produces `d∈Z¹(G/N,U^N)`, and inflate(descend(c′))=c′. Representative inflation and gauge invariance give inflate([d])=[c′]=[c]=a. The subgroup is never refined; no hypothetical cohomology bridge or chosen cocycle representative is built into the statement.

**Checks.**

- The coefficient group can be noncommutative. The `S₃` conjugation test shows why the reverse implication needs gauge normalization before literal cocycle descent. No compactness or discreteness is required under the explicit [Equivariant subgroup coset action](#nc-3-quotient-action) continuity hypothesis.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, printed pp. 5–6, continuous cocycle and gauge definitions; authored inflation–restriction deduction.

<a id="nc-3-h1-inflation-neutral-equivalence"></a>

**Inflation equivalence with the neutral restriction fibre.** Construct the pointed-set equivalence `H¹(G/N,U^N) ≃ {a ∈ H¹(G,U) | res_N(a)=1}`. Its forward map is exactly a `↦ (inflate_N(a), res_N(inflate_N(a))=1)`, and its inverse recovers the unique same-N source class. Joint continuity of the quotient action follows from [Joint continuity of the fixed-subgroup quotient action](#nc-3-quotient-fixed-action-continuity), not an extra hypothesis. This is not an equivalence with all of `H¹(G,U)`, nor a group isomorphism.

G is a group with a topology and separately continuous multiplication; in particular every topological group satisfies this assumption. U is a group with a topology and a jointly continuous G-action by group automorphisms. N is an arbitrary normal subgroup. Use the quotient topology on `G/N` and the topology and quotient action on the fixed `subgroup U^N`. No compactness, open/closed N, discrete/finite coefficients or commutativity is assumed. U is a topological group; this makes the coefficient gauge action on continuous cocycles available.

Provide the quotient action's ContinuousSMul by [Joint continuity of the fixed-subgroup quotient action](#nc-3-quotient-fixed-action-continuity) locally, without a global overlapping instance; the fixed subgroup inherits its topological group structure. Use [Neutrality of restriction after inflation](#nc-3-h1-restriction-inflation) to define inflation into the neutral-fibre subtype. [Injectivity of nonabelian inflation](#nc-3-h1-inflation-injective) proves injectivity after forgetting the subtype proof. [Nonabelian inflation–restriction exactness](#nc-3-h1-inflation-restriction-image) provides a source class for every neutral restricted class; subtype extensionality gives surjectivity. Apply Equiv.ofBijective with this specified forward map. Forward evaluation is definitional. `Equiv.symm_apply_apply` and `Equiv.apply_symm_apply` give the inverse APIs; forgetting the subtype proof yields their `H¹` equalities. [Inflation preserves the distinguished cohomology class](#nc-3-h1-inflation-one) proves pointedness.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.inflateNeutralEquiv_apply`: For every a `∈ H¹(G/N,U^N)`, the underlying ambient class of `inflateNeutralEquiv_N(a)` is `inflate_N(a)`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.inflateNeutralEquiv_symm_inflate`: For every a `∈ H¹(G/N,U^N)`, the inverse at the neutral-fibre element defined by `inflate_N(a)` equals a.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.inflateNeutralEquiv_apply_symm`: For every b in the neutral restriction fibre, inflating its inverse image gives the underlying class of b.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.inflateNeutralEquiv_one`: `inflateNeutralEquiv_N` sends the distinguished source class to the distinguished ambient class with its proved neutral restriction.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.inflateNeutralEquiv.test_one`: The forward equivalence sends the distinguished quotient class to the neutral-fibre element with underlying class 1.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.inflateNeutralEquiv.test_representative`: For each quotient cocycle d, the underlying class of `inflateNeutralEquiv_N([d])` is the genuine class `[inflate_N(d)]`.

The representing cocycle need not literally be 1, as the inherited `S₃` conjugation example exhibits.

- No surjectivity of inflation onto all of `H¹(G,U)` is asserted.

### 0.37 Gauge stabilizers, gauge witnesses and kernel injectivity
<a id="nc-3-gauge-stabilizer-fixed"></a>

**Gauge stabilizers are twisted invariants.** For a continuous cocycle c and `x∈U`, x belongs to the gauge stabilizer `Stab_U(c)` exactly when its underlying element in `Twist(c)` is G-fixed. No topology on the space of cocycles is required. The pointwise algebraic equivalence also holds for arbitrary functions c.

Standing hypotheses (H28).

Expand the ordered gauge equation `x c(g)(g•x)⁻¹=c(g)`. Multiply on the right by `g•x` and compare with the already specified twisted-invariant equation `c(g)(g•x)=x c(g)`.

**Checks.**

- For the neutral cocycle the stabilizer is the invariant subgroup of the original action.
- With trivial action, the stabilizer is the centralizer of the image of c; it need not be trivial.
- For the neutral cocycle and trivial action on `S₃`, both (01) and (12) fix the cocycle; the stabilizer is all `S₃`, while their two product orders differ.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1 continuous cocycle/gauge conventions, pp. 5–6; Proposition 2 freeness claim and complete proof, pp. 8–9.

- <a id="nc-3-gauge-transporter-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.gaugeTransporterEquiv_apply` (*Gauge transporter forward formula*): The underlying U-value of the transporter image of s is x s. *Proof.* Evaluate the forward subtype map.
- <a id="nc-3-gauge-transporter-inverse-value"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.gaugeTransporterEquiv_symm_apply` (*Gauge transporter inverse formula*): The underlying U-value of the transporter inverse at y is `x⁻¹y`. *Proof.* Evaluate the inverse subtype map.
- <a id="nc-3-gauge-transporter-continuity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.gaugeTransporterEquiv_continuous` (*Continuous gauge transporter*): The stabilizer-to-transporter equivalence is continuous. *Proof.* Multiply the continuous subtype inclusion by the constant x on the left and restrict its codomain.
- <a id="nc-3-gauge-transporter-inverse-continuity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.gaugeTransporterEquiv_symm_continuous` (*Continuous inverse transporter*): The transporter-to-stabilizer inverse is continuous. *Proof.* Multiply the continuous subtype inclusion by the constant `x⁻¹` and restrict its codomain.
- <a id="nc-3-gauge-witness-uniqueness"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.gauge_witness_unique_iff` (*Uniqueness of a gauge witness*): If `x•c=d`, all witnesses `y•c=d` equal x exactly when `Stab_U(c)` is the trivial subgroup. This is uniqueness of a group element, distinct from uniqueness of a class in kernel `H¹`. *Proof.* If witnesses are unique, apply uniqueness to x s for each stabilizer element s and cancel x. Conversely the transporter iff puts `x⁻¹y` in the trivial subgroup, forcing `y=x`.
- <a id="nc-3-kernel-gauge-fixed-projection"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.kernel_gauge_projects_fixed` (*Kernel gauge witnesses project to invariants*): Let `i:A→U` be continuous and equivariant, `f:U→V` continuous and equivariant, and `f∘i=1` pointwise. For `c,d∈Z¹(G,A)`, an ambient gauge x carrying `i∘c` to `i∘d` has `f(x)∈H⁰(G,V)`. No injectivity or surjectivity is needed for this lemma. *Proof.* Apply f pointwise to the gauge equality. Both cocycle values map to 1, so `f(x)(g•f(x))⁻¹=1` for every g. Cancel to obtain invariance. Uses [Coefficient map on continuous cocycles](#nc-3-coefficient-cocycle-map); [Nonabelian first cohomology as a pointed set](#nc-3-nonabelian-h1).
- <a id="nc-3-kernel-injectivity-stabilizer-lifts"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.kernelMap_injective_of_stabilizer_lifts` (*Kernel H¹ injectivity from stabilizer lifts*): Let `i:A→U` be continuous, equivariant and injective, with `range(i)=ker(f)` for a continuous equivariant `f:U→V`. Suppose for every `c∈Z¹(G,A)` and every `v∈H⁰(G,V)`, there is `t∈Stab_U(i∘c)` with `f(t)=v`. Then the inclusion map `H¹(G,A)→H¹(G,U)` is injective. Neither f-surjectivity nor a continuous section is assumed. *Proof.* Represent two equal ambient classes by c,d and a gauge x. Its projection is fixed. Lift `f(x)` to t stabilizing `i∘c`. The corrected gauge `x t⁻¹` lies in `ker(f)`, still carries `i∘c` to `i∘d`, and therefore comes from `y∈A`. Injectivity of i reflects the pointwise gauge equality, proving equality of the two original classes. Uses [Kernel gauge witnesses project to invariants](#nc-3-kernel-gauge-fixed-projection); [Coefficient map on nonabelian cohomology](#nc-3-coefficient-h1-map).
- <a id="nc-3-kernel-injectivity-fixed-trivial"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.kernelMap_injective_of_fixed_trivial` (*Kernel H¹ injectivity for trivial quotient invariants*): Under the same continuous equivariant injection and exact-image hypotheses, `H⁰(G,V)=1` implies injectivity of `H¹(G,A)→H¹(G,U)`. This is a sufficient hypothesis, not a necessary characterization of injectivity. *Proof.* Every fixed v equals 1; choose the identity element of the stabilizer as its lift and apply the stabilizer-lift criterion. Uses [Kernel `H¹` injectivity from stabilizer lifts](#nc-3-kernel-injectivity-stabilizer-lifts).
- <a id="nc-3-twisted-kernel-inclusion-injectivity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistedKernelInclusion_injective` (*Injective inclusion of the twisted kernel*): For `c∈Z¹(G,U)` and continuous equivariant `f:U→V`, if `H⁰(G,Twist(f∘c))=1` then the already constructed twisted-kernel `H¹` inclusion into `H¹(G,Twist(c))` is injective. The invariant condition belongs to the target inner twist, not automatically to the original V-action. *Proof.* Apply the general kernel criterion to the subtype inclusion of `ker(F_c)`, the continuous equivariant twisted map `F_c` and its exact kernel. The inherited action is the restricted inner action. Uses [Kernel `H¹` injectivity for trivial quotient invariants](#nc-3-kernel-injectivity-fixed-trivial); [`H¹` map from the twisted kernel](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-h1-inclusion); [Coefficient homomorphism between inner twists](#nc-3-twist-coefficient-map); [Continuity of a twisted coefficient map](#nc-3-twist-coefficient-continuity); [Equivariance between the two twisted actions](#nc-3-twist-coefficient-equivariance); [Continuous automorphism action on the twisted kernel](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-action); [Joint continuity on the twisted kernel](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-action-continuity).
- <a id="nc-3-embedded-kernel-inclusion-injectivity"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.embeddedKernelInclusion_injective` (*Injective H¹ of an abstract embedded kernel*): For a supplied topological embedding `i:A→U` exactly onto `ker(f)`, with its transported inner action, `H⁰(G,Twist(f∘c))=1` makes the embedded-kernel inclusion on `H¹` injective. The topology and multiplication on A are retained. *Proof.* Compare the two inclusions using the already specified pointed `H¹` equivalence E. Apply native-kernel injectivity and then injectivity of E. Uses [Injective inclusion of the twisted kernel](#nc-3-twisted-kernel-inclusion-injectivity); [`Continuous H¹` of an abstract embedded kernel](#nc-3-embedded-kernel-h1-equivalence); [Comparison of the two `H¹` inclusions](#nc-3-embedded-kernel-h1-inclusion-comparison).
- <a id="nc-3-embedded-kernel-fibre-unique"></a>`TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.embeddedKernel_fibre_existsUnique` (*Unique embedded-kernel class in a repointed fibre*): If additionally f is surjective, then for `a∈H¹(G,U)` there exists exactly one `b∈H¹(G,A_c)` with twistEquiv(c)(j(b))=a exactly when `f*(a)=[f∘c]`, provided `H⁰(G,Twist(f∘c))=1`. Uniqueness concerns a gauge class; it does not select or uniquely determine a cocycle or gauge element. *Proof.* Use the surjective-map image criterion to obtain a kernel class in the original repointed fibre. The twist equivalence and the new inclusion injectivity give uniqueness. Conversely any preimage lies in the specified fibre. Uses [`Injective H¹` of an abstract embedded kernel](#nc-3-embedded-kernel-inclusion-injectivity); [Abstract kernel image in the original repointed fibre](#nc-3-embedded-kernel-repointed-range); [Gauge-orbit bijection under twisting](#nc-3-twist-h1-equivalence).

**Checks.**

- `gauge_transporter_inverse`: Every transporter element is recovered after applying the transporter inverse and forward maps.
- `gauge_transporter_right_order`: If `x s≠s x` for a stabilizer element s, the transporter image is not s x. Swapping the side of the stabilizer correction fails.
- `gauge_transporter_continuous_roundtrip`: The inverse composed with the forward transporter map is continuous for the subspace topologies.
- `gauge_witness_nonunique`: A nonidentity stabilizer element s supplies a second witness `x s≠x` for the same cocycle gauge equality.
- `gauge_witness_unique`: If the stabilizer is trivial, every second gauge witness y equals the specified witness x.
- For the neutral cocycle and trivial action on `S₃`, both (01) and (12) fix the cocycle; the stabilizer is all `S₃`, while their two product orders differ.
- `injective_coefficients_noninjective_h1`: With discrete trivial actions, the injective homomorphism `C₃→S₃` sending a generator to `p=(01)(12)` maps the distinct `H¹` classes of identity and inversion `C₃→C₃` to the same S₃-valued `H¹` class: conjugation by (01) interchanges p and `p⁻¹`. Injectivity of a coefficient embedding alone is insufficient.
- `kernel_neutral_reflection`: Under the exact-image, coefficient-injectivity and trivial-quotient-invariants hypotheses, the inclusion sends a class to the neutral class exactly when the original class is neutral.
- `trivial_action_fixed_obstruction`: For a trivial G-action on V and a specified `v≠1`, `H⁰(G,V)` is not the trivial subgroup. The injectivity hypothesis cannot be silently discharged by naming an exact sequence.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1 continuous cocycle/gauge conventions, pp. 5–6; Proposition 2 freeness claim and complete proof, pp. 8–9.

Use [Gauge witnesses differ by a right stabilizer](#nc-3-gauge-transporter-characterisation); `MulAction.stabilizer`.

### Examples

Take the discrete groups `G=U=S₃` with trivial action and the identity homomorphism as a cocycle. At `g=(01)`, `h=(12)`, the cocycle product is (01)(12), whereas reversing the factors gives (12)(01), its inverse three-cycle. This fixes the ordered cocycle convention. For `G=C₂` with trivial action on `S₃`, the four cocycles are the homomorphisms sending the generator to 1 or one of the three transpositions. Gauge conjugation has two orbits, so `H¹` has two elements. Replacing this pointed orbit set by the set of homomorphisms loses the distinction between representatives and classes.

For `C₉→C₃`, choose the least-residue lift `a↦a` in {0,1,2}. With additive notation, its positive defect at (2,1) is `2+1−0=3` in `C₉`. Identifying the kernel `3C₉` with `C₃` gives 1. The inverse convention gives `−3=6` in `C₉` and `−1=2` in `C₃`. Thus their obstruction classes have opposite signs, but both are nonzero. At (0,1) the defect is zero. The distinction survives transport to the canonical continuous `H²` carrier.

Faithful coefficient maps need not be injective on `H¹`. With trivial actions, `C₃` embeds in `S₃`, and the two nontrivial homomorphisms `C₃→C₃` give distinct classes in `H¹(C₃,C₃)`. Their images send a generator to the two conjugate three-cycles, so they give the same S₃-valued class. The twisted fixed-quotient hypothesis in the injectivity criterion detects precisely the missing conjugating gauges.

For an inner twist of a trivial action by the identity cocycle `S₃→S₃`, the fixed group becomes the centre, hence has one element, whereas the original fixed group has six. For the cocycle determined by a transposition from `C₂`, the twisted fixed group is its centralizer, of order two. Twisting therefore changes `H⁰` as well as repointing `H¹`. The translation of twisted cocycles is `d(g)c(g)`; the reverse order does not give the same repointing map.

Finally, a finite quotient of a profinite source records cocycles valued in the fixed subgroup of its open normal kernel. Every ambient gauge relating two inflated cocycles is automatically fixed by that same kernel, so inflation reflects equality without refining the quotient.


The ordered cocycle law forces the identity value to be one. Gauge translation preserves this law and, under joint continuity of the action on the topological coefficient group, preserves continuity. These assertions use the inverse gauge parameter fixed above and require no topology on `H¹`.


For `G=U=S₃` acting on U by conjugation, `c(g)=g⁻¹` is an ordered cocycle. Put `a=(01)`, `x=(01)`, `y=(12)` and t=xy. The reversed gauge expression `d(g)=g(a⁻¹)c(g)a` gives `d(x)=x`, `d(y)=y` and `d(t)=1`. Its required cocycle right side at (x,y) is d(x)x(d(y))=yx≠1. Thus this expression does not preserve cocycles. In contrast, the declared constant gauge `a·c(g)=a c(g)g(a)⁻¹` equals `c(g)` in this example. Repointing a right torsor by `p↦p·a` gives `a⁻¹c(g)g(a)`, which is the declared gauge with parameter `a⁻¹` (Kim, published survey, p. 642, read together with the torsor action on pp. 637–641).

## Layer 1: Étale K(π,1) schemes and arithmetic paths

Connect the finite-cover category to continuous cohomology, prove the finite-cover effacement criterion and its geometric applications, and give arithmetic paths the semilinear action required by the first layer. Tangential specialization keeps its local inertia orientation.

### 1.1 Arithmetic paths and endpoint sections

<a id="tangential-fibre-functors"></a>

**Tangential fibre functors and their analytic comparison.** Let k be a field of characteristic zero, C a smooth geometrically connected curve over k, `x∈C(k)`, `U=C∖{x}`, and t a nonzero k-rational tangent vector at x. Define the tangential fibre functor `F_t` on finite étale covers of U as the composite of the restriction functor `R_x`, from finite étale covers of U to finite étale covers of the punctured tangent space `T°_x=T_x∖{0}` (at each point y above x, pass to the associated graded rings of the valuation filtrations, so that the cover becomes a finite étale cover of `T°_x≅𝔾_m`), with the fibre functor of `T°_x` at the point t. Over an algebraically closed k it is a fibre functor of the Galois category of U, and the choice of a compatible system `ζ=(ζ_n)` of roots of unity gives a canonical inertia generator `γ_t∈π₁(U,F_t)`, acting on the fibre of the cover `z↦zⁿ` of `T°_x` through `z↦ζ_n z`. Over a non-closed k, `F_t` has a continuous Gal(k̄/k)-action and the restriction of `F_t` to the constant covers `Spec(k′)×U` is the standard fibre functor of Spec k. In characteristic zero every finite étale cover of the punctured formal disc is tame, so the rational (Puiseux) and tame tangential fibre functors agree on the one category of finite étale covers of U. For `k=ℂ`, `F_t` is identified with the topological fibre functor at a point of a small punctured disc in the direction t, and `γ_t` with the positively oriented loop around x when `ζ_n=exp(2πi/n)`. The involution `ι(z)=1/z` of `P¹∖{0,1,∞}` carries the functor at `t₀` to the functor at `ι*t₀` and `γ_0` to `γ_∞`.

k of characteristic zero; C smooth, geometrically connected; x a k-point and `t≠0` a k-rational tangent vector. For the analytic comparison, `k=ℂ`; an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero is reduced to `ℂ` by the invariance of the fundamental group under extension of algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero, as in Chen's Remark 4.2.4. The zero tangent vector is excluded.

`R_x` is exact and preserves finite limits and coproducts, so the composite with a fibre functor of `T°_x` is a fibre functor. The canonical generator is defined on the cofinal system `z↦zⁿ` and is compatible with n | m because `ζ_m^(m/n)=ζ_n`. The Galois action comes from the k-rationality of t. Tameness in characteristic zero is the Puiseux theorem: every finite extension of k̄((z)) is `k̄((z^(1/n)))`. For the analytic comparison, a local coordinate identifies a punctured disc around x with a punctured disc of `T_x`; GAGA identifies analytic and algebraic finite covers; the positive loop acts on the n-th root as multiplication by `exp(2πi/n)`. For `ι`, compute `ι` on the cover `z↦zⁿ` near 0 and `∞`.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.Anabelian.tangentialFiber`: The functor `F_t` on finite étale covers of U.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.tangentialFiber.isFiberFunctor`: Over algebraically closed k, `F_t` is a fibre functor of the Galois category of U.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.tangentialFiber.inertiaGenerator`: The canonical `γ_t` determined by t and `ζ`.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.tangentialFiber.galoisAction`: Over a non-closed k, the continuous Gal(k̄/k)-action on `F_t`, trivial on the identification for constant covers.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.tangentialFiber.tame_eq`: The rational and tame tangential functors coincide in characteristic zero.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.tangentialFiber.analyticIso`: For `k=ℂ`, the identification with the fibre at a nearby point in direction t, carrying `γ_t` to the positive loop.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.tangentialFiber.inversion`: `ι*` identifies the functors at `t₀` and `ι*t₀` and sends `γ_0` to `γ_∞`.

**Checks.**

- For `U=𝔾_m=P¹∖{0,∞}`, `x=0`, t=d/dz and the cover `z↦zⁿ`, `F_t` is the set of n-th roots of 1 in the tangent line, of size n, and `γ_t` acts as multiplication by `ζ_n`; for `t′=λ·t` the fibre is the set of n-th roots of `λ`, so the two functors are isomorphic but not equal.
- Replacing `ζ` by `ζ⁻¹` replaces `γ_t` by `γ_t⁻¹`: over `ℂ` with `ζ_n=exp(−2πi/n)` the comparison sends `γ_t` to the negatively oriented loop, so the orientation clause is not automatic.
- In characteristic `p>0` the Artin–Schreier cover `y^p−y=1/z` of the punctured disc is wild, so the tame functor sees fewer covers than the rational one; the equality clause is restricted to characteristic zero.
- The constant cover `Spec(k(√2))×U` over `k=ℚ` has fibre the two embeddings of `ℚ(√2)` in k̄ under `F_t`, with Galois acting by swapping them: the restriction to constant covers is the fibre functor of Spec k.

The construction and its conventions follow [William Y. Chen](#reference-chen2024), §4.2, the functor `R_x` and Definitions 4.2.1–4.2.2, pp. 363–364, Proposition 4.2.3, pp. 364–365, and Remarks 4.2.4–4.2.5, p. 365; §4.3, the involution `ι` and Definition 4.3.1, pp. 365–366. Chen works over an algebraically closed field; the Galois action for a k-rational tangent vector is Deligne's (Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points, 1989, §15), which Chen cites in Remark 4.2.4.

Use [InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups](../InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups/README.md) §IG.1.2 (tame tangential fibres at a boundary point); [InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups](../InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups/README.md) §IG.3.1 (Riemann existence for punctured curves); `CategoryTheory.PreGaloisCategory.FiberFunctor`.

<a id="nc-0-arithmetic-geometric-paths"></a>

**Arithmetic path torsor.** Let `X/k` be geometrically connected, qcqs and finite type, with rational endpoints b,x (or tame rational tangential endpoints on a smooth curve, in characteristic zero). Import `F_b,F_x` on finite étale covers and their identifications `r_b,r_x` on constant covers K:FEt(k)→FEt(X). Define `P(b,x)` to be natural isomorphisms `p:F_b≅F_x` with `K*p=r_b` followed by `r_x` inverse. Equivalently these are geometric paths on X over a separable closure, not all arithmetic paths. Its profinite topology is the closed identity fibre of restriction to constants. It is a nonempty right `N_b`-torsor, `N_b=ker(q_b)`, by `p·h=p` after h. For endpoint sections `s_b,s_x`, `sigma(p)=s_x(sigma) p s_b(sigma)^(-1)`. With `alpha_b(sigma)(h)=s_b(sigma) h s_b(sigma)^(-1)`, this is a jointly continuous semilinear `Gamma_k` action and hence an equivariant topological torsor in the sense of [Equivariant topological torsors and their isomorphisms](#nc-3-equivariant-topological-torsors).

Geometrically connected qcqs finite-type `X/k`; chosen separable closure and geometric realizations of the endpoints. Endpoint sections and restriction-to-constants identifications are supplied by EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.0.A2 and §F.0.2. Tangential endpoints are k-rational nonzero vectors; full finite covers only in characteristic zero.

Use IG.0 natural-isomorphism paths and IG.1 exactness to identify the identity fibre with paths on X over the separable closure. Nonemptiness also follows by correcting an ordinary path with the endpoint section on constants. For any p, `h↦p·h` identifies the identity fibre with the kernel: freeness and transitivity are cancellation of natural isomorphisms. The identification is a homeomorphism with the imported profinite topology. Sections are compatible on constants, so `s_x` sigma `p s_b` sigma inverse stays in the fibre. Multiply the formulas to verify the group action and semilinearity; continuity is inherited from evaluation and composition. Apply [Torsors under U with compatible G-action are classified by `H¹(G, U)`](#nc-3-torsor-classification).

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `ArithmeticPath.ext`: Two arithmetic paths with equal underlying natural isomorphisms are equal; the restriction proof carries no extra data.
- `ArithmeticPath.restrict_id`: Restriction to constants, transported by `r_b` and `r_x`, is the identity.
- `ArithmeticPath.identity`: The identity natural isomorphism is the path from an endpoint to itself.
- `ArithmeticPath.rightMul`: Translate a path by a source automorphism restricting to identity.
- `ArithmeticPath.galoisAction`: Compatible source/target lifts induce the action a inverse, then p, then b.
- `ArithmeticPath.rightMul_val`: Underlying natural isomorphism of `p·h` is h followed by p.
- `ArithmeticPath.existsUnique_translation`: For natural isomorphisms `p,q:F≅H`, there is a unique source automorphism a with a followed by p equal to q. If p and q have the same restriction to constants, a restricts to the identity; this gives freeness and transitivity on the arithmetic path fibre.
- `ArithmeticPath.galoisAction_val`: Underlying natural isomorphism is a inverse followed by p followed by b.
- `pathAction_mul`: In kernel coordinates, pathAction(s0,s1,sigma*tau,h)=pathAction(s0,s1,sigma,pathAction(s0,s1,tau,h)).
- `pathAction_continuous`: The action on Gamma times `ker(q)` is jointly continuous.

- `arithmeticPath_identity`: The constructed identity path has underlying Iso.refl.
- `arithmeticPath_translation_ne`: For `h≠1` in the geometric kernel, `p·h≠p`.

<a id="nc-0-transferred-endpoint-section"></a>

**Path transport of an endpoint section.** For p in `P(b,x)`, define `t_x,p(sigma)=p^(-1) s_x(sigma) p`, a continuous section of `q_b`. For p replaced by `p·h`, `t_x,p·h=h^(-1)t_x,p h`, with h in `N_b`. Transport along p followed by q equals iterated transport. Thus the geometric-conjugacy class attached to one rational or tangential point is independent of the geometric path. Endpoint sections and ordinary basepoint change are supplied by EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§F.0.A2, F.0.2.

Same arithmetic endpoints and constants as [Arithmetic path torsor](#nc-0-arithmetic-geometric-paths). p lies over identity on constants; unrestricted arithmetic paths need not transport to a section of the same `q_b`.

Conjugation by a natural isomorphism is a continuous homomorphism on Aut groups. Use the restriction condition to check `q_b t_x,p=id`. Substitute `p·h` and cancel adjacent inverses. Associativity of natural-isomorphism composition gives the iterated-transport identity.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `transportedSection_apply`: `t_x,p(sigma)=p` inverse `s_x(sigma) p`.
- `transportedSection_changePath`: `t_x,p·h(sigma)=h` inverse `t_x,p(sigma) h`.
- `transportedSection_comp`: Transport along a composite is iterated transport.

**Checks.**

- `transportedSection_identity`: Identity transport leaves the continuous section unchanged.
- `transportedSection_translation`: Conjugating the changed-path section by h recovers the original.
- `transportedSection_inverse_order`: When h inverse g h differs from h g h inverse, backward transport uses the former.
- Path changes conjugate by geometric kernel elements.
- Changing the rational point is not a path-choice change and has no automatic conjugacy conclusion.

The construction and its conventions follow [The Stacks Project Authors](#reference-stacks), Theorem 58.6.2 (0BND); Lemma 58.14.3 (0BTX); [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), Section 1, Proposition 1 and proof, PDF pp. 5–7.

<a id="nc-0-arithmetic-path-cocycle"></a>

**Cocycle of a geometric arithmetic path.** For p in `P(b,x)` set `c_p(sigma)=p^(-1)sigma(p)` in `N_b`. Then `c_p(sigma*tau)=c_p(sigma) alpha_b(sigma)(c_p(tau))` and `c_p·h(sigma)=h^(-1)c_p(sigma) alpha_b(sigma)(h)`. It is continuous. Hence its class in the nonabelian `H¹(Γ_k, N_b)` of Layer 0 depends only on the equivariant path torsor. In coordinates for any continuous q:E→Gamma and two continuous sections s0,s1, pathAction(sigma,h)=s1(sigma) `h s0(sigma)^(-1)`, and `pathCocycle_h=h^(-1)pathAction(sigma,h)`. For geometry s1 is the transferred endpoint section at a chosen reference path; the kernel model is not a substitute geometric path type. The inverse-parameter gauge formula also holds in a common group frame.

Arithmetic-path carrier and jointly continuous action as above. `H¹` is the pointed gauge-orbit set of [Nonabelian first cohomology as a pointed set](#nc-3-nonabelian-h1).

Restriction to constants of p inverse sigma(p) is identity, so the value lies in the kernel. Write sigma(p)=p `c_p(sigma)` and use semilinearity to obtain the cocycle law. Substitute `p·h` for the gauge formula. Apply the torsor classification of Layer 0; prove continuity using the orbit-map homeomorphism. The coordinate formula follows after choosing one path.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `pathCocycle_apply`: Coordinate value equals h inverse s1(sigma) h s0(sigma) inverse.
- `pathCocycle_mul`: c(sigma*tau)=c(sigma) `alpha_b(sigma)(c(tau))`.
- `pathCocycle_changePoint`: At `h*k` the cocycle is k inverse `c_h(sigma) alpha_b(sigma)(k)`.

**Checks.**

- `pathCocycle_same_sections`: At `h=1` and `s0=s1` the cocycle is 1 at every sigma.
- `pathCocycle_changed_representative`: For equal sections, `alpha_b(sigma)(h)≠h` forces `c_h(sigma)≠1`.
- `pathCocycle_distinct_sections`: If s1(sigma)≠s0(sigma), `c_1(sigma)≠1`.

- Different path representatives are gauge-equivalent and can have different values.

<a id="nc-0-path-section-comparison"></a>

**Neutral path classes and conjugate sections.** For p in `P(b,x)`, `t_x,p(sigma)=c_p(sigma)s_b(sigma)`. The path class is neutral iff there exists a `Gamma_k`-fixed geometric path `b→x`, iff `t_x,p` is conjugate to `s_b` by an element of `N_b`. In coordinate form a fixed h satisfies s1(sigma)=h s0(sigma) h inverse for every sigma. Neutrality means `c_h(sigma)=k alpha_b(sigma)(k)` inverse for some k; the fixed path is `h·k`. These are existence statements, not uniqueness of the fixed path or surjectivity of rational points onto section classes. The cocycle at p is identically one exactly when p conjugates the endpoint section to the reference section.

Same endpoints; all conjugating elements lie in `N_b`.

Use sigma(p)=p `c_p(sigma)` to factor the transported section. Neutrality of the class (Layer 0) says some gauge translate of the chosen cocycle is identically 1; its path translate is fixed. Rearrange the fixed-path equation to the displayed section conjugacy.

**Checks.**

- At the identity path, pointwise neutrality is equivalent to equality of the two sections.
- The tests with equal sections give a neutral class even when a chosen representative has nontrivial values.
- A nonneutral finite quotient, such as a nontrivial Kummer projection, obstructs section conjugacy.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), Section 1, Proposition 1 and proof, PDF pp. 5–7.

<a id="nc-0-reference-section-change"></a>

**Reference section change twists the action.** After transferring both endpoint sections to `E_b`, let `c(sigma)=s1(sigma)s0(sigma)^(-1)`. Their actions on `N_b` satisfy `alpha_1(sigma)=Int(c(sigma))` composed with `alpha_0(sigma)`. Thus changing the reference rational or tangential basepoint changes the coefficient action by the cocycle twist of [Twisting by a cocycle](#nc-3-twisting). The corresponding path/H1 comparisons use that twisting, rather than equating elements of differently acted-on H1 sets.

s0,s1 continuous sections of the same restriction map.

Factor s1(sigma)=c(sigma)s0(sigma) and compute both conjugation actions. Use the path cocycle law and the twisting equivalence to identify the pointed torsor categories under the two actions.

**Checks.**

- For equal sections `c=1` and the actions agree.
- In a nonabelian kernel a noncentral c changes the action; no equality of raw cohomology classes under different actions is asserted.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), Section 1, Proposition 1 and proof, PDF pp. 5–7.

Use [Cocycle of a geometric arithmetic path](#nc-0-arithmetic-path-cocycle); [Twisting by a cocycle](#nc-3-twisting).

<a id="nc-0-arithmetic-path-functoriality"></a>

**Functoriality of arithmetic path classes.** A k-morphism `X→Y` carrying rational endpoints, or a morphism of pointed tame curves with specified compatible tangential fibre-functor identifications, sends `P_X(b,x)` to `P_Y(fb,fx)`, compatibly with the kernel homomorphism, `Gamma_k` actions, transported sections and cocycles. In extension coordinates, if q prime composed with f equals q and f composed with `s_i` equals `t_i`, then `f(c_h(sigma))=c_f(h)(sigma)`. Finite separable base extension restricts the Galois action and the class to the corresponding open subgroup, with specified comparison of geometric fibre functors. No functor on arbitrary boundary tangent vectors is claimed without that compatibility data.

Geometrically connected finite-type schemes; compatible endpoint fibre functors and sections. The field-extension comparison uses a chosen embedding of separable closures.

Apply the induced continuous kernel homomorphism to the defining cocycle formula and use section compatibility. Base extension uses the cartesian arithmetic exact sequences and restriction of sections; apply the same formula.

<a id="nc-0-rational-tangential-kummer"></a>

**Finite Kummer projections from a tangential basepoint.** Let k have characteristic zero, `U=P1_k` minus {0,1,infinity}, b0 the rational tangent vector lambda d/dz at 0 with lambda in k-units, and a in `U(k)`. For `n≥1`, the maps z and 1-z to `G_m` send the arithmetic path class `P(b0,a)` to the Kummer classes `kappa_n(a/lambda)` and `kappa_n(1-a)`, respectively. Identify the first endpoint torsor by the normalized tangent root and the second by the root of the constant value 1. The classes are independent of root/path choices. With lambda=1 and `a=2` over Q the `n=2` projections include the nontrivial classes of 2 and -1, so this rational endpoint cannot be identified with the tangential endpoint by a Galois-fixed geometric path.

Use IG.1 normalized tame tangent fibre on the finite Kummer covers `y^n=z` and `y^n=1-z`. At b0 their leading terms are lambda and 1, respectively. After choosing roots alpha of a and beta of lambda, the first path torsor quotient has representative sigma(alpha/beta)/(alpha/beta); the second is represented by an n-th root of 1-a relative to 1. Apply the pinned Kummer representative theorem. Changing roots is the imported gauge equivalence, and the neutral criterion is the pinned n-th-power theorem.

### 1.2 Tangential specialization and good paths

<a id="nc-0-local-inertia-orbit-model"></a>

**Local inertia orbits on branches.** For a branch set Y with positive integers `e_y`, use the finite Kummer model BranchFiber=disjoint union over y of `Z/e_y`. Let branchRotation shift each coordinate by 1; quotient its cyclic subgroup action by the orbit equivalence relation. The branch projection induces specializeLocal on this quotient. Two fibre elements have the same orbit exactly when they have the same branch label. Thus specializeLocal is bijective and each branch orbit has cardinality `e_y`. This is the local calculation for geometric tangential specialization, not a definition of the global scheme fibre functor.

Every ramification index is positive; the global finite-cover application has finitely many branches. A compatible primitive-root choice identifies local inertia with positive rotation; opposite generator gives the same orbit quotient.

ZMod addition by 1 is a permutation with inverse subtraction by 1. It preserves the branch label. Every residue on a given branch differs by an integer translate, so exactly one orbit occurs per branch. Factor the branch projection through the orbit quotient, then prove bijectivity and use ZMod.card.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `branchRotation_apply`: The permutation sends (y,i) to `(y,i+1)`.
- `specializeLocal_mk`: The class of (y,i) maps to y.
- `inertiaOrbit_iff`: Orbit equivalence is equivalent to equality of branch labels.
- `specializeLocal_bijective`: The induced branch map is bijective.
- `branch_card`: The y-branch fibre has cardinality `e_y`.

**Checks.**

- `inertiaOrbit_degree_three`: One branch of degree 3 has a singleton orbit quotient.
- `inertiaOrbit_distinct_branches`: Two degree-2 branches give distinct quotient points despite equal indices.
- `inertiaOrbit_unramified`: For `e_y=1` the branch rotation fixes every point.
- Disconnected covers retain every branch separately.
- The quotient is by a permutation action, not a manually imposed same-branch relation.

The construction and its conventions follow [William Y. Chen](#reference-chen2024), Proposition 4.2.3(b), pp. 364–365.

Use `MulAction.orbitRel.Quotient`; `ZMod`; `ZMod.card`.

<a id="nc-0-tangential-inertia-specialization"></a>

**Tangential specialization by inertia orbits.** Over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic zero, let C be a smooth connected separated finite-type curve, x a closed point, `U=C` minus {x}, and t a nonzero tangent vector at x. Normalize C in each finite étale cover `V→U`, obtaining a finite map `Y→C` with regular (hence smooth) source. There is a canonical specialization `F_t(V)→the` underlying point set `Y_x`, natural in V. After a compatible choice of primitive roots defines `gamma_t` in `Aut(F_t)`, specialization induces a canonical bijection of finite sets `<gamma_t>\F_t(V)≅Y_x`. Equivalently use the closed image of local tame inertia, since its action on a finite set factors through a finite quotient. The orbit over a branch y has size `e_y`. Neither injectivity of local inertia into pi1(U,t), connectedness of V, nor equality with the nonreduced scheme-theoretic fibre is asserted.

k algebraically closed of characteristic zero; C smooth connected separated of finite type and dimension one. Only covers of U, followed by their normalizations over C; not arbitrary finite morphisms with nondominating components. `t≠0` and compatible primitive roots fixed for `gamma_t`.

Import normalization finiteness and regular-curve/DVR geometry from SF.0/SF.3. Grade each branch by the valuation `ord_y/e_y`. For a local parameter z at x choose a branch parameter s with initial `z=s^e_y`. The graded tangent map is the `e_y`-th power map, and the IG.1 tangent fibre is its nonzero tangent fibre. Projection to the branch gives the canonical specialization, independent of the selected parameters. Apply the local orbit model and glue over branches. A map of covers induces compatible graded branch maps, proving naturality. Passing from the cyclic generator to closed inertia does not change a finite orbit.

**Checks.**

- For local `z=s^3` the three tangent lifts specialize to one branch.
- Two ramified branches of equal degree specialize to two distinct points.
- For `C=P1` and `U=A1` the local inertia map may be trivial; orbit specialization still holds for every finite étale cover.
- Natural squares commute for morphisms of finite étale covers.

The construction and its conventions follow [William Y. Chen](#reference-chen2024), Section 4.2 construction; Definition 4.2.1 and Proposition 4.2.3(b), pp. 362–365.

<a id="nc-0-chen-good-path"></a>

**Good path between tangential basepoints.** Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic zero and `U=P1_k` minus {0,1,infinity}. Fix nonzero tangent vectors t0,t1,tInfinity, compatible roots of unity and their inertia automorphisms gamma0,gamma1,gammaInfinity. A path `delta:F_t0≅F_tInfinity` is good if gamma0 and delta inverse gammaInfinity delta topologically generate `Aut(F_t0)`, and there is a path `epsilon:F_t0≅F_t1` for which (delta inverse gammaInfinity delta)(epsilon inverse gamma1 epsilon)gamma0=1. Multiplication is functional composition. The predicate can be stated natively for any three finite-set fibre functors, but geometric generation comes from the specified three-punctured curve.

Geometric tangential fibre functors; gamma generators come from compatible roots. Use topological generation, not abstract subgroup generation.

Import the IG.1 tangent fibre functors and IG.0 natural-isomorphism paths. Backward path transport is the pullAut helper. Define generation by topological closure of the subgroup generated by the two named automorphisms. Keep the ordered infinity, one, zero relation as a separate conjunct; existence of epsilon is part of the predicate.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `IsGoodPath.generates`: A good path exports topological generation by gamma0 and transported gammaInfinity.
- `IsGoodPath.relation`: A good path exports a path epsilon and the infinity, one, zero relation.
- `isGoodPath_iff`: The predicate is equivalent to exactly these two conditions.

**Checks.**

- `goodPath_trivial_group`: All identity inertia and the identity path are good when Aut F is trivial.
- `goodPath_identity_nonexample`: All identity inertia are not good when Aut F is nontrivial.
- `goodPath_ordered_relation`: If a,b topologically generate, identity paths with `gamma0=a`, gammaInfinity=b and `gamma1=b` inverse a inverse are good.
- `goodPath_reversed_order`: For noncommuting a,b the reverse product `a*(b inverse a inverse)*b` is not 1.

The construction and its conventions follow [William Y. Chen](#reference-chen2024), Definition 4.3.1, p. 366.

<a id="nc-0-chen-symmetric-path"></a>

**Symmetric tangential path.** On U as above, let iota(z)=1/z, take tInfinity=iota(t0), and use the cover-pullback functor J=iota star and endpoint identifications e0:J followed by `F_t0≅F_tInfinity` and eInfinity:J followed by `F_tInfinity≅F_t0`. Define invertPath(delta)=e0 inverse followed by J*delta followed by eInfinity. A path delta from t0 to tInfinity is symmetric if there exist ordinary integers r,s with `iota_*(delta)=gamma0^r` delta inverse `gammaInfinity^s`, in functional order. In arrow order this is `gammaInfinity^s` followed by delta inverse followed by `gamma0^r`. No independent abstract involution on the set of paths is introduced.

Endpoint identifications for the pullback by the geometric inversion. Ordinary integer witnesses, not profinite exponents; compatible inertia generators at the swapped endpoints.

Define the predicate by the displayed integer-power equation and derive witness/constructor/characterisation APIs. Examples use the identity functor with its unitor, so they test the equation independently of a nonexistent scheme instance.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `IsSymmetricPath.witnesses`: Export integers r,s witnessing the inversion equation.
- `isSymmetricPath_of_eq`: An integer-power equality constructs the predicate.
- `isSymmetricPath_iff`: The predicate is equivalent to existence of exactly those integer witnesses.

**Checks.**

- `symmetricPath_identity`: For identity pullback/unitor, identity inertia and identity path are symmetric.
- `symmetricPath_zero_inertia`: For identity pullback/unitor and identity inertia, a loop delta is symmetric iff delta squared is 1.
- `symmetricPath_square_nonexample`: In that model a loop with delta squared≠1 is not symmetric.
- Symmetry and goodness are distinct predicates.
- The pullback functor and endpoint identifications appear in the type of the signature.

The construction and its conventions follow [William Y. Chen](#reference-chen2024), Definition 4.3.1 and following existence argument, p. 366.

<a id="nc-0-symmetric-good-path-existence"></a>

**Existence of symmetric good paths.** For an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field k, `U=P1_k` minus {0,1,infinity}, any nonzero t0, tInfinity=iota(t0), any nonzero t1, and one compatible root-of-unity system defining the inertia generators, there exists a geometric path delta:t0→tInfinity which is both good and symmetric in the above senses. Over C it is represented by a path along the positive real direction with a small positively oriented detour around 1, adjusted at tangent germs; its peripheral system has product infinity, one, zero equal to 1 and the required integral inversion adjustments. The argument uses finite-cover Riemann existence with tangent-germ compatibility and invariance under algebraically closed characteristic-zero extension. This is existence of a geometric path, not a canonical or Galois-fixed choice.

Algebraically closed characteristic-zero k; tInfinity is exactly the inversion image of t0. All three tame inertia generators use the same compatible roots; source conventions for the analytic positive generator must be respected.

Over C choose tangent-germ connectors and the detoured path. The elementary punctured-sphere presentation proves topological generation and the ordered relation; inversion reverses the detour with integer turns at the two endpoints. Use BelyiMaps Layer 12 profinite Riemann existence for finite covers, together with [Tangential fibre functors and their analytic comparison](#tangential-fibre-functors), which identifies tangential fibres with analytic germs, to transport the path and all equalities to the finite-étale fibre functors. For general k take the algebraic closure in k of a finitely generated field containing the tangent coefficients, together with the algebraic cyclotomic data. Choose its embedding into C carrying the entire compatible primitive-root system to the standard analytic system: the corresponding embedding of the cyclotomic extension extends to an algebraic closure and then across a transcendence basis. Compare through algebraically closed characteristic-zero extensions using IG.1. This preserves the fibres, paths, inertia and both predicates; tangent connectors are chosen compatibly at the inversion-paired endpoints.

**Checks.**

- The witness satisfies both conjuncts of goodness and the integer symmetry equation.
- No assertion of a `Gamma_k`-fixed witness over a nonclosed field; the Kummer obstruction test precludes such an inference.

The construction and its conventions follow [William Y. Chen](#reference-chen2024), Section 4.3, paragraph following Definition 4.3.1, p. 366.

### 1.3 Étale K(π,1) for a class of coefficients

<a id="pi1-etale-comparison"></a>

**Comparison of continuous π₁-cohomology with étale cohomology.** Let X be a connected quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme with geometric point x and `π=π₁(X,x)`. The inclusion of finite étale X-schemes into all étale X-schemes induces a morphism of topoi `ρ:X_et→X_fet`, and the fibre functor at x identifies `X_fet` with the classifying topos `Bπ` of continuous π-sets. For a finite discrete π-module M let `L_x(M)=ρ*M`, the finite locally constant abelian sheaf corresponding to M. Define `εⁿ_M:Hⁿ_cont(π,M)=Hⁿ(X_fet,M)→Hⁿ(X_et,L_x(M))` as the edge map of the Leray spectral sequence of `ρ` (pullback followed by the counit). Then `εⁿ_M` is natural in π-equivariant maps of M, in pointed morphisms of schemes and in paths between geometric points. `ε⁰` and `ε¹` are isomorphisms for every X. `Rᵠρ_*L_x(M)` is the sheaf on `X_fet` associated to `(Y→X)↦Hᵠ_et(Y,L_x(M)|Y)`, so vanishing of these sheaves for `q>0` implies that every `εⁿ_M` is an isomorphism. The converse is asserted for the full `K(π,1)` property, quantified over every finite continuous π-module and every degree, not for a single fixed M. It uses the induced coefficients of every finite étale cover and Shapiro comparison to detect the higher-direct-image stalks.

X connected, quasi-compact and quasi-separated; M finite discrete with continuous π-action. No hypothesis on the order of M is needed for the construction or for degrees 0 and 1.

The equivalence between finite locally constant abelian sheaves and finite continuous π-modules (Stacks, Tag 0DV5) identifies `L_x` with `ρ*`. The cohomology of `Bπ` with coefficients in a discrete module is continuous group cohomology, computed as the colimit over open normal subgroups N of `Hⁿ(π/N,M^N)`. The edge maps of the Leray spectral sequence are pullback followed by the counit and are natural for commutative squares of topoi (Achinger, 2.3–2.4). In degree 0 both sides are `M^π`. In degree 1 the Leray sequence gives `0→H¹(X_fet,M)→H¹(X_et,L)→H⁰(X_fet,R¹ρ_*L)`, and `R¹ρ_*L=0` because a torsor under a finite locally constant sheaf is representable by a finite étale cover (Stacks, Tag 03RV), which kills its own class. The description of `Rᵠρ_*` is the definition of higher direct images for the topology of finite étale covers.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.edge`: The comparison `εⁿ_M`.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.edge_natural_coeff`: Naturality in equivariant coefficient maps.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.edge_natural_pointed`: Naturality for a pointed morphism `(X′,x′)→(X,x)`, through the induced map on `π₁`.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.edge_path`: For a path between geometric points, the induced isomorphism of fundamental groups commutes with `ε`.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.edge_zero_iso` and `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.edge_one_iso`: `ε⁰` and `ε¹` are isomorphisms.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.higherDirectImage_eq`: The description of `Rᵠρ_*L_x(M)` as a sheafified presheaf on finite étale covers.

**Checks.**

- For `X=Spec K`, K a field, `ρ` is an equivalence and `εⁿ_M` is the identity of Galois cohomology in every degree.
- For `X=P¹` over an algebraically closed field and `M=ℤ/ℓ`, `ℓ` invertible, `π=1` and `ε²_M:0→H²(P¹,ℤ/ℓ)≅ℤ/ℓ` is not surjective, while `ε⁰` and `ε¹` are isomorphisms; this is the degree-two failure the `K(π,1)` property rules out.
- Naturality for the pointed cover `Spec ℂ→Spec ℝ`: the induced map on `π₁` is the inclusion `1→Gal(ℂ/ℝ)`, and the nonzero class of `H¹(Gal(ℂ/ℝ),ℤ/2)≅ℤ/2` restricts to 0 on both sides of `ε¹`; a comparison that ignored the base point map would not commute with this restriction.

The construction and its conventions follow [Piotr Achinger](#reference-achinger-effacement-2014-v1), §1.3, p. 2; §2.3–2.4, pp. 5–6; §3.2, Definition 3.3 and the proof of Proposition 3.4(a), pp. 7–8; [Alexander Schmidt and Jakob Stix](#reference-schmidt-stix-2016), §2.3, pp. 826–827; [The Stacks Project Authors](#reference-stacks), Tag 0DV5 (Lemma 59.65.1) and Tag 03RV (Lemma 59.64.4).

<a id="key-etale-k-pi-1"></a>

**Étale K(π,1) for a specified finite coefficient class.** Let X be a connected locally noetherian scheme with geometric point x. Put `π = π₁ᵉᵗ(X,x)`, the profinite SGA fundamental group. Let C specify an isomorphism-invariant class of finite discrete abelian groups with continuous π-action, transported along pointed fundamental-group isomorphisms. Define Is(X,x;C) to mean that, for every M in C and every integer `n ≥ 0`, the canonical comparison `εⁿ_M : Hⁿ_cont(π,M) → Hⁿ_et(X,L_x(M))` is an isomorphism of abelian groups. `L_x(M)` is the finite locally constant étale sheaf corresponding to M, not an arbitrary constructible sheaf. The default full property uses all finite continuous π-modules. The p-primary property uses those whose underlying finite group has p-power order, with p prime; the constant-Fₚ comparison is a separately named specialization, not the definition of either full property. None of these coefficient restrictions changes `π` to its maximal pro-p quotient.

Connected locally noetherian X; a geometric point x and profinite finite-étale fibre-functor fundamental group. C is invariant under coefficient isomorphisms and transported by fundamental-group isomorphisms. No invertibility assumption on coefficient orders in this definition.

Import the non-affine finite-étale category, geometric-point fibre functor and profinite `π` from IG.0, building on the abstract Galois-category API and affine finite-étale fibres. Use the finite continuous π-module `/` finite locally constant sheaf dictionary and the canonical comparison `εⁿ` of [Comparison of continuous π₁-cohomology with étale cohomology](#pi1-etale-comparison), with the π-action from IG.0. ContinuousCohomology already supplies all cochain degrees; `εⁿ` compares it with étale cohomology and is not a new cohomology definition. Quantify over every allowed coefficient and every nonnegative degree; take isomorphism of the canonical map, not existence of an unrelated group isomorphism. Restriction of C is a logical implication. Geometric and base-point transports have their separate comparison formulas. The cohomological predicate makes sense on all connected locally noetherian schemes. Identification with Schmidt–Stix's raw pro-homotopy definition is the separately scoped [Comparison with raw étale `K(π,1)`](#nc-0-raw-homotopy-comparison); no such identification is asserted outside its stated hypotheses.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.Is.edgeIso`: From Is(X,x;C), for M in C and `n ≥ 0`, obtain the inverse of the canonical `εⁿ_M` with both inverse identities; it is natural in equivariant coefficient homomorphisms.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.Is.iff_all_comparisons`: Is(X,x;C) holds exactly when `εⁿ_M` is an isomorphism for every M in C and every `n ≥ 0`; checking only `n ≤ 1` is not sufficient.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.Is.of_subclass`: If `C′ ⊆ C`, then Is(X,x;C) implies Is(X,x;C′); in particular full finite coefficients imply p-primary coefficients and constant-Fₚ comparison.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.Is.pointedIso_iff`: For a pointed scheme isomorphism `f:(X,x) ≅ (Y,y)`, Is(X,x;f*D) iff Is(Y,y;D), using transported coefficients and the natural comparison square.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.Is.basePoint_iff`: For geometric points x,y and an étale path between their finite-étale fibre functors, Is(X,x;C) iff Is(X,y;transport C); full and p-primary classes are invariant under every such transport.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.Is.zero_coefficients`: For the class containing only the zero π-module, every comparison is `0 → 0` and Is(X,x;C) holds; this case is not evidence for the full property.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.Is.constantFp_edgeIso`: For p prime, the full or p-primary property supplies `Hⁿ_cont(π,Fₚ) ≅ Hⁿ_et(X,Fₚ)` via `ε` in every degree, with trivial π-action; the group in the source is still `π`.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.tests.field`: For every field K and separable geometric point, Is(Spec K,x;all finite coefficients) holds and `π` identifies with `Gal(K_sep/K)`, with `ε` equal to the Galois-cohomology comparison.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.tests.projective_line_degree_two`: For algebraically closed k and prime `ℓ` invertible in k, `π₁ᵉᵗ(P¹_k)=1` and `H²_et(P¹_k,Z/ℓ) ≅ Z/ℓ` is nonzero, while `H²_cont(1,Z/ℓ)=0`; hence the full property and the ℓ-primary property both fail although degrees zero and one agree.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.tests.affine_curve`: For a geometrically connected smooth affine curve over a characteristic-zero field, including `Gₘ` and `P¹` minus `{0,1,∞}`, the full finite-coefficient property holds; no claim that every open immersion preserves it is involved.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.tests.positive_genus`: For a geometrically connected smooth proper curve of genus at least one over a characteristic-zero field, the full property holds. Nonzero `H²_et` of an elliptic curve does not contradict it: its profinite fundamental group need not have vanishing `H²`.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.tests.product_char_zero`: For two geometrically connected geometrically unibranch characteristic-zero varieties with the full property, their product has it; over a non-algebraically-closed field the arithmetic `π₁` of the product is the fibre product over `Gal(k_sep/k)`, not the ordinary product.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.tests.artin_tower`: A finite characteristic-zero tower of smooth elementary curve fibrations ending in Spec k has the full property; this includes `M₀,n` for `n ≥ 4` after importing its moduli construction and forgetting-mark fibrations.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.tests.pro_p_not_coefficient_restriction`: The finite group `C₂` acts on `F₃` by negation. This is a 3-primary continuous coefficient with invariants 0. Its action does not descend to the trivial maximal pro-3 quotient of `C₂`; putting `F₃` with trivial action on that quotient gives invariants `F₃` instead. A p-primary coefficient restriction is not a licence to replace `π` by `π^(p)`.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.tests.zero_class`: The zero-coefficient class passes on `P¹`, whereas the full and invertible-prime primary classes fail there. The class argument must not be erased.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.tests.constantFp_not_pro_p_cohomology`: For `S₃` with trivial `F₃` coefficients the maximal pro-3 quotient is trivial, yet `H³(S₃,F₃)` is nonzero: the explicit normalized bar 3-cocycle c and cycle z in the reader pair to 1 mod 3. Even constant `F_p` coefficients in positive degrees do not generally permit replacing the full group by its maximal pro-p quotient. This is a group-cohomology boundary test, not a claim that a scheme with fundamental group `S₃` is `K(π,1)`.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.tests.prime_degree_cover`: For a smooth projective genus-one curve over algebraically closed characteristic-zero k and prime `p=3`, a nonzero character `π₁→F₃` gives a connected degree-3 étale cover; the zero character gives three disconnected copies. Multiplication-by-3 on an elliptic curve has degree 9, not 3.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.tests.prime_to_degree_does_not_kill`: For a smooth projective elliptic curve over algebraically closed characteristic-zero k, multiplication-by-2 has degree 4 and induces multiplication by `4=1` on `H²_et(E,μ₃)≅Z/3`. Thus this finite étale cover does not kill a nonzero degree-two class.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.tests.prime_power_tower`: For genus≥1, `p=3,a=2`, a degree-3 étale cover multiplies `H²(μ₉)` by 3 and does not kill the generator; a tower of two connected degree-3 covers has degree 9 and kills all `H²(μ₉)` classes.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.tests.tower_exponent_zero`: At `a=0` the prime-power tower is the identity, coefficient `μ₁` is zero and `H²(C,μ₁)=0`. This boundary is not the infinite coefficient `n=0`.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.tests.genus_after_prime_cover`: For a connected étale degree-3 cover of a smooth projective genus-2 curve over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, unramified Riemann–Hurwitz gives genus 4; a second degree-3 step gives genus 10. For genus one every such step retains genus one.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.tests.arithmetic_restriction_not_injective`: For `k=R`, `k_s=C` and `X=Spec R` with constant `Z/2` coefficients, `H²_et(X,Z/2)≅Z/2` but `H²_et(Spec C,Z/2)=0`. Both spectra have the full `K(π,1)` property. Separable-closure invariance is not injectivity of cohomology restriction; the finite cover `Spec C→Spec R` kills the nonzero class.
- Spec K passes for any field K; `P¹` over an algebraically closed field fails full finite coefficients in degree two.
- Farb–Kisin–Wolfson §2.3.1 only consumes the constant-Fₚ edge comparison. Their Lemma 3.2.2 proves an additional pro-p comparison for its particular torus-torsor fundamental groups; it is not a general consequence of the coefficient restriction.

The construction and its conventions follow [Alexander Schmidt and Jakob Stix](#reference-schmidt-stix-2016), §2.3, pp. 826–827; cohomological criterion in the proof of Lemma 2.7(b); [Benson Farb, Mark Kisin and Jesse Wolfson](#reference-farb-kisin-wolfson-2024-v2), §2.3.1, p. 16; Lemma 3.2.2, p. 24; [Piotr Achinger](#reference-achinger-all-primes-2017), §4, Definition 4.1 (version-of-record HTML); Proposition 4.2 and Lemma 4.3.

<a id="nc-0-coefficient-restriction"></a>

**Restriction of the allowed finite coefficients.** If `C′ ⊆ C`, then Is(X,x;C) implies Is(X,x;C′); in particular full finite coefficients imply p-primary coefficients and constant-Fₚ comparison.

The key definition applies; `C′ ⊆ C` on the same profinite π-module category.

For M in C′ use the inclusion to view M in C, then apply the same canonical `εⁿ_M` in each degree. No cohomological theorem or quotient of `π` is used.

**Checks.**

- Apply to all finite modules `→` p-primary modules `→` the trivial-action `Fₚ` module; do not assert either reverse implication.

The construction and its conventions follow [Benson Farb, Mark Kisin and Jesse Wolfson](#reference-farb-kisin-wolfson-2024-v2), §2.3.1, p. 16.

<a id="nc-0-pointed-isomorphism"></a>

**Invariance under pointed scheme isomorphism.** For a pointed scheme isomorphism `f:(X,x) ≅ (Y,y)`, Is(X,x;f*D) iff Is(Y,y;D), using transported coefficients and the natural comparison square.

A pointed scheme isomorphism; coefficient class transported along the induced π-isomorphism.

Use IG.0's fibre-functor transport and SF.2's naturality to form the comparison square with vertical cohomology isomorphisms. Conjugate `ε` across this square. Its being an isomorphism is equivalent on the two schemes, for each coefficient and degree; reverse f for the converse.

**Checks.**

- The identity transport gives the same canonical comparison; composition of two pointed isomorphisms agrees with their composite.

The construction and its conventions follow [Alexander Schmidt and Jakob Stix](#reference-schmidt-stix-2016), §2.3, p. 826; Appendix A.3.

<a id="nc-0-basepoint-transport"></a>

**Change of geometric base point.** For geometric points x,y and an étale path between their finite-étale fibre functors, Is(X,x;C) iff Is(X,y;transport C); full and p-primary classes are invariant under every such transport.

An étale path, meaning an isomorphism between the two finite-étale fibre functors; transport of C along its profinite π-isomorphism.

Import IG.0's path-induced conjugacy transport of π-actions and SF.2's compatible locally constant sheaf identifications. The induced cohomology isomorphisms commute with `ε`. Thus one canonical comparison is an isomorphism iff the other is. A different path differs by an inner π-isomorphism. The transported finite module and sheaf are naturally isomorphic, so the all-finite and p-primary assertions do not depend on that path. This does not construct rational-point sections or tangential specializations.

**Checks.**

- Full and p-primary coefficient classes are unchanged by conjugacy; an arbitrary non-invariant class must be transported, not silently identified.

The construction and its conventions follow [Alexander Schmidt and Jakob Stix](#reference-schmidt-stix-2016), §2.3, p. 826, sentence following the definition.

### 1.4 The finite-cover effacement criterion

<a id="finite-etale-pushforward-descent"></a>

**Finite étale pushforward and limit descent of finite coefficients.** (a) Let `f:Y→X` be finite étale. For every abelian sheaf F on `Y_et`, `f_*` is exact, `(f_*F)_x̄` is the product of the stalks `F_ȳ` over the geometric points ȳ above x̄ (permuted by the monodromy of the sheets), and the map `μ_f:Hᵠ(X,f_*F)→Hᵠ(Y,F)`, pullback followed by the counit `f*f_*F→F`, is an isomorphism in every degree. If F is finite locally constant with stalks of order supported on a set of primes P, so is `f_*F`. For a cartesian square with `g:X′→X` and `f′:Y′→X′`, the base change map `g⁻¹f_*F→f′_*g′⁻¹F` is an isomorphism and `g′*∘μ_f=μ_f′∘(base change)∘g*`. No normality, Galois condition or invertibility of deg f is assumed. (b) Every finite locally constant abelian sheaf F with stalks of order supported on P has a finite filtration by finite locally constant subsheaves whose graded pieces are locally constant sheaves of `𝔽_p`-vector spaces, `p∈P`. (c) Let k be a field with separable closure `k_s=colim k_i` over finite subextensions, and X a quasi-compact quasi-separated k-scheme. Finite étale covers of `X_(k_s)`, finite locally constant sheaves on it and morphisms between them descend to some `X_(k_i)`, and `colim_i Hᵠ(X_(k_i),F_i)≅Hᵠ(X_(k_s),F_s)`. In particular a class on `X_(k_s)` killed by a finite étale cover is the image of a class on some `X_(k_i)` killed by a descended cover.

(a) f finite étale; (b) X connected, F finite locally constant; (c) X quasi-compact and quasi-separated over k, `F_i` a compatible system with colimit `F_s`.

(a) For finite f, the stalk formula and exactness are Stacks, Proposition 59.55.2; the higher direct images vanish, so the Leray spectral sequence degenerates and `μ_f` is its edge map. Finite base change is Stacks, Lemma 59.55.3. Étale locally on X, Y is a disjoint union of copies of X, so `f_*` of a finite locally constant sheaf is finite locally constant with the same primes. (b) Under the equivalence with finite π₁-modules (Stacks, Tag 0DV5), take the filtration of the finite module by p-primary parts and then by the subgroups pʲM, each π₁-stable. (c) Schemes and morphisms of finite presentation descend along the limit of schemes with affine transition maps (Stacks, Lemma 32.10.1, Tag 01ZM), and being finite étale descends to a finite level (Stacks, Section 32.8, descending properties of morphisms). The cohomology statement is Stacks, Theorem 59.51.3 (Tag 09YQ). Descent of a killing cover follows by descending the cover and the vanishing of the pulled-back class at a finite level.

**Checks.**

- In characteristic three, the Artin–Schreier classes z and 1/z on `𝔾_m` have independent simple poles and give a `(ℤ/3)²` quotient of the full fundamental group; that group is not `ℤ̂`.
- For the degree-2 cover `f:𝔾_m→𝔾_m`, `z↦z²`, over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and `F=ℤ/2` on the source, `f_*ℤ/2` corresponds to the permutation module `𝔽₂[C₂]` of `π₁(𝔾_m)=ℤ̂`, a non-split extension of `𝔽₂` by `𝔽₂`, not the constant sheaf `(ℤ/2)²`; and `H⁰(X,f_*F)=H⁰(Y,ℤ/2)=ℤ/2`, not `(ℤ/2)²`.
- For `f=id`, `μ_f` is the identity; for `f:Y=X⊔X→X`, `μ_f` identifies `Hᵠ(X,F⊕F)` with `Hᵠ(X,F)²`: the product formula, not a sum over one sheet.
- For `k=ℝ` and `X=Spec ℝ`, `H²(X,ℤ/2)≅ℤ/2` but `H²(X_ℂ,ℤ/2)=0`: the colimit formula concerns the classes on `X_(k_s)`, and is not a claim that restriction from X to `X_(k_s)` is injective.

The construction and its conventions follow [The Stacks Project Authors](#reference-stacks), Proposition 59.55.2 and Lemma 59.55.3 (Section 59.55, Tag 03QN); Tag 0DV5 (Lemma 59.65.1); Theorem 59.51.3 (Tag 09YQ); Lemma 32.10.1 (Tag 01ZM) and Section 32.8; [Piotr Achinger](#reference-achinger-effacement-2014-v1), proof of Proposition 3.4(b)–(c), pp. 7–8.

Use [Comparison of continuous π₁-cohomology with étale cohomology](#pi1-etale-comparison); [SchemeAndStackFoundations](../SchemeAndStackFoundations/README.md) Layer SF.2 (sites and scheme cohomology).

<a id="nc-0-effacement-finite-cover-transfer"></a>

**Transport of class effacement to finite covers.** Assume every positive-degree étale cohomology class on X with every allowed coefficient can be killed by some finite étale surjective cover of X. For a finite étale map `f:Y→X`, any allowed coefficient F on Y, q&gt;0 and `α∈H^q_et(Y,F)`, there exists a finite étale surjective `g:X′→X` such that its base change `g′:Y×_X X′→Y` kills `α`. Y need not be connected and f need not be normal or surjective. The specified equality is `g′* μ_f(α′)=μ_f′(bc_*(g*α′))`, where `μ_f:H^q_et(X,f_*F)→H^q_et(Y,F)` is the pullback/counit isomorphism and `α′=μ_f⁻¹(α)`.

X is a connected noetherian scheme with a geometric point x; `π` is its full profinite finite-étale fundamental group. P is any set of primes. Allowed coefficients are finite locally constant abelian étale sheaves whose stalk orders have prime factors in P. No invertibility hypothesis on those primes is imposed.

Use the exact finite-étale direct image, preservation of finite locally constant coefficients, the base-change isomorphism `bc:g*f_*F≅f′_*g′*F` and the pullback/counit cohomology map `μ_f` of [Finite étale pushforward and limit descent of finite coefficients](#finite-etale-pushforward-descent)(a). Locally f is a finite disjoint union of copies of X, so exact finite products supply `R^j f_*F=0` for j&gt;0; these are generic sheaf-theoretic inputs, not local NC definitions. The stalk of `f_*F at x` is a finite product over the sheets, with sheet-permutation monodromy. Prime support is preserved under finite products. Apply the hypothesis to `α′=μ_f⁻¹(α)`; choose g killing `α′`. Use SF.2’s (2.4.2) square: `g′* μ_f(α′)=μ_f′(bc_*(g*α′))`. Its proof factors through cohomological pullback, base change and the adjunction counit; the last square is the triangle identity, not an arbitrary isomorphism of cohomology groups. The right side is zero by the choice of g. Finite étaleness and surjectivity survive base change, so g′ is the required cover of Y. For the empty Y the class is already zero.

**Checks.**

- For `f=id_X`, `μ` and the base-change identification are identities; the chosen cover is the original class-killing cover.
- For the nonnormal index-three `subgroup C₂⊂S₃` and `F₂` coefficients, direct image is the permutation module `F₂[S₃/C₂]`, with `H⁰,H¹,H²` dimensions (1,1,1). The constant rank-three module has (3,3,3), so replacing monodromy by a constant product fails.
- For `C₃⊂S₃` and `F₂` coefficients the cover degree is two, which is zero in `F₂`, but the direct-image comparison still works. No division by the degree is used.

The construction and its conventions follow [Piotr Achinger](#reference-achinger-effacement-2014-v1), §§2.1–2.6, (2.4.1–2); Proposition 3.4(a), pp. 5–8.

Use [SchemeAndStackFoundations](../SchemeAndStackFoundations/README.md) Layer SF.2 (sites and scheme cohomology); [InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups](../InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups/README.md) Layer IG.0.

<a id="nc-0-all-coefficient-effacement"></a>

**All-coefficient finite-cover criterion.** Is(X,x;P-supported finite coefficients) holds iff for every allowed finite locally constant abelian sheaf F, every q&gt;0 and every `α∈H^q_et(X,F)`, some finite étale surjective `g:X′→X` satisfies `g*α=0`. The `K(π,1)` side uses the canonical `ε^q`, all nonnegative degrees and the full `π`; the killing cover may depend on `F,q,α`. This equivalence is asserted for connected noetherian schemes without a geometric-unibranch restriction.

X is a connected noetherian scheme with a geometric point x; `π` is its full profinite finite-étale fundamental group. P is any set of primes. Allowed coefficients are finite locally constant abelian étale sheaves whose stalk orders have prime factors in P. No invertibility hypothesis on those primes is imposed.

For the forward direction use ProfiniteCohomology Layer 10’s canonical all-degree finite-quotient colimit and natural restriction/inflation. Any class is inflated from a finite quotient `π/N` with coefficients `M^N`. On restriction to N its class factors through positive cohomology of the trivial group, which vanishes. For finite M one may refine N by its open action kernel. IG.0 identifies N with a pointed finite étale cover, and naturality of `ε` kills the corresponding étale class. For the reverse direction apply [Transport of class effacement to finite covers](#nc-0-effacement-finite-cover-transfer) to every object Y of the finite-étale site. This gives killing of all allowed classes on every such object, including coefficients not descended from X. For disconnected Y treat its finitely many components and combine their covers. Use `ρ:X_et→X_fet` and the description in [Comparison of continuous π₁-cohomology with étale cohomology](#pi1-etale-comparison) of `R^qρ_*F` as the sheafification of `(Y→X)↦H^q_et(Y,F|Y)`. Finite-cover effacement at every site object makes this sheaf zero for q&gt;0. The unit is an isomorphism in degree zero by the finite-coefficient/sheaf dictionary. Leray for `ρ` now identifies the comparison from `H^q(X_fet,M)` to `H^q(X_et,L(M))` with `ε^q`. Under `X_fet≃Bπ` and the canonical continuous-cohomology comparison it is an isomorphism. Generic sites, derived direct image and the Leray spectral sequence come from SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2, and the comparison `εⁿ` from [Comparison of continuous π₁-cohomology with étale cohomology](#pi1-etale-comparison); no raw Artin–Mazur homotopy theorem is used.

**Checks.**

`- P=∅` admits only the zero finite coefficient and both sides hold on every X.
`- P={p}` retains all p-primary modules and their monodromy; `π` is not replaced by its maximal pro-p quotient.
- Degree-one classes die on their finite étale torsors via the diagonal section. Arbitrary small-site covers in place of finite covers would turn this into ordinary local effacement and fail to distinguish `P¹`.

The construction and its conventions follow [Piotr Achinger](#reference-achinger-effacement-2014-v1), Definition 3.3; Proposition 3.4(a), pp. 7–8; [Piotr Achinger](#reference-achinger-all-primes-2017), Definition 4.1; Proposition 4.2(a); Lemma 4.3.

<a id="nc-0-finite-etale-invariance"></a>

**Finite étale invariance of étale K(π,1).** For `f:Y→X` finite étale surjective, Is(X,x;P-supported finite coefficients) holds iff every connected component of Y has the corresponding property at any geometric point above it. This includes full and p-primary coefficients. It is not asserted for an arbitrary coefficient class lacking closure under finite-étale direct image and pullback; Y may be disconnected.

X is a connected noetherian scheme with a geometric point x; `π` is its full profinite finite-étale fundamental group. P is any set of primes. Allowed coefficients are finite locally constant abelian étale sheaves whose stalk orders have prime factors in P. No invertibility hypothesis on those primes is imposed.

Use [All-coefficient finite-cover criterion](#nc-0-all-coefficient-effacement) to express the property of X by killing allowed classes. The transfer lemma gives that same killing condition on Y; split into components and apply the criterion there, proving ascent. For descent, pull an allowed F and class `α` on X back along f. On each of the finitely many components of Y choose a finite étale surjective class-killing cover. Their finite disjoint union `Z→Y` kills `f*α`. The composite `Z→X` is finite étale surjective and kills `α` by functoriality. Apply [All-coefficient finite-cover criterion](#nc-0-all-coefficient-effacement) to X. Basepoint independence is the inherited transport theorem. Every coefficient still lies in the same prime-supported class, because pullback preserves its stalks and finite direct image has finite product stalks.

**Checks.**

- For `Y=X⊔X` over X the property agrees componentwise, with no arbitrary choice of a distinguished component.
- For Y empty and X nonempty, the map is not surjective and does not satisfy the theorem. Surjectivity must remain a hypothesis.
- A connected nonnormal finite étale cover has the same equivalence; no Galois action on the cover and no inverse of its degree is required.

The construction and its conventions follow [Piotr Achinger](#reference-achinger-effacement-2014-v1), Proposition 3.4(b), statement and proof, pp. 7–8; [Piotr Achinger](#reference-achinger-all-primes-2017), Proposition 4.2(b).
