<a id="nc-0-effacement-extension"></a>

**Two-cover dévissage of coefficients.** Let `0→F′→F→F″→0` be a short exact sequence of allowed finite locally constant abelian sheaves on X. Assume that for every finite étale `Y→X` and every q&gt;0 every class with coefficients F′|Y and every class with coefficients F″|Y dies after a finite étale surjective cover of Y. Then the same property holds for F|Y. No filtration by trivial one-dimensional π-modules is assumed.

X is a connected noetherian scheme with a geometric point x; `π` is its full profinite finite-étale fundamental group. P is any set of primes. Allowed coefficients are finite locally constant abelian étale sheaves whose stalk orders have prime factors in P. No invertibility hypothesis on those primes is imposed.

Fix Y,q and `α∈H^q(Y,F|Y)`. Kill its `image β∈H^q(Y,F″|Y)` on `h:Z→Y`, using the F″ assumption at Y. Exactness of pullback preserves the coefficient short exact sequence. By the cohomology long exact sequence on Z, `h*α` lifts to a class `η∈H^q(Z,F′|Z)`. This is existence of a lift after the first cover; it does not claim a splitting of `F→F″`. Apply the F′ assumption at Z to `η` and choose a second cover `j:W→Z` killing it. Coefficient-map naturality gives `(h∘j)*α=0`. The composite is finite étale surjective. The order and bases of the two covers are essential.

**Checks.**

- The zero end coefficient reduces to the other end without creating a spurious obstruction.
- The constant exact sequence `0→F_p→Z/p²→F_p→0` need not split. The two-cover argument still applies; a chosen lift need not be killed by the first cover.
- For `q=1` the finite étale torsor already kills each class. In `q=0` a nonzero invariant constant section cannot be killed by a surjective cover, so the positive-degree restriction is necessary.

The construction and its conventions follow [Piotr Achinger](#reference-achinger-all-primes-2017), Proposition 4.2(c), complete proof.

<a id="nc-0-finite-cover-effacement"></a>

**Finite-cover effacement criterion.** For a connected noetherian scheme X with geometric point x and a set of primes P, Is(X,x;P-supported finite coefficients) holds iff, for every connected finite étale cover `Y→X`, every finite abelian group A whose order has prime factors in P, every `q≥2` and `α∈H^q_et(Y,A)` for the constant sheaf A, there exists a finite étale surjective `Z→Y` killing `α`. All primes recover the previous full-coefficient criterion for geometrically unibranch varieties. Every finite cover Y is quantified; constant coefficients only on X are insufficient.

X is a connected noetherian scheme with a geometric point x; `π` is its full profinite finite-étale fundamental group. P is any set of primes. Allowed coefficients are finite locally constant abelian étale sheaves whose stalk orders have prime factors in P. No invertibility hypothesis on those primes is imposed.

For the forward direction, [Finite étale invariance of étale `K(π,1)`](#nc-0-finite-etale-invariance) gives the property on every connected finite cover. Apply [All-coefficient finite-cover criterion](#nc-0-all-coefficient-effacement) to its constant coefficient A. For the reverse direction, first trivialize each finite locally constant F on a finite étale cover of X. Split into finitely many connected components. The hypothesis kills all `q≥2` classes on every component; `q=1` classes die on their finite étale torsors. The two-cover extension lemma also permits reduction to constant prime-field tests on every finite cover. Compose the trivializing and class-killing covers and use the natural pullback composition law. This gives the all-coefficient killing condition on X. Apply [All-coefficient finite-cover criterion](#nc-0-all-coefficient-effacement). The direct cohomological proof uses the exact finite-direct-image/base-change and ρ/Leray inputs, not the raw-homotopy comparison. Ordinary étale-local coverings in place of finite étale covers are insufficient.

**Checks.**

- The cover X′ is part of the quantifier; replacing finite covers by arbitrary étale coverings or allowing only `X′=X` is not this criterion.
- The group-cohomology/finite-direct-image distinction is tested by `C₂⊂S₃` with `F₂` coefficients; the finite group model is a regression, not geometric certification.
- No raw-homotopy/profinite-completion equivalence outside geometric-unibranch varieties is inferred from this broader cohomological statement.

The construction and its conventions follow [Alexander Schmidt and Jakob Stix](#reference-schmidt-stix-2016), Lemma 2.7(b), proof, p. 827; finite-cover convention p. 821; [Piotr Achinger](#reference-achinger-effacement-2014-v1), Proposition 3.4(a–b), pp. 7–8; [Piotr Achinger](#reference-achinger-all-primes-2017), Proposition 4.2(a–c); Lemma 4.3.

### 1.5 The raw étale homotopy type

<a id="raw-etale-prospace"></a>

**Raw étale homotopy type.** For a locally noetherian pointed scheme (X,x), construct the pro-simplicial étale homotopy type from connected components of pointed étale hypercovers, with refinements and homotopies giving its object in the homotopy category of pointed pro-spaces. Define the raw homotopy pro-groups and the canonical classifying map to `Bπ₁`. For a connected geometrically unibranch variety, identify `π₁` with the profinite finite-cover fundamental group. Define locally constant finite abelian coefficients on the pro-space and compare their cohomology with étale sheaf cohomology, compatibly with the classifying map, fibre-functor paths and coefficients. Prove that the classifying map is a weak equivalence exactly when all these canonical finite-coefficient comparisons are isomorphisms in every degree. The word raw refers to the uncompleted étale pro-space; a p-completion is a distinct construction.

The identification of `π₁` with a profinite group and the finite-coefficient Whitehead criterion are restricted to connected geometrically unibranch varieties; this is the scope in which the homotopy pro-groups are profinite. Hypercovers and their refinements use the small étale site.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `etaleProspace.map`: Pointed scheme maps induce functorial maps up to the specified homotopies.
- `etaleProspace.pi1Equiv`: Identify `π₁` with the finite-cover group in the stated scope.
- `etaleProspace.cohomologyEquiv`: Identify finite local-system cohomology with the site cohomology naturally.
- `etaleProspace.classifyingMap`: Its pullback is the canonical `ε`, rather than an arbitrarily chosen cohomology isomorphism.
- `etaleProspace.whiteheadFinite`: Detect the classifying weak equivalence by all finite local coefficients.

**Checks.**

- For Spec of a separably closed field, the type is contractible.
- For `P¹` over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, `π₁` is trivial but its nonzero `H²` with prime torsion prevents equivalence to a point.
- Replacing all finite coefficients by p-primary coefficients does not assert the raw higher homotopy vanishing condition.

The construction and its conventions follow [Alexander Schmidt and Jakob Stix](#reference-schmidt-stix-2016), Introduction, p. 817; §2.3, pp. 826–828; Appendix A.3, Proposition A.16 and Definition A.17, pp. 864–866; finite-coefficient criterion in Lemma 2.7(b), p. 827.

### 1.6 Comparison with raw étale K(π,1)

<a id="nc-0-raw-homotopy-comparison"></a>

**Comparison with raw étale K(π,1).** For a connected geometrically unibranch variety X with geometric point x, the full finite-coefficient property agrees with the raw étale `K(π,1)` condition `π⁽raw⁾ₙ(X_et,x_et)=0` for every `n ≥ 2`, equivalently the canonical classifying morphism `X_et → Bπ₁(X_et,x_et)` is an isomorphism in `Ho(pro-ss_*)`. Here `π₁(X_et,x_et)` is profinite in this scope and identified with the SGA finite-étale `π` used by the cohomological definition. This equivalence is not asserted for an arbitrary non-geometrically-unibranch locally noetherian scheme.

Connected geometrically unibranch variety, not an arbitrary locally noetherian scheme. Full finite coefficients; a p-primary coefficient comparison alone is not an assertion about all raw higher homotopy groups.

Use [Finite-cover effacement criterion](#nc-0-finite-cover-effacement) and the cohomological weak-equivalence criterion of Artin–Mazur Theorem 4.3, as invoked for this precise scope by Schmidt–Stix §2.3. Use the raw étale pro-space construction, its homotopy pro-groups, finite-cover `π₁` identification in the stated scope and its canonical classifying morphism. Schmidt–Stix Proposition A.16 constructs the map corresponding to `id_π₁` through the nerve of the fundamental groupoid. Corollary A.18 then tests isomorphism on all homotopy groups: the `π₁` map is the identity and `Bπ₁` has no higher groups. The model-category and cohomological-detection proof leaves remain explicit, not routine automation.

**Checks.**

- The canonical map is essential, not an arbitrary equivalence. Outside the geometric-unibranch scope raw `π₁` may be a non-profinite pro-group, even though its profinite completion is the SGA `π₁`.

The construction and its conventions follow [Alexander Schmidt and Jakob Stix](#reference-schmidt-stix-2016), §2.3, pp. 826–827; Proposition A.16, Definition A.17 and Corollary A.18, pp. 864–866.

### 1.7 Fields and the projective line

<a id="nc-0-field"></a>

**Fields are étale K(π,1).** For every field K, with a separable geometric point x of Spec K, Is(Spec K,x;all finite coefficients) holds. Under `π ≅ Gal(K_sep/K)`, its comparison `εⁿ_M` is the canonical Galois-cohomology isomorphism in every degree and for every finite discrete continuous Galois module M.

K is a field; choose a separable closure inside the geometric-point field.

IG.0 identifies finite étale K-schemes and their fibre functor with finite continuous Galois sets. SF.2 imports Stacks 03QQ: abelian étale sheaves on Spec K correspond to discrete continuous Galois modules, global sections correspond to invariants, and their derived functors identify in every degree. Restrict that derived-functor comparison to finite modules. Its direction agrees with `ε`, so the quantified definition holds; invoke [Restriction of the allowed finite coefficients](#nc-0-coefficient-restriction) for every subclass.

**Checks.**

- For separably closed K, `π=1` and all positive cohomology vanishes. For general K, higher Galois cohomology need not vanish: `K(π,1)` does not mean `Hⁿ_et=0`.

The construction and its conventions follow [The Stacks Project Authors](#reference-stacks), 03QQ.

<a id="reduced-boundary-generalized-jacobian"></a>

**Generalized Jacobian of a reduced boundary.** For a smooth proper geometrically connected curve C over a characteristic-zero field k and a nonempty reduced finite étale divisor D, construct the relative degree-zero Picard group `J_D=Pic⁰(C,D)` of line bundles with a trivialization along D, as an fppf sheaf represented by a semiabelian variety. Construct the exact sequence `1→T_D→J_D→J_C→1`, where `T_D=(Res_(D/k)𝔾_m)/𝔾_m` and the denominator is diagonal. Include the group law, identity, inverse, functoriality for maps of pointed pairs and extension of the ground field. For a specified `b∈(C−D)(k)`, construct the pointed Abel map `a_b:C−D→J_D`, sending x to the rigidified class of x−b; without b retain the degree-one Picard torsor. For every `n≥1`, multiplication by n is finite étale and surjective and gives `0→T_D[n]→J_D[n]→J_C[n]→0` as finite étale group schemes. Over an algebraic closure its order is `n^(2g+r−1)`, where `r=deg D`.

Construct the rigidified Picard sheaf from divisors prime to D modulo functions equal to 1 along D, and descend the construction from a splitting field of D. The exact sequence of units gives the displayed torus, and divisibility of the geometric torus gives the torsion exact sequence. The proper Jacobian is supplied by JacobianChallenge D–F; the finite-field modulus and reciprocity construction belongs to AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors, §“Ramified rank-one curve reciprocity”. This target supplies the characteristic-zero reduced-boundary construction and its elementary torsion API.

**Checks.**

- If D is one rational point, the diagonal torus quotient is trivial and `J_D=J_C`; multiplication by n has degree `n^(2g)`.
- For `(C,D)=(ℙ¹,{0,∞})`, `J_D=𝔾_m`, the Abel map with b=1 is z↦z and `J_D[n]=μ_n`. For three rational punctures it is `𝔾_m²`, although `J_C=0`.
- For `C=ℙ¹_ℝ` and `D={i,−i}`, the torus is `(Res_(ℂ/ℝ)𝔾_m)/𝔾_m`. Complex conjugation acts by −1 on its rank-one character lattice, so it is not the split real torus. A construction using only rational boundary points misses this example.

The construction follows [Jean-Pierre Serre](#reference-serre-generalized-jacobians), Chapter V §1, no. 6, pp. 81–82; §2, nos. 7–9, pp. 82–89; §3, nos. 12–17, especially Theorem 3, pp. 91–98; §4, nos. 20–22, pp. 102–107. The torsion sequence follows from this extension and the supplied abelian-variety torsion theorem.

*Needs:* JacobianChallenge D–F (proper Picard/Jacobian and Abel maps); SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2–SF.3 (fppf sheaves, descent, divisors and Picard objects); AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry §§7.3–7.6 (Picard sheaves and rigidified line bundles); AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli §A3.2 (multiplication and finite étale torsion); ReductiveGroups Layer 0 (tori); ReductiveGroupsPartII §RG2.0a (affine restriction of scalars).

<a id="curve-kummer-cohomology"></a>

**Étale cohomology of curves with `μ_n` coefficients.** Let k be an algebraically closed field and `n≥1` invertible in k. (a) For a smooth projective connected curve X of genus g, there are canonical identifications `H⁰(X,μ_n)=μ_n(k)`, `H¹(X,μ_n)=Pic⁰(X)[n]≅(ℤ/n)^(2g)`, `H²(X,μ_n)=ℤ/n` through the degree, and `Hᵠ(X,μ_n)=0` for `q≥3`. (b) For a nonconstant morphism `π:X→Y` of smooth projective curves, `π*:H²(Y,μ_n)→H²(X,μ_n)` is multiplication by `deg π` under these identifications. (c) For a smooth affine curve X whose smooth compactification has genus g and `r≥1` points at infinity, `H¹(X,μ_n)≅(ℤ/n)^(2g+r−1)` and `Hᵠ(X,μ_n)=0` for `q≥2`. Choosing a primitive n-th root of unity gives the same statements for the constant sheaf `ℤ/n`.

k algebraically closed; n invertible in k; X, Y smooth connected curves, projective in (a)–(b), affine in (c).

Use the Kummer sequence `0→μ_n→𝔾_m→𝔾_m→0` on the étale site, `H¹(X,𝔾_m)=Pic(X)`, and the vanishing of `H^q(X,𝔾_m)` for `q≥2` on a smooth curve over an algebraically closed field; the n-torsion of `Pic⁰(X)` has order `n^(2g)`, and `Pic(X)/n=ℤ/n` through the degree. For (b), compute on the class of a line bundle of degree one: its pullback has degree `deg π`. For (c), use the localization sequence for the reduced boundary: `0→H¹(X̄,μ_n)→H¹(X,μ_n)→(ℤ/n)^r→ℤ/n→0`, whose last map sums the residues; higher affine cohomology vanishes by Stacks 03RR. This gives the displayed rank over `ℤ/n`. In characteristic zero its order agrees with the torsion order of [Generalized Jacobian of a reduced boundary](#reduced-boundary-generalized-jacobian); no identification with that torsion group without dualizing is used.

**Checks.**

- For `X=ℙ¹` and `n>1` invertible in k, `H¹(ℙ¹,μ_n)=0` and `H²(ℙ¹,μ_n)=ℤ/n≠0`, although `π₁(ℙ¹)=1`. At `n=1` all these coefficient groups are zero.
- For an elliptic curve E and multiplication by m, of degree `m²`, `π*` acts on `H²(E,μ_n)` as multiplication by `m²`, not by m.
- For `X=𝔾_m (g=0, r=2)`, `H¹(𝔾_m,μ_n)≅ℤ/n` and `H²=0`.

The construction and its conventions follow [The Stacks Project Authors](#reference-stacks), Lemma 59.69.1 (Tag 03RQ), Lemma 59.69.2 (Tag 0AMB) and Lemma 59.69.3 (Tag 03RR).

<a id="nc-0-projective-line-obstruction"></a>

**The degree-two obstruction on the projective line.** For algebraically closed k and prime `ℓ` invertible in k, `P¹_k` does not have the full finite-coefficient property, and does not have the ℓ-primary property. For `M=Z/ℓ` with trivial action, `ε²_M` has source zero and target isomorphic to `Z/ℓ`; it is not an isomorphism.

Algebraically closed k; prime `ℓ` distinct from char k, so `ℓ ≥ 2` and its constant coefficient is nonzero.

Import the geometric finite-étale fundamental-group computation `π₁(P¹_k)=1` from IG.0. Use the computation `H²_et(P¹_k,μ_ℓ)≅Z/ℓ` of [Étale cohomology of curves with `μ_n` coefficients](#curve-kummer-cohomology); a choice of primitive ℓth root gives the corresponding noncanonical identification for the constant `Z/ℓ` sheaf. The continuous cohomology of the trivial group in degree two is zero by the native/derived comparison and trivial-group calculation. The target is nonzero, so `ε²` cannot be an isomorphism; its coefficient belongs to both classes.

**Checks.**

- Degrees zero and one agree in this example. A definition checking only these degrees would falsely accept `P¹`. Do not use `μ_p ≅` constant `Z/p` in characteristic p.

### 1.8 Constant prime-field tests

<a id="nc-0-prime-field-effacement"></a>

**Constant prime-field tests on all finite covers.** For a connected noetherian scheme X with geometric point x and a set of primes P, Is(X,x;P-supported finite coefficients) holds iff for every connected finite étale cover `Y→X`, every `p∈P`, every `q≥2` and every `α∈H^q_et(Y,F_p)` with constant coefficients, there is a finite étale surjective `Z→Y` killing `α`. The prime-field and cover quantifiers are both essential. No assumption of a composition series of trivial π-modules is made.

X is a connected noetherian scheme with a geometric point x; `π` is its full profinite finite-étale fundamental group. P is any set of primes. Allowed coefficients are finite locally constant abelian étale sheaves whose stalk orders have prime factors in P. No invertibility hypothesis on those primes is imposed.

For necessity use [Finite étale invariance of étale `K(π,1)`](#nc-0-finite-etale-invariance) and [All-coefficient finite-cover criterion](#nc-0-all-coefficient-effacement) on Y with its constant `F_p` sheaf. For sufficiency, on every finite étale `Y→X` trivialize a finite locally constant coefficient F by a further finite étale cover. On its connected components the finite abelian coefficient group has a finite filtration with factors finite `F_p`-vector spaces for `p∈P`. Use the prime-field filtration of [Finite étale pushforward and limit descent of finite coefficients](#finite-etale-pushforward-descent)(b); it is not an invented filtration by trivial representations before monodromy is killed. Cohomology of constant finite vector coefficients is the finite direct sum of `F_p` cohomologies. Kill the finitely many component classes by taking a finite common refinement of their covers. Apply [Two-cover dévissage of coefficients](#nc-0-effacement-extension) along the filtration; its end-coefficient assumptions hold at every finite cover because the hypothesis quantifies them all. Degree-one classes die on finite étale torsors; the degree-zero comparison is invariants. Compose the trivializing and killing covers, apply [All-coefficient finite-cover criterion](#nc-0-all-coefficient-effacement) on X, and keep the canonical `ε` maps.

**Checks.**

- For P empty the criterion and the zero-coefficient property both hold.
- Constant `F_p` tests only on X do not state this theorem; Y must vary over connected finite covers, including nonnormal covers.
- The nonsplit sequence `0→F_p→Z/p²→F_p→0` uses two-cover effacement, and finite `F_p`-vector layers use common refinements; checking only simple coefficients in degree zero cannot replace the `q≥2` tests.

The construction and its conventions follow [Piotr Achinger](#reference-achinger-all-primes-2017), Proposition 4.2(c), complete proof.

### 1.9 Curves, prime-degree covers and products

<a id="nc-0-connected-prime-degree-cover"></a>

**A connected prime-degree étale cover.** For a connected smooth projective curve C of genus `g≥1` over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field k and a prime p, there exists a connected finite étale surjective k-morphism `f:D→C` of degree exactly p. The cover can be chosen to be a torsor under the constant additive group `F_p`; its translation action is induced by a nonzero continuous character of the full `π₁ᵉᵗ(C,x)`.

k is algebraically closed of characteristic zero; C is a connected smooth projective k-curve of genus `g≥1`. p is a prime number, so p is invertible in k. The fundamental group is the full profinite `π₁ᵉᵗ(C,x)`.

Use the Kummer calculation `H¹_et(C,μ_p)≅Pic⁰(C)[p]` of [Étale cohomology of curves with `μ_n` coefficients](#curve-kummer-cohomology) and the Jacobian p-torsion order `p^(2g)` from SF.3. Choose a primitive pth root in k only to identify `μ_p` with the constant `F_p` sheaf. Since `p≥2` and `g≥1`, this `H¹` group has a nonzero class. Use the degree-one comparison `H¹_et(C,F_p)≅Hom_cont(π,F_p)` for trivial action, valid for any connected scheme, from [Comparison of continuous π₁-cohomology with étale cohomology](#pi1-etale-comparison) and IG.0. This is not an invocation of the all-degree `K(π,1)` property. Let `χ` be the nonzero character corresponding to the chosen class. The image of `χ` is a nonzero additive subgroup of `F_p` and therefore all of `F_p`, using the prime-order simple additive group of ZMod p. Under IG.0's finite continuous π-set classification, the translation action `g·a=χ(g)+a` is transitive and has p elements. Its associated finite étale cover D is connected of degree p and surjective. Translation by `F_p` commutes with `π` and is simply transitive on every fibre, giving the indicated torsor. A zero character gives p disconnected copies of C and must not be used.

**Checks.**

- For `p=2` and genus one the cover is connected of degree 2, not multiplication-by-2 on an elliptic curve, whose degree is 4.
- For `g=0`, `Pic⁰[p]` is zero and this argument produces no nonzero character; the trivial torsor is disconnected.

The construction and its conventions follow [Alexander Schmidt](#reference-schmidt-curve-1996), Proposition 15, proof, printed pp. 243–244; [The Stacks Project Authors](#reference-stacks), 03RQ Lemma 59.69.1; 03RP Proposition 39.9.11(7).

<a id="nc-0-prime-cover-degree-two-killing"></a>

**Prime-degree covers kill degree-two prime torsion.** Let `f:D→C` be a connected finite étale cover of degree p between connected smooth projective curves over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, with p prime. Then `f*:H²_et(C,μ_p)→H²_et(D,μ_p)` is the zero homomorphism. After choosing one primitive pth root on the common base field, the same holds for constant `F_p` coefficients. This conclusion does not require genus≥1 once the cover is given.

Both curves are connected, smooth and projective over the same algebraically closed characteristic-zero field. f is finite étale surjective of degree p, p prime; the same coefficient identification is pulled back to D.

Use the Kummer-degree isomorphisms `d_C:H²(C,μ_p)≅Z/p` and `d_D` and the degree-pullback identity `d_D(f*α)=deg(f)·d_C(α)` of [Étale cohomology of curves with `μ_n` coefficients](#curve-kummer-cohomology). These are the generic curve computations of Stacks 03RQ and 0AMB, not a second Picard or cohomology definition in Layer 1. Since `deg(f)=p` and `p=0` in ZMod p, the right side vanishes for every `α`. Injectivity of `d_D` gives `f*α=0`. The map being zero, not merely its source and target having equal order, is the assertion. Pull back the single chosen `μ_p≅F_p` coefficient isomorphism to D. Naturality conjugates the zero `μ_p` map into the `constant-F_p` zero map; no independent roots of unity or transfer divided by p are used.

**Checks.**

- With `p=3`, degree 3 acts as zero on `Z/3`; degree 2 acts invertibly and does not kill its generator.
- On an elliptic curve, multiplication-by-p has degree `p²` and also kills `H²(μ_p)`, but it is not the exact degree-p witness of [A connected prime-degree étale cover](#nc-0-connected-prime-degree-cover).

The construction and its conventions follow [The Stacks Project Authors](#reference-stacks), 0AMB Lemma 59.69.2, statement and Kummer-boundary proof; [Alexander Schmidt](#reference-schmidt-curve-1996), Proposition 15, proof, printed pp. 243–244.

<a id="nc-0-geometric-smooth-curve"></a>

**Geometric smooth-curve finite-cover effacement.** For a connected smooth separated finite-type curve C over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, if C is affine or its smooth projective compactification has genus≥1, then Is(C,x;all finite coefficients) holds at every geometric point x. More explicitly, on every connected finite étale `Y→C` every class `α∈H^q_et(Y,F_p)`, p prime and `q≥2`, dies on a finite étale surjective cover of Y. In the affine case and in degrees `q≥3` the identity cover suffices.

k algebraically closed, characteristic zero; C connected smooth separated finite-type of dimension one. C affine or its smooth projective compactification has positive genus; genus-zero projective C is excluded.

Use SF.3's dichotomy: a nonproper smooth separated curve is affine, so the positive-genus nonaffine case is projective. For every connected finite étale `Y→C`, the affine case stays affine. In the projective case Y is smooth projective and unramified Riemann–Hurwitz gives `g(Y)=1+deg(Y/C)(g(C)−1)≥1`. Use the curve cohomology of [Étale cohomology of curves with `μ_n` coefficients](#curve-kummer-cohomology): for affine Y, `H^q(Y,F_p)=0` for `q≥2`; for projective Y, `H^q(Y,F_p)=0` for `q≥3` and `H²(Y,μ_p)≅Z/p` (03RQ). Use one root-of-unity identification for the constant `F_p` statements. Only `q=2` on projective positive-genus Y remains. Obtain a connected degree-p cover `Z→Y` by [A connected prime-degree étale cover](#nc-0-connected-prime-degree-cover); [Prime-degree covers kill degree-two prime torsion](#nc-0-prime-cover-degree-two-killing) kills the specified class. No use of the desired `K(π,1)` theorem is hidden in obtaining this cover. The quantifier covers every Y and every prime p, not just C and one p. Apply [Constant prime-field tests on all finite covers](#nc-0-prime-field-effacement) with P all primes to reach the canonical all-degree full finite-coefficient predicate. Basepoint-transport gives the statement at any geometric point. The raw pro-homotopy comparison is not a prerequisite.

**Checks.**

`- G_m` and `P¹` minus `{0,1,∞}` use affine vanishing; a smooth projective elliptic curve uses covers despite nonzero `H²`.
- A finite étale cover of a genus-2 curve of degree 3 has genus 4, so the prime-cover construction remains available after the first cover.
`- P¹` is not accepted: every connected finite étale cover is an isomorphism and the nonzero degree-two generator survives.

The construction and its conventions follow [Alexander Schmidt](#reference-schmidt-curve-1996), Proposition 15, proof, printed pp. 243–244; [The Stacks Project Authors](#reference-stacks), 03RQ and 03RR, complete Kummer proofs.

Use [Constant prime-field tests on all finite covers](#nc-0-prime-field-effacement); [A connected prime-degree étale cover](#nc-0-connected-prime-degree-cover); [Prime-degree covers kill degree-two prime torsion](#nc-0-prime-cover-degree-two-killing); [Change of geometric base point](#nc-0-basepoint-transport); [SchemeAndStackFoundations](../SchemeAndStackFoundations/README.md) Layer SF.2 (sites and scheme cohomology); [SchemeAndStackFoundations](../SchemeAndStackFoundations/README.md) Layer SF.3 (curves, divisors and Picard objects); [InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups](../InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups/README.md) Layer IG.0.

<a id="nc-0-separable-killing-descent"></a>

**A geometric killing cover descends to a finite extension.** Let k have characteristic zero with fixed separable closure `k_s`, X a separated finite-type k-scheme, F a finite locally constant abelian étale sheaf, q&gt;0 and `α∈H^q_et(X,F)`. If a finite étale surjective cover `h_s:Z_s→X_(k_s)` kills `α_(k_s)`, then there exist a finite separable `k⊆k′⊆k_s` and a finite étale surjective `h′:Z′→X_(k′)`, whose base change is `h_s` up to `X_(k_s)-isomorphism` after a possible further finite extension, such that `h′*α_(k′)=0`. Thus the composite `Z′→X` is finite étale surjective and kills `α`. Neither `Z_s` nor Z′ is required to be connected.

X separated of finite type over a characteristic-zero field; in particular X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. F finite locally constant and `α` a fixed positive-degree class; a genuine finite étale surjective killing cover over `k_s` is given.

Write `k_s` as the filtered union of its finite separable k-subextensions. By [Finite étale pushforward and limit descent of finite coefficients](#finite-etale-pushforward-descent)(c), the finite étale cover `Z_s` and its morphism descend to some `X_(k₀)`. Finite étale and surjectivity persist or descend after enlarging `k₀`; do not assume that descending equations alone proves these properties. The descended `Z₀` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply SF.2's canonical continuity isomorphism `colim_(k′/k₀ finite)` `H^q_et(Z₀×_(k₀)k′,h₀*F_(k′))≅H^q_et(Z_s,h_s*F_(k_s))`, natural in pullback. The image of `h₀*α_(k₀)` is zero. A representative mapping to zero in a filtered colimit of abelian groups becomes zero at some later finite stage. Enlarge to that k′ and base change `Z₀`. This second enlargement is necessary: descent of `h_s` alone does not make `h₀*α` vanish. Since `Spec k′→Spec k` is finite étale surjective, `X_(k′)→X` and the composite `Z′→X` are finite étale surjective. Pullback composition proves that the composite kills `α`. No injectivity of restriction to `k_s`, proper base change or arbitrary field-extension invariance is used.

**Checks.**

- For the zero class the identity cover suffices; no field extension is forced.
- A class that vanishes over `k_s` need not vanish over k. The conclusion supplies a finite extension/cover that kills it, not injectivity of the original restriction map.
- The killing field may depend on `F,q,α` and the chosen cover; a single field killing all classes is not asserted.

The construction and its conventions follow [Piotr Achinger](#reference-achinger-effacement-2014-v1), Proposition 3.4(c), finite-separable and separable-closure proof paragraph, p. 8; [The Stacks Project Authors](#reference-stacks), 09YQ Theorem 59.51.3; 03RV Lemma 59.64.4; 07RR Lemma 32.8.15.

Use [SchemeAndStackFoundations](../SchemeAndStackFoundations/README.md) Layer SF.2 (sites and scheme cohomology); [InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups](../InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups/README.md) Layer IG.0; [Finite étale pushforward and limit descent of finite coefficients](#finite-etale-pushforward-descent).

<a id="nc-0-separable-base-change"></a>

**Separable-closure invariance of finite-coefficient K(π,1).** For a geometrically connected separated finite-type scheme X over a characteristic-zero field k, with separable closure `k_s` and a geometric point x over `k_s`, Is(X,x;all finite coefficients) holds iff `Is(X_(k_s),x;all finite coefficients)` holds. Both sides use their own full profinite fundamental groups and their canonical `ε` maps; their étale cohomology groups are not asserted to be equal.

X geometrically connected, separated and finite type over a characteristic-zero field; chosen separable closure and geometric point. The coefficient class is all finite locally constant abelian coefficients, not an arbitrary unstable class.

For descent, take F,q&gt;0,α on X. If the geometric property holds, [All-coefficient finite-cover criterion](#nc-0-all-coefficient-effacement) supplies a finite étale cover of `X_(k_s)` killing `α_(k_s)`. Apply [A geometric killing cover descends to a finite extension](#nc-0-separable-killing-descent) and then [All-coefficient finite-cover criterion](#nc-0-all-coefficient-effacement) on X. For ascent, let `F_s,q>0,β_s` be geometric coefficient/class data. The descent of finite locally constant sheaves in [Finite étale pushforward and limit descent of finite coefficients](#finite-etale-pushforward-descent)(c), including their addition, zero and inverse maps, gives `F₀` on `X_(k₀)` for a finite separable `k₀/k`. Its canonical cohomology continuity supplies a class `β₁ at` a possibly larger finite `k₁` representing `β_s`. `X_(k₁)` is connected by geometric connectedness; [Finite étale invariance of étale `K(π,1)`](#nc-0-finite-etale-invariance) transfers the property of X to `X_(k₁)`. Apply [All-coefficient finite-cover criterion](#nc-0-all-coefficient-effacement) to `β₁`, then base change its finite étale surjective killing cover to `k_s`. Naturality kills `β_s`. Apply the all-coefficient criterion on `X_(k_s)` and preserve its canonical comparison. The proof never replaces `π` by its geometric subgroup or pro-p quotient; nor does it identify `H^q(X,F)` with `H^q(X_(k_s),F_s)`.

**Checks.**

- For Spec k the equivalence agrees with the field test, though positive-degree Galois cohomology over k need not agree with the zero positive-degree étale cohomology of `Spec k_s`.
- The separable closure need not be finite; replacing its projection by a finite étale morphism is false.
- An open curve is allowed: the argument uses affine-transition continuity and finite-presentation descent, not properness.

The construction and its conventions follow [Piotr Achinger](#reference-achinger-effacement-2014-v1), Proposition 3.4(c), separable-closure case, p. 8.

Use [All-coefficient finite-cover criterion](#nc-0-all-coefficient-effacement); [Finite étale invariance of étale `K(π,1)`](#nc-0-finite-etale-invariance); [A geometric killing cover descends to a finite extension](#nc-0-separable-killing-descent); [SchemeAndStackFoundations](../SchemeAndStackFoundations/README.md) Layer SF.2 (sites and scheme cohomology); [InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups](../InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups/README.md) Layer IG.0; [Finite étale pushforward and limit descent of finite coefficients](#finite-etale-pushforward-descent).

<a id="nc-0-smooth-curve"></a>

**Smooth curves of affine or positive-genus type.** For a geometrically connected smooth curve C over a characteristic-zero field k, if C is affine or its smooth proper model has genus at least one, then Is(C,x;all finite coefficients) holds for every geometric point x.

Smooth geometrically connected curve over a characteristic-zero field; affineness or positive genus of its smooth proper model. The genus-zero proper curve is excluded.

Base change C to the fixed separable closure `k_s`. In characteristic zero `k_s` is algebraically closed; SF.3 preserves smoothness, geometric connectedness, affineness and genus of the smooth proper model. Apply [Geometric smooth-curve finite-cover effacement](#nc-0-geometric-smooth-curve). Its proof works on every connected finite étale cover: affine higher cohomology vanishes, while positive-genus projective degree-two classes die on connected prime-degree covers. The degree-one canonical comparison is used to obtain covers and does not assume `K(π,1)`. Apply [Separable-closure invariance of finite-coefficient `K(π,1)`](#nc-0-separable-base-change) to descend the full finite-coefficient property to C, and use [Change of geometric base point](#nc-0-basepoint-transport) for the chosen geometric point. No raw-homotopy theorem or identification of arithmetic and geometric étale cohomology is used. Schmidt 1996 Proposition 15 and Schmidt–Stix Lemma 2.7(a) give the broader raw any-field result. This target keeps the characteristic-zero geometric-curve scope. The direct cohomological proof uses finite-cover effacement. The raw homotopy theorem additionally uses the explicit étale pro-space comparison, with its separate geometric-unibranch hypotheses.

**Checks.**

`- Gₘ` and `P¹` minus `{0,1,∞}` pass. A smooth proper genus-one curve passes; `P¹` fails by the separate degree-two obstruction.

The construction and its conventions follow [Alexander Schmidt and Jakob Stix](#reference-schmidt-stix-2016), Lemma 2.7(a), p. 827, citing Schmidt 1996 Proposition 15; [Alexander Schmidt](#reference-schmidt-curve-1996), Proposition 15, proof, printed pp. 243–244; [Piotr Achinger](#reference-achinger-effacement-2014-v1), Proposition 3.4(c), p. 8.

Use [Étale `K(π,1)` for a specified finite coefficient class](#key-etale-k-pi-1); [Geometric smooth-curve finite-cover effacement](#nc-0-geometric-smooth-curve); [Separable-closure invariance of finite-coefficient `K(π,1)`](#nc-0-separable-base-change); [Change of geometric base point](#nc-0-basepoint-transport); [SchemeAndStackFoundations](../SchemeAndStackFoundations/README.md) Layer SF.3 (curves, divisors and Picard objects).

<a id="nc-0-positive-family-effacement"></a>

**One cover kills a finite family of positive-degree classes.** Let W be a connected noetherian scheme with a geometric point and the full finite-coefficient étale `K(π,1)` property. For any finite index set I, primes `p_i`, positive degrees `q_i` and classes `a_i` in `H^{q_i}_et(W,F_{p_i})`, with constant coefficients, there is a pointed connected finite étale surjective `f:W′→W` such that `f*a_i=0` for every i. The cover may depend on the entire finite family.

The full canonical finite-coefficient property of W; I is finite and every `q_i>0`. A lift of the geometric point is selected on each cover. No uniform cover for all classes or degrees is asserted.

Use [All-coefficient finite-cover criterion](#nc-0-all-coefficient-effacement) with each constant finite `F_{p_i}` sheaf to choose one finite étale surjective cover killing `a_i`. This criterion covers every `q_i>0`, including degree one; the prime-field criterion stated only in degrees at least two cannot replace it here. Use IG.0's pointed finite-cover dictionary: take the finite fibre product of the chosen covers over W and its connected component through the tuple of chosen geometric lifts. That component is finite étale surjective over connected noetherian W and maps to every chosen cover. Use SF.2's canonical pullback composition and zero-preservation: each class remains zero after refinement. For I empty choose `id_W`. The connected component is selected using the chosen point, not a normality assumption.

**Checks.**

- The empty family is killed by the identity cover; a family of zero classes also needs no enlargement.
- A family containing a degree-one class is included. In the elementary `H¹` torsor argument, the finite étale `F_p` torsor acquires a section after pullback to itself and then to its chosen connected component.
- Only finitely many killing covers are intersected. No claim of an open subgroup simultaneously killing infinitely many classes is used.

The construction and its conventions follow [Alexander Schmidt and Jakob Stix](#reference-schmidt-stix-2016), Lemma 2.7 and its proof, p. 827.

Use [All-coefficient finite-cover criterion](#nc-0-all-coefficient-effacement); [InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups](../InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups/README.md) Layer IG.0; [SchemeAndStackFoundations](../SchemeAndStackFoundations/README.md) Layer SF.2 (sites and scheme cohomology).

<a id="prime-field-kunneth"></a>

**Künneth for prime-field coefficients.** Let k be a separably closed field, W and T schemes of finite type over k, and p a prime invertible in k. The external product `⊕_(i+j=q)Hⁱ(W,𝔽_p)⊗Hʲ(T,𝔽_p)→Hᵠ(W×_kT,𝔽_p)` is an isomorphism for every q, natural for pullback along morphisms of pairs. No properness or smoothness is assumed.

k separably closed; W, T of finite type; p invertible in k. In the applications k is algebraically closed of characteristic zero.

Use EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.2.6 (`VanishingCycles.etaleKunneth`), specialized to constant `𝔽_p` complexes. Its derived external-product formula identifies `RΓ(W×_kT,𝔽_p)` with `RΓ(W,𝔽_p)⊗ᴸ_(𝔽_p)RΓ(T,𝔽_p)`. Over the coefficient field, the canonical direct sum on cohomology has no Tor terms. Pullback naturality is inherited from the supplied external cup product.

**Checks.**

- For `W=T=𝔾_m` over `ℂ` and `p=2`, `H¹(𝔾_m,𝔽_2)=𝔽_2` and `H¹(𝔾_m×𝔾_m,𝔽_2)=𝔽_2²`, `H²=𝔽_2`: the formula gives dimensions 1,2,1 although neither factor is proper.
- If W is a geometric point, the formula is the identity on every cohomology group of T.
- With `ℤ/4` coefficients the Künneth map has Tor terms, so the clean sum formula is stated for prime-field coefficients only.

The construction and its conventions follow [The Stacks Project Authors](#reference-stacks), Lemma 59.97.9 (Section 59.97, Tag 0F13).

Use [EtaleCohomologyFoundations](../EtaleCohomologyFoundations/README.md) §F.2.6 (`VanishingCycles.etaleKunneth`).

<a id="pi1-products"></a>

**Fundamental groups of products.** Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and X, Y connected k-schemes, X of finite type, with geometric points a, b and c over them. The projections induce an isomorphism `π₁(X×_kY,c)≅π₁(X,a)×π₁(Y,b)`. Consequently connected finite étale covers of the form `X′×_kY′` are cofinal among connected finite étale covers of `X×_kY`. Over a field k of characteristic zero with algebraic closure k̄, for geometrically connected X, Y with X of finite type and Y quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the arithmetic group is the fibre product `π₁(X×_kY)≅π₁(X)×_(Gal(k̄/k))π₁(Y)`, compatibly with the projections.

k of characteristic zero (algebraically closed for the first statement); X connected of finite type, Y connected; for the arithmetic statement X, Y geometrically connected, X of finite type and Y quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

The geometric statement is SGA 1, Exposé XIII, Proposition 4.6 (the Künneth formula for `π₁`), in characteristic zero where every prime is different from p and resolution of singularities supplies the strong desingularisation hypothesis; for X proper it is already SGA 1, Exposé X, Corollaire 1.7. Open subgroups of a product of profinite groups contain products of open subgroups, which gives cofinality. For the arithmetic statement, compare the homotopy exact sequences `1→π₁(Z_k̄)→π₁(Z)→Gal(k̄/k)→1` for `Z=X`, Y, `X×_kY` (Stacks, Lemma 58.14.3) and apply the geometric isomorphism to the kernels.

**Checks.**

- For `X=Y=𝔾_m` over `ℂ`, `π₁(𝔾_m²)=ℤ̂²` and the degree-n² cover `(z,w)↦(zⁿ,wⁿ)` is a product cover, as is every cover of `𝔾_m²` up to refinement.
- Over `k=ℚ` with `X=Y=Spec ℚ(i)`, `X×_ℚY` is disconnected (two copies of `Spec ℚ(i)`); geometric connectedness is needed for the fibre-product formula.
- The arithmetic group of `X×_kY` is the fibre product over `Gal(k̄/k)`, not `π₁(X)×π₁(Y)`: for `X=Y=Spec k` this would give Gal×Gal instead of Gal.

The construction and its conventions follow [SGA 1](#reference-sga1), Exposé XIII, Proposition 4.6, p. 310; Exposé X, Corollaire 1.7, pp. 203–204; [The Stacks Project Authors](#reference-stacks), Lemma 58.14.3 (Tag 0BTX).

Use [EtaleCohomologyFoundations](../EtaleCohomologyFoundations/README.md) §F.0.A2 (the arithmetic exact sequence); [InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups](../InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups/README.md) Layer IG.0.

<a id="nc-0-product-cover-effacement"></a>

**Prime-field effacement on every cover of a product.** Let X,Y be geometrically connected geometrically unibranch varieties over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field k, each with the full finite-coefficient étale `K(π,1)` property. For a pointed connected finite étale cover `Z→X×_kY`, a prime p, q&gt;0 and `c∈H^q_et(Z,F_p)`, there are pointed connected finite étale covers `X″→X` and `Y″→Y` and a finite étale surjective map `h:X″×_kY″→Z` over `X×_kY` such that `h*c=0`. The two covers may depend on Z,p,q,c; Z itself need not be a product or a Galois cover.

Algebraically closed k of characteristic zero; separated finite-type geometrically connected geometrically unibranch X and Y; their full canonical finite-coefficient properties; constant `F_p` with p prime and q&gt;0.

The projection-compatible product isomorphism is [Fundamental groups of products](#pi1-products); EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.0.2 supplies the dictionary between pointed covers and finite continuous sets. If K is the open subgroup for Z in G×H, take `U=i_G⁻¹K` and `V=i_H⁻¹K` with `i_G(g)=(g,1)`, `i_H(h)=(1,h)`. Use OpenSubgroup.comap/prod, `Subgroup.prod_le_iff` and `map_le_iff_le_comap` to obtain `U×V≤K`, maximal among such rectangles. Compactness makes both coset sets finite without requiring K normal. The same IG.0 dictionary realizes U,V as connected covers X′,Y′, and the equivariant surjection `(G×H)/(U×V)→(G×H)/K` as a finite étale surjective map `X′×Y′→Z`. This realizes a domination, not an isomorphism with Z. Pull c back to X′×Y′. Use the canonical, pullback-natural external-product isomorphism `⊕_{i+j=q} H^i_et(X′,F_p)⊗_{F_p}H^j_et(Y′,F_p)→H^q_et(X′×Y′,F_p)` of [Künneth for prime-field coefficients](#prime-field-kunneth). Every tensor and the direct sum have finite support; no choice of cohomology basis or finite-dimensionality is needed. Write the pulled-back class as a finite sum of `a_s×b_s`. For each summand choose `a_s` if its degree is positive, and otherwise `b_s`, whose degree is then q&gt;0. Finite-etale-invariance gives the full property of X′ and Y′. Apply [One cover kills a finite family of positive-degree classes](#nc-0-positive-family-effacement) to the two finite designated families to get `X″→X′` and `Y″→Y′`. Degree one, including an `H¹⊗H¹` summand in degree two, must be included. Naturality and bilinearity of the external product make every pulled-back summand zero, hence kill c. Compose the refinement with `X′×Y′→Z`. Product/base-change/composition preservation of finite étaleness and surjectivity are imported from IG.0/SF.2, as are connectedness and geometric-unibranch stability.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.ProductSmoke.diagonal_C2`: For the diagonal K in `C₂×C₂`, the quotient has two cosets while the largest contained product subgroup is trivial and has four cosets. The proof requires a product refinement, not that the original cover be a product.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.ProductSmoke.diagonal_S3_nonnormal`: The diagonal in `S₃×S₃` is nonnormal, yet its finite coset set and the rectangular domination are valid. No quotient-group structure is required.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.ProductSmoke.mixed_degree_one`: For graded `F₂` spaces having generators in degrees 0,1,2, maps killing degree two but preserving degree one retain the nonzero `H¹⊗H¹` coordinate in total degree two. Killing every positive-degree designated factor removes it.
- `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne.ProductSmoke.nonfield_canonical_map`: For a,b in `Z/4` with `2a=2b=0`, `ab=0`; nevertheless 2 is nonzero and satisfies `2·2=0`. This exact arithmetic fixture detects the zero canonical cycle-product map in the free complex `[Z/4 --2→ Z/4]`; its homology/tensor bridge is an explicitly untyped generic input.
- For `R=Z/4` and the free cochain complex `C=[R --2→ R]` in degrees 0,1, both `H⁰(C)⊗_R H⁰(C)` and `H⁰(C⊗_R C)` have order two, but the canonical map is zero: the generating cycles `2⊗2` map to `4=0`. An abstract isomorphism or a degreewise tensor formula over arbitrary torsion coefficients cannot replace the prime-field canonical map.

The construction and its conventions follow [Alexander Schmidt and Jakob Stix](#reference-schmidt-stix-2016), Lemma 2.7 and its proof, p. 827; [The Stacks Project Authors](#reference-stacks), Section 59.97, Lemma 59.97.9 and printed proof; canonical map in 59.97.8.

<a id="nc-0-geometric-product"></a>

**Binary geometric products preserve the full property.** Over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field k, the product `X×_kY` of two geometrically connected geometrically unibranch k-varieties with the full finite-coefficient étale `K(π,1)` property has that full property, defined by the canonical comparisons in all degrees and with its full profinite fundamental group.

Both factors are separated finite-type geometrically connected geometrically unibranch k-varieties; k algebraically closed of characteristic zero; all finite coefficients.

The product is connected and noetherian, its connected finite étale covers are dominated by products of covers of the factors by [Fundamental groups of products](#pi1-products), and it is geometrically unibranch because the factors are and k is algebraically closed. For every connected finite étale `Z→X×Y`, every prime p and `q≥2`, [Prime-field effacement on every cover of a product](#nc-0-product-cover-effacement) supplies a finite étale surjective refinement killing each `constant-F_p` class. Apply the already owned [Constant prime-field tests on all finite covers](#nc-0-prime-field-effacement) criterion with P the set of all primes. Its coefficient trivialization and dévissage recover every finite continuous coefficient module, not merely constant `F_p`. Preserve the canonical comparison and the full fundamental group.

**Checks.**

- With `X=Spec k`, the product and its canonical comparison recover those of Y.
- The conclusion is not the vanishing of `H^q_et(X×Y,F_p)`. It is that the canonical group-to-sheaf comparison is an isomorphism.
- The two factors may be nonproper. No maximal-pro-p quotient or universal one-cover killing assertion is substituted.

The construction and its conventions follow [Alexander Schmidt and Jakob Stix](#reference-schmidt-stix-2016), Lemma 2.7 and its proof, p. 827.

<a id="nc-0-products"></a>

**Characteristic-zero products of étale K(π,1) varieties.** Over a characteristic-zero field k, a finite product of geometrically connected geometrically unibranch k-varieties having the full finite-coefficient property again has that property.

Each factor is a geometrically connected geometrically unibranch variety; k has characteristic zero; full finite coefficients.

Use the already owned [Separable-closure invariance of finite-coefficient `K(π,1)`](#nc-0-separable-base-change) equivalence to pass to the algebraic closure of k; characteristic zero identifies the separable and algebraic closures. Use its finite-cover and class descent and its eventual-zero continuity comparison; no injectivity of a single restriction map is needed. For two geometric factors apply [Binary geometric products preserve the full property](#nc-0-geometric-product). Its [Prime-field effacement on every cover of a product](#nc-0-product-cover-effacement) proof kills one prime-field class on every arbitrary connected finite cover, using connected product refinements and finite families including degree one. Induct on the finite number of factors. The empty product is Spec k by field; the one-factor case is the hypothesis. Import product stability of the geometric conditions so every induction step satisfies [Binary geometric products preserve the full property](#nc-0-geometric-product). Apply [Separable-closure invariance of finite-coefficient `K(π,1)`](#nc-0-separable-base-change) back over k. The geometric rectangular-subgroup argument is not applied to the two arithmetic groups: their product group over k is a fibre product over `G_k`.

**Checks.**

- Over nonclosed k the arithmetic product `π₁` is a fibre product over `G_k`, not a direct product. No positive-characteristic product theorem is asserted.
- The empty product is Spec k and the one-factor product is the original variety. Every binary step imports geometric connectedness and geometric-unibranch stability.
- No further universal-cover filtered cohomology interchange is needed specifically for this product construction; affine-transition continuity remains necessary in its [Separable-closure invariance of finite-coefficient `K(π,1)`](#nc-0-separable-base-change) prerequisite.

The construction and its conventions follow [Alexander Schmidt and Jakob Stix](#reference-schmidt-stix-2016), Lemma 2.7(b) and proof, p. 827.

### 1.10 Homotopy fibres of elementary fibrations

<a id="elementary-homotopy-fibre"></a>

**Homotopy fibre of an elementary curve fibration.** For a smooth elementary fibration `X→Y` in characteristic zero with nonempty affine geometric curve fibres, construct the pointed pro-homotopy fibre sequence `X_y,et→X_et→Y_et` and its long exact sequence of raw homotopy groups. The map on `π₁` is the geometric fibration map from the finite-cover dictionary. Show that the geometric affine fibre is a raw `K(π,1)`, so vanishing of higher homotopy for Y implies it for X. The compactification is smooth proper with geometrically connected fibres and its removed divisor is finite étale over Y.

Use the exact [Elementary curve fibrations preserve étale `K(π,1)`](#nc-0-elementary-fibration) compactification and boundary hypotheses, not an arbitrary smooth morphism.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `elementaryFibration.homotopyFibre`: Give the comparison from the geometric fibre to the homotopy fibre.
- `elementaryFibration.homotopyExact`: Provide the pointed long exact sequence.
- `elementaryFibration.pi1Exact`: Its degree-one maps agree with finite-cover transport.

**Checks.**

- For the product of an affine hyperbolic curve and Y, recover the split fibre sequence.
- A proper `P¹` fibre has nonzero higher information and does not meet the affine-fibre conclusion.
- Boundary ramification over Y is excluded by the finite étale hypothesis.

The construction and its conventions follow [Alexander Schmidt and Jakob Stix](#reference-schmidt-stix-2016), §2.3, Proposition 2.8 and its proof, pp. 827–828; finite covers in Lemma 2.1, pp. 821–822.

### 1.11 Elementary fibrations and Artin towers

<a id="nc-0-elementary-fibration"></a>

**Elementary curve fibrations preserve étale K(π,1).** Let `f:X→Y` be an elementary fibration of smooth connected varieties over a characteristic-zero field: X is the complement of a divisor D, finite étale over Y, in a smooth proper geometrically connected curve family `X̄→Y`, and each fibre of `X→Y` is a nonempty affine curve. If Y has the full finite-coefficient property, then X has it.

Smooth connected varieties and the specified elementary curve fibration; characteristic zero; full finite coefficients on Y.

Use [Comparison with raw étale `K(π,1)`](#nc-0-raw-homotopy-comparison) to turn the hypothesis on Y into vanishing of its higher raw étale homotopy. The geometric fibre is a smooth affine curve, hence has the raw property by [Smooth curves of affine or positive-genus type](#nc-0-smooth-curve). Pull f back over the filtered pointed finite étale covers of Y. Apply the elementary homotopy-fibre construction and its long exact sequence, with Schmidt–Stix Lemma 2.1's invariance of higher groups under finite covers. That sequence, together with `π₁` of the universal finite-cover system of Y being trivial, identifies the higher homotopy exact sequence for `X_y → X → Y`. In each degree `n ≥ 2` the fibre and base terms vanish, hence so does `πₙ(X)`. Convert back with [Comparison with raw étale `K(π,1)`](#nc-0-raw-homotopy-comparison). The higher homotopy sequence is used in every degree; the arithmetic `π₁` exact sequence alone does not imply higher vanishing.

**Checks.**

- An iterated tower must retain the smooth/proper compactification and finite étale boundary data; a general smooth morphism is not covered.

The construction and its conventions follow [Alexander Schmidt and Jakob Stix](#reference-schmidt-stix-2016), Proposition 2.8 and proof, pp. 827–828; Lemma 2.1, pp. 821–822.

<a id="nc-0-artin-neighbourhood"></a>

**Artin towers give étale K(π,1) examples.** For a finite tower `X=X_r→⋯→X₀=Spec k` of smooth connected characteristic-zero varieties with each arrow an elementary curve fibration as specified in [Elementary curve fibrations preserve étale `K(π,1)`](#nc-0-elementary-fibration), X has the full finite-coefficient property. In particular this applies to strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhoods of Schmidt–Stix Definition 6.1, whose additional product-embedding condition must not be omitted when naming that stronger notion.

Characteristic-zero field; finite tower with actual [Elementary curve fibrations preserve étale `K(π,1)`](#nc-0-elementary-fibration) data at every arrow.

The initial field is `K(π,1)` by [Fields are étale `K(π,1)`](#nc-0-field). Induct on the length, applying [the elementary-fibration theorem](#nc-0-elementary-fibration) at each arrow. The stronger hyperbolicity and product embeddings are not required for this induction but are required to call the object strongly hyperbolic. For `n ≥ 4` use the explicit model `M₀,n = {(x₄,…,x_n) ∈ (P¹∖{0,1,∞})^(n−3) : x_i ≠ x_j for i ≠ j}`. Forgetting the last coordinate `M₀,n+1 → M₀,n` is an elementary curve fibration: the relative compactification is `P¹×M₀,n → M₀,n`, the removed divisor is the disjoint union of the n sections 0, 1, `∞`, `x₄`, …, `x_n`, hence finite étale of degree n, and every fibre is `P¹` minus n points. The tower `M₀,n → ⋯ → M₀,4 = P¹∖{0,1,∞} → Spec k` therefore satisfies the hypothesis (Schmidt–Stix, Definition 6.1 and the example after it, p. 845).

**Checks.**

`- M₀,4=P¹` minus `{0,1,∞}`; the forgetful tower of the explicit model gives `M₀,n` for every `n ≥ 4`. For `n = 5` the fibre of `M₀,5 → M₀,4` over `x₄` is `P¹` minus the four points 0, 1, `∞`, `x₄`. This does not prove the anabelian reconstruction theorem of Schmidt–Stix §6.

The construction and its conventions follow [Alexander Schmidt and Jakob Stix](#reference-schmidt-stix-2016), Definition 6.1 and following `M₀,n` example, p. 845.

Use [Fields are étale `K(π,1)`](#nc-0-field); [Elementary curve fibrations preserve étale `K(π,1)`](#nc-0-elementary-fibration).

<a id="nc-0-prime-power-degree-two-killing"></a>

**Prime-power towers kill higher prime-power torsion.** For C a connected smooth projective curve of genus `g≥1` over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field k, a prime p and `a≥0`, there exists a connected finite étale surjective `f:D→C` of degree `p^a`, given by a tower of a connected degree-p covers, such that `f*:H²_et(C,μ_(p^a))→H²_et(D,μ_(p^a))` is zero. For `a=0` the identity cover and the zero coefficient `μ_1` give the assertion. The composite cover need not be Galois over C.

k is algebraically closed of characteristic zero; C is a connected smooth projective k-curve of genus `g≥1`. p is a prime number, so p is invertible in k. The fundamental group is the full profinite `π₁ᵉᵗ(C,x)`. a is a natural number, including zero; no common witness for all a is claimed.

For `a=0` choose C itself. For the induction step apply [A connected prime-degree étale cover](#nc-0-connected-prime-degree-cover) to the curve at that stage. SF.3's finite-étale Riemann–Hurwitz formula `g(D)=1+p(g(C)−1)` guarantees genus≥1, so the induction can be repeated. Finite étale covers compose, and their degrees multiply. A tower of a degree-p covers is connected and its composite has degree `p^a`; connectedness of each chosen source is retained. Do not assert that successive Galois covers have a Galois composite. Apply the degree-pullback formula of [Étale cohomology of curves with `μ_n` coefficients](#curve-kummer-cohomology) with `n=p^a≥1`. Multiplication by `p^a` in `Z/(p^a)` is zero, so the map kills every class at once. A single degree-p cover only multiplies `H²(μ_(p^a))` by p and does not suffice when a&gt;1. With a primitive `p^a`-th root chosen on k the same conclusion holds for constant `Z/(p^a)` coefficients. Higher coefficient dévissage of arbitrary monodromy is a different step, supplied by [Constant prime-field tests on all finite covers](#nc-0-prime-field-effacement).

**Checks.**

- At `p=3,a=2`, the degree-3 map on `Z/9` sends 1 to `3≠0`; the degree-9 tower map sends every class to zero.
- At genus `2,p=3`, one prime-degree step has genus 4 and the two-step source genus 10; at genus one all sources have genus one.
`- a=0` corresponds to `n=1`, not `n=0`; the latter coefficient is not part of the finite Kummer calculation.

The construction and its conventions follow [Alexander Schmidt](#reference-schmidt-curve-1996), Proposition 15, proof, printed pp. 243–244; [The Stacks Project Authors](#reference-stacks), 0AMB Lemma 59.69.2; 03RQ Lemma 59.69.1.

### 1.12 Pro-p covers and arithmetic cohomology

<a id="pro-p-curve-comparison"></a>

**Geometric pro-p and arithmetic p-power comparison.** For a smooth hyperbolic curve over a characteristic-zero field, compare the p-power étale cohomology on the geometric pro-p cover system with the continuous cohomology of its maximal geometric pro-p fundamental group. Construct the comparison for `ℤ/p^m(j)`, then its derived `ℤ_p` limit, preserving cup products, trace and the arithmetic action of the full `G_K`. The arithmetic group is the relative geometric-pro-p extension. Compare its Hochschild–Serre sequence with the étale arithmetic sequence; rationalizing gives the same Chern class and degree maps. Include the `lim¹` terms before using the Mittag–Leffler hypotheses appropriate to these finite curve groups.

The geometric fibre is hyperbolic and characteristic zero. The arithmetic quotient remains `G_K`. Cofinality is in the p-primary geometric-cover calculation, not in all finite covers.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `proPCurve.finiteComparison`: Give the natural finite coefficient comparison.
- `proPCurve.integralComparison`: Give the derived inverse-limit comparison with explicit `lim¹`.
- `proPCurve.cupComparison`: Identify cup, trace and degree classes.
- `proPCurve.arithmeticComparison`: Identify the arithmetic edge maps and Chern class.

**Checks.**

- For a punctured affine genus-zero hyperbolic curve, the geometric pro-p group is free and degree-two geometric cohomology vanishes.
- For a proper genus-g curve, its surface relation retains the nonzero degree-two class.
- For `S₃` and constant `F₃`, the maximal pro-3 quotient loses `H³`; this theorem does not assert a general full-group comparison.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m99), §0, geometric pro-p conventions, author pp. 13–16; §8, arithmetic Chern classes, pp. 42–47; [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m96), §§1–2, printed pp. 576–582.

<a id="cofinal-artin-neighbourhoods"></a>

**Cofinal hyperbolic Artin neighbourhoods.** For a finitely generated regular field extension `K/k` in characteristic zero, construct cofinal geometrically connected smooth k-models whose nonempty open subsets admit, after shrinking, a tower of elementary fibrations with hyperbolic geometric curve fibres ending at `Spec k`. For arbitrary finitely generated `K/k`, let k′ be the relative algebraic closure of k in K, construct the towers over k′ and retain the finite extension k′/k in arithmetic comparisons. Prove the cofinality needed to recover the function-field absolute Galois group from the groups of these neighbourhoods. Construct the exact geometric fundamental-group sequences at each step and their compatibility with shrinking and geometric field extension. Distinguish these towers from the additional product-embedding condition in a strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhood.

Cofinality concerns generic-point neighbourhoods of geometrically connected smooth models of a regular extension in characteristic zero, over k′ in the general case.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `artinNeighbourhood.exists`: Construct the required tower after shrinking.
- `artinNeighbourhood.cofinal`: Every nonempty generic neighbourhood contains one.
- `artinNeighbourhood.pi1Sequence`: Give the geometric extension for each fibration step.

**Checks.**

- A regular extension of transcendence degree zero has `K=k`; in general the zero-dimensional base is `Spec k′`. For `K=ℚ(i)` over `k=ℚ`, shrinking cannot replace `Spec ℚ(i)` by `Spec ℚ`.
- An affine smooth curve has a single fibration step after removing enough points to make it hyperbolic.
- A given `K(π,1)` tower does not by itself prove the existence or cofinality statement.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m99), §15, Lemma 15.8, author pp. 77–80; [Alexander Schmidt and Jakob Stix](#reference-schmidt-stix-2016), §6, Definition 6.1, p. 845, and Lemma 6.3 with proof, pp. 847–850.

### Examples

For a separably closed field, the finite-cover group is trivial and positive-degree étale cohomology of finite locally constant coefficients vanishes. For `P¹` over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, the group is still trivial but `H²(P¹,F_p)` is one-dimensional. Its comparison map from group cohomology cannot be an isomorphism. This discriminates the `K(π,1)` predicate from a definition involving `π₁` alone.

Finite direct image must retain sheet monodromy. Let `H=C₂⊂S₃=G` and use the three-sheeted cover of classifying finite-cover topoi. Direct image of `F₂` is the permutation module `F₂[G/H]`. Shapiro gives `H^q(G,F₂[G/H])≃H^q(H,F₂)`, of dimension one in each `q≥0`. Treating the stalk as a constant rank-three module would instead give three copies. In degree zero the correct invariants are the constant functions on the transitive sheet set, of dimension one.

The raw and pro-p homotopy conditions differ even when the maximal pro-p group is trivial. Write `S₃` as pairs `(a,e)∈F₃⋊F₂`, with multiplication `(a,e)(b,f)=(a+(−1)^e b,e+f)`. Use integer lifts `a∈{0,1,2}` and set `s(g)=(−1)^e`. The normalized carry cocycle is

```text
β(g,h) = (a(g)+s(g)a(h)−a(gh))/3 mod 3.
c(g,h,k) = a(g)s(g)β(h,k) mod 3.
```

The numerator is divisible by three, and `β` has the sign-twisted `F₃` action. Consequently c is a degree-three cocycle with trivial coefficients. For `r=(1,0)`, the bar cycle `z=[r|r|r]+[r|r²|r]` has boundary zero over `F₃`. The two values of c are 0 and 1, so `⟨c,z⟩=1`. Thus `H³(S₃,F₃)` is nonzero. Every homomorphism `S₃` to a finite 3-group is trivial, so the maximal pro-3 quotient loses this raw cohomology class. A p-primary cover theorem does not imply an all-primes raw statement.

For a smooth proper geometric curve of genus `g≥1` in characteristic zero, a connected finite étale cover of degree p pulls the degree class in `H²(−,F_p)` to p times that class, hence to zero. Constructing a connected cover uses the nonzero p-torsion of its Jacobian and the finite-cover dictionary. In a separable field extension, descending the cover and descending the equality that its pulled-back class is zero are separate finite-data steps.

On `P¹−{0,1,∞}`, the unit tangent at 0 is a base-point fibre functor, although 0 is not an ordinary endpoint of the open curve. Its finite Kummer projections measure z and 1−z. In `P¹−{∞}=A¹` the geometric fundamental group is trivial, so the local inertia map has zero image. This prevents confusing a local inertia group with an injective subgroup in every affine curve.


In a common group frame, the path cocycle satisfies the cocycle equation for conjugation by the reference section. If both sections split the same quotient q and `q(p)=1`, its values lie in `MonoidHom.ker q`. The latter hypothesis is necessary to interpret p as a geometric path.
