## Layer 2: Unipotent fundamental groups and their realizations

The characteristic-zero unipotent/Lie foundation precedes neutral geometric unipotent reconstruction. Use the supplied neutral tensor equivalence for geometric unipotent categories, then the group and path realizations, their two distinct finite towers, Hodge filtration, Frobenius paths and endpoint-compatible comparison. The two-step Malcev construction precedes reconstruction of curves.

<a id="split-unipotent-quotients"></a>

**Unipotent groups and their homogeneous quotients in characteristic zero.** Let k be a field of characteristic zero. (a) For a unipotent algebraic group U over k the exponential map `exp:Lie(U)_a→U` is an isomorphism of schemes, with group law given by the Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff series, and `U↦Lie(U)` is an equivalence between unipotent algebraic groups and finite-dimensional nilpotent Lie algebras; every unipotent group is split (has a subnormal series with quotients `𝔾_a`) and is isomorphic as a variety to affine space. Central quotients and the lower central series correspond to those of the Lie algebra, and a pro-unipotent group is the limit of its finite-dimensional unipotent quotients along surjections. (b) For a closed `subgroup H⊆U`, not necessarily normal, the fppf quotient sheaf `U/H` of right cosets is represented by a smooth affine variety isomorphic to `𝔸^(dim U−dim H)`, and `U→U/H` is a trivial right H-torsor: there is a section, so `U≅(U/H)×H` as schemes with right H-action. (c) For every k-algebra R, including non-reduced ones, every fppf H-torsor over Spec R is trivial, and `(U/H)(R)=U(R)/H(R)`. (d) For a pro-unipotent `U=lim U_n` and a compatible system of closed subgroups `H_n⊆U_n` with surjective transition maps, `(lim U_n/H_n)(R)=U(R)/H(R)` for every R.

k of characteristic zero; U unipotent (hence split and smooth); H a closed subgroup; R any k-algebra.

(a) is the characteristic-zero theory of unipotent groups: exp is an isomorphism of schemes, Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff gives the group law, and Lie is an equivalence. In characteristic zero `𝔾_a` has no proper nontrivial subgroups, so every unipotent group is split, and a split unipotent group is an affine space as a variety. (b) The quotient `U/H` exists as a separated scheme of finite type and is quasi-affine. Prove it is affine space by induction on dim U: choose a central `subgroup Z≅𝔾_a` of U. If `Z⊆H`, then `U/H=(U/Z)/(H/Z)`. Otherwise `Z∩H=1`, ZH is a closed subgroup, and U/H→U/ZH is a torsor under Z acting by translation, trivial over the affine base U/ZH, so U/H≅(U/ZH)×𝔸¹. (c) H is split, so `H¹(Spec R,H)=0` by dévissage to `H¹(Spec R,𝔾_a)=H¹(Spec R,O)=0`; the long exact sequence of pointed sets for `1→H→U→U/H→1` then gives `(U/H)(R)=U(R)/H(R)`. (d) Take limits of the exact sequences `1→H_n(R)→U_n(R)→(U_n/H_n)(R)→1`. The transition maps `H_(n+1)(R)→H_n(R)` are surjective by (c) applied to the unipotent kernel, so the `lim¹` term vanishes.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.Unipotent.exp_isIso`: `exp:Lie(U)_a→U` is an isomorphism of schemes, with BCH multiplication.
- `TauCeti.Unipotent.lieEquiv`: The equivalence between unipotent groups and nilpotent Lie algebras.
- `TauCeti.Unipotent.isSplit`: Every unipotent group over a field of characteristic zero is split.
- `TauCeti.Unipotent.homogeneousQuotient_isAffineSpace`: `U/H≅𝔸^(dim U−dim H)` for every closed H.
- `TauCeti.Unipotent.quotient_section`: `U→U/H` has a section; `U≅(U/H)×H`.
- `TauCeti.Unipotent.torsor_trivial`: Every H-torsor over an affine scheme is trivial.
- `TauCeti.Unipotent.quotient_points`: `(U/H)(R)=U(R)/H(R)` for every k-algebra R.
- `TauCeti.Unipotent.proQuotient_points`: The pro-unipotent version (d).

**Checks.**

`- U=𝔾_a²`, H the diagonal `𝔾_a: U/H≅𝔸¹` by `(x,y)↦x−y`, and `(U/H)(R)=R²/R` for every R.
- U the Heisenberg group of unitriangular 3×3 matrices with entries a (position 1,2), b (2,3) and c (1,3), and H the subgroup with `b=c=0`: right multiplication by H changes only a, so `U/H≅𝔸²` by `(a,b,c)↦(b,c)`, while conjugating an element of H with entry s by an element with `b≠0` creates the (1,3) entry −sb, so H is not normal; `(U/H)(R)=U(R)/H(R)` holds for every R, including `R=k[ε]/(ε²)`.
- In characteristic `p>0`, `H=α_p⊂U=𝔾_a` has quotient `𝔾_a/α_p≅𝔾_a` through Frobenius `x↦x^p`; for `R=k[t]`, `H(R)=0` and the map `U(R)/H(R)=R→(U/H)(R)=R` is `r↦r^p`, which misses t. The characteristic-zero hypothesis is used.
- For `𝔾_m/μ₂` over `ℚ`, the sheaf quotient contains the point 2, which has no rational square-root lift; its raw pointwise coset presheaf does not supply every sheaf section.
- A torus is not unipotent: `𝔾_m`-torsors over Spec R (line bundles) need not be trivial, so (c) fails for `H=𝔾_m`.

The construction and its conventions follow [J. S. Milne](#reference-milne-iag), 3.28, p. 61; Theorem 9.28, p. 146; Proposition 15.28, p. 257; Proposition 15.31, p. 258; Proposition 15.35, p. 260; Theorem 15.36, p. 261; 15.55–15.56, p. 266; Theorem 19.25 (Kostant–Rosenlicht), p. 342; §22.j, the vanishing of `H¹(S,U)` for affine S and split U, p. 405.

Use [TauCetiRoadmap.ReductiveGroups](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups/README.md#layer-5-solvable-and-unipotent-groups-the-unipotent-radical); [TauCetiRoadmap.ReductiveGroups](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups/README.md#layer-3-subgroups-quotients-components); `TauCeti.SmoothUnipotentAffineGroupSchemeCat`; `CommHopfAlgCat.fppfHomogeneousQuotient`; `CommHopfAlgCat.isPullback_fppfHomogeneousQuotientTorsor`; `CommHopfAlgCat.isLocallySurjective_fppfHomogeneousQuotientSheafProjection`; [SchemeAndStackFoundations](../SchemeAndStackFoundations/README.md) Layer SF.1 (descent, algebraic spaces and stacks).

### 2.0 Linear periods and word coordinates

<a id="linear-period-exactness"></a>

**De Rham exactness and Hodge–Tate grading.** Let `K/ℚ_p` be finite and let V be a finite-dimensional continuous `ℚ_p`-representation of `G_K`. Use FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory §R07.P7.1 for `D_HT`, its grading, Hodge–Tate admissibility and `gr D_dR≃D_HT`, through `GaloisRep.deRhamSupplierEquiv`. For `ℚ_p` coefficients, extend the coefficient field to contain the embeddings of K and descend by its coefficient-extension compatibility. Degree i is `(ℂ_p(i)⊗V)^{G_K}`, with labelled weight −i. Prove `deRhamStrictExact`: on a short exact sequence of de Rham representations, `D_dR` is exact with the induced filtrations and every induced morphism is strict. Prove tensor and dual compatibility of these strict-exactness interfaces with the supplied graded comparison. On semistable representations, prove exactness and strictness of `D_st` and its K-extension using the supplied comparison and full faithfulness; on crystalline representations restrict to `N=0`. This does not assert closure of crystalline representations under arbitrary extensions. ([Brinon–Conrad](#reference-brinon-conrad), §§5.1–5.2; Propositions 6.3.2–6.3.3, pp. 76–78; Proposition 9.1.11, p. 135; Proposition 9.2.14, p. 146.)

The API includes `deRhamStrictExact` and compatibility of strict exactness with tensor products, duals and finite base extension. Full faithfulness itself is consumed from FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory §R07.3.3.

**Checks.**

- For `V=ℚ_p(1)`, `D_dR` has its only jump in degree −1 and the graded Hodge–Tate space has its only nonzero piece in degree −1; changing to the dual changes the sign.
- For `V=0` every graded piece and period invariant is zero; evaluation is the isomorphism of zero spaces.
- Over ramified K, `D_st` remains a K₀-space; its filtered realization is `K⊗_{K₀}D_st`. Treating both spaces as K₀-filtered copies of equal dimension loses this scalar extension.

*Needs:* PadicPeriodRings §§1.4–1.5, 4.1–4.3; FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory §§R07.P7.1, R07.3.0–R07.3.3; arithmetic tensor invariants and continuous cohomology as in the supplier contracts.

<a id="linear-geometric-period-comparisons"></a>

**Linear geometric period comparisons.** For a smooth proper K-scheme X with a smooth proper `O_K`-model, construct `geometricLinearPeriodComparison` between `B_cris ⊗ Hⁱ_ét(X_K̄, ℚ_p)` and `B_cris ⊗_{K₀} Hⁱ_crys(X_κ/W(κ))[1/p]`. It preserves Galois action, Frobenius, products, Tate twists and cycle classes, and after extension to `B_dR` agrees with the strict filtered de Rham comparison. Include the Hodge–Tate decomposition `ℂ_p ⊗ Hⁿ_ét ≅ ⊕_(i+j=n) ℂ_p(−i) ⊗_K Hʲ(X, Ωⁱ)`. For a smooth proper model with a relative normal-crossings divisor D, use logarithmic crystalline and logarithmic de Rham complexes to obtain the corresponding comparisons for `X∖D`, with compact supports where required for trace duality. For a semistable pair use `B_st`, the Hyodo–Kato complex, the chosen uniformizer and `N_π=eN_p`; the good-reduction relative-boundary case has `N=0`. These are linear comparisons; the two-endpoint multiplicative enhancement is [Two-augmentation multiplicative comparison](#pointed-multiplicative-comparison). ([Yamashita](#reference-yamashita-open), *p-adic étale cohomology and crystalline cohomology for open varieties*, Theorems 1.1–1.4, pp. 3–4, and Theorems 2.2–2.3, 2.5 and 2.7, pp. 6–9, the open-variety comparisons; Brinon–Conrad, Theorem 2.2.3, p. 13.)

Prove `geometricLinearPeriodComparison_pullback`, `geometricLinearPeriodComparison_cup`, `geometricLinearPeriodComparison_twist`, the comparison with trace and supported cycle classes, and compatibility with finite base extension and the smooth-lift comparison. The nonproper comparison retains the proper smooth compactification and normal-crossings boundary hypotheses.

**Checks.**

`- X=Spec K` gives the supplied comparison of unit period invariants, with `H⁰` of dimension one and positive cohomology zero.
- For `X=ℙ¹`, `H²` is `ℚ_p(−1)`: covariant crystalline Frobenius is `pσ` and `Fil¹` is the whole line. The dual Tate line has Frobenius `p⁻¹σ`.
- For the smooth pair `(ℙ¹,{0,∞})`, `H¹` of `𝔾_m` is `ℚ_p(−1)`, and dlog z is its logarithmic de Rham class. Omitting the boundary from the de Rham complex incorrectly makes this class disappear.

*Needs:* [De Rham exactness and Hodge–Tate grading](#linear-period-exactness); CrystallineCohomology §§CR.2.3, CR.3.2–CR.3.4, CR.3:duality.1 and Layers CR.5–CR.6; EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§F.4–F.6; SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer SF.2.

<a id="generalized-jacobian-etale-comparison"></a>

**Finite étale and Tate-module comparison for the generalized Jacobian.** For the characteristic-zero pair `(C,D)` of [Generalized Jacobian of a reduced boundary](#reduced-boundary-generalized-jacobian), put `X=C−D` and specify `b∈X(k)`. Pulling back the multiplication-by-n covers of `J_D` along `a_b` identifies `π₁(X_k̄,b)ᵃᵇ/n` with `J_D[n](k̄)` for every `n≥1`, compatibly with divisibility transitions, the Galois action, maps of pointed pairs and field extension. Thus `H¹_et(X_k̄,ℤ/n)=Hom(J_D[n](k̄),ℤ/n)` and `H¹_et(X_k̄,μ_n)=Hom(J_D[n](k̄),μ_n)`. Passing to p-power inverse limits and rationalizing gives the contravariant identification `H¹_et(X_k̄,ℚ_p)=Hom(V_pJ_D,ℚ_p)` and its dual covariant identification `H¹_et(X_k̄,ℚ_p)∨=V_pJ_D`, without a Tate twist. With `μ_(p^m)` coefficients the limit is instead `Hom(T_pJ_D,ℤ_p(1))`. Division points of `a_b(x)` give the endpoint Kummer class under these same maps.

Spread the pointed pair to a finitely generated characteristic-zero subfield and embed it in ℂ. Serre's period-lattice isomorphism for the reduced modulus identifies the map on integral first homology. Use the supplied finite-cover comparison to identify its reduction modulo n with the pullback of the multiplication cover. Since the map is the algebraic Abel pullback, field-extension invariance descends its isomorphism and retains Galois equivariance; no embedding into ℂ is part of the result. Torsion maps are covariant, while cohomology pullback is contravariant.

**Checks.**

- For `X=𝔾_m`, `T_pJ_D=ℤ_p(1)` and `H¹_et(X_k̄,ℚ_p)=ℚ_p(−1)`; with μ coefficients `H¹_et(X_k̄,μ_n)=ℤ/n`. Identifying untwisted H¹ with the Tate module fails this test.
- For `X=ℙ¹−{0,1,∞}`, the two boundary loops give `J_D[n]=μ_n²` and `V_pJ_D=ℚ_p(1)²`; the proper Jacobian would give zero.
- For the nonsplit real divisor `{i,−i}`, complex conjugation acts trivially on `J_D[3](ℂ)`: the boundary sign cancels the cyclotomic sign. For the split pair `{0,∞}` it acts by −1. At `n=1` every displayed finite module is zero.

Sources: [Jean-Pierre Serre](#reference-serre-generalized-jacobians), Chapter V §3, no. 19, Proposition 11 and its corollary, pp. 99–101, for the Abel map on homology; ComplexComparisonPartII §§C6.2–C6.3 for Riemann existence and finite-coefficient comparison. The Tate-module statements follow by inverse limits and duality.

*Needs:* [Generalized Jacobian of a reduced boundary](#reduced-boundary-generalized-jacobian); ComplexComparisonPartII §§C6.2–C6.3; EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§F.0–F.4 (finite covers, field-extension invariance and adic limits); SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.3 (spreading out); AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli §A4.4 for the proper specialization.

<a id="generalized-jacobian-derham-comparison"></a>

**Filtered de Rham comparison for the generalized Jacobian.** For the same characteristic-zero pointed pair, prove that Abel pullback `H¹_dR(J_D/k)→H¹_dR(X/k)` is an isomorphism, natural in pointed pairs and field extension. On X use the logarithmic complex `[O_C→Ω¹_C(log D)]` and its Hodge filtration. On `J_D` use the Hodge filtration from a smooth proper compactification with normal-crossings boundary, proving independence of that compactification. The isomorphism is strict: `F¹H¹_dR(X)=H⁰(C,Ω¹_C(log D))` identifies with the invariant differentials on `J_D`, and `H¹_dR(X)/F¹=H¹(C,O_C)`. In particular the covariant dual quotient `H¹_dR(X)∨/F⁰` is `Lie(J_D)`, with dimensions `2g+r−1`, `g+r−1` and g for H¹, F¹ and its quotient respectively. For `K/ℚ_p` finite, if C extends to a smooth proper model and D to a reduced finite étale relative divisor, identify the dual of this filtered isomorphism with `D_dR(V_pJ_D)` through the étale comparison and the logarithmic period comparison. Retain the toric Tate line; no proper-abelian comparison alone supplies it.

For total H¹ spread to ℂ and apply Serre's homology isomorphism and the supplied ordinary and logarithmic de Rham–Betti comparisons. For F¹ apply his invariant-differential pullback theorem; the reduced modulus gives precisely simple logarithmic poles. The residue sequence gives the Hodge quotient and proves strictness. Prove scalar-extension compatibility of these algebraic maps and descend the isomorphisms from ℂ. At a good-reduction pair use the linear logarithmic period comparison, then dualize with its filtration and twist conventions.

**Checks.**

- With one rational boundary point, logarithmic differentials have zero residue there and are regular; this recovers the proper Jacobian H¹ and its g-dimensional Lie quotient.
- For `𝔾_m`, H¹ is the line dlog z, lies entirely in F¹ and has dual period realization `ℚ_p(1)` with filtration jump −1. The quotient of the dual by F⁰ is its one-dimensional Lie algebra.
- For three rational punctures on `ℙ¹`, dlog z and dlog(1−z) give two F¹ directions and `Lie(J_D)` has dimension two; dropping the boundary kills both.

Sources: [Jean-Pierre Serre](#reference-serre-generalized-jacobians), Chapter V §2, no. 10, Proposition 5, pp. 89–90 (invariant differentials), and §3, no. 19, Proposition 11, pp. 99–101 (total homology); ComplexComparisonPartII §§C5.1, C5.5, C5.7 (de Rham and logarithmic comparisons). The p-adic identification uses [Linear geometric period comparisons](#linear-geometric-period-comparisons), with its smooth-pair hypotheses.

*Needs:* [Generalized Jacobian of a reduced boundary](#reduced-boundary-generalized-jacobian); [Finite étale and Tate-module comparison for the generalized Jacobian](#generalized-jacobian-etale-comparison); ComplexComparisonPartII §§C5.1, C5.5, C5.7; EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§G.1–G.3 (normal-crossings compactifications); [De Rham exactness and Hodge–Tate grading](#linear-period-exactness); [Linear geometric period comparisons](#linear-geometric-period-comparisons).

<a id="infinitesimal-period-model"></a>

**Infinitesimal de Rham period model.** For the preceding smooth proper pair, define `infinitesimalPeriodModel` as the derived t-adic completion of its logarithmic de Rham cochain algebra after scalar extension from K to `B_dR⁺`. Use the convolution of the t-adic and Hodge filtrations; at each finite t-level the cochains compute logarithmic de Rham cohomology of that scalar-extended pair. Construct the equivalent logarithmic infinitesimal-site realization by the characteristic-zero Poincaré lemma. Include unit, cup product, pullback, both evaluations at specified interior K-points, derived reduction modulo tʳ for `r≥1` and the comparison after inverting t. Prove independence of the chosen embedding or hypercover resolution. After inverting t, use [Linear geometric period comparisons](#linear-geometric-period-comparisons) to identify this model with geometric étale cohomology; no integral `B_cris` comparison or crystalline extension theorem follows just from defining this model. (Olsson, §§5–6, the multiplicative de Rham and crystalline models; CrystallineCohomology §CR.5.4, the logarithmic Poincaré resolution, applied in characteristic zero.)

Its API is `infinitesimalPeriodModel_mod`, `infinitesimalPeriodModel_complete`, `infinitesimalPeriodModel_augmentations`, `infinitesimalPeriodModel_cup` and `infinitesimalPeriodModel_invert_t`.

**Checks.**

- For a point the model is `B_dR⁺` in degree zero, with the identity augmentation.
- Two distinct endpoints give two evaluations on the same algebra; replacing them with a single augmentation does not define the two-sided path bar construction.
- Reduction modulo t followed by passage to cohomology retains derived base change. Replacing a complex by its cohomology before reduction is not the definition.

*Needs:* [Linear geometric period comparisons](#linear-geometric-period-comparisons); PadicPeriodRings §1.5 and §4.1; SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer SF.2; CrystallineCohomology §CR.5.4; DerivedModuleAlgebra §§1.2–1.6 (derived completion, quotient towers and reduction maps).

<a id="word-algebra-shuffle"></a>

**Word algebra and shuffle coordinates.** For a finite-dimensional characteristic-zero vector space W, use the native tensor algebra for concatenation and its augmentation completion `∏_(n≥0) W^⊗n`. Its finite word modules are the quotients by augmentation powers; they are modules rather than Hopf quotients. Prove `wordShuffleDuality`: the restricted dual coordinate algebra has shuffle multiplication and deconcatenation coproduct, paired with concatenation and the primitive coproduct on the completed tensor algebra. Prove compatibility with degree truncation, unit, antipode, the affine universal connection and its horizontal transport. These are the word coordinates used in §2.4, with the order of path composition fixed there. (Kim 2009, §1, pp. 95–100; Besser, §3, Theorem 3.6, pp. 9–10.)

The API includes `wordShuffleDuality`, `wordCoordinate_empty`, `wordCoordinate_shuffle`, `wordCoordinate_deconcatenation`, `wordModule_truncation` and compatibility with the completed path-algebra action.

**Checks.**

- The empty word has value one on every group-like path and is the multiplicative unit of coordinates.
- The shuffle of a one-letter word with itself is twice the repeated word. A product assigning coefficient one fails this test.
- Two distinct letters have different concatenations; the shuffle product of their coordinate functions is their sum. Treating the word algebra itself as commutative confuses the paired algebras.

*Needs:* Mathlib `TensorAlgebra`, tensor products, duals and inverse limits of finite word modules. Sections 2.2–2.4 identify these algebraic coordinates with the completed path algebra and its universal connections.

### 2.1 Neutral tensor reconstruction

<a id="neutral-tensor-reconstruction"></a>

**Neutral tensor category and Hopf reconstruction.** Let K be a characteristic-zero field and C an essentially small K-linear rigid abelian symmetric tensor category with `End(1)=K` and an exact faithful K-linear tensor functor ω:C→finite-dimensional K-vector spaces. Use PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology §RD.6.64 (`RD6.neutralTannakian_recognition`) for the Hopf algebra of matrix coefficients, representation of `Aut^⊗(ω)` on every commutative K-algebra, and the tensor equivalence with finite-dimensional representations. For a commutative K-algebra R and an exact faithful K-linear tensor fibre functor `η:C→Proj_R`, construct `Isom^⊗(R⊗ω,η)` as an affine fpqc torsor under `Aut^⊗(ω)_R`, with right precomposition and commuting left postcomposition by `Aut^⊗(η)`. Here `Proj_R` consists of finite projective R-modules. C need not have a tensor generator, so the representing groups may be proaffine. Identify the unit-generated extension subcategory with the pro-unipotent quotient, and compare this reconstruction with Tau Ceti's finite-comodule equivalence when the Hopf algebra was given initially.

All coends use a fixed small skeleton; scalar extension and tensor isomorphisms are considered on every commutative K-algebra. Faithfulness and exactness are hypotheses.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `NeutralTensor.tensorIsomTorsor`: Represent tensor isomorphisms with left and right coactions.
- `NeutralTensor.tensorIsomTorsor_repEquiv`: For `C=Rep_K(G)` with G an affine group scheme of finite type and ω the forgetful functor, identify this torsor with PadicHodgeTheory §5.5's `tensorIsomTorsor`. On every R-algebra S the comparison sends a tensor isomorphism to itself; it intertwines right precomposition and left postcomposition and commutes with base change in R and tensor isomorphisms of η. The finite-type torsor is faithfully flat of finite presentation. Under `g·p=p∘g⁻¹`, the comparison preserves its class in SchemeAndStackFoundations §§1.15 and 2.3's common fppf torsor-class carrier `NonabelianH1`, using PadicHodgeTheory §5.5's `tensorIsomTorsor_rightToLeft` and `tensorIsomTorsor_actions`. No connectedness or reductivity hypothesis is imposed on G.
- `NeutralTensor.unipotentQuotient`: Identify the unit-extension subcategory.

**Checks.**

- For finite-dimensional vector spaces with the identity fibre functor the group is trivial.
- For representations of `G_a`, recover its coordinate Hopf algebra and its unipotent group.
- Truncating objects to a fixed extension length is not tensor-closed: lengths n and m can produce length `n+m`.
- For `η=R⊗ω` with nonzero R and finite-type G, the comparison identifies the identity tensor isomorphism and the neutral torsor class on both sides.
- For `G=GL₂`, precomposition by `a=((1,1),(0,1))` followed by `b=((1,0),(1,1))` sends p to `p∘a∘b`, with `ab≠ba`. Postcomposition by h sends this to `h∘p∘a∘b` on both sides of the comparison; the common left G-action is `g·p=p∘g⁻¹`.
- For `G=μ₂/ℚ`, descend the forgetful functor over `ℚ(√2)` using the cocycle `σ↦σ(√2)/√2`. Both constructions give the nonneutral torsor `Spec ℚ(√2)`, which becomes neutral over `ℚ(√2)`; an fpqc torsor need not have a rational tensor isomorphism.

The construction and its conventions follow [Pierre Deligne and James S. Milne](#reference-deligne-milne), §2, Theorem 2.11 and its proof, note pp. 21–29; §3, Theorem 3.2(a)–(b) and Remark 3.3(b), pp. 31–32. Finite presentation in the finite-type case descends from G after an fpqc trivialization. The unipotent specialization follows [Amnon Besser](#reference-besser), §2, Tannakian categories and fibre functors, PDF pp. 2–5; [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §1, published pp. 97–101.

Use [PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology](../PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology/README.md) §RD.6.64 (`RD6.neutralTannakian_recognition`); [Unipotent groups and their homogeneous quotients in characteristic zero](#split-unipotent-quotients); `CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory`; `ModuleCat`; [PadicHodgeTheory](../PadicHodgeTheory/README.md) §5.5 (`tensorIsomTorsor`, `tensorIsomTorsor_actions` and `tensorIsomTorsor_rightToLeft`); [SchemeAndStackFoundations](../SchemeAndStackFoundations/README.md) §§1.2, 1.15 and 2.3 (affine descent, torsors and their common class carrier).

### 2.2 Unipotent categories, fundamental groups and path torsors

<a id="nc-2-unipotent-length"></a>

**Unipotent length.** In a neutral Tannakian category C over a characteristic-zero field k, with unit 1, let `C_n` be the full subcategory of objects admitting a filtration `E=E_0 ⊇ E_1 ⊇ … ⊇ E_(n+1)=0` with each `E_i/E_(i+1)` a finite direct sum of 1. Zero summands are allowed. Write IsUnipotentLength(n,E) for this property, and Un(C) for the full subcategory of objects satisfying it for some n. Thus `C_0` consists of trivial objects, including zero. Filtrations witness a property; they are not extra data on the objects or extra restrictions on the full subcategory morphisms. Tensor products of lengths n and m have length at most `n+m`; `C_n` need not be tensor closed. For finite-dimensional linear representations over any field, the allowed length is monotone and the diagonal tensor action satisfies the same sum bound.

C is k-linear, abelian, rigid symmetric monoidal, with `End(1)=k` and an exact faithful k-linear tensor fibre functor to finite-dimensional vector spaces.

Construct the filtration predicate using subobjects and finite biproducts. An equivalent recursion extends a length-n object by a trivial object. Use exactness of tensor and the product filtration for tensor products; intersect and image filtrations for subobjects and quotients, and the dual filtration for duals. The union is an abelian rigid tensor subcategory.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `IsUnipotentLength.trivial`: Length zero is equivalent to being a finite direct sum of units.
- `IsUnipotentLength.mono`: Length n implies length `n+1` by inserting a zero graded layer.
- `IsUnipotentLength.extension`: An extension of length n by a trivial object has length `n+1`.
- `IsUnipotentLength.tensor`: Lengths n and m give tensor length at most `n+m`.
- `UnipotentCategory`: The full subcategory selected by the existence of a finite unipotent length, with its inherited morphisms.

**Checks.**

- `length_zero_object`: Zero is of length zero.
- `length_unit_sum`: A sum of two copies of the unit is of length zero.
- `length_nonsplit_extension`: For a nonsplit extension of unit by unit in a neutral unipotent category, the middle term has length one and does not have length zero.
- The zero object and every finite sum of units have length zero.
- A nontrivial extension of 1 by 1 has length one but not zero.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Appendix A.1, Definition A.1 and the paragraph before Definition A.2, pp. 934–935; [Bruno Chiarellotto and Bernard Le Stum](#reference-cls), Propositions 2.3.2 and 2.3.5, pp. 93–95.

<a id="nc-2-invariant-vector-criterion"></a>

**Invariant vectors and unipotence.** For a neutral Tannakian category C over a characteristic-zero field k, the following are equivalent: every object is a successive extension of units; its reconstructed affine group is pro-unipotent; every nonzero object E has a nonzero morphism `1→E`. The zero object is excluded from the last quantifier. In each finite-dimensional representation, an invariant line and induction on dimension produce a full unipotent flag. A nonzero finite-dimensional unipotent representation has a nonzero invariant vector over any field.

Neutral Tannakian hypotheses of [Unipotent length](#nc-2-unipotent-length).

Apply neutral reconstruction, imported from neutral tensor reconstruction, to pass between objects and finite-dimensional representations. For a pro-unipotent group all nonzero representations have invariants. Conversely apply the invariant hypothesis repeatedly to quotients; the resulting flag realizes every finite tensor-generated image in upper triangular matrices with unit diagonal. Finite tensor-generated images are unipotent; their inverse limit is pro-unipotent.

**Checks.**

- A one-dimensional representation with a nontrivial character has no nonzero invariant vector and cannot be unipotent.
- In finite-dimensional vector spaces with their usual tensor product the reconstructed group is trivial and every nonzero object has a nonzero vector.
- The assertion with zero included fails, since `Hom(1,0)=0`.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Definition A.1, p. 934; [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Section 1, pp. 97–100; Section 2, p. 114.

Use [Unipotent length](#nc-2-unipotent-length); [Neutral tensor category and Hopf reconstruction](#neutral-tensor-reconstruction).

<a id="nc-2-realization-categories"></a>

**Geometric unipotent categories.** For a smooth geometrically connected characteristic-zero curve `Y/k` with `b∈Y(k)`, define `C_dR(Y)` as the unipotent full subcategory of finite locally free `O_Y`-modules with integrable k-connection; morphisms are horizontal `O_Y`-linear maps. Its fibre `ω_b` is `b*E`. For a prime p and chosen geometric b, `C_et(Y_bar,ℚ_p)` is the unipotent full subcategory of finite-rank lisse `ℚ_p`-sheaves on `Y_bar`, with stalk fibre `ω_b`. In a smooth proper good-reduction compactification (𝒳,𝒟) over `W(F_q)`, with 𝒟 finite étale and `𝒴=𝒳−𝒟`, `C_rig(Y_0)` is the unipotent full subcategory of overconvergent isocrystals over `K_0=Frac W(F_q)`, with fibre `at b_bar`. Each category is neutral Tannakian, with finite-dimensional `Ext^1(1,1)`, identified with the corresponding `H^1`. Algebraic vector bundles, local systems and general isocrystals are imported objects; the new construction selects their unipotent categories and proves the fibre hypotheses.

Finite-rank objects; geometric connectedness makes endomorphisms of the unit equal to the coefficient field. For `C_rig`, a smooth good-reduction pair with finite étale boundary, possibly empty, and an integral endpoint. Only rational endpoints are constructed in this part; tame tangential endpoints need a separate logarithmic fibre construction.

Apply [Unipotent length](#nc-2-unipotent-length) in the three imported geometric categories. Prove subquotient closure by the invariant-vector filtration, and exact faithful evaluation using connectedness and horizontal/local-system uniqueness. Identify extensions of unit by unit with `H^1` using the connection Čech–de Rham cocycle, the local-system cocycle, or the rigid de Rham complex. For rigid `H^1`, apply RD.5 finiteness to the constant unit with its canonical Frobenius structure; this does not assume a Frobenius structure on every unipotent object. CLS Remark 2.3.4(iii) also proves finite cohomology of successive unit extensions by induction. Finiteness of algebraic de Rham `H¹` of a smooth curve and of its étale `H¹` (Stacks, Lemmas 59.69.1 and 59.69.3, at each finite level) is standard; neither RD.4 alone nor the restricted Coleman scalar `H^1` datum proves all three instances. Build tensor/dual/pullback and basepoint evaluation in each of the three realization categories; check symmetry and unit compatibility, rather than assuming an arbitrary tensor category is neutral.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `UnipotentRealizations.etale`: The full unipotent subcategory of the imported geometric rational local systems.
- `UnipotentRealizations.deRham`: The full unipotent subcategory of algebraic integrable connections.
- `UnipotentRealizations.rigid`: The full unipotent subcategory of imported overconvergent isocrystals.
- `UnipotentRealizations.fiber`: Exact faithful tensor evaluation at the specified endpoint.
- `UnipotentRealizations.pullback`: A morphism of pointed smooth curves induces the pullback tensor functor and compatible fibre identification; identity and composition agree.

**Checks.**

- `realization_unit`: In each realization the fibre of the tensor unit is the coefficient field.
- `realization_nontrivial_rank_one`: A rank-one representation with a nonidentity monodromy scalar has no unipotent filtration.
- `realization_extension`: A nonsplit geometric extension of the unit by itself belongs to `C_1`, while its fibre sequence is exact.
- The trivial connection and constant `ℚ_p`-sheaf lie in `C_0`.
- A rank-one local system with nontrivial monodromy is excluded.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Section 1, pp. 97–100; Section 2, pp. 114–116; [Bruno Chiarellotto and Bernard Le Stum](#reference-cls), Proposition 2.3.2 and Remark 2.3.4(iii), pp. 93–94; Proposition 2.4.1, pp. 95–97; [Amnon Besser](#reference-besser), Section 2, Proposition 2.13, pp. 6–7.

<a id="nc-2-tannakian-groups"></a>

**Unipotent fundamental group.** For each category in [Geometric unipotent categories](#nc-2-realization-categories), let `U_b` be the affine group scheme representing `R↦Aut^⊗(ω_b⊗R)` on all commutative coefficient algebras R, constructed by the imported neutral reconstruction. It is pro-unipotent, and `C≃Rep_fd(U_b)`. The étale realization is over `ℚ_p` and the de Rham realization over k. Pullback along `f:(Y,b)→(Z,c)` induces `U_b(Y)→U_c(Z)`; basepoint paths act by conjugation. Finite-dimensional tensor generators produce algebraic unipotent quotients, whose inverse limit is `U_b`. This specializes neutral reconstruction; it does not reconstruct a group from a Hopf algebra chosen in advance.

[Geometric unipotent categories](#nc-2-realization-categories) and the invariant-vector criterion.

Apply neutral tensor reconstruction to each established neutral category, and [Invariant vectors and unipotence](#nc-2-invariant-vector-criterion) to identify pro-unipotence. Construct morphisms by restriction of tensor automorphisms along pullback, checking all coefficient algebras and base change. Compare with the pinned fixed-Hopf comodule reconstruction when the category is presented as finite comodules; do not claim that result constructs the geometric Hopf algebra.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `UnipotentFundamentalGroup.points`: R-points are tensor automorphisms of the scalar-extended fibre functor, not arbitrary natural endomorphisms.
- `UnipotentFundamentalGroup.pullback`: Pointed pullback induces a group-scheme morphism, covariant in the pointed curve.
- `UnipotentFundamentalGroup.map_comp`: The group map for `g∘f` is the composition of the group maps.
- `UnipotentFundamentalGroup.fixedHopf`: For the finite-comodule presentation, the R-point equivalence is the pinned fgPointTensorIsoEquiv, with its convolution convention.

**Checks.**

- `group_trivial_category`: Every tensor automorphism of the usual fibre on finite-dimensional k-vector spaces is the identity.
- `group_fixed_hopf`: On FGComoduleCat the point group is the convolution group of k-algebra maps `H→R`.
- `group_unit_constraint`: A natural scalar multiplication by 2 on every fibre in characteristic zero is not a tensor automorphism, since its unit component is not identity.
- The trivial Tannakian category yields the trivial group over every coefficient algebra.
- For the algebraic de Rham category on `G_m` in characteristic zero, `U≅G_a`.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Section 1, pp. 97–100; Section 2, pp. 114–115; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Appendix A.1, pp. 934–935.

<a id="nc-2-tensor-paths"></a>

**Tensor paths.** For endpoints b,x define `P(b,x)(R)=Isom^⊗(ω_b⊗R,ω_x⊗R)`. Import representability and fpqc torsor descent from neutral tensor reconstruction: `P(b,x)` is an affine right `U_b`-torsor by `p·g=p∘g`, with commuting left `U_x`-action. Path composition is `(p_23,p_12)↦p_23∘p_12`; inversion reverses endpoints; `P(b,b)=U_b`. These are scheme statements over every coefficient algebra, rather than a classification of just rational points. A path identifies `U_b` and `U_x` by `g↦p g p^−1`.

Neutral categories and fibres of [Geometric unipotent categories](#nc-2-realization-categories).

Apply neutral reconstruction to identify the two fibres with fibre functors on finite comodules over the reconstructed Hopf algebra, then apply neutral tensor reconstruction tensor-isomorphism representability and its torsor theorem. The fixed-Hopf case is a consequence of this reduction, not a construction of the geometric category. Define actions, identity, inverse and composition in the category of tensor functors. Check the torsor isomorphism `P×U→P×P` after faithfully flat trivialization, then descend. Compare the point carrier directly with the category of bundled lax monoidal functors and its monoidal natural isomorphisms.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TensorPath.identity`: The identity tensor isomorphism is a path `b→b`.
- `TensorPath.rightMul`: For `p:b→x` and `g∈U_b`, first apply g and then p.
- `TensorPath.comp`: For `p:b→x` and `q:x→y`, compose to `q∘p`.
- `TensorPath.inverse`: The inverse path goes from x to b.
- `TensorPath.conjugate`: A path transports source tensor automorphisms to target tensor automorphisms.
- `TensorPath.ext`: Paths agree if all their fibre maps agree.

**Checks.**

- `path_identity_comp`: Composing the identity at either endpoint leaves a path unchanged.
- `path_right_action_free`: If `p·g=p` then `g=1`.
- `path_comp_order`: For vector-space fibre maps, the component of q after p is `q_E∘p_E`; a noncommuting pair detects the reversed convention.
- At equal endpoints composition is the tensor-automorphism multiplication, with the order specified.
- A natural transformation whose unit component is zero is excluded, even though it is a valid element of a finite path module.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Section 1, pp. 98–104; Section 2, pp. 114–116; [Amnon Besser](#reference-besser), Section 3, pp. 7–9; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Appendix A.1.2, pp. 936–937.

<a id="nc-2-etale-galois"></a>

**Galois structure and completion.** For `Y/k` and k-rational endpoints b,x, descent from `Y_bar` gives continuous semilinear `G_k`-actions on `U_et` and `P_et(b,x)`, compatible with all algebraic operations and finite-dimensional coordinate pieces. In profinite path coordinates the formula is `σ(p)=s_x(σ) p s_b(σ)^−1`. Restriction of finite-cover paths to unipotent lisse `ℚ_p`-sheaves yields the geometric pro-unipotent `ℚ_p` completion: every continuous unipotent finite-dimensional `ℚ_p` representation factors through its tensor category, and hence through an algebraic quotient of `U_et`. No surjectivity of profinite points onto all `U_et(ℚ_p)-points` is asserted.

Characteristic-zero base field, a separable closure and rational endpoints. Continuity means the usual p-adic topology on each finite-dimensional representation; not a discrete topology on `ℚ_p`.

Import the rational local-system/continuous-representation equivalence and Layer 1 arithmetic geometric paths. Pull back the geometric local systems by `σ` and use rational endpoint stalk identifications. Descent cocycles give the Galois actions and `σ(p·g)=σ(p)·σ(g)`. Apply neutral reconstruction to the unipotent representation subcategory. Finite objects supply finite-dimensional Galois-stable pieces; continuity follows from the imported continuous local systems.

**Checks.**

- For `b=x`, the identity path is Galois fixed and the action is by group automorphisms.
- The displayed action respects the right action, even when neither endpoint section becomes equal under a chosen ordinary path.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Section 2, pp. 114–116; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Section 2.1, pp. 896–898; Appendix A.1, pp. 934–937.

### 2.3 The two finite towers

<a id="nc-2-central-quotients"></a>

**Lower central depth.** For U in [Unipotent fundamental group](#nc-2-tannakian-groups), put `Γ_1U=U` and `Γ_(r+1)U` equal to the closed normal subgroup scheme generated by commutators of U with `Γ_rU`. Define `U⟨n⟩=U/Γ_(n+1)U` for `n≥0` as an fpqc quotient group scheme. It is finite type and unipotent for these curves, `U⟨0⟩=1`, and `U⟨1⟩` is the additive group on `H^1∨`. Quotienting a path torsor by `Γ_(n+1)` gives a right U⟨n⟩-torsor. The tower maps, path composition and realization structures descend. Kim writes `U_r=U/Z_r` with `Z_1=U`, so `U⟨n⟩` equals his `U_(n+1)`. LowerCentralSeries of the top subgroup starts at index zero; its index n matches `Γ_(n+1)` on abstract points only, and does not supply schematic quotient representability.

Characteristic zero; finite-dimensional `H^1`; pro-unipotent U from a curve. Use schematic closure and fpqc quotients; abstract quotients of rational points are not substituted.

Construct schematic lower central terms or equivalently use the closed lower central ideals in the pronilpotent Lie algebra via characteristic-zero unipotent group/Lie equivalence. The bracket gives a surjection from finite-dimensional tensor powers of `H^1∨` onto each successive Lie graded piece; induction gives finite-dimensional depth-n Lie algebra and a finite-type unipotent group. Descend the characteristic subgroup and torsor quotient along a trivializing faithfully flat cover. Verify indexing against the abstract lowerCentralSeries, retaining the representability boundary.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `UnipotentDepth.quotient`: The canonical fpqc group-scheme quotient map `U→U⟨n⟩`.
- `UnipotentDepth.transition`: For `m≤n` there is `U⟨n⟩→U⟨m⟩`, with identity and composition laws.
- `UnipotentDepth.pathQuotient`: Quotient `P(b,x)` by `Γ_(n+1)`, preserving its scheme torsor structure.
- `UnipotentDepth.nativeIndex`: On an abstract group, top.lowerCentralSeries n uses `Γ_(n+1)` indexing; no assertion equating an abstract point quotient with the scheme quotient.

**Checks.**

- `depth_zero`: The quotient by `Γ_1` is trivial.
- `depth_one_abelian`: For an abelian group `Γ_2` is trivial; the abstract depth-one quotient is the group itself.
- `depth_index`: `Γ_(n+1)` corresponds to lowerCentralSeries n, so the first commutator term is index one.
- For `G_a` the depth-one quotient is `G_a` and all higher central commutators vanish.
- A nonabelian two-step unipotent group has nontrivial depth-two commutators, whereas its depth-one quotient is abelian.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Section 1, pp. 100–104; Section 2, pp. 115–116; [Amnon Besser](#reference-besser), Theorem 3.6 and Lemma 3.7, pp. 9–11.

Use [Unipotent groups and their homogeneous quotients in characteristic zero](#split-unipotent-quotients); [Unipotent fundamental group](#nc-2-tannakian-groups); [Tensor paths](#nc-2-tensor-paths); `Subgroup.lowerCentralSeries`; [TauCetiRoadmap.ReductiveGroups](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups/README.md#layer-5-solvable-and-unipotent-groups-the-unipotent-radical).

<a id="nc-2-length-algebra"></a>

**Completed path algebra.** For a neutral unipotent C with finite-dimensional `Ext^1(1,1)`, let `A(C,ω)` be the completed enveloping/distribution algebra of `Lie(U_ω)`, with its augmentation ideal I. Put `A_n=A/I^(n+1)` and equip it with the finite filtration `I^i/I^(n+1)`. Each `A_n` is finite dimensional, `A_0=k`, and multiplication induces `A_n⊗A_n→A_n`. The complete coproduct is defined by primitive Lie elements; it gives length-compatible maps `A_(r+s)→A_r⊗A_s`. The coordinate Hopf algebra is the direct limit of `A_n∨`. `A_n` is not a Hopf quotient in general: for a primitive T, `Δ(T²)` contains `2T⊗T`. The C-object corresponding to the left regular `A_n`-module is written `𝒜_n(ω)`.

Neutral unipotent C, characteristic zero, finite-dimensional `Ext^1(1,1)`. `I^(n+1)` is a closed two-sided ideal in the complete algebra.

Use neutral tensor reconstruction and the characteristic-zero unipotent/Lie equivalence. Complete the enveloping algebra in augmentation powers; finite generation of the abelianized Lie algebra bounds each graded piece by a finite tensor power. Apply the finite-dimensional representation equivalence to the left regular `A_n`-module. Dualize the length-compatible coproduct and multiplication. Their compatible finite pieces construct the coordinate Hopf algebra and its direct-limit identification; do not equip an individual length quotient with a nonexistent Hopf quotient structure.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `UnipotentLengthAlgebra.augmentation`: The augmentation `A_n→k` sends the unit to one and I to zero.
- `UnipotentLengthAlgebra.transition`: The pointed surjective map `A_(n+1)→A_n`.
- `UnipotentLengthAlgebra.graded`: The i-th length grade is `I^i/I^(i+1)`, a quotient of `(Ext^1(1,1)∨)^⊗i`.
- `UnipotentLengthAlgebra.coordinate`: The direct limit of the linear duals `A_n∨` is the coordinate Hopf algebra, with products using length `r+s`.
- `UnipotentLengthAlgebra.regularObject`: The C-object `𝒜_n` whose fibre is the regular left `A_n`-module.

**Checks.**

- `length_algebra_zero`: `A_0` is k with its usual augmentation.
- `length_algebra_ga`: For `G_a`, `A_1` has basis 1,T and `T²=0`.
- `length_algebra_not_hopf`: In characteristic zero, the primitive coproduct does not factor through the quotient `k[T]/T²` as a coalgebra map to its tensor square.
- For `U=G_a`, `A_n=k[T]/(T^(n+1))`, while `O(U)=k[t]` is infinite dimensional.
- At `n=1`, `T²` is zero in `A_1` but its proposed coproduct is not zero in `A_1⊗A_1`.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Appendix A.1.1, pp. 934–935; [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Section 1, pp. 98–101; Section 2, pp. 115–116; [Amnon Besser](#reference-besser), Theorem 3.6, pp. 9–10.

<a id="nc-2-universal-pointed"></a>

**Universal pointed object.** A pointed object is (E,e) with `e∈ω(E)`. A universal pointed length-n object is a length-n E together with e such that, for every `V∈C_n`, evaluation `f↦ω(f)(e)` is a bijection `Hom_C(E,V)→ω(V)`. In particular each prescribed fibre vector determines exactly one morphism. Equivalently (E,e) is initial among pointed objects with that prescribed target vector. This property is stated in the full length subcategory; augmentation filtrations make the maps compatible with the usual unipotent filtration convention. A pointed pro-object is a compatible tower of such objects with transition maps preserving e.

Neutral unipotent category and fibre functor; finite length n.

Define the evaluation function and its bijectivity as the universal property. Apply it twice to obtain the unique pointed isomorphism between two universal objects. The two composites are identity by uniqueness. Use the property to construct unique pointed transition maps and their composition law.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `IsUniversalPointed.lift`: For a length-n V and `v∈ω(V)`, produce the unique map carrying e to v.
- `IsUniversalPointed.lift_eval`: Evaluation of lift(v) at e is v.
- `IsUniversalPointed.lift_unique`: Maps from E into a length-n object agree if their values at e agree.
- `IsUniversalPointed.pointedIso`: Two universal pointed objects have a unique pointed isomorphism.

**Checks.**

- `universal_unit`: On the trivial tensor category, (k,1) has the universal evaluation property.
- `universal_extra_summand`: For pointer (1,0) in `k²`, projection onto the first coordinate and the sum of the two coordinates both send the pointer to 1 and are distinct.
- `universal_eval_unique`: Two maps from a universal pointed object to a specified length-n target with equal pointer image must coincide.
- At length zero (1,1) represents the usual fibre on trivial objects.
`- (1⊕1,(1,0))` has existence of maps to all trivial pointed targets but does not have uniqueness.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Definition A.2 and Lemma A.3, p. 935; [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Section 1, pp. 98–100; Lemma 3, pp. 108–110.

Use [Unipotent length](#nc-2-unipotent-length); `ModuleCat.of`.

<a id="nc-2-universal-object-existence"></a>

**Existence of universal length objects.** The pair `(𝒜_n(ω),1)` obtained from [Completed path algebra](#nc-2-length-algebra) is universal pointed length n. Its pointed quotient maps to `𝒜_(n−1)` give a compatible universal pointed pro-object. The length-zero member is the unit, and its fibre algebra is `A_n`. Evaluation is k-linear as well as bijective.

Neutral unipotent C with finite-dimensional `Ext^1(1,1)`, characteristic zero.

Under Tannaka reconstruction, a length-n representation is annihilated by `I^(n+1)`; prove this by its trivial graded filtration and conversely use powers of I. An A-linear map `A_n→V` is determined by 1, and any v defines `a↦a·v`. Transport this elementary regular-module property through the representation equivalence. Quotient maps preserve the unit and define the inverse system. Uniqueness implies all transition diagrams commute.

**Checks.**

- For `G_a` and `n=1`, multiplication by T on `k[T]/T²` is the nontrivial two-dimensional regular representation.
- At length zero the regular object is the unit, and evaluation is the scalar Hom identification.
- The only map to the unit carrying 1 to 1 is the augmentation.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Lemma A.3 and its preceding construction, p. 935; [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Section 1, pp. 98–100; Section 2, pp. 115–116.

<a id="nc-2-finite-path-module"></a>

**Finite path module.** For fibres `ω,ν` on a neutral unipotent C, define `M_n(ω,ν)=Nat(ω|C_n,ν|C_n)`, with its k-vector-space structure from pointwise linear operations. Evaluation `α↦α_(𝒜_n(ω))(1)` is a canonical linear isomorphism `M_n(ω,ν)≅ν(𝒜_n(ω))`. In particular `M_n(ω,ω)≅A_n(ω)`, as an algebra with categorical composition; `M_n(ω,ν)` is a right `A_n(ω)-module`. Tensor paths act by postcomposition and identify this with the associated finite bundle `P(ω,ν)×^Uω A_n`. Composition `M_n(ν,λ)×M_n(ω,ν)→M_n(ω,λ)` is bilinear and associative. Duality gives the endpoint-reversed linear isomorphism, with reversal of composition. No invertibility or tensor constraint is required of an element of `M_n`.

The finite universal objects exist; `C_n` is the full length subcategory. All coefficient fibres are over the same field; geometric comparison first extends scalars when needed.

Apply [Existence of universal length objects](#nc-2-universal-object-existence) to each V,v to define the inverse to evaluation and prove its naturality using lift uniqueness. Use natural transformation composition for the algebra and right module structure. Reconstruct the associated finite bundle after a faithfully flat tensor path trivialization and descend it. Dualize components on `V∨` and use the double-dual tensor identification; this reverses endpoints and composition.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `FinitePathModule.eval`: Evaluate a natural transformation on the universal pointer.
- `FinitePathModule.evalEquiv`: Evaluation identifies `M_n(ω,ν)` linearly with `ν(𝒜_n(ω))`.
- `FinitePathModule.comp`: Bilinear composition, with q after p, is associative and unital at equal endpoints.
- `FinitePathModule.rightMul`: Precomposition by a source natural endomorphism gives the right `A_n`-module action.
- `FinitePathModule.reverseDual`: Duality reverses endpoint order and reverses the order in a composite.

**Checks.**

- `finite_path_zero`: The zero natural transformation is an element and evaluates to zero.
- `finite_path_comp_order`: On a constant vector-space fibre, comp(q,p) has component `q∘p`.
- `finite_path_not_tensor`: The zero natural transformation fails the tensor unit constraint, so the finite path module and tensor-path carrier are distinct.
- For the trivial category, `M_0=k`, whereas the tensor path scheme is a point.
- The zero natural transformation belongs to `M_n` but is not a tensor path.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Lemma A.4 and the composition paragraph, pp. 936–937; [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Section 1, pp. 98–101.

Use [Existence of universal length objects](#nc-2-universal-object-existence); [Tensor paths](#nc-2-tensor-paths); `CategoryTheory.NatTrans.appLinearMap`; [Neutral tensor category and Hopf reconstruction](#neutral-tensor-reconstruction).

### 2.4 The affine and proper universal objects and the Hodge filtration

<a id="nc-2-affine-universal"></a>

**Affine universal connection.** Let Y be a smooth geometrically connected affine curve over k of characteristic zero, with `b∈Y(k)`, and choose forms `ω_1,…,ω_m` whose classes are a basis of `H^1_dR(Y)`. Put `V=H^1_dR(Y)∨` with dual generators `T_i` and `W_≤n=⊕_(j=0)^n V^⊗j`. On `W_≤n⊗O_Y` define `∇(w⊗f)=w⊗df−Σ_i(T_iw)⊗fω_i`, with terms of degree `n+1` set to zero. The pointer at b is the empty word 1. Descending word-degree subbundles give trivial graded connections. This is an integrable algebraic connection: `Ω²_Y=0`. Its associative algebra is the truncated concatenation algebra on V. The imported Coleman word algebra has shuffle multiplication: take the coefficient-space coalgebra of words of length at most n, with deconcatenation, and dualize it to obtain this concatenation algebra. Do not take an algebra quotient of the shuffle algebra by words of length greater than n. The connection uses left-prepending; right multiplication by constant elements is horizontal.

Affine smooth curve, rational b, finite-dimensional `H^1` with a represented basis. If the compactification has genus g and d geometric boundary points, d&gt;0, then `m=2g+d−1`.

Import the Coleman word basis and deconcatenation coalgebra on the coefficient spaces. The length-at-most-n coefficient subspace is a finite subcoalgebra; its linear dual has truncated concatenation multiplication on the dual generators V. Tensor this algebra with `O_Y` using AlgebraicVectorBundles. Shuffle multiplication is the coordinate product, not the multiplication of the universal module. Define the connection by the displayed Leibniz rule. Word-degree proves unipotence and finite rank, and curve dimension proves integrability. Right multiplication commutes with left-prepending, hence is horizontal; do not claim left multiplication is horizontal for arbitrary noncentral words.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `AffineUniversalConnection.empty`: The empty-word section and its pointer at b.
- `AffineUniversalConnection.nabla`: The connection is `d−Σ_i L_(T_i)ω_i` with degree overflow zero.
- `AffineUniversalConnection.truncate`: Word truncation gives horizontal pointed maps between lengths.
- `AffineUniversalConnection.rightMul`: Right multiplication by a constant word element is horizontal.
- `AffineUniversalConnection.rank`: Its rank is `Σ_(j=0)^n m^j`, with `0^0=1`.

**Checks.**

- `affine_length_zero`: At length zero, every prepend operator vanishes and the connection is the ordinary derivation.
- `affine_one_generator`: In length one for one generator, prepend sends empty word to T and T to zero.
- `affine_order_noncommuting`: With two generators and length two, ∇ applied to `T_2` contains `−T_1T_2ω_1`, rather than `−T_2T_1ω_1`.
- At `n=0` this is `(O_Y,d)`.
- For `Y=G_m` with ω=dt/t and `n=1`, ∇1=−T·dt/t and `∇T=0`.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Section 4.2, equation (21), p. 910; [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Lemma 2, pp. 107–108; Lemma 3, pp. 108–110.

Use [Geometric unipotent categories](#nc-2-realization-categories); [Word algebra and shuffle coordinates](#word-algebra-shuffle); [SchemeAndStackFoundations](../SchemeAndStackFoundations/README.md) Layer SF.0 (schemes and morphisms); `Derivation`.

<a id="nc-2-affine-universality"></a>

**Kim’s affine universal property.** The affine connection in [Affine universal connection](#nc-2-affine-universal), pointed by the empty word at b, is isomorphic as a pointed connection to `𝒜_n(C_dR(Y),ω_b)`. For every length-n unipotent connection E and every vector `v∈b*E`, there is exactly one horizontal morphism f with `f_b(1)=v`. The vector is in the fibre, not an arbitrary global section. Changing the cohomology basis yields the uniquely pointed universal isomorphism, with the nonlinear gauge correction when representatives differ by exact forms.

Hypotheses of [Affine universal connection](#nc-2-affine-universal).

Use the affine normal form: unipotent bundles are split as `O_Y`-modules, and gauge changes remove exact parts of connection matrices using affine `H^1` representatives. Use Kim’s universal word connection and its holonomy/word independence argument to identify the completed algebra; at finite length the regular-module evaluation property gives existence and uniqueness. Apply [Universal pointed object](#nc-2-universal-pointed) uniqueness to basis changes. The gauge correction is required; an arbitrary basis change alone cannot handle exact differences.

**Checks.**

- For E=unit and `v=a`, the unique map is a times augmentation.
- On `G_m` a nonconstant global function is not the image of 1 under a horizontal map from the length-zero unit connection.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Lemmas 2–3, pp. 107–110; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Theorem 4.2, p. 910.

Use [Affine universal connection](#nc-2-affine-universal); [Existence of universal length objects](#nc-2-universal-object-existence); [Universal pointed object](#nc-2-universal-pointed); [SchemeAndStackFoundations](../SchemeAndStackFoundations/README.md) Layer SF.2 (sites and scheme cohomology); [Word algebra and shuffle coordinates](#word-algebra-shuffle).

<a id="nc-2-affine-composition"></a>

**Composition in affine word coordinates.** The affine trivialization `s_0(b,x):W_≤n→M_n(b,x)` induced by the universal connection satisfies `comp(s_0(x_2,x_3)(f_2),s_0(x_1,x_2)(f_1))=s_0(x_1,x_3)(f_2 f_1)`. Multiplication is truncated concatenation in the displayed order. For equal endpoints it is an algebra isomorphism. The associated action of a source algebra element is right multiplication in these coordinates.

One affine curve, one chosen cohomology basis, and endpoints in `Y(k)`.

Right multiplication by `f_1` defines a horizontal endomorphism of the universal connection. Evaluate at its pointer and apply the unique pointed-map property. The resulting natural transformation realizes `f_1` in [Finite path module](#nc-2-finite-path-module). Compose the natural transformations and evaluate; right multiplication gives `f_2 f_1`, fixing the convention without commuting the words.

**Checks.**

- With two generators and `n=2`, composing coordinate `T_1` then `T_2` gives `T_2T_1`, distinct from `T_1T_2`.
- The empty word is the identity endomorphism.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Lemma 4.3, equations (22)–(24), p. 911.

Use [Finite path module](#nc-2-finite-path-module); [Kim’s affine universal property](#nc-2-affine-universality).

<a id="nc-2-proper-maximal-quotient"></a>

**Proper extendable quotient.** Let X be a smooth proper geometrically connected characteristic-zero curve and `j:Y↪X` a nonempty affine open containing b. Restriction `C_dR(X)→C_dR(Y)` is fully faithful. The canonical pointed map `𝒜_n(Y)→j*𝒜_n(X)` is surjective, and its target is the maximal length-n pointed quotient extending to an integrable connection on all of X with no logarithmic poles. Every horizontal map from `𝒜_n(Y)` to a restricted length-n connection from X factors uniquely through it. The proper length graded pieces are quotients of `V_X^⊗i`, not free tensor powers in general.

Smooth proper X, rational basepoint in nonempty affine Y, characteristic zero.

Prove restriction full faithfulness in characteristic zero on the horizontal Hom connection: a rational horizontal section with a pole of maximal order r&gt;0 has derivative of order `r+1`, while a regular connection matrix contributes at most order r. The leading pole coefficient cannot cancel, so the section extends across each removed smooth point. Apply this to Hom of two regular connections. Before using the image, extend any subconnection of a restricted regular connection: across a removed smooth point, saturate its generic subspace inside the regular bundle over the local DVR. The intersection is stable under the connection because both the generic subspace and the ambient regular bundle are stable; saturation makes the submodule and quotient locally free on a curve. It is unipotent by subquotient closure. The image of the universal map thus extends to X and contains the pointer. Universal pointed evaluation on X supplies its retraction from `𝒜_n(X)`; uniqueness makes the composite the identity, forcing surjectivity. For each extendable target, universal pointed evaluation on X gives the unique factorization. Extendable quotients are exactly the ones with zero residues in their canonical logarithmic extension.

**Checks.**

- For `X=P¹`, `𝒜_n(X)` is the unit for all n, even though puncturing creates nontrivial universal word generators.
- For a positive-genus proper curve the degree-two cup-product relation prevents the proper algebra from being the free tensor algebra.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Corollary 4.4 and its proof, pp. 911–912; [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Section 1, p. 111; [Amnon Besser](#reference-besser), Lemma 2.14, Corollary 2.15 and Proposition 2.16, p. 7; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan and Netan Dogra](#reference-bdii), Lemma 6.7, §6.5.1, p. 33 of the author manuscript.

Use [Kim’s affine universal property](#nc-2-affine-universality); [Existence of universal length objects](#nc-2-universal-object-existence); [SchemeAndStackFoundations](../SchemeAndStackFoundations/README.md) Layer SF.2 (sites and scheme cohomology).

<a id="nc-2-filtered-path"></a>

**Hodge filtered path fibres.** A filtered unipotent connection is an integrable connection E with a finite, exhaustive, separated descending filtration `F^iE` by subbundles, satisfying `∇F^iE⊆F^(i−1)E⊗Ω¹` (or `Ω¹(log D)` on the canonical extension of an open curve). For `𝒜_n(b)`, filter its constant kernel `I^n/I^(n+1)` by the quotient filtration from `V_dR^⊗n`, where `V_dR=H^1_dR∨` has the dual Hodge filtration. The Hodge filtered path fibre at x is `x*𝒜_n(b)` with the resulting filtration. On the dual coordinate ring this induces the multiplicative filtration and `F^0` path subtorsor. The existence and uniqueness of the geometric filtration are the theorem [Hadian’s universal Hodge filtration](#nc-2-hadian-filtration), not fields assumed in this definition.

Smooth proper curve or the canonical logarithmic extension to its smooth proper compactification. Dual filtration convention: `F^i(V∨)` annihilates `F^(1−i)V`. General filtered modules and Hodge filtrations are imported from p-adic Hodge theory.

Specify the filtration and transversality on the imported connection; the subbundle condition makes fibre restriction exact. Use the augmentation length grades and the quotient of the tensor Hodge filtration for the universal kernels. Restrict the filtered bundles at endpoints; dualize to filtered coordinate objects and check tensor/coalgebra compatibility using the universal construction.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `FilteredPathFiber.filtration`: For each integer i the subspace `F^i` in the endpoint fibre.
- `FilteredPathFiber.graded`: The associated length grade has the quotient tensor Hodge filtration.
- `FilteredPathFiber.unit`: The universal pointer at b lies in `F^0`.
- `FilteredPathFiber.dual`: Dualization uses annihilators of `F^(1−i)`, and comparison maps are strict filtered maps.
- `FilteredPathFiber.truncate`: Length transition maps preserve the Hodge filtration.

**Checks.**

- `filtered_unit`: The filtered unit is k for `i≤0` and zero for i&gt;0.
- `filtered_dual_index`: For a one-dimensional space with its only graded piece in degree one, its dual has its only graded piece in degree minus one.
- `filtered_augmentation_quotient`: A filtered quotient of a finite path fibre carries the image filtration, rather than an arbitrary splitting filtration.
- At length zero the unit filtration is k in degrees `i≤0` and zero for i&gt;0.
- Frobenius is not required to preserve the Hodge filtration.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Section 4.3 and Theorem 4.5, pp. 912–913; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan and Netan Dogra](#reference-bdii), Definition 6.2 and Proposition 6.1, p. 30; Remarks 4–5, p. 31 of the author manuscript; [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Section 1, pp. 103–104.

Use [Geometric unipotent categories](#nc-2-realization-categories); [Completed path algebra](#nc-2-length-algebra); [Finite path module](#nc-2-finite-path-module); [De Rham exactness and Hodge–Tate grading](#linear-period-exactness); [SchemeAndStackFoundations](../SchemeAndStackFoundations/README.md) Layer SF.0 (schemes and morphisms).

<a id="nc-2-filtered-extension"></a>

**Filtered extension classification.** For filtered integrable connections E,F on a smooth proper curve X, with logarithmic poles along a reduced divisor D when present, extensions that are strict on filtered bundles are classified by `H¹` of the two-term complex `F^0 Hom(E,F)→F^(−1) Hom(E,F)⊗Ω¹_X(log D)`. The differential is the induced Hom connection. Forgetting the filtration is induced by inclusion into the full logarithmic de Rham complex. This is a classification of extension classes; uniqueness of a class does not by itself imply equality of filtrations on a fixed underlying bundle.

Finite exhaustive separated subbundle filtrations and Griffiths transversality. Proper X and logarithmic canonical extensions if D is nonempty.

Choose local filtered splittings, which exist for strict extensions of vector bundles. Their differences form a Čech 1-cochain in `F^0 Hom`; connection off-diagonal terms form a 0-cochain in `Ω¹(log D)⊗F^(−1) Hom`. The cocycle and horizontality equations are precisely the total degree-one hypercohomology cocycle condition. Changes of filtered splitting give coboundaries. Reconstruct the extension from such a cocycle and check the inverse construction; the forgetful map is the inclusion of complexes.

**Checks.**

- For D empty and E=F=unit with trivial filtration, the displayed filtered complex has `O_X→Ω¹_X`, the usual de Rham extension complex.
- Changing a filtered splitting changes the cocycle by a coboundary.

The construction and its conventions follow [Majid Hadian](#reference-hadian), Thesis §2.2, Proposition 2.2.3 and proof, p. 29; Lemma 2.2.1, p. 27; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan and Netan Dogra](#reference-bdii), Proposition 6.1, p. 30; Remark 5, p. 31 of the author manuscript.

Use [Hodge filtered path fibres](#nc-2-filtered-path); [SchemeAndStackFoundations](../SchemeAndStackFoundations/README.md) Layer SF.2 (sites and scheme cohomology).

<a id="nc-2-hadian-filtration"></a>

**Hadian’s universal Hodge filtration.** For a pointed smooth proper curve `X/k` in characteristic zero, the universal connection `𝒜_n(b)` has a unique Hodge filtration by subbundles, rigidified at b, such that Griffiths transversality holds, the sequence `V_dR^⊗n⊗O_X→𝒜_n(b)→𝒜_(n−1)(b)→0` induces the specified quotient tensor filtration on the kernel and the inductively specified filtration on the quotient, and `1_b∈F^0`. Start with the unit filtration `at n=0`. Equivalently construct the canonical logarithmic universal connection on a nonempty affine `Y⊂X`, rigidify it by the pointer, and pass to the maximal no-pole quotient. Filtered quotients inherit the image filtration. The affine bundle without its compactification does not satisfy a uniqueness theorem.

Smooth proper X, characteristic zero, rational b; `n≥1`. On an auxiliary affine open use its canonical logarithmic extension to X, including nilpotent residues; impose the basepoint pointer normalization.

Use [Filtered extension classification](#nc-2-filtered-extension) to lift the underlying universal extension class with the prescribed graded filtration. Hadian’s filtered Ext calculation gives the lift and uniqueness of its class on the proper compactification. Rigidify the filtered universal extension at the pointed fibre. A pointed connection automorphism is identity by [Universal pointed object](#nc-2-universal-pointed), turning the isomorphism-class result into uniqueness for the normalized universal object. For proper X use [Proper extendable quotient](#nc-2-proper-maximal-quotient) and the filtered quotient construction. The kernel is a quotient of the tensor grade; it is not assumed to be the entire tensor power.

**Checks.**

- For `n=0`, the pointer 1 lies in the usual `F^0` of the unit.
- At `n=1` for genus g proper X, the `V_dR` part has filtration `F^0=ann H^0(X,Ω¹)`, of dimension g.
- The same uniqueness assertion on an affine bundle alone is excluded.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Theorem 4.5 and Remark 4.6, pp. 912–913; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan and Netan Dogra](#reference-bdii), Lemma 6.4, Remarks 4–5 and Corollary 6.2, pp. 30–31 of the author manuscript; [Majid Hadian](#reference-hadian), Thesis §2.2, Proposition 2.2.7 and Remark 2.2.8, pp. 31–32.

Use [Hodge filtered path fibres](#nc-2-filtered-path); [Filtered extension classification](#nc-2-filtered-extension); [Universal pointed object](#nc-2-universal-pointed); [Proper extendable quotient](#nc-2-proper-maximal-quotient).

### 2.5 Frobenius, horizontal transport and the crystalline comparison

<a id="nc-2-rigid-fibre"></a>

**Residue-disc fibre.** For a unipotent overconvergent isocrystal E and a rational special-fibre point z, define `ω_z(E)` as the horizontal sections of E on the residue disc ]z[. For any lift `x∈]z[(K_0)`, evaluation is a canonical tensor-natural isomorphism `ω_z(E)≅E_x`. For x,y in the same disc, define `T_(x→y)=ev_y∘ev_x^−1`. It composes, is horizontal, respects tensor products and the unit, and is independent of any chosen coordinate on the disc. These are local fibre identifications; they do not identify different discs until [Canonical Frobenius path](#nc-2-canonical-frobenius-path) is proved.

Smooth good-reduction curve and unipotent overconvergent connection. Endpoints rational over `K_0`; otherwise extend the unramified coefficient field first.

Import the isocrystal evaluation at a point from RD.3 and represent it on the residue disc by horizontal sections. Use the unipotent filtration and recursively solve the connection using local primitives on the disc; uniqueness with a prescribed value proves evaluation is an isomorphism. Tensor naturality and composition follow from uniqueness, not from a choice of basis.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `RigidHorizontalFiber.horizontal`: The kernel of the connection on disc sections, as a coefficient-field vector space.
- `RigidHorizontalFiber.eval`: Evaluation at a lift is a tensor-natural linear isomorphism.
- `RigidHorizontalFiber.transport`: Transport from x to y is evaluation at y after inverse evaluation at x.
- `RigidHorizontalFiber.transport_comp`: `T_(y→z)∘T_(x→y)=T_(x→z)`.
- `RigidHorizontalFiber.tensor`: Evaluation and transport commute with the tensor structure and send the unit to one.

**Checks.**

- `rigid_unit`: Horizontal sections of the trivial rank-one connection are the coefficient constants.
- `rigid_same_endpoint`: Transport from x to itself is identity.
- `rigid_nilpotent_transport`: For a constant nilpotent matrix N with `N²=0` in d−Ndt, transport is `1+(y−x)N` and therefore has the positive sign.
- For the trivial connection the horizontal sections are the constants and every evaluation is identity.
- For d−Ndt on a disc with `N²=0`, transport `x→y` is `1+(y−x)N`.

The construction and its conventions follow [Amnon Besser](#reference-besser), Section 2, equations (2.4)–(2.7), p. 6; [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Section 1, p. 102; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Theorem 5.3 and §5.2, p. 920.

Use [Geometric unipotent categories](#nc-2-realization-categories); [PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology](../PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology/README.md) layer RD.3 (overconvergent stratifications and connections).

<a id="nc-2-rigid-frobenius-equivalence"></a>

**Frobenius pullback equivalence.** On the unipotent isocrystal category of a smooth curve over `F_q` with the stated good-reduction compactification, pullback by the q-power Frobenius is a `K_0`-linear tensor autoequivalence. For p-power Frobenius before iteration it is σ-semilinear. Unit and endpoint fibre identifications give actions on tensor paths and all finite universal path modules. Frobenius preserves the length filtration; preservation of the Hodge filtration is not part of the statement.

Smooth special fibre descending to `F_q`; `K_0=Frac W(F_q)`. Use the overconvergent unipotent category, not arbitrary F-isocrystals defined by choosing a matrix.

Use CLS Proposition 2.4.2. Its induction on unipotent length reduces full faithfulness to `H^0` and essential surjectivity of extensions to `H^1`, on which Frobenius is invertible. Pullback is tensor and preserves the unit; q-power iteration removes coefficient semilinearity over `K_0`. Transport its functor and fibre identifications through [Tensor paths](#nc-2-tensor-paths) and [Finite path module](#nc-2-finite-path-module).

**Checks.**

- Frobenius pullback of the unit is the unit.
- A p-power map over `W(F_q)[1/p]` is semilinear unless its coefficient Frobenius has been iterated q times appropriately.

The construction and its conventions follow [Bruno Chiarellotto and Bernard Le Stum](#reference-cls), Proposition 2.4.2 and proof, pp. 96–97; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Section 5.1, pp. 918–919.

Use [Geometric unipotent categories](#nc-2-realization-categories); [Residue-disc fibre](#nc-2-rigid-fibre); [Tensor paths](#nc-2-tensor-paths); [Finite path module](#nc-2-finite-path-module); [PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology](../PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology/README.md) layer RD.4 (rigid cohomology).

<a id="nc-2-frobenius-normalization"></a>

**Normalized universal Frobenius.** At a Frobenius-fixed special endpoint `b_0`, pullback of the universal pointed isocrystal `(𝒜_n(b_0),1)` is universal. There is exactly one pointed horizontal isomorphism `Φ_n:F*𝒜_n(b_0)≅𝒜_n(b_0)` carrying the identified base fibre pointer to 1. It commutes with length transition maps, yields the identity on `A_0`, and on the graded pieces induces the quotient of the tensor powers of Frobenius on `H^1_rig∨`. At other lifts of the same endpoint use [Residue-disc fibre](#nc-2-rigid-fibre) transport to express this normalization.

Good-reduction hypotheses and a q-power Frobenius fixing the special endpoint. The comparison of the base fibres is specified; an unnormalized horizontal isomorphism is not canonical.

Apply the tensor autoequivalence to the universal pointed evaluation property; the endpoint identification preserves its pointer. Use the unique pointed isomorphism of [Universal pointed object](#nc-2-universal-pointed). Uniqueness forces compatibility with all transitions. On the augmentation generators the map is the `H^1-dual` Frobenius; multiplicativity and quotient compatibility give its action on tensor graded pieces.

**Checks.**

- At length zero `Φ_0` sends 1 to 1 and is identity.
- Multiplying a universal Frobenius map by a nonidentity source automorphism changes the pointer normalization and is excluded.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Lemma 5.2, equations (37)–(38), p. 919.

Use [Frobenius pullback equivalence](#nc-2-rigid-frobenius-equivalence); [Existence of universal length objects](#nc-2-universal-object-existence); [Universal pointed object](#nc-2-universal-pointed); [Completed path algebra](#nc-2-length-algebra).

<a id="nc-2-berthelot-ogus"></a>

**Nonabelian Berthelot–Ogus comparison.** For a smooth proper pair (𝒳,𝒟) over `W(F_q)`, with 𝒟 finite étale, and `Y=𝒳_K0−𝒟_K0`, analytification is a `K_0`-linear tensor equivalence `C_dR(Y)≃C_rig(Y_0)`. For an integral lift x of a special endpoint, its fibre comparison `ι_x` is [Residue-disc fibre](#nc-2-rigid-fibre) evaluation. Hence the groups, tensor path schemes, universal objects and finite path modules compare canonically, with coefficient extension if needed. For x,y in one residue disc, the induced de Rham path is local parallel transport. For 𝒟 empty this applies to the proper curve; the affine free-word computation is not applied to the proper curve without taking its quotient.

Smooth proper compactification over the unramified DVR with smooth finite étale boundary, possibly empty. Only unipotent connections/isocrystals.

Apply CLS Proposition 2.4.1. Use its induction on length, identifying Hom with horizontal `H^0` and extension classes with `H^1` via algebraic/rigid linear comparison. Compare endpoint fibres by [Residue-disc fibre](#nc-2-rigid-fibre) evaluation; use neutral reconstruction and tensor-isomorphism representability to pass to groups and schemes. Universal pointed uniqueness gives finite-object comparison and compatibility with path composition and all length transitions.

**Checks.**

- The comparison sends the unit to the unit and the universal pointer to the universal pointer.
- On a single residue disc its endpoint comparison is exactly `T_(x→y)`, not a new arbitrary path choice.

The construction and its conventions follow [Bruno Chiarellotto and Bernard Le Stum](#reference-cls), Proposition 2.4.1 and proof, pp. 95–97; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J.
