<a id="nc-2-path-frobenius"></a>

**Frobenius on de Rham paths.** Use [Nonabelian Berthelot–Ogus comparison](#nc-2-berthelot-ogus) and the endpoint fibre comparisons to transport rigid q-Frobenius to `P_dR(b,x)` and to `M_n^dR(b,x)`. If `b_0,x_0` are Frobenius-fixed lifts in the same respective discs, put `τ(g)=T_(x_0→x)∘g∘T_(b→b_0)`. Then `φ_n(b,x)=τ∘φ_n(b_0,x_0)∘τ^−1`. At the fixed lifts, `φ_n(b_0,x_0)` is the fibre of `Φ_n` under the universal evaluation isomorphism. The operators preserve length, commute with composition and the source action, and retain their coefficient semilinearity before q-iteration. They need not preserve Hodge filtration.

Good-reduction pair, integral rational endpoints in the good open, and specified Frobenius-fixed lifts when this coordinate formula is used.

Define the action through the rigid tensor functor and endpoint identifications, then transfer it through [Nonabelian Berthelot–Ogus comparison](#nc-2-berthelot-ogus). Use [Normalized universal Frobenius](#nc-2-frobenius-normalization) and [Finite path module](#nc-2-finite-path-module) evaluation to identify the fixed-lift operator. Change lifts by [Residue-disc fibre](#nc-2-rigid-fibre) transport; naturality gives the conjugation formula and its compatibility with length/composition.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `PathFrobenius.fixedLift`: The fixed-lift finite path operator obtained from `Φ_n`.
- `PathFrobenius.transport`: Transport the fixed-lift operator by `τ`.
- `PathFrobenius.changeLift`: Changing a disc lift conjugates the path operator by the corresponding two-sided transport.
- `PathFrobenius.comp`: Frobenius of a composable pair is the composition of their Frobenius images.
- `PathFrobenius.truncate`: The Frobenius operators commute with length transitions.

**Checks.**

- `frobenius_fixed_lifts`: Identity transport leaves the fixed-lift operator unchanged.
- `frobenius_two_sided`: For linear maps represented by source A and target B, `τ(g)=B∘g∘A` and the transported operator is `τφτ^−1`.
- `frobenius_conjugation_fixed`: If `φ(g)=g`, then `τφτ^−1` fixes `τ(g)`; reversing one endpoint transport generally fails this equality.
- At fixed lifts the conjugating transport is identity.
- Changing both endpoints gives two-sided transport in the specified order.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Section 5.2, equation (42), pp. 920–921; [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Section 1, pp. 102–104.

<a id="nc-2-frobenius-lang"></a>

**Unipotent Frobenius Lang theorem.** Let U be a pro-unipotent rigid fundamental group of a smooth `F_q` curve in the stated good-reduction pair. Its q-Frobenius `φ` has no eigenvalue one on any positive augmentation/Lie graded piece: `H^1_rig∨` has weights −1 (proper) or −1 and −2 (open), and the grades are tensor-power quotients. The Lang map `L_φ:U→U`, `g↦g^−1φ(g)`, is an isomorphism of affine schemes, compatible with finite lower central quotients and scalar extension. This is not asserted to be a group homomorphism. More generally the same proof applies when `φ−1` is invertible on every finite Lie graded piece.

Good-reduction smooth curve over a finite field and its geometric unipotent group; characteristic-zero coefficients. Weight/no-eigenvalue-one hypothesis at every positive grade; a single `H^1` eigenvalue statement without its tensor-grade consequence is insufficient.

Import the rigid `H^1` weights. Length-algebra bounds positive grades by tensor powers of `H^1∨`, so all eigenvalues have strictly negative weights and none is one. Solve `g^−1φ(g)=h` successively in the complete augmentation algebra, where the next correction is determined by the invertible linear map `φ−1` on the next grade. Use the coproduct and uniqueness of this solution to show it is group-like. The construction is functorial over coefficient algebras, giving a scheme inverse rather than just a pointwise bijection.

**Checks.**

- For `U=G_a` and `φ=a·id` with `a≠1`, Lang is multiplication by a−1.
- For `U=G_a` and `φ=id`, Lang is zero and is not invertible, so the weight hypothesis cannot be dropped.

The construction and its conventions follow [Amnon Besser](#reference-besser), Theorem 3.1, Theorem 3.6 and Proposition 3.8, pp. 7–12.

<a id="nc-2-canonical-frobenius-path"></a>

**Canonical Frobenius path.** For any two endpoint fibres of the good-reduction unipotent rigid category, the Frobenius action on their tensor path torsor has a unique fixed point `p_φ(b,x)`, rational over the coefficient field. The paths satisfy `p_φ(x,y)∘p_φ(b,x)=p_φ(b,y)`, `p_φ(b,b)=1`, and are natural under pointed curve maps. They are unchanged after replacing a common Frobenius by a positive power. Through [Nonabelian Berthelot–Ogus comparison](#nc-2-berthelot-ogus) they supply tensor-natural horizontal transport between distinct residue discs, agreeing with [Residue-disc fibre](#nc-2-rigid-fibre) transport inside a disc. These canonical paths do not require a choice of logarithm or a Hodge-filtration-preserving Frobenius.

Good-reduction pair and the Frobenius Lang hypothesis; endpoints defined over the coefficient field after a common finite extension if needed.

Trivialize the torsor over a field extension and write `φ(p)=p·h`. Solving the resulting twisted Lang equation gives a unique fixed path by [Unipotent Frobenius Lang theorem](#nc-2-frobenius-lang). Uniqueness makes the fixed path invariant under descent automorphisms, so it descends to the coefficient field. Identity, composition, pullback, Frobenius power independence and local agreement follow because both sides are fixed tensor paths and the fixed path is unique.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `CanonicalFrobeniusPath.fixed`: The canonical path is fixed by the specified Frobenius.
- `CanonicalFrobeniusPath.unique`: Any Frobenius-fixed tensor path equals the canonical path.
- `CanonicalFrobeniusPath.comp`: Canonical paths compose with endpoint order `b→x→y`.
- `CanonicalFrobeniusPath.sameDisc`: Within one residue disc, canonical transport is the local horizontal transport.
- `CanonicalFrobeniusPath.power`: A common positive Frobenius power gives the same canonical path.

**Checks.**

- `canonical_equal_endpoint`: The fixed path at equal endpoints is identity.
- `canonical_additive`: For `φ(z)=2z+c` on an additive torsor in characteristic zero, the unique fixed point is −c.
- `canonical_identity_fails`: Identity Frobenius on the additive line has more than one fixed point and does not meet the unique-fixed-path hypotheses.
- At equal endpoints the canonical fixed point is the identity.
- For an additive torsor with φ(z)=az+c and `a≠1`, the fixed point is `c/(1−a)`.

The construction and its conventions follow [Amnon Besser](#reference-besser), Corollaries 3.2–3.3 and Proposition 3.4, pp. 8–9; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Section 5.2.1, equations (39)–(41), p. 921.

Use [Unipotent Frobenius Lang theorem](#nc-2-frobenius-lang); [Tensor paths](#nc-2-tensor-paths); [Nonabelian Berthelot–Ogus comparison](#nc-2-berthelot-ogus); [Residue-disc fibre](#nc-2-rigid-fibre).

<a id="nc-2-word-path-bridge"></a>

**Word coordinates and global transport.** In the affine universal connection and its proper extendable quotient, the tensor path `p_φ(a,c)` corresponds under [Finite path module](#nc-2-finite-path-module) and affine trivialization to the truncated word element `I(a,c)=1+Σ_(0<|w|≤n)(∫_a^c w)w`, with the outermost integral matching left-prepending. For endpoints in one residue disc the coefficients are the local iterated integrals defined by horizontal recursion and the initial value. For cross-disc endpoints define them by the canonical Frobenius tensor path. Section 5.0 identifies them with Coleman functions. Consequently the two-sided transport of a finite path module is `v↦I(x_0,x) v I(b,b_0)`. This map intertwines the endpoint Frobenius operators. The local coefficient formula and the global Frobenius identification are separate dependencies.

Good-reduction compactification, affine open, chosen `H^1` forms and consistent word convention. Frobenius-normalized transport is the canonical tensor path; its word coefficients define the functions whose analytic algebra and uniqueness are constructed in Layer 5.

Identify a horizontal solution of [Affine universal connection](#nc-2-affine-universal) with its coefficient recursion; local word expansions satisfy the recursion and initial value, so agree on each disc. For cross-disc endpoints define the word coefficients by [Canonical Frobenius path](#nc-2-canonical-frobenius-path) and prove their transport identities algebraically. Section 5.0 identifies these coefficients with Coleman functions using its algebra and uniqueness theorem. Apply [Composition in affine word coordinates](#nc-2-affine-composition) to the two endpoint transports to obtain the ordered word product, and pass to the proper quotient if appropriate.

**Checks.**

`- I(a,a)=1` and `I(c,d)I(a,c)=I(a,d)`, including cross-disc endpoints under the global hypothesis.
- At one generator and length one, transport is `1+(∫_a^cω)T`.
- At a noncommutative length-two word the order distinguishes `I(x_0,x)vI(b,b_0)` from a formula with reversed factors.

### 2.6 Pointed crystalline comparison

<a id="olsson-unipotent-comparison"></a>

**Olsson's nonabelian crystalline comparison in the unipotent case.** Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, `V=W(k)`, K=Frac V, 𝒳 smooth and proper over V and `𝒟⊂𝒳` a divisor with normal crossings relative to V, with `𝒳°=𝒳∖𝒟`. Let `C_et` be the category of unipotent smooth `ℚ_p`-sheaves on `𝒳°_K̄` and `C_dR` the category of unipotent modules with integrable connection on `𝒳°_K` with logarithmic poles along 𝒟 and nilpotent residues, with its Frobenius structure from the log-crystalline realization. For integral points `x,y∈𝒳°(V)`, let `P^et_(x,y)=Isom^⊗(ω^et_x,ω^et_y)` and `P^dR_(x,y)=Isom^⊗(ω^dR_x,ω^dR_y)`. Then: (i) there is an isomorphism of Hopf algebras `O(π₁(C_dR,x))⊗_K B_cris≅O(π₁(C_et,x̄))⊗_(ℚ_p) B_cris` compatible with Frobenius and the Galois action; (ii) the Galois representation `O(P^et_(x,y))` is ind-crystalline, and `D_cris(O(P^et_(x,y)))` is canonically isomorphic to `O(P^dR_(x,y))` with its Frobenius, compatibly with the torsor structures under the groups of (i) and with composition of paths; (iii) `Lie(π₁(C_et,x̄))` is a pro-object of crystalline representations with `D_cris` equal to `Lie(π₁(C_dR,x))`; (iv) for a point b of 𝒟(V) at which the log structure satisfies Olsson's Assumption 9.2 (true after an étale extension of V), the same comparison holds at the tangential base point at b, and it is compatible with the local monodromy group at b.

k perfect of characteristic p; `V=W(k)` unramified; `𝒳/V` smooth proper; 𝒟 a relative normal-crossings divisor; `x,y∈𝒳°(V)` integral points, or a boundary point b as in (iv). In the unipotent case the reductivity Assumption 1.6 holds trivially (the reductive quotients are trivial) and the unit isocrystal has zero, hence nilpotent, residues. Olsson remarks that the arguments extend to 𝒳 defined over a finite, possibly ramified, extension of `W(k)`, but gives the proofs over `W(k)` only; the ramified case is the separate target [Good-reduction comparison over ramified p-adic fields](#ramified-endpoint-comparison).

Olsson compares the pointed de Rham and étale stacks over the localisation `B̃_cris` of `B_cris` by carrying out Faltings' construction on equivariant differential graded algebras (Thom–Sullivan cochains) rather than on cohomology (Theorem 1.7). The Hopf algebra isomorphism over `B̃_cris (7.17.2)` descends to `B_cris` by Appendix D, Theorem D.3 (`B̃_cris`-admissible implies crystalline), giving (7.17.3) and Theorem 1.8; Lemma 7.18 then gives Theorem 1.10, which is (iii). The path statement (ii) is Theorem 1.11, proved in §§8.27–8.32 with the base-point-free version of §8. The tangential statement (iv) is Theorem 9.28 with Theorem 9.46. Specialising `C_et` and `C_dR` to the unipotent categories gives the statements above; Frobenius on `C_dR` is the one of the log-crystalline realization.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.Anabelian.olssonHopfComparison`: Statement (i).
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.olssonPathComparison`: Statement (ii), with compatibility with torsor actions and path composition.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.olssonLieComparison`: Statement (iii).
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.olssonTangentialComparison`: Statement (iv).

**Checks.**

- At `x=y`, (ii) is the Hopf algebra comparison (i) applied to the coordinate ring of the group, with the identity path corresponding to the counit on both sides.
- On the abelianisation, (iii) recovers the crystalline comparison for `H¹_et(𝒳°_K̄,ℚ_p)^∨` and `H¹_dR(𝒳°_K)^∨`, including for `𝒟≠∅` the boundary classes.
- Crystallinity of each graded piece of the lower central series does not imply that `O(P^et_(x,y))` is crystalline, since extensions of crystalline representations need not be crystalline; (ii) is a statement about the whole ind-representation.

The construction and its conventions follow [Martin C. Olsson](#reference-olsson), §1.1, pp. 1–2; §1.5 and Assumption 1.6, p. 4; Theorems 1.7–1.11, pp. 4–5; §1.14 and its closing remark on ramified bases, pp. 6–7; (7.17.2)–(7.17.3) and Lemma 7.18, p. 69; §§8.27–8.32, p. 83; §9.1, Assumption 9.2, p. 85; Theorem 9.28, p. 96; Theorem 9.46, p. 104; Appendix D, Theorem D.3, p. 132.

<a id="pointed-multiplicative-comparison"></a>

**Two-augmentation multiplicative comparison.** For a smooth proper pair (𝒳,𝒟) over the Witt vectors of a finite field, construct the enhanced rational logarithmic crystalline, de Rham and geometric étale cochain algebras with augmentations at two integral sections of 𝒳−𝒟. Produce a multiplicative comparison over `B_cris` compatible with both augmentations, Frobenius and Galois; its de Rham extension is strict for the Hodge filtration. Apply the reduced two-sided bar construction to obtain the coordinate algebra of the tensor path torsor, retaining coproduct, endpoint composition and coordinate coactions. Prove that finite path-coordinate subspaces are captured by finite-dimensional Galois-stable crystalline subspaces. This is an enhancement of degreewise comparison, not an inference from crystalline `H¹`.

The unramified base is K₀=Frac `W(F_q)`. The boundary is relative normal crossings; the unit local system has nilpotent boundary monodromy. The comparison itself is [Olsson's nonabelian crystalline comparison in the unipotent case](#olsson-unipotent-comparison), statements (i) at equal endpoints and (ii) for two integral endpoints; what remains here is the bar-construction description of the path coordinate ring with its coproduct, endpoint composition and coactions.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `pointedComparison.augmentations`: Preserve both endpoint evaluations.
- `pointedComparison.bar`: Compare the two-sided bar algebras and their coactions.
- `pointedComparison.crystallineSubspaces`: Apply the ind-crystalline subrepresentation criterion.
- `pointedComparison.filtration`: Recover the strict filtered de Rham comparison.

**Checks.**

- For equal endpoints, the path comparison is the Hopf comparison.
- For two different endpoints, retain both augmentations rather than a group comparison at only one point.
- A crystalline `H¹` representation with an arbitrary extension does not imply crystallinity of that extension.

The construction and its conventions follow [Martin C. Olsson](#reference-olsson), §§5–6; Theorems 1.7–1.11, pp. 3–5; §7, Lemma 7.18 and Sub-Lemma 7.19, pp. 69–70; §8.27–8.32, pp. 83–85; Appendix D, Theorem D.3, pp. 130–136.

<a id="ramified-endpoint-comparison"></a>

**Good-reduction comparison over ramified p-adic fields.** Extend the endpoint-compatible unipotent comparison to a smooth proper good-reduction pair over `O_K` for every finite `K/ℚ_p` and integral endpoints. Olsson remarks that his arguments apply to a model over a finite, possibly ramified, extension of `W(k)`, but writes the proofs over `W(k)` only ([Olsson's nonabelian crystalline comparison in the unipotent case](#olsson-unipotent-comparison)); the target is to carry this out. Construct it from the multiplicative logarithmic comparison on the integral pair over `O_K`, identify the crystalline realization over the maximal unramified subfield `K₀`, and extend it to the filtered de Rham realization over K. Prove that monodromy is zero for the good-reduction model and that the coordinate algebra and finite path modules are crystalline. Descent from an unramified model is a separate compatible case; a ramified base change does not make an arbitrary `O_K`-model descend to `W(k)`.

The integral pair is smooth proper with relative normal-crossing boundary. The comparison includes both endpoint augmentations and the nilpotent local-system boundary condition.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `ramifiedPathComparison.crystalline`: Give the zero-monodromy crystalline comparison.
- `ramifiedPathComparison.filtered`: Identify its K-extension with the strict de Rham realization.
- `ramifiedPathComparison.baseChange`: Preserve endpoint and finite-depth maps under finite field extension.

**Checks.**

- For an unramified K, recover the Witt-vector comparison.
- For a good-reduction pair over a ramified K that descends from an unramified model, recover base change of that comparison.

### 2.7 Crystalline path comparisons

<a id="nc-2-crystalline-path-coordinates"></a>

**Crystalline coordinate path comparison.** Let (𝒳,𝒟) be a smooth proper good-reduction pair over `W(F_q)`, with 𝒟 a relative finite étale divisor, and let b,x be integral sections of `𝒴=𝒳−𝒟`. For the geometric unipotent étale path scheme `P_et(b,x)`, `O(P_et)` is an ind-crystalline `G_K0`-representation. There is a canonical comparison `D_cris(O(P_et))≅O(P_rig(b_bar,x_bar))` and, after the rigid/de Rham identification, its scalar extension is `O(P_dR(b,x))`. It is compatible with Frobenius, the Hodge filtration after de Rham extension, tensor structures, endpoint composition and the coordinate coactions; `at b=x` it is a Hopf-algebra comparison. Every finite-dimensional Galois-stable subspace occurring in the coordinate union is crystalline. This is a nonlinear geometric comparison; the ordinary comparison for `H^1` alone does not imply it.

Unramified `K_0=Frac W(F_q)`, smooth proper model and relative smooth boundary, integral endpoints. Olsson’s relative setup is specialized to the unit local system/isocrystal: trivial reductive hull and zero, hence nilpotent, local monodromy. Filtered compatibility uses the associated filtered crystalline objects, not a Frobenius-preserved Hodge filtration.

Apply the unit specialization of Olsson’s pointed schematic comparison, obtained from the multiplicative crystalline/étale cochain comparison over the enlarged crystalline period ring. The group/path comparison is its degree-zero homotopy consequence. Use Olsson’s finite Galois-stable coordinate-piece argument and descent from the enlarged ring to `B_cris`. The admissibility/subspace lemmas ensure genuine continuous crystalline finite pieces. Use tensor compatibility to identify coordinate coactions and endpoint composition; rigid/de Rham evaluation identifies the endpoint Frobenius. Filtered association supplies strict de Rham compatibility. The two-augmentation multiplicative comparison identifies the path coactions. Its crystalline finite-dimensional subspace criterion supplies the full path-coordinate result; an `H¹` comparison alone does not supply that criterion.

**Checks.**

- For `b=x` the comparison respects augmentation, multiplication and coproduct.
- For the unit coordinate subspace it is the usual comparison of `ℚ_p` with `K_0`.

The construction and its conventions follow [Martin C. Olsson](#reference-olsson), Author manuscript of 24 March 2008, §§1.5–1.11, pp. 4–6; §§8.27–8.32, pp. 83–85; Sub-Lemma 7.19, pp. 69–70; Appendix D, Theorem D.3, p. 132; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan and Netan Dogra](#reference-bdii), Lemma 6.1 and proof, §6.2, p. 29 of the author manuscript; [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Section 2, pp. 116–119.

<a id="nc-2-finite-path-comparison"></a>

**Finite crystalline path comparison.** Under [Crystalline coordinate path comparison](#nc-2-crystalline-path-coordinates), each finite `M_n^et(b,x)` is crystalline and `D_cris(M_n^et(b,x))≅M_n^rig(b_bar,x_bar)`; identifying with the de Rham fibre gives a filtered Frobenius comparison after scalar extension. The comparisons commute with length transitions, bilinear composition and the source algebra action. On grade n they make the diagram from `D_cris((H^1_et∨)^⊗n)≅(H^1_dR∨)^⊗n` to the corresponding quotient length grades commute; a proper curve’s grade is not asserted to equal the entire tensor power. For finite ramified extensions `K/K_0` of a good-reduction pair, `D_cris` takes values over `K_0` and `D_dR` over K; base change of the established crystalline data supplies the K version. No new ramified-model comparison is inferred without a descent theorem.

Hypotheses of [Crystalline coordinate path comparison](#nc-2-crystalline-path-coordinates); finite path modules identified by universal evaluation. For the base-change clause, the model and endpoints descend to the displayed unramified pair.

Identify `O(P_et)` with the union of `M_n^et∨`, using [Completed path algebra](#nc-2-length-algebra) and [Finite path module](#nc-2-finite-path-module). Each finite dual is a Galois-stable crystalline subobject of the ind-coordinate ring. Use exact tensor duality of `D_cris` on crystalline representations to dualize the finite coordinate comparison. Compatibility with augmentation and coactions identifies the precise universal length piece, not just a vector space with matching dimension. Use `H^1` comparison on the augmentation generator and tensor exactness on its quotient grades. Extend coefficients along the imported period-functor base change for models that descend.

- At `n=0` this is the unit comparison; `at n=1` its nontrivial grade is the dual `H^1` comparison.

Balakrishnan and Netan Dogra](#reference-bdii), Lemma 6.1 and proof, p. 29 of the author manuscript; [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Section 2, pp. 116–119.

### 2.8 Abelian arithmetic Kummer comparison

<a id="abelian-kummer-mordell-weil"></a>

**Rational abelian Kummer and Sha comparison.** Let `A/F` be an abelian variety over a number field. Use [SelmerIwasawaCohomology](../SelmerIwasawaCohomology/README.md) §2.12a for `abelianKummer`, the local images `KummerLocal` and their good-reduction/unramified comparison, `abelianSelmerGroup`, `abelianSha`, `abelianDescent_exact` and `abelianSelmerGroup_finite`. Use [HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions](../HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions/README.md) §1.1 for `kummer` and its fppf/Galois comparison with `abelianKummer`, §§1.6–1.7 for `finite_quotient_nsmul` and `fg_points`, and §§0.18–0.20 for canonical heights and their kernel. Construct the inverse-limit rational Kummer/Sha comparison below and its compatibility with geometric path classes. The finite-level inputs have the coefficient and field-change compatibility of these suppliers. ([Poonen](#reference-poonen-rational-points), Theorems 6.5.10(i), 8.4.9 and Remark 8.4.5, pp. 182, 241–243.)

**Checks.**

- Rationalization kills every torsion point in the Kummer domain. A nonzero `V_p Sha(A/F)` remains as the quotient of the rational Selmer space; finite generation alone does not remove it.
- For `A=0` and for `n=1`, the Kummer quotient and the corresponding Selmer group are zero; no nonzero class can be introduced by the definition.
- For `E:y²=x³−x` over `ℚ`, the point (0,0) has nonzero class modulo 2: a rational half would force `(x²+1)²=0` in the duplication formula. This rejects a Kummer map that kills every rational two-torsion point.
- At every n, a point in nA(F) has zero Kummer class, and a class of A[n] outside the local Kummer image is excluded from `Selⁿ`. Using all `H¹` in place of `Selⁿ` fails this local test.
- A nonzero torsion point has canonical height zero; the height is positive on a nontorsion F-point. For every P, the value at [2]P is four times the value at P.
- Replacing `h_L` by `h_L+C` gives the same canonical limit, whereas changing the normalization to `2^(−m)` fails the quadratic scaling test.
- A constant positive-dimensional abelian variety over `ℂ(t)` contains the uncountable `subgroup A(ℂ)`; its points are not finitely generated. The number-field hypothesis is essential.

The resulting rational tower has `A(F)⊗ℚ_p ↪ H¹(G_F,V_pA)` and `0 → A(F)⊗ℚ_p → Sel_p(A/F) → V_p Sha(A/F) → 0`, where `Sel_p` is the inverse limit of the finite Kummer Selmer groups followed by rationalization. Prove the transition and exactness statements using the finite n-torsion groups, compact inverse limits and rational flatness. The tower is compatible with all local Kummer maps. A comparison with a separately defined Bloch–Kato Selmer group requires equality of the imposed local conditions; the Sha term is retained unless its rational Tate module vanishes. These are the inputs to Layer 4's depth-one cut, rather than an equality obtained by substituting the Mordell–Weil rank.

*Needs:* SelmerIwasawaCohomology §2.12a (number-field abelian descent, local Kummer images, Selmer and Sha); HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions §1.1 (fppf comparison), §§1.6–1.7 (weak Mordell–Weil and finite generation) and §§0.18–0.20; AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli §§A1.5, A3.2 and A4.1; JacobianChallenge Layer E; ProfiniteCohomology Layers 5 and 9; ArithmeticGaloisDuality §§R02.1, R02.3; SelmerIwasawaCohomology §§0.6–0.10, 2.1–2.3 (limits and Selmer kernels); NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties §5.0a (good-reduction finite étale torsion); ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights §1.13 (Weil heights and ample Northcott); Mathlib `ContinuousCohomology.tateShafarevich` and `AddCommGroup.fg_of_descent'`.

### 2.9 The depth-one realization bridge

<a id="jacobian-differential-kummer"></a>

**Jacobian differential and rational Kummer comparison.** For a smooth proper geometrically connected curve `X/k` with rational b and Jacobian J, prove that Abel–Jacobi pullback identifies `H¹_dR(J)` with `H¹_dR(X)`, preserving the Hodge filtration, cup/polarization conventions and field extension. Compare the dual of the Hodge quotient with Lie J. Identify the depth-one étale path of x with the inverse-limit rational Kummer class of [x−b], with the same path orientation. At a good-reduction p-adic place, identify its crystalline/de Rham comparison with the Jacobian Tate-module comparison and its period with the abelian logarithm, after the compensating sign for the period `I⁻¹γ`. For `X=C−D` with nonempty reduced finite étale D in characteristic zero and `b∈X(k)`, use [Generalized Jacobian of a reduced boundary](#reduced-boundary-generalized-jacobian), [Finite étale and Tate-module comparison for the generalized Jacobian](#generalized-jacobian-etale-comparison) and [Filtered de Rham comparison for the generalized Jacobian](#generalized-jacobian-derham-comparison) for the same path/Kummer statement with `J_D`. Its local comparison requires a smooth proper model of C and a reduced finite étale relative boundary D; its Lie quotient includes the boundary torus.

The rational base point fixes Abel–Jacobi. Good reduction is imposed for the crystalline comparison, not the global geometric identifications.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `abelJacobi.deRhamEquiv`: Give the filtered pullback equivalence.
- `abelJacobi.tatePathKummer`: Identify the rational path cocycle with Kummer.
- `abelJacobi.depthOnePeriod`: Give the sign-normalized local logarithm identity.

**Checks.**

- At `x=b`, every class and logarithm is zero.
- For `G_m`, the open-curve boundary direction gives `log(x/b)` with the fixed orientation.
- A finite `μ_n` Kummer isomorphism alone does not identify the rational Tate-module limit.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §1, pp. 97–102; Introduction, p. 93 (the abelian logarithm comparison); §2, pp. 115–117 (the étale realization); [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), §3.1 and §5.1, pp. 901–905 and 917–919.

### 2.10 Depth one and the limits of unipotent information

<a id="nc-2-depth-one-jacobian"></a>

**Depth one and the Jacobian.** For a smooth proper geometrically connected curve `X/k` with rational b and Jacobian J, the Abel–Jacobi morphism `a_b:X→J` induces canonical abelian realization identifications `U_et⟨1⟩≅V_pJ` as an additive group with Galois action, and `U_dR⟨1⟩≅H^1_dR(X)∨≅H^1_dR(J)∨` as additive filtered groups. Their good-reduction comparison is the ordinary Jacobian Tate-module/de Rham comparison. At a proper local good-reduction field, `F^0 H^1_dR(X)∨=ann H^0(X,Ω¹)`, and the quotient by `F^0` is `Lie(J)`. `P_et⟨1⟩(b,x)` is the rational Kummer torsor for `[x−b]∈J(k)`, and the de Rham period lies in the displayed quotient `Lie(J)`. For `X=C−D` in characteristic zero with nonempty reduced finite étale D and `b∈X(k)`, [Generalized Jacobian of a reduced boundary](#reduced-boundary-generalized-jacobian) supplies `J_D`; [Finite étale and Tate-module comparison for the generalized Jacobian](#generalized-jacobian-etale-comparison) and [Filtered de Rham comparison for the generalized Jacobian](#generalized-jacobian-derham-comparison) give `U_et⟨1⟩=V_pJ_D`, `U_dR⟨1⟩=H¹_dR(X)∨` and the Lie quotient `Lie(J_D)`. The local crystalline statement requires a smooth proper model of C with reduced finite étale relative boundary D.

Proper smooth geometrically connected curve, rational b; coefficient p in the étale realization. Good reduction is required only for crystalline comparison and the local filtered statement. The Jacobian and Abel–Jacobi construction are imported from JacobianChallenge; the cohomological bridges are separate inputs, including the Tate-module/H¹ comparison of SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.3 and the Jacobian differential and rational Kummer comparison.

The first augmentation/Lie graded piece is `Ext^1(1,1)∨=H^1∨`, so central depth one is its vector group. Import the Jacobian and the pointed Abel–Jacobi morphism from JacobianChallenge B–F, and the untwisted étale `H^1`/Tate-module identification and Abel–Jacobi pullback from InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups §IG.0.T1 (finite-level curve–Jacobian `H¹` comparison) and AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli §A4.4 (étale `H¹` and the Tate module). Dualize with the same covariance. For endpoint compatibility, pull back the finite étale multiplication-by-`p^r` covers of J along `a_b`: their fibre over x is the division-point torsor of [x−b], and the fibre over b has its zero lift. Passing to the Tate-module inverse limit and rationalizing gives the Kummer torsor. The exact de Rham Abel–Jacobi `H^1` comparison and proper curve Hodge calculation are additional requirements, not assertions supplied by the cited B–F layers. Apply the linear abelian-scheme comparison and the dual Hodge filtration. The annihilator description gives `Lie(J)` as the quotient; the identification of linear path coefficients with ordinary integrals is supplied by [Coleman functions and normalized primitives](#coleman-functions-primitives) after its construction in §5.0.

**Checks.**

- For a genus-g proper curve the depth-one vector group has dimension 2g and its `F^0` has dimension g.
- For `P¹` the proper depth-one group is trivial; puncturing twice gives the one-dimensional boundary realization of `G_m`.
- For an elliptic curve with origin b, the Abel–Jacobi map is the identity, and the depth-one torsor is its usual rational Kummer torsor.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Introduction, pp. 93–95; Section 1, pp. 100–104; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Section 2.1, pp. 896–898; proof of Lemma 5.4, pp. 923–924.

<a id="nc-2-finite-cover-boundary"></a>

**Finite covers are not unipotent points.** The geometric pro-unipotent `ℚ_p` group does not recover the full profinite fundamental group or all finite étale covers. In characteristic zero, `G_m` has nontrivial finite étale covers `t↦t^m` for m&gt;1, while its de Rham unipotent group is `G_a` and its geometric `ℚ_p`-unipotent étale realization is the additive Tate realization `ℚ_p(1)`. The additive rational point group is uniquely m-divisible for each m&gt;0 and has no nontrivial finite abstract group quotient. It therefore cannot replace the profinite finite-cover classifier. A finite-rank unipotent representation and a finite covering set are different objects.

Geometric characteristic-zero `G_m` and `ℚ_p` coefficients. No comparison between realisations is used without its coefficient extension.

Apply [Kim’s affine universal property](#nc-2-affine-universality) to the one-generator `H^1` of `G_m`, or the continuous representation equivalence to its procyclic geometric p-adic monodromy, to obtain the additive unipotent realization. Use the imported finite-cover theory to exhibit the degree-m étale power map. Any finite quotient of a divisible abelian group is divisible, and the only finite divisible abelian group is trivial. The full geometric profinite group has the displayed nontrivial quotient, so its finite-cover information cannot be reconstructed from the additive `ℚ_p` points.

**Checks.**

- The cover `t↦t²` remains nontrivial even though the additive `ℚ_p` point group has no quotient of order two.
- No statement that all rational points of a pro-unipotent group determine all finite covers is admitted.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Introduction, pp. 90–94; Section 1, Lemma 3, pp. 108–110.

Use [Kim’s affine universal property](#nc-2-affine-universality); [Galois structure and completion](#nc-2-etale-galois); [EtaleCohomologyFoundations](../EtaleCohomologyFoundations/README.md) §F.0.2 (finite étale Galois categories, paths and monodromy); [Arithmetic path torsor](#nc-0-arithmetic-geometric-paths).

### 2.11 The two-step Malcev quotient

<a id="two-step-malcev"></a>

**Two-step geometric Malcev quotient.** For a geometric pro-p fundamental group Π of a characteristic-zero hyperbolic curve, construct its universal continuous two-step unipotent `ℚ_p` quotient and the corresponding nilpotent Lie algebra. Set `H=H₁_et(Xbar,ℚ_p)`. Its degree-one quotient is H and its central degree-two kernel is `(∧²H)/im(H₂→∧²H)`, where `H₂→∧²H` is dual to cup product. For an affine curve `H₂=0`; for a proper curve the image is the symplectic relation line. Prove the universal property for continuous maps to every two-step unipotent `ℚ_p` group and functoriality under pointed curve maps and Galois action. This construction uses no anabelian reconstruction.

The coefficient field has characteristic zero, including `Q₂`; BCH uses `1/2` in the field. The relation and the cup pairing have the same trace normalization.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `MalcevTwoStep.universal`: Factor every continuous map to a two-step unipotent group uniquely.
- `MalcevTwoStep.bracket`: Identify the bracket with wedge modulo the cup-dual relation.
- `MalcevTwoStep.functorial`: Preserve pointed maps and arithmetic actions.
- `MalcevTwoStep.realization`: Identify the quotient with depth two of the étale unipotent realization.

**Checks.**

- For two free generators the centre is one-dimensional with bracket `[e₁,e₂]`.
- For a proper elliptic curve the symplectic relation kills `∧²H`, so the unipotent group is abelian.
- For a proper genus-two curve the centre has dimension binom(4,2)−1=5.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m99), §3, two-step quotient and its Hodge–Tate analysis, author pp. 21–27; [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §1, published pp. 97–101.

Use [Neutral tensor category and Hopf reconstruction](#neutral-tensor-reconstruction); [Geometric pro-p and arithmetic p-power comparison](#pro-p-curve-comparison); [EtaleCohomologyFoundations](../EtaleCohomologyFoundations/README.md) §§0.11, F.5–F.6 (trace, Poincaré duality and purity).

### 2.12 Tangential unipotent fibres

<a id="integral-tangential-realizations"></a>

**Integral tangential realization and comparison.** Let 𝒳 be a smooth proper curve over `O_K` with relative finite étale divisor 𝒟. At `b∈𝒟(O_K)` choose a nonzero tangent vector that is an `O_K`-basis of the tangent line. Construct the unipotent de Rham fibre functor from logarithmic connections with nilpotent residue and the corresponding étale and rigid/log-crystalline fibre functors. Compare their tensor paths, finite length modules, lower-central quotients and endpoint compositions. A change of tangent scales the residue exponential and its Kummer character; an integral unit tangent is the crystalline good-reduction datum. Prove the same strict filtered, Frobenius and Galois comparisons as for integral interior endpoints, using the local log point and its tangential evaluation.

The tangent is integral and a unit in its line; a vector multiplied by a uniformizer is not this datum. Characteristic-zero coefficients and nilpotent residues are used.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `tangentialUnipotent.fibre`: Give tensor-natural log-residue evaluation.
- `tangentialUnipotent.path`: Give the endpoint-compatible tensor path scheme.
- `tangentialUnipotent.comparison`: Give the finite-module crystalline and filtered comparison.
- `tangentialUnipotent.scale`: Compute unit scaling through the residue/Kummer character.

**Checks.**

- For a zero residue connection, tangential evaluation is ordinary constant evaluation.
- On `P¹−{0,1,∞}` over Z, the unit tangent at 0 supplies the base point even though no ordinary Z-point exists.
- A zero tangent fails to define the punctured tangential fibre.

The construction and its conventions follow [Martin C. Olsson](#reference-olsson), §9.1–9.11, pp. 85–89; §9.17–9.23, pp. 90–94; Theorem 9.46 and §§9.47–9.58, pp. 104–110; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Ishai Dan-Cohen, Minhyong Kim and Stefan Wewers](#reference-bdckw-2018v4), §2.1, p. 8.

### 2.13 Unramified arithmetic path realizations

<a id="good-model-unramified-paths"></a>

**Good-model inertia and arithmetic factorization.** For a smooth proper model with relative normal-crossing divisor over `O_F[1/T]`, and an integral interior or unit-tangential base point, prove that the geometric p-adic unipotent group and every permitted integral endpoint path have trivial inertia at each finite `v∉T` with `v∤p`. Construct jointly continuous actions factoring through `G_(F,T)`, together with coefficient, endpoint and depth compatibility. At a local `v≠p`, a proper good-reduction path is unramified. After a fixed finite extension giving good reduction, a proper path is potentially unramified. The group action alone does not establish this statement for the path torsor.

T contains p-adic places and all bad model and boundary places. Endpoints extend integrally in the stated model.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `goodModel.inertiaGroup`: Prove trivial inertia on each finite-depth geometric group.
- `goodModel.inertiaPath`: Prove the corresponding result for endpoint paths.
- `goodModel.factorArithmetic`: Construct the continuous `G_(F,T)-action`.
- `goodModel.potentialPath`: Transport the unramified statement through a fixed finite extension.

**Checks.**

- The constant path at the base point has trivial cocycle at every place.
- A boundary collision or nonintegral endpoint is excluded from the integral path statement.
- A potentially good model can have nontrivial inertia before its chosen extension.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §1, pp. 91–96 and 101–106; [Minhyong Kim and Akio Tamagawa](#reference-kt), Theorem 0.1 and its proof, author pp. 1–5.

Use [InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups](../InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups/README.md) Layer IG.1 (arithmetic fundamental groups, inertia and specialization); [ArithmeticGaloisDuality](../ArithmeticGaloisDuality/README.md) Layer R02.3 (restricted ramification and the S-idele class formation); [Integral tangential realization and comparison](#integral-tangential-realizations).

### Examples

The finite length tower differs from the lower-central tower. For one generator T, the algebra `K[T]/(T²)` has `Δ(T)=T⊗1+1⊗T`, but `Δ(T²)=2T⊗T` modulo `T²` in each factor. In characteristic zero this is nonzero. Therefore the length-one quotient is a module-algebra truncation and is not a Hopf quotient. The lower-central quotient of a one-dimensional abelian unipotent group is unchanged at every positive depth.

For two free generators the first graded Lie dimensions are 2,1,2. For a proper genus-two curve there are four degree-one generators and a single symplectic relation in degree two, giving dimensions 4 and `6−1=5 at` the first two grades. Its two-step group has underlying exponential coordinates `H⊕(Λ²H/⟨ω⟩)`; multiplication contains the one-half commutator term. Forgetting that term makes the reconstructed alternating bracket zero.

For an affine universal connection `d−ΣT_iω_i`, words multiply by concatenation in its completed path algebra. Functions on the group are dual and multiply by shuffle. The two length-one functions satisfy `f_i f_j=f_ij+f_ji`, including the multiplicity two when `i=j`. Substituting concatenation for this product changes the coordinate Hopf algebra.

The period compares two paths with the same source. With `pφ` represented by I and pH by `γ`, the equation pφ·u=pH gives `u=I⁻¹γ`. For upper-triangular unipotent 3×3 matrices `I=1+E₁₂` and `γ=1+E₂₃`, this is `1−E₁₂+E₂₃−E₁₃`. In contrast `γI⁻¹=1−E₁₂+E₂₃` has no `E₁₃` term. The central coordinate is therefore a concrete test of the source-translation convention.

For a gauge G=1−aE with `E²=0`, differentiating G contributes −daE. The connection-change formula must preserve that sign. A gauge with a pole on an auxiliary affine open need not extend to the proper curve; the no-pole quotient discards exactly such obstructions. The Hodge filtration is unique only after the compactification, logarithmic extension and base-point rigidification are specified.

Two endpoint augmentations matter in the crystalline comparison: equal endpoints recover the Hopf algebra, whereas unequal endpoints give its path comodule. A comparison of group algebras at a single point cannot specify the second endpoint. For a ramified local field, the special-fibre realization is over its maximal unramified subfield `K₀` and the Hodge realization is over K; they are compared after the prescribed scalar extension.


For a finite-dimensional representation over any field, extension length zero means that the action is trivial, including on nonzero vector spaces. A length-n filtration has `n+1` graded layers, agreeing with `C_n` and the exact-category extension length above.

## Layer 3: Anabelian reconstruction

Recover source-qualified curves and their maps from relative arithmetic groups. Finite-field, stable-log, local pro-p and sub-p-adic statements retain their separate hypotheses and endpoints.

### 3.1 Relative arithmetic interfaces

<a id="nc-1-relative-outer-hom"></a>

**Relative outer open homomorphisms.** For surjections `q_X:Π_X→Γ` and `q_Y:Π_Y→Γ` of profinite groups, OverHom consists of continuous homomorphisms f with `q_Y∘f=q_X`. RelativeOuterHom is its quotient by f∼g iff g=Int(d)∘f for some `d∈ker(q_Y)`; the open locus consists of classes with open image. `Γ` is fixed pointwise.

`q_X` and `q_Y` continuous surjective `Π_X`, `Π_Y` and `Γ` profinite.

Form the subtype of continuous homomorphisms satisfying the commuting square. Use target geometric conjugation to define a setoid; openness is invariant under conjugation. Compose representatives; f maps the source geometric kernel into the target one, so composition descends.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.Anabelian.OverHom`: Continuous homomorphism with `q_Y∘f=q_X`.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.relativeHomSetoid`: The relation on OverHom: g∼f when one element of `ker(q_Y)` conjugates f to g on every element; reflexive, symmetric and transitive with conjugators 1, `d⁻¹` and `e·d`.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.RelativeOuterHom`: Geometric-conjugacy quotient of OverHom.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.RelativeOuterHom.ofHom`: The class of a continuous homomorphism over `Γ`.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.RelativeOuterHom.eq_iff`: Two representatives give the same class exactly when a target kernel element conjugates one to the other.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.RelativeOuterHom.comp`: Composition over `Γ` descends and is associative.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.RelativeOuterHom.open_iff`: Openness of a class means openness of the range of any representative.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.RelativeOuterHom.openClasses`: The set of classes having a representative with open range; by `open_iff` every representative of such a class has open range.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.Anabelian.relativeHom_self_test`: The identity over q represents the identity class; composing with it leaves every class fixed.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.relativeHom_kernel_conj_test`: Int(d) and identity have the same class whenever `q(d)=1`.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.relativeHom_base_change_test`: For `q_X=q_Y=id_Γ`, the only relative homomorphism is identity; any nonidentity automorphism of `Γ` is excluded.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.relativeHom_sign_test`: For the discrete sign map `q:S_3→C_2`, conjugation by a transposition is a relative endomorphism over `C_2` whose class differs from the identity class: it inverts the kernel `A_3`, whereas every `A_3-conjugation` fixes `A_3` pointwise. A definition quotienting by conjugation by all of `S_3` would identify the two classes.
- A map over a nontrivial automorphism of `Γ` fails the commuting-square condition.
- A constant curve map has geometric image trivial and is excluded by openness.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m99), §0, author-copy pp. 14–16; Theorem 14.1 and Corollary 15.5, pp. 71–79.

Use `ContinuousMonoidHom`; `ContinuousMonoidHom.comp`; [EtaleCohomologyFoundations](../EtaleCohomologyFoundations/README.md) §F.0.A2 (the arithmetic exact sequence); [EtaleCohomologyFoundations](../EtaleCohomologyFoundations/README.md) §F.0.2 (finite étale Galois categories, paths and monodromy).

<a id="nc-1-relative-outer-isom"></a>

**Relative outer isomorphisms.** `RelativeOuterIsom(q_X,q_Y)` consists of continuous group equivalences e over the identity of `Γ`, modulo target `ker(q_Y)` conjugation. Its inversion and composition are compatible with RelativeOuterHom. An inverse must be continuous, not just an algebraic inverse.

Same profinite extensions as [Relative outer open homomorphisms](#nc-1-relative-outer-hom).

Restrict the previous relation to ContinuousMulEquiv representatives. The commuting square transports to the inverse; geometric conjugation is transported across e.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.Anabelian.OverIsom`: Continuous multiplicative equivalence commuting with `q_X,q_Y`.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.relativeIsomSetoid`: The same target-kernel conjugacy relation on OverIsom.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.RelativeOuterIsom`: Quotient of OverIsom by target geometric inner conjugations.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.RelativeOuterIsom.ofIsom`: The class of a continuous multiplicative equivalence over `Γ`.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.RelativeOuterIsom.eq_iff`: Equality is witnessed by one target geometric conjugator on every element.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.RelativeOuterIsom.symm`: Inversion swaps X and Y and is well-defined on classes.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.RelativeOuterIsom.toHom`: The underlying relative Hom class has open image and respects composition.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.RelativeOuterIsom.trans`: Composition of relative isomorphism classes over `Γ` is well defined and associative, with the identity class as unit and symm as inverse.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.Anabelian.relativeIsom_id_test`: The reflexive equivalence gives the identity and its inverse.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.relativeIsom_conj_test`: An inner equivalence by `d∈ker q` is the identity outer class.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.relativeIsom_base_test`: Over `q=id_Γ`, there is exactly one relative isomorphism; `Γ` automorphisms are not silently admitted.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.relativeIsom_sign_test`: For the discrete sign map `q:S_3→C_2`, conjugation by a transposition is a relative automorphism over `C_2` whose class is not the identity class; quotienting by conjugation by all of `S_3` would make it trivial.
- Recover both directions of the original continuous equivalence.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m96), §0, pp. 571–574; Theorems 10.1–10.2, pp. 625–626.

Use [Relative outer open homomorphisms](#nc-1-relative-outer-hom); `ContinuousMulEquiv`; [EtaleCohomologyFoundations](../EtaleCohomologyFoundations/README.md) §F.0.A2 (the arithmetic exact sequence).

<a id="nc-1-relative-pro-p"></a>

**Geometrically pro-p arithmetic quotient.** Put `Δ=ker(q:Π→Γ)` and `N_p=image(proPKernel p Δ→Π)`. `N_p` is closed normal in Π because proPKernel is characteristic under continuous conjugations. Define `Π^(p)=Π/N_p`, obtaining `1→Δ(p)→Π^(p)→Γ→1`. Only `Δ` is pro-p completed. The construction preserves relative homomorphisms and sends open-image maps to open-image maps.

p prime; `Π,Γ` profinite; q continuous surjective.

Apply the pro-p-kernel construction to the closed geometric `subgroup Δ`. Arithmetic conjugation restricts to a continuous automorphism of `Δ`; its pro-p kernel is invariant. Factor q and relative maps through the closed normal quotient; identify the kernel with Δ/proPKernel `p Δ`. Use quotient-map openness to transport open images.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.Anabelian.relativeProPKernel`: Image in Π of the geometric pro-p kernel; normal closure agrees with this image.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.relativeProPKernel_normal`: relativeProPKernel is a normal subgroup of Π.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.RelativeProP`: Π modulo relativeProPKernel.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.RelativeProP.projection`: Continuous projection to `Γ`; surjective when q is surjective. For compact Hausdorff Π and Hausdorff `Γ` its kernel is continuously isomorphic to the maximalProPQuotient of `ker(q)`.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.RelativeProP.map`: Every relative continuous homomorphism descends, naturally and compatibly with classes.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.RelativeProP.open_map`: An open-image relative map induces an open-image map on these quotients.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.RelativeProP.mk`: Continuous quotient map from Π to its relative geometric pro-p quotient; its composite with projection is q.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.RelativeProP.lift`: A relative continuous homomorphism factors through this quotient when the target geometric kernel has trivial proPKernel; on profinite target kernels this is equivalent to being pro-p.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.RelativeProP.lift_comp_mk`: The lifted relative map composed with the continuous quotient map is the supplied homomorphism.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.RelativeProP.lift_unique`: A relative map out of the quotient agreeing after precomposition with mk equals the constructed lift.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.RelativeProP.projection_exists`: Existence form of projection: for compact Hausdorff Π, Hausdorff `Γ` and surjective q there is a continuous surjection `π` to `Γ` with π∘mk=q whose kernel is continuously isomorphic to maximalProPQuotient p (ker q).
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.RelativeProP.lift_exists_unique`: Existence-and-uniqueness form of lift, `lift_comp_mk` and `lift_unique`: for any continuous `π` with π∘mk=q, a relative homomorphism into a target whose geometric kernel has trivial proPKernel factors uniquely through mk as a homomorphism over `π`.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.Anabelian.relativeProP_identity_test`: For `q=id_Γ`, `Δ=1`, so `Π^(p)≃Γ` even when `Γ` is not pro-p.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.relativeProP_field_test`: For `Γ=1`, `Π^(p)` is the maximalProPQuotient p Π.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.relativeProP_prime_to_p_test`: For `Π=C_ℓ×C_p→C_ℓ` with `ℓ≠p`, `Π^(p)≃Π`; completing the whole Π would lose `C_ℓ`.
- The full `Γ` survives even when `Γ` has finite quotients of order prime to p.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m99), §0, author-copy pp. 14–16; Corollary 15.5, pp. 77–79.

Use `TauCeti.proPKernel`; `TauCeti.map_proPKernel_eq`; `TauCeti.proPKernel_le_comap`; `TauCeti.maximalProPQuotient`; `QuotientGroup.lift`; [Relative outer open homomorphisms](#nc-1-relative-outer-hom); [EtaleCohomologyFoundations](../EtaleCohomologyFoundations/README.md) §F.0.A2 (the arithmetic exact sequence).

### 3.2 Admissible log-cover systems and decomposition groups

<a id="admissible-log-coverings"></a>

**Admissible coverings of pointed stable curves.** Let `f^log:C^log→S^log` and `h^log:D^log→S^log` be symmetrically pointed stable log curves over a fine log scheme `S^log`, with marked divisors `μ_f` and `μ_h`. A morphism `π^log:C^log→D^log` is a log admissible covering of degree d if `π^log` is log étale and the induced map on characteristic monoids sends `Γ_D` into `⋃_(i≤d)(1/i)Γ_C`; `π` is finite and of degree d on a dense open subset of every fibre of h; `μ_f⊆π⁻¹(μ_h)⊆d·μ_f`; and f is smooth at c exactly when h is smooth `at π(c)`. A morphism `π:C→D` of the underlying pointed stable curves is an admissible covering if, étale locally on S, it underlies a log admissible covering for some fine log structure on S. Then: (a) every admissible covering carries a canonical log structure on S for which it is log admissible, and admissible coverings agree with the Harris–Mumford ones defined by local equations at the nodes; (b) at a node, in the local chart xy=sⁱ upstairs over `uv=s^(ie)` downstairs, the covering is `u=xᵉ`, `v=yᵉ` with the same index e on both branches, e is invertible on S, and `e≤d`; (c) over a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring A with n invertible, the punctured spectrum of the strict henselisation of A[x,y]/(xy−sⁿ) has `π₁≅ℤ/n` with universal cover given by the chart of index 1; (d) over the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring with generic point `η`, an admissible covering of the generic fibres has at most one extension; if d! is invertible in A it extends after a tamely ramified extension of A, the extension being the normalisation of D in the function field of `C_η`. Galois conditions are not imposed, and the étale degree on a component may be divisible by the residue characteristic, since log étaleness only constrains the local indices at nodes and marked points.

`S^log` fine; the curves symmetrically pointed stable; for (c)–(d), A strictly henselian, n or d! invertible as stated.

(a) Compare log structures at the nodes: the log étale condition at a node is exactly the existence of the local equations, and Kato's criterion for log étaleness forces the index to be invertible; conversely, given Harris–Mumford equations, send log u to `e·log x` and log v to `e·log y`, which respects `log u+log v=log s` and descends because the construction is canonical (Lemmas of §§3.7–3.8). (b) is the local computation in the chart. (c) The index-1 chart is regular, so its punctured spectrum is simply connected, and the index-n map is finite étale of degree n on punctured spectra. (d) Uniqueness: the generic fibre is schematically dense. Existence: take the normalisation, apply Abhyankar's lemma at the generic points of the special fibre and at the marked points (tame since d! is invertible), purity of the branch locus elsewhere, and (c) at the nodes.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.Anabelian.IsLogAdmissibleCovering`: The five conditions on `π^log`.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.IsAdmissibleCovering`: Existence of a log admissible lift étale locally on S.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.IsAdmissibleCovering.canonicalLogStructure`: The canonical log structure on S and the equivalence with the Harris–Mumford definition.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.IsAdmissibleCovering.nodeIndex_le`: The local index at a node is invertible and at most d.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.IsAdmissibleCovering.extend_unique` and `TauCeti.Anabelian.IsAdmissibleCovering.extend_exists`: Statement (d).

**Checks.**

- The identity of a smooth pointed curve is an admissible covering of degree 1 with every node index `e=1`, the equality case of `e≤d`.
- Over `𝔽̄_p`, an étale cover of degree p of a smooth component (an Artin–Schreier cover of an elliptic curve, say) is admissible away from the nodes, so a component degree divisible by p is allowed; but a node with local index `e=p` fails log étaleness, because Kato's criterion needs the index invertible.
- Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from 2, the map `z↦z²` from `(P¹;0,∞,1,−1)` to `(P¹;0,∞,1)`, both stable, satisfies `μ_f⊆π⁻¹(μ_h)⊆2μ_f`, since `π⁻¹(μ_h)=2[0]+2[∞]+[1]+[−1]`; if −1 is not marked upstairs, `π⁻¹(μ_h)` contains −1 outside `μ_f` and the second inclusion fails. In characteristic 2 the markings 1 and −1 collide and the square map is inseparable, so this example is excluded.
- In (d), without the hypothesis that d! be invertible a wildly ramified generic covering need not extend; the existence clause is stated only under it.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m95), §3.5 and its Definition and observations, pp. 19–20; §3.6, p. 20; §§3.7–3.11, pp. 21–24; §3.12, Lemma, p. 24; §3.13, Lemma, pp. 24–25.

Use [InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups](../InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups/README.md) §IG.5.4 (admissible G-covers); [CrystallineCohomology](../CrystallineCohomology/README.md) Layers CR.5:log-algebra and CR.5 (logarithmic structures and logarithmic crystalline cohomology); [SchemeAndStackFoundations](../SchemeAndStackFoundations/README.md) SF.4 (stable pointed curves and their moduli).

<a id="nc-1-log-admissible-system"></a>

**Admissible stable log-cover system.** A stable log curve is a stable pointed curve with the log structure pulled back from the boundary log structure on its stable-curve moduli family, over a standard log point. A finite generically étale cover is pre-admissible if its stable extension is multi-admissible; it is potentially pre-admissible if this holds after a finite tame base extension. The admissible arithmetic group is Π modulo the intersection of the co-admissible open subgroups. Its base quotient is the tame log-point Galois group `Γ^t`. Multi-admissible means a disjoint union of admissible connected covers. The imported admissibility predicate requires a finite map of fibrewise generic degree d, preservation of the smooth/node loci, marked-divisor bounds `μ_C≤π*μ_D≤dμ_C`, étaleness off nodes and markings, tame marking ramification, and strict-henselian node charts xy=a, `uv=a^e`, `u=x^e`, `v=y^e` with `1≤e≤d` invertible on the base. Equivalently it has the source’s log-étale lift and characteristic-generator multiplicity bound. Total cover degree need not be invertible.

Residue characteristic p&gt;0; stable log curve of hyperbolic type; pointed branches included.

Use genuine étale sheaves of monoids and charts from CR.5 and stable models from StableReduction. Use the admissible coverings of [Admissible coverings of pointed stable curves](#admissible-log-coverings), which allow étale components of degree divisible by p, together with the admissible G-covers of IG.5; Layer 3 owns their cofinal arithmetic reconstruction system. Form the cofiltered family of potentially pre-admissible pointed covers, with cofinal orderly Galois covers. Take the quotient characterized by this family; record geometric kernel and tame base quotient, rather than substituting ordinary étale `π₁`.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.Anabelian.AdmissibleLogCoverSystem`: Pointed stable log curve and its cofiltered potentially pre-admissible covers.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.AdmissibleLogCoverSystem.admissibleGroup`: Quotient by the intersection of co-admissible subgroups with its map to `Γ^t`.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.AdmissibleLogCoverSystem.orderly_cofinal`: Orderly Galois covers form a cofinal subfamily.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.AdmissibleLogCoverSystem.tame_baseChange`: Further tame base extensions induce the prescribed compatible system.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.Anabelian.admissible_identity_test`: The identity stable log cover is pre-admissible and represents the top subgroup.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.admissible_orderly_test`: Computing the intersection using all co-admissible covers or orderly Galois covers gives the same quotient.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.admissible_wild_base_test`: A cover requiring a genuinely wild base extension is not declared potentially pre-admissible merely because its generic cover is étale.
- Distinguish admissible `log π₁`, special ordinary étale `π₁` and the intermediate quotient used in §3.
- The identity cover of a nodal curve has `d=e=1`; an erroneous strict bound e&lt;d would exclude it. Étale p-degree covers are allowed despite a total degree divisible by p.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m96), Definitions 2.1, 2.4, 2.5 and 2.7, Lemma 2.6, Corollary 2.8, pp. 580–585; [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m95), the definitions in §§3.3–3.6 and §3.9, the unnumbered Proposition of §3.11 and the unnumbered Lemmas of §§3.12–3.13, author-copy pp. 18–25.

Use [CrystallineCohomology](../CrystallineCohomology/README.md) §CR.5:log-algebra.1 (log structures); [CrystallineCohomology](../CrystallineCohomology/README.md) §CR.5:log-algebra.1 (log charts); [CrystallineCohomology](../CrystallineCohomology/README.md) §CR.5:log-algebra.2 (Kummer morphisms of log schemes); [TauCetiRoadmap.StableReduction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction/README.md#layer-8-canonical-contraction-and-unpointed-stable-reduction); [TauCetiRoadmap.StableReduction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction/README.md#layer-9-marked-stabilization-and-stable-pointed-reduction); [EtaleCohomologyFoundations](../EtaleCohomologyFoundations/README.md) §F.0.2 (finite étale Galois categories, paths and monodromy); [InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups](../InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups/README.md) §IG.1.2 (tame and prime-to-p quotients); [InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups](../InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups/README.md) §IG.5.4 (admissible G-covers of marked curves); [InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups](../InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups/README.md) Layer IG.5 (configuration spaces and Hurwitz moduli); [SchemeAndStackFoundations](../SchemeAndStackFoundations/README.md), SF.4 (the stable-curve stack): the universal pointed stable family; [SchemeAndStackFoundations](../SchemeAndStackFoundations/README.md), SF.4 (versal deformation of nodes and smoothness of the stable-curve stack): independent node-smoothing parameters and boundary charts in stable moduli.

<a id="nc-1-tower-decomposition"></a>

**Decomposition subgroups from recovered towers.** For a compatible component or point tower `x=(x_i)` in finite-cover geometric data with Π-actions, define `D_x=⋂_i Stab_Π(x_i)`. Recover inertia as the subgroup acting trivially on the underlying component while retaining its action on the log branches. Changing the lift by a gives `D_(a·x)=aD_xa⁻¹`; do not replace `D_x` by a normal closure.

Compatible cofiltered cover tower; recovered finite-level Π-actions; closed stabilizers.

Intersect point stabilizers. Compare membership with fixing every finite level; cofinal restriction leaves the intersection unchanged. For component inertia separately forget the component log structure; its kernel can still act nontrivially on that log structure.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.Anabelian.towerDecomposition`: Intersection of point stabilizers at every finite level.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.towerDecomposition.mem_iff`: An element belongs exactly when it fixes every `x_i`.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.towerDecomposition.conjugate`: Transporting the tower by a conjugates the subgroup by a.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.towerDecomposition.cofinal`: A cofinal compatible subsystem computes the same subgroup.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.towerDecomposition.isClosed`: Closed finite-level stabilizers give a closed tower subgroup.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.Anabelian.towerDecomposition_singleton_test`: A one-level tower has exactly the point stabilizer.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.towerDecomposition_regular_test`: For one level with the regular left action of Π on itself, the stabilizer of 1 is the trivial subgroup.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.towerDecomposition_trivial_test`: For the action on a singleton, the tower stabilizer is the whole group.
- For a nonnormal point stabilizer, conjugation changes the subgroup while preserving its conjugacy class.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m96), Proposition 4.1, pp. 589–590; Proposition 5.2, pp. 594–595.

Use `MulAction.stabilizer`; [EtaleCohomologyFoundations](../EtaleCohomologyFoundations/README.md) §F.0.A1 (decomposition and inertia groups); [Admissible stable log-cover system](#nc-1-log-admissible-system); [Admissible coverings of pointed stable curves](#admissible-log-coverings).

### 3.3 Finite-field points, functions and addition

<a id="nc-1-finite-field-decomposition"></a>

**Recover finite-field tame point decomposition groups.** For a smooth geometrically connected affine hyperbolic curve U over a finite field k, its arithmetic tame group recovers its geometric kernel, arithmetic Frobenius, #k, compactification genus and number of geometric punctures, and the conjugacy classes of decomposition groups of all points of its smooth compactification, distinguishing punctures from interior points. The recovery is compatible with every open subgroup and finite constant extension.

k finite; U affine and hyperbolic; full geometric tame quotient with full `G_k` retained.

Use tame abelianization modulo torsion to identify the geometric kernel; Frobenius weights on prime-to-p abelianization recover #k and the type. Use Hurwitz to characterize covers extending étale over the compactification and Lefschetz traces to decide whether each cover has points over a finite constant extension. A section is geometric precisely when every associated finite cover has such a point; Kummer differences across all covers identify sections attached to one lifted point. Generate its decomposition group from these sections and distinguish a cusp by the multiplicity of splittings; invoke separated decomposition groups to obtain uniqueness.

**Checks.**

- The Frobenius generator is recovered, although `G_k≃Ẑ` alone does not recover #k.
- The compactification may be proper, but the input U is punctured; no claim reconstructs arbitrary proper finite-field curves here.

The construction and its conventions follow [Akio Tamagawa](#reference-t97), Proposition 2.8, Lemma 2.9 and Corollary 2.10, pp. 151–155; Propositions 3.3–3.5 and 3.7–3.8, Remark 3.6, pp. 156–162.

<a id="nc-1-linear-system-addition"></a>

**Recover addition from valuations and unit congruences.** Let `C_1,C_2` be smooth proper connected curves over algebraically closed fields, with function fields `F_i`. A multiplicative monoid isomorphism `Φ:F_1→F_2` and a bijection of their points that preserve each normalized valuation, identify chosen finite sets `S_i` of at least three points, and preserve `1+m_P at` every `P∈S_1` determine an additive Φ, hence a field isomorphism.

Valuations preserve their integral normalization; `Φ(0)=0`; `|S_1|≥3`; preservation of `1+m`, not only O×.

Riemann–Roch produces minimal functions with two-dimensional pole spaces and prescribed values `0,1,∞ at` three marked points. Preserving valuations identifies minimal pole spaces; local unit congruences recover the coefficients of ax+b and force addition on constants and the rational subfields generated by these minimal functions. Generic degree-g divisors and Abel-map birationality show these rational subfields multiplicatively generate F. Compatible evaluations on a dense set glue their ring maps, so addition holds on all of F.

**Checks.**

- On `P¹`, use marked `0,1,∞` and a coordinate to recover x↦ax+b.
- A valuation-preserving multiplicative map without the three unit-congruence conditions is not accepted as a field map.

The construction and its conventions follow [Akio Tamagawa](#reference-t97), Lemma 4.7, Definition 4.8 and Lemmas 4.9–4.11, 4.13 and 4.16, Claims 4.12 and 4.14–4.15, pp. 167–175.

Use [TauCetiRoadmap.AlgebraicCurves](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicCurves/README.md#layer-4-repartitions-weil-differentials-and-riemannroch); [TauCetiRoadmap.JacobianChallenge](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge/README.md#layer-d-the-relative-picard-functor-and-the-jacobian-scheme); [TauCetiRoadmap.AlgebraicCurves](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicCurves/README.md#layer-12-the-dictionary--function-fields--curves-and-the-comparison-contracts).

<a id="nc-1-finite-field-tame-isom"></a>

**Tame affine reconstruction over finite fields.** An isomorphism of the arithmetic tame fundamental groups of smooth geometrically connected affine hyperbolic curves over finite fields is induced by a unique isomorphism of their pointed universal tame covers. Hence scheme isomorphisms `U_1≃U_2` correspond bijectively to these group isomorphisms modulo inner automorphisms by the whole arithmetic tame group `Π_2`, which is the full deck group of the universal tame cover; refining this to geometric conjugacy needs the separate centre-freeness of the base. Field automorphisms of the finite constants may occur; k-linearity and cyclotomic degree are extra conditions used in log gluing.

Affine hyperbolic curves over finite fields; continuous tame group isomorphism; full arithmetic quotient.

Recover points, decomposition groups and Frobenius at every finite cover. Local and global function-field reciprocity identify the kernel of the restricted-product-to-abelian-group map with multiplicative global functions; transfer gives compatibility across covers. After passing to a cover with at least three geometric punctures, recover valuations and principal-unit congruences and apply linear-system addition. Intersect local rings to recover the affine scheme and its cover tower; Frobenius lifts topologically generate the arithmetic group, which verifies recovery of the given isomorphism.

**Checks.**

- The function-field map is additive and compatible with the given group map on every finite tame cover.
- Composing a group isomorphism with conjugation by an arithmetic (Frobenius-lifting) element of `Π_2` gives the same scheme isomorphism; the bijection is with classes modulo all of `Inn(Π_2)`, not modulo geometric conjugation only.

The construction and its conventions follow [Akio Tamagawa](#reference-t97), Lemma 4.1, p. 163; Theorem 4.3, Lemma 4.4 and Corollary 4.5 and Claim 4.6, pp. 164–168; completion of Lemma 4.16, p. 175.

### 3.4 Stable-log reconstruction of the special fibre

<a id="nc-1-cyclotomic-degree"></a>

**Cyclotomic calibration and reconstruction degree.** For an admissible group isomorphism between singular stable log curves over a finite field, compare its maps on the marked normalization-component cyclotomic inertia copies with their fixed cyclotomic identifications. The common scalar is the reconstruction-theoretic degree `d_RT∈p^Z⊂Q_{>0}`. Node comparison forces the component scalars to agree. Degree-one is a restriction on these calibrated identifications, not mere preservation of abstract inertia subgroups.

At least one special curve nonsmooth; admissible group isomorphism over the same tame base; calibrations fixed.

Recover the normalization-component tame groups and their branch inertias. Apply tame affine reconstruction to identify each scalar as a power of p. Use adjacency at nodes and connectedness to obtain one positive rational scalar.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.Anabelian.ReconstructionDegree`: Common calibrated scalar in `p^Z` for singular admissible isomorphisms.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.ReconstructionDegree.component_eq`: Every component gives the same scalar.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.ReconstructionDegree.comp`: Degrees multiply under composition and invert under inversion.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.ReconstructionDegree.one_iff`: Degree one means identity on all calibrated cyclotomic inertia copies.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.Anabelian.reconstructionDegree_identity_test`: The identity isomorphism has degree 1.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.reconstructionDegree_frobenius_test`: A relative Frobenius comparison has cyclotomic degree p and is excluded from degree-one reconstruction.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.reconstructionDegree_composition_test`: Composing degrees `p^a` and `p^b` gives `p^(a+b)`, with inverse `p^(-a)`.
- Independent inversion or prime-adic rescaling of one branch is rejected by the cyclotomic diagrams.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m96), §6, pp. 596–600; Lemma 7.1 and Theorem 7.2, pp. 602–605.

<a id="nc-1-sturdy-cover"></a>

**Cofinal sturdy orderly covers.** A stable log hyperbolic curve admits a cofinal system of orderly covers whose normalization components all have genus at least two. Further finite tame extensions and covers can separate the branch combinatorics and make the required nodes rational. These changes are tracked with descent data; they are not hypotheses silently imposed on the original curve.

M96 admissible system; residue characteristic p&gt;0.

Use stable-cover extension and the cofinal orderly criterion. Construct prime-to-p covers with genus growth on every component, then untangle the finitely many branch incidences. Take common refinements of the finitely many choices and retain deck actions for descent.

**Checks.**

- Every open co-admissible subgroup contains a sturdy orderly subgroup; characteristic two requires the source’s separate combinatorial argument.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m96), Definition 1.1, pp. 574–575; Lemma 2.9, pp. 585–587; Proposition 4.2, pp. 590–592.

**Recover ordinary special-fibre étale quotient.** The admissible arithmetic group intrinsically determines its ordinary special-fibre étale quotient, compatibly with component data and finite covers. A cyclic prime torsor lifts through `Z_ℓ` precisely when it kills the appropriate node inertia. Use Frobenius weight `q^m` to separate residual tame base ramification from ordinary étale torsors. Intersect the kernels across all covers to obtain the characteristic ordinary-special quotient.

**Recover node thickness and log gluing.** At a stable node with chart `xy=t^e`, the calibrated two branch inertia embeddings determine the full integer `e≥1` and the Kummer gluing torsor identifying the branch log structures. Express the characteristic monoid by `x+y=e·t` and the two inertia restriction maps using that integer. Recover e from the compatible cyclotomic embeddings, not from an abstract prime-to-p group alone. Recover the Kummer class of the gluing line/torsor from the two restrictions and assemble the log structures along the normalization conductor.

**Local generic isomorphisms have degree one.** A `G_K`-compatible isomorphism of arithmetic fundamental groups of proper hyperbolic curves over `K/ℚ_p` finite has p-adic and every ℓ-adic fundamental-class scalar equal to 1; on singular admissible reduction its reconstruction degree is also 1.

**Checks.**

- Only equality of already maps is concluded; arbitrary Tate-module morphisms need not be effective.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m99), Theorem 14.1, author-copy pp. 71–73; §15 proof, pp. 74–77; [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m96), §10, pp. 624–626.
