### 3.5 Centre-freeness of the geometric and local Galois groups

<a id="nc-1-geometric-centre-free"></a>

**Centre-freeness of hyperbolic geometric kernels.** For every smooth geometrically connected hyperbolic curve in characteristic zero, the geometric full profinite and pro-p fundamental groups are centre-free. Proper curves have genus≥2 and use surface pro-p groups; affine curves use nonabelian free pro-p groups of `rank 2g+r−1≥2`. The admissible stable-log geometric kernel in finite-field reconstruction is also centre-free after cofinal [Cofinal sturdy orderly covers](#nc-1-sturdy-cover) reduction.

Characteristic-zero curve type 2g−2+r&gt;0; the proper case has `r=0` and `g≥2`. The stable-log case uses its admissible cover family.

Descend to a finite characteristic-zero model, use algebraically closed base-extension invariance and Riemann existence, and transport the surface/free presentations. Apply the nonabelian free pro-p or negative-Euler-characteristic surface pro-p centre theorem to every open subgroup. A central element detected in an abelian pro-ℓ quotient of a closed central subgroup is detected in a pro-ℓ quotient of an open subgroup; this transfers centre triviality to the full profinite group. For the log geometric kernel, Artin–Schreier class killing makes the relevant maximal pro-p groups nonabelian free after sturdy covers; apply the same open-subgroup criterion.

**Checks.**

- Rank-two `Z_p²` is not included; genus≥2 is used.

The construction and its conventions follow [Akio Tamagawa](#reference-t97), Lemmas 1.5 and 1.8 and Proposition 1.11, pp. 144–146; [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m96), Lemma 7.3, pp. 605–606.

Use [TauCetiRoadmap.ProfiniteProPGroups](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteProPGroups/README.md#layer-7-demushkin-groups-their-invariants-and-the-orientation); [TauCetiRoadmap.ProfiniteProPGroups](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteProPGroups/README.md#layer-4-free-pro-p-and-pro-c-groups-on-finite-sets); [EtaleCohomologyFoundations](../EtaleCohomologyFoundations/README.md) §F.0.2 (finite étale Galois categories, paths and monodromy); [TauCetiRoadmap.ProfiniteCohomology](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology/README.md#layer-10-continuous-cohomology-in-all-degrees); [Cofinal sturdy orderly covers](#nc-1-sturdy-cover); [InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups](../InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups/README.md) §IG.1.3 (invariance under algebraically closed base extension in characteristic zero); [InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups](../InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups/README.md) §IG.3.1 (Riemann existence for punctured curves).

<a id="nc-1-local-galois-centre-free"></a>

**Local Galois centre-freeness.** For `K/ℚ_p` finite, `Z(G_K)=1`; the same holds for finitely generated extensions by induction on an Artin-neighborhood tower. This input is established before Hom reconstruction over sub-p-adic fields.

Full absolute Galois groups; local finite p-adic K or finitely generated p-adic extension.

The tame quotient has trivial centre by its Frobenius/cyclotomic semidirect description. Use local duality and degree-p unramified restriction to kill `H²` of wild inertia. Its nonabelian free pro-p structure (including the `H¹ rank` test) then kills a central element in the wild kernel. For finitely generated extensions use the centre-free geometric kernel and local base in the Artin-neighborhood induction.

**Checks.**

- Local Hom recovery needs this local case only; the sub-p-adic case depends on the already established finitely-generated reconstruction.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m99), Lemmas 15.6–15.7, author-copy pp. 79–80.

Use [TauCetiRoadmap.ProfiniteProPGroups](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteProPGroups/README.md#layer-4-free-pro-p-and-pro-c-groups-on-finite-sets); [TauCetiRoadmap.ProfiniteCohomology](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology/README.md#layer-10-continuous-cohomology-in-all-degrees); [EtaleCohomologyFoundations](../EtaleCohomologyFoundations/README.md) §F.0.A2 (the arithmetic exact sequence); [Centre-freeness of hyperbolic geometric kernels](#nc-1-geometric-centre-free); [Artin towers give étale `K(π,1)` examples](#nc-0-artin-neighbourhood); Layer 1, étale `k(π,1)` schemes and arithmetic paths; [TauCetiRoadmap.ClassFieldTheory](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory/README.md#layer-5-local-coefficients-the-brauer-group-the-local-invariant-and-duality); [TauCetiRoadmap.LocalFieldsRamification](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamification/README.md#layer-4-the-tame-quotient-of-the-absolute-galois-group); [Cofinal hyperbolic Artin neighbourhoods](#cofinal-artin-neighbourhoods).

### 3.6 Canonical relations

<a id="nc-1-canonical-relations"></a>

**Canonical relations with section multiplication.** For a smooth proper curve `C/K` put `V_C=H⁰(C,ω_C)`. For each `N≥1`, `R_N(C)` is the kernel of the multiplication `μ_N:V_C^⊗N→H⁰(C,ω_C^⊗N)`. A transported differential map `θ:V_Y→F_∞` preserves canonical relations exactly when `Ψ_N(θ^⊗N(R_N(Y)))=0` for every N, where `Ψ_N` is multiplication in the completed differential target. The LinearMap.ker supplies the kernel carrier.

Smooth proper curves; genuine canonical sheaf and section multiplication; completed targets with their multiplication.

Construct `μ_N` from the already-owned sheaf tensor and section operations. Use the kernel and provide permutation and field-base-change compatibility. Define transported relation vanishing degree by degree; testing only degree one or injectivity of `θ` does not suffice.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.Anabelian.CanonicalRelations`: Kernel of the canonical section multiplication `μ_N`.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.CanonicalRelations.mem_iff`: A tensor belongs exactly when its product section is zero.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.CanonicalRelations.baseChange`: Flat field extension transports the multiplication kernel with its tensor identifications.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.CanonicalRelations.transport_iff`: Relation preservation is equivalent to vanishing of the target multiplication on the image of each kernel.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.CanonicalRelations.factor`: Vanishing on the kernel factors the composite through the image of `μ_N`; do not assert `μ_N` surjective.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.Anabelian.canonicalRelations_degree_one_test`: For `N=1`, `μ_1` is identity and `R_1=0`.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.canonicalRelations_zero_product_test`: If `μ_N(r)=0`, every relation-preserving transported multiplication kills r.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.canonicalRelations_injection_test`: An injective linear map may send a tensor in `ker μ` to one with nonzero product; such a map fails `transport_iff`.
- For nonhyperelliptic curves, relations cut out the canonical image; hyperelliptic cases first pass to the source’s étale cover.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m99), §12, author-copy pp. 62–65; Corollary 13.4, pp. 68–69.

Use `LinearMap.ker`; [TauCetiRoadmap.StableReduction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction/README.md#layer-2-coherent-curve-theory-duality-and-positivity); [TauCetiRoadmap.AlgebraicCurves](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicCurves/README.md#layer-12-the-dictionary--function-fields--curves-and-the-comparison-contracts).

<a id="nc-1-completed-differential-comparison"></a>

**Completed toric differential comparison.** For `U=Spec K(X)`, write `H_U` for its geometric pro-p abelianization and `H_F=H_X^F` for the largest `Γ_K`-submodule of the proper curve’s abelianization `H_X` having no nonzero torsion-free quotient on which an open subgroup of `Γ_K` acts trivially (the part that potentially extends to a p-divisible group, as in [Formal Kummer geometry on disk covers](#nc-1-fi-geometric-section)). Push the point-inertia extension to its universal torsion-free cyclotomic quotient `H_T,U`, obtaining `0→H_T,U→H_T,X→H_F→0`. Its continuous dual `C_T,X` has a completed generalized-Jacobian Hodge–Tate comparison: after completed tensoring with `Ô_K`, the p-adic completion of the integers of an algebraic closure, and inverting p, it identifies with completed logarithmic differential terms with Tate twist (−1), together with the weight-zero term `F_0=H¹(𝒳,O_𝒳)` for the chosen stable integral model 𝒳. Projection to completed logarithmic differentials therefore has the weight-zero kernel; only the quotient by that kernel embeds. Finite-rank approximants, one for each closed point `℘≠x`, and one integral bound independent of ℘ permit completion. Tensor multiplication on the resulting completed differential space defines `Ψ_N`.

K p-adic finite; proper hyperbolic X; a stable `O_K`-model and a rational point after a common finite extension normalizes the inertia product. Keep completed tensor products, the p-adic completed direct sum dual to inertia, and inversion of p separate. `F_∞` denotes the space of log-differential sections over the pointed stable-model limit; the maps to it use its p-adic completion, written `F̂_∞`.

Describe the inertia product over all points other than the chosen point, then push to the universal torsion-free cyclotomic quotient and dualize the resulting exact extension. For each closed point `℘≠x`, identify x with ℘ to get a singular curve and its generalized Jacobian `J′_℘`; pass to its quotient `J_℘`, an extension of `J_X` by `G_m`, and pull it back along the Raynaud good-reduction cover of `J_X`. Faltings’ comparison for this good-reduction semi-abelian scheme gives an integral map `C_T,℘⊗Ô_K→(F_0⊗Ô_K)⊕(F_℘⊗Ô_K(−1))` with an inverse up to `p^n`, where n does not depend on ℘. Complete the finite-rank extension sums. Proposition 11.3 becomes an isomorphism after p-inversion, with differential summand `F̂_T,X(−1)` and weight-zero summand `F_0`; do not discard the latter before projecting. Embed the completed differential summand in `F̂_∞` with its lattice and torsion-free comparison, and identify the projection kernel as the weight-zero part. Define `Ψ_N` using multiplication of the completed log sections.

**Checks.**

- An ordinary uncompleted direct sum of point inertia or a varying comparison bound does not supply `F_∞`.
- The `F_0` summand survives in `C_T,X` after scalar extension and is killed by the differential projection; no injection of the whole `C_T,X` is claimed. The differential quotient becomes injective only after removing this kernel and making the stated scalar extension.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m99), Lemmas 11.1–11.2, the comparison `(∗)_℘` and Proposition 11.3, author-copy pp. 57–62.

### 3.7 Geometric sections and arithmetic line bundles

<a id="relative-hodge-tate-small-base"></a>

**Relative Hodge–Tate theory over a small logarithmic base.** Let K be a p-adic field with perfect residue field, `S=Spec R→Spec O_K` geometrically connected and smooth, and `D⊆S` a relative normal-crossings divisor, with S small: étale over `O_K[X₁,…,X_d]` with D the inverse image of `X₁⋯X_d=0`. Let R̄ be the normalisation of R in the maximal extension of `R⊗K̄` étale outside D, `Γ_R` its Galois group over `R_K`, `Δ_R` the kernel of `Γ_R→Γ_K`, and let hats denote p-adic completion and subscripts K tensoring with K. Then for every `j∈ℤ: (1) H⁰(Δ_R,R̂̄_K(j))=R̂_K̄(j)` and `H¹(Δ_R,R̂̄_K(j))=Ω_(S^log/O_K)⊗_R R̂_K̄(j−1)`; `(2) H⁰(Γ_K,R̂_K̄)=R̂_K`, `H¹(Γ_K,R̂_K̄)=R̂_K`, and `Hⁿ(Γ_K,R̂_K̄(j))=0` for `j≠0` and `n=0,1`; `(3) Hⁿ(Γ_R,R̂̄_K)=R̂_K` and `Hⁿ(Γ_R,R̂̄_K(−1))=0` for `n=0,1`. (4) For an r-pointed stable log curve `f^log:X^log→S^log` of genus g with `2g−2+r≥1`, let H be the `ℤ_p`-dual of the relative first étale cohomology of X over `U_K=(S∖D)_K`, a free `ℤ_p`-module of `rank 2g (r=0)` or `2g+r−1 (r>0)` with `Γ_R`-action, `H₀=(R¹f_*O_X)^∨` and `H₁=(f_*ω_(X^log/S^log))^∨`. There is a natural `Γ_R`-equivariant exact sequence `0→H₁⊗_R R̂̄_K(1)→H⊗_(ℤ_p)R̂̄_K→H₀⊗_R R̂̄_K→0`.

K p-adic with perfect residue field; (S,D) small; the curve stable with log structure pulled back from the moduli stack; all statements are rational (after `⊗K`), not integral.

(1) is Faltings' computation of almost étale Galois cohomology (Faltings 1988, §I, Theorem 4.4(i) for `H⁰` and (iv) for `H¹`, tensored with `K(j)`). (2) is Tate's computation for `R=O_K`, extended to `O_K`-flat R by the same argument. (3) follows from (1) and (2) by the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence for `1→Δ_R→Γ_R→Γ_K→1`. (4) is the Hodge–Tate part of Faltings' comparison theorem in the relative logarithmic setting; only the Hodge–Tate statement is needed, not the crystalline one, and a logarithmic version of Hyodo's relative Hodge–Tate decomposition gives an alternative proof.

**Checks.**

- For `S=Spec O_K` and `D=∅ (d=0)`, `Ω_(S^log/O_K)=0`, so (1) says `H¹(Δ_R,·)=0` and (2) is Tate's theorem: `H⁰(Γ_K,ℂ_p(j))=0` and `H¹(Γ_K,ℂ_p(j))=0` for `j≠0`, while both are K for `j=0`.
- For `P¹` minus three points `(g=0, r=3)`, `H₀=0` and `H₁` has `rank g+r−1=2`, so (4) says `H⊗R̂̄_K≅H₁⊗R̂̄_K(1)`: the boundary classes go to the `H₁` term with the twist (1), and H, of `rank 2g+r−1=2`, is `ℤ_p(1)²` as the dual of the boundary part of `H¹`.
- The statements are about `R̂̄_K`, not the integral R̂̄; integral bounds are the subject of the next target, in good reduction only.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m99), §2, opening setup, p. 19; Lemmas 2.1–2.3, p. 20; Proposition 2.4 and its proof, p. 21; [Gerd Faltings](#reference-faltings1988), §I, Theorem 4.4, pp. 270–271.

Use [PadicPeriodRings](../PadicPeriodRings/README.md) §4.1 (topological period rings and structure maps); [PadicPeriodRings](../PadicPeriodRings/README.md) §§4.2–4.3 (period tensor invariants and admissibility); [De Rham exactness and Hodge–Tate grading](#linear-period-exactness); [EtaleCohomologyFoundations](../EtaleCohomologyFoundations/README.md) §F.0.A2 (the arithmetic exact sequence); [CrystallineCohomology](../CrystallineCohomology/README.md) Layers CR.5:log-algebra and CR.5 (logarithmic structures and logarithmic crystalline cohomology).

<a id="integral-hodge-tate-differentials"></a>

**Integral Hodge–Tate bounds for differentials in good reduction.** Let K be a p-adic local field and `n₀″` an integer with `v_p(𝔇_(K/ℚ_p))≤v_p(p^(n₀″))`; put `n₀′=n₀″+ord_p(g!)` and `n₀=n₀′+2`. Let `𝒢→Spec O_K` be a semi-abelian scheme of relative dimension g, an extension of an abelian scheme by a torus, so that 𝒢 has a smooth compactification with normal-crossings boundary. Let `L⊇K` be a p-adic field whose residue field is a function field in one variable over the residue field k of K, with k algebraically closed in it and `m_K O_L=m_L`, and `Γ_(L/K)=ker(Γ_L→Γ_K)`. Then: (1) the `Γ_K`-module `H¹(𝒢_K̄,K̄^∧)` is Hodge–Tate; if `H^Ω_𝒢` denotes the quotient of `H¹(𝒢_K̄,Ô_K̄(1))` by its weight-one part and `Ω^inv_𝒢` the invariant differentials, there is a natural `Γ_K`-equivariant map `Ω^inv_𝒢⊗_(O_K)(p^(n₀)O_K̄/p^(n₀+n)O_K̄)→H^Ω_𝒢⊗ℤ/pⁿ` with an inverse up to the factor `p^(n₀)`, for every `n≥1`. (2) The quotient `H^Ω_L` of `H¹(Γ_(L/K),Ô_L(1))` by its torsion is p-adically separated, and there is a natural `Γ_K`-equivariant map `Ω_(O_L/O_K)⊗(p^(n₀)O_K̄/p^(n₀+n)O_K̄)→H^Ω_L⊗ℤ/pⁿ` with an inverse up to `p^(n₀)`. (3) These maps are compatible with a morphism `Spec O_L→𝒢`: differentiating it on the left corresponds to the map on `H¹` on the right. The constant `n₀` depends only on K and g, not on n, on L, or on the morphism.

`K/ℚ_p` finite; 𝒢 semi-abelian over `O_K` (good reduction for the compactified group); L as stated. The bad-reduction version of Faltings' argument has gaps and gives only rational results, so it is not used.

Faltings 1988, §II, Theorems 2.4 and 3.1 give (1) for a smooth `O_K`-scheme with normal-crossings compactification, with the denominator `g!·ρ`, where `ρ` is controlled by the different of K and by the tame ramification allowed; the extra 2 in `n₀` absorbs `1/(p−1)≤1` and `(e−1)/e<1`. Faltings 1988, §I, Theorem 4.2 gives (2) for the one-dimensional relative situation `O_L/O_K`, and separatedness is its torsion-free quotient statement. (3) is the functoriality of Faltings' construction for the morphism `Spec O_L→𝒢`. Apply these to the semi-abelian group attached to the Jacobian (whose p-adic completion agrees with that of the Jacobian's semi-abelian model) as in the convergence argument for nondegenerate sections.

**Checks.**

- For `K=ℚ_p (n₀″=0)` and `g=1`, `n₀=ord_p(1)+2=2`: the inverse loses at most `p²`, independently of n; a bound growing with n would not give the convergence statement (∗)ind.
- For `p≤g`, `ord_p(g!)>0` and the loss increases; for `g<p` it does not depend on g.
- Replacing 𝒢 by the Jacobian of a curve with bad reduction is excluded: only rational statements are available there.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m99), §9, the Remark and consequences (1)–(3) of Faltings' theory, p. 51, and their use in proving (∗)ind, pp. 49–52; [Gerd Faltings](#reference-faltings1988), §I, Theorem 4.2, pp. 268–269; §II, Theorem 2.4, p. 283, and Theorem 3.1, p. 288.

Use [Relative Hodge–Tate theory over a small logarithmic base](#relative-hodge-tate-small-base); [NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties](../NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties/README.md) §§3.13–3.14 (Raynaud extensions and polarized uniformization); [FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory](../FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory/README.md) Layer R07 (integral p-adic Hodge theory of p-divisible groups).

<a id="nc-1-weight-zero-quotient"></a>

**Weight-zero two-step quotient.** For a proper hyperbolic curve over a p-adic field or its smooth relative family, let M be the two-step `ℚ_p` Malcev Lie algebra of its geometric pro-p group, `H=M^ab` and `H_0` its weight-zero Hodge–Tate quotient. Push the commutator part to `Λ²H_0`, obtaining `U_X`. Its inverse `image B_X` of the weight-one part of H has a unique equivariant projection onto `Λ²H_0`. Quotient `U_X` by that projection’s kernel to obtain `0→Λ²H_0→Z_X→H_0→0`. This is the specific Layer 3 quotient, not a new general unipotent fundamental group.

p-adic relative Hodge–Tate comparison; two-step Malcev quotient from Layer 2; genus at least two for the splitting test.

For proper curves the kernel of `Λ²H→M^[1]` is the dual cup-product line; its image in `Λ²H_0` vanishes. Use separated Hodge–Tate weights to split `B_X` equivariantly over the completed geometric base ring. Take the kernel quotient and retain its exact sequence and section-dependent arithmetic action; the underlying quotient is independent of geometric inner conjugation.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.Anabelian.WeightZeroTwoStep`: The canonical quotient `Z_X` and its exact extension by `Λ²H_0`.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.WeightZeroTwoStep.comm_quotient`: The two-step commutator quotient maps to `Λ²H_0`, with the proper-curve cup relation killed.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.WeightZeroTwoStep.inner_independent`: Geometric inner conjugation yields the canonical same underlying weight-zero extension.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.WeightZeroTwoStep.section_action`: A section induces the arithmetic action; its change is described by the wedge defect.

**Checks.**

- `TauCeti.Anabelian.weightZero_affine_relation_test`: For an affine curve the two-step commutator relation kernel is zero; for a proper curve it is the single dual cup line.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.weightZero_wedge_test`: For `dim H_0≥2` and `δ≠0`, some v has `δ∧v≠0`, so the translated section does not preserve a splitting.
- `TauCeti.Anabelian.weightZero_inner_test`: Conjugate geometric-basepoint choices identify the underlying extension without asserting equal chosen section actions.
- Keep the geometric and arithmetic actions distinct: a section changes the arithmetic action on `Z_X`.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m99), Lemma 3.1, Definitions 3.2 and 3.4, author-copy pp. 22–27.

Use Layer 2, unipotent fundamental groups and their realizations; [Relative Hodge–Tate theory over a small logarithmic base](#relative-hodge-tate-small-base); [Integral Hodge–Tate bounds for differentials in good reduction](#integral-hodge-tate-differentials); [TauCetiRoadmap.ProfiniteCohomology](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology/README.md#layer-12-the-graded-cup-product-in-all-degrees); [EtaleCohomologyFoundations](../EtaleCohomologyFoundations/README.md) §F.0.A2 (the arithmetic exact sequence); [EtaleCohomologyFoundations](../EtaleCohomologyFoundations/README.md) §§0.11, F.5–F.6 (trace, Poincaré duality and purity); [Two-step geometric Malcev quotient](#two-step-malcev).

<a id="nc-1-j-geometric-section"></a>

**Jacobian-geometric section test.** Over any finite extension K′ of K with `Pic¹(K′)≠∅` (for instance one over which X has a point), the degree-one Picard arithmetic extension has a canonical weight-zero geometric section, independent of the chosen `Pic¹(K′)` point up to conjugation by the weight-zero quotient. A section of the curve or generic-point arithmetic group over `Γ_K` is J-geometric when, after restriction to `Γ_K′`, its induced weight-zero `Pic¹` section equals that canonical section. Restriction is injective on `H¹` of the weight-zero quotient, so the condition does not depend on K′ and, when `Pic¹(K)≠∅`, agrees with the test over K itself. For `K/ℚ_p` finite with `Pic¹(K)≠∅` it means that the abelianized section comes from a `Pic¹(K)` point, not necessarily an `X(K)` point.

Proper genus-at-least-two curve; p-adic Hodge–Tate realization; `Pic¹` torsor, with its possible lack of K-points retained.

**Formal Kummer geometry on disk covers.** Let S′ normalize the disk `Spec O_K[[t]]` in a finite extension of its function field. An irreducibly splittable proper hyperbolic curve family becomes a constant curve `Z/K′` with `Z(K′)` nonempty after this extension; `S′→Spec O_(K′)` has a section and geometrically irreducible fibres. For its geometric abelianization `H_X`, let `H_X^I` be the quotient by potentially cyclotomic submodules, `H_X^F` the largest submodule with no nonzero potentially trivial torsion-free quotient, and `H_X^FI` the image of `H_X^F` in `H_X^I`. For a section whose constant-family map factors through `Γ_(S′)`, subtract a constant geometric Picard section to obtain `δ∈H¹(S′_K,H_X)`. F-geometry means `δ` lies, up to a nonzero integer multiple, in the image of the formal Kummer `subgroup H¹_f(S′_K,H_X^F)`. FI-geometry means its image in `H¹(S′_K,H_X^I)` similarly lies in the image of `H¹_f(S′_K,H_X^FI)`. These are predicates on this family and section, not on an arbitrary representation.

Subtract the canonical constant geometric Picard section in `H¹` and define the two conditions using its F and FI terms. Retain saturation and finite-base-change compatibility; never identify FI and F without the irreducibly-splittable theorem.

### 3.8 Tame points, Frattini towers and curve-map effectivity

<a id="nc-1-tame-point-existence"></a>

**Prime-to-p line bundles yield tame points.** Let M be a complete mixed-characteristic DVR field with residue field `k((t))`, where k is finite of characteristic p. A proper hyperbolic M-curve with a line bundle of degree prime to p has a point over a finite tame extension `M′/M`. If `L⊂M` has the same uniformizer, `k_L` is a one-variable function field over k, and `k_L→k((t))` is completion at a k-valued point, then for a curve defined over L a tame point over M′ descends to a tame extension `L′/L` of the same ramification index.

Complete mixed-characteristic DVR fields with the compatible integral-ring inclusion `m_L O_M=m_M`; the indicated residue completion at a k-valued point; line degree prime to p; regular proper model over `O_L`.

Take a sufficiently ample prime-to-p power and a separable Bertini divisor. Choose a closed point of degree prime to p. In its Galois closure, normality of the wild pro-p kernel puts it inside every conjugate of the point stabilizer (each contains a p-Sylow subgroup); the faithful action forces that kernel to vanish, giving a tame extension. Use a regular model, geometric regularity of the residue completion and Hensel lifting to compare tame points with their exact ramification index.

**Checks.**

- The residue field here is a function field; the local finite-residue Galois-group roadmap cannot stand in for these DVR results.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m99), Proposition 8.1 and Lemma 8.2, author-copy pp. 45–46.

<a id="nc-1-canonical-cover-descent"></a>

**Canonical covers descend the tower point.** The compatible point supplied above is defined over L, and its decomposition section recovers `α`. In characteristic zero a connected cyclic étale cover of degree greater than two of a proper hyperbolic curve is nonhyperelliptic; an étale cover of a nonhyperelliptic curve is nonhyperelliptic. This permits canonical embeddings throughout a cofinal cover tower.

Nondegenerate `α`; tame points on every Frattini cover; characteristic-zero canonical maps. For each fixed cover level n the p-primary component-group bound is uniform in the deeper sequence index m; a field extension may depend on n but not on m.

The limiting canonical image is uniquely determined by `α` and defined over L. For each fixed cover n, bound the p-primary component-group defect uniformly over `m≥n`. Enlarge the constants by a field depending on n but independent of m, obtain the unique limiting canonical image, and descend that image to L by its α-characterization. Pass to a nonhyperelliptic étale cover, where the canonical map is an embedding; descend the unique points and their compatibilities.

**Checks.**

- A genus-two curve is hyperelliptic, so the proof cannot start by embedding it canonically.
- This is a theorem for the specified nondegenerate sections with points on every cover, not the section conjecture.
- No single component-group bound or auxiliary field extension is asserted for all n; only each fixed-n limit is uniform in m.

<a id="nc-1-canonical-relation-vanishing"></a>

**Arithmetic maps preserve all canonical relations.** An open relative generic-point pro-p homomorphism induces an injective differential map `θ:H⁰(Y,ω_Y)→F̂_∞` for which `Ψ_N(θ^⊗N(R_N(Y)))=0` for every N.

`K/ℚ_p` finite; proper hyperbolic target; compatible generic-point input; all disk normalizations retain a section and geometric irreducibility.

If a transported relation were nonzero, choose a stable marked blowup and a generic special component where its differential pullback `κ_L` is nonzero. For the particular normalized disk family, prove normality by the geometrically regular completion comparison of Lemma 13.1. For a nodal chart `xy=π^e` over its regular base, the divisor of `x−s_x` is the graph plus vertical components; those components are Q-Cartier and the irreducible-fibre hypothesis controls the branches. Lemma 13.3 therefore makes the graph Q-Cartier. This is a special calculation, not a general assertion about Weil divisors on normal schemes. Its formal Jacobian class makes the source section F/FI-geometric. Every target Frattini cover receives a prime-to-p line bundle and a tame point; nondegeneracy and tower-point descent make the transported section geometric over L. Evaluation at that geometric point forces the purported relation to vanish, contradicting the chosen component.

**Checks.**

- Verify every degree N; an injection of `H⁰` spaces without this property does not imply a curve map.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m99), Proposition 12.1, Lemmas 13.1–13.3 and Corollary 13.4, author-copy pp. 62–69.

<a id="nc-1-inertia-and-regularity"></a>

**Annihilate inertia and recover regular differentials.** The differential map induced by an open generic-point homomorphism to `Π_Y` lands in `H⁰(X,ω_X)`, and the group homomorphism factors through `Π_X` when X is a smooth proper source. Residues of the transported differentials vanish at every closed point.

Proper hyperbolic X,Y; target replaced by a nonhyperelliptic finite étale cover when needed; relation preservation already proved.

A nonzero residue at x forces nontrivial image of its inertia. Choose a finite target p-cover detecting that inertia and pull it back to a ramified source cover at x′. Canonical relations place the residue projective point on the canonically embedded target cover. The ramification stabilizer fixes this point, contradicting the free action on an étale target cover; all residues vanish and the map factors through the proper-source group.

**Checks.**

- The argument detects nontrivial inertia on a finite cover; killing only its abelianization is insufficient.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m99), Theorem 14.1 proof, author-copy pp. 69–72; Lemma 15.2, pp. 74–76.

**Effectivity of the recovered canonical map.** An injective K-linear map on canonical differentials obtained above, preserving all canonical relations and the finite-cover compatibilities, determines a dominant K-map `X→Y`. For nonhyperelliptic Y its canonical ideal gives the function-field embedding, which extends uniquely over the proper smooth source; a cofinal nonhyperelliptic cover handles general Y.

Use the canonical ring/image and relation ideal to obtain a rational map into Y’s canonical image. Compare function fields via the scheme/function-field dictionary and extend through the regular proper curve. Descend the nonhyperelliptic-cover morphism with its deck action. Repeat on all p-covers to identify its relative outer pro-p homomorphism with the prescribed one.

### 3.9 Hom and Isom theorems over p-adic and number fields

<a id="hyperbolic-hom-schemes"></a>

**Dominant maps between proper hyperbolic curves.** Let M be a noetherian integral scheme over `ℚ` and `X→M`, `Y→M` proper smooth curves with geometrically connected fibres of genus at least two. The functor of M-morphisms `X→Y` is represented by a scheme `Hom_M(X,Y)` locally of finite type over M. Its open and closed subscheme `H_M=Hom^dom_M(X,Y)` of fibrewise nonconstant morphisms is finite and unramified over M. Consequently, after shrinking M to a dense open subscheme, `H_M` is finite étale over M, and a nonconstant morphism on one fibre over the shrunken M lifts to a morphism `X_L→Y_L` over a finite extension L of the function field. The constant morphisms form the separate component Y, which is not finite over M and is excluded.

M noetherian, integral, of characteristic zero; X, Y proper smooth with geometrically connected fibres of genus `≥2` (proper hyperbolic). The open-curve variant needs the logarithmic tangent bundle and is not stated here.

Representability: the graph of a morphism is a closed subscheme of `X×_MY`, so Hom is an open subscheme of the Hilbert scheme of `X×_MY`. Unramified: the tangent space of Hom at a nonconstant `f:X_m→Y_m` is `H⁰(X_m,f*T_(Y_m))`, which vanishes because `f*T_(Y_m)` has degree `(2−2g_Y)·deg f<0`. Quasi-finite: the Riemann–Hurwitz formula bounds deg f by `(2g_X−2)/(2g_Y−2)`, which bounds the Hilbert polynomial of the graph. Proper: extend a nonconstant generic-fibre map over a discrete valuation ring. Such a map can be ramified, so extension of finite étale covers alone does not suffice. Resolve the rational map from the smooth relative curve; the exceptional curves are rational and map constantly to the smooth hyperbolic target, which has no rational curves. Descent across the resolution extends the map, and its positive degree is preserved. This gives the valuative criterion for the dominant Hom locus; Lemma 8.3 supplies the finite étale special case used in reconstruction. In characteristic zero a finite unramified morphism is étale over a dense open subscheme.

**Checks.**

- For `X=Y` a curve of genus 2 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, Riemann–Hurwitz gives `deg f≤1`, so `H=Aut(X)`, a finite reduced scheme (of order at least 2, the hyperelliptic involution).
- For a constant map f, `f*T_Y` is trivial and `H⁰` is one-dimensional: constant maps are not unramified points, which is why they are excluded.
- For an elliptic curve E (genus 1, not hyperbolic) the translations give a positive-dimensional `Hom^dom(E,E)`; the genus hypothesis cannot be dropped.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m99), the paragraph after Lemma 15.2, author-copy p. 76; [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m96), Lemma 8.3 and its proof, pp. 610–611.

<a id="nc-1-local-pro-p-hom"></a>

**Local relative pro-p Hom theorem.** For proper hyperbolic curves X,Y over `K/ℚ_p` finite, dominant K-morphisms `X→Y` correspond bijectively to continuous open relative homomorphisms `Π_X^(p)→Π_Y^(p)` over `G_K`, modulo target `Δ_Y^(p)` inner conjugation. The generic-source form says that every continuous open relative map from `Π_(K(X))` to `Π_Y^(p)` determines a dominant rational K-map X⇢Y, which extends over the proper smooth source and factors the group map through `Π_X^(p)`.

K p-adic finite; fixed p; geometric relative quotients; proper genus≥2; dominant equals nonconstant.

For surjective image first use generic-point J-geometry, canonical relation preservation and effectivity. An open image is the group of a connected finite étale target cover after the compatible field adjustment; recover the morphism to this cover and descend. Use finite-cover comparisons and faithfulness to prove uniqueness and recovery of the original group map. Base Galois centre-freeness makes the recovery conjugator geometric.

**Checks.**

- Source-generic and proper-curve cases are distinguished; constants fail the open-image condition.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m99), Theorem 14.1 and Corollary 14.2, author-copy pp. 71–73.

<a id="nc-1-punctured-elliptic-isom"></a>

**Punctured elliptic reconstruction for the centre argument.** For K finitely generated over `ℚ_p` and elliptic K-curves E,F, put `U=E−{0}` and `V=F−{0}`. Every continuous isomorphism `Π_U^(p)≃Π_V^(p)` of the punctured curves’ arithmetic groups over `G_K`, modulo target geometric inner conjugation, induces a unique K-isomorphism `U≃V`. It extends to an isomorphism of the smooth proper compactifications, so `j(E)=j(F)`.

One puncture on each elliptic curve; full `G_K` retained; quotient by geometric inner conjugation; no use of sub-p-adic centre-freeness.

Choose cofinal p-power étale covers ramified to arbitrarily high order at the punctures. After refinement, the compactifications of source and target have genus at least two, as measured by Hurwitz. Compose with the generic-source and proper-target quotients and apply the finitely-generated generic-point reconstruction to the compactifications. Compare with covers whose puncture ramification exceeds the recovered map degree. Since the pulled-back cover is étale on the source affine curve, the map cannot hit a target puncture there. Apply the same construction to the inverse and descend compatible deck actions; uniqueness gives inverse affine maps and hence the compactification isomorphism.

**Checks.**

- A proper genus-one Isom theorem is not asserted; removing the origin supplies hyperbolicity.
- This helper precedes the sub-p-adic centre argument, avoiding a dependency on Corollary 15.5.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m99), Corollary 14.2 and its proof, author-copy p. 73; Corollary 15.3, p. 77; application in Lemma 15.8, p. 80.

<a id="nc-1-galois-centre-free"></a>

**Centre-freeness needed for geometric conjugacy.** Absolute Galois groups of p-adic local fields, finitely generated extensions of `ℚ_p` and sub-p-adic fields have trivial centre. Consequently, a conjugator between two homomorphisms over the identity of `G_K` has trivial image in `G_K` whenever the source arithmetic projection is surjective.

Sub-p-adic K with chosen embedding; full `G_K`, not its pro-p quotient.

For continuous homomorphisms f,g over a surjective source projection and a centre-free base G, if `g(x)=a f(x) a⁻¹` for every x, then a lies in the target projection kernel. Projecting the conjugacy identity and using surjectivity makes the image of a central.

For p-adic K use the tame quotient and cohomological freeness/nonabelianity of wild inertia. For finitely generated extensions induct with an Artin-neighborhood/free-curve sequence. If a central element acts nontrivially on a finite Galois extension generated by `α`, choose an elliptic curve with `j=α` and remove its origin. Over a finitely generated p-adic composite field, the punctured-elliptic Isom helper identifies this curve with its conjugate, forcing `α` to equal its moved value. Project the conjugacy relation to `G_K`; its surjective source forces the conjugator’s image to be central.

**Checks.**

- Do not invoke sub-p-adic centre-freeness in the earlier finitely-generated proof; separate the local and finitely-generated cases to avoid a logical cycle.
- For an abelian nontrivial base and the identity extension, every base element conjugates the identity map to itself, although only the identity is geometric. Centre-freeness is essential.
- Surjectivity is essential: with trivial source and centre-free base `S₃`, every target element conjugates the unique source map, including elements with nonidentity base image.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m99), Lemmas 15.6–15.8, author-copy pp. 79–80.

<a id="nc-1-number-field-isom"></a>

**Number-field profinite Isom theorem.** For a number field K and smooth geometrically connected proper K-curves X,Y of genus at least two, `Isom_K(X,Y)→RelativeOuterIsom(Π_X→G_K,Π_Y→G_K)` is bijective. No rational point on either curve is assumed.

Full profinite groups; continuous equivalences over the identity of `G_K`; quotient by target geometric inner conjugation.

Spread the curves and their finite unramified Isom scheme over a localization of `O_K`, then shrink it to finite étale; fix `ℓ` invertible there. At closed primes, local special-fibre reconstruction supplies the unique log isomorphism with the prescribed ℓ-adic action. Lift through the finite étale Isom scheme after a finite extension of K; faithfulness and equivariance supply the Galois cocycle and descend the resulting curve isomorphism. Perform the comparison on every finite étale cover to recover the entire original group isomorphism, then use centre-freeness of `G_K` to make the conjugator geometric.

**Checks.**

- For the genus-two curve `y²=x⁵−1` over Q, identity and the hyperelliptic involution produce distinct classes.
- The proof descends without assuming `X(K)` nonempty.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m96), Theorems 10.1–10.2 and §10 proof, pp. 624–626.

### 3.10 Relative extension comparison

<a id="centre-free-extension-pullback"></a>

**Centre-free extension pullback.** For a topologically finitely generated profinite centre-free group `Δ` and an exact profinite extension `1→Δ→Π→G→1`, construct `Π≃Aut_cont(Δ)×_(Out_cont(Δ))G` by conjugation and the extension's outer action. The fibre-product topology is the one; prove this is an isomorphism of profinite groups over G and on `Δ`. For two such extensions, identify relative outer isomorphisms with outer-equivariant isomorphisms of geometric kernels in the scope where extension recovery gives the comparison.

`Δ` is centre-free and topologically finitely generated. Use the continuous `Aut/Out` topology, rather than a discrete abstract automorphism group.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `centreFreeExtension.pullbackEquiv`: Give the extension isomorphism over G.
- `centreFreeExtension.kernel`: Identify `Δ` with inner automorphisms.
- `centreFreeExtension.outerMap`: Give the relative/geometric comparison for isomorphisms, over the fixed arithmetic quotient.

**Checks.**

- For `G=1`, the fibre product is `Inn(Δ)≃Δ`.
- A nontrivial central kernel invalidates injectivity of conjugation.
- An abstract automorphism lacking continuity is excluded.

The construction and its conventions follow [Akio Tamagawa](#reference-t97), §7A, Lemma 7.1 and its pullback proof, printed p. 188.

### 3.11 Arithmetic and geometric Isom; sub-p-adic and full profinite Hom

<a id="nc-1-geometric-outer-comparison"></a>

**Arithmetic and geometric formulations of Isom.** For these number-field curves, restriction identifies relative outer arithmetic isomorphisms over `G_K` with geometric group isomorphisms `Δ_X≃Δ_Y` modulo target `Δ_Y` inner automorphisms whose outer classes intertwine the two `G_K` outer actions. The fixed `G_K` is not allowed to vary. Composed with the number-field Isom theorem, this gives M96 Theorem `10.2: Isom_K(X,Y)→Out_ρ(Δ_X,Δ_Y)` is bijective.

Proper hyperbolic curves; centre-free topologically finitely generated profinite geometric kernels; fixed profinite arithmetic extensions over `G_K`.

Use the centre-free extension pullback constructed in Layer `3: Π≃Aut_cont(Δ)×_(Out_cont(Δ))G_K`, with its continuous inverse. An outer-equivariant geometric isomorphism extends over the identity of `G_K`; changing its representative changes the extension by target geometric conjugation. Restriction gives the inverse comparison. An intertwining geometric equivalence therefore extends over the identity of `G_K`, uniquely up to geometric inner equivalence. Restrict back and check the two identifications, using the generic continuous outer-action interfaces.

**Checks.**

- The conclusion is exactly outer equivariance; it does not assert an equality of chosen lifts `G_K→Aut(Δ)`.
- The comparison itself is group theory; the dependency on [Number-field profinite Isom theorem](#nc-1-number-field-isom) is used only for the composite Theorem 10.2 form.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m96), Theorem 7.4, p. 607; Theorem 10.2, p. 626; [Akio Tamagawa](#reference-t97), §7A, Lemma 7.1 and its pullback proof, p. 188.

<a id="nc-1-sub-p-adic-hom"></a>

**Sub-p-adic relative pro-p Hom theorem.** A sub-p-adic field K is a field admitting an embedding into a finitely generated extension of `ℚ_p`. For every such K and proper hyperbolic K-curves, dominant maps correspond bijectively to open relative geometric pro-p Hom classes over `G_K`. In particular every number field is sub-p-adic via a completion at a place above p.

Chosen embedding `K→L` with L finitely generated over `ℚ_p`; arithmetic groups retain the entire `G_K`; no finite generation of K itself.

`anabelian_isom` states the equivalent full finite-étale-category Isom form for proper hyperbolic curves over every such K. It uses Mathlib’s `MorphismProperty.Over` with property `AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite ⊓ AlgebraicGeometry.Etale`, so its objects are the actual finite étale scheme maps and its arrows are scheme maps over the curve. Given an equivalence from the covers of X to those of Y, and a natural isomorphism between the induced constant-cover functors, there is a unique K-isomorphism `f:X≅Y` whose inverse-pullback functor is naturally isomorphic to that equivalence. Smooth relative dimension one, properness, geometric connectedness, finite-dimensional coherent `H¹` and genus at least two are explicit hypotheses. The embedding of K into L and finite field-generation of L over `ℚ_p` express the sub-p-adic condition. By the finite Galois-category equivalence this is the profinite relative Isom theorem; centre-freeness of `G_K` identifies the categorical conjugacy with the geometric conjugacy for maps over the fixed quotient. No rational point on X or Y is required.

Restrict the relative group map to `G_L` and reconstruct an L-morphism using the finitely-generated result. Define it over an intermediate finite Galois extension `K′/K` using the finite unramified dominant Hom scheme. `G_K`-equivariance, uniqueness and all-cover compatibility supply its descent cocycle to K.

**Checks.**

- For `K=Q`, embed into `ℚ_p` and recover maps over Q after `G_Q` descent, not merely over `ℚ_p`.
- For a genus-two curve, the identity and hyperelliptic involution give distinct cover-equivalence classes, so uniqueness does not collapse its automorphism group.
- Compatibility with constant covers is essential: an arbitrary equivalence of geometric cover categories over an algebraic closure does not recover the K-curve. Curves of the same genus have isomorphic geometric profinite groups.
- The categorical Isom form retains curves with no K-rational point; a rational fibre functor is not an extra hypothesis.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m99), Definition 15.4 and Corollary 15.5, author-copy pp. 77–79. The full profinite form is Theorem 16.5 and its following remark, author-copy p. 85, with the finite-cover interpretation supplied by Stacks Theorem 58.6.2 (0BND).

<a id="nc-1-full-profinite-hom"></a>

**Number-field full profinite Hom theorem.** For a number field K and proper smooth geometrically connected curves X,Y of genus≥2, `Hom_K^dom(X,Y)→RelativeOuterHom_open(Π_X→G_K,Π_Y→G_K)` is bijective. The input is the full profinite group, the homomorphism is continuous with open image, and only target geometric conjugacy is removed.

Number field K; dominant/nonconstant K-maps; full arithmetic groups; no section conjecture.

Descend the full relative homomorphism to its geometric pro-p quotient and use sub-p-adic Hom reconstruction to obtain a unique K-map. For every finite étale target cover, including covers of degree not a p-power, pull it back along the original full homomorphism and repeat the pro-p reconstruction on that cover. The resulting compatible maps identify the full original homomorphism with the induced map, up to target arithmetic conjugacy; centre-freeness of `G_K` makes that conjugacy geometric. Injectivity follows from the pro-p theorem and faithfulness.

**Checks.**

- A K-isomorphism of the two curves gives an isomorphism of their arithmetic extensions over the same `G_K`, and its inverse is reconstructed too.
- It is insufficient to compare only p-power covers in the full-profinite conclusion.
- For `y²=x⁵−1` over Q the identity is recovered; constant maps are absent.

The construction and its conventions follow [Shinichi Mochizuki](#reference-m99), Theorem 16.5 and its full-profinite remark, author-copy pp. 85–87, restricted here to proper one-dimensional curves.

### Examples

An arithmetic reconstruction fixes the base quotient. If both extensions are the identity `Γ→Γ`, there is exactly one map over `Γ`. Quotienting by arbitrary automorphisms of `Γ` would introduce extra maps and change the relative Hom problem.

For a centre-free geometric kernel `Δ`, the extension pullback `Aut_cont(Δ)×_(Out_cont(Δ))G` identifies its kernel with `Inn(Δ)≃Δ`. When G is trivial, this recovers `Δ` itself. If `Δ` instead has a nontrivial centre, conjugation loses its central elements, so the proposed extension isomorphism cannot be injective. This is why centre-freeness is an input to the arithmetic/geometric outer comparison.

The admissible stable-cover degree inequality allows equality. The identity cover has local index `e=1` and degree `d=1`. An inequality e&lt;d would reject it. A cover may have component étale degree divisible by the residue characteristic while all marking and node indices are invertible; tameness is a local-index condition, rather than a prime-to-characteristic condition on the entire degree.

Dominant maps between fixed hyperbolic curves form the finite locus used in reconstruction. Constant maps to a positive-dimensional target vary with the target point, so the full Hom scheme need not be finite. The finite étale spreading argument first isolates the dominant generic locus and then shrinks the base. It cannot be applied to all maps at once.

A rational point of `Pic¹` is a relative Picard point. Its Brauer obstruction may prevent a representing line bundle. After a finite extension kills that obstruction, rational p-adic `H¹` restriction remains injective because restriction followed by corestriction is multiplication by the nonzero extension degree. The argument needs both operations; simply declaring the relative Picard point to be a divisor omits a real step.

Finite-field tame reconstruction, stable log special-fibre reconstruction and local geometrically pro-p Hom reconstruction keep different carriers. The local pro-p extension retains the full Galois quotient. The canonical line bundle obtained from the corrected stable-log relation is `K_Y`, with its degree and pole behavior; a symbol for an unspecified ample bundle would not give the canonical map required by the Hom argument.


For a continuous quotient q, a relative open representative into the identity quotient is forced to equal q. Existence of that representative additionally imposes openness of its image; uniqueness alone does not assert that every q has open image.

## Layer 4: Cohomology varieties and Selmer conditions

Pass from individual topological coefficient groups to algebra-valued unipotent points, effective filtered torsors and finite-type cohomology varieties. Form crystalline and unramified local conditions on every coefficient algebra before constructing global Selmer varieties.

### 4.1 Galois coefficient families

<a id="nc-3-galois-coefficient-family"></a>

**Galois coefficient family.** For a commutative ring K and a topological group G, a GaloisCoefficientFamily P assigns to each commutative K-algebra R a group with a Hausdorff point topology and an action of G by automorphisms. Require continuity of the action and of cochain operations on every finite power `G^n`: pointwise products, inverses, constant gauge translation and the ordered defect must preserve continuity. Each algebra map `f:R→S` gives a continuous equivariant group homomorphism `P(f)`, with identity and composition laws. A family of ordinary topological groups with jointly continuous actions is a special case. For arbitrary algebra-valued unipotent points use the compact-coordinate comparison below; no ordinary product-topology group instance is inferred from the final topology alone. This structure specifies no representability.

K is a commutative ring; G is a topological group. Fix universes for coefficient algebras and point types. Operations on continuous maps from `G^n` satisfy the stated continuity axioms. Ordinary topological-group coefficient families satisfy them for arbitrary G; the final-coordinate unipotent specialization assumes G compact Hausdorff.

Use CommAlgCat for coefficient changes and group and topology structures on each point type. Bundle the coefficient functor laws, equivariance, action continuity and cochain continuity. Define the cocycle subtype and its constant gauge action using these axioms. The compact coefficient comparison proves the axioms for the final coordinate topologies of geometric unipotent points; it is distinct from the ordinary topological-group specialization.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.NC3.GaloisCoefficientFamily.equivariance`: `P(f)(g·x)=g·P(f)(x)`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.NC3.GaloisCoefficientFamily.identity`: `P(id_R)(x)=x`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.NC3.GaloisCoefficientFamily.composition`: `P(g∘f)(x)=P(g)(P(f)(x))`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.NC3.GaloisCoefficientFamily.continuous`: `P(f)` is continuous in the supplied point topologies.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.NC3.GaloisCoefficientFamily.obj`: For each R, the point type `P(R)`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.NC3.GaloisCoefficientFamily.group`: The group structure on every `P(R)`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.NC3.GaloisCoefficientFamily.topology`: The point topology on every `P(R)`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.NC3.GaloisCoefficientFamily.action`: The G-action by group automorphisms on every `P(R)`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.NC3.GaloisCoefficientFamily.map`: Each algebra map gives the continuous group homomorphism `P(R)→P(S)`.

**Checks.**

- For `U=𝔾_a` and `R=E[ε]/ε²`, write points as `(a,b)=a+bε`; multiplication is `(a,b)+(c,d)=(a+c,b+d)`.
- For the Heisenberg group over this R, the (1,3)-entry of a product is `z+z′+xy′`; with `x=ε`, `y′=1` and `z=z′=0`, it is the nonzero element ε.
- For `R=E[t]`, augmentation `t↦0` sends the nonzero additive point t to zero, whereas the identity coefficient map fixes t.
- For trivial G-action, Z1 is the set of continuous homomorphisms, while H1 is its quotient by constant conjugation. The interface never substitutes Hom for this gauge quotient.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), Section 1, Lemmas 1–5, printed pp. 2–4.

### 4.2 Final topologies on unipotent points

<a id="unipotent-final-topology"></a>

**Finite-dimensional final topology on unipotent points.** For a characteristic-zero p-adic field E and every commutative E-algebra R, give each coordinate space `R^m` the final topology from its finite-dimensional E-vector subspaces with their usual topology. Transport the coordinate topology to split-unipotent `U(R)` independently of polynomial exponential coordinates. Prove continuity of polynomial maps between these coordinate spaces, inverses and coefficient maps. A compact-domain cochain has coordinate image in a finite-dimensional coefficient subspace, stable after enlarging the span for the finitely many products and defect maps used in central induction. Prove compact factorization without sequential compactness: an infinite-dimensional compact set would contain a countable linearly independent subset; every subset of that subset has finite intersection with each finite-dimensional subspace and is closed for the final topology. It would therefore be an infinite closed discrete compact subspace, a contradiction. Do not identify the final topology on `R^m` with an ordinary product topology without a product-compatibility theorem. For period algebras use their own topology and completed tensor products with a separate comparison.

Coordinate stages are finite-dimensional split unipotent groups, and algebra-valued continuous cochains use the declared final coordinate topology. Compact domains are arbitrary compact Hausdorff spaces, not only metrizable ones.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `unipotentPointTopology.independent`: Identify coordinate changes as homeomorphisms.
- `unipotentPointTopology.compactFactor`: Give the finite-dimensional compact factorization used by cochains.
- `unipotentPointTopology.polynomial`: Control polynomial maps and finite-product scalar extensions.
- `unipotentPointTopology.periodCompare`: State and prove the separate period-topology compatibility for each local condition.

**Checks.**

- For `R=E`, recover the usual finite-dimensional p-adic topology.
- For a finite extension E′, scalar extension is continuous and uses the E-vector-space topology.
- A sequential argument alone does not establish the compact-factorization statement for a nonmetrizable profinite domain.
- With infinitely many independent coordinate vectors, their set is closed discrete; it cannot lie in a compact image.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, Lemmas 1–4, preprint pp. 2–3; compact factorization uses the closed-discrete argument stated here in place of a subsequence argument.

Use [TauCetiRoadmap.ReductiveGroups](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups/README.md#layer-5-solvable-and-unipotent-groups-the-unipotent-radical); [Unipotent groups and their homogeneous quotients in characteristic zero](#split-unipotent-quotients).

<a id="compact-coefficient-cohomology"></a>

**Compact-coordinate cocycle comparison.** For compact Hausdorff G and split unipotent algebra-valued coefficients with the final coordinate topologies, construct the continuous cocycle subtype and its constant gauge action. Prove that ordered cocycle products, inverses, gauges, inner twists and central defects preserve continuity on every compact cochain domain `G^n`: combine finite-dimensional coordinate images, enlarge their finite coefficient span under the polynomial operations, and use the finite G-stable Hopf filtration for the semilinear action. Carry the orbit-set classification, coefficient functoriality and central obstruction calculation of Layer 0 through this compact-cochain interface. If the coefficient point group has an ordinary topological-group structure compatible with these topologies, identify this construction with the topological-group version; the abstract Layer 0 theorems retain their original generality. For arbitrary R, the all-algebra cohomology functor uses the compact-cochain construction, without assuming an ordinary product-topology group instance.

G is compact Hausdorff; the finite coordinate filtration is G-stable. Each operation is polynomial at finite unipotent depth and each cochain has finite-dimensional coordinate image. Period coefficient conditions additionally use their stated completed-topology comparison.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `compactCochain.operations`: Preserve continuous maps from compact domains under each ordered operation.
- `compactCochain.gauge`: Give the constant gauge action on continuous cocycles.
- `compactCochain.topologicalComparison`: Identify the orbit set with the ordinary topological-group construction when its product-compatibility hypothesis holds.
- `compactCochain.centralDefect`: Preserve the [Positive central defect](#nc-3-positive-defect) sign and its canonical additive `H²` comparison.
- `compactCochain.coefficient`: Preserve arbitrary algebra changes, including nonreduced coefficients.

**Checks.**

- For `R=E` the construction is the usual continuous nonabelian `H¹`.
- For `R=E[ε]/(ε²)`, retain the infinitesimal coordinates in products and gauges.
- For an algebra of uncountable E-dimension, test cocycle continuity on compact coordinate images; no countable-basis or convergent-subsequence argument enters.
- For the least-residue `C₉→C₃` lift, the defect at (2,1) remains 3 and its inverse remains 6.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, Lemmas 1–5 and Proposition 1, preprint pp. 2–7; compact-coordinate refinement of its cohomology construction.

### 4.3 Algebra-valued cohomology

<a id="nc-3-unipotent-point-topology"></a>

**Continuous unipotent points.** Instantiate the compact-cochain GaloisCoefficientFamily by `P_n(R)=U_n(B⊗_K R)`, using the smooth-unipotent Hopf/group-scheme dictionary and a finite-type filtered G-stable coordinate Hopf algebra. Here B is a complete Hausdorff characteristic-zero topological field with continuous semilinear G-action, `K⊂F=B^G` and [F:K]&lt;∞. For each coordinate power `(B⊗_K R)^m` use its final topology from finite-dimensional B-subspaces; chart transitions and coefficient maps are continuous in these declared coordinate topologies. Prove the action `G×P_n(R)→P_n(R)` continuous using compactness of G and the finite G-stable coordinate filtration. Prove all compact-cochain operation axioms by finite-dimensional factorization. A regular central vector quotient section is continuous on points. The final topology on a coordinate power is not identified with the ordinary product of its factors without a separate proof.

G compact Hausdorff B complete Hausdorff topological field with continuous field automorphism action K is a subfield of `F=B^G` and [F:K]&lt;∞. finite-type filtered Hopf coordinates with finite-rank G-stable filtration and compatible semilinear action.

### 4.4 Effective filtered torsor descent

<a id="effective-filtered-torsor-descent"></a>

**Effective filtered affine torsor descent.** For a finitely generated split pro-unipotent group with finite-dimensional filtered Hopf pieces, construct the equivalence between continuous algebra-valued cocycles modulo gauge and affine torsors with the specified semilinear G-action and locally free filtered coordinate algebra. The equivalence preserves the unit, coaction, filtration, finite-depth projection and coefficient extension. Prove the all-algebra comparison, including nonreduced algebras, before applying the represented cohomology functor.

Filtered pieces are locally free of the stated finite ranks, with locally split filtration. Descent data are continuous in the point topology just specified.

### 4.5 Cohomology varieties and representability

<a id="nc-3-filtered-affine-torsor-comparison"></a>

**Filtered affine torsor comparison.** For filtered finite-type unipotent `U_n` over `B⊗_K R`, classify equivariant affine right `U_n`-torsors whose coordinate rings have an exhaustive filtration by finite-rank locally free pieces of the same ranks as the corresponding pieces of the group coordinate ring. Require the filtration inclusions to be locally split and universally injective, the torsor coaction to preserve the filtration, and the semilinear G-action on each finite piece to be continuous. Isomorphisms are equivariant filtered affine torsor isomorphisms. Every such torsor has a point, since fppf torsors under a split unipotent group over an affine base are trivial ([Unipotent groups and their homogeneous quotients in characteristic zero](#split-unipotent-quotients)(c)); the category consists of the torsors for which translation by some point is a strict filtered isomorphism `U_n≅P`. Evaluation at such a point gives a natural bijection of their isomorphism classes with `H1(G,U_n(B⊗R))`. Coefficient-base descent and the reconstruction by a cocycle must be effective in this filtered affine category; a nonempty topological torsor bijection alone does not establish these facts.

Characteristic zero; a smooth split unipotent group of finite depth; an affine coefficient base; exhaustive filtrations by locally free finite-rank pieces with locally split, universally injective inclusions; a filtration-compatible torsor coaction; torsors admitting a point at which translation is a strict filtered isomorphism; effective descent along the coefficient base.

Apply torsor triviality over affine bases ([Unipotent groups and their homogeneous quotients in characteristic zero](#split-unipotent-quotients)(c)), obtained by induction through vector groups and the vanishing of affine quasi-coherent `H¹`. Use a point to identify the underlying affine right torsor with `U_n` and verify strict filtration. Construct the cocycle from the semilinear G-action using [Continuous unipotent points](#nc-3-unipotent-point-topology); reconstruct the filtered affine torsor by twisting the Hopf coaction. Compare the affine construction on points with the accepted parent torsor classification and verify descent of algebra morphisms.

**Checks.**

- An empty point space is excluded only after the affine triviality theorem; filtered algebra isomorphism must be proved, not inferred from a homeomorphism.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), Section 1, filtered torsor definition and Proposition 1, printed pp. 4–7.

**Finite-level representability.** Let `U_n` be a finite-depth tower of characteristic-zero smooth split unipotent groups over B, with central vector layers `V_i`, regular sections of `U_{i+1}→U_i`, continuous semilinear G-action and the coefficient topology above. The inverse-depth limit is an affine proalgebraic functor.

Form the scheme-theoretic zero fibre, retaining nilpotent algebra points. Split the linear map `C1→B2` on its image, so a universal obstruction-zero class has a continuous lift. Twisted invariants of `U_i` vanish by induction from vanishing graded H0. The parent central H1 action is consequently free, giving the product with `H1(V_i)`. The product and zero fibre are affine finite type. Transition morphisms supply the affine proalgebraic limit.

### 4.6 Local neutral loci

<a id="bloch-kato-subgroups"></a>

**The Bloch–Kato subgroups `H¹_e⊆H¹_f⊆H¹_g`.** Let K be a finite extension of `ℚ_p` and V a finite-dimensional continuous `ℚ_p`-representation of `G_K`. Define `H¹_e(K,V)=ker(H¹(K,V)→H¹(K,V⊗B_cris^(φ=1)))`, `H¹_f(K,V)=ker(H¹(K,V)→H¹(K,V⊗B_cris))` and `H¹_g(K,V)=ker(H¹(K,V)→H¹(K,V⊗B_dR))`. Then `H¹_e⊆H¹_f⊆H¹_g`, the three are functorial in V, and when V is de Rham (respectively crystalline) a class lies in `H¹_g` (respectively `H¹_f`) exactly when the corresponding extension `0→V→E→ℚ_p→0` is de Rham (respectively crystalline). For an extension of global representations, the global `subgroup H¹_g(G_F,V)` is the set of classes unramified at almost all places and in `H¹_g at` every place above p. For a unipotent coefficient group the same definitions with torsors give the De Rham and crystalline torsor classes, and `H¹_f(G_v,U)⊆H¹_g(G_v,U)`.

`K/ℚ_p` finite; V finite-dimensional continuous; the period rings `B_cris⊆B_dR` with their Galois actions.

The inclusions come from `ℚ_p⊆B_cris^(φ=1)⊆B_cris⊆B_dR:` a class dying in `H¹(K,V⊗B)` dies in `H¹(K,V⊗B′)` for `B⊆B′`. Functoriality is that of `H¹`. The extension description: `E⊗B` splits as a Galois module exactly when the class dies in `H¹(K,V⊗B)`, and for `B=B_dR` or `B_cris` (with V de Rham, respectively crystalline) this is equivalent to E being de Rham, respectively crystalline, by dimension count of `D_B(E)`. For unipotent coefficients, a torsor P is De Rham when `D(P)⊗B_dR≅P⊗B_dR` compatibly with all structures, and the crystalline condition with `B_cris` implies the De Rham one.

**Checks.**

- For `V=ℚ_p(1)` and `K=ℚ_p`, `H¹(ℚ_p,ℚ_p(1))=(limₙ ℚ_p^×/(ℚ_p^×)^(pⁿ))⊗ℤₚℚ_p` is 2-dimensional, `H¹_f=H¹_e` is the 1-dimensional image of `ℤ_p^×`, and `H¹_g` is all of `H¹`; so the inclusion `H¹_f⊆H¹_g` can be strict, and a definition using `B_dR` for `H¹_f` would be wrong.
- For `V=ℚ_p` (trivial), `H¹(ℚ_p,ℚ_p)=Hom(G_(ℚ_p),ℚ_p)` is 2-dimensional, `H¹_f` is the 1-dimensional unramified line and `H¹_e=0`, so `H¹_e⊆H¹_f` can be strict.
- If V is crystalline with `D_cris(V)^(φ=1)=0` and `D_cris(V^*(1))^(φ=1)=0`, then `H¹_e=H¹_f=H¹_g`; this applies to `V_pE` for an elliptic curve E with good reduction, recovering the equality used for elliptic curves.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §3, De Rham torsors, arXiv v1 p. 15; [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §2, the inclusion `H¹_f⊆H¹_g` for unipotent torsors, p. 118; [Laurent Berger](#reference-berger2002), Proposition II.5 and the remark identifying `H¹_g` as the kernel of the dual exponential map, p. 13. The definitions are those of Bloch and Kato (The Grothendieck Festschrift I, 1990, §3).

<a id="nc-3-local-neutral-locus"></a>

**Local neutral locus.** For set-valued algebra functors F,T, a natural transformation `f:F→T` and a natural neutral point e of T, define `neutralLocus(R)={x∈F(R):f_R(x)=e_R}`. Its algebra maps are restrictions of F maps. For an inertia restriction map this gives `H1_un`; for extension of coefficients `Qp→B_dR` or `Qp→B_cris` it gives `H1_g` or `H1_f` respectively, once the continuous cohomology functors are supplied. The definition uses every coefficient algebra R; it asserts no representability or closedness.

CommAlgCat K F,T covariant Set-valued functors f natural e natural.

Form the fibre subtype over the natural neutral point. Naturality preserves membership under each coefficient map. Use subtype extensionality for functor laws and universal factoring of neutralized maps.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.NC3.neutralLocus_mem`: A class lies in the subtype iff `f_R(x)=e_R`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.NC3.neutralLocus_ext`: Two subtype elements are equal iff their underlying `F(R)` values are equal.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.NC3.neutralLocus_map_val`: Coefficient maps have underlying value `F(a)(x)`.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.NC3.neutralLocus_inclusion`: The natural inclusion into F is pointwise injective.

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.NC3.neutralLocus_inclusion_injective`: The inclusion is injective at every R.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.NC3.neutralLocus_lift_comp`: The lifted natural map composed with inclusion is the original `a:E→F`.

### 4.7 Local invariant lifting

<a id="central-local-invariant-lifts"></a>

**All-algebra local invariant lifting and differences.** For the geometric finite-depth central sequence `1→V_n→U_(n+1)→U_n→1`, construct the invariant lifts needed for its local conditions over every coefficient algebra R and every geometric residue extension. At p use the crystalline path comparison and the Frobenius-Lang construction to lift relevant invariant `B_cris⊗R` points. At a fixed unramified place use its inertia action and the corresponding invariant lifting hypothesis in that local branch. Prove that translation of a local neutral lift by a linear finite-condition class stays neutral and that the unique difference of two neutral lifts satisfies exactly the linear condition. Give the resulting affine linear defect equations and show they are closed zero fibres at each induction step.

The crystalline and unramified branches have their stated invariant-lifting hypotheses; invariants are not assumed exact for arbitrary central extensions. Algebra extension and nilpotent coefficient algebras are included.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `localCentral.invariantLift`: Construct the relevant invariant lift in the geometric branch.
- `localCentral.addition`: Preserve the local neutral condition.
- `localCentral.difference`: Identify precisely the linear condition on the difference.
- `localCentral.closedDefect`: Give the representing closed affine linear zero fibre.

**Checks.**

- At depth one the neutral locus agrees with the linear Bloch–Kato finite condition.
- For a nonsurjective invariant map the unconditional difference assertion is unavailable.
- For `R=E[ε]/(ε²)`, the equations retain their infinitesimal condition.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §4, Comments II, central Selmer induction and the `H_w`-invariant lifting step, published pp. 127–130; [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2005), §1, Propositions 2–3, printed pp. 8–10.

### 4.8 Local conditions and Selmer varieties

Require the global H1(V)-action and difference classification on all coefficient algebras and after field extension, with all corresponding twisted quotient invariants trivial so that this action is free. Then every nonempty geometric fibre is a torsor under the vector scheme `Sel_T(V)`. After choosing a point it is isomorphic to that vector scheme on all algebras over the geometric residue field. Consequently `dim Sel_T(U_{n+1})≤dim Sel_T(U_n)+dim_Qp Sel_T(V)`; the obstruction zero fibre can make the inequality strict.

After a point of a geometric fibre is chosen, the all-algebra action/difference identities give inverse natural maps between that fibre functor and the vector Selmer functor. <a id="nc-3-depth-two-cup-obstruction"></a>

**A nonzero depth-two obstruction.** Let X,Y,Z be continuous topological additive G-modules and `β:X×Y→Z` a continuous G-equivariant bilinear pairing. The Heisenberg extension `U=X×Y×Z` has law `(x,y,z)(x′,y′,z′)=(x+x′,y+y′,z+z′+β(x,y′))`. For cocycles `a∈Z1(G,X)`, `b∈Z1(G,Y)`, the section `g↦(a(g),b(g),0)` has positive defect `β(a(g),g·b(h))`; its H2 class is the oriented cup product `[a]∪_β[b]`. It lifts iff that class is zero. For local Galois `G=G_k` with k/Qp finite, X=Qp, Y=Z=Qp(1) and the scalar pairing, local Tate duality supplies a,b with nonzero cup product in `H2(G_k,Qp(1))≃Qp`; that depth-two class does not lift. This example tests obstruction theory, not the H0-vanishing representability hypothesis, since X has nonzero invariants.

Continuous bilinear G-equivariant `β` continuous cup comparison local p-adic duality with nonzero H1(Qp) for the nonzero Galois specialization.

Import the continuous cup convention and rational local Tate duality. For V=Qp, H0 has dimension 1 and H2 is dual to H0(Qp(1))=0; the local Euler characteristic therefore gives dim H1(Qp)=1+[k:Qp]&gt;0. Choose a nonzero class and a dual Qp(1) class with nonzero pairing, identified by the local invariant with H2(Qp(1))≃Qp. As a separate explicit sign check take discrete `G=Z²`, `X=Y=Z=Q`, trivial action and coordinate homomorphisms. The two-cochain `m(g)n(h)` is not a coboundary because all trivial-action one-cochain coboundaries on abelian G are symmetric, while it takes 1 and 0 on the swapped coordinate generators.

### 4.9 Tangential Selmer conditions

<a id="tangential-selmer-conditions"></a>

**Tangential global Selmer conditions.** Apply the integral tangential fibre functors to the finite-depth global coefficient family and its path torsors. Construct the global `G_(F,T)-cohomology` variety, crystalline local condition at p and prescribed away-place local Kummer images with that base point. Prove representability, coefficient and depth compatibility and independence under the stated unit-tangent changes through the base-point path comparison. Integral endpoint paths lie in these conditions. This construction supplies the tangential Selmer scheme used for `P¹−{0,1,∞}` over Z.

Use a fixed integral unit tangent and the smooth pair over `O_F[1/T]`. The p-condition uses the full tangential crystalline comparison.

### Examples

For a depth-two Heisenberg quotient with central pairing `⟨−,−⟩`, the defect of a lifted pair of abelian cocycles is represented by `(g,h)↦⟨a(g),g·b(h)⟩`. Its cup order is fixed by the positive differential. Interchanging the convention negates its `H²` class, so it preserves the obstruction's zero locus but changes its value. The `C₉→C₃` computation in Layer 0 gives a finite nonliftable example. The arithmetic analogue uses the local invariant map and rational coefficient duality on their canonical carriers.

Invariant lifting is needed before taking linear differences of locally neutral lifts. In a central sequence `1→V→U′→U→1`, invariants need not be right exact. If a fixed U-point has no fixed lift, a chosen U′-lift can contribute a nonzero V-cocycle. Declaring every difference automatically finite would erase that defect. At p, the geometric crystalline comparison and Frobenius-Lang construction supply the specific invariant lift; the unramified branch retains its own lifting hypothesis.

All-algebra representability includes `R=E[ε]/(ε²)`. The tangent coefficient is not discarded by replacing an R-valued torsor with its E-valued points. Locally free filtered pieces and strict affine descent preserve that infinitesimal direction. A rank drop in a filtered coordinate piece does not define the same functor.

The central invariant factor in Kim's induction is `V^B/V`. It is a quotient of the central vector group, rather than a duplicate of the previous unipotent stage. For `V=0` it is a point; for a nontrivial central vector group its coordinates detect the remaining invariant conditions. The central fibre dimension is bounded by the corresponding linear Selmer dimension, even when some fibres are empty.

At depth one, the crystalline Selmer condition agrees with the Bloch–Kato finite condition on the Jacobian's rational Tate module. Globally its exact sequence retains the rational Tate module of Sha. A nonzero Sha direction is therefore present in the full Selmer variety and is removed only by the separate Mordell–Weil cut of Layer 5.


Replacing each local condition by a subset shrinks their localization-preimage intersection, by `Set.iInter_mono` and `Set.preimage_mono`. If every global Kummer class satisfies all local conditions, containment in a finite refined locus and injectivity of the global-point localization imply finiteness of the global points. No dimension or representability conclusion follows from the set intersection alone; an empty refinement excluding infinitely many global points fails the containment hypothesis.

## Layer 5: Albanese maps and Chabauty–Kim finiteness

Construct local and global path-class maps and their crystalline periods. Combine scheme image dimension, density on every open subdisc and compact analytic charts to prove finite Chabauty–Kim loci, including the Mordell–Weil cut needed by quadratic Chabauty.

### 5.0 Analytic functions of tensor paths

<a id="residue-discs-logarithmic-ends"></a>

**Residue discs and logarithmic ends.** Let `K/ℚ_p` be finite and (𝒳,D) a smooth proper `O_K`-curve with finite étale relative boundary. Define the residue domains as tubes under specialization, using RigidAnalyticGeometry §6.2's rigid spaces. At a rational smooth special-fibre point, a parameter identifies its K-valued disc with `m_K`; rescale `t=πs` to identify these points with the compact domain `O_K`. At a boundary point use the punctured tube and a fixed branch of the p-adic logarithm; allow functions polynomial in log t with analytic coefficients and nilpotent logarithmic residues. Nonrational closed points are treated over their unramified residue extensions, retaining descent. Prove coordinate-change and restriction identities, convergence on smaller closed discs, and invariance under changes of parameter compatible with the tangent. (Besser, §2, especially (2.4)–(2.7), pp. 5–6; Kim 2009, §1, pp. 101–103.)

The API includes `residueTube_parameter`, `residueTube_rescale`, `logarithmicEnd_restrict`, `logarithmicEnd_changeParameter` and compatibility with [Residue-disc fibre](#nc-2-rigid-fibre).

**Checks.**

- The ordinary disc is `t∈πO_K`, not all of `O_K` before rescaling. For a ramified extension its radius is set by `π` rather than by p.
- The form dt/t has no analytic primitive `at t=0`; its logarithmic primitive on the punctured tube is log t with the chosen branch.
- For a trivial connection, horizontal sections on a disc are constants. For d−Ndt with `N²=0`, transport from x to y is `1+(y−x)N`, agreeing with Layer 2's sign.
