<a id="coleman-functions-primitives"></a>

**Coleman functions and normalized primitives.** On a smooth geometrically connected good-reduction affine pair over finite `K/ℚ_p`, fix `K↪ℂ_p` and a logarithm branch with `log(p)=a∈K`. Use ColemanIntegration L1.7–L1.9 for a Frobenius-structured datum, with its `(H0)`, `(H1)`, `(Hi)` and `(Hw)` hypotheses after extension to `ℂ_p`, and L1.12–L1.23 for the analytic Coleman algebra, evaluation, differential, normalized primitives and transport independence. Construct the comparison of its finite-word realization with the unipotent overconvergent connections, horizontal functionals and tensor paths of Layer 2. The K-valued form uses K coefficients and K-rational base data; prove that these tensor-path realizations descend to K inside the supplier's `ℂ_p` algebra. Define `colemanFunctions` by transport of that K-form, with evaluation on K-points. Identify its differential and constants K, and transport the supplier's injective restriction to every nonempty residue disc and primitive laws. For curves every Coleman one-form is closed. Match ordinary base values and unit-tangential base values; the latter use the constant term on regular nonnegative-power logarithmic word expansions, with the supplier's simple-pole and pullback-normalization hypotheses. Identify the recursion `dI_(iw)=ω_i I_w`, with i the outermost letter, and the shuffle product. Under these identifications the supplier's transport equals [Canonical Frobenius path](#nc-2-canonical-frobenius-path), agrees with local horizontal transport and respects pullback. Independence of normalized realizations under a change of Frobenius lift carries L1.22's common fixed base or compatible tangential normalization; the algebra and integration modulo constants are lift-independent without that common-base condition. Proper-curve domains are assembled by §5.2. (Besser, Proposition 3.4, Definition 3.5, pp. 8–9; Propositions 4.11–4.12, Corollaries 4.13–4.14 and Theorem 4.15, pp. 13–14; Theorem 5.7, pp. 18–19.)

The transported API includes `colemanFunctions_eval_injective`, `colemanFunctions_differential`, `colemanFunctions_ker_d`, `colemanPrimitive`, `colemanPrimitive_derivative`, `colemanPrimitive_baseValue` and `colemanPrimitive_unique`. These are adapters to ColemanIntegration L1.17–L1.23, with the coefficient-field and normalization identifications above, and compare its word coefficients with the Layer 2 Frobenius paths.

**Checks.**

- The normalized primitive of df from b to x is `f(x)−f(b)`. Adding a nonzero constant violates the prescribed base value.
- A Coleman function vanishing on one nonempty open subdisc is zero on every disc of the connected pair; independently chosen locally analytic functions on different discs do not satisfy this property.
- For an iterated primitive of one form `ω`, the product of two depth-one integrals is twice the repeated depth-two integral. This agrees with `wordShuffleDuality` and rejects an unordered concatenation rule.

The comparison uses those tensor paths and the supplied analytic realization.

<a id="punctured-line-polylogarithms"></a>

**Punctured-line logarithms and dilogarithms.** On `ℙ¹∖{0,1,∞}` use the polylogarithms of ColemanIntegration L2.3–L2.18 and the comparison above, with its coefficient-field and branch identifications. For the odd-p specialization over `ℚ_p`, take `log(p)=0` and the unit tangent at 0. Identify the regularized depth-one tensor-path integrals with log z and `log(1−z)` for `ω₀=dz/z` and `ω₁=dz/(z−1)`. Define `colemanDilogarithm` as the transported supplier function `Li₂⁰`, so it equals `−I_(01)` in the first-letter-outermost convention: `dI_(01)=log(1−z)dz/z` and the regularized base value is zero. Transport its series `∑_(n≥1) zⁿ/n²` on `|z|<1`, derivative `dLi₂(z)=−log(1−z)dz/z`, reflection `Li₂(z)+Li₂(1−z)=−log z log(1−z)` and inversion `Li₂(z)+Li₂(z⁻¹)=−(log z)²/2`, using L2.9 and L2.18. At a sixth root of unity these give `Li₂(ζ₆⁻¹)=−Li₂(ζ₆)`. Their use in a point-identification theorem leaves nonvanishing of `Li₂(ζ₆)` as an explicit hypothesis. (BDCKW, §§6.1–6.3, pp. 43–45, and §8.2; Kim 2005, §2, the punctured-line iterated integrals.)

The API consists of the transported adapters `colemanDilogarithm_series`, `colemanDilogarithm_derivative`, `colemanDilogarithm_reflection`, `colemanDilogarithm_inversion` and the regularized tangential value at 0, with `colemanDilogarithm=Li₂⁰=−I_(01)`.

**Checks.**

- The series has zero constant term and linear coefficient one, whereas `I_(01)=−z−z²/4−⋯` near 0. Thus `colemanDilogarithm=−I_(01)`; using the forward coefficient without the minus sign fails both the derivative and normalization.
- For a root of unity `ζ` with `ζ≠1`, `log ζ=0`, and the inversion identity gives opposite dilogarithm values `at ζ` and `ζ⁻¹`.
- If p≡1 mod 3, vanishing at the two primitive sixth roots is simultaneous; their nonzero values do not follow merely from either functional equation.

### 5.1 Admissible torsors and the unipotent Albanese map

<a id="nc-4-admissible-period"></a>

**The period of an admissible path torsor.** Let K be a characteristic-zero p-adic field and `U_n` the finite-depth de Rham unipotent group of Layer 2. Write `H_n=F⁰U_n`, a closed split unipotent subgroup, not assumed normal, and `Q_n=U_n/H_n` for the represented quotient by right multiplication. On a commutative K-algebra R, an admissible right `U_n`-torsor T has the Layer 2 finite coordinate filtration, a compatible Frobenius with a unique fixed point `p_φ`, and a Hodge reduction `F⁰T` with an R-point `p_H`. Define admissiblePeriod(T)=[u] in `Q_n(R)`, where `p_φ·u=p_H`. Changing `p_H` to `p_H·h` changes u to uh for `h∈H_n(R)`, hence preserves its class. Quotient representability and triviality of split-unipotent torsors over affine bases are imported inputs. Point reduction: for a Torsor `U_nᵒᵖ T`, u is the underlying `U_n` element of `p_H` divided by `p_φ` in the opposite group; the point quotient is Mathlib's left-coset carrier `U_n/H_n` with relation `u⁻¹v∈H_n`. The group-coordinate criterion identifies equality of period cosets with membership of `p_H⁻¹p′_H` in the Hodge subgroup, for any subgroup without a normality hypothesis.

`U_n` and its filtered/Frobenius path structure come from Layer 2; Frobenius Lang invertibility uses the positive-weight hypotheses there, not an arbitrary automorphism of an arbitrary unipotent group. All R are commutative K-algebras, including nonreduced ones; `H_n` is smooth split unipotent and the Hodge torsor is trivial over Spec R.

Use the imported homogeneous quotient sheaf and its affine representation; the affine torsor-vanishing input identifies `Q_n(R)` with right-multiplication orbits `U_n(R)/H_n(R)`. Use the Layer 2 Frobenius Lang scheme isomorphism after coefficient extension to obtain the unique fixed section on every affine coefficient algebra; identify `T(R)` with `U_n(R)`, retaining the right-action order. The field-endpoint canonical-path theorem alone does not supply this all-algebra step. Hodge points differ by right multiplication by `H_n`; quotient this difference.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `admissiblePeriod_eq_mk`: The period is the coset of the unique u with `p_φ·u=p_H`.
- `admissiblePeriod_hodge_change`: For `h∈H_n(R)`, replacing `p_H` by `p_H·h` leaves the period unchanged.
- `admissiblePeriod_eq_iff`: For fixed `p_φ`, the periods of `p_H` and `p′_H` coincide iff `u⁻¹u′∈H_n(R)`.
- `admissiblePeriod_self`: Choosing `p_H=p_φ` gives [1].
- `admissiblePeriod_transport`: A right `U_n`-equivariant isomorphism of torsor point carriers preserving the two chosen points preserves the period.

**Checks.**

- `admissiblePeriod_identity`: On the self-torsor `Uᵒᵖ`, with `p_φ=op(1)` and `p_H=op(g)`, the period is [g], not `[g⁻¹]`.
- `admissiblePeriod_right_change`: On that self-torsor, for `h∈H`, the periods of op(g) and op(gh) agree, even for nonnormal H.
- `admissiblePeriod_left_change_fails`: In `S₃` take H generated by `h=(01)`, `g=(12)`. With `p_φ=1`, the periods of g and hg differ, although those of g and gh agree.
- `admissiblePeriod_inverse_fixed_path`: In the self-torsor for `U=Multiplicative(ℚ)`, `H={1}`, put g=ofAdd(1), `p_φ=op(g)` and `p_H=op(1)`. The period is `[g⁻¹]`, and differs from [g]. This catches replacing the ordered ratio by the forward fixed-path coordinate or ignoring `p_φ`.
- No group structure on `Q_n` is asserted when `H_n` is nonnormal.
- For the neutral filtered Frobenius torsor with `p_H=p_φ`, the period is [1].

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §1, Lemma 1 and the definition preceding Proposition 1, pp. 104–105.

Use [Hodge filtered path fibres](#nc-2-filtered-path); [Canonical Frobenius path](#nc-2-canonical-frobenius-path); [Unipotent Frobenius Lang theorem](#nc-2-frobenius-lang); [SchemeAndStackFoundations](../SchemeAndStackFoundations/README.md) §§1.15–1.17 (torsors, contracted products and quotient sheaves); [TauCetiRoadmap.ReductiveGroups](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups/README.md#layer-3-subgroups-quotients-components); `Torsor`; `QuotientGroup.leftRel`; [TauCetiRoadmap.ReductiveGroups](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups/README.md#layer-5-solvable-and-unipotent-groups-the-unipotent-radical); [Unipotent groups and their homogeneous quotients in characteristic zero](#split-unipotent-quotients).

<a id="nc-4-admissible-classification"></a>

**Admissible torsors and the Hodge quotient.** Under the hypotheses of [The period of an admissible path torsor](#nc-4-admissible-period), the period gives a natural bijection, for every commutative K-algebra R, between isomorphism classes of admissible `U_n`-torsors and `Q_n(R)`. Isomorphisms preserve the right torsor action, coordinate filtration, Frobenius and Hodge filtration. This represents the finite-level admissible-torsor functor, rather than merely classifying K-points. The Hodge structure is the full Layer 2 normalized multiplicative filtration; a reduction to `H_n` without that structure is not silently substituted for it.

Admissibility, split-unipotent affine torsor vanishing and normalized filtered structure as in [The period of an admissible path torsor](#nc-4-admissible-period).

An isomorphism preserves `p_φ` by its uniqueness and maps Hodge points to Hodge points, so periods agree. For equal cosets, the unique `p_φ-compatible` torsor isomorphism differs in Hodge coordinates by an element of `H_n`, and preserves the normalized filtration. For `g∈U_n(R)`, use the standard filtered torsor `U_n,R` with Frobenius `φ_g(h)=g⁻¹φ(gh)`; its fixed point is `g⁻¹` and its Hodge point 1, giving period [g]. Apply the finite central quotient to Kim Proposition 1 and verify scalar-extension naturality.

**Checks.**

- The twisted Frobenius satisfies `φ_g(hk)=φ_g(h)φ(k)`; it is generally not a group homomorphism.
- The construction works on `R=K[ε]/(ε²)`, not just reduced points.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §1, Proposition 1 and its proof, pp. 105–106.

Use [The period of an admissible path torsor](#nc-4-admissible-period); [Hadian’s universal Hodge filtration](#nc-2-hadian-filtration); [Unipotent Frobenius Lang theorem](#nc-2-frobenius-lang); [Lower central depth](#nc-2-central-quotients); [TauCetiRoadmap.ReductiveGroups](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups/README.md#layer-3-subgroups-quotients-components); [TauCetiRoadmap.ReductiveGroups](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups/README.md#layer-5-solvable-and-unipotent-groups-the-unipotent-radical); [Unipotent groups and their homogeneous quotients in characteristic zero](#split-unipotent-quotients).

<a id="nc-4-local-albanese"></a>

**The finite-depth de Rham Albanese map.** Fix a smooth geometrically connected hyperbolic curve `X/K`, a smooth proper `O_K`-model X̄ with finite étale boundary D (possibly empty), the open model `𝒳=X̄∖D` and `b∈𝒳(O_K)`. Use `U_n=U/Γ_{n+1}` for `n≥1` and the right path torsor `P_n(b,x)` from b to x. Define `localAlbanese_n:𝒳(O_K)→Q_n(K)` by `x↦admissiblePeriod(P_n(b,x))`. The map is a p-adic analytic map on each residue disc, with local coordinates furnished by iterated Coleman integrals and an algebraic Hodge trivialization. It is not asserted to be a morphism of algebraic K-schemes. At b it equals [1]. Kim's `U_{n+1}` is this `U_n`; Kim `U_1` is trivial and Kim `U_2` is our depth one.

The base point is integral and the compactification and boundary have good reduction at the chosen p-adic place. Layer 2 supplies the canonical Frobenius path and normalized Hodge reduction. For an arbitrary ramified `K/ℚ_p`, assume the endpoint-compatible rigid/de Rham and crystalline geometric comparisons for this model and these endpoints. The Layer 2 targets [Nonabelian Berthelot–Ogus comparison](#nc-2-berthelot-ogus) and [Crystalline coordinate path comparison](#nc-2-crystalline-path-coordinates) cover unramified models; [Finite crystalline path comparison](#nc-2-finite-path-comparison) extends only models and endpoints descending to that setup. The [ramified endpoint comparison](#ramified-endpoint-comparison) supplies this model and endpoint enhancement; scalar extension alone does not supply it.

Push the Layer 2 tensor path family to the n-th central quotient. Apply [Admissible torsors and the Hodge quotient](#nc-4-admissible-classification) fibrewise, independent of the chosen local Hodge section. Use the word-path comparison of Layer 2 and Coleman local expansions for discwise analyticity.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `localAlbanese_apply`: At x the map is admissiblePeriod of the two chosen paths in `P_n(b,x)`.
- `localAlbanese_base`: The normalized constant path at b gives `localAlbanese_n(b)=[1]`.
- `localAlbanese_reindex`: Reindexing the endpoint family along `f:Y→𝒳(O_K)` composes `localAlbanese_n` with f.
- `localAlbanese_hodge_change`: A pointwise change `p_H(x)↦p_H(x)h(x)`, with `h(x)∈H_n(K)`, preserves the function.
- `localAlbanese_tower`: For `m≤n`, the induced quotient `q_nm` satisfies `q_nm∘localAlbanese_n=localAlbanese_m`.

**Checks.**

- `localAlbanese_self_family`: For every endpoint, if the Hodge and fixed paths coincide, the resulting family is constant [1].
- `localAlbanese_trivial_hodge`: For the `Uᵒᵖ` self-torsor family indexed by `g∈U`, `H={1}`, `p_φ(g)=1` and `p_H(g)=op(g)`, the value at g is [g].
- `localAlbanese_fibre_change`: For arbitrary `h(x)∈H`, the self-torsor endpoint family op(g(x)h(x)) gives the same map as op(g(x)).
- The depth-zero extension is the constant map to a point; depth one is nontrivial.
- The base point maps to the neutral coset and higher-depth maps project to lower-depth maps.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §1, definition of the de Rham map after Proposition 1, p. 106; introduction p. 93.

<a id="nc-4-iterated-coordinates"></a>

**Iterated integrals as Albanese coordinates.** On an affine open of `X_K` choose the Layer 2 universal connection and its algebraic trivialization g, and choose an algebraic Hodge trivialization `p_H=gγ`. Let `p_φ(x)u(x)=g(x)`. Then `localAlbanese_n(x)` is the class of `u(x)γ(x)` in `Q_n`. In the Layer 2 affine trivialization the Frobenius path has word element `I(b,x)`, while g has coordinate 1; hence `u=I(b,x)⁻¹` and the period representative is `I(b,x)⁻¹γ(x)`. The coefficients of I are the imported Coleman iterated integrals; coefficients of `I⁻¹` are their antipode combinations. Kim’s variable u in his proof must not be identified with Layer 2’s forward path element without transporting the trivialization convention. In the convention `dI_{iw}=ω_i I_w`, the first letter is the outermost integration, `I_∅=1`, and the coefficients of `uγ` are `∑_{w=ab}(I⁻¹)_aγ_b`, preserving multiplication order. On proper curves use the imported maximal extending quotient of an affine universal connection; do not treat all affine words as independent coordinates on the proper group. Regular functions on `Q_n` pull back to Coleman functions, analytic on every ordinary residue disc.

Good-reduction datum of [The finite-depth de Rham Albanese map](#nc-4-local-albanese); the affine trivializations and word-path identification are the Layer 2 imported constructions. Only ordinary discs of 𝒳 are evaluated; logarithmic boundary germs are not added to the integral-point domain.

Use the ordered torsor equation `p_φuγ=p_H` and the shuffle/deconcatenation word realization. The Hodge factor `γ` is algebraic, so finite polynomial coordinate expressions are Coleman functions. Pass from the affine group to the central quotient and to the proper extending quotient when required.

**Checks.**

- At the normalized base point the period is the neutral coset, and the constant word coefficient remains one.
- A bare list of single integrals cannot encode depth two.
- The empty coefficient is 1, and reversing factors u and `γ` changes noncommuting coordinates.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §1, proof of Theorem 1 and Lemma 4, pp. 111–114, with the universal connection pp. 106–111.

### 5.2 Coleman charts on proper curves

<a id="proper-curve-coleman-charts"></a>

**Coleman integration on a proper curve with good reduction.** Let `K/ℚ_p` be finite with residue field `κ`, and 𝒳 a smooth proper curve over `O_K` with geometrically connected fibres. (a) For any two distinct closed points `y₁,y₂` of the special fibre `𝒳_κ`, choose lifts to relative effective divisors `𝒟₁,𝒟₂⊂𝒳`, finite étale over `O_K` of degrees `[κ(y₁):κ]` and `[κ(y₂):κ]` (Hensel's lemma); then `𝒴ᵢ=𝒳∖𝒟ᵢ` are affine, every residue disc of `𝒳(O_K)` lies in `𝒴₁(O_K)` or `𝒴₂(O_K)`, and the two charts cover `𝒳(O_K)`. The divisors need not consist of K-rational points. (b) Coleman functions on the tubes of `𝒴₁`, `𝒴₂` (the algebra of [Coleman functions and normalized primitives](#coleman-functions-primitives) for each pair `(𝒳,𝒟ᵢ)`) glue uniquely on the overlap, because Coleman functions form a sheaf for the Zariski topology on the special fibre and are determined by their restriction to any nonempty open (Coleman's uniqueness principle). Hence iterated Coleman integrals of algebraic differentials on `𝒳_K` are well-defined functions on `𝒳(O_K)`, independent of the charts. (c) On each residue disc, a local parameter t reducing to a uniformiser at the reduction point identifies the disc with the maximal ideal `m_K` of `O_K`, and each iterated integral is given by a power series in t converging on the open unit disc of `ℂ_p`; the K-points of the disc form the compact set `m_K`, which is strictly smaller than the geometric disc.

`K/ℚ_p` finite; 𝒳 smooth proper over `O_K` with geometrically connected fibres; `𝒳_κ` has at least two closed points (always true, since `𝒳_κ` is a curve over a finite field).

(a) A closed point y of `𝒳_κ` has residue field `κ(y)` finite over `κ`, hence separable; 𝒳 is smooth, so y lifts to an `O_(K(y))-point` with `K(y)` the unramified extension of degree `[κ(y):κ]`, whose image is a finite étale relative divisor. The complement of a nonempty relatively ample effective divisor in a proper curve is affine. A residue disc reduces to a single closed point x, and x differs from `y₁` or `y₂`. (b) Besser's Tannakian theory defines Coleman functions on any rigid triple, in particular on `(𝒳_κ̄,𝒳_κ̄,𝒳^)`, and proves the sheaf property; his comparison theorem identifies them on each affine chart with the functions of [Coleman functions and normalized primitives](#coleman-functions-primitives). Galois equivariance descends from the completed maximal unramified extension to K. (c) Expand the horizontal sections of the unipotent connection in the local parameter; convergence on the open disc is the Dwork-type estimate already used for affine charts.

**Checks.**

- If `𝒳_κ(κ)` has exactly one point y, a chart removing a rational point covers every disc except ]y[, and the second chart must use a closed point of degree at least two; the construction does not need two rational residue discs.
- For `𝒳=P¹` over `ℤ_p` with `y₁` the reduction of 0 and `y₂` that of `∞`, the charts are `P¹∖{0}` and `P¹∖{∞}`: the disc of 0 lies only in the second chart, the disc of `∞` only in the first, and every other disc in both, so a single chart would miss a disc.
- By the uniqueness principle two Coleman functions on `𝒴₁` that agree on one nonempty residue subdisc agree everywhere; hence the gluing in (b) only needs agreement on one disc of the overlap, and a function defined chart by chart with mismatched constants of integration on the overlap does not glue.
- For K ramified of index e, the K-points of a residue disc form `m_K`≅t-values of valuation `≥1/e`, which is larger than the `ℚ_p`-points `pℤ_p` but still compact; the analytic zero bounds are applied on these compact sets, not on the whole open disc.

The construction and its conventions follow [Amnon Besser](#reference-besser), §1 (rigid triples), p. 2; Proposition 4.21, p. 16; §5 (comparison with Coleman's theory), pp. 16–19; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), §4.1, the affine open `Y=X∖D`, p. 909; §5.5, p. 925; §§6.4–6.6, the two affine charts and the remaining disc, pp. 930–934.

### 5.3 Kim density on residue discs

<a id="nc-4-residue-disc-density"></a>

**Kim density on every residue disc.** For [The finite-depth de Rham Albanese map](#nc-4-local-albanese)'s smooth hyperbolic good-reduction pair over a finite extension `K/ℚ_p`, `n≥1`, and every nonempty integral residue disc `B⊆𝒳(O_K)`, the `image localAlbanese_n(B)` is Zariski dense in the geometrically integral affine K-variety `Q_n`. Equivalently any regular `f∈O(Q_n)` that vanishes on this whole disc is zero. The conclusion is K-Zariski density, not automatic `ℚ_p`-Zariski density in `Res_{K/ℚ_p}Q_n`. Density is asserted separately on each disc, so a nonzero regular equation has nonzero analytic pullback on every disc.

All good-reduction and integrality hypotheses of [The finite-depth de Rham Albanese map](#nc-4-local-albanese). `n≥1` in our indexing, corresponding to Kim `n+1≥2`; hyperbolicity means `2g−2+deg` D&gt;0.

Kim Lemma 4 proves the affine forward horizontal word coefficients independent over algebraic functions via complex monodromy and induction on word length. For the group-like shuffle series, inversion sends a length-r word coefficient to `(−1)^r` times the reversed-word coefficient. Thus the inverse coefficients retain this independence. Right multiplication by the algebraic Hodge factor `γ` is unitriangular in word length, with `γ_empty=1`. Hence the corrected representative `I⁻¹γ` is dense in the affine group and its image in `Q_n` is dense. Use the surjective proper extending quotient to pass from an auxiliary affine curve to the proper curve. Choose a finite étale boundary divisor avoiding the chosen disc; it need not be a K-rational point in a different disc. The integral charts are those of [Coleman integration on a proper curve with good reduction](#proper-curve-coleman-charts), whose auxiliary divisor may have degree greater than one. On another nonempty disc choose an integral lift c. Canonical path composition gives `I(b,x)=I(c,x)I(b,c)`; multiplication by the constant group-like factor, inversion and the algebraic Hodge correction preserve the triangular independence argument. This proves density for the original base point on every disc, rather than inferring it merely from global density.

**Checks.**

- Translating the canonical path by a fixed cross-disc path preserves density for the original base point; density of a union of discs alone does not imply this.

**Density on every open residue subdisc.** For a finite-depth unipotent de Rham Albanese map of a hyperbolic good-reduction curve, prove that the image of every nonempty open p-adic subdisc of an ordinary residue disc is Zariski dense in the homogeneous quotient target. Show that a regular function vanishing on that image has a Coleman pullback zero on the subdisc, hence on the connected residue disc by analytic identity and on the required Coleman domain by uniqueness. Use the geometric hyperbolic curve, the homogeneous quotient, the canonical path comparison and ordinary interior endpoint discs.

### 5.4 Crystalline periods and étale path classes

<a id="nc-4-crystalline-period"></a>

**The represented crystalline period map.** Let `K/ℚ_p` be finite and let `L_n=H¹_f(G_K,U_n^et)` be the represented finite-depth crystalline torsor functor of Layer 4. The Layer 2 filtered, Frobenius and multiplicative period comparisons send a crystalline torsor T over a `ℚ_p`-algebra R to an admissible de Rham `U_n`-torsor over `K⊗_{ℚ_p}R`. Compose with [Admissible torsors and the Hodge quotient](#nc-4-admissible-classification) to obtain a natural transformation `D_n(R):L_n(R)→Q_n(K⊗R)`, and hence a morphism of `ℚ_p`-schemes `crystallinePeriodMap_n:L_n→Res_{K/ℚ_p}Q_n`. On `ℚ_p`-points the target is `Q_n(K)`. The neutral torsor maps to [1]. No inverse of `D_n` is asserted. Affine reduction takes the resulting pullback `d*:O(Res Q_n)→O(L_n)` and sends an R-point c to `c∘d*`; `d*` is derived from crystalline torsors through [Olsson's nonabelian crystalline comparison in the unipotent case](#olsson-unipotent-comparison) and [Good-reduction comparison over ramified p-adic fields](#ramified-endpoint-comparison).

Representability over all `ℚ_p`-algebras and coefficient-compatible crystalline conditions, as in Layer 4. The nonlinear comparison respects multiplication, both path augmentations, torsor coactions, Hodge filtration and Frobenius; linear `H¹` comparison alone is insufficient. For `K≠ℚ_p` the represented target is the Weil restriction, not `Q_n` as a `ℚ_p`-scheme by omission of its field. For an arbitrary ramified `K/ℚ_p`, assume the endpoint-compatible rigid/de Rham and crystalline geometric comparisons for this model and these endpoints. The Layer 2 targets [Nonabelian Berthelot–Ogus comparison](#nc-2-berthelot-ogus) and [Crystalline coordinate path comparison](#nc-2-crystalline-path-coordinates) cover unramified models; [Finite crystalline path comparison](#nc-2-finite-path-comparison) extends only models and endpoints descending to that setup. The [ramified endpoint comparison](#ramified-endpoint-comparison) supplies this model and endpoint enhancement; scalar extension alone does not supply it.

Apply the nonlinear coordinate-period functor to each crystalline torsor, together with the finite coordinate filtrations. Use [Admissible torsors and the Hodge quotient](#nc-4-admissible-classification) over `K⊗R`. Check naturality on coefficient rings; import the Weil restriction adjunction and apply represented-functor naturality to produce the scheme morphism.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `crystallinePeriodMap_apply`: On affine R-points, c is sent to `c∘d*`, where `d*` is the crystalline period pullback.
- `crystallinePeriodMap_coeff`: For `α:R→R′`, `α∘(c∘d*)=(α∘c)∘d*`.
- `crystallinePeriodMap_neutral`: Under compatible augmentations `ε_L∘d*=ε_Q`, the neutral point maps to the neutral point.
- `crystallinePeriodMap_tower`: The represented period morphism commutes with each finite-depth projection.
- `crystallinePeriodMap_ext`: Equality of pullbacks is detected by all coefficient points, including the universal point of the affine source.

**Checks.**

- `crystallinePeriodMap_identity`: For `d*=id_A` and any R-point `c:A→R`, the point reduction sends c to c.
- `crystallinePeriodMap_universal`: At `R=O(L_n)` and `c=id`, the point reduction returns `d*` itself.
- `crystallinePeriodMap_dual_numbers`: For `A=ℚ[t]`, `R=ℚ[ε]/(ε²)`, `d*=id` and `c(t)=ε`, the output still sends t to `ε≠0`. Passing to reduced points would give the wrong output.
- Nilpotent coefficient maps are retained, and `D_n` commutes with depth projection.
- For `K=ℚ_p` no Weil restriction is needed; invertibility is not a prerequisite of the finiteness argument.

**The local étale path-class map.** For the good-reduction datum of [The finite-depth de Rham Albanese map](#nc-4-local-albanese), define `localEtaleAlbanese_n(x)=[P_n^et(b,x)]∈H¹_f(G_K,U_n^et)(ℚ_p)` for `x∈𝒳(O_K)`. The right geometric étale path torsor has continuous `G_K`-action and its ind-coordinate ring is crystalline by the Layer 2 nonlinear good-reduction comparison. The cocycle class is independent of a chosen geometric path used to express it. It is a class in a pointed set, not an element of a group at nonabelian depth. The base point gives the neutral class. The crystalline condition is proved for these geometric path torsors; it is not inferred from unrestricted extension-closure of crystalline representations.

<a id="nc-4-global-etale-albanese"></a>

**The global étale path-class map.** Let F be a number field, `R=O_{F,S}`, `𝒳/R` a smooth hyperbolic curve with smooth proper compactification and finite étale boundary, and `b∈𝒳(R)`. Fix p and T containing S and every p-adic place, and assume the Layer 2 geometric `G_F`-actions on `U_n^et` and every permitted path torsor factor continuously through `G_{F,T}`. For `x∈𝒳(R)`, define `globalEtaleAlbanese_n(x)=[P_n^et(b,x)]∈Sel_T(U_n)(ℚ_p)`, provided every chosen local condition contains the local path class of each permitted global point. In particular at the selected good place `v∉S` over p use the crystalline condition. Good places outside T have unramified path classes; additional bad-place conditions must be justified, not discarded. In the proper case take D empty, S containing bad reduction places, and `𝒳(R)=X(F)` by properness. At b the map is neutral if all selected conditions contain the neutral path class.

Integral global base point and chosen good place `v∉S` with completion K. T is finite. At each finite place outside T, inertia acts trivially on `U_n^et` and on every permitted geometric path torsor, giving continuous `G_{F,T}-actions`. Layer 2 [Galois structure and completion](#nc-2-etale-galois) supplies `G_F`-actions but does not prove this factorization; the [good-model inertia and arithmetic factorization](#good-model-unramified-paths) theorem supplies this in Layer 2. Every imposed local condition is coefficient-stable and contains the geometric local classes relevant to 𝒳(R); Selmer representability is an additional input when the scheme is used.

Take the geometric path with its continuous `G_F`-action and use the explicit inertia-triviality/factorization input to descend the group and torsor actions to `G_{F,T}`. Good-model factorization is [Good-model inertia and arithmetic factorization](#good-model-unramified-paths), not a consequence of [Galois structure and completion](#nc-2-etale-galois) alone. Use the torsor comparison of Layer 0 to form the nonabelian cohomology class. Verify membership at all imposed local conditions; then factor through the Selmer functor. For a proper curve apply the valuative criterion at the places outside S to identify the global domain.

- `globalEtaleAlbanese_localize`: At v, localization is `localEtaleAlbanese_n` of the image of x in `𝒳(O_K)`.

- `globalEtaleAlbanese_kummer_test`: For a proper curve at depth one, the underlying class is `κ(AJ_b(x))` in the rational Tate-module Selmer space.

### 5.5 Chabauty–Kim loci

<a id="nc-4-kim-loci"></a>

**The exact, period-image and closed-image loci.** Put `Y=𝒳(O_K)`, `j_n=localAlbanese_n`, `j_n^et=localEtaleAlbanese_n`, and `ℓ_n=selmerPeriod_n` on `ℚ_p`-points (interpreted in `Q_n(K)`). Define `crystallineLocus_n={y∈Y:∃s∈S_n(ℚ_p), loc_n(s)=j_n^et(y)}` and `deRhamLocus_n={y∈Y:∃s∈S_n(ℚ_p), ℓ_n(s)=j_n(y)}`. Let `Z_n` be the reduced Zariski closure of the geometric image of the full scheme morphism `ℓ_n` in `Res_{K/ℚ_p}Q_n`; define `closedDeRhamLocus_n={y∈Y:j_n(y)∈Z_n(ℚ_p)}`. Then `crystallineLocus_n⊆deRhamLocus_n⊆closedDeRhamLocus_n`. The first inclusion uses the [Compatibility of global paths, localization and periods](#nc-4-fundamental-diagram); equality requires a separate saturation/injectivity property of `D_n`. The second inclusion need not be equality: taking the geometric image closure does not promise a `ℚ_p`-rational Selmer lift. For a K-valued auxiliary morphism use its own geometric image closure and call the resulting enlarged locus by that morphism, not by an unexplained change of scalars. Set reductions take the supplied maps between point carriers, and for the closed locus the supplied point subset `Z_n(ℚ_p)`; computing that subset from the scheme morphism is a separate geometric interface.

The same domains, coefficient points, local conditions and good place are used in all maps. `Z_n` is the closure of the scheme image, not the p-adic closure and not merely the closure of rational source points.

Define the two inverse images of set-theoretic point images. Import the closed reduced subscheme attached to the scheme-image closure for the third definition. Apply the commutative comparison triangle and the inclusion of each source-point image in the geometric image closure.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `crystallineLocus_mem`: y belongs iff its crystalline class has a `ℚ_p`-rational global Selmer lift.
- `deRhamLocus_mem`: y belongs iff its de Rham period has a `ℚ_p`-rational Selmer preimage under `ℓ_n`.
- `closedDeRhamLocus_mem`: y belongs iff its period lies in the point subset of the geometric image closure.
- `kimLoci_inclusions`: Under `D_n∘j_n^et=j_n`, the three loci are included in order.
- `deRhamLocus_mono`: Enlarging the supplied global period image enlarges its inverse-image locus.
- `kimLoci_ext`: Equality of supplied point maps, images and closed-image point subsets gives equality of the corresponding loci.

**Checks.**

- `kimLoci_identity`: For any point map `j:Y→Q` and global period map `id_Q`, deRhamLocus(j,id)=Y.
- `kimLoci_empty_source`: For an empty global point carrier, deRhamLocus is empty, regardless of the local point map.
- `kimLoci_square_image`: On `ℚ`-points of `A¹` let `ℓ(u)=u²` and `j(t)=t`. The point −1 is absent from the image locus but belongs to the closed-image locus since the geometric scheme image is dense in `A¹`. This tests the image/closure distinction, not the p-adic topology.
- These are sets of local points, not sets of de Rham periods; no injectivity of `j_n` is assumed.
- A positive-dimensional or all-target closed image alone supplies no finiteness.

**Depth projection and change of conditions for the loci.** For `m≤n` suppose the quotient `U_n→U_m` induces maps `S_n→S_m`, `L_n→L_m` and `Q_n→Q_m` preserving every chosen local condition and commuting with the local and global period diagrams. No unconditional equality with the closed-image locus or with the rational point set is asserted.

**Global points lie in the Chabauty–Kim loci.** In the global good-reduction datum, with all imposed local conditions verified on every allowed geometric path, `ι_v(𝒳(R))⊆crystallineLocus_n⊆deRhamLocus_n⊆closedDeRhamLocus_n` for every `n≥1`. - For an open curve it bounds only the selected S-integral domain.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Introduction p. 95 and §3 p. 121.

<a id="nc-4-regular-pullback"></a>

**Pullback of regular period functions.** For `A_n=O(Q_n)` and `Y=𝒳(O_K)`, define `regularAlbanesePullback_n:A_n→(Y→K)` by `f↦(y↦f(j_n(y)))`. It is a K-algebra homomorphism, and [Iterated integrals as Albanese coordinates](#nc-4-iterated-coordinates) shows its image consists of the corresponding Coleman functions on ordinary integral discs. The algebra-valued refinement targets the imported Coleman function algebra once its carrier and the geometric evaluation bridge are available; the function-valued map itself is fully expressible on K-points viewed as K-algebra homomorphisms `A_n→K`. Disc-density implies that restriction of this map to any nonempty residue disc is injective. If f vanishes on the global Selmer geometric image closure, its pullback vanishes on the de Rham and closed-image loci, and hence on allowed global points.

The period variety is affine and geometrically integral over K; use the geometric K-variant of the image closure if `K≠ℚ_p`. Local point evaluation uses the Layer 2 word-path convention and Coleman membership uses §5.0.

Compose algebra-valued K-points with the coordinate algebra element f, preserving sums, products, constants and one. Apply [Iterated integrals as Albanese coordinates](#nc-4-iterated-coordinates) for Coleman membership. Apply [Kim density on every residue disc](#nc-4-residue-disc-density) for injectivity and [The exact, period-image and closed-image loci](#nc-4-kim-loci) definitions for the vanishing claim.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `regularAlbanesePullback_apply`: For a K-point `j(y):A_n→K`, the value at y is `j(y)(f)`.
- `regularAlbanesePullback_add`: Pullback of `f+g` is the sum of the two pullbacks.
- `regularAlbanesePullback_mul`: Pullback of fg is the product of the two pullbacks.
- `regularAlbanesePullback_const`: A scalar `r∈K` pulls back to the constant function r.
- `regularAlbanesePullback_reindex`: Reindexing local points along a map composes each pulled-back function with that map.
- `regularAlbanesePullback_injective_disc`: If `j(B)` is K-Zariski dense, pullback to B is injective.

**Checks.**

- `regularAlbanesePullback_affine_coordinate`: For `A=K[t]`, `Y=K` and `j(a)` evaluation at a, the pullback of t at a is a.
- `regularAlbanesePullback_product_test`: For the same family, the pullback of `t(t+1) at` a is `a(a+1)`, so an additive-only substitute fails.
- `regularAlbanesePullback_unit_test`: For that family over a nontrivial field, pullback of 1 is the nonzero constant 1, including `at a=0`; a derivative or normalized primitive is not this map.
- A nonzero regular f cannot pull back to the zero function on an entire nonempty residue disc.
- Individual vanishing values are allowed; injectivity is not injectivity of `j_n` on points.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §1, proof of Theorem 1 pp. 111–114; §3, p. 121.

<a id="nc-4-selmer-annihilator"></a>

**A regular equation from a small Selmer image.** Let k be a characteristic-zero field, S a finite-type affine k-scheme, Q a geometrically integral affine finite-type k-scheme, and `ℓ:S→Q` a k-morphism. Let Z be the reduced closed subscheme whose underlying set is the closure of the geometric image of `ℓ`. If dim S&lt;dim Q, then `dim Z≤dim S`, `Z≠Q`, and there exists a nonzero `f∈O(Q)` vanishing on Z. The same conclusion holds under the weaker hypothesis dim Z&lt;dim Q. Here dimensions are Krull dimensions of schemes, not vector-space ranks of their coordinate rings. Nilpotents of S are retained in `ℓ` but do not enlarge the topological image; f need only vanish on the reduced closure, not pull back to zero on a nonreduced S. For S empty take Z empty and `f=1`. At `k=ℚ_p`, apply this to `selmerPeriod_n`. For `K≠ℚ_p` one may apply it instead to the auxiliary K-morphism `(S_n)_K→Q_n` under `dim_{ℚ_p}S_n<dim_K Q_n`; merely having `dim S_n<dim Res Q_n` does not give this conclusion in `Q_n`.

Finite type is required for the image dimension bound; Q is integral and affine for a nonzero global regular equation. All dimensions and the image morphism are over the same stated field.

In coordinate algebras, take finite-type k-algebras A and B, B a domain, and `period:B→ₐ[k]A` with `ringKrullDim A<ringKrullDim B`. The dimension inequality gives `b≠0` with `period(b)=0`. To obtain this stronger choice for a nonreduced source, raise a nonzero equation for the reduced image closure to a power killing its nilpotent pullback; B being a domain preserves nonvanishing. This algebraic statement holds over any field.

For each irreducible component of the reduced source, use the generic fibre dimension formula to bound the dimension of its image closure. Take the finite union of component image closures; strict inequality makes it proper. A proper reduced closed subscheme of an affine integral scheme has a nonzero defining ideal; choose f in that ideal. For the K-variant use the Weil restriction counit and invariance of source dimension under field extension.

**Checks.**

- For `ℓ:A¹→A¹` given by `u↦u²`, dimensions are equal and `Z=Q`, so the theorem supplies no equation even though many k-points have no lift.
- For a constant map into `A²`, a coordinate vanishing at the image point is a possible nonzero f.
- For `B=k[t]`, `A=k[ε]/(ε²)` and `t↦ε`, t vanishes on the reduced image but does not pull back to zero; `t²` is a nonzero element of the coordinate-map kernel. Requiring the first reduced-image equation itself to pull back to zero would be false.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §3, dimension argument pp. 120–121; Conjecture 1 p. 96.

Use [The global Selmer period morphism](#nc-4-selmer-period); [SchemeAndStackFoundations](../SchemeAndStackFoundations/README.md) §0.7 (fibre-dimension formula); [SchemeAndStackFoundations](../SchemeAndStackFoundations/README.md) §0.7 (dimension of algebraic schemes); [ReductiveGroupsPartII](../ReductiveGroupsPartII/README.md) §RG2.0a.1 (Weil restriction and its adjunction); `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.zeroLocus`; [SchemeAndStackFoundations](../SchemeAndStackFoundations/README.md) Layer SF.0 (schemes and morphisms).

### 5.6 Strassmann's theorem on compact charts

<a id="strassmann-bound"></a>

**Strassmann on a compact analytic chart.** Use the restricted-series carrier, evaluation, rescaling and Strassmann theorem of RestrictedPowerSeries Layers 0–1 and §§2.1–2.4, on native `PowerSeries` with `PowerSeries.IsRestricted` and its restricted subring. Its generic theorem bounds distinct roots of any nonzero restricted series over a complete nonarchimedean field, at any positive radius and in complete isometric field extensions. For a finite `K/ℚ_p`, an ordinary integral residue chart `t∈πO_K` and `f(t)=Σa_n t^n` analytic on the geometric open unit disc, construct the supplied unit-radius restricted series `f(πs)=Σa_nπ^n s^n` on `O_K`. Prove its evaluation agrees with the chart pullback, that it remains nonzero, and that its number of distinct roots is at most the largest index N attaining `max_n |a_nπ^n|`, by the supplied theorem. This residue-chart comparison and its Chabauty zero-set application are the targets here.

The original series is nonzero and `|π|<1`; the rescaled coefficients tend to zero. Since `π≠0`, every nonzero coefficient remains nonzero after rescaling, so the rescaled series has a largest maximizing index.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `residueChart.rescale`: Produce the restricted series on the supplied carrier and identify its evaluation with the chart pullback.
- `residueChart.nonzero`: Preserve nonvanishing under the nonzero rescaling.
- `residueChart.zeroBound`: Apply the compact chart bound.

**Checks.**

- For `f(s)=s−a` with `|a|≤1`, `N=1` and there is exactly one root.
- For `f=1`, `N=0` and there are no roots.
- For `f=0`, N is undefined and the zero bound is inapplicable.
- Analyticity on the full open geometric disc alone does not yield this bound until the compact K-point chart is specified.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §3, proof of Theorem 1, pp. 119–121; compact-chart specialization of its zero argument.

Use [RestrictedPowerSeries](../RestrictedPowerSeries/README.md) Layers 0–1 and §§2.1–2.4 (native restricted-series carriers, evaluation, rescaling and Strassmann); [Residue discs and logarithmic ends](#residue-discs-logarithmic-ends); `AnalyticAt`; [Coleman integration on a proper curve with good reduction](#proper-curve-coleman-charts).

### 5.7 Chabauty–Kim finiteness

<a id="nc-4-finite-annihilator-locus"></a>

**Finiteness under discwise nonvanishing.** Let `K/ℚ_p` be finite and let `Y=𝒳(O_K)` be the integral tube in a smooth proper good-reduction compactification with finite étale boundary removed. Let `j:Y→Q(K)` have Coleman-analytic regular-function pullbacks on each ordinary residue disc. If Z⊊Q is a closed subset and some `f∈O(Q)`, `f≠0`, vanishes on Z and `f∘j` is not identically zero on each nonempty integral residue disc, then `{y∈Y:j(y)∈Z(K)}` is finite. In particular the image-defined locus contained in that set is finite. Every disc has K-points parametrized by `m_K=πO_K`; the pullback on the open geometric disc has a convergent power series, and substituting `t=πs` produces a nonzero restricted series on the compact closed unit disc `O_K`. Strassmann then gives finitely many zeros in each disc, and there are finitely many residue discs. The statement supplies finiteness, not an effective uniform bound or equality with global points.

Finite extension K is essential for compactness and a finite residue field; the full `C_p`-disc is not the domain. The local functions are analytic on the whole ordinary open geometric residue disc and nonzero on each integral disc. Only integral discs disjoint from the removed boundary are used; no open punctured-disc compactness assertion is made.

The compact-chart zero theorem applies over any nontrivially normed field: if D is compact, f is analytic on a neighborhood of each point of D, and f has no zero germ at any point of D, then `{t∈D:f(t)=0}` is finite. Isolated zeros and compactness prove this formulation without a connectedness assumption. Whole-disc analyticity and nonvanishing on every subdisc supply its germ hypothesis in the curve application; local analyticity and a single nonzero value alone do not.

Use the good-reduction residue-disc parameterization of [Residue discs and logarithmic ends](#residue-discs-logarithmic-ends) and the finiteness of 𝒳(k). Rescale `t=πs`: convergence at a real radius strictly between `|π|` and 1 implies the rescaled coefficients tend to zero. Apply [Strassmann on a compact analytic chart](#strassmann-bound) to each nonzero rescaled series. Take a finite union of finite zero sets, then its subset cut out by Z.

**Checks.**

- On a rescaled compact chart, the pullback `s−a` for `a∈O_K` has exactly the single zero a; the nonzero constant pullback has none.
- If `f∘j` vanishes identically on one disc, that disc may remain wholly in the locus and the criterion does not apply.
- An arbitrary nonzero function analytic only on an open disc need not have finitely many zeros throughout that geometric disc.
- A locally constant function on `ℤ_p` that is zero on `pℤ_p` and one elsewhere is locally analytic and nonzero, but has infinitely many zeros. It violates the zero-germ hypothesis of the compact-chart zero theorem.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §3, the Coleman-function zero-set argument, p. 121.

Use [Pullback of regular period functions](#nc-4-regular-pullback); [Residue discs and logarithmic ends](#residue-discs-logarithmic-ends); [Residue-disc fibre](#nc-2-rigid-fibre); [Strassmann on a compact analytic chart](#strassmann-bound); [Coleman functions and normalized primitives](#coleman-functions-primitives).

<a id="nc-4-dimension-finiteness"></a>

**Conditional Chabauty–Kim finiteness.** Let `X/ℚ` be smooth geometrically connected hyperbolic, with integral global base point b and the good models, ramification set and local conditions of [The global étale path-class map](#nc-4-global-etale-albanese). Choose `p∉S` and depth `n≥1`. Assume the global Selmer functor of Layer 4 is represented by a finite-type affine scheme `S_n` and the crystalline comparison gives the morphism `ℓ_n:S_n→Q_n at K=ℚ_p`. If `dim S_n<dim Q_n`, then `closedDeRhamLocus_n`, `deRhamLocus_n` and `crystallineLocus_n` are finite, and consequently `𝒳(ℤ[S⁻¹])` is finite. If X is proper, `X(ℚ)` is finite. One may replace the inequality by a proper geometric image closure together with a nonzero regular annihilator; Kim discwise density supplies the needed nonvanishing. No assertion that a depth satisfying the inequality exists is included: Kim Conjecture 1 and motivic conjectural dimension inputs remain hypotheses, not theorems of Layer 5. For a number field F, use [Finiteness under discwise nonvanishing](#nc-4-finite-annihilator-locus) with its explicit K-nonvanishing hypothesis, or the auxiliary K-morphism bound `dim S_n<dim_K Q_n`; a bound against `dim_{ℚ_p}Res Q_n` alone is insufficient without stronger Weil-restriction discwise density.

All local conditions contain the allowed global path classes, including bad places. Use the endpoint-compatible path comparison, effective torsor descent, all-algebra local invariant lifting and Selmer representability constructed in Layers 2 and 4. The strict dimension inequality is a verified or assumed mathematical input, never silently concluded from the theorem.

The affine finite-chart form has the following hypotheses. For finite-type K-algebras `A=O(S)` and integral `B=O(Q)`, the period morphism is `period:B→ₐ[K]A` and a local point is `j(x):B→ₐ[K]K`. The closed period locus consists of x whose evaluation kills `ker(period)`. A strict Krull-dimension inequality, finitely many compact charts covering Y, analytic evaluation of every b in B, and absence of a zero germ for every `b≠0` make that locus finite. A set of global points in Y with witnesses `j(x)=a∘period` is finite as well. This form works over any nontrivially normed field satisfying the explicit chart hypotheses; for curves, residue-disc density and the preceding geometric comparisons supply them.

Use [A regular equation from a small Selmer image](#nc-4-selmer-annihilator) to choose a nonzero regular equation for the geometric Selmer period image closure. Use [Kim density on every residue disc](#nc-4-residue-disc-density) and [Pullback of regular period functions](#nc-4-regular-pullback) to obtain a nonzero analytic function on every integral disc. Apply [Finiteness under discwise nonvanishing](#nc-4-finite-annihilator-locus) and the three locus inclusions. Use [Global points lie in the Chabauty–Kim loci](#nc-4-rational-integral-containment) and the injective field embedding to deduce global finiteness.

**Checks.**

- For a proper genus-g curve at depth one the target has dimension g; the source dimension is a Selmer dimension, not automatically the Mordell–Weil rank.
- The statement applies even when the period map itself is not injective.
- A zero-dimensional refinement excluding a global Kummer class proves finiteness only of its own locus. Every application to the full global domain requires the stated Kummer-image containment at every place.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Conjecture 1 and following conditional implication, p. 96; §3 proof pp. 120–121.

Use [A regular equation from a small Selmer image](#nc-4-selmer-annihilator); [Kim density on every residue disc](#nc-4-residue-disc-density); [Finiteness under discwise nonvanishing](#nc-4-finite-annihilator-locus); [Global points lie in the Chabauty–Kim loci](#nc-4-rational-integral-containment).

### 5.8 Abelian logarithms

<a id="abelian-logarithm"></a>

**Local abelian logarithm.** For every abelian variety `A/K` over a finite extension `K/ℚ_p`, construct the continuous locally analytic homomorphism `abelianLog: A(K)→Lie(A)(K)`, with differential the identity, finite torsion kernel and a local analytic inverse on a sufficiently small open subgroup. Good reduction is not required. Use the smooth Néron model supplied by NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties §1.1 and the integral commutative formal group, identity chart and normalized logarithm of HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions §§1.15a–1.16. These formal constructions, including their convergence, inverse and change-of-parameter laws, are supplied inputs.

Choose a deep congruence subgroup H identified by `SmoothGroup.formalIdentityChart` with an ideal on which `formalLogarithm_smallIdeal_equiv` is an analytic group isomorphism. The finite-index quotient `A(K)/H` has an exponent m. Define `log_A(P)=m⁻¹ log_H(mP)`, with values in the intrinsic Lie algebra using the differential of the chart. Additivity of the supplied logarithm proves independence of m; its uniqueness and parameter-change laws prove independence of the chart. Injectivity on H gives the torsion kernel, and finite index bounds that torsion inside `A[m]`. This uses local compactness, not global finite generation. Extend homomorphisms through the Néron models to prove functoriality; normalized uniqueness gives compatibility with every finite extension of K.

Construct the unique homomorphism of `ℂ_p`-Lie groups `A(ℂ_p)→Lie(A)(ℂ_p)` with differential the identity. It restricts to these finite-extension logarithms and gives their continuous locally analytic extension to all `ℂ_p`-points. Use that the quotient by any open subgroup of `A(ℂ_p)` is torsion, as in Katz–Rabinoff–Zureick-Brown §3.3 and the proof of Proposition 3.16. Finite-extension points alone are not the carrier of this map. The pairing `⟨P,ω⟩=ω(log_A(P))` for invariant differentials has torsion left kernel and zero right kernel over finite K; the image contains a full Lie lattice. All base-change and morphism comparisons use this same pairing.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `abelianLog.add`: The logarithm is additive.
- `abelianLog.derivative`: Its differential at zero is the identity.
- `abelianLog.kernel`: Its kernel on `A(K)` is the finite torsion subgroup.
- `abelianLog.functorial`: Respect every abelian-variety homomorphism over K.
- `abelianLog.formal`: Restrict to the supplied normalized formal logarithm on H.
- `abelianLog.baseChange`: Respect finite extensions and the restriction of the `ℂ_p` logarithm.
- `abelianLog.cp`: The compatible locally analytic logarithm on all `A(ℂ_p)`.
- `abelianLog.pairing`: Evaluation against invariant differentials, with the stated two kernels.
- `abelianLog.unique`: Agreement on an open subgroup determines the logarithm over finite `K/ℚ_p` uniquely.

**Checks.**

- `log_A(0)=0`, and every torsion point maps to zero. For `E:y²+y=x³−x²` over `ℚ₅`, `(0,0)` has order 5, so the global logarithm has no global inverse.
- Split multiplicative elliptic reduction still has a Néron formal chart and a deep subgroup on which the logarithm is an isomorphism. A smooth proper group model is not required.
- The supplied multiplicative formal logarithm is `log(1+t)`, and the additive one is T. A zero series fails the identity differential condition.
- In dimension zero the Lie algebra is zero and the abelian variety is the trivial group.
- A `ℂ_p`-point need not be defined over a finite extension of `ℚ_p`; `abelianLog.cp` has that point in its domain and agrees with the formal logarithm near zero.

The construction and its conventions follow [Eric Katz, Joseph Rabinoff and David Zureick-Brown](#reference-krzb), §3.3, Definition 3.8, pp. 18–19, and proof of Proposition 3.16, p. 22; [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Introduction, p. 93. The formal-group inputs are HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions §§1.15a–1.16, with Katz Appendix Lemma′, pp. 501–502, and Mattuck Theorem 7, §§13–14, pp. 114–118, as located there.

Use [HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions](../HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions/README.md) §§1.15a–1.16; [NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties](../NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties/README.md) §1.1; [TauCetiRoadmap.JacobianChallenge](../JacobianChallenge/README.md) Layer E; [AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli](../AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli/README.md) §A3.2 (finite multiplication kernels).

<a id="coleman-abelian-comparison"></a>

**Coleman and abelian logarithm comparison.** For a smooth proper geometrically connected good-reduction curve `X/K` over finite `K/ℚ_p`, with `b∈X(K)`, identify the Coleman integral from b to x of `ω` with the pairing of the corresponding invariant differential on J with `log_J([x−b])`. Respect the depth-one period sign and Abel–Jacobi pullback. Prove equality by agreement of local derivatives and Frobenius-normalized transport, rather than choosing unrelated primitives.

The curve is proper and has good reduction; the base point fixes both normalizations. The equality holds after every finite extension and on `X(ℂ_p)` through the same `abelianLog.cp` and the supplied Coleman evaluation. This target owns the generic equality; its depth-one tensor-path specialization is §5.9.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `colemanAbelian.integral`: State the normalized equality for every regular one-form.
- `colemanAbelian.basepoint`: Changing base point subtracts the corresponding logarithm.
- `colemanAbelian.depthOne`: Identify the same equality with the depth-one Albanese quotient.

**Checks.**

- At `x=b` both sides are zero.
- Changing b to b′ changes the integral by the constant integral from b to b′.
- Finite-extension evaluation and `ℂ_p` evaluation agree under the fixed embedding and logarithm normalization.
- An open-curve logarithmic differential has a boundary component and requires the generalized-Jacobian version.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Introduction, p. 93 (the abelian logarithm comparison); §2, pp. 115–117 (the étale realization); [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), §5.1, pp. 917–919.

### 5.9 Depth one: the abelian logarithm

<a id="nc-4-depth-one-period"></a>

**The depth-one Albanese and abelian logarithm.** For a proper smooth geometrically connected genus-g curve `X/ℚ` with `b∈X(ℚ)` and good reduction at p, use Layer 2's abelianization `U_1^et=V_pJ` and the filtered de Rham identification `U_1^dR=H¹_dR(X/ℚ_p)^∨`, `H_1=Ann(H⁰(X,Ω¹))`, `Q_1≃Lie(J)`. With the Lie identification normalized to the endpoint Kummer/Abel–Jacobi comparison, the local crystalline path class is `κ_p(AJ_b(x))` and the identified de Rham period is `log_J(AJ_b(x))`. Pairing with `ω∈H⁰(X,Ω¹)` gives the single Coleman integral `∫_b^xω`. Fix the convention explicitly: in Layer 2's universal connection `d−∑T_iω_i` the forward Frobenius path has coefficient `+I_i`; our torsor ratio has representative `I⁻¹γ`, so its raw first-level coordinate is `γ_i−I_i`. The Lie comparison sends the raw quotient coordinate with the compensating sign to the usual logarithm; it does not identify `+I_i` with that raw torsor ratio. This sign normalization leaves linear-subspace loci unchanged. For `X=C−D` with nonempty reduced finite étale D, the open-curve identifications use [Generalized Jacobian of a reduced boundary](#reduced-boundary-generalized-jacobian), [Finite étale and Tate-module comparison for the generalized Jacobian](#generalized-jacobian-etale-comparison) and [Filtered de Rham comparison for the generalized Jacobian](#generalized-jacobian-derham-comparison); the local comparison carries their good-reduction pair hypotheses. The proper abelian logarithm result in this target does not replace these toric inputs.

Proper curve and Layer 2's de Rham H¹/Hodge–Abel–Jacobi bridge; good-reduction rational Tate-module comparison. Use the same path direction `b→x` and the displayed ratio convention in every realization.

Import the Layer 2 depth-one group and cohomology bridge; do not reconstruct J, the Tate module or the Hodge exact sequence. Use [Depth-one Kummer and Selmer comparison](#nc-3-depth-one-selmer-comparison) for the Kummer class. Use [Local abelian logarithm](#abelian-logarithm) and [Coleman and abelian logarithm comparison](#coleman-abelian-comparison), transporting the raw coordinate sign through the normalized Lie identification.

**Checks.**

- Depth one here is Kim `U_2`, and `Q_1` has dimension g; depth zero is trivial.
- For `x=b` every pairing is zero; for a differential the derivative of the paired period is `ω`, with the above sign normalization.
- The open-curve target includes puncture directions and needs the generalized Jacobian; deleting them would change the definition.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Introduction, bottom of the tower p. 93 and abelian diagram p. 95; §1 word conventions pp. 109–112.

### 5.10 The Mordell–Weil logarithmic span

<a id="padic-closure-dimension"></a>

**Mordell–Weil logarithmic span and annihilators.** Let `J/F` be an abelian variety and v a good-reduction place above p. Identify the Lie algebra over `ℚ_p` of the closure of `J(F)` in `J(K_v)` with the `ℚ_p`-span `W₀` of its logarithms, and put `W=K_v·W₀` inside `Lie J(K_v)`. Prove `dim_(K_v) W≤r`, where r is the Mordell–Weil rank, and construct its annihilator in invariant differentials with dimension `g−dim_(K_v) W`. The closure is a `ℚ_p`-analytic subgroup and need not be a `K_v`-analytic subgroup; its `K_v`-linear hull is W. For a curve embedded in J, pair these differentials with Abel–Jacobi pullback and Coleman integration. No equality `dim W=r` is asserted without a localization-independence hypothesis.

Finite generation of `J(F)` is used. The closure Lie algebra uses `ℚ_p`; its scalar hull and the annihilator use `K_v`. The natural map `K_v⊗_(ℚ_p) W₀→Lie J(K_v)` may have a kernel, so a tensor product is not silently identified with its image.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `mordellWeil.logSpan`: Define the localization span.
- `mordellWeil.logDim_le_rank`: Bound its dimension.
- `mordellWeil.annihilator`: Compute the annihilator dimension.
- `mordellWeil.annihilatingIntegral`: Every rational curve point has zero normalized integral against an annihilator.

**Checks.**

- For rank zero `W=0` and every regular differential annihilates it.
- For rank one, an infinite-order generator has nonzero logarithm because the kernel is torsion, so `dim W=1`. For rank at least two, linear dependence of localized logarithms can make dim W smaller than r.
- When `r=g`, a zero-dimensional annihilator requires the additional log-span isomorphism.
- Over a proper finite extension `K_v/ℚ_p`, a one-dimensional `ℚ_p` logarithmic span is not itself a `K_v`-line; take its `K_v`-linear hull before computing the annihilator.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Introduction, p. 93 (the abelian logarithm comparison); §2, pp. 115–117 (the étale realization); [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), §3.1, pp. 901–905.

### 5.11 Depth one: classical Chabauty

<a id="nc-4-depth-one-locus"></a>

**The precise classical Chabauty comparison.** In [The depth-one Albanese and abelian logarithm](#nc-4-depth-one-period)'s proper setting, let `W_S⊆Lie(J)(ℚ_p)` be the image of the linear global Selmer space under the normalized logarithmic period map, and `W_MW=span_{ℚ_p}{log_J(P):P∈J(ℚ)}`. The de Rham image locus at depth one is `{x∈X(ℚ_p):log_J(AJ_b(x))∈W_S}`, equivalently the common zero set of `∫_b^xω` for all linear forms `ω∈Ann(W_S)`. The image is already a closed linear subspace, so its period-image and geometric-closed-image loci coincide in this linear setting. For the usual local conditions the Mordell–Weil Kummer map lies in the Selmer space, giving `W_MW⊆W_S`; if additional conditions are imposed, this containment must be an explicit hypothesis. The classical common-annihilator Chabauty locus is obtained by replacing `W_S` with `W_MW`, and is a subset of the Selmer locus under that containment. If `W_S=W_MW`, the two loci agree. A rank bound rank J(ℚ)&lt;g gives `dim W_MW<g` and classical finiteness by [Mordell–Weil logarithmic span and annihilators](#padic-closure-dimension) and [Strassmann on a compact analytic chart](#strassmann-bound), but gives finiteness of the full depth-one Selmer locus only with `dim W_S<g (e.g. W_S=W_MW)`. No vanishing of a Tate–Shafarevich contribution or equality Selmer=Mordell–Weil is assumed without a stated extra input. The common-annihilator locus is logarithmically saturated; it is not asserted equal to `AJ_b⁻¹` of the literal topological closure of `J(ℚ)`.

All [The depth-one Albanese and abelian logarithm](#nc-4-depth-one-period) hypotheses; the represented depth-one Selmer space and period map are linear over `ℚ_p`. Containment of the whole Mordell–Weil Kummer image is needed when comparing its classical locus with a refined Selmer locus. Equality of the two period subspaces is a separate hypothesis.

Use the linear rational Tate-module Selmer and Kummer comparison of [Depth-one Kummer and Selmer comparison](#nc-3-depth-one-selmer-comparison). Identify the first de Rham map with the logarithm by [The depth-one Albanese and abelian logarithm](#nc-4-depth-one-period). Use the double-annihilator identity to express membership in `W_S` by all annihilating linear forms. Use the annihilating differentials of [Mordell–Weil logarithmic span and annihilators](#padic-closure-dimension) and the residue-disc zero bound of [Strassmann on a compact analytic chart](#strassmann-bound) for classical finiteness; retain the separate Selmer dimension input.

**Checks.**

- If `W_S=Lie(J)` and `W_MW` is proper, the full Selmer locus is `X(ℚ_p)` while the classical locus can be finite.
- For `W=0` the period-image locus is the zero logarithm fibre; for `W=Lie(J)` it is the whole local curve.
- The annihilator formulation preserves constants of integration through the same global base point b.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Introduction, comparison with classical Chabauty p. 95; §3, p. 121.

Use [The exact, period-image and closed-image loci](#nc-4-kim-loci); [The depth-one Albanese and abelian logarithm](#nc-4-depth-one-period); [Depth-one Kummer and Selmer comparison](#nc-3-depth-one-selmer-comparison); [Mordell–Weil logarithmic span and annihilators](#padic-closure-dimension); [Strassmann on a compact analytic chart](#strassmann-bound); `Subspace.forall_mem_dualAnnihilator_apply_eq_zero_iff`; `Subspace.finrank_add_finrank_dualAnnihilator_eq`.

### 5.12 Away-place images and proper Selmer cuts

<a id="finite-away-kummer-image"></a>

**Finite away-place Kummer images.** For a proper smooth curve over a finite extension `L/Q_l` with `l≠p`, and a chosen rational base point, prove that its finite-depth `ℚ_p`-unipotent Kummer map on `X(L)` has finite image. Use a regular proper model and its smooth reduction points; points with the same reduction have identical prime-to-l nilpotent path class, and the `ℚ_p`-unipotent quotient factors through that path system. Construct the finite image as the set of classes, independent of the regular model. For the integral affine domains of a regular minimal model with horizontal boundary removed, prove finite image by local constancy on the compact integral domain, as in BDCKW §2.5. Potential good reduction makes proper paths potentially unramified. For an affine pair it does so only when the pair has good reduction after extension and both endpoints remain integral in that pair; the integral domain in the original model alone does not imply this.

The coefficient prime p differs from the local residue characteristic l. Properness gives the finite cover of all local points; the affine statement concerns the specified compact integral domain, rather than all points of the affine curve.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `localKummer.finiteImage`: Give the finite image on the domain.
- `localKummer.sameReduction`: Identify classes in one smooth reduction class.
- `localKummer.modelIndependent`: Preserve the image under dominating regular models.

**Checks.**

- The base point maps to the neutral class.
- Points in the same smooth reduction class have equal finite-depth image.
- The `p=l` crystalline case is not this finite-image theorem.
- On `y²=x³−25x` with `b=(−4,6)`, the integral endpoint `(0,0)` gives a nonzero central local class at 5 for `p=13`; finite image does not mean neutral image or potential unramifiedness.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim and Akio Tamagawa](#reference-kt), Theorem 0.1, Corollary 0.2 and proof, author pp. 1–5; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Ishai Dan-Cohen, Minhyong Kim and Stefan Wewers](#reference-bdckw-2018v4), §§2.1–2.5, pp. 8–9; [Francesca Bianchi](#reference-bianchi), §2.1.1, pp. 7–9.

Use [Good-model inertia and arithmetic factorization](#good-model-unramified-paths); [InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups](../InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups/README.md) Layer IG.1 (arithmetic fundamental groups, inertia and specialization).

<a id="mordell-weil-selmer-cut"></a>

**Proper-curve Mordell–Weil Selmer cut.** For a proper good-reduction curve `X/Q`, define the depth-n stringent Selmer variety by the crystalline condition at p, the finite local Kummer images at every bad place `v≠p` and the inverse image of the rational Mordell–Weil Kummer subspace at depth one. Represent it by the corresponding closed fibre intersections, prove rational-point containment and compatibility with localization and depth maps, and identify its depth-one dimension with the dimension of that rational Kummer subspace. Use the same cut in the central fibre dimension induction. This avoids replacing the whole Bloch–Kato Selmer dimension by the Mordell–Weil rank.

The finite local images are closed points in their represented local cohomology spaces. The rational Kummer subspace is supplied as a vector subfunctor.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `properSelmer.mwCut`: Define the closed depth-one inverse image.
- `properSelmer.localImageCut`: Intersect the bad-place conditions.
- `properSelmer.rationalPath`: Include every rational path class.
- `properSelmer.centralFibre`: Restrict the linear central-difference calculation to the same cut.

**Checks.**

- At depth one, a nonzero Sha contribution to the full Selmer group is removed by the Mordell–Weil cut.
- An empty local image makes the corresponding intersection empty.
- Replacing a local image by all unramified classes can enlarge the locus.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), §3.1, pp. 901–905; §4, pp. 906–917; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Ishai Dan-Cohen, Minhyong Kim and Stefan Wewers](#reference-bdckw-2018v4), §2, pp. 8–12.

<a id="tangential-albanese"></a>

**Tangential Albanese and period maps.** With an integral unit-tangential base point, construct the local étale Kummer map, global path-class map, de Rham Albanese map and crystalline period morphism at every finite depth. Prove their fundamental localization/comparison square on all coefficient algebras. Integral interior endpoints lie in the prescribed Selmer conditions. Their Coleman coordinates are the regularized iterated integrals normalized by the tangent, and the same every-subdisc density and compact-chart finite-zero argument applies to interior residue charts.

Use the tangential realization and Selmer constructions of Layers 2 and 4. Removed boundary points are not added to the integral endpoint domain.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `tangentialAlbanese.local`: Construct the local class map.
- `tangentialAlbanese.global`: Construct the global class map.
- `tangentialAlbanese.period`: Give the crystalline-to-de Rham period.
- `tangentialAlbanese.square`: Prove the fundamental diagram and finite-depth compatibility.

**Checks.**

- On `P¹−{0,1,∞}`, depth-one coordinates are log z and `log(1−z)`.
- At depth zero the target is a point.
- A boundary point is excluded as an ordinary integral endpoint.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Ishai Dan-Cohen, Minhyong Kim and Stefan Wewers](#reference-bdckw-2018v4), §§2–3, pp. 8–14; [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §§1 and 3, pp. 91–106 and 115–121.

### Examples

A regular equation cutting out a proper Selmer image pulls back to a Coleman function. Density on every nonempty open subdisc makes that pullback nonzero on every local chart. Ordinary integral points of a good-reduction curve over a finite `K/ℚ_p` occupy compact parameter charts `t∈πO_K`. If `f(t)` is analytic on the geometric open unit disc, substitution `t=πs` gives a restricted series on `O_K` with coefficients tending to zero. Strassmann uses the largest index N of a coefficient of maximal norm. For `f(s)=s−a` with `|a|≤1`, `N=1` and there is one root; for `f=1` there are none; `f=0` has no such N. A statement about a whole geometric open disc requires this compact-chart step before giving a finite bound on K-points.

An auxiliary affine chart need not be the complement of a second rational residue disc. Over `F₂`, the smooth genus-two curve `y²+y=x⁵+x³+1` has no affine F₂-points: `at x=0` or 1 its right side is 1, whereas `y²+y=0`. Its smooth compactification has the single rational point at infinity. The characteristic-two derivative with respect to y is 1, so the affine model is smooth. A proper smooth lift over `Z₂` has only that rational reduction disc, and an auxiliary finite étale divisor of higher degree provides the affine chart used for Coleman transport.

At depth one over `ℚ_p`, let W be the `ℚ_p`-span of logarithms of the rational Mordell–Weil group. The classical Chabauty annihilators have dimension g−dim W, which is at least g−r. Rank `r=g` does not by itself show `W=Lie J`. Torsion points contribute zero logarithm. An infinite-order rank-one generator has nonzero logarithm; for higher rank, independent rational generators can have linearly dependent logarithms. Over a larger finite extension K, distinguish the `ℚ_p`-analytic closure from the K-linear span of its logarithms; their dimensions use different fields.

For stringent proper-curve Selmer conditions, impose the finite away-place Kummer images and the Mordell–Weil depth-one subspace. The full Bloch–Kato Selmer group can have an extra Sha direction. Replacing its dimension by r in a depth-two estimate would remove a direction without imposing the cut. Kim–Tamagawa gives finite away-place images for proper curves when the residue prime differs from the coefficient prime; the p-adic crystalline place is a separate condition.

For `K/ℚ_p` of degree d, compare both sides after Weil restriction to `ℚ_p`, multiplying the K-dimension of the de Rham target by d. Comparing that number with an unadjusted K-dimension on the Selmer side would manufacture a false strict inequality.


The group-frame identity `I·(I⁻¹γ)=γ` fixes the right period direction before passing to the homogeneous coset; it makes no normality assumption on `F⁰U`.

The proved period example applies right Hodge translation `γ↦γh` for `h∈H` and verifies equality in the homogeneous coset relation for every subgroup H, including nonnormal ones.
