## Layer 6: Quadratic Chabauty and height equations

Turn rational divisor correspondences into depth-two quotients and mixed extensions. The local height equation keeps every bad-place correction and compares it with a global bilinear height; determinants and equivariant features give usable equations.

### 6.1 Mixed extensions and Nekovář's p-adic heights

<a id="mixed-extensions"></a>

**Mixed extensions with graded pieces `ℚ_p`, V, `ℚ_p(1)`.** Let G be a profinite group (`G_T` for a finite set of places T, or a decomposition group `G_v`) and `W₀,…,W_n` continuous finite-dimensional `ℚ_p`-representations with `Hom_G(Wᵢ,Wⱼ)=0` for `i<j`. A mixed extension with graded pieces `W₀,…,W_n` is a representation M with a filtration `M=M₀⊃M₁⊃…⊃M_(n+1)=0` and isomorphisms `αᵢ:Mᵢ/Mᵢ₊₁≅Wᵢ`; morphisms are filtered isomorphisms compatible with the `αᵢ`. Let `U(W₀,…,W_n)` be the unipotent group of block unitriangular automorphisms of `⊕Wᵢ` preserving the descending filtration `⊕ⱼ≥ᵢWⱼ`: its blocks map `Wᵢ` to Wⱼ only for `j≥i`, and its diagonal blocks are identities. This fixes the matrix direction independently of the words upper and lower. Give it the induced continuous G-action. Sending M to the right U-torsor Φ(M) of filtered isomorphisms `f:⊕Wᵢ≅M` inducing `αᵢ⁻¹` on the graded pieces, with right action `f·u=f∘u` and semilinear action `g(f)=g_M∘f∘g_⊕W⁻¹` defines a bijection Φ from isomorphism classes of mixed extensions to `H¹(G,U(W₀,…,W_n))`, which identifies crystalline (respectively semistable) mixed extensions at v|p with `H¹_f` (respectively `H¹_st`). For `(W₀,W₁,W₂)=(ℚ_p,V,ℚ_p(1))`, U is a central extension `1→ℚ_p(1)→U→V⊕Hom(V,ℚ_p(1))→1`, `π₁(M)=φ₀,₁(M)` and `π₂(M)=φ₁,₂(M)` are the two adjacent extension classes, and `M↦M*(1)` is an involution. Partial Baer sums `M+₁,ₙ₋₁N` (when `φ₁,ₙ₋₁` agree) and `M+₂,ₙN` (when `φ₂,ₙ` agree) are defined, and a function is bi-additive when it is additive for both.

G profinite; the `Wᵢ` continuous and finite-dimensional with `Hom_G(Wᵢ,Wⱼ)=0` for `i<j`, which forces mixed extensions to have no nontrivial automorphisms and `H⁰(G,U)=1`. The crystalline and semistable classifications require the graded pieces themselves to be crystalline or semistable, respectively. The dual-and-twist involution on the three-piece type uses the fixed Jacobian polarization `V≅V*(1)`; for arbitrary graded pieces duality instead reverses and dualizes the type. Finite-type representability for `G=G_T` additionally uses finite-dimensional continuous cohomology of the successive Hom representations and the central representability hypotheses of Layer 4; invariant vanishing alone is not a finiteness assertion.

Φ(M) is a torsor because two filtered isomorphisms inducing the `αᵢ` differ by an element of U; the G-action is by conjugation. The inverse twists `⊕Wᵢ` by a torsor. The central extension description is the block structure for `n=2`. The vanishing of `Hom_G(Wᵢ,Wⱼ)` for `i<j` kills automorphisms. For `G=G_T` combine it with the finite-cohomology and central representability hypotheses of Layer 4 to obtain affine finite-type representability.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `MixedExtension`: Mixed extensions with given graded pieces and their isomorphism classes.
- `MixedExtension.classify`: The bijection Φ with `H¹(G,U(W₀,…,W_n))`, compatible with the crystalline and semistable conditions.
- `MixedExtension.pi1` and `MixedExtension.pi2`: The adjacent extension classes in `H¹(G,V)` and `H¹(G,Hom(V,ℚ_p(1)))`.
- `MixedExtension.dual`: The involution `M↦M*(1)`.
- `MixedExtension.baerSum₁` and `MixedExtension.baerSum₂`: The partial Baer sums.
- `MixedExtension.dcris`: For v|p and crystalline M, the mixed extension `D_cris(M)` of filtered φ-modules with graded pieces `ℚ_p`, `V_dR=D_cris(V)`, `D_cris(ℚ_p(1))`.

**Checks.**

- For `n=1`, mixed extensions of `W₀` by `W₁` are `Ext¹(W₀,W₁)=H¹(G,Hom(W₀,W₁))`, and `U=Hom(W₀,W₁)` is a vector group.
- The split extension `ℚ_p⊕V⊕ℚ_p(1)` corresponds to the trivial class of `H¹(G,U)`, and `π₁`, `π₂` of it vanish.
- With `W₀=W₁=ℚ_p` and trivial G, the split extension has the nontrivial automorphisms `(x,y)↦(x,y+λx)`. Nevertheless both its isomorphism-class set and `H¹(1,𝔾_a)` have one element: the Hom-vanishing hypothesis removes automorphisms, rather than being necessary for the class-set bijection. A groupoid equivalence retains these automorphisms.
- For `G=G_v` with `v∤p` and `V=V_pJ`, `H¹(G_v,V)=0`, so every mixed extension is `V⊕N` with N an extension of `ℚ_p` by `ℚ_p(1)`, and Φ identifies classes with `H¹(G_v,ℚ_p(1))`.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan and Netan Dogra](#reference-bd1), §4.1, Definitions 4.1, 4.2 and 4.4 and Remark 4.3, p. 13; §4.2, Definitions 4.5–4.6 and Lemma 4.7, p. 14; §4.3, p. 14; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), §3.3, Definitions 3.3–3.4, p. 904; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan and Netan Dogra](#reference-bdii), §3.1, author pp. 10–12.

Use [Torsors under U with compatible G-action are classified by `H¹(G, U)`](#nc-3-torsor-classification); [SelmerIwasawaCohomology](../SelmerIwasawaCohomology/README.md) Layer 4 (finite conditions); [PadicPeriodRings](../PadicPeriodRings/README.md) §§4.2–4.3 (period tensor invariants and admissibility); [De Rham exactness and Hodge–Tate grading](#linear-period-exactness).

<a id="nekovar-local-heights"></a>

**Nekovář's local heights.** Let `X/ℚ` be a smooth projective curve with good reduction at p, `V=V_pJ` (equivalently `H¹_et(X_ℚ̄,ℚ_p)^∨`), and fix a continuous idèle class character `χ:𝔸^×_ℚ/ℚ^×→ℚ_p` and a section `s:V_dR/Fil⁰→V_dR` of the Hodge quotient with isotropic image, equivalently an isotropic complementary subspace to `Fil⁰`. For `v≠p`, `H⁰(G_v,V)=0=H¹(G_v,V)`, so a mixed extension M of `ℚ_p,V,ℚ_p(1)` over `G_v` splits as `V⊕N` with N an extension of `ℚ_p` by `ℚ_p(1)`; define `h_v(M)=χ_v([N])`, where `χ_v:H¹(G_v,ℚ_p(1))≅(limₙ ℚ_v^×/(ℚ_v^×)^(pⁿ))⊗ℤₚℚ_p→ℚ_p` is induced by the local component of `χ` through Kummer theory. For `v=p` and M crystalline, with `D_cris(M)=M₀⊃M₁⊃M₂` as a mixed extension of filtered φ-modules, the extension class of `D_cris(M)` in `Ext¹(ℚ_p,M₁)` is an element of `M₁/Fil⁰`; lift it to `M₁` by s and project to `M₂≅D_cris(ℚ_p(1))` by the canonical φ-equivariant splitting of `M₂⊂M₁`, which exists for weight reasons. The result c lies in `D_cris(ℚ_p(1))≅H¹_f(G_p,ℚ_p(1))`, and `h_p(M)=χ_p(c)`. Then: each `h_v` is continuous, bi-additive and symmetric `(h_v(M)=h_v(M*(1)))`; `h_p` is an algebraic function on `H¹_f(G_p,U)`; `h_v(M)=0` when `v≠p` and M is unramified, and more generally when M is potentially unramified; changing s changes `h_p` by a bilinear function of `(π₁(M),π₂(M))` on `V_dR/Fil⁰`; and `h_v` is linear in `χ`.

`X/ℚ` smooth projective of genus `g≥1` with good reduction at p; `χ` continuous with `χ_p` ramified (so that `χ_p` is nonzero on `H¹_f(G_p,ℚ_p(1))`); s with isotropic image for the symmetry statement. Its kernel is zero for every section and cannot express the isotropy condition.

For `v≠p`, `H⁰(G_v,V)=0` because `J(ℚ_v)[p^∞]` is finite, `H²(G_v,V)=H⁰(G_v,V*(1))^∨=0` by local duality and `V*(1)≅V`, and the local Euler characteristic is zero, so `H¹=0`; the splitting then follows. For `v=p`, `Ext¹` of `ℚ_p` by a filtered φ-module W with `W^(φ=1)=0` is `W/Fil⁰W`, computed by comparing a φ-splitting with a filtered one. Algebraicity: the construction is a polynomial function on `U_dR/F⁰`. Potentially unramified vanishing: over a finite Galois extension trivialising the inertia action, the class of N restricts to zero, and restriction is injective on `H¹(G_v,ℚ_p(1))` because `ℚ_p(1)` has no invariants under the open subgroup. Change of splitting: the difference of two splittings is a linear map `V_dR/Fil⁰→Fil⁰V_dR`, and the difference of heights is the corresponding bilinear form.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `localHeight`: The local height `h_v` for `v≠p` and `h_p` on crystalline mixed extensions.
- `localHeight_biadditive` and `localHeight_symm`: Bi-additivity and symmetry for isotropic s.
- `localHeight_algebraic`: `h_p` is algebraic on `H¹_f(G_p,U)`.
- `localHeight_potentiallyUnramified`: `h_v(M)=0` for `v≠p` and M potentially unramified.
- `height_change_splitting`: Changing s changes `h_p` by a bilinear form in `(π₁,π₂)`.
- `height_character_smul`: `h_v` is linear in `χ`; the zero character gives the zero height.

**Checks.**

- The split mixed extension has height 0 at every v.
- For `v≠p` and `M=V⊕N` with N the Kummer extension of an element `u∈ℚ_v^×` of valuation 1, `h_v(M)=χ_v(u)=the` value of `χ_v` on a uniformiser; for u a unit it is 0, the unramified case.
- At a place `v=ℓ≠p` of good reduction, `M=V⊕N` with N the Kummer class of `ℓ` has unramified graded pieces but is ramified, and `h_v(M)=χ_v(ℓ)`, which is nonzero for a suitable `χ`; the vanishing statement needs M itself potentially unramified, not only its graded pieces.
- For `χ=0` every height vanishes, so a nonzero character is needed to use `h_p` as a coordinate.
- On a four-dimensional symplectic de Rham space with basis `a₁,a₂,b₁,b₂`, `〈aᵢ,bⱼ〉=δᵢⱼ` and `Fil⁰=span(a₁,a₂)`, the section with `image span(b₁,b₂)` is isotropic. The section with `image span(b₁+a₂,b₂)` has zero kernel but pairing `〈b₁+a₂,b₂〉=1`, so it fails the symmetry hypothesis.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan and Netan Dogra](#reference-bd1), §4.3, pp. 14–15; §4.3.1, p. 15; §4.3.2, Lemma 4.8 and Remark 4.9, pp. 15–16; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), §3.1, p. 901; §3.2 and Lemma 3.2, p. 903; §3.3, (12) and Definition 3.4, p. 904; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan and Netan Dogra](#reference-bdii), §3.4, author pp. 15–18. The underlying construction is Nekovář's (On p-adic height pairings, Séminaire de Théorie des Nombres, Paris 1990–91, §§2–4), as recalled in these sources.

Use [Mixed extensions with graded pieces `ℚ_p`, V, `ℚ_p(1)`](#mixed-extensions); [ArithmeticGaloisDuality](../ArithmeticGaloisDuality/README.md) §D7.5 (local duality over finite and coefficient fields); [ArithmeticGaloisDuality](../ArithmeticGaloisDuality/README.md) §D7.4 (the local invariant map); [SelmerIwasawaCohomology](../SelmerIwasawaCohomology/README.md) §0 (S-unit Kummer theory); [PadicPeriodRings](../PadicPeriodRings/README.md) §§4.2–4.3 (period tensor invariants and admissibility); [De Rham exactness and Hodge–Tate grading](#linear-period-exactness).

<a id="nekovar-semistable-local-height"></a>

**The local height on semistable mixed extensions.** Keep the good-reduction Jacobian representation V, character `χ` and Hodge section s above, and put `K=ℚ_p`. For a mixed extension M write `E₂=M₁`, so that `0→ℚ_p(1)→E₂→V→0`, and let `x∈H¹(K,E₂)` classify `0→E₂→M→ℚ_p→0`. Assume that both adjacent extension classes are finite: `E₂` is crystalline and the `image π(x)` lies in `H¹_f(K,V)`. These assumptions hold when M is semistable, because `H¹_st(K,V)=H¹_f(K,V)` for a good-reduction Jacobian, also after the polarized identification `V≅V*(1)`. Define the height on this adjacent-finite domain, and hence on `H¹_st(K,U(ℚ_p,V,ℚ_p(1)))`, as follows.

The finite and unrestricted cohomology sequences are

```text
0 → H¹_f(K,ℚ_p(1)) → H¹_f(K,E₂) → H¹_f(K,V) → 0,
0 → H¹(K,ℚ_p(1)) → π⁻¹(H¹_f(K,V)) → H¹_f(K,V) → 0.
```

The injections use `H⁰(K,V)=0`. The unrestricted sequence is surjective because its connecting obstruction is the cup product with the finite class of `E₂`, and the finite local conditions for V and `V*(1)` annihilate one another under local duality. For the finite sequence, the Bloch–Kato exponentials identify the three terms with their de Rham quotients: `D_cris(V)` and `D_cris(E₂)` have no φ-fixed vectors. Good reduction and the Weil weights ensure that the φ-spectrum of V is disjoint from that of `ℚ_p(1)`, so there is a unique φ-equivariant splitting `j_φ:D_dR(V)→D_dR(E₂)`. The composition of s, `j_φ` and the quotient to `D_dR(E₂)/Fil⁰`, transported by the exponentials, gives a section `r_s:H¹_f(K,V)→H¹_f(K,E₂)`. Let `w_s(y)` be the unique finite Tate class whose image is `y−r_s(π(y))`.

Choose `y∈H¹_f(K,E₂)` with `π(y)=π(x)`, and let `k∈H¹(K,ℚ_p(1))` be the unique class with `x−i(y)=j(k)`. Set `w′_s(x)=u(w_s(y))+k`, where i and u are the inclusions of finite classes into unrestricted cohomology, and define `h_p(M)=χ_p(w′_s(x))`. Replacing y by `y+j(a)`, with a finite Tate class, adds a to `w_s(y)` and subtracts a from k, so the result is independent of the choice. This uses the full Kummer group, including its valuation direction; it does not apply a crystalline formula to `D_st(M)`.

The interface is `localHeight_st` on semistable classes, `localHeight_st_lift_independent`, `localHeight_st_agrees_crystalline`, and `localHeight_st_central_translation`. The latter states `h_p(M+d)−h_p(M)=χ_p(d)=inv_p(χ_p∪d)`, with the reciprocity and cup-product convention of the preceding height target. Include `localHeight_st_biadditive`, `localHeight_st_symm` for isotropic s, and `localHeight_st_change_splitting` and `localHeight_st_character_smul` with the same formulas as on crystalline classes. Functoriality of the two cohomology rows under pushout and pullback proves partial Baer additivity. Dualize the rows using local duality and the polarization; the two Hodge splittings are adjoint precisely for isotropic s, giving symmetry. The difference of two `r_s` is a map into the finite Tate term, giving the bilinear change-of-splitting formula. The central term k is independent of s, and `χ` acts linearly on both terms.

**Checks.**

- For a crystalline x, take `y=x: k=0` and the formula is `χ_p(w_s(x))`, the preceding crystalline height.
- Replacing a chosen lift y by `y+j(a)` for a nonzero finite Tate class a changes the two summands by `+a` and −a; their sum is unchanged.
- The split mixed extension has `x=0` and height zero.
- For `M=V⊕N(p(1+p))`, the two adjacent classes vanish. Its Tate extension has valuation one, so M is semistable and not crystalline. Taking `y=0` gives `h_p(M)=χ_p(p(1+p))`; for the logarithmic character with `χ_p(p)=0` this equals `χ_p(1+p)`, which is nonzero, including `p=2`. Restricting the construction to `H¹_f(K,U)` would lose this input.
- Translating this M by the Kummer class of `(1+p)` changes the height by `χ_p(1+p)`; reversing the central-translation sign fails this test.

The cohomological construction is [Amnon Besser](#reference-besser-heights2002), §4, diagram (4.4), Definition 4.1, Lemma 4.2 and Definition 4.3, pp. 6–7; the Hodge/Frobenius splitting is §6, equation (6.1), p. 10. Its restriction to crystalline mixed extensions and the semistable domain are [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan and Netan Dogra](#reference-bd1), §4.3, pp. 14–16; the global translation and isotropic symmetry are §4.3.3, pp. 16–17. The signs here are fixed by the displayed cohomology construction and the central Kummer check, rather than by a comparison with Coleman–Gross heights.

Use [Nekovář's local heights](#nekovar-local-heights); [Mixed extensions with graded pieces `ℚ_p`, V, `ℚ_p(1)`](#mixed-extensions); [The Bloch–Kato subgroups `H¹_e⊆H¹_f⊆H¹_g`](#bloch-kato-subgroups); [ArithmeticGaloisDuality](../ArithmeticGaloisDuality/README.md) §D7.5 (local duality); [The Bloch–Kato subgroups `H¹_e⊆H¹_f⊆H¹_g`](#bloch-kato-subgroups).

<a id="nekovar-global-height"></a>

**The global height and its decomposition into local heights.** With the data of [Nekovář's local heights](#nekovar-local-heights) and T the set of bad places together with p, define h on `H¹_st(G_T,U(ℚ_p,V,ℚ_p(1)))` (classes semistable at p) by `h(M)=Σ_(v∈T)h_v(loc_v M)`, using [The local height on semistable mixed extensions](#nekovar-semistable-local-height) at p. Then h is invariant under the action of `H¹_st(G_T,ℚ_p(1))`, because `h_v(c+d)=h_v(c)+loc_v(χ∪d)` and the sum of the local invariants of a global class is zero. Hence h factors through `H¹_f(G_T,V)×H¹_f(G_T,V)` via `M↦(π₁(M),π₂(M)*(1))`, and the factored map is bilinear; it is Nekovář's global p-adic height pairing `h:H¹_f(G_T,V)×H¹_f(G_T,V*(1))→ℚ_p` for `(χ,s)`. It is symmetric when s is isotropic, and changing s or scaling `χ` changes it as for the local heights.

As for [Nekovář's local heights](#nekovar-local-heights); T finite containing p and the bad places; `H¹_st(G_T,V)=H¹_f(G_T,V)` for `V=V_pJ`.

Additivity: the central `ℚ_p(1)` acts on each local term by adding the cup product with `χ_v`; summing over v and applying global reciprocity (the sum of local invariants of a global class in `H²(G_T,ℚ_p(1))` vanishes) gives invariance. Bi-additivity and continuity give bilinearity after factoring through the quotient by `H¹_st(G_T,ℚ_p(1))`, which is `H¹_f(G_T,V)⊕H¹_f(G_T,V*(1))`. Symmetry follows from the local symmetry.

**Checks.**

- If `π₁(M)=0`, `h(M)` depends only on the class of M modulo `ℚ_p(1)-translation`, and is 0 when also `π₂(M)=0`.
- For a global class M and `d∈H¹_st(G_T,ℚ_p(1))`, the local heights at individual places change by `loc_v(χ∪d)`, which can be nonzero, while the sum does not change: the local heights are not themselves globally bilinear.
- Changing the sign of `χ` changes the sign of h.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan and Netan Dogra](#reference-bd1), §4.3.3, pp. 16–17; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), §3.1, equation (11) and the decomposition into local heights, p. 901; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan and Netan Dogra](#reference-bdii), §3.5, author pp. 18–19.

Use [Nekovář's local heights](#nekovar-local-heights); [The local height on semistable mixed extensions](#nekovar-semistable-local-height); [ArithmeticGaloisDuality](../ArithmeticGaloisDuality/README.md) Layer D7 (derived continuous cohomology and compact arithmetic duality); [SelmerIwasawaCohomology](../SelmerIwasawaCohomology/README.md) Layer 4 (finite conditions).

### 6.2 Rational classes and the rank obstruction

<a id="rational-rosati-descent"></a>

**Rational Rosati descent.** Let A be an abelian variety over a field k of characteristic zero with a polarization `λ:A→A^∨` defined over k, and † the Rosati involution `α↦λ⁻¹α^∨λ` of `End⁰(A)=End(A)⊗ℚ`. The map `L↦λ⁻¹∘φ_L` induces an isomorphism from `NS(A)⊗ℚ`, where `NS(A)=Pic(A)/Pic⁰(A)` is formed over k, onto the †-fixed subspace of `End⁰(A)`. In particular, for a Jacobian with its principal polarization, symmetric correspondences defined over k give Néron–Severi classes defined over k, without using geometric Galois-invariant classes.

k of characteristic zero (perfect suffices); A an abelian variety over k; `λ` a polarization defined over k.

Injectivity: `Pic(A)→Pic(A_k̄)^(Gal)` is injective by Hilbert 90 because `O(A_k̄)^×=k̄^×`, so `NS(A)→NS(A_k̄)` is injective, and `L↦φ_L` is injective on `NS(A_k̄)`. Image in the fixed part: `φ_L` is defined over k, and over k̄ the element `λ⁻¹φ_L` is †-fixed. Surjectivity: if `α∈End⁰(A)` is †-fixed, choose n with `ψ=nλα` a homomorphism `A→A^∨` over k; it is symmetric `(ψ^∨=ψ)`. The line bundle `L=(1,ψ)*P_A`, with `P_A` the Poincaré bundle, is defined over k, and `φ_L=ψ+ψ^∨=2ψ`, as one checks after base change to k̄ by the theorem of the square; so `α=(2n)⁻¹λ⁻¹φ_L`.

**Checks.**

- For `A=E` an elliptic curve over `ℚ` without CM, `End⁰(E)=ℚ`, every element is †-fixed and `NS(E)⊗ℚ=ℚ` (generated by a point), so both sides are 1-dimensional.
- For `A=E×E` with E without CM, `End⁰(A)=M₂(ℚ)` with † the transpose for the product polarization; the fixed part is the 3-dimensional space of symmetric matrices, matching `NS(E×E)⊗ℚ` of rank 3 (the two fibres and the diagonal).
- For `A=E×E′` with E′ the quadratic twist of a non-CM elliptic curve `E/ℚ` by `ℚ(√d)`, over `ℚ`, `Hom(E,E′)=0` and both sides have dimension 2; over `ℚ(√d)` the graph of `E≅E′` appears and both sides have dimension 3. Using `End⁰(A_k̄)` without Galois invariants would give 3 over `ℚ`, which is wrong.

The construction and its conventions follow [J. S. Milne](#reference-milne-av), §8, the Poincaré sheaf, p. 37; §10, the Néron–Severi group and Corollary 10.18, p. 50; §14, Proposition 14.2, p. 61; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), proof of Lemma 2.4, p. 900.

Use [AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli](../AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli/README.md) §A2 (dual abelian varieties and polarizations); [AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli](../AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli/README.md) §A6 (endomorphisms and the Rosati involution); [TauCetiRoadmap.JacobianChallenge](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge/README.md#layer-e-abelian-varieties).

<a id="correspondence-cycle-classes"></a>

**Divisor correspondences acting on H¹⊗H¹.** Let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g over a field F of characteristic zero, `H¹` a Weil cohomology of X with coefficient field L of characteristic zero (étale `ℚ_p`, or de Rham), `τ` the swap of X×X and `π₁,π₂` the projections. For `Z∈Pic(X×X)⊗ℚ` let `ξ_Z` be the Künneth component of its cycle class in `H¹⊗H¹(1)≅End(H¹)` (Poincaré duality). Fix the alternating pairing `〈u,v〉=tr(u∪v)`, and identify `u⊗v` with `T(u⊗v):w↦〈u,w〉v` (Tate twists are included in the pairing). Thus `tr(T(u⊗v))=〈u,v〉`. The swap on the middle Künneth summand is minus the ordinary tensor flip. These choices fix all signs below. Then: `ξ_(τ*Z)` is the adjoint of `ξ_Z` for the cup-product pairing (with the Koszul sign fixed together with the Künneth isomorphism), so that for a Jacobian it corresponds to the Rosati involution; pullbacks `π₁*Z₁` and `π₂*Z₂` have zero H¹⊗H¹-component; the trace of `ξ_Z` as an endomorphism of `H¹` equals the image of `ξ_Z` under the cup product `H¹⊗H¹(1)→H²(1)≅L`; and if J is absolutely simple and Z is symmetric `(τ*Z=Z+π₁*Z₁+π₂*Z₂)`, `ξ_Z` lies in `∧²H¹(1)`. The map `Z↦ξ_Z` is compatible with base change of F and with the comparison isomorphisms between étale and de Rham realizations.

X smooth projective geometrically connected over F of characteristic zero; L of characteristic zero; for the `∧²` statement J absolutely simple.

Take cycle classes of divisors on X×X and project by the Künneth decomposition. For `A=T(u⊗v)`, the alternating pairing gives `A†=−T(v⊗u)`; hence the graded swap −flip corresponds to the adjoint, without an unspecified sign; a pullback from one factor lies in `H²⊗H⁰` or `H⁰⊗H²`. The trace identity is the definition of the trace of an endomorphism given by an element of `H¹⊗H¹(1)≅H¹⊗(H¹)^∨` through the Poincaré pairing. For the `∧²` statement, a symmetric correspondence induces a Rosati-symmetric element of `End(J)⊗ℚ`, which lies in the image of `NS(J)⊗ℚ` by [Rational Rosati descent](#rational-rosati-descent), and the class of a divisor on J lies in `H²(J)(1)=∧²H¹(1)`.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `correspondenceClass`: `Z↦ξ_Z∈H¹⊗H¹(1)`.
- `correspondenceClass_swap`: `ξ_(τ*Z)` is the adjoint of `ξ_Z`.
- `correspondenceClass_pullback`: Pullbacks from either factor have `ξ=0`.
- `correspondenceClass_trace`: `tr(ξ_Z)=cup(ξ_Z)` under `H²(1)≅L`.
- `correspondenceClass_symmetric_mem_wedge`: Symmetric Z with J absolutely simple gives `ξ_Z∈∧²H¹(1)`.
- `correspondenceClass_comparison`: Compatibility with base change and with the étale–de Rham comparison.

**Checks.**

- For a symplectic basis `aᵢ,bᵢ` with `〈aᵢ,bⱼ〉=δᵢⱼ`, the diagonal middle component is `Σᵢ(bᵢ⊗aᵢ−aᵢ⊗bᵢ)`. Our T sends it to −id with trace −2g. Subtracting the two fibre classes does not change it, so this symmetric correspondence is not nice for `g≥1`. For `g=0` its middle component is zero and it is again not nice.
- Define `Γ_σ={(σ(x),x)}`. Its middle component acts as `−σ*`, and the swapped graph acts as `−(σ⁻¹)*`. This graph direction is part of the convention.
- On `H=ℚ²` with `〈(x₁,x₂),(y₁,y₂)〉=x₁y₂−x₂y₁`, the simple tensor `u⊗v` acts by `w↦〈u,w〉v` and has trace `u₁v₂−u₂v₁`, the cup pairing. Thus `T(b⊗a−a⊗b)(w)=−w`, whose trace is −2; `T(a⊗b)` has matrix diag(0,1), with trace `1=〈a,b〉`. Reversing the pairing would reverse both values.
- If either simple-tensor factor is zero, its endomorphism is zero. With `a=(1,0)`, `b=(0,1)`, T(b⊗a)=diag(−1,0), which differs from T(a⊗b)=diag(0,1); exchanging the factors without the graded minus sign fails the adjoint convention.
- For a pullback `π₁*Z₁`, `ξ=0` although the class in `H²(X×X)` is nonzero: the Künneth projection, not the whole cycle class, is used.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), §2.3, the definitions of symmetric and nice correspondences, Lemma 2.4 and its proof, p. 900; Remark 2.5, p. 901; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan and Netan Dogra](#reference-bd1), §6.2, the cycle class `cl_Z` through Künneth projectors, p. 25.

Use [EtaleCohomologyFoundations](../EtaleCohomologyFoundations/README.md) §§0.9–0.11, F.6 (cycle and Chern classes, localization, purity and Gysin maps); [EtaleCohomologyFoundations](../EtaleCohomologyFoundations/README.md) §§0.11, F.5–F.6 (trace, Poincaré duality and purity); [EtaleCohomologyFoundations](../EtaleCohomologyFoundations/README.md) §F.2.6 (`VanishingCycles.etaleKunneth`), with the [prime-field specialization](#prime-field-kunneth); [SchemeAndStackFoundations](../SchemeAndStackFoundations/README.md) SF.5 (Chow groups and intersection theory).

<a id="nc-5-nice-correspondence"></a>

**Nice rational correspondence.** Let `X/Q` be smooth, proper and geometrically connected, of genus g&gt;1, with b in `X(Q)`. In `C=Pic(X×X)⊗Q` let P be the sum of the two pullback subspaces. A correspondence Z is nice when swap*Z−Z belongs to P, its `H1⊗H1` Kunneth component cl(Z) is nonzero, and the induced endomorphism `E_Z` of H1 has trace zero. Nontrivial means nonzero in this component, not merely a nonzero divisor or Picard class. The same predicate applies after scalar extension, but a p-adic class is not thereby a rational correspondence.

The Kunneth cycle-class map, correspondence action and principal polarization come from their geometric owners. Rational coefficients permit subtracting the scalar trace part.

Form the pullback subspace in the rational Picard group and impose symmetry in its quotient. Extract the `H1⊗H1` component; impose its nonvanishing and trace zero. On supplied modules the three conditions are an explicit predicate.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `IsNiceCorrespondence.nonzero`: A nice class is nonzero.
- `IsNiceCorrespondence.smul`: Multiplication by a nonzero coefficient preserves niceness.
- `IsNiceCorrespondence.add_pullback`: Adding d in the pullback subspace preserves niceness when swap(d)−d stays in that subspace and both trace and cl vanish on it.

**Checks.**

- `nice_nonzero_primitive`: For `C=Q²`, `P=0`, swap=id, trace=first coordinate and cl=second coordinate, (0,1) is nice.
- `nice_nonzero_trace`: With these data (1,1) is not nice.
- `nice_zero_class`: For trace=0 and cl=second coordinate, the nonzero element (1,0) is not nice.
- Zero and a nonzero pullback class cannot be nice.
- Symmetry modulo pullbacks is distinct from equality of divisors under swapping.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), §2.3, definition before Lemma 2.4, p. 900.

Use [AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli](../AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli/README.md) §A2.10 (the Néron–Severi group); [SchemeAndStackFoundations](../SchemeAndStackFoundations/README.md), SF.5: rational cycles, intersections, push-pull and the first Chern class; `LinearMap.ker`; [Divisor correspondences acting on `H¹⊗H¹`](#correspondence-cycle-classes); [Rational Rosati descent](#rational-rosati-descent).

<a id="nc-5-nice-trace-criterion"></a>

**Primitive class and trace criterion.** For a symmetric rational correspondence Z on X whose Jacobian is absolutely simple, its Kunneth tensor is alternating (with the graded Kunneth sign). Its cup product is zero exactly when `E_Z` has trace zero, under the trace H2(X)(1)≅coefficient field. Consequently Z is nice exactly when cl(Z) is nonzero and cup(cl(Z))=0. The nonzero qualification is essential; the zero correspondence satisfies the latter equation alone.

X and the polarization as in [Nice rational correspondence](#nc-5-nice-correspondence). Use the duality conventions of H1 and `V=H1_et(Xbar,Qp)*`, with their Tate twist.

Import the rational NS-to-Rosati-symmetric-Hom identification from A2; the alternating tensor is its cohomological realization. The correspondence trace equals cup followed by H2 trace. Combine with the explicit nonzero condition; do not use the unqualified converse in the printed Lemma 2.4.

**Checks.**

- A primitive zero class is rejected.
- The Kunneth sign explains why geometric symmetry gives an alternating H1 tensor.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Lemma 2.4 and proof, p. 900.

<a id="nc-5-depth-two-quotient"></a>

**Depth-two height quotient.** Put V=VpJ and W2=coker(Qp(1)→∧²V), the cup-dual relation. The imported proper depth-two group has central exact sequence `1→W2→U2→V→1`. A nonzero alternating cup-zero rational cycle class gives a `G_Q`-equivariant surjection `q_Z:W2→Qp(1)`. Define `U_Z=U2/ker(q_Z)`, as an fpqc group-scheme quotient, so `1→Qp(1)→U_Z→V→1` is central and its commutator is `q_Z` applied to the imported commutator. At the linear central grade the carrier is `W2/ker q_Z`, identified with Qp(1) by the first isomorphism theorem.

A nonzero alternating cup-zero rational cycle class supplies `q_Z` by duality. The kernel is closed, normal and Galois stable; characteristic zero and finite type come from Layer 2. A nice correspondence supplies this class under [Primitive class and trace criterion](#nc-5-nice-trace-criterion), which retains its absolutely-simple-J hypothesis. The general rank criterion instead obtains primitive classes directly from rational NS and does not use that hypothesis.

Use the proper cup-dual presentation of U2, not the affine free fundamental group. Factor the cycle functional through W2 because it kills the cup-dual relation. Nonzero to a one-dimensional target is surjective. Import the schematic central pushout and preserve the Galois action; use the module quotient only for its central grade.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `DepthTwoHeightQuotient.centralMap`: The central projection is the quotient map `W2→W2/ker q`.
- `DepthTwoHeightQuotient.centralEquiv`: For surjective q, the central quotient is linearly equivalent to its Tate target.
- `DepthTwoHeightQuotient.centralEquiv_apply`: The equivalence takes the class of z to `q(z)`.
- `DepthTwoHeightQuotient.centralMap_eq_zero`: The central class of z is zero exactly when `q(z)=0`.
- `DepthTwoHeightQuotient.central_exact`: The geometric central extension has the stated kernel, projection and commutator.

**Checks.**

- `quotient_coordinate`: For `q:Q²→Q` the first coordinate, (3,5) and (3,0) give the same central class and q is surjective.
- `quotient_zero_map`: For `q=0` every central class vanishes.
- `quotient_retains_nonzero_class`: For the coordinate projection, the class of (1,0) is nonzero.
- The centre is a Tate line only for a nonzero functional.
- Retain the proper cup relation and the schematic quotient.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), §2.3, pp. 900–901 and exact sequence(10), p. 897; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan and Netan Dogra](#reference-bd1), §3, Lemma 3.2, pp. 11–12.

Use [Nice rational correspondence](#nc-5-nice-correspondence); [Lower central depth](#nc-2-central-quotients); [Central extensions: the action of `H¹(G, Z)` and the connecting map to `H²`](#nc-3-central-extension); `LinearMap.quotKerEquivOfSurjective`; [Divisor correspondences acting on `H¹⊗H¹`](#correspondence-cycle-classes).

<a id="nc-5-rank-picard-criterion"></a>

**Quadratic Chabauty rank criterion.** Let `X/Q` be smooth, projective and geometrically connected with genus g&gt;1 and rational basepoint, J its Jacobian, p a prime of good reduction, `r=rank J(Q)`, and `rho_Q=rank NS(J/Q)`. With the Layer 5 Selmer locus defined by crystalline conditions at p, local Kummer images at all bad places and projection to the global Mordell–Weil Kummer image, `r<g+rho_Q−1` implies `X(Qp)_2` is finite. It contains `X(Q)`. No equality between global `H1_f(G_T,V)` and J(Q)⊗Qp, no ordinary-reduction hypothesis and no replacement of `rho_Q` by the geometric Picard number are assumed.

Use p-adic coefficients and the reduced Selmer variety convention of BD I §2.3, as fixed in Layer 5. The number field is Q; the extra unit and splitting hypotheses for other fields are outside this selected theorem.

From `A2/A6` import rational NS and its symmetric-Hom injection and finite rank. Primitive rational NS classes form a space of dimension `rho_Q−1` after removing the theta/trace direction. Push U2 to an extension of V by `rho_Q−1` Tate lines. The global crystalline/unramified Tate-line kernel has dimension zero over Q, using the S-unit/Kummer and local conditions; finite bad Kummer images contribute no dimension. The Mordell–Weil cut bounds the global Selmer dimension by r. The local crystalline quotient has dimension `g+rho_Q−1` by strict extension classification and the Bloch–Kato dimension formula. The strict inequality gives non-dominance. Import Layer 5 discwise density and analytic finiteness to conclude.

**Checks.**

- When `rho_Q=1` the strict bound reduces to r&lt;g.
- The boundary `r=g+rho_Q−1` does not assert finiteness.
- A larger geometric NS rank without rational descent does not improve this bound.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan and Netan Dogra](#reference-bd1), §2.3 and Remark 2.3, p. 9; §3, Lemma 3.2 and proof, pp. 11–12; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Theorem 2.3, p. 899.

Use [Depth-two height quotient](#nc-5-depth-two-quotient); [AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli](../AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli/README.md) §A2.10 (the Néron–Severi group); [AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli](../AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli/README.md) §A6.16 (finiteness of the Néron–Severi group); Layer 5, albanese maps and chabauty–kim finiteness; [SelmerIwasawaCohomology](../SelmerIwasawaCohomology/README.md) §0.9 (the Kummer identification for S-units); [SelmerIwasawaCohomology](../SelmerIwasawaCohomology/README.md) §4.9 (the Bloch–Kato local condition); [SelmerIwasawaCohomology](../SelmerIwasawaCohomology/README.md) §2.12a (number-field abelian descent and local Kummer images); [HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions](../HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions/README.md) §1.1 (fppf comparison) and §§1.6–1.7 (Mordell–Weil); [Rational abelian Kummer and Sha comparison](#abelian-kummer-mordell-weil); [Proper-curve Mordell–Weil Selmer cut](#mordell-weil-selmer-cut); [Rational Rosati descent](#rational-rosati-descent).

<a id="nc-5-admissible-tate-class"></a>

**Admissible de Rham Tate class.** For `H=H1_dR(X/Qp)` with Frobenius phi at a good prime p, define admissibility of Z in `H⊗H` by five explicit conditions: `Z≠0`; (phi⊗phi)(Z)=pZ; Z belongs to `Fil1(H⊗H)`; cup(Z)=0; and swap(Z)=−Z. The filtration is the tensor filtration; phi is on H1, not on its Tate dual. These are necessary conditions for a nice rational correspondence, and they do not construct one.

The geometric specialization is over Qp, so phi is linear; a ramified coefficient-field extension requires its imported semilinear comparison. Nonvanishing is retained from the opening paragraph of §4.4, p.913; it accompanies the four displayed de Rham conditions.

Use the tensor product, its commutor and the tensor of phi with itself. Impose membership in the supplied tensor filtration and the kernel of cup, with the eigenvalue and alternating condition. Keep algebraicity and rational descent as separate evidence in [Realization of a rational nice class](#nc-5-nice-class-realization).

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `IsAdmissibleTateClass.nonzero`: An admissible class is nonzero.
- `IsAdmissibleTateClass.smul`: A nonzero scalar multiple remains admissible.
- `IsAdmissibleTateClass.not_zero`: The zero tensor is never admissible.

**Checks.**

- `tate_wedge_eigenvalue`: For `H=Q²`, phi=diag(1,2), Fil1=all and cup=0, `e1⊗e2−e2⊗e1` is admissible with eigenvalue 2. This is a linear test, not a geometric curve.
- `tate_zero_rejected`: With the same data zero is rejected.
- `tate_symmetric_tensor_rejected`: With phi=diag(1,2), Fil1=all and cup=0, `e1⊗e2+e2⊗e1` is rejected although it is nonzero and has eigenvalue 2. This isolates the alternating condition.
- `tate_wrong_frobenius`: The nonzero wedge is rejected with phi=id and required eigenvalue 2.
- `tate_wrong_filtration`: With phi=diag(1,2), cup=0 and Fil1=zero, the nonzero wedge is rejected. All other conditions hold.
- `tate_nonzero_cup_rejected`: With phi=diag(1,2) and Fil1=all, the wedge is rejected by the linear test functional cup(x⊗y)=x1*y2, since its value is 1. All other conditions hold; this test functional is not asserted to be a geometric alternating cup pairing.
- Changing to the dual Frobenius without the twist changes the eigenvalue and is rejected.
- Admissibility is never used as an algebraic-cycle lifting theorem.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), §4.4, opening nonzero hypothesis and conditions(a)–(d), pp. 913–914; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv23), §3.5.2, Remark 3.17, p. 16.

Use `TensorProduct.map`; `TensorProduct.comm`; `LinearMap.ker`; [Linear geometric period comparisons](#linear-geometric-period-comparisons); `TensorProduct.lift`.

<a id="nc-5-nice-class-realization"></a>

**Realization of a rational nice class.** A nonzero rational nice correspondence produces an admissible de Rham Tate class at every good prime, under the tensor-compatible crystalline cycle comparison. Only this forward implication is asserted. An arbitrary p-adic linear combination satisfying the admissibility conditions need not belong to the rational algebraic-correspondence space, even when the two stated Picard ranks agree.

Use the rational class, its symmetric `Hom/NS` realization and the good-reduction crystalline cycle class, with tensor and cup compatibility. The nice-to-alternating implication here uses [Primitive class and trace criterion](#nc-5-nice-trace-criterion), including absolute simplicity. For the general rank theorem, rational NS classes give alternating classes on H2(J) directly; that theorem does not depend on this specialized correspondence implication.

A rational divisor cycle has the required Frobenius eigenvalue and Hodge filtration by cycle comparison. Apply the alternating and cup/trace criterion and injectivity on rational divisor classes. The proposed converse would confuse the intersection of a rational lattice with a filtration with the intersection of its p-adic span; it is excluded.

**Checks.**

- Input includes a rational cycle, with no inferred lift from de Rham linear algebra.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), §4.4, forward cycle-class paragraph before Lemma 4.7, p. 913; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv23), Remark 3.17, p. 16.

### 6.3 The height representation

<a id="nc-5-height-module"></a>

**Depth-two height module.** Let `A2(b)=A(b)/I³` be the imported length-two pointed universal module for the proper curve. Its central grade T=coker(Qp(1)→V⊗²) embeds in A2(b). The correspondence functional `q_Z:T→Qp(1)` factors through the proper relation. Define `A_Z(b)=A2(b)/i(ker q_Z)`, with its Galois action, weight filtration and identified grades Qp,V,Qp(1). Its U2 action factors faithfully through `U_Z`. Its de Rham version is the analogous pushout of the proper universal connection; it is a module, not a Hopf-algebra quotient.

The augmentation length is 2, so the exponent is 3; it is separate from the lower central indexing. The functional on `V⊗²` restricts to the alternating quotient and kills the cup-dual relation. Use the alternating cup-zero rational class as input. When it is selected through the named [Nice rational correspondence](#nc-5-nice-correspondence) theorem, retain the absolutely-simple-J hypothesis.

Import A2 and its graded representation from [Completed path algebra](#nc-2-length-algebra) and [Finite path module](#nc-2-finite-path-module). Quotient only the kernel in the central grade; keep the top and middle grades and the pointer. The kernel of the U2 representation is exactly `ker q_Z`, by the explicit unipotent action on the length-two quotient. Descend the action and connection.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `DepthTwoHeightModule.mk`: The projection `A2→A_Z` is the quotient map.
- `DepthTwoHeightModule.relation`: If `q(z)=0`, the class of `i(z)` vanishes.
- `DepthTwoHeightModule.lift`: A linear map on A2 killing `i(ker q)` descends uniquely to `A_Z`.
- `DepthTwoHeightModule.lift_mk`: The descended map evaluates on a quotient class as the original map.
- `DepthTwoHeightModule.lift_unique`: A map from the quotient agreeing with f on every class mk(a) equals lift(f). Together with `lift_mk` this states existence and uniqueness separately.
- `DepthTwoHeightModule.grades`: Identifies the weight grades with Qp,V,Qp(1), preserving their specified identifications.
- `DepthTwoHeightModule.action`: The imported U2 action descends to a faithful `U_Z` action.
- `DepthTwoHeightModule.deRham`: Gives the proper filtered connection pushout with its pointer.

**Checks.**

- `module_zero_quotient`: For `A=T=Q`, `i=id` and `q=0`, the whole quotient vanishes.
- `module_identity_quotient`: For `i=q=id` on Q, the class of 1 survives.
- `module_other_grades_preserved`: For `i:Q→Q²` the second-coordinate inclusion and `q=0`, the class of (1,0) survives. This detects quotienting the whole ambient module.
- The retained dimension is2g+2.
- No Hopf structure on the single augmentation quotient is asserted.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), §3.4, pp. 906–907; §4.4, pp. 914–915; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan and Netan Dogra](#reference-bd1), §5.1, pp. 17–20.

<a id="nc-5-height-module-twist"></a>

**Twisted height module.** For a right `U_Z` torsor P with compatible Galois action, define `HeightModuleTwist(P)=P×^{U_Z}A_Z(b)`, using the faithful left `U_Z` action on the module. It is a mixed extension with the fixed graded identifications Qp,V,Qp(1). For the path torsor from b to x write `A_Z(b,x)`. Contracted product, endpoint transport and the neutral torsor identification are those of Layer 0; Layer 6 applies them to this particular representation.

P is a genuine nonabelian torsor, not an arbitrary cocycle without quotient equivalence. Retain top and bottom grade rigidifications; isomorphisms induce the identity on the named grades.

Import torsor classification and twisting, then descend the `U_Z`-equivariant vector-space/representation sheaf along P. The central weight flag is `U_Z` stable and therefore descends with the graded identifications. Use neutral torsor and composition compatibility to recover `A_Z(b)` and endpoint functoriality.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `HeightModuleTwist.neutral`: Twisting by the neutral torsor recovers `A_Z(b)` with its flag and grades.
- `HeightModuleTwist.compose`: Composing endpoint path torsors induces the corresponding transport isomorphism of twisted modules.
- `HeightModuleTwist.classes`: The upper and lower extension projections are the imported mixed-extension pi1 and pi2, with the fixed graded identifications.

**Checks.**

- `twist_neutral`: For `P=U_Z` with its neutral torsor structure the twist is `A_Z(b)`.
- `twist_endpoint`: For `x=b` the depth-one upper class is 0; the lower class is the Chow–Heegner constant c, which need not vanish.
- `twist_nontrivial_center`: Twisting a fixed pair of adjacent extensions by a nonzero crystalline Tate-line class changes the central mixed-extension class; it is not killed by forgetting the centre.
- Transport acts on the source side with the convention inherited from Layer 2.
- Changing a torsor representative does not change the mixed-extension isomorphism class.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), §3.4, definition of `A_Z(b,x)`, pp. 906–907; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan and Netan Dogra](#reference-bdii), §3.1, pp. 12–14.

### 6.4 Correspondences and relative cohomology

<a id="relative-cycle-mixed-extension"></a>

**Relative cycle and Chow–Heegner comparison.** For a proper pointed curve `X/Q` and a rational divisor correspondence Z on X×X satisfying the stated primitive and symmetry conditions, construct the relative étale and de Rham cohomology extensions of the pair obtained by removing the diagonal and the base-point fibres. Apply the correspondence, project to the primitive `H¹⊗H¹` component and identify the resulting rigidified three-step mixed extension with the depth-two path height module. Identify its two extension classes with the Abel–Jacobi class and the Chow–Heegner divisor class. Preserve the endpoints, Galois action, Tate twist and strict de Rham filtration; the central grade is `ℚ_p(1)`, with no extra twist on `A_Z`.

Use rational divisors and intersection/push-pull operations on the stated pair. Mixed extensions and heights are those of [Mixed extensions with graded pieces `ℚ_p`, V, `ℚ_p(1)`](#mixed-extensions) and [Nekovář's local heights](#nekovar-local-heights).

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `relativeCycle.mixedExtension`: Construct the rigidified relative-cohomology extension.
- `relativeCycle.pathComparison`: Identify it with the specific path quotient.
- `relativeCycle.pi1`: Compute its Abel–Jacobi extension class.
- `relativeCycle.pi2`: Compute the Chow–Heegner extension class.
- `relativeCycle.filteredComparison`: Preserve the strict filtered realization.

**Checks.**

- For the zero correspondence, the primitive height quotient vanishes and does not give a nice nonzero class.
- The constant path at the base point has split endpoint extension.
- Adding a pulled-back divisor changes only the specified normalization, not the primitive tensor class.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan and Netan Dogra](#reference-bd1), §§3–4 and §6, Theorem 6.3, arXiv v2 pp. 9–17 and 25–28; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan and Netan Dogra](#reference-bdii), §§3–4, author pp. 10–22; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), §4, pp. 906–917.

### 6.5 Local realization of the height module

<a id="nc-5-height-module-comparison"></a>

**Crystalline comparison for the height module.** For X/Qp with good reduction and the rational cycle Z, the crystalline path comparison induces a strict, tensor- and cycle-compatible isomorphism `D_cris(A_Z^et(b,x))≅A_Z^dR(b,x)`. It preserves the pointer, weight grades, Hodge filtration, Frobenius and the cup-dual quotient functional, after passing to the proper quotient and its central pushout. Applying ordinary H1 comparison alone does not prove that the mixed extension is crystalline.

The whole finite path module is crystalline by the imported nonlinear comparison; b,x are good-reduction local points. The good-reduction cycle class comparison sends the same rational correspondence to its de Rham functional.

Import Layer 2 finite path comparison and genuine `D_cris` with its exact strict tensor structure from [De Rham exactness and Hodge–Tate grading](#linear-period-exactness). Pass to the proper quotient, and use compatibility of cycle classes, cup and tensor duality to identify the two central kernels. Apply strict exactness to the quotient `A_Z` and to its path twist; preserve the pointed normalization.

**Checks.**

- Use the mixed extension, not only its semisimplified graded pieces.
- The comparison is strict filtered and phi-equivariant.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), §5.4, Lemma 5.4 and proof, pp. 923–924.

<a id="nc-5-chow-heegner-class"></a>

**Rational Chow–Heegner constant.** For a rational divisor correspondence Z intersecting the endpoint fibres and diagonal properly, choose a rational auxiliary point o avoiding the supports. Put `D_Z(b,x)=Delta*Z−i_b*Z−i_x*Z+(Z·X_b+Z·X_x−Z·Delta)o`, a degree-zero divisor. In the source conventions, relative cohomology realizes `E_Z=A_Z(b,x)^*(1)`, the Tate dual of the twist, with the same identified grades Qp,V,Qp(1). The divisor comparison identifies `E_Z` with `H_X(x−b,D_Z(b,x))` in those grades; no further Tate twist is applied. The equality of their local heights gives `h_v(A_Z)=h_v(E_Z)=h_v(x−b,D_Z)` by Tate-dual symmetry. Hence `c_Z=[I A_Z(b)]` is the Kummer class of the associated rational Chow–Heegner divisor class. In the normalized de Rham frame its local logarithm is `C*(beta_phi(b,b)−beta_Fil(b))`, with C the cup matrix in the stated H1 convention. The first statement, not this numerical formula alone, proves rational Mordell–Weil realization.

Use proper intersections or a proved moving lemma; handle `x=b` by the pointed limiting/base-fibre construction rather than the distinct-endpoint relative cohomology formula alone. Auxiliary-point and representative changes are controlled by the imported cycle/relative-cohomology functoriality.

Check degree zero using the intersection-number correction. Import the general relative-cohomology realization of the length-two path module. Pull back the relative-cohomology sequence by the rational cycle class, twist by(1) to form `E_Z=A_Z^*(1)`, and compare via support/excision with `H_X(x−b,D_Z)` in identical grades. Use Tate-dual height symmetry to recover the `A_Z` height. The extra(−1) in the arXiv Theorem 6.3 display is incompatible with §6.2 and the subsequent proof and is not used. Take the lower extension at the basepoint to obtain the rational class, then use strict path comparison and cup duality to obtain the local formula.

**Checks.**

- Its degree is 0 after the explicit correction.
- The constant c is not forced to 0 by `pi1(A_Z(b,b))=0`.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan and Netan Dogra](#reference-bd1), §6.3, Theorem 6.1, pp. 24–25; Definition 6.2 and Theorem 6.3, pp. 26–29; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Remark 3.11, p. 908; Remark 5.6 and equation(47), p. 925.

<a id="nc-5-twist-two-classes"></a>

**Adjacent extension classes of the twist.** For x in `X(Q)`, `pi1(A_Z(b,x))=kappa(x−b)` and `pi2(A_Z(b,x))=E_Z kappa(x−b)+c_Z`, where `c_Z=[I A_Z(b)]` is the Kummer realization of a rational Chow–Heegner point. After localization and the Bloch–Kato logarithm these become `AJ_b(x)` and `E_Z AJ_b(x)+c_Z` in `W=H0(X_Qp,Omega1)*`. Both global classes lie in the Mordell–Weil Kummer image; the statement does not identify that image with the entire global `H1_f`.

Duality identifies `V*(1)` with V via the chosen principal polarization. Use the rational-cycle Chow–Heegner comparison; no assumption that `c_Z=0`.

The upper quotient of the length-two twist is the depth-one path representation, giving kappa(x−b). The lower subextension is the correspondence image of this class plus its value at b; compare with the divisor construction in [Rational Chow–Heegner constant](#nc-5-chow-heegner-class) to establish rational Mordell–Weil realization. Apply the imported Bloch–Kato and Coleman/Jacobian logarithm compatibility.

**Checks.**

- At b the first class is 0 and the second is `c_Z`.
- No Tate–Shafarevich finiteness assumption is inserted.

<a id="nc-5-twist-injective"></a>

**Injectivity of the specialized twisting map.** The twisting map `tau:H1_f(G,U_Z)→mixed` extensions with graded pieces Qp,V,Qp(1) is injective for the specified global or local Galois group and [Depth-two height module](#nc-5-height-module) representation. The proof must show that, for every twist arising from a torsor, the G-fixed locus of the pointed quotient `Aut_gr(A_Z)/U_Z` consists exactly of its distinguished coset. It is never empty: the neutral coset is fixed. Faithfulness of `U_Z→Aut_gr(A_Z)` alone does not imply injectivity on H1.

`Aut_gr` means flag-preserving automorphisms inducing the identity on all named graded pieces. The negative-weight quotient representations and their torsor twists have no invariant vectors for these Galois groups; finite-dimensional continuity and the group-theoretic exact sequence come from Layer 0.

Translate a fibre of `H1(U_Z)→H1(Aut_gr(A_Z))` to the neutral fibre by the imported nonabelian twisting equivalence. Filter the homogeneous quotient by its negative-weight vector-space pieces and prove that a fixed coset is the neutral one, successively; rational Frobenius weight arguments also hold on the twisted graded pieces. Use the fixed-coset/nonabelian exact sequence, not an empty fixed-locus claim, to obtain injectivity on every fibre.

**Checks.**

- The neutral coset is fixed.
- The argument addresses every twisted fibre, not just the kernel of a map of pointed sets.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan and Netan Dogra](#reference-bdii), §4, Lemma 4.2 and proof, p. 20; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan and Netan Dogra](#reference-bd1), §5.1, pp. 18–20.

<a id="nc-5-height-prevalue"></a>

**Specialized local height formula.** Choose the Hodge splitting `V_dR=Fil0⊕W`, with complementary projections s1 onto `W=s(V_dR/Fil0)` and s2 onto Fil0. In a fixed weight-graded frame, let `alpha_phi,beta_phi,gamma_phi` be the Frobenius splitting coordinates and `beta_Fil,gamma_Fil` the Hodge coordinates of the compared `A_Z(b,x)`. Define `HeightPrevalue=gamma_phi−gamma_Fil−beta_phi(s1 alpha_phi)−beta_Fil(s2 alpha_phi)`. The local height is the chosen Qp-linear character functional `chi_p` on the Tate-line de Rham quotient applied to this prevalue. This is linear evaluation after identifying the Tate-line coordinate, not an application of an idele character to a multiplicative scalar.

The lower and upper splitting coordinates have the imported weight-graded normalization. The two projections sum to the identity and come from the same Hodge splitting; the formula itself is defined for arbitrary supplied linear maps.

Apply the shared mixed-extension height construction to the strictly compared module. Compute the difference of the unique Frobenius splitting and the chosen Hodge splitting; use the chosen projection to subtract both beta terms with negative signs. Identify the resulting Tate-line class and apply the local linear functional.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `HeightPrevalue.zero_alpha`: For alpha=0 the prevalue is `gamma_phi−gamma_Fil`.
- `HeightPrevalue.gamma_add`: Adding a to `gamma_phi` adds a to the prevalue.
- `HeightPrevalue.character_smul`: A Qp-linear local character sends `a*z` to `a*chi(z)`.
- `HeightPrevalue.local_height`: Under the genuine mixed-extension splitting hypotheses, `h_p(A_Z(b,x))` equals `chi_p(HeightPrevalue)`.

**Checks.**

- `preheight_two_negative_terms`: For `V=Q²` with W the first coordinate and Fil0 the second, `s1(x,y)=(x,0)`, `s2(x,y)=(0,y)`, alpha=(1,2), `beta_phi=2*first`, `beta_Fil=3*second`, `gamma_phi=7` and `gamma_Fil=1`, the result is −2.
- `preheight_zero_alpha`: Changing alpha to 0 gives 6.
- With alpha=(1,2) as before, changing `gamma_phi` from 7 to 8 gives −1.
- `preheight_projection_order`: With the same alpha, beta and gamma data, exchanging s1 and s2 gives 6 instead of −2. This detects reversal of the chosen-complement and Fil0 projections.
- Both beta terms have negative signs.
- Holding the adjacent classes fixed does not force the local height to be fixed under a central change.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), §3.3, equations(16)–(17), pp. 905–906; Lemma 5.5, p. 924.

Use [Crystalline comparison for the height module](#nc-5-height-module-comparison); `Module.Dual`; [Nekovář's local heights](#nekovar-local-heights).

<a id="nc-5-local-height-coordinates"></a>

**Height and first extension as local coordinates.** For a nonzero nice quotient `U_Z` and a nonzero chosen local height functional `chi_p`, the map `(pi1,h_p∘tau_p):H1_f(G_p,U_Z)→H1_f(G_p,V)×Qp` is an isomorphism of schemes. In an affine presentation of a central fibre, `h_p` has the form a*(gamma−F(alpha)) with `a≠0`, so its inverse is gamma=h/a+F(alpha). The height is algebraic on this Selmer variety even though its pullback to the curve is analytic. Nonzero `chi_p` is indispensable.

The mixed-extension classifier, crystalline extension groups and the faithful twist are genuine imported objects. Over Qp, the chosen local character is an isomorphism on the Tate-line de Rham quotient.

Classify the crystalline central fibre as a torsor for `H1_f(G_p,Qp(1))≅Qp`. The preheight formula has a nonzero linear coefficient in the central coordinate, giving a polynomial fibre inverse. Use the imported global algebraic classifier and strict filtrations to patch these coordinates; the set equivalence alone does not prove a scheme isomorphism.

- A zero local functional collapses the central fibre and gives no such isomorphism.

### 6.6 Local terms and the height pair

<a id="nc-5-away-height-vanishes"></a>

**Vanishing for potentially unramified extensions.** For `v≠p`, a mixed extension M of Qp,V,Qp(1) which becomes unramified over a finite local extension satisfies `h_v(M)=0`. The hypothesis is on the whole mixed extension, not merely its graded pieces. In particular, proper path modules and their height pushouts at places of potential good reduction satisfy it by the imported path theorem after good-reduction base change.

This is `localHeight_potentiallyUnramified` of [Nekovář's local heights](#nekovar-local-heights), applied to path modules; the splitting `M≅V⊕N` is the one used there to define `h_v`. The finite local extension may be chosen Galois.

Invoke the generic vanishing theorem; its proof splits the V extensions away from p and reduces to a Tate-line extension. The Tate-line class becomes zero over the unramified extension. Inflation–restriction and zero local Tate invariants make restriction injective, so it was zero already. Apply to the path twist using proper potential-good reduction, not to an arbitrarily manufactured unramified semisimplification.

**Checks.**

- A ramified extension with unramified graded pieces is not covered.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), §3.2, Lemma 3.2 and proof, p. 903.

Use [Twisted height module](#nc-5-height-module-twist); Layer 5, albanese maps and chabauty–kim finiteness; [SelmerIwasawaCohomology](../SelmerIwasawaCohomology/README.md) §2.16 (local duality for the finite condition).

<a id="nc-5-finite-bad-height-image"></a>

**Finitely many bad-place heights.** For every finite place `v≠p`, the proper depth-two local Kummer map `j2,v:X(Qv)→H1(G_v,U2)` has finite image. Projecting to `U_Z`, twisting by `A_Z` and applying `h_v` therefore gives a finite set `Gamma_v`. At good places `Gamma_v={0}`. Thus only finitely many bad places enter the correction set, and all of them must be retained. Finiteness supplies no algorithm for computing `Gamma_v`.

X is a proper smooth curve over Q; an affine integral variant needs its own local domain and boundary hypotheses, which are not stated here. Use the p-adic unipotent quotient of the local path fundamental group with `v≠p`.

Import the local finite-image theorem from Layer 5, where the general Kim–Tamagawa specialization belongs. Take the image through the quotient, twist and height maps; a function on a finite image still has finite image. Use generic good-place vanishing outside a finite set. No bad contribution is discarded on grounds of finiteness alone.

**Checks.**

- The result is finite image, not identically zero at every bad place.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim and Akio Tamagawa](#reference-kt), Corollary 0.2, p. 1; §2, p. 6; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Theorem 3.6 and equation(19), p. 907.

Use Layer 5, albanese maps and chabauty–kim finiteness; [Twisted height module](#nc-5-height-module-twist); [Vanishing for potentially unramified extensions](#nc-5-away-height-vanishes); `Set.Finite.image`; [Finite away-place Kummer images](#finite-away-kummer-image); [Nekovář's local heights](#nekovar-local-heights).

<a id="nc-5-away-height-constants"></a>

**Signed away-place correction set.** For a finite index set T0 of all bad places different from p and finite local image sets `Gamma_v⊆Qp`, define `Upsilon={−sum_v t_v : t_v in Gamma_v for every v}`. It is finite, equals{0} for T0 empty or all `Gamma_v={0}`, and is a sound correction set even if `Gamma_v` are finite proved upper bounds rather than exact images. For `globalHeight=heightAtP+sum_v t_v`, the residual heightAtP−globalHeight lies in Upsilon. This fixes the positive sign printed in BDMTV equation(19).

Finite local images or proved finite supersets are supplied for every bad place. All height functions use one common idele character and compatible global/local normalization.

Form the finite product of the `Gamma_v` and map it by negative summation. For a global path extension, apply the generic local-to-global height sum identity and the membership of each local term. A proved finite enlargement preserves rational containment; exact equality of local images is separate evidence.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `AwayHeightConstants.finite`: Finite local sets and a finite index set give a finite correction set.
- `AwayHeightConstants.mem`: Every tuple of allowed local values yields its negative sum in Upsilon.
- `AwayHeightConstants.mono`: Enlarging each local set enlarges Upsilon.
- `AwayHeightConstants.all_zero`: All singleton-zero local sets give Upsilon={0}.
- `AwayHeightConstants.height_sum`: The global height sum identity puts heightAtP−globalHeight in Upsilon.

**Checks.**

- `away_empty`: For the empty place set the correction set is{0}.
- `away_nonzero_one_place`: One local set{2} gives correction set{−2}.
- `away_nonzero_two_places`: Local sets{1} and{2} give{−3}.
- `away_nonzero_cannot_be_dropped`: For local set{3}, neither 3 nor 0 belongs to the correction set.
- A singleton away-place value 3 produces correction −3, not 3 or 0.
- Upper bounds do not certify the exact depth-two locus.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan and Netan Dogra](#reference-bd1), Theorem 1.2(ii), p. 4 and Proposition 5.5, p. 21; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), equations(18)–(19), Lemma 3.7, pp. 907–908.

<a id="nc-5-quadratic-chabauty-pair"></a>

**Quadratic Chabauty pair.** Fix `W=H0(X_Qp,Omega1)*`, `AJ_b:X(Qp)→W`, a finite correction set Upsilon⊆Qp, an endomorphism `E:W→W`, a constant c in W and a Qp-bilinear form B:W×W→Qp. A quadratic Chabauty pair consists of theta:X(Qp)→Qp and Upsilon with these associated data such that: on every residue disc the joint map `(AJ_b,theta)` is given by convergent power series and is Zariski dense on every nonempty open subdisc; and for every x in `X(Q)`, `theta(x)−B(AJ_b(x),E AJ_b(x)+c)` belongs to Upsilon. Charts cover the local domain by finitely many images of the closed p-adic unit ball after rescaling. Density is the explicit assertion that a polynomial vanishing on any such open subdisc is the zero polynomial.

The curve application has g&gt;1; the genus-zero example only tests the interface. Charts are analytic on neighborhoods of the compact rescaled domains. The residue-disc power-series theorem supplies density on subdiscs.

Form joint coordinates indexed by one height coordinate and g Abel–Jacobi coordinates. Express analyticity with the power-series predicate and density by multivariate polynomial evaluation, with no opaque density placeholder. Require finite corrections and rational containment in the residual locus. A theta-only density statement is insufficient.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `IsQuadraticChabautyPair.rational_mem`: A rational point belongs to the local domain and has residual in Upsilon.
- `IsQuadraticChabautyPair.weaken_constants`: Replacing Upsilon by a finite superset preserves the pair.
- `IsQuadraticChabautyPair.non_graph`: On no nonempty open subdisc can theta equal a polynomial in the Abel–Jacobi coordinates.

**Checks.**

- `pair_identity_height`: For `g=0`, X=Qp, one identity chart on Zp, theta(t)=t, rational test set{0}, Upsilon={0}, and `E=c=B=0`, the pair predicate holds. This is not a geometric genus-zero QC theorem.
- `pair_constant_abel_jacobi_rejected`: With `g=1` and AJ=0 constant, theta(t)=t and the same chart, the pair predicate fails since the polynomial AJ-coordinate vanishes.
- `pair_wrong_correction_rejected`: For the `g=0` identity interface, replacing Upsilon={0} by{1} loses the rational test point 0.
- A constant Abel–Jacobi coordinate violates joint density even when theta is nonconstant.
- Analyticity only on an arbitrary disconnected neighborhood does not justify a zero bound without the subdisc density condition.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), §1.4, conditions(a)–(b), equation(5), pp. 890–891.

Use `AnalyticOnNhd`; `Padic`; `MvPolynomial.eval`.

<a id="nc-5-pair-of-heights"></a>

**Quadratic Chabauty pair from heights.** Assume the good-reduction proper-curve hypotheses, a nonzero rational nice correspondence, `r=g` and an isomorphism J(Q)⊗Qp→W induced by the p-adic logarithm (equivalently the required finite-index closure hypothesis together with `r=g`). Choose a nonzero idèle class character and an isotropic Hodge splitting as in [Nekovář's local heights](#nekovar-local-heights). Set `theta(x)=h_p(A_Z(b,x))`, Upsilon to the negative sum of all away-place image sets, `E=E_Z`, `c=c_Z`, and B to the global bilinear height restricted to the Mordell–Weil image and transported to W. These data form a quadratic Chabauty pair. No assertion that the entire global `H1_f` equals this image is needed.

The two adjacent extension classes lie in the Mordell–Weil image by [Adjacent extension classes of the twist](#nc-5-twist-two-classes), including the rational Chow–Heegner constant. The nonzero local character gives the height-coordinate isomorphism. The splitting is any isotropic splitting allowed in [Nekovář's local heights](#nekovar-local-heights); ordinary reduction or Panchishkin conditions are not added to this selected proper-curve theorem. For the selected [Nice rational correspondence](#nc-5-nice-correspondence) source chain, J is absolutely simple. An extension to nonsimple J needs a separately verified correspondence-to-alternating comparison; the general rank/Picard theorem is already nonsimple.

Use [Height and first extension as local coordinates](#nc-5-local-height-coordinates) and Layer 5 subdisc unipotent Albanese density to obtain the required joint density. Import Coleman/Layer 2 power-series descriptions for analyticity. Restrict the global bilinear pairing of [The global height and its decomposition into local heights](#nekovar-global-height) to the two Mordell–Weil classes and transport it along the logarithm isomorphism. Apply the global sum of local heights: `theta−B=−sum_away h_v`, so the corrected Upsilon gives containment. Use [Finitely many bad-place heights](#nc-5-finite-bad-height-image) for finiteness of Upsilon.

**Checks.**

- Rank g alone does not certify the logarithm isomorphism.
- The local height is used without falsely asserting that it is itself globally bilinear.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), §1.4, p. 890; Lemma 3.7 and proof, pp. 907–908; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan and Netan Dogra](#reference-bd1), Proposition 5.5, pp. 20–22.

Use [Quadratic Chabauty pair](#nc-5-quadratic-chabauty-pair); [Height and first extension as local coordinates](#nc-5-local-height-coordinates); [Adjacent extension classes of the twist](#nc-5-twist-two-classes); [Signed away-place correction set](#nc-5-away-height-constants); Layer 5, albanese maps and chabauty–kim finiteness; [Word coordinates and global transport](#nc-2-word-path-bridge); [Proper-curve Mordell–Weil Selmer cut](#mordell-weil-selmer-cut).

<a id="nc-5-pair-finite-locus"></a>

**Finiteness of the residual height locus.** For a quadratic Chabauty pair, the set {x in X(Qp): `theta(x)−B(AJ_b(x),E AJ_b(x)+c)` in Upsilon} is finite and contains `X(Q)`. More generally the finite-chart interface has a finite residual locus on its covered local domain. This is a finite p-adic superset, not a rational-point completeness theorem and not in general the exact depth-two Chabauty–Kim locus.

Use the compact closed chart domains and density on every nonempty open subdisc. Layer 5 supplies the analytic zero theorem for the imported convergent series, with the relevant compactness/subdisc hypotheses.

The finite-chart theorem applies in arbitrary finite coordinate dimension m. It uses `AJ:X→K^m`, a scalar height θ, a linear E, a vector c and a bilinear B. The joint coordinates indexed by `Option (Fin m)` place θ at `none` and AJ at `some i`. On finitely many compact charts covering Y, all coordinates are analytic and no nonzero multivariate polynomial in them has a zero germ at a chart point. For finite Υ the residual locus is finite, and so is every global point set in Y whose residuals lie in Υ. These explicit hypotheses give the same conclusion over any nontrivially normed field.

For each alpha in Upsilon the polynomial `T−B(W,E W+c)−alpha` is nonzero because its T coefficient is 1. Joint subdisc density makes its analytic pullback nonzero on every open subdisc. Invoke the Layer 5 analytic zero theorem on each compact chart, then take finite unions of finite zero sets and their chart images. Use `rational_mem` for containment. Identifying every surviving point as rational requires a separate certified exclusion argument.

**Checks.**

- A density assertion on one disc cannot be applied to an unchecked disc.
- An analytic function allowed to vanish identically on an open subdisc is rejected.
- With constant AJ and θ both zero and `Υ={0}`, an infinite compact chart lies wholly in the residual locus. The nonzero height-coordinate polynomial vanishes on it, so joint density fails.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), §1.4, explanation after equation(5), p. 891.

### 6.7 Determinants and equivariant features

<a id="nc-5-height-determinant"></a>

**Corrected height determinant.** Let psi(x) in `k^m` be the coordinate vector of the height feature `AJ_b(x)⊗(E AJ_b(x)+c)`, in a selected tensor-feature space, and anchors P1,…,Pm with known residuals `alpha_i`. For a candidate residual alpha form the `(m+1)×(m+1)` matrix whose first row is (theta(x)−alpha,psi(x)) and ith anchor row is `(theta(P_i)−alpha_i,psi(P_i))`. HeightDeterminant is its Matrix.det. Candidate and anchor residuals are subtracted separately. To use its vanishing as a height equation, the anchor feature matrix must have nonzero determinant. At an anchor with its own residual correction, the determinant vanishes because two rows coincide.

k is a field; the geometric application uses Qp. For arithmetic use alpha and all `alpha_i` belong to the complete signed correction set. X may index pairs (correspondence, point): candidate and anchor features may come from different correspondences if their corrected heights are evaluations of the same global functional on the same balanced feature space. This is the cross-class anchor convention in the `X_s(13)` application.

Index rows and columns by a distinguished height entry and m feature coordinates. Construct the matrix from the explicit formula and apply the determinant. Use row subtraction to prove the equation theorem when the anchor feature matrix is invertible.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `HeightDeterminant.matrix_first`: The top-left matrix entry is theta(x)−alpha.
- `HeightDeterminant.duplicate_row`: At an anchor with the same residual correction, the candidate row repeats an anchor row, so the determinant is 0.
- `HeightDeterminant.equation`: If the feature matrix is invertible and anchor corrected heights equal a linear functional L on their features, determinant 0 is equivalent to theta(x)−L(psi(x))=alpha.

**Checks.**

- `determinant_empty_features`: For `m=0`, theta(x)=x, candidate `x=7` and alpha=2, the determinant is 5.
- `determinant_nonzero_corrections`: For `m=1`, psi(x)=x, theta(x)=x+5, anchor 4 with correction −1 and candidate 2 with correction 2, the matrix is ((5,2),(10,4)), so its determinant is 0; dropping the corrections gives 10.
- `determinant_basis_cannot_be_omitted`: For `m=1` and the identically zero feature, any candidate has determinant 0, including `x=7` with theta(x)=x and alpha=0. This is not a finite equation.
- A singular anchor feature matrix can make the determinant vanish identically.
- m counts independent features, not merely available rational points.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Lemma 1.5, equation(6) and proof, pp. 891–892.

Use `Matrix.det`; [Signed away-place correction set](#nc-5-away-height-constants).

<a id="nc-5-determinant-criterion"></a>

**Determinant criterion with independent anchors.** Under the pair hypotheses, suppose the selected feature vectors `psi(P_i)` form a basis of the height-feature space and the anchor residuals `alpha_i` are correct. Then for each alpha in Upsilon, `HeightDeterminant_alpha(x)=0` is equivalent to `theta(x)−B(AJ_b(x),E AJ_b(x)+c)=alpha`. Its zero set is therefore finite; the union over alpha contains `X(Q)`. Without the feature-basis hypothesis none of these finiteness or equivalence conclusions follows merely from a determinant.

The bilinear pairing factors through a linear functional on the selected feature space. Feature coordinates are expressed in a fixed basis and the anchor feature matrix is invertible.

Subtract the column combination representing the height functional from the height column; anchor height entries become zero. Expand by that column: determinant is the candidate residual minus alpha, times the nonzero anchor feature determinant. Apply [Finiteness of the residual height locus](#nc-5-pair-finite-locus) for the finite union of residual levels.

**Checks.**

- The zero-feature determinant example fails the required basis hypothesis.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Netan Dogra, J. Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), Lemma 1.5, pp. 891–892.

Use [Corrected height determinant](#nc-5-height-determinant); [Finiteness of the residual height locus](#nc-5-pair-finite-locus).

<a id="nc-5-balanced-height-features"></a>

**Equivariant balanced height features.** Let `K_p=K⊗Qp` be a commutative finite etale Qp-algebra acting on W. If the chosen Hodge splitting is `K_p`-equivariant and the polarized height satisfies `B(a u,v)=B(u,a v)`, the Qp-valued bilinear form factors through a Qp-linear functional on `W⊗_{K_p}W`. If W is free of rank 1 over `K_p` and `dim_Qp K_p=g`, this balanced feature space has Qp dimension g, whereas `W⊗_{Qp}W` has dimension `g²`. The selected rational-point features must still be a Qp-basis. A Qp-valued form is not asserted `K_p`-linear into Qp without a `K_p`-module structure on that target.

The balancing action is the adjoint-compatible action for the selected polarization; equality with the same a on each side is verified for the real-multiplication application. `K_p` can be a product of fields. Freeness over `K_p`, rather than vector-space dimension alone, is required.

Import tensor-product universal properties and the shared equivariant splitting variation theorem. Balancing kills the defining tensor relations. Use a rank-one `K_p` basis to identify the balanced tensor with `K_p`, then restrict scalars to Qp. Read off dimensions and require the anchor feature determinant to certify the basis used for interpolation.

**Checks.**

- For `K_p=Qp×Qp` and `W=K_p`, the balanced dimension is 2 while the ordinary tensor dimension is 4.
- For the cubic real-multiplication example dimensions are 3 and 9; three dependent vectors still do not form a basis.

Steffen Muller, Jan Tuitman and Jan Vonk](#reference-bdmtv), §1.7, pp. 894–895; Remark 3.9, p. 908; §6.4.1, p. 932; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan and Netan Dogra](#reference-bdii), §4, Lemma 4.4, p. 22; §5, Lemma 5.3(1)–(2) and proof, pp. 22–23.

### 6.8 Potentially good reduction and independence of choices

<a id="nc-5-potential-good-pair"></a>

**Pair for potentially good reduction.** Under the [Quadratic Chabauty pair from heights](#nc-5-pair-of-heights) hypotheses, if X has potentially good reduction at every finite place, every away-from-p height image is{0}, so the corrected correction set is{0}. Then (theta,{0}) is a quadratic Chabauty pair. Potential good reduction at a single bad place does not dispose of another bad place.

The imported path representation is potentially unramified at every `v≠p` after a good-reduction extension. The same nonzero character and Hodge splitting are used throughout.

Apply [Vanishing for potentially unramified extensions](#nc-5-away-height-vanishes) at each place to the path twist. Use `AwayHeightConstants.all_zero`, and then [Quadratic Chabauty pair from heights](#nc-5-pair-of-heights) with that set.

**Independence of height choices.** Changing the allowed Hodge splitting changes theta and the transported global bilinear pairing by the same bilinear expression `D(AJ_b(x),E AJ_b(x)+c)`, so their residual and its height locus agree. Arbitrary unrelated characters are not identified by this scaling argument.
