The preheight convention is

```text
γφ − γFil − βφ(s₁α) − βFil(s₂α).
```

In a two-dimensional frame, take `α=(1,2)`, `s₁(a,b)=(a,0)`, `s₂(a,b)=(0,b)`, `βφ(a,b)=2a`, `βFil(a,b)=3b`, `γφ=7` and `γFil=1`. The value is `7−1−2−6=−2`. Reversing the two projections makes both correction values zero and gives 6. This checks the projections’ order as well as the two minus signs. Changing `γφ` by t changes the preheight by t.

The global height is the sum of its local contributions. If the only away-place height is 3, the corrected p-height equals the global bilinear height minus 3. Thus `Υ={−3}`. Taking `Υ={3}` reverses the locus equation. Under a fixed potentially good extension, potentially unramified mixed extensions have zero away-height; an arbitrary ramified extension does not satisfy that vanishing.

A nice correspondence must have zero primitive cup contraction and a nonzero primitive symmetric tensor class. The zero correspondence meets the first requirement but fails the second. Passing from a rational span of lattice classes to every p-adic class in its span requires an additional assertion and is not implicit in the lattice-to-p-adic realization map.

The local height coordinate is recovered through the nonzero idele character and a chosen filtration splitting. The zero character makes every corresponding height zero and cannot provide an inverse coordinate. At `rank r=g`, expressing the global bilinear form through local logarithms also requires the localization isomorphism. Equality of ranks alone supplies no basis.

For a corrected determinant with `m+1` rows, the selected m rational anchor rows must give a full-rank feature matrix. Repeated anchors can make every such determinant zero. When an anchor minor is nonzero, the vanishing determinant is exactly the affine height relation for the remaining row. The nonzero-minor hypothesis is part of the criterion.

The relative-cycle comparison gives the three graded pieces `ℚ_p`, V and `ℚ_p(1)`. Adding a pullback preserves symmetry modulo pullbacks, trace zero and the primitive class when the swap stabilizes that condition and trace and class kill the pullback space. A finite place set and finite local value sets give a finite signed correction set, and the global height identity puts `h_p−h` in that set. The determinant uses the candidate correction in the first row and each anchor’s own correction in its row. A linear feature functional fitting the anchor heights and a nonzero determinant of the anchor feature matrix make determinant zero equivalent to `θ(x)−L(ψ(x))=α`. The nonzero determinant is the basis hypothesis, rather than a nonvanishing condition on the candidate height.

## Layer 7: Sections and the conjectural frontier

Separate proved injectivity and conditional dimension estimates from the section and eventual-equality conjectures. Free-Lie and surface-group characters, rational Selmer vanishing and tangential base points provide the precise hypotheses of the conditional bridges.

### 7.0 Rational Tate Selmer dimensions

<a id="arithmetic-higher-k-inputs"></a>

**Arithmetic higher K-group finiteness and rank.** For every number field F, write `K_m(𝒪_F)=exactKGroup(P(𝒪_F),m)` on the split exact category of finite projective modules supplied by GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic §§6.1.1–6.1.7; `exactKGroup` is its consumer alias of GeneralAlgebraicKTheory §§2.2–2.6's `KGroup`. Prove that these groups are finitely generated for `m≥0`, and, for `k≥2`, that `K_(2k−2)(𝒪_F)` is finite and `rank K_(2k−1)(𝒪_F)` is `r₁+r₂` for odd k and `r₂` for even k. Here r₁ and r₂ count the real embeddings and complex pairs of F. The arithmetic finite-generation theorem and its integer-ring consequences are targets here. The generic K-group carrier remains with its supplier; use ColemanIntegration L3.Fa.1 for scheme specialization/localization and L3.Fc.1 for the complex regulator and Borel rank theorem.

For every positive-rank finite projective `𝒪_F`-module P, construct the integral Steinberg module as the top reduced homology of the building of proper nonzero subspaces of `P⊗F`, and prove finite generation of `H_i(Aut(P),St(P⊗F))` for all i≥0, with the usual rank-one augmented-homology convention. Quillen's filtration of the supplied Q-construction with these groups proves K-group finite generation. The rank-zero category contributes its zero object. The supplied localization sequence and finite-field K-groups identify `K_m(𝒪_F)⊗ℚ` with `K_m(F)⊗ℚ` for m≥2. Transport the supplied odd-degree Borel rank calculation through this identification. For the even-degree part, prove Borel's rational vanishing for `K_(2k−2)(𝒪_F)` by the even primitive part of stable rational arithmetic-group cohomology, and combine with finite generation to obtain finiteness. The rational vanishing alone would not imply integral finiteness. The complex regulator is imported on the common K-group carrier, not constructed again.

The API is `arithmeticK.finiteGeneration`, `arithmeticK.evenFinite` and `arithmeticK.oddRank`. GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic's generic K-groups and ColemanIntegration's regulator foundations precede these arithmetic targets; these targets precede the higher-Chern comparison below. GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic's arithmetic motivation section supplies none of the arithmetic finiteness or higher-Chern theorems.

### 7.1 Sections and the section conjecture

<a id="nc-6-section-classes"></a>

**Conjugacy classes of Galois sections.** Let k be a field with separable closure `k^s` and `Γ_k = Gal(k^s/k)`, and let X be a quasi-compact geometrically connected k-scheme with a geometric point x̄ of `X_{k^s}`. Write `π = π_1^ét(X, x̄)`, `Δ = π_1^ét(X_{k^s}, x̄)` and pr: `π → Γ_k` for the projection of the arithmetic exact sequence `1 → Δ → π → Γ_k → 1` (IG.1). A section is a continuous group homomorphism `s: Γ_k → π` with pr `∘ s = id`. The geometric kernel acts on sections by `(δ·s)(σ) = δ s(σ) δ⁻¹`. The set of sections modulo this action is Sect(X/k). Equivalently, `π` acts by `γ·s = c_γ ∘ s ∘ c_{pr(γ)⁻¹}` (conjugation `c_γ`), and this action has the same orbits, because `π = Δ·s(Γ_k)` and `s(τ)` acts trivially on s. A change of geometric base point along a geometric arithmetic path restricting to identity on constant covers, as in [Arithmetic path torsor](#nc-0-arithmetic-geometric-paths), induces a bijection of the sets of classes that does not depend on the path, so Sect(X/k) depends only on `X/k` up to canonical bijection. When a reference section `s_0` is fixed, `s ↦ [σ ↦ s(σ) s_0(σ)⁻¹]` identifies Sect(X/k) with the nonabelian `H¹(Γ_k, Δ)` of Layer 0, where `Γ_k` acts on `Δ` by conjugation through `s_0`; the class of `s_0` goes to the base point.

k any field; X quasi-compact and geometrically connected over k, so that the sequence of IG.1 is exact. Sections are continuous homomorphisms of profinite groups; the equivalence relation is conjugation by the geometric kernel `Δ` only. No hyperbolicity or properness is assumed in the definition; those hypotheses enter the theorems that use it.

Import the exact sequence `1 → Δ → π → Γ_k → 1` and its continuity from EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.0.A2. Check that `δ·s` is again a continuous section (pr kills `Δ`) and that this is a group action; take orbits with Mathlib's orbit quotient. Show that Kim's π-action has the same orbits: write `γ = δ s(τ)` and compute `c_{s(τ)} ∘ s ∘ c_{τ⁻¹} = s`. Base-point change: a geometric arithmetic path restricting to identity on constant covers `p: x̄ → x̄'` gives compatible isomorphisms of `π` and `Δ` (IG.0); two such paths differ by an element of `Δ`, which acts trivially on classes. With a reference section `s_0`, the difference `σ ↦ s(σ)s_0(σ)⁻¹` is a continuous 1-cocycle for the `s_0-twisted` action, conjugation by `δ` changes it by the coboundary of `δ`, and every cocycle c gives the section `c·s_0`; this is the bijection with `H¹(Γ_k, Δ)` ([Nonabelian first cohomology as a pointed set](#nc-3-nonabelian-h1), [Reference section change twists the action](#nc-0-reference-section-change)).

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `SectionClasses.mk`: The class `[s] ∈` Sect(X/k) of a continuous section s of pr.
- `SectionClasses.mk_eq_mk_iff`: `[s] = [t]` if and only if `t = δ s δ⁻¹` for some `δ` in the geometric kernel `Δ`.
- `SectionClasses.orbit_eq_kim`: The orbits of Kim's action of the whole group `π (γ·s = c_γ ∘ s ∘ c_{pr(γ)⁻¹})` are exactly the Δ-conjugacy classes.
- `SectionClasses.equivH1`: For a fixed section `s_0`, the map `[s] ↦ [σ ↦ s(σ)s_0(σ)⁻¹]` is a bijection Sect(X/k) `≅ H¹(Γ_k, Δ)` with `Γ_k` acting through `s_0`, sending `[s_0]` to the base point.
- `SectionClasses.map`: A k-morphism `f: X → Y` with compatible geometric base points induces Sect(X/k) `→` Sect(Y/k), independent of the geometric arithmetic path restricting to identity on constant covers chosen to compare base points, with `map_id` and `map_comp`.
- `SectionClasses.restrict`: For a finite separable extension `k'/k`, restriction of a section to `Γ_{k'}` gives Sect(X/k) `→ Sect(X_{k'}/k')`, compatible with map.
- `SectionClasses.basepointEquiv`: A geometric arithmetic path `x̄ → x̄'` restricting to identity on constant covers induces a bijection of the sets of classes; two such paths induce the same bijection.
- `GaloisSection.diff`: The difference cocycle `σ ↦ s(σ)s_0(σ)⁻¹` of two sections, with values in the geometric kernel `Δ`.
- `GaloisSection.diff_mul`: diff(στ) `=` diff(σ) `· s_0(σ)` diff(τ) `s_0(σ)⁻¹`: the difference is a 1-cocycle for the conjugation action through `s_0`.
- `SectionClasses.map_mk`: SectionClasses.map `f [s] = [f ∘ s]` for a morphism of extensions f over `Γ_k`.

**Checks.**

- For `X=Spec ℚ`, an arithmetic path γ with nontrivial inner conjugation sends the identity section to `σ↦γσγ⁻¹`, which does not split the fixed identity quotient. Restriction to identity on constants excludes it.
- `SectionClasses.spec_field_unique`: For `X = Spec k`, Sect(X/k) has exactly one element, the class of the identity section of `π = Γ_k`.
- `SectionClasses.projectiveLine_unique`: For `X = P¹_k`, Sect(X/k) has exactly one element, because the geometric kernel is trivial.
- `SectionClasses.gm_kummer`: For char `k = 0` and `X = G_{m,k}` with the reference section of the point 1, SectionClasses.equivH1 identifies `Sect(G_m/k)` with `H¹(k, Ẑ(1))`, and Kummer theory identifies this with the profinite completion `lim_n k^×/k^{×n}`.
- `SectionClasses.raw_sections_not_classes`: For `X = G_{m,Q}`, a section s and its conjugate `δ s δ⁻¹` by `δ ∈ Ẑ(1)` with `δ² ≠ 1` differ as homomorphisms (complex conjugation acts on Ẑ(1) by inversion, so the difference cocycle `δ·σ(δ)⁻¹` is nontrivial `at σ = c`) but have the same class: a definition that forgets the quotient is wrong.
- For `X = Spec k` the kernel `Δ` is trivial, `π = Γ_k`, and Sect(Spec `k/k`) has exactly one element.
- For `X = P¹_k` the kernel `Δ` is trivial (`P¹` is simply connected over `k^s`), so Sect(P¹/k) is one point although `P¹(k)` is infinite when k is.
- For `X = G_{m,k}` in characteristic zero `Δ = Ẑ(1)` and `Sect(G_m/k) ≅ H¹(k, Ẑ(1)) ≅ lim_n k^×/k^{×n}` by Kummer theory.

<a id="nc-6-section-class-map"></a>

**The section map of rational points.** For `X/k` as in [Conjugacy classes of Galois sections](#nc-6-section-classes) and `x ∈ X(k)`, the k-rational point gives a section `s_x` of `π_1^ét(X, x̄_x) → Γ_k` for a geometric point `x̄_x` over x (IG.1), whose image is a decomposition group of a point of the universal pro-étale cover over x. Transporting `s_x` along any geometric arithmetic path restricting to identity on constant covers `x̄_x → x̄` ([Path transport of an endpoint section](#nc-0-transferred-endpoint-section)) gives a section of pr whose Δ-conjugacy class does not depend on the path. The section map is `κ_X: X(k) →` Sect(X/k), `x ↦ [s_x]`. If `b ∈ X(k)` is a reference point and Sect(X/k) is identified with `H¹(Γ_k, Δ)` through `s_b`, then `κ_X(x)` is the class of the `Γ_k`-equivariant `Δ`-torsor of étale paths from b to x ([Arithmetic path torsor](#nc-0-arithmetic-geometric-paths)). The map is natural for k-morphisms and compatible with restriction to finite separable extensions. `κ_X(x) = κ_X(y)` holds exactly when the path torsor `P(x, y)` has a `Γ_k`-fixed path ([Neutral path classes and conjugate sections](#nc-0-path-section-comparison)).

X quasi-compact and geometrically connected over k; `x ∈ X(k)`. The map uses only rational points. Tangential base points give cuspidal sections of open curves (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups §IG.1.2) that are not values of `κ_X` on `X(k)`.

A k-point `x: Spec k → X` induces `Γ_k = π_1(Spec k) → π_1(X, x̄_x)`, a section by functoriality (IG.1). Transport along a geometric arithmetic path `p: x̄_x → x̄` restricting to identity on constant covers gives `p s_x p⁻¹`; replacing p by `h·p` with h in the target geometric kernel conjugates the result by h ([Path transport of an endpoint section](#nc-0-transferred-endpoint-section)). With reference b, the difference cocycle of the transported `s_x` against `s_b` is the cocycle of the path torsor `P(b, x)` ([Cocycle of a geometric arithmetic path](#nc-0-arithmetic-path-cocycle)). Naturality follows from functoriality of path torsors and sections ([Functoriality of arithmetic path classes](#nc-0-arithmetic-path-functoriality)).

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `sectionClassMap_eq_pathTorsor`: With a reference point b, `κ_X(x)` corresponds under SectionClasses.equivH1 to the class of the path torsor `P(b, x)` in `H¹(Γ_k, Δ)`.
- `sectionClassMap_base`: Under the identification with `H¹` through `s_b`, `κ_X(b)` is the base point.
- `sectionClassMap_natural`: For a k-morphism `f: X → Y`, `κ_Y ∘ f =` SectionClasses.map `f ∘ κ_X` on `X(k)`.
- `sectionClassMap_restrict`: For finite separable `k'/k`, SectionClasses.restrict `∘ κ_X = κ_{X_{k'}} ∘ (X(k) → X(k'))`.
- `sectionClassMap_eq_iff`: `κ_X(x) = κ_X(y)` if and only if the `Γ_k`-equivariant torsor of geometric paths from x to y has a `Γ_k`-fixed element.

**Checks.**

- `sectionClassMap_spec_field`: For `X = Spec k` the section map is the bijection between one-point sets.
- `sectionClassMap_projectiveLine_not_injective`: For `X = P¹_Q`, `κ_X(0) = κ_X(1)` although `0 ≠ 1`, since Sect(P¹/Q) is a point; hyperbolicity is needed for injectivity.
- `sectionClassMap_gm_eq_kummer`: For `X = G_{m,Q}` with reference point 1, `κ_X` is the Kummer map `Q^× → lim_n Q^×/Q^{×n}`; it is injective because `Q^× = {±1} ×` (free abelian group) has no nontrivial element divisible by every n, and `κ_X(−1) ≠ κ_X(1)` since −1 is not a square.
- `sectionClassMap_gm_not_surjective`: For `X = G_{m,Q}`, `κ_X` is not surjective: `Q^×` is countable while `lim_n Q^×/Q^{×n}` is uncountable.
- For `X = Spec k`, `κ_X` is the unique map from a point to a point.
- For `X = P¹_k` with k infinite, `κ_X` is constant and not injective.
- For `X = G_{m,k}` with reference `b = 1`, `κ_X(a)` is the Kummer class of a `∈ k^×`.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Introduction, p. 90; [Jakob Stix](#reference-stix-2008v1), §1.1, p. 1; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Ishai Dan-Cohen, Minhyong Kim and Stefan Wewers](#reference-bdckw-2018v4), §1.2, p. 2.

<a id="nc-6-kummer-section-comparison"></a>

**Sections of an abelian variety and the Kummer map.** Let `A/k` be an abelian variety and `n ≥ 1` invertible in k. Multiplication by n is finite étale and geometrically Galois, with geometric deck group A[n](k^s) and its natural `Γ_k`-action. The `Γ_k`-stable geometric kernel defines a quotient `π_1(A/k) → π^{[n]}(A/k)`, an extension of `Γ_k` by A[n](k^s). For a `∈ A(k)`, let `s_a` and `s_0` be the images in `π^{[n]}(A/k)` of sections attached to a and to the origin. Then the difference cocycle `σ ↦ s_a(σ) s_0(σ)⁻¹`, with values in A[n](k^s), represents the Kummer class `δ_n(a) ∈ H¹(k, A[n])` of [Rational abelian Kummer and Sha comparison](#abelian-kummer-mordell-weil), with the sign convention `δ_n(a)(σ) = σ(b) − b` for any b with nb `=` a. In characteristic zero, passing to the limit over all n gives the profinite Kummer class of a in `H¹(k,T̂A)`, with `T̂A=lim_n A[n](k^s)`. In characteristic `ℓ>0`, take only n prime to ℓ and use the prime-to-ℓ Tate module `T̂^(ℓ′)A=lim_(n,ℓ)=1 A[n](k^s)` and the corresponding Kummer class. For a smooth proper geometrically connected curve X with a rational point b and ordinary Jacobian J, combining with the Abel–Jacobi map `ι_b` and InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups §IG.0.T1 and AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli §A4.4 (Tate module and étale `H¹` of the Jacobian), the abelianised section map of X is `x ↦` Kummer class of [x − b], using the prime-to-characteristic quotient in positive characteristic. For an open curve `C−D`, the corresponding boundary-inclusive statement uses the generalized Jacobian `J_D` of Layer 2.

A abelian variety over k; n invertible in k (all n when char `k = 0`). The ordinary-Jacobian clause requires X smooth, proper and geometrically connected; its positive-characteristic version uses only prime-to-characteristic covers. Sign convention: Kummer cocycle `σ(b) − b` with nb `=` a, equal to the difference cocycle `s_a s_0⁻¹`.

Identify the fibre of `[n]: A → A` over 0 with A[n](k^s); `s_0` acts on it through the natural Galois action. To let `s_a` act on the fibre over 0, choose the path from 0 to a given on the cover [n] by translation by a fixed b with nb `=` a. Compute `s_a(σ)(P) = −b + σ(P + b) = σ(P) + (σ(b) − b)`, so `s_a(σ)s_0(σ)⁻¹` is translation by `σ(b) − b`, a Kummer cocycle ([Rational abelian Kummer and Sha comparison](#abelian-kummer-mordell-weil)). Compatibility of the covers [nm] `→ [n]` gives the inverse limit statement; for smooth proper geometrically connected curves use the Abel–Jacobi functoriality of sections and the identification of T̂J (prime to the characteristic when positive) with the corresponding abelianised geometric fundamental group (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups §IG.0.T1 and AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli §A4.4).

**Checks.**

- For `E:y²=x³−2` over `ℚ`, the cover [2] has degree four and geometric deck group of order four, but its rational deck group is trivial because `E[2](ℚ)=0`.
- For `E: y² = x³ − x` over Q and a `= (0, 0)`, `δ_2(a) ≠ 0` because `E(Q) = E`[2](Q) `≅ (Z/2)²` and so `2E(Q) = 0`; hence the images of `s_a` and `s_0` in `π^{[2]}(E/Q)` are not conjugate.
- For a `= 0` the difference cocycle is trivial and `δ_n(0) = 0`.
- For `X=𝔾_m/ℚ`, `b=1`, `x=−1`, the mod-two section class is nonzero since −1 is not a square, whereas the ordinary Jacobian of `ℙ¹` is zero. For `ℙ¹−{0,1,∞}`, the generalized Jacobian is `𝔾_m²`; both toric directions are required.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jakob Stix](#reference-stix-2008v1), Appendix B, Proposition 44 and proof, p. 22.

<a id="nc-6-section-map-injective"></a>

**Injectivity of the section map.** Let k be a field such that, for every abelian variety `A/k`, the group `A(k)` has no nonzero element divisible by every `n ≥ 1` invertible in k. If `X/k` is a geometrically connected variety that admits an immersion into an abelian variety over k, then `κ_X: X(k) →` Sect(X/k) is injective. Consequently, for a number field k and a smooth projective geometrically connected curve `X/k` of genus `g ≥ 1` (in particular for every proper hyperbolic curve, `g ≥ 2`), the section map `κ_X` is injective.

The divisibility hypothesis concerns all abelian varieties over k; over a number field it follows from the Mordell–Weil theorem. For a curve, `X(k) = ∅` makes the statement empty; otherwise a rational point b gives the Abel–Jacobi closed immersion `X → J` for `g ≥ 1`. The theorem is stated for every field satisfying the divisibility hypothesis; its number-field instance is derived here from Mordell–Weil.

If `X(k)` is empty there is nothing to prove; otherwise fix an immersion `ι: X → A` over k (for a curve, the Abel–Jacobi map at b, JacobianChallenge Layer F). By naturality of the section map `(sectionClassMap_natural)` it suffices to show injectivity for A, since `ι` is injective on k-points. If `κ_A(x) = κ_A(y)`, then for every n the images in `π^{[n]}(A/k)` are conjugate, so by [Sections of an abelian variety and the Kummer map](#nc-6-kummer-section-comparison) `δ_n(x − y) = 0`, that is `x − y ∈` nA(k) for all n. By hypothesis `x − y = 0`. Over a number field `A(k)` is finitely generated ([Rational abelian Kummer and Sha comparison](#abelian-kummer-mordell-weil)), and a finitely generated abelian group has no nonzero element divisible by every n: write it as `Z^r ⊕` (finite) and take n a multiple of the torsion exponent.

**Checks.**

- Elliptic curves over Q: for `E: y² = x³ − x`, the four rational points have pairwise distinct section classes.
- The non-example `P¹_Q` (no immersion into an abelian variety, `κ` constant) shows the immersion hypothesis cannot be dropped.
- The elementary step: in `Z ⊕ Z/6`, an element divisible by every `n ≥ 1` is zero.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jakob Stix](#reference-stix-2008v1), Appendix B, Theorem 45 and Remark 46, p. 22, with the proof of Theorem 45 on p. 23; §1.1, p. 2; [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Introduction, p. 90.

<a id="nc-6-section-conjecture"></a>

**Grothendieck's section conjecture.** For a field k and a quasi-compact geometrically connected k-scheme X, the proposition SectionConjecture(X/k) states that the section map `κ_X: X(k) →` Sect(X/k) is a bijection. `GrothendieckSectionConjecture` quantifies over every number field k and every smooth projective geometrically connected curve `X/k` of genus at least 2. This is the number-field restriction of the printed statement over fields finitely generated over `ℚ`. Define `GrothendieckSectionConjectureFinitelyGenerated` by the same curve hypotheses and bijectivity, quantifying instead over every field k finitely generated as a field over `ℚ`. Both are open propositions; any result that uses either lists it among its hypotheses. By [Injectivity of the section map](#nc-6-section-map-injective), the number-field instance is equivalent to surjectivity of `κ_X`; in particular it predicts that a curve without rational points has no sections. The cuspidal form for affine hyperbolic curves is specified below; the birational and p-adic forms are different statements.

The propositions concern rational points and geometric-kernel conjugacy classes of continuous sections; none is asserted. The genus bound and the respective base-field hypotheses belong to the global conjectures, not to SectionConjecture(X/k). Finite generation is as a field: `ℚ(t)` is included in the finitely-generated version. In Mathlib this hypothesis is `Algebra.EssFiniteType ℚ k`, not `Algebra.FiniteType ℚ k`, which would exclude `ℚ(t)`.

Define SectionConjecture(X/k) as bijectivity of `κ_X` ([The section map of rational points](#nc-6-section-class-map)). Define the two global propositions with their respective field quantifiers and smooth projective geometrically connected curves of genus `≥ 2`. The finitely-generated proposition implies the number-field proposition because a finite extension of `ℚ` is finitely generated as a field. Derive the number-field equivalence with surjectivity from [Injectivity of the section map](#nc-6-section-map-injective).

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `sectionConjecture_iff_surjective`: For a number field k and a smooth projective geometrically connected curve `X/k` of genus `≥ 1`, SectionConjecture(X/k) holds if and only if `κ_X` is surjective.
- `sectionConjecture_isEmpty_iff`: If `X(k) = ∅`, SectionConjecture(X/k) holds if and only if Sect(X/k) `= ∅`, that is, the arithmetic sequence has no continuous section.
- `GrothendieckSectionConjecture`: The proposition: for every number field k and every smooth projective geometrically connected curve `X/k` of genus `≥ 2`, SectionConjecture(X/k).
- `GrothendieckSectionConjectureFinitelyGenerated`: The proposition: for every field k finitely generated over `ℚ` and every smooth projective geometrically connected curve `X/k` of genus `≥ 2`, SectionConjecture(X/k).
- `sectionConjecture_of_equiv`: SectionConjecture is invariant under isomorphism of k-schemes, via SectionClasses.map and `sectionClassMap_natural`.
- The section conjecture uses the geometric-kernel conjugacy classes of sections of `pr:π→Γ_k` and the rational-point map `κ_X:X(k)→Sect(X/k)`; bijectivity is asserted for this geometric map.

**Checks.**

- `sectionConjecture_spec_field`: SectionConjecture(Spec `k/k`) holds: both sides are one-point sets.
- `not_sectionConjecture_projectiveLine`: `SectionConjecture(P¹_Q/Q)` fails because `κ` is constant on the infinite set `P¹(Q)`; a statement without the genus bound is false.
- `not_sectionConjecture_gm`: `SectionConjecture(G_{m,Q}/Q)` fails because the Kummer map `Q^× → lim_n Q^×/Q^{×n}` is injective but not surjective; injectivity alone is not the conjecture.
- Hoshi's pro-p non-example: for some prime p and number field k, a smooth projective geometrically connected curve `X/k` of genus `≥ 2` has a continuous section of `π₁(X)/ker(Δ → Δ^(p)) → Γ_k` whose `Δ^(p)`-conjugacy class comes from no point of `X(k)`, where `Δ = π₁(X_k̄)` and `Δ^(p)` is its maximal pro-p quotient. Thus the geometrically pro-p analogue of `GrothendieckSectionConjecture` fails surjectivity, with the full `Γ_k` retained: Yuichiro Hoshi, [*Existence of nongeometric pro-p Galois sections of hyperbolic curves*](https://ems.press/journals/prims/articles/4307), *Publ. RIMS* (2010).
- `sectionConjecture_iff_bijective`: SectionConjecture(X/k) is exactly bijectivity of `κ_X`; for an abstract section datum with a non-injective point map (two points with equal sections) it fails.
- SectionConjecture(Spec `k/k`) holds for every field k.
- `SectionConjecture(P¹_Q/Q)` and `SectionConjecture(G_{m,Q}/Q)` both fail, for different reasons (non-injective, non-surjective).
- A genus-two curve over `ℚ(t)` is quantified over by `GrothendieckSectionConjectureFinitelyGenerated`, but not by `GrothendieckSectionConjecture`; every genus-two curve over a number field occurs in both.
- `ℚ̄` and `ℚ_p` are outside both global quantifiers: neither is finitely generated as a field over `ℚ`.

The construction and its conventions follow [Alexander Grothendieck](#reference-grothendieck-faltings-1983), letter to Faltings, formulation (7) and its proper-curve qualification; [Jakob Stix](#reference-stix-2013), Introduction, Conjecture 2, p. xiv, and Remark 3, p. xv; [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Introduction, p. 90; [Jakob Stix](#reference-stix-2008v1), §1.1, Conjecture 1, p. 1; [Jennifer S. Balakrishnan, Ishai Dan-Cohen, Minhyong Kim and Stefan Wewers](#reference-bdckw-2018v4), §1.2, p. 2 and §3.4, p. 13.

Use [The section map of rational points](#nc-6-section-class-map); [Injectivity of the section map](#nc-6-section-map-injective); `Function.Bijective`.

<a id="nc-6-cuspidal-section-conjecture"></a>

**Cuspidal packets and the affine section conjecture.** Let k be a characteristic-zero field and `U = X ∖ D` a smooth geometrically connected affine curve, with X its smooth projective compactification and D a nonempty reduced finite étale divisor. Assume hyperbolicity, `2g(X) − 2 + deg(D) > 0`. For `d ∈ D(k)`, put `U_d = U ×_X Spec(O^h_{X,d})`, the punctured henselian neighbourhood at d. Its arithmetic group fits into `1 → Ẑ(1) → π₁(U_d) → Γ_k → 1`. Define `CuspidalPacket(U/k,d)` as the image of `Sect(U_d/k) → Sect(U/k)`. A class is cuspidal at d precisely when a representative factors through this local group, equivalently through the corresponding decomposition subgroup after a geometric conjugation. A rational nonzero tangent vector supplies a local section and hence an element of the packet.

For k finitely generated as a field over `ℚ`, define `CuspidalSectionConjecture(U/k) : Prop` to say that the natural map from the disjoint union `U(k) ⊔ (⨿_(d ∈ D(k)) CuspidalPacket(U/k,d))` to `Sect(U/k)` is bijective. Thus each class comes either from a unique rational point of U or from a unique rational cusp d and a class in its packet; interior-point classes and the packets are pairwise distinct. This is a conjectural exhaustion statement, not a theorem asserting that every section is geometric. Its number-field restriction uses the same definition.

The passage between `GrothendieckSectionConjecture` and `CuspidalSectionConjecture` involves lifting sections from X to open subcurves U, the cuspidalisation problem studied by Mohamed Saïdi, [*The cuspidalisation of sections of arithmetic fundamental groups*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aim.2012.04.002), *Adv. Math.* (2012).

The packet question concerns a family of conjugacy classes per cusp, not one chosen class. After choosing a local section, `Sect(U_d/k)` is a torsor identified with `H¹(k, Ẑ(1)) = lim_n k×/(k×)^n`; no canonical origin is required for the packet definition. Over number fields the local-to-global map on section classes is injective, different packets are disjoint and no packet meets the interior-point image. Each packet is uncountable there. These assertions use the hypotheses in Stix's Theorem 17 and Corollary 19; no singleton or cardinality assertion is made over arbitrary characteristic-zero fields. Rational tangent vectors provide classes but are not asserted to exhaust a packet.

Construct the local sequence from the tame punctured branch of IG.1.2 and the characteristic-zero Kummer tower. Apply SectionClasses.map and take its range, with geometric-kernel conjugacy on both sides. Under injectivity of section maps for all smooth projective curves of genus `≥ 2` over finite extensions of k, Stix's finite étale neighbourhood argument proves packet injectivity and separation from each other and from interior points; [Injectivity of the section map](#nc-6-section-map-injective) supplies this hypothesis for number fields. The bijectivity proposition itself makes sense for every such hyperbolic pair over a characteristic-zero field; the affine conjecture quantifies over fields finitely generated over `ℚ`.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `CuspidalPacket`: The subset of section classes obtained from the local section classes at the specified rational cusp.
- `CuspidalSectionConjecture`: Bijectivity of the geometric interior-point and packet map, with every member of each cuspidal packet retained.
- This bijectivity is equivalent to injectivity of the interior-point map, disjointness of its image from every packet, disjointness of packets at distinct cusps, and exhaustion of the section classes by the interior image and the packets.
- Under this proposition, a section class belonging to two packets has equal cusp indices.
- With empty boundary, the packet decomposition reduces to bijectivity of the proper-curve section map.

**Checks.**

- For `U = ℙ¹_ℚ ∖ {0,1,∞}`, the inequality is `−2 + 3 > 0`. The points 2 and 3 give distinct interior section classes, and the three rational cusps give disjoint uncountable packets, each disjoint from those point classes. The assertion that these interior classes and three packets exhaust `Sect(U/ℚ)` is the conjecture, not a consequence of their construction.
- A model section-class set `P ⊔ (D × ℤ)` with interior inclusion and packets `{(d,n) | n ∈ ℤ}` satisfies the abstract proposition: even three cusps can each retain many classes. Collapsing each packet to one class changes the assertion.
- If two different cusp indices have overlapping packets, or an interior class lies in a packet, the abstract bijectivity proposition fails. For an empty cusp index set it is exactly bijectivity of the interior map.
- The nonhyperbolic example `U = G_m` has identical packets at 0 and `∞`, both equal to all of `Sect(G_m/k)`. It therefore fails the pairwise separation requirement; the hyperbolicity hypothesis cannot be discarded.

The construction and its conventions follow [Jakob Stix](#reference-stix-cuspidal-2012), §1.2, Definition 1 and the affine-conjecture discussion, and §4.1, Theorem 17, Remark 18(3) and Corollary 19; [Jakob Stix](#reference-stix-2013), Introduction, Conjecture 6, p. xvi, with the accompanying cuspidal interpretation; [Alexander Grothendieck](#reference-grothendieck-faltings-1983), the third formulation and its discussion of packets at infinity.

### 7.2 Kim's dimension conjecture

<a id="nc-6-kim-dimension-conjecture"></a>

**Kim's dimension conjecture.** Setting (Kim 2009, pp.91–96): X is a smooth hyperbolic curve over Q, `𝒳 ⊂ 𝒳′` a smooth model over `Z[1/S]` with smooth compactification and smooth complement, `b ∈ 𝒳(Z[1/S])` or an integral tangential base point (for a tangential base point the unipotent group, Selmer variety and Albanese map are those of Layers 2, 4 and 5 at the tangential fibre functor, constructed by the integral tangential realization, Selmer and Albanese targets), `p ∉ S` a prime of good reduction and `T = S ∪ {p}`. Depth n means the quotient `U⟨n⟩ = U/Γ_{n+1}U` of the `ℚ_p`-unipotent étale fundamental group U of `X_{Q̄} at b` (Layer 2), which is Kim's `U_{n+1}`; `S_n = H¹_f(G_T, U⟨n⟩)` is the Selmer variety (classes crystalline at p, no condition at the other places of T), an affine `ℚ_p`-scheme of finite type (Layer 4), and `Q_n = U_dR⟨n⟩/F⁰` is the target of the depth-n de Rham Albanese map at p (Layer 5). The proposition `KimDimensionConjecture(X, p)` states: there is `n ≥ 1` with `dim S_n` &lt; `dim Q_n` (Kim 2009, Conjecture 1). By [Conditional Chabauty–Kim finiteness](#nc-4-dimension-finiteness) the inequality at one depth n gives finiteness of `𝒳(Z[1/S])`, and of `X(Q)` when X is proper. State the conjecture as a named proposition; every conditional consequence lists it as a hypothesis. A represented closed refinement `S′_n⊆S_n` can only lower the dimension. To deduce finiteness of a specified global point set from the refined inequality, require that every point in that set has its global Kummer class in `S′_n`, including every imposed bad-place condition.

X hyperbolic over Q (`2g − 2 + s > 0` where s is the number of geometric points of the boundary); `p ∉ S` of good reduction for 𝒳′ and the boundary. Dimensions are Krull dimensions of the represented affine schemes; `dim Q_n = dim U_dR⟨n⟩ − dim F⁰U_dR⟨n⟩`. Depth indexing follows Layer 2/Layer 5 (depth 1 is the abelian quotient). Use the integral tangential realization, Selmer and Albanese constructions for a tangential base point, and the integral interior versions for an S-integral point.

Take `S_n` from [Selmer functor](#nc-3-selmer-functor) and [Finite-level representability](#nc-3-finite-level-representability) with only the crystalline condition at p. Take `Q_n` and the de Rham Albanese map from [The finite-depth de Rham Albanese map](#nc-4-local-albanese). Define the proposition as the existence of a depth with the strict inequality. If b is tangential and `𝒳(Z[1/S])` is nonempty, change to an S-integral base point by `kimDimensionConjecture_basepoint` (twisting by the path torsor, BDCKW §2.9), which preserves `dim S_n` and `dim Q_n`; if `𝒳(Z[1/S])` is empty the finiteness statement is empty. Prove `finite_of_kimDimensionConjecture` from [Conditional Chabauty–Kim finiteness](#nc-4-dimension-finiteness) at that depth (with [Global points lie in the Chabauty–Kim loci](#nc-4-rational-integral-containment)).

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `KimDimensionConjecture`: The proposition `∃ n ≥ 1`, `dim S_n` &lt; `dim Q_n` for the data (X, 𝒳, b, p, S).
- `finite_of_kimDimensionConjecture`: `KimDimensionConjecture(X, p)` implies that `𝒳(Z[1/S])` is finite, and that `X(Q)` is finite if X is proper.
- `kimDimensionConjecture_of_refined`: For a represented closed refinement `S′_n⊆S_n`, `dim S′_n≤dim S_n`, so the unrefined inequality implies the refined inequality. If every allowed global point has its Kummer class in `S′_n`, the refined inequality gives finiteness of that point set by §5.7. A dimension bound for a refinement alone gives no containment and does not imply the unrefined dimension conjecture.
- `kimDimensionConjecture_basepoint`: The proposition does not depend on the integral base point b: change of base point gives isomorphic Selmer varieties (BDCKW §2.9) and the de Rham dimensions are independent of b.
- `dim_Q_eq_sum`: `dim Q_n = Σ_{k=1}^{n} (d_k − f_k)`, where `d_k = dim gr_k U` and `f_k = dim F⁰ gr_k U_dR` ([Dimensions of the lower central quotients](#nc-6-graded-central-dimensions)).
- The dimension condition is `∃ n ≥ 1, dim S_n < dim Q_n`, using the represented Selmer and de Rham schemes.
- Lowering the Selmer dimensions pointwise preserves the strict inequality (the dimension form of `kimDimensionConjecture_of_refined`).

**Checks.**

- `kimDimensionConjecture_depth_one_chabauty`: For a proper curve of genus g over Q whose Jacobian has p-adic Bloch–Kato Selmer rank r, the depth-1 inequality `dim S_1` &lt; `dim Q_1` is the classical condition r &lt; g.
- `kimDimensionConjecture_thrice_punctured_Z`: For `P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞}` over `Z (S = ∅): dim S_1 = 0 (H¹_f(G_T, ℚ_p(1)) = Z^× ⊗ ℚ_p = 0)` and `dim Q_1 = 2`, so the inequality holds `at n = 1`.
- `kimDimensionConjecture_thrice_punctured_half`: For `P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞}` over `Z[1/2]: dim S_1 = 2 = dim Q_1`, so depth 1 fails, while `dim S_2 = 2` &lt; `3 = dim Q_2 (H¹(G_T, ℚ_p(2)) = 0)`; the inequality first holds at depth 2.
- `not_kimDimensionConjecture_gm`: For the non-hyperbolic `G_m` over `Z[1/2]`, `U = ℚ_p(1)` is abelian, `U⟨n⟩ = U⟨1⟩`, and `dim S_n = 1 = dim Q_n` for every n, so the inequality never holds, matching the infinitude of `G_m(Z[1/2]) = ±2^Z`.
- `kimDimensionConjecture_needs_crystalline`: Dropping the crystalline condition at p is wrong: for `P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞}` over Z, `H¹(G_T, ℚ_p(1)) = Z[1/p]^× ⊗ ℚ_p` is one-dimensional, so the unconditioned depth-1 variety has dimension `2 = dim Q_1`.
- At depth 1 for a proper curve of genus g whose Jacobian has p-adic Selmer rank r, the inequality is r &lt; g, Chabauty's condition ([The precise classical Chabauty comparison](#nc-4-depth-one-locus)).
- For `P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞}` over Z the inequality already holds at depth 1 (0 &lt; 2).

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), Introduction, Conjecture 1 and the paragraph after it, p. 96; §3, pp. 120–121.

### 7.3 Free Lie and surface-group characters

<a id="open-curve-product-cohomology"></a>

**Étale cohomology of open curves, powers and Weil restrictions.** Let F be a field of characteristic zero, X̄ a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over F of genus g, `D⊂X̄` a reduced divisor, finite étale over F with `s=#D(F̄)≥1` geometric points, and `X=X̄∖D`. (a) There is a `G_F`-equivariant exact sequence `0→H¹(X̄_F̄,ℚ_p)→H¹(X_F̄,ℚ_p)→ℚ_p(−1)^(D(F̄))→ℚ_p(−1)→0`, where `G_F` permutes the factors of `ℚ_p(−1)^(D(F̄))` through its action on `D(F̄)` and the last map is the sum; so `H¹(X_F̄)` is an extension of the boundary part `ker(ℚ_p(−1)^(D(F̄))→ℚ_p(−1))`, of dimension s−1, by `H¹(X̄_F̄)`, and `dim H¹(X_F̄)=2g+s−1`. (b) For every `n≥1`, `H¹(X_F̄,ℚ_p)^⊗n` is a `G_F`-stable direct summand of `Hⁿ(Xⁿ_F̄,ℚ_p)`, and likewise with twists. (c) For a finite extension `F′/F`, a smooth projective geometrically connected variety V′ over F′ and `i≥1`, `Ind_(G_F′)^(G_F)Hⁱ(V′_F̄,ℚ_p)` is a `G_F`-stable direct summand of `Hⁱ((Res_(F′/F)V′)_F̄,ℚ_p)`, with T containing the places ramified in `F′/F` and the bad-reduction places, so that `G_(F′,T′)` is the finite-index subgroup of `G_(F,T)` determined by F′, and by Shapiro's lemma `Hᵐ(G_(F′,T′),Hⁱ(V′_F̄)(r))≅Hᵐ(G_(F,T),Ind Hⁱ(V′_F̄)(r))` embeds as a summand of `Hᵐ(G_(F,T),Hⁱ((Res V′)_F̄)(r))`, for T′ the places above T.

F of characteristic zero; D finite étale over F and nonempty; for (c), V′ smooth projective and geometrically connected, `i≥1`. The arithmetic cohomology consequence assumes F is a number field and T contains the primes above p, bad-reduction primes and primes ramified in `F′/F`, with T′ the places above T.

(a) Localisation (Gysin) for the closed immersion `D_F̄→X̄_F̄` with purity `H²_D(X̄,ℚ_p)=ℚ_p(−1)^(D(F̄))`, and `H²(X_F̄)=0` since `X_F̄` is affine; the map to `H²(X̄_F̄)=ℚ_p(−1)` is the sum of the Gysin classes, each of which is the point class. The dimension count agrees with the affine-curve computation. (b) Künneth gives `Hⁿ(Xⁿ)=⊕_(i₁+…+iₙ=n)⊗Hⁱʲ(X)`, whose summand with all `iⱼ=1` is `H¹^⊗n`; the projector is algebraic (built from the Künneth decomposition) and Galois-equivariant. (c) Over F̄, `Res_(F′/F)V′` becomes the product of the conjugates `V′_σ` over embeddings `σ:F′→F̄`, permuted by `G_F`; Künneth gives the summand `⊕_σ Hⁱ(V′_σ)⊗H⁰(others)=⊕_σHⁱ(V′_σ)`, which is the induced representation. Shapiro's lemma identifies the cohomology of the induced module.

**Checks.**

- For `X=P¹∖{0,1,∞}` over `ℚ`, `g=0` and `s=3`, so `H¹(X_ℚ̄)=ker(ℚ_p(−1)³→ℚ_p(−1))≅ℚ_p(−1)²` with trivial permutation action since the three points are rational.
- For `X̄=P¹` and `D={±√2}`, `s=2` and the boundary part `ker(ℚ_p(−1)²→ℚ_p(−1))` is `ℚ_p(−1)⊗ε`, with `ε` the quadratic character of `ℚ(√2)`: the permutation action is visible and is not trivial.
- For `n=2` and X a proper curve of genus g, `H²(X²)` has dimension `1+4g²+1` and the summand `H¹⊗H¹` has dimension `4g²`: the other two summands `H²⊗H⁰` and `H⁰⊗H²` are not part of `H¹^⊗2`.
- For `F′/F` quadratic and `V′=P¹`, `H⁰(Res V′)=ℚ_p` has dimension 1, whereas `Ind H⁰(V′)` has dimension 2. The induced-summand assertion requires `i≥1`; it cannot count the identical degree-zero summand once for each factor. In degree 2 the two factor classes are distinct and give the asserted 2-dimensional induced summand.

The construction and its conventions follow [The Stacks Project Authors](#reference-stacks), Lemma 59.69.3 (Tag 03RR) and Lemma 59.97.9 (Tag 0F13).

<a id="free-lie-character"></a>

**Witt character and the surface relation.** For a finite-dimensional characteristic-zero vector space H with an endomorphism `τ` and an integer `n≥1`, construct the degree-n free Lie functor `L_n(H)` and prove the Witt character formula `tr(τ|L_n(H))=(1/n)Σ_(d|n)μ(d) tr(τ^d|H)^(n/d)`. For a proper genus-g surface relation, identify the enveloping-algebra Hilbert series `1/(1−2g t+t²)`, and derive the Labute dimensions by logarithmic derivative and Möbius inversion. Identify these with the graded Lie dimensions of the geometric unipotent curve group. For complex conjugation c, the open-curve character uses the proper and boundary eigenspaces; it is not forced to be zero in odd degree.

`n≥1`; characteristic zero permits division by n. For the surface case `g≥2` and the nonzero symplectic relation has degree two.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `freeLie.wittCharacter`: Give the endomorphism trace formula.
- `surfaceLie.hilbertSeries`: Give the single-relation Hilbert series.
- `surfaceLie.labuteDimension`: Derive the graded dimension formula.
- `curveLie.complexConjugation`: Compute the character with the open boundary term.

**Checks.**

- For `m=2` free generators, dimensions at degrees 1,2,3 are 2,1,2.
- For `g=2` proper surface type, degrees 1 and 2 have dimensions 4 and 5.
- For `P¹−{0,1,∞}`, complex conjugation acts as −1 on both degree-one Tate generators, so odd-degree trace is negative dimension.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §§1 and 3, pp. 99–101 and 121–126; [John P. Labute](#reference-labute1967), Théorème 2 and its specialization, printed pp. 142–144.

Use [Lower central depth](#nc-2-central-quotients); [InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups](../InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups/README.md) §IG.3.1 (Riemann existence for punctured curves); [Étale cohomology of open curves, powers and Weil restrictions](#open-curve-product-cohomology).

### 7.4 Conditional routes to the dimension conjecture

<a id="nc-6-graded-central-dimensions"></a>

**Dimensions of the lower central quotients.** Let X be a smooth curve over a number field with smooth compactification of genus g and `s ≥ 0` boundary points over the algebraic closure, hyperbolic (`2g − 2 + s` &gt; 0), and for `n≥1` let `d_n = dim gr_n U`, where `gr_n U = Γ_nU/Γ_{n+1}U` for the `ℚ_p`-unipotent étale (or de Rham) fundamental group U of Layer 2. If `s ≥ 1`, U is the unipotent completion of a free group on `m = 2g + s − 1` generators and `Σ_{k | n} k·d_k = m^n` (Witt), so `d_n = (1/n) Σ_{k | n} μ(k) m^{n/k}`. If `s = 0` (so `g ≥ 2`), U is the completion of a surface group with one relation of degree 2 and `Σ_{k | n} k·d_k = α^n + β^n` with `α`, `β = g ± √(g² − 1)` (Labute), so `d_n = (1/n) Σ_{k | n} μ(k)(α^{n/k} + β^{n/k})`. In both cases `gr_1 U = H₁` has dimension m (resp. 2g), `gr_n U` is a `G_T`-equivariant quotient of `H₁^{⊗n}`, and `d_n ~ λ^n/n` with `λ = m` (resp. `α`); in the hyperbolic case `λ` &gt; g.

Hyperbolic smooth curve; the dimensions are those of the graded pieces of the lower central series of the `ℚ_p`-unipotent completion, equal to the ranks of the graded pieces of the discrete group. `gr_n` is taken with `Γ_1U = U`, so `gr_1 U` is the abelianisation `H₁`.

The topological fundamental group of the complex points is free on m generators `(s ≥ 1)` or the one-relator surface group `(s = 0)`; the unipotent completion has the same graded Lie algebra tensored with `ℚ_p` ([Galois structure and completion](#nc-2-etale-galois), [Lower central depth](#nc-2-central-quotients)). Free case: the graded Lie algebra is free on `H₁`, and Witt's formula ([Witt character and the surface relation](#free-lie-character)) gives `d_n`. Surface case: the graded Lie algebra is the free Lie algebra on 2g generators modulo the ideal generated by the symplectic element of degree 2; its enveloping algebra has Hilbert series `1/(1 − 2g t + t²)`, which gives the stated divisor sum (Labute). `gr_n` is spanned by iterated brackets of degree-1 elements, so it is a quotient of `H₁^{⊗n}`; the asymptotics follow from the divisor sums.

**Checks.**

`- m = 2 (P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞}): d_1`, …, `d_5 = 2`, 1, 2, 3, 6.
`- g = 2`, `s = 0: d_1 = 4`, `d_2 = 5 (= dim Λ²H₁ − 1)`, `d_3 = 16`.
`- g = 1`, `s = 0` (not hyperbolic): the formula gives `d_1 = 2` and `d_n = 0` for `n ≥ 2`, the abelian case.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §3, proof of Proposition 2, pp. 122–123; [John P. Labute](#reference-labute1967), Théorème 2, printed pp. 142–144; derive the curve specialization by the symplectic relation.

<a id="nc-6-selmer-vanishing-conjecture"></a>

**Vanishing of the strict Selmer groups of tensor powers.** Let F be a number field, `X/F` a smooth curve, p a prime and T a finite set of places of F containing the places above p, the archimedean places and the places of bad reduction of X and its boundary. Put `V_n = H¹_ét(X_{F̄}, ℚ_p)^{⊗n}(1)`, a continuous `ℚ_p`-representation of `G_T`. For a finite-dimensional continuous representation V of `G_T`, `Sel⁰_T(V)` is the kernel of `H¹(G_T, V) → ⊕_{w ∈ T} H¹(G_w, V)`, the group `Ш¹_T(V)` with rational coefficients. The proposition `SelmerVanishing(X, p, T)` states that `Sel⁰_T(V_n) = 0` for all sufficiently large n (Kim 2009, Conjecture 2). It is open in general and is stated as a named proposition.

Continuous cohomology of the profinite group `G_T` with `ℚ_p`-coefficients (limits of lattices, as in ArithmeticGaloisDuality). The local maps are restrictions to decomposition groups `G_w` for `w ∈ T`; no condition is imposed outside T beyond being unramified there.

Define `V_n` from `H¹` of the curve with the `G_T` action (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups §IG.0.T1 and AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli §A4.4 for the proper part; Layer 2 for the unipotent comparison). Define `Sel⁰_T(V)` as the kernel of localisation, `Ш¹_T(V)` of ArithmeticGaloisDuality §R02.4.2, extended to rational coefficients by ArithmeticGaloisDuality §D7.6. Define the proposition by an eventually-true statement in n.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `SelmerVanishing`: The proposition: `Sel⁰_T(V_n) = 0` for all sufficiently large n.
- `sel0_eq_sha1`: `Sel⁰_T(V)` is `Ш¹_T(V)` of ArithmeticGaloisDuality with rational coefficients.
- `sel0_dual_sha2`: Poitou–Tate: `Sel⁰_T(V)` is dual to `Ш²_T(V^∨(1))`; for `V = V_n`, `V^∨(1) = H₁^{⊗n}` with `H₁ = H¹(X_{F̄}, ℚ_p)^∨`, so SelmerVanishing is equivalent to `Ш²_T(H₁^{⊗n}) = 0` for n ≫ 0.
- `sel0_mono_T`: For `T ⊆ T′`, inflation identifies `Sel⁰_{T′}(V)` with a subspace of `Sel⁰_T(V)`.
- `selmerVanishing_of_finite_extension`: If `F′/F` is finite, SelmerVanishing over F′ implies it over F, since restriction is injective on `H¹` with `ℚ_p`-coefficients.
- `EventuallyVanishing`: The form on dimension sequences: `dim n = 0` for all large n; SelmerVanishing is the instance `dim n = dim Sel⁰_T(V_n)`.

**Checks.**

- `selmerVanishing_thrice_punctured`: For p odd and `X = P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞}` over Q, `Sel⁰_T(V_n) = 0` for every `n ≥ 2: V_n ≅ ℚ_p(1 − n)^{2^n}`, `Ш¹_T(ℚ_p(j))` is dual to `Ш²_T(ℚ_p(1 − j))`, and `H²(G_T, ℚ_p(m)) = 0` for `m ≥ 2` (Soulé).
- `sel0_eq_sha1_test`: For any V, `Sel⁰_T(V)` equals the kernel of the localisation map of ArithmeticGaloisDuality §R02.4.2 after tensoring with `ℚ_p`.
- `selmerVanishing_needs_local_conditions`: For p odd, dropping the local conditions is wrong: for `X = P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞}` over Q and every even `n ≥ 2`, `V_n ≅ ℚ_p(1 − n)^{2^n}` with 1 − n odd, so complex conjugation acts on it by −1 and Tate's global Euler characteristic formula gives `dim H¹(G_T, ℚ_p(1 − n)) ≥ 1`. The unrestricted `H¹(G_T, V_n)` is therefore nonzero for infinitely many n, while `Sel⁰_T(V_n) = 0` for every `n ≥ 2 (selmerVanishing_thrice_punctured)`.
- `selmerVanishing_zero_rep`: For `V = 0`, `Sel⁰_T(V) = 0`.
- For p odd and `P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞}` over Q, `V_n ≅ ℚ_p(1 − n)^{2^n}` and `Sel⁰_T(V_n) = 0` for `n ≥ 2`.
- For `n = 1` and a proper curve, `V_1 ≅ V_pJ` by the Weil pairing and `Sel⁰_T(V_pJ)` is the fine Selmer space of J.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §3, Conjecture 2 and the definition of `Sel⁰_T` before it, p. 121.

Use [Soulé rational Tate cohomology](#soule-rational-tate-cohomology) for the unconditional odd-p example; [ArithmeticGaloisDuality](../ArithmeticGaloisDuality/README.md) §R02.4.2 (restricted products of local cohomology); [ArithmeticGaloisDuality](../ArithmeticGaloisDuality/README.md) §D7.6 (Poitou–Tate for lattices and rational coefficients); [InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups](../InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups/README.md) §IG.0.T1 (finite-level curve–Jacobian `H¹` comparison); [AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli](../AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli/README.md) §A4.4 (étale `H¹` and the Tate module); [Galois structure and completion](#nc-2-etale-galois); `Filter.Eventually`.

<a id="nc-6-h2-growth-bound"></a>

**Kim's H² estimate.** Assume `SelmerVanishing(X, p, T)` for `X/F` as in [Vanishing of the strict Selmer groups of tensor powers](#nc-6-selmer-vanishing-conjecture), with compactification of genus g and s boundary points. Then there is an explicit polynomial P, depending only on g, s and |T|, such that `dim_{ℚ_p} H²(G_T, gr_n U) ≤ P(n)·g^n` for all sufficiently large n (with `g^n` read as 0 when `g = 0` and `n ≥ 2`, where the local invariants vanish). At a place `w ∤ p` the local contribution is at most `n·dim Gr^W_2·g^{n−1} + (n(n−1)/2)(dim Gr^W_1)²·g^{n−2}` from the weight filtration of `H¹` attached to semistable reduction, plus the boundary contribution `n·max(s−1,0)·g^{n−1}`; at w | p it is at most `n·(g+max(s−1,0))·g^{n−1}`, from the Hodge–Tate weights of `H¹`. For a proper curve `(s=0)` the boundary contribution is zero and the two Hodge–Tate multiplicities are g and g; the open formula `g+s−1` is used only when `s≥1`.

`SelmerVanishing(X, p, T)` holds; n is beyond the threshold it provides. `gr_n U` is the `G_T`-equivariant quotient of `H₁^{⊗n}` of [Dimensions of the lower central quotients](#nc-6-graded-central-dimensions), `H₁ = H¹(X_{F̄}, ℚ_p)^∨`.

`H²` is right exact on `ℚ_p`-representations of `G_T`: for finite p-primary M, `H³(G_T, M) ≅ ⊕_{v real}` `H³(G_v, M)` is killed by 2 (ArithmeticGaloisDuality §R02.4.4; `cd_p(G_T) = 2` when p is odd or F is totally imaginary), so after passing to lattices and inverting p (ArithmeticGaloisDuality §D7.6) `H³` vanishes with `ℚ_p`-coefficients for every p, including `p = 2` when F has a real place. Hence `H²(G_T, H₁^{⊗n}) ↠ H²(G_T, gr_n U)`. By SelmerVanishing and Poitou–Tate `(sel0_dual_sha2)`, `Ш²_T(H₁^{⊗n}) = 0`, so `H²(G_T, H₁^{⊗n})` injects into `⊕_{w ∈ T} H²(G_w, H₁^{⊗n})`. Local duality (ArithmeticGaloisDuality §D7.5): `dim H²(G_w, H₁^{⊗n}) = dim H⁰(G_w, H¹^{⊗n}(1))`. For `w ∤ p`: by the Gysin sequence (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§0.9–0.11, F.6) `H¹(X_{F̄})` is an extension of the boundary part `ker(ℚ_p(−1)^{D(F̄)} → ℚ_p(−1))`, which is `ℚ_p(−1)^{s−1}` after a finite extension making the boundary points rational (invariants only grow), by `H¹` of the compactification X′; the invariants of `H¹^{⊗n}(1)` are bounded by the sum of those of the induced graded pieces. On `H¹(X′)`, after a finite extension giving semistable reduction, the weight filtration `W_0 ⊂ W_1 ⊂ W_2` has `dim W_0 = dim Gr_2 ≤ g` (DWP.10). Invariants come only from weight-zero tensors: one factor of weight 2 (from `Gr_2` of `H¹(X′)` or from the boundary) and n − 1 of weight 0, or two factors of weight 1 and n − 2 of weight 0, which gives the stated count. For w | p: with the convention `HT(χ) = +1` of [De Rham exactness and Hodge–Tate grading](#linear-period-exactness), `H¹(X′_{F̄})` is de Rham with Hodge–Tate decomposition `(H¹(X′, O) ⊗ C_p) ⊕ (H⁰(X′, Ω¹) ⊗ C_p(−1))` ([Linear geometric period comparisons](#linear-geometric-period-comparisons) for the proper curve X′, [De Rham exactness and Hodge–Tate grading](#linear-period-exactness) de Rham ⇒ Hodge–Tate), and the boundary part has dimension `max(s−1,0)`; when `s≥1` it is `C_p(−1)^{s−1}`. In that open case this is Kim's decomposition `(H¹(X′, O) ⊗ C_p) ⊕ (H⁰(X′, Ω¹(log D)) ⊗ C_p(−1))`, of dimensions g and `g + s − 1`. For `s=0` use the proper decomposition with dimensions g and g. On each graded piece of `H¹^{⊗n}(1)` the invariants embed in the weight-zero part (Tate, [De Rham exactness and Hodge–Tate grading](#linear-period-exactness)), which needs exactly one factor from the `C_p(−1)` part, giving `n·(g+max(s−1,0))·g^{n−1}`.

**Checks.**

- For `P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} (g = 0)` the bound gives `H²(G_T, gr_n U) = 0` for `n ≥ 2`, consistent for odd p with Soulé's vanishing `H²(G_T, ℚ_p(n)) = 0`.
- For a proper genus-one curve `s=0`, the boundary has dimension 0 and the Hodge–Tate multiplicities are (1,1), so the p-place tensor estimate is n, not 0. At a split multiplicative place the weight-zero subspace of `H¹⊗H¹(1)` has two basis tensors and monodromy sends their sum to a nonzero multiple of the lowest-weight tensor; its kernel has dimension 1. Substituting `s−1=−1` into a boundary count would give the false bound 0.
- For `g ≥ 2` the bound grows like `n²g^n`, slower than `d_n ~ α^n/n` since `α = g + √(g² − 1)` &gt; g.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §3, Lemma 6 and proof, pp. 124–125.

<a id="nc-6-vanishing-implies-dimension"></a>

**Selmer vanishing implies the dimension conjecture.** Let X be a smooth hyperbolic curve over Q with the data of [Kim's dimension conjecture](#nc-6-kim-dimension-conjecture). If `SelmerVanishing(X, p, T)` holds, then `KimDimensionConjecture(X, p)` holds; hence `𝒳(Z[1/S])` is finite (and `X(Q)` if X is proper). Choose P with nonnegative integer coefficients and `k₀≥1` such that `dim H²(G_T,gr_k U)≤P(k)g^k` for every `k≥k₀`, and put `C=Σ_{1≤k<k₀} dim H²(G_T,gr_k U)`. For every `n≥1`, `dim S_n ≤ Σ_{1≤k≤n} dim H¹(G_T,gr_k U) ≤ Σ_{1≤k≤n} d_k⁻ + C + Σ_{k₀≤k≤n} P(k)g^k`, while `dim Q_n ≥ Σ_{1≤k≤n}(d_k−g^k)`. The latter lower bound exceeds the former upper bound for arbitrarily large n of suitable parity. Here `d_k⁻` is the dimension of the (−1)-eigenspace of complex conjugation on `gr_k U`. It satisfies `d_k⁻ = (d_k − τ_k)/2` with `τ_k` the trace of complex conjugation, computed from its trace t on `H₁`. In the proper case `τ_k = 0` for odd k (`gr_k U` is pure of odd weight −k). In the affine case `τ_k = (1/k) Σ_{e | k} μ(e) t_e^{k/e}` with `t_e = t` for odd e and `t_e = m` for even e; either |t| &lt; m, and then `|τ_k| = o(d_k)`, or `t = −m` (genus 0 with all boundary points real), and then complex conjugation acts on `gr_k U` by `(−1)^k`. In every case `Σ_{k ≤ n} d_k⁺ ≥ c·λ^n/n` for infinitely many n, with `λ` &gt; g.

`SelmerVanishing(X, p, T)`; X hyperbolic over Q; `T = S ∪ {p}` with p of good reduction. For each graded piece use `(d_k−tr(c))/2` for the negative complex-conjugation eigenspace; the proper pure-weight specialization and the open boundary contribution are distinct.

The central extensions `1 → gr_{n}U → U⟨n⟩ → U⟨n−1⟩ → 1` make `H¹(G_T, U⟨n⟩)` fibred over a subvariety of `H¹(G_T, U⟨n−1⟩)` with fibres torsors under `H¹(G_T, gr_n U)` ([Central extensions: the action of `H¹(G, Z)` and the connecting map to `H²`](#nc-3-central-extension), [Finite-level representability](#nc-3-finite-level-representability)), so `dim S_n ≤ Σ_{k ≤ n} dim H¹(G_T, gr_k U)`. `H⁰(G_T, gr_k U) = 0` for `k ≥ 1` (weights of `H₁` are −1 and −2), so Tate's global Euler characteristic formula over Q (ArithmeticGaloisDuality §R02.4.4, with rational coefficients) gives `dim H¹ − dim H² = d_k⁻`. Keep the initial H² contribution C and apply [Kim's `H²` estimate](#nc-6-h2-growth-bound) only for `k≥k₀`. Bound `dim F⁰ gr_k U_dR` by `g^k` (`F⁰` of `H₁^{dR ⊗k}` has dimension `dim H¹(O)^{⊗k} = g^k`), so `dim Q_n ≥ Σ_{k ≤ n} (d_k − g^k)`. Trace of complex conjugation c: in the affine case `gr_• U` is the free Lie algebra on `H₁` with c acting through `H₁`, so `τ_k` is given by the graded character formula of free Lie algebras applied to the involution c ([Witt character and the surface relation](#free-lie-character)). On `H₁`, c has trace 0 on the compact part (it is antisymplectic) and trace 1 − r on the boundary part of the Gysin sequence (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§0.9–0.11, F.6), r being the number of real boundary points; hence `t = 1 − r`, and `t = −m` exactly when `g = 0` and every boundary point is real. In the proper case `τ_k = 0` for odd k because `gr_k U` is pure of odd weight −k. Compare: `dim Q_n−dim S_n ≥ Σ_{1≤k≤n} d_k⁺ − C − Σ_{k₀≤k≤n} P(k)g^k − Σ_{1≤k≤n} g^k`, and by [Dimensions of the lower central quotients](#nc-6-graded-central-dimensions) and the trace computation `Σ_{k ≤ n} d_k⁺ ≥ c·λ^n/n` for infinitely many n with `λ` &gt; g; choose such n. Finiteness then follows from `finite_of_kimDimensionConjecture`.

For natural-valued dimension sequences h₁, h₂ and d⁻ with `h₁(k)=d⁻(k)+h₂(k)` for `k≥1`, a threshold `k₀≥1` and bounds `h₂(k)≤e(k)` for `k≥k₀` give `Σ_{1≤k≤n} h₁(k) ≤ Σ_{1≤k≤n} d⁻(k) + Σ_{1≤k<k₀} h₂(k) + Σ_{k₀≤k≤n} e(k)` for every n. Apply this with `e(k)=P(k)g^k`; the finite initial sum remains present when `g=0`.

**Checks.**

- For a proper curve of genus 2, `λ = 2 + √3 ≈ 3.73` &gt; `2 = g`, and the counting step succeeds once `Σ_{1≤k≤n, k odd} d_k/2 > C + Σ_{k₀≤k≤n} P(k)2^k + Σ_{1≤k≤n} 2^k`.
- For `P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞}` complex conjugation acts on `gr_k U ≅ ℚ_p(k)^{d_k}` by `(−1)^k`, so `d_k⁺ = d_k` for even k and 0 for odd k; the count succeeds once the even-degree sum exceeds C.
- For `X=ℙ¹∖{0,1,∞}`, `S={2}`, `b=2`, `p=3` and `T={2,3}`, `gr₁U=ℚ₃(1)²`. The S-unit Kummer identification gives `dim H¹(G_T,gr₁U)=4`, while `d₁⁻=2`. Soulé's calculation gives `H²(G_T,gr_k U)=0` for `k≥2`, so one may take `k₀=2` and `C=2`. Consequently `Σ_{1≤k≤n} dim H¹(G_T,gr_k U)=Σ_{1≤k≤n} d_k⁻+2` for every `n≥1`; the zero genus error term cannot replace C.
- With `k₀=1` the initial sum is empty and C is zero; the summation interface then gives the all-degree bound. For `n<k₀` its tail sum is empty and the full initial sum still bounds the partial H² sum.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §3, Proposition 2 and proof, pp. 122–124.

<a id="nc-6-bloch-kato-implies-vanishing"></a>

**Bloch–Kato implies Selmer vanishing.** Let `X/F` be a smooth curve over a number field and p, T as in [Vanishing of the strict Selmer groups of tensor powers](#nc-6-selmer-vanishing-conjecture). Suppose that, for every `n ≥ 2`, the group `H¹_g(G_F, H^n(X^n_{F̄}, ℚ_p(1)))` of classes unramified at almost all places and de Rham (potentially semistable) at the places above p is spanned by the image of K-theory under the étale Chern class map, as predicted by the Bloch–Kato conjecture (their Conjecture 5.3, as cited by Kim). Since the relevant K-group `K^{(1)}_{1−n}(X^n)` is zero for `n ≥ 2`, this hypothesis says that `H¹_g(G_F, H^n(X^n_{F̄}, ℚ_p(1))) = 0` for `n ≥ 2`. Then `SelmerVanishing(X, p, T)` holds; in fact `Sel⁰_T(V_n) = 0` for every `n ≥ 2`.

The Bloch–Kato fragment for the motives `h^n(X^n)(1)`, `n ≥ 2`, is a hypothesis; it is not a theorem of any roadmap. For open X the smooth variety `X^n` is not proper and the hypothesis is the corresponding statement for its cohomology.

By Künneth, `V_n = H¹(X_{F̄}, ℚ_p)^{⊗n}(1)` is a `G_F`-stable direct summand of `H^n(X^n_{F̄}, ℚ_p(1))`. A class in `Sel⁰_T(V_n)` is unramified outside T and locally trivial at T, so it lies in `H¹_g(G_F, V_n) ⊆ H¹_g(G_F, H^n(X^n_{F̄}, ℚ_p(1)))` (the Bloch–Kato subgroups `H¹_f ⊆ H¹_g`). The weight-graded piece `K^{(1)}_{2r−n−1}` with `r = 1` is a negative K-group of the regular scheme `X^n` for `n ≥ 2`, hence zero, so the hypothesis gives `H¹_g = 0` and therefore `Sel⁰_T(V_n) = 0`.

**Checks.**

- For zero coefficient representation, both strict Selmer and `H¹_g` are zero, and the summand inclusion is the zero map.
- For p odd and `P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞}` over Q the conclusion holds unconditionally `(selmerVanishing_thrice_punctured)`, consistent with Soulé's theorem.
- The hypothesis is used only through the vanishing of `H¹_g`; no regulator computation enters.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §3, Observation 1 and the paragraph before it, pp. 121–122.

<a id="nc-6-weight-splitting-implies-vanishing"></a>

**Weight filtrations on extensions imply Selmer vanishing.** Let `X/F` and `V_n` be as in [Vanishing of the strict Selmer groups of tensor powers](#nc-6-selmer-vanishing-conjecture) and `n ≥ 3`. Suppose every extension `0 → V_n → E → ℚ_p → 0` of `G_T`-representations whose class lies in `Sel⁰_T(V_n)` carries a finite increasing filtration W by `G_T`-subrepresentations, strictly compatible with the maps of the extension, inducing on `ℚ_p` the filtration pure of weight 0 and on `V_n` a filtration with `W_0V_n = 0`. Then `Sel⁰_T(V_n) = 0`. The hypothesis is what Kim (following Scholl) derives from the Fontaine–Mazur conjecture together with the expectation that such extensions are `ℚ_p`-linear combinations of extensions of geometric origin; it is a stated hypothesis here. For proper X, `V_n` is pure of weight n − 2 and `W_0V_n = 0` for `n ≥ 3`; for open X the weights of `V_n` lie in [n − 2, 2n − 2] and the same conclusion holds.

The weight-filtration hypothesis on each extension class in `Sel⁰_T(V_n)`; `n ≥ 3`. Weights of `V_n` come from the weights 1 (compact part) and 2 (boundary part) of `H¹ at` good places.

Strictness gives `v ∈ W_0E` mapping to `1 ∈ ℚ_p`. `W_0E ∩ V_n = W_0V_n = 0` since all weights of `V_n` are at least `n − 2 ≥ 1: at` good places `H¹` of the compactification is pure of weight 1 (WEC R34.2) and the boundary part of the Gysin sequence (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§0.9–0.11, F.6) has weight 2. Hence `W_0E` is a one-dimensional `G_T`-stable complement of `V_n`, the extension splits and its class is zero.

**Checks.**

- For `n = 2` and proper X, `V_2` has weight 0 and the argument does not apply.
- For `P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞}`, `V_n = ℚ_p(1 − n)^{2^n}` has weight `2n − 2 ≥ 4` for `n ≥ 3`.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §3, Observation 2 and the argument after it, p. 122.

<a id="nc-6-weak-jannsen-implies-dimension"></a>

**Weak Jannsen vanishing implies the dimension conjecture for affine curves.** Let X be a smooth affine hyperbolic curve over `Q (s ≥ 1)` with compactification X′ of genus g and the data of [Kim's dimension conjecture](#nc-6-kim-dimension-conjecture). Assume the weak Jannsen conjecture: there is k &gt; 0 such that `H²(G_T, H^i(V_{Q̄}, ℚ_p)(r)) = 0` for every smooth projective `V/Q` with good reduction outside T, every i and every `r ≥ i + k`. Then `KimDimensionConjecture(X, p)` holds, so `𝒳(Z[1/S])` is finite.

X affine `(s ≥ 1)`; the weak Jannsen vanishing is a hypothesis for all smooth projective `V/Q` with good reduction outside T. Kim records that the argument was not adapted to the compact case.

Pass to the finite extension F′ over which all boundary points are rational; `F′/Q` is unramified outside T, and corestriction makes the `H²` estimate over F′ suffice. The hypothesis over Q gives the required vanishing over F′. For `i≥1` and geometrically connected smooth projective `V′/F′`, use the [induced-summand theorem](#open-curve-product-cohomology) for `Res_(F′/ℚ)V′` and Shapiro, with good reduction outside T. For `i=0`, apply the weak Jannsen hypothesis directly to the finite étale `ℚ`-scheme `Spec F′`, whose geometric `H⁰` is `Ind_(G_F′)^(G_ℚ)ℚ_p`. Thus `H²(G_(F′,T′),ℚ_p(r))=0` for `r≥k`, with T′ above T. The powers of the compactification used below are geometrically connected, so these cases suffice. Use the dual Gysin sequence `0 → ℚ_p(1)^{s−1} → H₁(X) → H₁(X′) → 0` (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§0.9–0.11, F.6) and, in the Grothendieck group, expand `H₁(X)^{⊗n}` into tensor products of `V = H₁(X′) ≅ H¹(X′)(1)` and `ℚ_p(1)`. `V^{⊗l}` is a direct summand of `H^l(X′^l_{Q̄})(l)` (Künneth), so `H²(G_T, V^{⊗l}(r)) = 0` for `r ≥ k` by the hypothesis. For `g ≥ 1`: the Weil pairing embeds `ℚ_p(1)` in `V^{⊗2}` as a direct summand; writing `V^{⊗2k} = M ⊕ ℚ_p(k)` and iterating, `dim H²(G_T, V^{⊗n}(l)) ≤ C·a^n` with a `= ((2g)^{2k} − 1)^{1/(2k)}` &lt; `2g ≤ m`. For `g = 0`, `V = 0` and `H₁(X)^{⊗n} = ℚ_p(n)^{(s−1)^n}`, and `H²(G_T, ℚ_p(n)) = 0` for `n ≥ k` is the hypothesis for `V = Spec Q (i = 0)`, so the bound holds with 0 for `n ≥ k`. Combine with the Euler characteristic and the graded dimensions `d_n ~ m^n/n` as in [Selmer vanishing implies the dimension conjecture](#nc-6-vanishing-implies-dimension).

**Checks.**

- For a quadratic `F′/ℚ` and `V′=ℙ¹`, `H⁰(Res V′)` has dimension one but `Ind H⁰(V′)` has dimension two; `Spec F′` has the required two-dimensional geometric `H⁰`.
- For `g = 0` every tensor power of `H₁` is a sum of Tate twists and the hypothesis reduces to Tate-cohomology vanishing, supplied for odd p by Soulé's vanishing of `H²(G_T, ℚ_p(r))` for `r ≥ 2`.
- The bound `C·a^n` with a &lt; m is the only input from the hypothesis.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §3, statement of the weak Jannsen conjecture, Observation 3 and its proof, pp. 125–126.

<a id="nc-6-cm-rank-one-finiteness"></a>

**Integral points on punctured CM elliptic curves of rank one.** Let `E/ℚ` have complex multiplication, let `𝒳` be the regular minimal model of `X=E−{O}` with the zero section removed, and choose `b∈𝒳(ℤ)`. Let p be an odd good-reduction prime, S the bad primes and `T=S∪{p}`. Assume `dim H¹_f(G_ℚ,V_pE)=1`; rank one together with finiteness of `Ш(E)[p^∞]` suffices. For `v∈S` put `C_v=Im(j_v:𝒳(ℤ_v)→H¹(G_v,U⟨2⟩))`, with its finite reduced scheme structure. Define `Sel_T(U⟨2⟩)` by the crystalline condition at p, these bad-place Kummer conditions and the neutral conditions at good places away from p. Prove that every global integral Kummer class belongs to this Selmer scheme and that `dim Sel_T(U⟨2⟩)≤1<2=dim U_dR⟨2⟩/F⁰`. Consequently `𝒳(ℤ)` is finite. If there is no integral base point, the global point set is empty.

Use [Finite away-place Kummer images](#finite-away-kummer-image) for the specified integral domains. The finitely many tuples `η=(η_v)∈∏_(v∈S) C_v` give closed pieces by imposing `loc_v=η_v`; their union is the stringent Selmer scheme. Potential good reduction of E does not identify these conditions with the neutral potentially-unramified condition on the punctured curve.

Here `1→ℚ_p(1)→U⟨2⟩→V_pE→1`. At every `v≠p`, `H⁰(G_v,V_pE)=H¹(G_v,V_pE)=0`, so local central differences have unique coordinates in `H¹(G_v,ℚ_p(1))`. For a fixed tuple η, any two lifts of the same geometric depth-one class differ by a global central class whose localization is zero at every away place and is finite at p. Prove this on all coefficient algebras over each geometric residue field, using the crystalline invariant lifting and freeness hypotheses of [Central Selmer dimension bound](#nc-3-central-selmer-dimension). The difference group is `H¹_f(G_ℚ,ℚ_p(1))=ℤ^×⊗ℚ_p=0`, so each nonempty geometric fibre is zero-dimensional; η need not be zero. The depth-one image lies in `H¹_f(G_ℚ,V_pE)`, of dimension one by hypothesis. Finite union over η gives the bound. On the de Rham side `gr₂U=Λ²V_pE≅ℚ_p(1)` and `F⁰(gr₂U_dR)=0`, so the quotient dimension is `3−1=2`. The localization square puts every integral point into the finite union; apply §5.7 to that containing refinement.

**Checks.**

- For `E:y²=x³−25x`, `b=(−4,6)`, `x=(0,0)` and `p=13`, both points are integral. At 5 the type is `I₀*`; Bianchi's normalization gives `λ₅(b)=0`, `λ₅(x)=−log₁₃(5)≠0`. The ordinary-basepoint path coordinate is their difference divided by two in BDCKW's normalization, so the nonneutral member of `C₅` is required.
- That path never becomes unramified: after every finite extension at 5, `H¹_unr(−,ℚ₁₃(1))=0` because Frobenius minus one is invertible, and rational restriction is injective. Over `ℚ₅(√5)`, `x=5X`, `y=5√5Y` gives `Y²=X³−X`; b reduces to O and x does not. The original integral endpoints need not stay integral in the good punctured pair.
- With a fixed tuple η the difference of two lifts has zero away coordinates even when η is nonzero. Imposing the neutral tuple alone can discard integral points.
- The depth is 2 in this roadmap's indexing, Kim's `U_3`. Its central linear Selmer group is zero; its depth-one Selmer dimension is an explicit hypothesis, not rank alone.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §4, pp. 127–129, for the central dimension calculation; [Jennifer S. <a id="nc-6-pseudo-null-implies-dimension"></a>

**Pseudo-nullity implies the dimension conjecture for punctured CM curves.** Let `E/Q` have complex multiplication by an order in the imaginary quadratic field K, with ring of integers `O_K`, `X = E ∖ {O}`, p an odd prime of good reduction, `F_1 = Q(E[p])`, `F_∞ = Q(E[p^∞])`, `G_∞ = Gal(F_∞/F_1)`, `Λ = ℤ_p[[G_∞]]`, and I the Galois group of the maximal abelian unramified pro-p extension of `F_∞` in which the primes above T split completely. Assume that the CM action is defined over `F_1` and fix a compatible rank-one identification `T_pE≅O_K⊗ℤ_p`. Assume its Tate image is open in `(O_K⊗ℤ_p)ˣ` and its congruence image `G_∞` is torsion-free of rank two and contains every scalar in `1+p^rℤ_p` for some `r≥1`. Also assume a topological `ℤ_p`-algebra identification `Λ≅ℤ_p[[T_1,T_2]]` from a chosen `ℤ_p`-basis of `G_∞`, with Λ a Noetherian regular local domain of dimension three. Assume the Coates–Sujatha conjecture that I, a finitely generated Λ-module, is pseudo-null. Then KimDimensionConjecture holds for X (working over `F_1`, which suffices because corestriction is surjective on `H²`), and hence 𝒳(Z) is finite.

The CM open image, scalar homotheties, rank-two congruence image and two-variable ring identification with its regular-local properties are explicit hypotheses, as is pseudo-nullity of I. Use the general Noetherian integrally closed domain definition of pseudo-nullity in PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras §4.1; its one-variable coordinate theorem does not supply this Λ identification. The `H²` estimate is reduced to `F_1`; local terms are bounded as in [Kim's `H²` estimate](#nc-6-h2-growth-bound) with `g = 1`.

It suffices to bound `dim H²(G_T, H₁^{⊗n})` by a polynomial in n; the local contributions are bounded as in [Kim's `H²` estimate](#nc-6-h2-growth-bound), so it suffices to bound `Ш²_T(H₁^{⊗n})`. By Poitou–Tate this is dual to `Sel⁰_T(H¹^{⊗n}(1))`. The Hochschild–Serre sequence for `F_∞/F_1` in continuous cohomology of the inverse system `H¹(Ē, Z/p^i)^{⊗n}(1)` (ArithmeticGaloisDuality D7, continuous inverse-system Hochschild–Serre) identifies it, after inverting p, with `Hom_Λ(I, H¹^{⊗n}(1))`: the terms `H^j(G_∞, H¹^{⊗n}(1)) ⊗ Q` vanish for `j = 1`, 2 and `n ≠ 2`, because the scalar-image hypothesis puts the homothety `u=1+p^r` of `T_pE` in `G_∞`; it is central and acts on `H¹^{⊗n}(1)` by `u^{2−n}≠1` for `n≠2`. Pseudo-nullity makes `I ⊗ ℚ_p` finite-dimensional: the `ℤ_p`-torsion of I maps to zero in every `ℚ_p`-vector space, and `I′ = I/I[p^∞]` is pseudo-null with p a nonzerodivisor, so dim I′/pI′ `≤ 0`, I′/pI′ is finite, and I′ is finitely generated over `ℤ_p` by Nakayama's lemma for compact modules. A p-torsion pseudo-null module such as `Λ/(p,T₁)` need not be finitely generated over `ℤ_p`; only the rational finite-dimensional conclusion is used here. A Frobenius element of `G_∞` therefore has finitely many eigenvalues on `I ⊗ ℚ_p`, and by weights `Hom_Λ(I, H¹^{⊗n}(1)) = 0` for n ≫ 0. Conclude as in [Selmer vanishing implies the dimension conjecture](#nc-6-vanishing-implies-dimension) with the polynomial bound.

**Checks.**

- The hypothesis is about `F_∞ = Q(E[p^∞])`, a two-dimensional p-adic Lie extension of `F_1` in the CM case.
- A one-variable coordinate `ℤ_p[[T]]` has dimension two and cannot supply this dimension-three ring. The module `Λ/(p,T₁)` is pseudo-null but has infinite dimension over `𝔽_p`; its rationalization is zero, so only rational finite-dimensionality is concluded.
- With `g = 1` the local bound is polynomial in n, and `d_n ~ 2^n/n` for `m = 2`.

The construction and its conventions follow [Minhyong Kim](#reference-kim2009), §4, Observation 4 and its proof, pp. 130–131.

### 7.5 The thrice-punctured line

<a id="nc-6-genus-zero-dimension"></a>

**The dimension conjecture for the thrice-punctured line.** Let `X = P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞}` over `Z[1/S]` with S a finite set of primes, `b ∈ 𝒳(Z[1/S])` an S-integral base point (if `𝒳(Z[1/S])` is empty there is nothing to prove), and `p ∉ S` an odd prime. Then `KimDimensionConjecture(X, p)` holds, hence `X(Z[1/S])` is finite (Siegel's theorem for this curve). Explicitly `gr_n U ≅ ℚ_p(n)^{r_n}` with `r_n` the Witt numbers for `m = 2`, `F⁰ = 0` on `U_dR` so `dim Q_n = Σ_{k ≤ n} r_k`, and `dim S_n ≤ |S|·2 + Σ_{3 ≤ k ≤ n, k odd}` `r_k`, which is smaller for n large.

`thricePuncturedLine_sIntegralPoints_finite` in `Suggested.lean` states the S-integral finiteness conclusion using Mathlib’s ring `(S : Set (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum ℤ)).integer ℚ`: its elements x with `IsUnit x ∧ IsUnit (1 - x)` form a finite set. These are exactly the integral points avoiding 0, 1 and ∞. The conclusion holds for every finite S without a chosen base point or auxiliary prime. The Selmer dimension inequality remains the geometric target above.

S finite, `p ∉ S` odd (the rational Tate cohomology comparison below assumes odd p); `T = S ∪ {p}`; the base point is S-integral, as in Kim 2005 p.17. Uses Soulé's computation of `H¹(G_T, ℚ_p(k))`: zero for even `k ≥ 2` and one-dimensional for odd `k ≥ 3`. Kim 2005 also takes p large compared with the depth for its comparison maps; here the comparison is that of Layer 5, for every prime of good reduction.

`H₁ = ℚ_p(1)²` and `gr_n U` is a quotient of `H₁^{⊗n}`, so `gr_n U ≅ ℚ_p(n)^{r_n}` with `r_n` from [Dimensions of the lower central quotients](#nc-6-graded-central-dimensions). `H¹_f(G_T, ℚ_p(1)) = Z[1/S]^× ⊗ ℚ_p` has dimension |S| (SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0, S-unit Kummer identification); `H¹(G_T, ℚ_p(k)) = 0` for even `k ≥ 2` and has dimension one for odd `k ≥ 3` (the [rational Tate cohomology comparison](#soule-rational-tate-cohomology)). The [Central extensions: the action of `H¹(G, Z)` and the connecting map to `H²`](#nc-3-central-extension) fibration gives `dim S_n ≤ 2|S| + Σ_{odd 3 ≤ k ≤ n} r_k` ([Central extensions: the action of `H¹(G, Z)` and the connecting map to `H²`](#nc-3-central-extension)). Since the Hodge filtration of `H¹_dR` is `F¹ =` everything, `F⁰U_dR` is trivial and `dim Q_n = Σ_{k ≤ n} r_k`; the even-degree terms make the difference positive for large n. Finiteness follows from [Conditional Chabauty–Kim finiteness](#nc-4-dimension-finiteness).

**Checks.**

`- S = ∅: 𝒳(Z)` is empty, and the depth-one dimensions, which need no base point, are `dim H¹_f(G_T, ℚ_p(1)²) = 0` &lt; `2 = dim Q_1`.
`- S = {2}`: depth 1 gives `2 = 2`, depth 2 gives 2 &lt; 3, in agreement with BDCKW §8.2.
