### 7.6 Kim's conjecture on eventual equality

<a id="nc-6-kim-conjecture"></a>

**Kim's conjecture on eventual equality.** Let `𝒳 → Spec Z` be a regular minimal model of a hyperbolic curve over Q in one of the three cases of BDCKW §2.1 (`P¹` minus a reduced horizontal divisor with at least three geometric points; the regular minimal model of a smooth proper curve of genus `≥ 2`; or the complement of a nonempty reduced horizontal divisor in the regular minimal model of a smooth proper curve of genus `≥ 1`), b an integral point or integral tangent vector, p an odd prime of good reduction and T a finite set of primes containing p and the bad primes. Let `U⟨n⟩` be the depth-n quotient of the `ℚ_p`-unipotent étale fundamental group (BDCKW's `U_n`), `j_v: 𝒳(Z_v) → H¹(G_v, U⟨n⟩)` the local unipotent Kummer maps, and put `C_v={1}` at every good place `v≠p`, `C_v=Im j_v` at a bad place. Define `Sel_n(𝒳) = ⋂_{v ≠ p} loc_v⁻¹(C_v) ⊆ H¹_f(G_T, U⟨n⟩)`, with scheme structure given by the sum of the ideals of these finite reduced conditions. At a good place only `Im j_v⊆{1}` holds without a nonempty local domain; equality requires `𝒳(ℤ_v)≠∅`. Put `X(ℤ_p)_n = j_p⁻¹(loc_p(Sel_n(𝒳))) ⊆ 𝒳(ℤ_p)`. These sets decrease with n, contain 𝒳(Z), and do not depend on T or b. The proposition `KimConjecture(𝒳, p)` states that `X(ℤ_p)_n = 𝒳(Z)` for all sufficiently large n (BDCKW Conjecture 3.1). For a finite set S of primes with `p ∉ S`, form global classes over `G_(T∪S)` and drop the conditions `at v ∈ S` to obtain `Sel_{n,S}(𝒳)`, `X(ℤ_p)_{S,n} ⊇ 𝒳(Z[1/S])`, and the S-integral proposition `KimConjecture_S(𝒳, p): X(ℤ_p)_{S,n} = 𝒳(Z[1/S])` for n large (BDCKW §8.1). Both are open and are stated as named propositions; BDCKW do not formulate a version over other number fields (§3.2), and none is stated here.

𝒳 a regular minimal Z-model as in BDCKW §2.1; p odd of good reduction for 𝒳 and b. In Layer 5 terms, `X(ℤ_p)_n` is the crystalline locus `crystallineLocus_n` for the conditions `C_v={1}` at good `v≠p`, `C_v=Im j_v` at bad v, and the crystalline condition at p. These conditions specify the good-place convention used in the punctured-line computations. Taking every literal local image defines a stronger variant, empty whenever an away local integral domain is empty. Depth indexing: `U⟨n⟩ = U/Γ_{n+1}U`, so `n = 1` is the abelian depth. When b is an integral tangent vector (as for `P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞}` over Z, which has no integral point), the Selmer scheme, the local Kummer maps and the loci use Layers 2, 4 and 5 at the tangential fibre functor: the integral tangential realization, Selmer and Albanese constructions.

Represent `H¹_f(G_T, U⟨n⟩)` and the localisation maps ([Selmer functor](#nc-3-selmer-functor), [Selmer representability](#nc-3-selmer-representability)). Finiteness of `Im j_v` at bad `v≠p` (Kim–Tamagawa, as cited by BDCKW 2.5) and the imposed neutral condition at every good `v≠p` make `Sel_n(𝒳)` a closed subscheme; define `X(ℤ_p)_n` through the local Kummer map `j_p` ([The exact, period-image and closed-image loci](#nc-4-kim-loci)). Monotonicity in n and containment of 𝒳(Z) follow from [Depth projection and change of conditions for the loci](#nc-4-locus-compatibilities) and [Global points lie in the Chabauty–Kim loci](#nc-4-rational-integral-containment). For independence of T, each added good place has the imposed condition `{1}`, even when its local integral domain is empty. The action there is unramified; neutral localization kills inertia, so BDCKW §2.8's inflation lemma descends the class from `G_T′` to `G_T`. Conversely good-place unramified H¹ is neutral by the Frobenius weight argument in Kim–Tamagawa, §2, proof of Corollary 0.3, pp. 6–7, so inflation preserves the conditions. For b use BDCKW §2.9, twisting by the integral path torsor `P(b,c)`; it is unramified at good places and preserves the neutral condition. Define the propositions as eventual equality.

The interface consists of the following named results.

- `kimLocus`: `X(ℤ_p)_n = j_p⁻¹(loc_p(Sel_n(𝒳))) ⊆ 𝒳(ℤ_p)`.
- `kimLocus_antitone`: `X(ℤ_p)_{n+1} ⊆ X(ℤ_p)_n` for every `n ≥ 1`.
- `integral_subset_kimLocus`: `𝒳(Z) ⊆ X(ℤ_p)_n` for every n.
- `kimConjecture_iff_exists_subset`: `KimConjecture(𝒳, p)` holds if and only if `X(ℤ_p)_n ⊆ 𝒳(Z)` for some n, by the two previous items.
- `kimLocus_eq_crystallineLocus`: `X(ℤ_p)_n` equals Layer `5's crystallineLocus_n` for the displayed good-place neutral and bad-place image conditions.
- `kimLocus_indep_T`: For `T ⊆ T′` both containing p and the bad primes, the Selmer schemes for T and T′ are isomorphic compatibly with `loc_p`, so `X(ℤ_p)_n` does not depend on T.
- `kimLocus_indep_basepoint`: Twisting by the path torsor `P(b, c)` identifies the Selmer schemes for integral base points b and c compatibly with `loc_p` and the Kummer maps, so `X(ℤ_p)_n` does not depend on b.
- `kimConjectureS`: The S-integral proposition: `X(ℤ_p)_{S,n} = 𝒳(Z[1/S])` for n large, with `KimConjectureS ∅ = KimConjecture`.
- Eventual equality means `X(ℤ_p)_n = 𝒳(Z)` for all sufficiently large n.
- For an antitone family L with `G ⊆ L n` for all n, eventual equality holds if and only if `L n ⊆ G` for some n.
- `eventualEquality_iInter`: For an antitone family, eventual equality with G implies `⋂_n L n = G`; the converse fails `(kimConjecture_not_intersection)`.

**Checks.**

- For `𝒳=Spec ℤ[z,1/z,1/(1−z)]`, `𝒳(ℤ₂)=∅` because modulo 2 one of z and 1−z is zero. Hence `Im j₂=∅`, whereas the imposed good-place condition is `{1}`. The literal-image variant is empty at every depth, including p=7; it cannot have the two primitive sixth roots as its depth-one locus.
- `kimConjecture_thrice_punctured_p5`: For `𝒳 = P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞}` over Z with the tangential base point at 0 and `p = 5`, `X(Z_5)_1 = ∅ = 𝒳(Z)`, so the conjecture holds from depth 1 (BDCKW §6.1).
- `kimLocus_thrice_punctured_p7`: For the same 𝒳 and `p = 7`, `X(Z_7)_1 = {ζ_6, ζ_6⁵} ≠ 𝒳(Z) = ∅`: equality is eventual, not at depth 1 (BDCKW §6.2).
- `kimConjecture_not_intersection`: Eventual equality is stronger than `⋂_n X(ℤ_p)_n = 𝒳(Z)`: for the decreasing family `L_n = G ∪ {m ∈ ℕ : m ≥ n}` with G finite, the intersection is G but no `L_n` equals G, so a definition by the intersection would accept it.
- `kimConjectureS_empty`: For `S = ∅` the S-integral Selmer scheme is `Sel_n(𝒳)` and KimConjectureS reduces to KimConjecture.
- `kimLocusS_half_contains`: For `P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞}` over `Z[1/2]` and an odd prime p, the three points 2, −1 and `1/2` lie in `X(ℤ_p)_{{2},2}`, the zero set of `2Li_2(z) + log(z)log(1 − z)` (BDCKW §8.2).
- For `P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞}` over Z and `p = 5`, `X(Z_5)_1 = ∅ = 𝒳(Z)` ([Kim's conjecture at depth one for the thrice-punctured line](#nc-6-thrice-punctured-depth-one)).
- For `P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞}` over Z and `p = 7`, `X(Z_7)_1` consists of the two primitive sixth roots of unity, so equality fails at depth 1.

The good-place convention replaces the unconditional equality `Im j_v={1}` in BDCKW Remark 2.6 by inclusion, with equality for nonempty domains; Definition 2.7 is interpreted using the conditions `C_v` displayed here. <a id="nc-6-thrice-punctured-depth-one"></a>

**Kim's conjecture at depth one for the thrice-punctured line.** Let `𝒳 = P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞}` over Z with the tangential base point at 0. Then `𝒳(Z) = ∅`. At depth 1, `U⟨1⟩ = ℚ_p(1)²`, `Sel_1(𝒳) = 0` and `j_p(z) = (log z, log(1 − z))`, so `X(ℤ_p)_1` is the set of `z ∈ ℤ_p` with z and 1 − z both roots of unity, which is the set of primitive sixth roots of unity lying in `ℤ_p`. Hence for `p = 3` or p ≡ 2 mod 3, `X(ℤ_p)_1 = ∅` and `KimConjecture(𝒳, p)` holds from depth 1. For p ≡ 1 mod 3, `X(ℤ_p)_1 = {ζ_6, ζ_6⁵}`; `Sel_2(𝒳) = 0` by Soulé's vanishing `H¹(G_T, ℚ_p(2)) = 0`, and `X(ℤ_p)_2 = ∅` if and only if the p-adic dilogarithm `Li_2(ζ_6)` is nonzero. For a specified prime p ≡ 1 mod 3, the conclusion `X(ℤ_p)_2 = ∅` carries `Li_2(ζ_6) ≠ 0` as an explicit hypothesis.

p odd; `𝒳(Z) = ∅` because z and 1 − z cannot both be units of Z. The depth-two statement for p ≡ 1 mod 3 is an equivalence with a nonvanishing condition, not an unconditional equality. The tangential base point at 0 is the integral unit tangent, with the crystalline and global conditions of Layers 2, 4 and 5.

𝒳(Z) is empty: the only units are ±1, and `1 − 1 = 0`, `1 − (−1) = 2`. `Sel_1(𝒳) = 0`: it is `(Z^× ⊗ ℚ_p)²` with the good-place neutral conditions of [Kim's conjecture on eventual equality](#nc-6-kim-conjecture) ([Depth-one Kummer and Selmer comparison](#nc-3-depth-one-selmer-comparison), SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0, S-unit Kummer identification). The local Kummer map at the tangential base point has as coordinates the regularised iterated integrals from 0 ([Iterated integrals as Albanese coordinates](#nc-4-iterated-coordinates), at the integral unit-tangential base point): `∫dz/z = log z` and `∫dz/(z − 1) = log(1 − z)` at depth 1, and the depth-2 coordinate `−Li_2(z)` ([Punctured-line logarithms and dilogarithms](#punctured-line-polylogarithms)). A zero of the p-adic logarithm on `ℤ_p^×` is a root of unity, and z, 1 − z both roots of unity forces z to be a primitive sixth root of unity. A primitive sixth root of unity lies in `ℤ_p` exactly when p ≡ 1 mod 3. For p ≡ 1 mod 3, `Sel_2(𝒳) = 0` because `H¹(G_T, ℚ_p(2)) = 0`, so `X(ℤ_p)_2` is cut out by the depth-2 coordinate `−Li_2(z)` as well; since `Li_2(ζ_6⁻¹) = −Li_2(ζ_6)` ([Punctured-line logarithms and dilogarithms](#punctured-line-polylogarithms), with `log ζ_6 = 0`), the two candidates vanish or survive together.

**Checks.**

- At `p=3`, `Φ₃(1+X)=X²+3X+3` is Eisenstein, so `ℚ₃` has no primitive cube root and hence no primitive sixth root. The depth-one integral locus is empty.
`- p = 5: X(Z_5)_1 = ∅`.
`- p = 7: X(Z_7)_1 = {3, 5}` modulo the identification of `ζ_6` with the Teichmüller lifts of 3 and 5, the primitive sixth roots of unity mod 7.
- At `p=7`, BDCKW §6.3's nonvanishing gives `X(ℤ₇)_2=∅`, although `X(ℤ₇)_1` has two points.
- The congruences `p ≡ 3,5 mod 8` make 2 nonsquare in `ℚ_p`; BDCKW §7.6 uses this for the genus-two cover `y²=8x⁶−108x⁴−1296x²+11664` of `y²=x³−891x+4374` with the origin removed. These are distinct curves from the thrice-punctured line.

### Examples

For a free Lie algebra on two generators, the Witt formula gives dimensions 2, `(4−2)/2=1` and `(8−2)/3=2` in degrees 1,2,3. For a proper genus-two curve, the symplectic relation removes one degree-two direction from `Λ²` of a four-dimensional space, giving 5. On `P¹−{0,1,∞}`, complex conjugation acts by −1 on both degree-one Tate generators. It therefore has trace `−d_n` in odd degree n, so the negative eigenspace has dimension `d_n`, rather than `d_n/2`. The proper-curve odd-degree count is a different specialization.

For odd p, Soulé's rational Tate calculation starts at twist `k=2: H²` vanishes, `H¹` is zero for even k and has dimension one for odd `k≥3`. The weight-one group is instead the S-unit calculation. An odd sum beginning with `k=1` counts the wrong group; the first higher odd contribution is `k=3`.

For `Λ=ℤ_p[[T₁,T₂]]`, the module `Λ/(p,T₁)=F_p[[T₂]]` is pseudo-null but is not finitely generated over `ℤ_p`. It contributes zero after tensoring with `ℚ_p`. The dimension argument uses finite-dimensionality of `I⊗ℚ_p`, established through the p-torsion-free quotient, rather than finite generation of I itself. At `p=2` with real places, integral `H³` may contain 2-torsion while rational `H³` still vanishes.

Let `L_n={0}∪{n,n+1,…}` in the natural numbers. This is a decreasing sequence with intersection {0}, but no `L_n` equals {0}. Thus intersection equality is weaker than eventual equality of the Chabauty–Kim loci. The named eventual-equality conjecture retains its quantifier `∃N`, `∀n≥N`.

For the thrice-punctured line, use the integral unit tangent at 0. The depth-one coordinates are log z and `log(1−z)`. A common zero in `ℤ_p` with z and 1−z units makes both roots of unity and forces a primitive sixth root in the source-qualified calculation. For `p=3,5`, the depth-one locus is empty (BDCKW §6.1). For `p=7`, the two depth-one candidates disappear at depth two: BDCKW §6.3 establishes `Li₂(ζ₆) ≠ 0` numerically for primes `p ≡ 1 mod 3` below `10⁵`. The conditions `p ≡ 3,5 mod 8` in §7.6 concern a genus-two cover of a punctured elliptic curve, with `d=2` nonsquare in `ℚ_p`. The base point is tangential because this open curve has no ordinary Z-point.


For an antitone family of loci containing all rational points, eventual equality implies intersection equality. The containment hypotheses preserve the early loci as well as the tail; intersection equality by itself does not imply a stable tail.

## Downstream consumers

EffectiveDiophantineMethods consumes §5.8's global abelian logarithm, integration pairing and regular Coleman/abelian equality, together with the residue-chart zero bounds, path equations and quadratic height loci of Layers 5–6. Its §4.2 abelian-logarithm names and §4.6 regular comparison use these common constructions; its finite data and effective applications belong there. ColemanIntegration supplies the analytic Coleman algebra and transport; the generic Jacobian comparison belongs to §5.8 here. HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions §§1.15a–1.16 remains the sole supplier of formal groups, identity charts and their convergent formal logarithms. The supplier order is formal charts and logarithms, Coleman integration, the global logarithm and comparisons here, then their effective applications. Generic restricted-series zero bounds come from RestrictedPowerSeries §2.4, and analytic Coleman functions, primitives and polylogarithms from ColemanIntegration L1–L2; Layer 5 supplies their tensor-path comparisons and Chabauty applications. PeriodsAndSpecialValues uses tangential path periods and the two finite towers. Arithmetic Galois and moduli applications use the relative outer reconstruction interfaces of Layer 3. General motives and K-theory may consume the supplied neutral tensor reconstruction and the Tate-character and Selmer comparisons constructed here.

A theorem identifying all rational points from these equations assumes the stated local images, complete correction sets, rank and completeness of the specified zero sets. Named conjectures remain hypotheses of their conditional consequences.
